records.title: Motion-Guided Query-based Transformer for Visible-Event Tracking
records.abstract: While deep learning has significantly advanced visual tracking, modern RGB trackers are no longer limited to single-frame appearance matching. Recent works have leveraged short-term temporal information, utilizing historical trajectory prediction and appearance evolution to assist tracking. However, due to the temporal sparsity of RGB data, these methods struggle with challenging scenarios such as high-speed motion and occlusions, where trajectory and appearance cues become unreliable. To address these limitations, we propose a novel query-based RGB-E tracker that effectively leverages rich temporal information provided by event modality. Our encoder-decoder architecture features a Context Encoder for cross-modal feature fusion and a Motion-Guided Decoder incorporating two key modules: Query Memory Enhancement (QME) and Motion-Guided Decoder Block (MGDB). The MGDB module thoroughly models event motion information to handle complex motion patterns, while the QME module employs long-term memory to prevent tracking failures caused by appearance variations. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on three RGB-E benchmarks, illustrating the effectiveness of motion cues.

records.title: OmniEraser: Remove Objects and Their Effects in Images with Paired Video-Frame Data
records.abstract: Inpainting algorithms have achieved remarkable progress in removing objects from images, yet still face two challenges: 1) struggle to handle the object's visual effects, such as shadow and reflection; 2) easily generate shape-like artifacts and unintended content. In this paper, we propose Video4Removal, a large-scale dataset comprising over 100,000 high-quality samples with realistic object shadows and reflections. By constructing object-background pairs from video frames with off-the-shelf vision models, the labor costs of data acquisition can be significantly reduced. To avoid generating shape-like artifacts and unintended content, we propose Object-Background Guidance, an elaborated paradigm that takes both the foreground object and background images. It can guide the diffusion process to harness richer contextual information. Based on the above two designs, we present OmniEraser, a novel method that seamlessly removes objects and their visual effects using only object masks as input. Extensive experiments show that OmniEraser significantly outperforms previous methods, particularly in complex in-the-wild scenes. And it also exhibits a strong generalization ability in anime-style images. Datasets, models, and codes will be published.

records.title: DST-AD: Dual-Stream Spatio-Temporal Representation Learning for Anomaly Detection in Dynamic Graphs
records.abstract: In order to detect abnormal behavior in continuous-time dynamic graphs, it is essential to model the intricate relationship between space and time. Existing methods typically couple these two domains, thereby obscuring the distinct properties of each anomaly type. To address this, we introduce DST-AD (Dual Stream Spatio-Temporal Representation Learning for Anomaly Detection in Dynamic Graphs), a self-supervised framework that explicitly decouples spatial and temporal representations.In this architecture, we utilize the dynamics of differential equations to model the temporal evolution of nodes, while simultaneously capturing spatial topology by explicitly modeling the bilinear interactions between local temporal attention and global time-constrained random walks. This approach enables the detection of anomalies based on significant deviations from either the expected temporal trajectory or the current spatial context.Extensive empirical evaluations on real-world datasets demonstrate that DST-AD achieves performance comparable to or surpassing state-of-the-art baselines. Our code is available at https://github.com/lemon10182020-netizen/DST-AD.

records.title: Multi-Focus Temporal Shifting for Precise Event Spotting in Sports Videos
records.abstract: Precise Event Spotting (PES) in sports videos requires frame-level recognition of fine-grained actions from single-camera footage. Existing PES models typically incorporate lightweight temporal modules such as the Gate Shift Module (GSM) or the Gate Shift Fuse to enrich 2D CNN feature extractors with temporal context. However, these modules are limited in both temporal receptive field and spatial adaptability. We propose Multi-Focus Temporal Shifting Module (MFS) that enhances GSM with multi-scale temporal shifts and Group Focus Module, enabling efficient modeling of both short and long-term dependencies while focusing on salient regions. MFS is a lightweight, plug-and-play module that integrates seamlessly with diverse 2D backbones. To further advance the field, we introduce the Table Tennis Australia dataset, the first PES benchmark for table tennis containing over 4,800 precisely annotated events. Extensive experiments across five PES benchmarks demonstrate that MFS consistently improves performance with minimal overhead, achieving leading results among lightweight methods (+4.09 mAP, 45 GFLOPs). All code and datasets are publicly available at https://github.com/AugustRushG/MFS

records.title: Zero-shot Video Grounding via Temporal Logic
records.abstract: Video Temporal Grounding (VTG) aims to precisely localize a target video segment within an untrimmed video given a natural language query. Despite significant progress driven by Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), existing supervised VTG methods still suffer from prohibitive annotation overhead and limited generalization capability. Conversely, while training-free approaches eliminate the need for labeled data by relying on frame-text similarity, they fundamentally fail to model the temporal dependencies and structure inherent in queries, which severely limits their scalability to handle long videos and complex queries. To overcome these limitations, we propose Temporal Logic with Iterative Coverage Thresholding (TL-ICT), a novel zero-shot framework that addresses VTG by explicitly and systemically modeling the temporal structure of the query. TL-ICT harnesses the strong reasoning capabilities of pre-trained Large Language Models (LLMs) to parse the complex temporal logic within the queries, integrating this high-level semantic reasoning with an Iterative Coverage Thresholding (ICT) algorithm for robust and precise temporal localization. Extensive experiments on Charades-STA and ActivityNet Captions datasets validate that TL-ICT achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot performance, particularly showing significant advancements in handling complex sequential and temporal reasoning queries. This work establishes TL-ICT as an efficient, highly effective, and pioneering zero-shot solution for Video Temporal Grounding.

records.title: Frequency-guided Temporal-spatial Feature Enhancement for Weakly Supervised Temporal Action Localization
records.abstract: Weakly supervised temporal action localization (WTAL) aims to detect action instances using only video-level labels. However, existing methods rely on temporal-spatial feature modeling and still face significant challenges in accurately perceiving and localizing action boundaries. The frequency-domain analysis naturally encodes low-frequency static semantics and high-frequency motion variations from a global perspective, which offers a new avenue for uncovering implicit information beyond temporal-spatial features. Therefore, this paper proposes a frequency-guided temporal-spatial feature enhancement network (FTFENet) that leverages frequency analysis to enhance temporal-spatial representations. Specifically, FTFENet designs frequency enhanced representation learning, which constructs adaptive frequency filters for content-aware frequency selection, capturing discriminative frequency cues. Meanwhile, a frequency energy modulation strategy further adjusts the spectral magnitude distribution, amplifying action-relevant components while suppressing redundant responses, thereby improving action sensitivity and feature discriminability. Extensive experiments on WTAL benchmarks validate the effectiveness of FTFENet, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

records.title: Beyond Naturalness: Metric-Guided Generation of Domain-Semantic 3D Motions
records.abstract: Generating 3D virtual teachers with high pedagogical quality is a pivotal challenge in educational technology. Existing motion generation methods primarily focus on physical naturalness and kinematic plausibility, largely neglecting domain-specific semantics such as enthusiasm and organization. Consequently, generated avatars may achieve kinematic realism yet fail to exhibit instructional effectiveness. To bridge this gap, we present a novel data-driven framework for generating physically natural and pedagogically effective 3D teacher motions. Our contributions are threefold: First, we construct TeacherMotion3D, the first 3D teacher-motion dataset for one-on-one tutoring with fine-grained pedagogical ratings. This dataset decouples motion from appearance, enabling privacy-preserving and view-invariant analysis. Second, we propose TeacherMotionCritic, a domain-specific evaluation metric that bridges low-level kinematic features with expert-rated pedagogical scores, establishing a quantitative benchmark for instructional quality. Third, we develop TeacherMotionGen, a generative framework that incorporates TeacherMotionCritic as a semantic guide. By steering the diffusion-based generation process with pedagogical feedback, our model synthesizes virtual teacher motions that are both kinematically plausible and pedagogically effective. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TeacherMotionGen outperforms state-of-the-art generic motion generators in instructional scenarios, both quantitatively and qualitatively.

records.title: Towards a Generalizable Bimanual Foundation Policy via Flow-based Video Prediction
records.abstract: Learning a generalizable bimanual manipulation policy is extremely challenging for embodied agents due to the large action space and the need for coordinated arm movements. Existing approaches rely on Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to acquire bimanual policies. However, transferring knowledge from single-arm datasets or pre-trained VLA models often fails to generalize effectively, primarily due to the scarcity of bimanual data and the fundamental differences between single-arm and bimanual manipulation. In this paper, we propose a novel bimanual foundation policy by fine-tuning the leading text-to-video models to predict robot trajectories and training a lightweight diffusion inverse dynamics model for action generation. Given the lack of embodied knowledge in text-to-video models, we introduce a two-stage paradigm that fine-tunes independent text-to-flow and flow-to-video models derived from a pre-trained text-to-video model. Specifically, optical flow serves as an intermediate variable, providing a concise representation of subtle movements between images. The text-to-flow model predicts optical flow to concretize the intent of language instructions, and the flow-to-video model leverages this flow for fine-grained video prediction. Our method mitigates the ambiguity of language in single-stage text-to-video prediction and significantly reduces the robot-data requirement by avoiding direct use of low-level actions. In experiments, we collect high-quality manipulation data for real dual-arm robot, and the results of simulation and real-world experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

records.title: RL-AdaptTrack: Reinforcement Learning-based Adaptive Frame Rate Control for Efficient Multi-Object Tracking
records.abstract: Deploying Multi-Object Tracking (MOT) on resource-constrained edge devices is challenging due to the high computational cost of processing video streams. While scene complexity and target dynamics vary significantly over time, traditional MOT systems rigidly operate at fixed frame rates. This inflexibility leads to substantial computational waste in simple scenes and potential latency in complex ones. In this paper, we propose RL-AdaptTrack, a reinforcement learning-based framework that dynamically adjusts frame rates to optimize the trade-off between tracking performance and computational efficiency. Unlike prior adaptive approaches that focus on resolution tuning or require expensive online profiling, RL-AdaptTrack formulates frame rate control as a Markov Decision Process (MDP). This formulation allows the agent to learn policies that account for the temporal dependencies of tracking, balancing immediate efficiency gains against long-term tracking stability. To enable effective training, we introduce a multi-variant strategy generation method that systematically constructs diverse frame rate scheduling policies, addressing the challenge of sample scarcity. Extensive experiments on MOT17 and MOT20 demonstrate that RL-AdaptTrack achieves 28.53% and 54.44% computational savings with negligible MOTA degradation (1.7% and 0.1%, respectively), significantly outperforming both fixed frame rate baselines and rule-based adaptive strategies.

records.title: Augmenting Visual Projection with Multi-Text Alignment for Multimodal Chart Understanding
records.abstract: Accurate chart understanding is essential for scientific analysis, yet the visual projector serving as the core of chart comprehension in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) struggles to capture the heterogeneous and multi-source nature of chart information. This limitation prevents existing architectures from fully exploiting the rich semantic cues and structural patterns embedded in the charts. We introduce MQCA, a Multi-Query Chart Adapter that enhances modality alignment through three lightweight branches, each trained by a different chart-related textual representation: captions, tables, and code. These branches learn complementary semantic aspects of the charts and inject them into the visual features before merging with the base projector. MQCA is fully compatible with standard MLLMs frameworks and adds only minimal inference overhead. Experiments on image-text alignment metric and multiple downstream chart understanding benchmarks show that MQCA consistently boosts performance, e.g., MQCA improves the accuracy of the MLP projector on the ChartQA benchmark by 4.19%, confirming that integrating multi-source chart cues during training leads to richer, more informative, and chart-aware visual representations.

records.title: Decoupled Sensitivity-Consistency Learning for Weakly Supervised Video Anomaly Detection
records.abstract: Recent weakly supervised video anomaly detection methods have achieved significant advances by employing unified frameworks for joint optimization. However, this paradigm is limited by a fundamental sensitivity–stability trade-off, as the conflicting objectives for detecting transient and sustained anomalies lead to either fragmented predictions or over-smoothed responses. To address this limitation, we propose DeSC, a novel Decoupled Sensitivity-Consistency framework that trains two specialized streams using distinct optimization strategies. The temporal sensitivity stream adopts an aggressive optimization strategy to capture high-frequency abrupt changes, whereas the semantic consistency stream applies robust constraints to maintain long-term coherence and reduce noise. Their complementary strengths are fused through a collaborative inference mechanism that reduces individual biases and produces balanced predictions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DeSC establishes new state-of-the-art performance by achieving 89.37%AUC on UCF-Crime (+1.29%) and 87.18%AP on XD-Violence (+2.22%). Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/DeSC.

records.title: Uni-Classifier: Leveraging Video Diffusion Priors for Universal Guidance Classifier
records.abstract: In practical AI workflows, complex tasks often involve chaining multiple generative models, such as using a video or 3D generation model after a 2D image generator. However, distributional mismatches between the output of upstream models and the expected input of downstream models frequently degrade overall generation quality. To address this issue, we propose Uni-Classifier (Uni-C), a simple yet effective plug-and-play module that leverages video diffusion priors to guide the denoising process of preceding models, thereby aligning their outputs with downstream requirements. Uni-C can also be applied independently to enhance the output quality of individual generative models. Extensive experiments across video and 3D generation demonstrate that Uni-C consistently improves generation quality in both workflow-based and standalone settings, highlighting its versatility and strong generalization capability.

records.title: OncoDrugs: Embodied Oncology Knowledge Perception and Extraction from Multimedia Sources
records.abstract: Personalized tumor treatment hinges on the accurate acquisition of evidence regarding complex gene-drug interactions, yet existing oncology knowledge extraction methods suffer from notable limitations—they do not integrate structured clinical guidelines with dynamic literature resources. To address existing gaps and advance intelligent embodied healthcare in oncology, OncoDrugs is proposed as an embodied framework dedicated to the perception and extraction of multimodal knowledge of oncology. As a core component of embodied intelligent healthcare, OncoDrugs integrates structured knowledge mined from clinical guidelines with real-time insights extracted from PubMed literature by a two-stage multi-agent system. Evaluations on expert-verified benchmarks show that the proposed method achieves exceptional performance. By allowing for comprehensive multimodal knowledge perception, the proposed system can reduce treatment planning time and support precision oncology for rare genomic mutations.

records.title: Knowledge-Preserved Model Tuning in Null-Space for Robust Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding
records.abstract: Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding aims to localize object tubes based on textual queries. While recent methods have achieved remarkable success, they mainly focus on high-quality(HQ) inputs, neglecting the widespread presence of low-quality(LQ) videos in real-world scenarios. Although tuning methods like LoRA can adapt to degraded inputs, they inevitably disrupt pre-trained knowledge. To address this, we propose Null-Space Tuning (NST). This framework exploits the geometric property that adding vectors within the null-space of frozen weights to the layer input does not affect the output. Leveraging this, NST injects learnable residuals into input features that can be selectively invisible to the pre-trained backbone. Specifically, NST combines the Quality-Adaptive Unit and Dual-Space Reparameterization to synthesize these residuals by confining components for HQ inputs to the null-space, while directing restoration components for LQ inputs to the non-null space. As the frozen weights eliminate null-space components, we effectively rectify degraded inputs while preserving pre-trained knowledge for HQ inputs. Extensive experiments show that NST outperforms state-of-the-art methods on our Mixed-Quality benchmark.

records.title: Enabling Consistent Low-Latency Delivery for Video Upstreaming over Wi-Fi Networks
records.abstract: Wi-Fi connectivity has become increasingly pervasive for upstreaming video. However, dynamic variations in Wi-Fi latency have become a major source of delay jitter, severely affecting the upstreaming performance. In this paper, we propose RefineUp, a driver-state-aware transmission optimization dedicated to video upstreaming over Wi-Fi. By capturing the wireless dynamics from the Wi-Fi driver layer, we design a Wi-Fi status monitor to track the driver's data backlog and hardware retry counts. RefineUp further incorporates a control logic to optimize the sending rate generated by congestion control algorithms (CCAs) and the retransmission timing of the transport protocols. To ensure broad compatibility, RefineUp supports rate and retransmission refinement for both kernel- and user-space video frameworks. Real-world evaluations using different video frameworks show that RefineUp ensures consistent low-latency during upstreaming over Wi-Fi networks, suppressing the 99.9th-percentile frame delay by 42.6% and reducing the rebuffering ratio by over 40%.

records.title: ORMamba: Ordinal Regressive Multiscale Temporal Fusion Mamba for Action Quality Assessment
records.abstract: Action Quality Assessment (AQA) aims to evaluate the performance of specific actions. Given an action video for AQA, state-of-the-art(SOTA) approaches have generally cast the scoring task as a regression problem that maps spatiotemporal deep video features to overall action quality scores. However, these approaches often struggle to capture long-range temporal dependencies, further leading to limited regression performance, especially when addressing imbalanced data distributions. To address these issues, we propose Ordinal Regression Mamba (ORMamba), an novel end-to-end AQA framework. ORMamba uses a multiscale temporal fusion Mamba module for capturing long-range spatiotemporal dynamics across action segments, explicitly models action execution mistakes for discriminative representations, and integrates ordinal regression for coarse-to-fine scoring, which significantly boost the overall performance. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that ORMamba attains SOTA performance across both short-term and long-term AQA benchmarks, thereby confirming the effectiveness of our proposed method. Our code is available at https://github.com/chengchen-ccnu/ORMamba.

records.title: Flexible and Efficient Input-Adaptive Multiple Object Tracking
records.abstract: Most existing end-to-end Multiple Object Tracking (MOT) methods employ a static, one-size-fits-all inference for all inputs. This rigid processing not only wastes computational resources on simple instances but also introduces redundancy and noise, diluting critical tracking cues. In this paper, we propose a flexible MOT architecture that adaptively tailors inference depth to enhance computational efficiency and counteract noise accumulation. First, to address redundancy, we introduce a Recurrent Monitor Subnetwork that adaptively adjusts the inference depth of the input. Unlike conventional early-exit networks that rely on independent routers—often leading to unstable exit decisions, our method continuously monitors the state of the tracked object, ensuring the reliability of input-adaptive inference. Complementing this, we propose a Guided Focus Module (GFM) to mitigate noise accumulation during deep inference. The GFM leverages fine-grained spatial details from shallow embeddings to guide deep attention, effectively filtering noise while retaining target-specific semantics. Extensive experiments on three benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple metrics, and 1.3× faster inference compared with the baseline.

records.title: Personalized Educational Scenario Generation in Virtual Reality for Daily Energy Management
records.abstract: Energy waste is common in daily life but can be mitigated by improving energy management skills, which is vital for reducing consumption and carbon emissions. We propose a VR-based framework that generates personalized energy education scenarios. User behaviors in the virtual environment are recorded to model individual attributes, including spatial interaction patterns and energy management proficiency. A large language model (LLM) personalizes scene layouts and generates narrative scenarios targeting users’ weakest energy-related behaviors while maintaining coherence and interactivity. User interactions dynamically update the state model, enabling storylines to adapt in real time. In a user study comparing our approach with a free-exploration VR group and a slideshow-based instruction group, results show that personalized VR training significantly enhances the ability to identify energy waste and delivers a superior educational experience.

records.title: Adaptive Event Camera Denoising with Spatiotemporal Density Filtering
records.abstract: Dynamic Vision Sensors, also known as event cameras, generate asynchronous events with high temporal resolution, but often suffer from background activity noise and hot-pixel events, which degrade tasks such as reconstruction and motion estimation. This paper proposes an adaptive denoising method that integrates spatiotemporal Gaussian-weighted modeling with an adaptive threshold strategy. Using the spatiotemporal distribution of events, the method dynamically adjusts denoising strength and adapts to varying noise patterns across regions and time. Polarity-separated processing and a multi-iteration mechanism further improve the discrimination of real events. Experiments on labeled and unlabeled datasets show that the proposed method achieves a higher Noise Event Removal rate (NeRr) and Effective Event Removal rate (VeRr) than mainstream algorithms and improves SNR by 33.7%, SSIM by 23.3% and AOCC by 16.5%. The results demonstrate strong denoising capacity and structural preservation under diverse illumination and noise conditions, with robust cross-scene generalization.

records.title: H-VSSM: A Hilbert-Driven Context-Shunting Framework for Robust Structural Defect Detection
records.abstract: While Visual State Space Models (VSSMs) offer linear complexity for long-range dependency modeling, their standard anisotropic scanning strategies inevitably disrupt 2D spatial locality. We identify that this neighborhood breaking is particularly detrimental to the topological continuity of fine-grained structural cracks. To bridge this gap, we propose H-VSSM, a Hilbert-driven framework designed to maximize topological fidelity. Central to our approach is the Fluid Hilbert-based Structure-Aware Selective Scan (H-SS2D). By leveraging the isotropic nature of the Peano-Hilbert curve, H-SS2D ensures that geometrically adjacent pixels remain contiguous in the 1D sequence, effectively mitigating the fragmentation issues inherent in linear scans. Complementing this, we introduce a Feature Shunt Attention Module (FSAM) that employs a divide-and-conquer strategy to decouple high-frequency crack details from background noise, alongside an Edge Information Enhanced Module (EIEM) for multi-scale context aggregation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that H-VSSM establishes a new state-of-the-art. On the challenging DeepCrack dataset, it achieves an F1 score of 94.02% and mIoU of 93.22%, outperforming recent competitors, demonstrating exceptional robustness in complex scenarios. The code is available at: https://github.com/chen-yuzhi/HVSSM.

records.title: Reviving the Scene Behind You: Camera-Controllable Background Animation for Human Motion Videos
records.abstract: In this paper, we explore the task of reviving static scene images into dynamic and coherent environments, conditioned on a human foreground video, a camera pose sequence, and a reference scene image. This task presents several challenges: 1) the generated background should accurately follow the camera movements and remain synchronized with the human subject; 2) newly revealed regions during camera shifts need to appear seamless and visually coherent; and 3) the background content must maintain consistent textures to preserve spatial and temporal continuity. To address these challenges, we propose DynaScene, a multi-task learning framework that integrates camera pose control with auxiliary tasks, i.e., background outpainting and scene variation, to enable realistic and temporally consistent video background generation. Additionally, we introduce a large-scale human video dataset comprising over 200K high-resolution and motion-rich clips, 10x larger than existing real-world human video datasets, providing a valuable resource for human-centric video synthesis tasks.

records.title: V-CORE: Temporally Consistent Video Understanding for Video-LLM
records.abstract: Recent Video Large Language Models (Video-LLMs) have shown strong multimodal reasoning capabilities, yet remain challenged by video understanding tasks that require consistent temporal ordering and causal coherence. Many parameter-efficient Video-LLMs rely on unconstrained bidirectional projectors to model inter-frame interactions, which can blur temporal ordering by allowing later frames to influence earlier representations, without explicit architectural mechanisms to respect the directional nature of video reasoning. To address this limitation, we propose V-CORE, a parameter-efficient framework that introduces explicit temporal ordering constraints for video understanding. V-CORE consists of two key components: (1) Learnable Spatial Aggregation (LSA), which adaptively selects salient spatial tokens to reduce redundancy, and (2) a Causality-Aware Temporal Projector (CATP), which enforces structured unidirectional information flow via block-causal attention and a terminal dynamic summary token acting as a causal sink. This design preserves intra-frame spatial interactions while ensuring that temporal information is aggregated in a strictly ordered manner. With 4-bit QLoRA and a frozen LLM backbone, V-CORE can be trained efficiently on a single consumer GPU. Experiments show that V-CORE achieves strong performance on the challenging NExT-QA benchmark, reaching 61.2% accuracy, and remains competitive across MSVD-QA, MSRVTT-QA, and TGIF-QA, with gains concentrated in temporal and causal reasoning subcategories (+3.5% and +5.2% respectively), directly validating the importance of explicit temporal ordering constraints.

records.title: TimeColor: Flexible Reference Colorization via Temporal Concatenation
records.abstract: Most colorization models condition only on a single reference, typically the first frame of the scene. However, this approach ignores other sources of conditional data, such as character sheets, background images, or arbitrary colorized frames. We propose TimeColor, a sketch-based video colorization model that supports heterogeneous, variable-count references with the use of explicit per-reference region assignment. TimeColor encodes references as additional latent frames which are concatenated temporally, permitting them to be processed concurrently in each diffusion step while keeping the model's parameter count fixed. TimeColor also uses spatiotemporal correspondence-masked attention to enforce subject-reference binding in addition to modality-disjoint RoPE indexing. These mechanisms mitigate shortcutting and cross-identity palette leakage. Experiments on Sakuga-42M under both single- and multi-reference protocols show that TimeColor improves color fidelity, identity consistency, and temporal stability over prior baselines. Our project page is available at https://bconstantine.github.io/TimeColor/.

records.title: HuM-Eval: A Coarse-to-Fine Framework for Human-Centric Video Evaluation
records.abstract: Video generation models have developed rapidly in recent years, where generating natural human motion plays a pivotal role.However, accurately evaluating the quality of generated human motion video remains a significant challenge. Existing evaluation metrics primarily focus on global scene statistics, often overlooking fine-grained human details and consequently failing to align with human subjective preference.To bridge this gap, we propose HuM-Eval, a novel human-centric evaluation framework that adopts a coarse-to-fine strategy. Specifically, our framework first utilizes a VLM to perform a coarse assessment of global video quality. It then proceeds to a fine-grained analysis, using 2D pose to verify anatomical correctness and 3D human motion to evaluate motion stability.Extensive experiments demonstrate that HuM-Eval achieves an average human correlation of 58.2%, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines. Furthermore, we intro- duce HuM-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark comprising 1,000 diverse prompts, and conduct a detailed evaluation of existing text-to-video models, paving the way for next-generation human motion generation.

records.title: Multi-Object Tracking based on ID switch Correction
records.abstract: Motion information (MI) plays a critical role in Multi-Object Tracking (MOT), especially when dealing with target deformation, occlusion and complex background etc. In this paper, a novel spatiotemporal alignment scheme of motion information (MI) has been proposed to address the shortcomings of existing methods in MI modelling. Through the propagation of historical trajectory state and dynamic fusion, it overcomes the accumulated error in single-frame and enhances the discrimination of similar motions under occluded scenarios. Then, a block based appearance feature extraction and fusion mechanism has been developed, which splits the detection bounding boxes into multiple regions and selectively focuses on visible parts to suppress the negative impact of occlusion. Finally and most importantly, an identity correction mechanism based on motion-appearance consistency has been presented, which enables fast error recovery through abnormal trajectory detection and bidirectional backtracking, thereby improving the fault tolerance of long-term tracking. Extensive experiments on mainstream datasets have demonstrated the superiority of our tracker, which provides an efficient and robust solution for pedestrian tracking in complex scenarios.

records.title: Spatiotemporally Decoupled Autoregressive Diffusion Model for Human Motion Generation
records.abstract: Text-driven human motion synthesis has made substantial development with two core modules of motion representation and generative architecture. For representation, Vector Quantization (VQ)-based methods compress motion data into discrete tokens while latent-based models operate directly in continuous space. However, both of these representations exhibit significant limitations. VQ-based methods suffer from inherent information loss, which compromises the quality, diversity, and generalization of generated motions, while continuous representation on holistic whole-body motion hinders part-level flexibility. For architecture, diffusion and autoregressive diffusion models have demonstrated their superiority, yet the fine-grained controllability over individual body parts is also limited. Thus, we propose a unified spatiotemporally decoupled framework named DeMoDiff, which jointly redesigns representation and architecture. To enhance representation extraction capabilities and offer greater part-level controllability, we present a spatial-temporal VAE that encodes each body joint rather than compressing the whole-body motion into a single latent space. Then, we incorporate spatial-temporal masking and attention mechanisms into an autoregressive diffusion generator, achieving both generative capability and controllable editability. Extensive experiments on the HumanML3D and KIT-ML datasets demonstrate that our model achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction performance and compelling motion generation results. Moreover, our framework demonstrates strong temporal and spatial editing capabilities, further validating its effectiveness.

records.title: Visual Tracking with Decoupled Classification and Regression Features
records.abstract: One-stream Transformer trackers have achieved remarkable success which implement feature extraction and relation modelling within a unified backbone. However, they suffer a critical contradiction: the classification task focuses on discriminative parts, while regression emphasizes the geometric information of the complete object contour. Inspired by the task-specific context decoupling strategy in object detection, we propose PGTrack in this paper, which decouples geometric modeling from semantic discrimination. Firstly, we introduce a set of Object Proposals via an inverted attention mechanism, which decomposes the search region into distinct entities to capture the shape of the object. Meanwhile, we present a Prototype-Guided Proposal Selection module to determine the optimal candidate location. It utilizes the global attention prior to construct a target prototype, so as to select the object with the highest similarity to the template. Extensive experiments on 4 mainstream benchmarks demonstrate that PGTrack outperforms other popular methods with appealing results.

records.title: DSVG: A Dual-Stream Framework for Multi-Task Visual Grounding with Decoupled Multimodal Alignment and Visual Perception
records.abstract: Visual grounding aims to localize a target object in the image based on a given textual description. Although most advanced methods employ modality-shared encoding to extract robust representations, they often attenuate fine-grained visual details in pursuit of stronger multimodal semantic alignment. To overcome this limitation, we propose a dual-stream visual encoding framework that effectively decouples multimodal semantic alignment from detailed visual perception. Specifically, one multimodal branch is designed with prompt-guided modulation and noun-masked pretraining to achieve semantic alignment between the image and text, producing target-specific semantic features and semantic-aligned visual features. In parallel, a separate visual branch performs semantically guided visual encoding to extract detail-aware features capturing fine-grained visual cues of the target and semantically similar objects. Finally, the semantic-aligned and detail-aware visual features are fused to generate the predictions by integrating complementary information. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate that our method consistently achieves state-of-the-art results, validating the advantage of disentangling semantic alignment from visual perception. Our code is available in the supplementary materials.

records.title: Multi-Drone Video Tracking with Scene Context Perception and Proactive Temporal Prediction
records.abstract: Multi-drone collaborative video tracking offers large field-of-view advantages over single-drone systems. However, existing trackers mainly rely on geometric constraints for multi-view fusion without fully exploiting visual semantic consistency. Besides, they typically operate with a reactive collaboration mechanism, where calibration message routing across multiple drones suffers from excessive delay as it initiates solely upon tracking failures. To address these issues, a novel multi-agent collaborative tracking framework is proposed, advancing toward unified scene understanding and proactive risk prediction. Specifically, we introduce a semantic-aware fusion module that quantifies viewpoint complementarity via dual-level scene representations. Furthermore, we design a hierarchical proactive collaboration method that anticipates tracking anomalies by predicting fluctuations in confidence scores and motion trajectories, thereby triggering progressive interventions beforehand. Extensive experiments on the MDOT benchmark demonstrate that our method outperforms other state-of-the-art trackers, especially in full occlusion and out-of-view scenarios.

records.title: Robust 4D Action Segmentation in Corrupted Point Cloud Videos
records.abstract: 4D point cloud videos enable fine-grained modeling of dynamic actions by capturing 3D geometry and temporal evolution, yet existing action segmentation methods largely assume complete and noise-free observations. In realistic point cloud acquisition, severe occlusions and missing regions significantly degrade geometric perception and limit model robustness. To address this challenge, we propose a novel method, termed Shape Preservation Enhancement (SPE), which is able to perform as a plug-and-play module to overcome missing shape cues in corrupted observations. Specifically, it reinforces shape perceptibility by enhancing multi-view depth projections and injecting 2D shape priors into 3D point features. Moreover, we further construct a novel benchmark dataset HOI4D-C, which contains four representative corruption types to evaluate the robustness of 4D point cloud action segmentation. We evaluate our SPE method on both HOI4D and HOI4D-C, demonstrating its effectiveness and robustness across diverse model architectures under both complete and corrupted point cloud observations, consistently achieving state-of-the-art results.

records.title: FAST: A Synergistic Framework of Attention and State-space Models for Spatiotemporal Traffic Prediction
records.abstract: Accurate traffic forecasting is challenging due to complex spatiotemporal dependencies and long-range correlations. While Transformer-based models excel at capturing global dependencies, their quadratic attention cost hampers scalability; conversely, recent selective state space models such as Mamba offer linear-time efficiency but struggle with spatial reasoning on graph-structured data. We propose FAST, a synergistic Framework of Attention and State-space models for spatiotemporal Traffic forecasting, a unified framework that combines the representational power of attention with the efficiency of state-space modeling. FAST adopts a Temporal-Spatial-Temporal (TST) architecture, where attention-based temporal modules learn both short- and long-term temporal dynamics, and a Mamba-based spatial module efficiently models long-range spatial dependencies in linear time. A learnable multi-source spatiotemporal embedding integrates historical flow, temporal context, and node attributes into adaptive contextual representations. A multi-level skip prediction mechanism fuses features from different layers, improving multi-scale dependency modeling and training stability. Experimental results on three benchmark datasets (PeMS04, PeMS07, and PeMS08) demonstrate that our proposed FAST model consistently outperforms existing SOTA methods. Specifically, FAST achieves up to 4.3% lower RMSE and 2.8% lower MAE compared with the best-performing baselines, highlighting its superior accuracy, scalability, and generalizability for large-scale spatiotemporal sequence modeling.

records.title: DAHERC: Dynamic Alignment and Hierarchical Encoding Framework for MultiModal Emotion Recognition in Conversation
records.abstract: Multimodal Emotion Recognition in Conversation (MMERC) aims to identify the emotional states of speakers using multimodal data. However, most existing methods rely on a text-centric approach, treating text as the primary reference for feature alignment. This strategy overlooks the dynamic nature of communication, where acoustic or visual cues often carry the core emotional information, particularly when the text is ambiguous. To address this, we propose a novel framework named DAHERC. Firstly, we introduce a Dynamic Symmetric TriModal Attention (DSTA) module to achieve symmetric alignment across text, audio, and visual modalities. Secondly, to gain a more comprehensive understanding of emotions, we introduce a hierarchical contextual modeling strategy built upon feature alignment. This includes a speaker state tracker to capture individual emotional inertia, and a global atmosphere branch to grasp the overall tone of the conversation. This enables the model to comprehend dialogues holistically, from micro-level interactions to macro-level atmosphere. Finally, extensive experiments on the IEMOCAP and MELD datasets show that our model outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods.

records.title: Leveraging Subjective Emotional Cues in Redirected Walking: An Experimental Investigation on Perceptual Gains
records.abstract: This study investigates how subjective emotional states influence the perception of translation and rotation gains in Redirected Walking (RDW). We hypothesize that (1) positive emotion reduces redirection sensitivity, and (2) negative emotion enhances detectability. To test this, we designed rotation and translation tasks with emotion induction and measured detection thresholds (DTs) under neutral, positive, and negative conditions in a user study (N = 15). The results show significant DT variations across emotional states, with positive emotion generally expanding usable gain ranges and reducing redirection noticeability. A follow-up EEG study (N = 11) further confirmed the reliability of emotional induction and its correspondence with behavioral trends. Additional application experiments demonstrated that users in positive emotional states tolerated larger gains and achieved more efficient space utilization. These findings suggest that emotion-aware RDW parameter adaptation can improve locomotion performance and user experience in VR.

records.title: LaTAP-Track: Language-Guided Temporal Attention Pooling for Referring Multi-Object Tracking
records.abstract: Referring Multi-Object Tracking (RMOT) is a pivotal technique in multimedia understanding, aiming to localize and track specific targets continuously based on natural language queries. Despite recent progress in spatial feature alignment, existing approaches typically resort to static global average pooling for temporal aggregation. This paradigm treats all frames uniformly, inevitably diluting transient yet discriminative visual cues crucial for distinguishing targets. To address this limitation, we propose LaTAP-Track, a novel framework equipped with a Language-Guided Temporal Attention Pooling (LG-TAP) module. Departing from conventional uniform fusion, LG-TAP implements an active retrieval mechanism where textual semantics function as dynamic queries to reweight temporal frames, selectively highlighting high-value visual segments. By adaptively allocating attention based on cross-modal relevance, our approach effectively captures fine-grained, semantics-aligned motion and attribute cues. Extensive evaluations on the Refer-KITTI benchmark demonstrate the superiority of our method: LaTAP-Track achieves a HOTA score of 50.03%, surpassing the strong baseline (iKUN) by a substantial margin of 5.47 points. These results underscore the potential of semantic-driven dynamic aggregation in complex multimedia analysis.

records.title: Visual Causal Intervention for 3D Egocentric Multimodal Hand Trajectory Forecasting
records.abstract: 3D Egocentric Multimodal Hand Trajectory Forecasting (3D EMHTF) aims to predict future 3D hand motions from egocentric visual observations and historical trajectories. While previous works have achieved remarkable improvements in quantitative results, we identify that existing works process historical trajectories as confounders that introduce a backdoor path, allowing models to forecast future trajectories directly from past trajectories and undermining genuine visual reasoning. Such a limitation makes these existing methods suffer from low interpreterability and spurious correlation. To address this issue, we propose a causal intervention that blocks the backdoor path by enforcing partial missingness in historical trajectories, encouraging models to utilize visual information. Based on this principle, we develop a causal intervention module, termed VCI, which aims to boost multimodal reasoning capability in the 3D EMHTF models. Moreover, we also introduce two new benchmarks, i.e., H2O-CR and EgoPAT3D-CR, for more correctly evaluating trajectory dependency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our proposed VCI method achieves state-of-the-art performance consistently across both original and our newly proposed benchmarks.

records.title: MPLNet: A Feature Aggregation Framework for Multi-morphology Power Line Instance Detection
records.abstract: Accurate detection of power lines from a UAV perspective is a fundamental prerequisite for effective UAV-based intelligent inspection. However, existing detection approaches suffer from substantial limitations when confronted with various challenges, such as insufficient discriminative features and diverse morphologies. To address these challenges, we propose a lightweight multi-morphology power-line instance detection framework, termed MPLNet. Specifically, features are effectively aggregated via a Dynamic Region-of-Interest module (DyROI) and a Dynamic Spatial Attention (DSA) mechanism, which efficiently highlight power-line regions while suppressing background noise. Furthermore, an Adaptive Linear Intersection-over-Union (ALIoU) Loss is introduced to evaluate detection performance across power lines with various shapes. Experimental results on extensive datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in both detection accuracy and computational efficiency.

records.title: DTS2: A Decoupled Two-Stage Semantic Alignment Framework for Nighttime Infrared and Visible Image Fusion
records.abstract: Constrained by the scarcity of paired low-light and normal-light images in the infrared and visible image fusion domain, existing nighttime image fusion methods often rely on unsupervised strategies, frequently leading to color distortion and detail loss. To address this issue, We propose a Decoupled Two-Stage Semantic Alignment Framework. First, we design a Decoupled Two-Stage Semantic Alignment mechanism (DTS2). In Stage 1, a visible encoder is trained on low-light enhancement datasets to restore details and suppress darkness. In Stage 2, an infrared encoder and a fusion decoder are trained to integrate thermal radiation and complementary features. During inference, these components are cascaded into an end-to-end model, enabling simultaneous enhancement and fusion without paired data.Furthermore, we introduce a Multi-Scale Texture Refinement Module (MSTRM) and a Darkness-Aware Feature Enhancement Module (DAFEM) to improve texture contrast and dark-region details. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance, outperforming state-of-the-art algorithms across multiple metrics.The code will be available at https://github.com/Vegetvigbird/DTS2.

records.title: Hierarchical Cross-View Prompt Learning with View-Aware Attention for Aerial-Ground Person Re-Identification
records.abstract: Aerial-Ground Person Re-Identification (AGPReID) matches individuals across aerial and ground views, facing significant appearance gaps caused by viewpoint variations. Existing approaches typically address view discrepancy via attribute alignment or view decoupling, yet they often fail to explicitly model cross-view consistency and underutilize local features, limiting matching performance. To overcome this, we propose a novel Hierarchical Prompt and View-Aware Attention Transformer (HP-VAAT). Its core components include: a Hierarchical Cross-View Prompt (HCVP) module that learns global and local view-consistent prompts for multi-granularity alignment, and a View-Aware Attention (VAA) mechanism that incorporates view-specific biases to adaptively attend to discriminative regions across viewpoints. Together, these components enhance both global consistency and local discriminability. Experiments across three AGPReID benchmarks confirm the effectiveness and robustness of our approach.

records.title: Robust Event-Frame Object Detection via Spatio-Temporal-Modality-Scale Adaptive Selection
records.abstract: Conventional frame-based cameras often fail under rapid motion, overexposure, or low-light conditions due to limited dynamic range and fixed frame rates. In contrast, event cameras excel in these scenarios with high temporal resolution and dynamic range, but lack color and texture information. Existing event-frame fusion methods mostly emphasize feature fusion while overlooking critical ``selection" across spatio-temporal, modality, and scale dimensions. We propose EF-ASNet, a novel detection framework that pioneers adaptive feature selection, including data-level cross-modal selection, feature-level spatio-temporal and modality selection, and pre-decision multi-scale selection. Extensive experiments show our method improves mAP by \textbf{+17.7} on DSEC and \textbf{+4.4} on PKU-DDD17-Car, while achieving the fastest inference speed among comparable methods. Our approach demonstrates robustness in low-light, overexposure, and high-speed motion scenarios. Code will be released.

records.title: MYOLO-BoT: Accurate Behavior Recognition and Stable Tracking for Captive Proboscis Monkeys
records.abstract: Behavior recognition is critical for captive wildlife conservation, enabling early warning of abnormal behaviors and reducing injury risks. However, in real-world complex multi-target scenarios, existing methods face limitations like insufficient detection accuracy, frequent ID switching and loss in tracking. To address these issues, this study proposes a two-stage framework MYOLO-BoT, integrating improved YOLOv8 and optimized BoT-SORT. In the recognition stage, multi-dimensional optimizations are implemented for YOLOv8: the backbone network integrates Dilated Efficient Layer Aggregation Network(DELAN), with semantic comprehension enhanced through Image-Text feature fusion; additionally, the MDown and the attention-based detection head (AttDetect) are designed to improve representational capacity while reducing computational overhead. In the tracking stage, the matching strategy of BoT-SORT is optimized by expanding its matching space to alleviate the ID switching issue. Additionally, a State Space Model (SSM) is introduced to enhance the prediction accuracy of the target's motion state. Experiments were performed on a real-world proboscis monkey behavior recognition dataset. The proposed method achieves a mAP of 88.3% with its FLOPs reduced to 5.0G in the recognition stage and attains 64.2% MOTA and 73.4% IDF1 in the tracking stage, outperforming all baselines. These results validate the superiority of the proposed method in terms of accurate recognition, efficient tracking, and model lightweighting.

records.title: Interpretable Reinforcement Learning with Self-Abstraction and Refinement
records.abstract: We propose ReLIC, a reinforcement learning method with interactivity for composite tasks. Traditional RL methods lack interpretability, so it is difficult to integrate expert knowledge and refine the trained model. ReLIC is composed of a high-level logical model, low-level action policies, and a self-abstraction and refinement module. At its high level, it takes in predicates as its input so that we can design a synthesis algorithm to illustrate our high-level model's logical structure as an automaton, demonstrating our model's interpretability. At its low level, deep reinforcement learning is utilized for detailed action control to maintain high performance. Furthermore, based on the structured information provided by the automaton, ReLIC leverages GPT-4o to generate expert predicates and refine the automaton by injecting expert predicates and performing joint training, thereby enhancing RELIC's performance. ReLIC outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in several benchmarks with continuous state and action spaces. Additionally, ReLIC does not require humans to hard-code logical structures, so it can solve logically uncertain tasks.

records.title: RegInf: Region-driven DNN Inference via Motion Continuity in Multi-Camera Video Analytics
records.abstract: Edge video analytics is constrained by the high cost of DNN inference and limited edge resources. Prior studies commonly reduce redundancy via spatio-temporal filtering, but they rely on learned components or pixel-level differences rather than directly exploiting the spatio-temporal continuity of object motion. To address this challenge, we propose RegInf, a novel region-driven DNN inference framework via motion continuity to accelerate multi-camera video analytics. To confine inference to carefully selected regions, RegInf introduces a two-stage region abstraction, including 1) Discovery regions: Capture newly emerging objects using scene semantics, and 2) Tracking regions: Track object movement over time with minimal input. Furthermore, RegInf jointly merges and schedules regions across multiple camera pipelines, maximizing inference efficiency under shared resource constraints. We implement and evaluate RegInf using benchmark datasets of real-world video streams. The results show that RegInf achieves 16.34% higher accuracy than state-of-the-art methods, while reducing end-to-end inference latency by 79.31% and improving throughput by 3.60×.

records.title: Multimodal Aspect-Level Sentiment Analysis Based on Gated Noise Filtering and Emotion-Relevance Interaction
records.abstract: Multimodal Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (MABSA) infers fine-grained sentiment polarity toward specific aspects by jointly modeling text and images. Despite progress in cross-modal fusion, two challenges remain in multi-aspect settings: (1) multimodal noise, where aspect-irrelevant content distracts sentiment learning; and (2) weak cross-modal sentiment alignment, as visual evidence can be ambiguous and textual--visual sentiments may conflict, limiting multimodal complementarity. To address these issues, we propose a Gated Noise-filtered Sentiment-Relevance Interaction (GNSRI) framework. It employs a gated noise-filtering module to suppress sentiment-irrelevant features and enhance aspect-aware sentiment cues, and a sentiment-relevance interaction module to capture consistent and conflicting cross-modal signals at micro and macro levels. Finally, a learnable decision fusion mechanism adaptively combines predictions from textual, visual, and cross-modal branches at the aspect level. Experiments on public MABSA benchmarks show that GNSRI outperforms state-of-the-art methods, improving accuracy by 1.94\% and 2.06\% on Twitter-2015 and Twitter-2017, respectively.

records.title: VideoFocus: Active Refinement with Hierarchical Memory Reasoning for Long Video Understanding
records.abstract: Understanding long videos requires MLLMs to capture scattered evidence within constrained context windows. Traditional long-text models are easily distracted by irrelevant information and overlook key details. Meanwhile, retrieval-based methods demand substantial computational resources for preprocessing, while fragmented results disrupt temporal coherence. Motivated by human perception, we introduce VideoFocus, an agentic framework that actively and efficiently extracts critical evidence via an iterative Skimming-Memorizing-Refining workflow. We first employ Query-Aware Importance Sampling to segment the video by event peaks and select highly relevant frames through inverse transform sampling. Subsequently, the Dynamic Hierarchical Memory system enables the agent to maintain a comprehensive understanding of the complete event evidence chain. When evidence is insufficient, the agent proactively performs fine-grained resampling on key events to ensure accurate question answering. Empirically, VideoFocus improves accuracy by 3.3% to 5.2% across various VLM base models, while requiring only 38.9% of the execution time of current state-of-the-art methods.

records.title: A Simple and Strong Baseline for One-Frame Attack on Single Object Tracking
records.abstract: Visual object tracking (VOT) is a cornerstone of computer vision applications in multimedia, but deep neural network-based trackers are highly vulnerable to adversarial attacks. Existing attack methods are often ineffective against Transformer-based trackers and typically require perturbations across all video frames, leading to high computational costs and detection risks. In this paper, we propose One-Frame Attack (OFA), a simple yet strong iterative attack that injects adversarial perturbations solely into the first frame of a video sequence. OFA optimizes a suppress-activate loss to disrupt the tracker's attention mechanism or prediction output. Extensive experiments on OTB100, VOT2018, and LaSOT demonstrate that OFA significantly degrades the performance of heterogeneous trackers with minimal attack frequency.

records.title: QG-MOTR: End-to-End Multi-Camera Tracking via Query Graph Construction
records.abstract: Conventional Multi-Camera Multi-Object Tracking (MCMOT) methods generally adhere to a rigid tracking-by-detection paradigm. They rely heavily on external advanced detectors for input and precise camera calibration for spatial alignment. In this paper, we present QG-MOTR, a fully end-to-end, calibration-free framework. Instead of relying on pre-computed detection boxes, we leverage the query-based mechanism of MOTR to jointly perform detection and tracking within single views. Furthermore, we propose a Cross-Camera Association Network (CCAN) to model pairwise query relations across views, constructing a Query Graph which dynamically models the spatial topology of targets across views. This design enables the system to be optimized jointly, enhancing the performance of cross-camera association. Crucially, our approach effectively bypasses the rigid dependency on camera parameters and is robust to varying camera numbers, making it suitable for real-world applications. Experimental results verify that QG-MOTR achieves outstanding performance on cross-camera association while maintaining competitive results on single-view metrics.

records.title: Efficient Spatial-Temporal Focal Adapter with SSM for Temporal Action Detection
records.abstract: Temporal human action detection aims to identify and localize action segments within untrimmed videos, serving as a pivotal task in video understanding. Despite the progress achieved by prior architectures like CNN and Transformer models, these continue to struggle with feature redundancy and degraded global dependency modeling capabilities when applied to long video sequences. These limitations severely constrain their scalability in real-world video analysis. State Space Models (SSMs) offer a promising alternative with linear long-term model- ing and robust global temporal reasoning capabilities. Rethinking the application of SSMs in temporal modeling, this research constructs a novel framework for video human action detection. Specifically, we introduce the Efficient Spatial Temporal Focal (ESTF) Adapter into the pre-trained layers. This module inte- grates the advantages of our proposed Temporal Boundary-aware SSM(TB-SSM) for temporal feature modeling with efficient processing of spatial features. We perform comprehensive and quantitative analyses across multiple benchmarks, comparing our proposed method against previous SSM-based and other structural methods. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our improved strategy significantly enhances both localization performance and robustness, validating the effectiveness of our proposed method.

records.title: JANet: Joint Attention-Based Video Saliency Prediction via a Dual-Branch Network
records.abstract: Human eye movements during free viewing are influenced not only by scene-level visual information, but also by high-level social cues such as gaze, body posture, and language, a phenomenon known as joint attention (JA). However, most existing video saliency models primarily rely on scene-based cues and largely overlook the impact of joint attention on visual attention allocation. To address this limitation, we propose a joint-attention-aware video saliency prediction framework that explicitly models social interaction cues. As a foundation for this study, we first construct JADataset, an eye-tracking benchmark of interactive videos with explicit JA cues collected from 24 participants under free-viewing conditions, to support the study of JA-aware saliency modeling. Building on this benchmark, we propose JANet, a dual-branch network for JA-conditioned video saliency prediction, which fuses scene appearance cues and pose-guided interaction cues through a gated cross-attention module, followed by a spatiotemporal decoder to generate frame-level saliency maps. Extensive quantitative and qualitative evaluations on JADataset demonstrate that JANet consistently outperforms conventional video saliency models, validating that pose-guided joint attention cues effectively complement bottom-up saliency for interactive video understanding.

records.title: OPAL: Offline Preference Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Models
records.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have advanced generalist robotic control. However, current approaches rely heavily on Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) over mixed-quality demonstrations. By indiscriminately treating noisy data as ground truth, these methods yield sub-optimal performance, while existing offline RL methods grapple with reward sparsity and a dependency on privileged state information. To bridge this gap, we propose OPAL (Offline Preference Alignment), a holistic framework that extracts fine-grained control signals directly from static datasets. Our approach integrates a \textit{Contrastive Anchor Strategy} for efficient preference annotation, an \textit{Embodied Preference Transformer} to decouple physical outcomes from action intents, and \textit{Rank-Tangent Reweighting} to non-linearly suppress suboptimal behaviors. Extensive experiments demonstrate that OPAL effectively stabilizes offline fine-tuning, yielding substantial performance improvements on the \textit{LIBERO} benchmark.

records.title: BlurTrack: Taming Dual-Motion Blur in UAV Multi-Object Tracking via Relative Blur Adaptation
records.abstract: UAV multi-object tracking (MOT) is severely affected by dual-motion blur, where camera ego-motion and target motion jointly degrade appearance cues and lower detection confidence, which in turn destabilizes data association and increases identity switches. In contrast to deblurring-oriented approaches that primarily aim to restore blurred frames, we propose BlurTrack, a blur-aware tracking-by-detection framework that explicitly models blur-dependent reliability for robust detection and association. BlurTrack first introduces SRB-Q, a self-supervised module that estimates relative blur from unlabeled videos to provide blur cues for subsequent reliability learning. We then design a Blur Head to predict an association-reliability score, optimized by a blur-aware loss with a dynamic margin to better separate blurred positives from hard negatives. Finally, BlurMatch is integrated into standard two-stage association to perform reliability-guided matching for previously unmatched candidates, improving recall while maintaining identity consistency under heavy blur. Experiments on VisDrone2019-MOT and UAVDT demonstrate consistent gains over the ByteTrack baseline (up to +1.5 MOTA points), achieving 45.3% MOTA and 61.5% IDF1 on VisDrone and 54.3% MOTA and 70.9% IDF1 on UAVDT.

records.title: DOT: Dual-Track Optimal Transport Framework for Item Cold-Start Recommendation
records.abstract: Cold-start recommendation faces a fundamental challenge arising from the Heterogeneity Gap: the topological structures of the semantic manifold (content) and collaborative manifold (interactions) are often divergent. Existing generative methods address cold-start by enforcing point-to-point alignment between content-derived embeddings and interaction embeddings, which can overlook such geometric mismatch and may lead to distorted representations or reduced diversity (mode collapse). To mitigate this issue, we propose DOT, a Dual-track Optimal Transport framework. DOT consists of three key components. (1) A dual-track architecture decouples semantic preservation from collaborative adaptation; a stochastic replacement strategy trains downstream modules on a mixture of real and generated interaction embeddings to reduce the training--inference gap. (2) A distribution-level alignment objective based on Optimal Transport (OT) regularizes the geometry of generated embeddings by encouraging them to cover the support of real interaction embeddings at the batch level. (3) An adaptive gating module dynamically balances collaborative and content-based signals based on feature reliability. Extensive experiments on three public datasets demonstrate that DOT consistently improves cold-start recommendation accuracy over strong baselines. Further ablation and visualization studies verify the effectiveness of our framework in resolving the geometric mismatch and achieving competitive cold-start performance.

records.title: FIS-OT: Feature-Induced Optimal Transport for Unsupervised Action Segmentation
records.abstract: Unsupervised action segmentation is a challenging task. It involves finding action categories and boundaries in videos without labels. Existing Optimal Transport (OT) methods use global constraints. This causes them to overlook the use of local information. Furthermore, existing Optimal transport architectures are prone to confirmation bias because they overly trust the pseudo-labels they generate. This causes models to learn from noise in the early training stages. To address these issues, we propose FIS-OT. It is a novel Feature-Induced Structured Optimal Transport framework. First, we introduce a Feature Enhanced Generator(FEG) module. It serves as an internal regularizer. By using triplet loss, FEG captures local consistency. It provides robust supervision that is independent of noisy pseudo-labels. Second, we propose a Feature-Induced Residual Structural Prior. This combines a fixed temporal backbone with dynamic feature similarities. This design ensures temporal continuity. It also allows the solver to adapt to complex action structures. Finally, we establish a cyclic optimization loop. This aligns local feature learning with global structural alignment. Extensive experiments on the three datasets show the effectiveness of our method.

records.title: Occlusion-aware Learning and Facial Action Units Prior for Facial Expression Recognition
records.abstract: Since the increasing demand for emotional human-computer interaction, facial expression recognition has become a crucial research area in computer vision. However, a computer faces challenges to obtain accurate facial expression information due to the occlusion uncertainty, thus making incorrect judgments. In this paper, we propose a novel facial expression recognition network (dubbed OALNet) with an occlusion aware learning network that can perceive image-level facial occlusion. We also introduce the facial action coding system to provide the action units (AUs) prior knowledge for the extraction of expression-related facial local features. Specifically, the pretrained Occlusion Prediction network accurately perceives the occlusion degree of each image and adaptively adjusts the importance weights between the global and local features, thus focusing on the most discriminative features. The local feature extraction module introduces the expert prior knowledge of AUs to focus on local regions of the face that are strongly correlated with facial expressions. Furthermore, a Cross Query Transformer module is presented for the efficient fusion of global and local features. The proposed OALNet is evaluated on both occlusion and non-occlusion facial datasets. Experiments on these benchmark datasets show that the proposed OALNet achieves state-of-the-art performance. Ablation studies confirm that our Occlusion Aware network, Action Units-guided Local Feature Extraction module, and Cross Query Transformer module are beneficial to improving the performance of facial expression recognition.

records.title: TARNet: A Temporal-Aware Multi-Scale Architecture for Closed-Set Speaker Identification
records.abstract: Closed-set speaker identification aims to assign a speech utterance to one of a predefined set of enrolled speakers and requires robust modeling of speaker-specific characteristics across multiple temporal scales. While recent deep learning approaches have achieved strong performance, many existing architectures provide limited mechanisms for modeling temporal dependencies across different time scales, which can restrict the effective use of complementary short-, mid-, and long-term speaker characteristics. In this paper, we propose TARNet, a lightweight Temporal-Aware Representation Network for closed-set speaker identification. TARNet explicitly models temporal information at multiple time scales using a multi-stage temporal encoder with stage-specific dilation configurations. The resulting multi-scale representations are fused and aggregated via an Attentive Statistics Pooling (ASP) module to produce a discriminative utterance-level speaker embedding. Experiments on the VoxCeleb1 and LibriSpeech datasets show that TARNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods while maintaining competitive computational complexity, making it suitable for practical speaker identification systems. The code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/YassinTERRAF/TARNet}.

records.title: AlignTalk: Aligning Speech with Video Frames for Improved Temporal Grounding in Video LLMs
records.abstract: Video Temporal Grounding (VTG) requires Video Large Language Models (Video-LLMs) to not only recognize events within a video but also to pinpoint their temporal occurrence and generate temporally grounded outputs. However, existing Video-LLMs often struggle to represent and describe temporal information in a consistent way, making it difficult to reliably specify when an event occurs and to ground responses to precise moments in a video. We present AlignTalk, a time-sensitive VideoLLM for fine-grained temporal understanding and grounding. AlignTalk introduces a Time-Prompted Image Q-Former that injects a length-normalized multi-scale temporal prior via soft time tokens derived from time-bucket indices. Additionally, we impose an ASR Adapter Fusion module that leverages automatic speech recognition (ASR) to enhance frame-level speech–vision alignment through lightweight MLP. Experiments on long-video temporal grounding benchmarks show that AlignTalk consistently improves temporally grounded generation and localization over strong baselines.

records.title: Hierarchical Spatio-Temporal Decoupling Alignment for Text-Video Retrieval
records.abstract: A significant challenge in text-video retrieval is the semantic gap between text and video, primarily stemming from the capacity disparity between dense, spatio-temporally coupled signals and sparse natural language. Existing text-video retrieval methods mainly focus on multi-grained alignment to bridge the semantic gap. However, they often overlook the inherent capacity imbalance between video and text feature spaces. To address this issue, we propose Hierarchical Spatio-Temporal Decoupling Alignment (HSTDA), a novel method that balances the information capacity of video and text. Specifically, HSTDA introduces a density-guided token aggregation module to extract hierarchical visual features for temporal decoupling. Subsequently, we utilize a set of learnable queries to capture distinct semantic concepts for spatial decoupling, effectively compressing redundant video information to match the textual capacity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that HSTDA offers a superior trade-off between accuracy and efficiency.

records.title: Automated Spatio-Temporal Mapping of Teacher Movement and Speech from Single-View Classroom Videos
records.abstract: Understanding how teachers move and interact in classroom environments is essential for analyzing instructional strategies and promoting equitable learning experiences. However, existing classroom analysis methods often process spatial and verbal modalities in isolation and typically require extensive manual annotations. To address these challenges, we propose ST-Track, a spatio-temporal mapping framework that automatically extracts teacher trajectories from video and aligns them with classroom speech. First, a single-frame manual annotation initializes single-object tracking and estimates a planar floor homography. Then, tracked teacher positions are projected to a normalized top-down map and temporally smoothed to reduce jitter. Meanwhile, classroom audio is transcribed via automatic speech recognition (ASR) and subsequently aligned to the trajectory by timestamp matching, thereby producing a unified spatio-temporal visualization. In practical classroom scenarios, ST-Track achieves low projection error while requiring minimal supervision, and remains scalable to long durations. Our method bridges visual and audio signals in a unified spatio-temporal space and provides a reproducible solution for multimodal classroom analytics.

records.title: Visually Perceived, Causally Grounded: A Robust Multimodal Framework for Financial Volatility Forecasting
records.abstract: Financial volatility forecasting is pivotal for risk management, yet existing time-series models often rely solely on numerical history, neglecting the rich visual semantics embedded in K-line charts and the causal logic within unstructured data. To bridge this gap, we propose a robust cross-modal framework that integrates visual perception with knowledge-guided reasoning. Our approach innovatively maps price variance to the vertical dispersion of anisotropic heatmaps, explicitly encoding market uncertainty into visual features. Simultaneously, it incorporates a Financial Knowledge Graph to capture non-visual event-driven shocks and utilizes latent adversarial training to learn regime-invariant representations under market stress. Experiments on the S&P 500 and CSI 300 datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms state-of-the-art multimodal and visual baselines in both forecasting accuracy and robustness.

records.title: RCR: Robust Confident Refine Framework for Composed Image Retrieval
records.abstract: Composed Image Retrieval (CIR) aims to retrieve a target image using a query that combines a reference image and a textual description, and this manner benefits users to express their intent more effectively. At present, most CIR methods implicitly assume that the Query-Target pairs (QTp) during training are perfectly aligned. However, in practical scenarios, due to annotation errors in manual labeling, these QTp inevitably suffer from false correlation issues, namely noisy correspondences (NC). To address the influence of NC, we propose a new Robust Confidence Refine (RCR) framework, which divides the data into three subsets and uses adaptive weights to refine the correspondences of samples in different subsets, enabling the model to effectively improve its robustness even under the impact of NC. Specifically, RCR consists of two main components: (1) Robust Consensus Partition (RCP) module, which employs dual neural networks to compute sample association confidences and partitions QTp into clean, vague, and noisy sets via consensus Partition, so that the model can obtain reliable correspondences from RCP for robust learning. (2) Sample-Aware Refine (SAR) function, which employs adaptive weights derived from association confidences to refine sample correspondences within each data partition, and further adjusting the strength of original correspondence to correct QTp mismatches, thereby enhancing the model’s matching accuracy. The experimental results show that the proposed RCR demonstrates an improvement of 1.43%, 1.07% and 2.70% on the CIRR, FashionIQ and LaSCo datasets.
