records.title: Modular Retrieval-Augmented Generalization for Human Action Recognition
records.abstract: Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU)-based Human Activity Recognition (HAR) aims to interpret and classify user behaviors from temporal motion signals. Recently, deep learning frameworks have advanced this task by learning and extracting discriminative spatiotemporal representations, significantly improving recognition performance. However, IMU-based HAR still faces several critical challenges, particularly limited training samples and static knowledge utilization, both of which severely hinder its large-scale deployment. In this paper, we introduce MoRA, the first Retrieval-Augmented Module specifically designed for motion series. It can be flexibly integrated into any existing HAR model, enhancing recognition performance while maintaining inference efficiency. To address issues such as information redundancy in retrieval results and rigid fusion strategies, we propose an uncertainty-adaptive fusion unit within MoRA. This unit leverages previous physical knowledge from IMU signals to dynamically adjust the fusion strategy between original outputs and retrieved information, enabling more robust recognition. Extensive experiments on ten real-world datasets demonstrate that MoRA significantly improves the performance of existing IMU-based HAR models, consistently delivering stable and effective gains. The source code of MoRA is available at: https://github.com/liavonpenn/mora

records.title: KFMRec: A Knowledge-Driven and Frequency-Modulated Framework for Multi-Modal Recommendation
records.abstract: Incorporating multi-modal representations into recommender systems has shown great potential for capturing user preferences. However, existing approaches often neglect the intrinsic temporal, structural, and spectral dependencies underlying user behaviors, resulting in incomplete cross-modal understanding. To address this issue, we propose KFMRec, a unified Kolmogorov–Frequency–Modulated Recommendation Framework that jointly models temporal dynamics, behavior structures, and spectral consistency in a single architecture.KFMRec introduces a Multi-Scale Temporal Hypergraph (MTHG) to construct time-aware hyperedges across multiple granularities, enabling interpretable short-, periodic-, and long-term preference learning. A Behavior-Driven Knowledge Graph (BKG) is then derived from intra- and inter-user co-occurrence patterns, enhancing collaborative representation without external knowledge. Furthermore, a Spectral Denoising Module with KAN Gating leverages frequency-domain transformation and learnable Kolmogorov–Arnold gating to suppress modality-specific noise while amplifying informative signals. Finally, a Dual Alignment Loss combining Graph Contrastive and Mahalanobis Alignment objectives enforces both structural and statistical coherence across modalities.Extensive experiments on three real-world multi-modal datasets demonstrate that KFMRec consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in accuracy, robustness, and interpretability, offering a unified and explainable paradigm for temporal–structural–spectral modeling in multi-modal recommendation.

records.title: Extend Multi-Scale Subgraph Features to Enhance Node Representation for Robust Graph Matching
records.abstract: Graph matching is a fundamental pattern recognition task in multimodal applications, yet it remains challenging due to its NP-hard quadratic assignment nature. While recent graph neural network (GNN) approaches relax this into continuous optimization, their reliance on global node embeddings suffers from feature homogenization, degrading the critical affinity matrix’s discriminative power. We propose MSS, a plug-and-play module that redefines affinity computation through localized subgraph similarity: for each node, we extract its centered subgraph, learn hierarchical structural representations, and construct an affinity matrix from subgraph-level features, preserving discriminability while mitigating over-smoothing. Experiments across complete/partial matching tasks show consistent gains (1.2–2.2% F1 improvement), with universal compatibility for any GNN-based matcher producing doubly stochastic matrices. Our work establishes subgraph-driven affinity as a new paradigm for accurate and scalable graph matching.

records.title: Image-Inspired Scanning and Retrieval for Fast Vulnerability Detection in Long Smart Contracts
records.abstract: Smart contracts often involve excessive context, where sparse vulnerabilities are embedded within extensive benign code. Existing deep learning models, particularly those relying on global semantic encoding, struggle to filter out this context-irrelevant noise. We argue that vulnerability detection essentially involves identifying specific \textit{local} features rather than comprehending the entire global logic. To this end, we propose the \underline{\textbf{C}}ode \underline{\textbf{C}}ompositional \underline{\textbf{R}}es\underline{\textbf{Net}} (CCRNet). CCRNet treats code as a 1-D image, utilizing Code Compositional Encoding and an improved ResNet-based backbone (LSeq-ResNet) to scan for local vulnerability patterns. To train CCRNet for vulnerability representation, we design a vulnerability-aware contrastive learning framework incorporating multi-stage training, specialized loss design, and training data composition. Finally, we build a K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) classifier using CCRNet to validate the embedding quality. Experiments on a large-scale benchmark show that our method outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by 5.85\% in F1-score.

records.title: 3D Model Retrieval via Text-enhanced Multi-modal Feature Alignment
records.abstract: Cross-modality alignment is pivotal for bridging the gap between visual perception and 3D geometric understanding in cross-modal 3D retrieval. In this work, we propose a novel approach for cross-modal 3D shape retrieval by leveraging textual guidance to enhance cross-modal feature alignment. Specifically, we introduce a Cross-Modal Feature Reconstruction (CMFR) module to facilitate fine-grained alignment by reconstructing image features from point features (and vice versa) under semantic guidance from text features. Furthermore, we employ the Hard Negative Noise Contrastive Estimation (HN-NCE) in the contrastive loss to learn more discriminative features and achieve more accurate multimodal alignment for image-shape pairs that are difficult to distinguish. Extensive experiments on the ScanNet dataset show that our method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in instance-level 3D model retrieval, demonstrating that our method effectively integrates complementary cross-modal information and achieves fine-grained cross-modal alignment.

records.title: QRS: Post-Filtering Based Query Augmentation in Cross-Modal Document Retrieval
records.abstract: Cross-modal query augmentation for visually-rich documents faces a fundamental dual bottleneck: unstable rewriting and insufficient modal generalization. Existing Large Language Model (LLM)-base methods, while promising, suffer from high output volatility and are confined primarily to the text modality, severely limiting their reliability in multimodal scenarios. To break through these limitations, we propose the Query Rewrite-Selection (QRS) framework, a novel two-stage approach engineered for robustness. QRS uniquely integrates a Rewriter leveraging Reinforcement Learning(RL) to mitigate local optima, with a pioneering Selector module that acts as a post-filtering mechanism to counter LLM output volatility. Extensive evaluation on challenging cross-modal datasets demonstrates QRS’s superior performance, achieving a significant 2.2% absolute improvement in NDCG@5. Critically, QRS represents the first system to demonstrate the stable and effective application of query augmentation in cross-modal retrieval, establishing a new state-of-the-art. Our code will be made available upon acceptance.

records.title: Uncertainty-aware Mixture-of-Expert Structure and Hierarchical Fusion for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
records.abstract: Multimodal sentiment analysis aims to understand human sentiment by fusing various modalities like speech, vision, and text. However, the reliability of each modality can vary across different samples. For example, one video might have clear audio but blurry visuals, while another might have clear text but noisy audio. This sample-level uncertainty poses significant challenges to both feature processing and multimodal fusion. To address these challenges, we propose the Uncertainty-driven Mixture-of-Expert and Fusion Network (UMFNet), a framework that quantifies and leverages this uncertainty. Specifically, for feature processing, we introduce the Uncertainty-aware Mixture-of-Expert Module (UMM), which dynamically allocates the number of experts based on the modality's uncertainty. In terms of multimodal fusion, we propose the Uncertainty-guided Hierarchical Fusion Module (UHFM), which allows more reliable modalities to guide the integration of less reliable ones. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UMFNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods across various evaluation metrics.

records.title: MGTS: Personalized Message Generation and Counterfactual Target Selection for Efficient Multi-Agent Coordination
records.abstract: Effective communication is essential for efficient coordination in cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning. However, broadcasting undifferentiated messages to all teammates often leads to information overload, which in turn complicates decision-making and undermines collaborative efficiency. While prior work commonly adopts gating or attention mechanisms to highlight salient information, these approaches generally lack a quantitative value assessment of the messages transmitted to specific agents. Consequently, they may still suffer from inefficient information exchange and miscoordination in complex environments. To address these limitations, we introduce a framework for Personalized Message Generation and Counterfactual Target Selection (MGTS). Specifically, MGTS estimates communication weights using counterfactual message values and produces agent-specific messages, thereby filtering redundant information and promoting more effective inter-agent coordination. We evaluate MGTS on the Level-Based Foraging environment and the StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge benchmark. Our empirical results demonstrate that MGTS learns sophisticated coordination strategies and outperforms a range of mainstream methods overall.

records.title: LocYQuery: Language-Driven Positioning in Global Indoor Point Cloud Maps
records.abstract: Language-driven localization in large-scale indoor point cloud maps remains an extremely challenging yet critical capability. Existing indoor localization works focus solely on local object referencing tasks, while outdoor methods are limited to scenarios with sparse object distributions, failing to address the unique challenges of indoor global localization where dense and diverse irrelevant objects introduce significant noise. To bridge this gap, we formalize the indoor global localization task and construct the ScanNetPPMap dataset, the first benchmark aligning global indoor point cloud maps with natural language descriptions based on the ScanNet++ dataset. We further propose LocYQuery, a three-stage framework specifically designed for language-driven localization in global indoor maps. Our method first performs submap retrieval, then employs an Object-clue contrastive Filtering Network to semantically pre-filter irrelevant objects, and finally predicts precise coordinates in the refined submap. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LocYQuery statistically significantly outperforms existing methods in recall and robustness.

records.title: LS-CLIP: Autoencoder-Based Mining of CLIP's Local Semantics in Cross-Domain Image Retrieval
records.abstract: Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP) excels in image retrieval but struggles with local-semantic understanding, which further exacerbates the domain gap in cross-domain image retrieval (CDIR). Existing methods often depend on extensive manual annotations for local supervision and ignore CLIP's native local-semantic capabilities. We reveal CLIP patch features inherently embody cross-domain stable local semantic anchors, mitigating CDIR’s core misalignment. We propose a plug-and-play Local Semantics CLIP (LS-CLIP). First, a self-supervised Semantic Reconstruction Module (SRM) is designed to purify local semantic anchors from patch features by separating noise via compression-reconstruction, enabling multi-granularity retrieval adaptation. Second, Feature Moment Transfer (FMT) is introduced to align the statistical distribution of cross-domain features, eliminating domain-specific statistical shifts and enhancing feature space stability. We construct the CDIR-Flickr30k dataset to validate the universality of local semantic enhancement for cross-domain alignment. Experiments show that LS-CLIP achieves SOTA with strong generalizability and works for CLIP variants to consistently improve performance.

records.title: Matching Before Fusion: Learning Multimodal Relation Extraction with Noisy Correspondences
records.abstract: Multimodal Relation Extraction (MRE) aims to extract relationships between entity pairs by leveraging both textual and visual cues, which is essential for applications including open-source intelligence analysis, social media understanding, and the construction of multimodal knowledge graphs. Real-world MRE corpora constructed from web-scraped or automatically annotated posts, however, often contain noisy sentence–image correspondences, where images are only weakly related or even irrelevant to the underlying textual relations, and existing methods rarely address this issue explicitly. This paper presents MBF (Matching Before Fusion), a framework that estimates and exploits relation-level correspondence confidence prior to multimodal fusion. MBF first derives per-sample matching losses from a warm-up sentence-image matching model and fits a two-component Beta mixture model to distinguish clean from noisy instances, yielding relation-level confidence scores. These scores then guide a correspondence-aware fusion module that down-weights unreliable visual evidence and a multi-granularity learning module that performs sentence–image contrastive matching and entity–object supervised contrastive learning. Experiments on the MNRE dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of MBF, which achieves an improvement of 3.04% in F1 score compared to existing baselines.

records.title: ViRe-Agent: Multi-Modal Composed Retrieval with Dynamic Scene Segmentation for Cross-Duration Video
records.abstract: Existing multimodal video retrieval systems are limited by weak intent understanding and rigid similarity-based matching, especially when handling composed queries that integrate heterogeneous inputs (e.g., text + image or text + video). Current agent-based video systems focus primarily on long-video reasoning and question answering, but do not address dynamic retrieval strategy selection across multiple modalities. To fill this gap, we propose ViRe-Agent, a retrieval agent that formulates multimodal search as a policy-driven decision process. The core contribution lies in a Light MDP routing mechanism, which selects an optimal retrieval policy (semantic, similarity, composed, or fingerprint-based) conditioned on both query intent and segment-level video semantics. This formulation enables learnable policy selection rather than heuristic matching. We further integrate scene segmentation and multi-modal fingerprinting to support cross-duration queries and provenance tracing. Extensive experiments across five retrieval settings (text→video, image→video, video→video, text+image→video, and text+video→video) demonstrate consistent improvements over recent baselines including CoVR, TransVCL, and CLIP4Clip, with gains up to 4.6% R@1 on real-world data. Our code will publicly available at https://vire-agent.vercel.app/.

records.title: Probabilistic Prototype Networks and Contrastive Learning for Unsupervised Cross-Modal Hashing
records.abstract: Unsupervised cross-modal hashing has become a research hotspot due to its high search efficiency and independence of labels. Existing unsupervised methods typically employ pairwise associations or feature similarity to guide hash function learning, which overlooks data's multi-label semantics and struggles to model higher-order one-to-many similarity relationships. To address this limitation, we propose a Probabilistic Prototype Network and Contrastive Learning for Unsupervised Cross-modal Hashing (PPN-UCH) method. Firstly, we use CLIP encoders to extract features from training samples, maximizing pairwise similarity through contrastive learning. Secondly, we design a GMM-based probabilistic prototype network that parses multi-label category attributes of cross-modal instances through probabilistic clustering, thereby generating the high-order similarity matrix and clustering prototypes. Finally, the cross-modal hashing optimization module is designed based on pseudo-labels and prototypes, enhancing the multi-label semantic and discriminative capabilities of the hash codes. Extensive experiments on two benchmark datasets demonstrate that our PPN-UCH outperforms state-of-the-art unsupervised methods.

records.title: IntNDI: Interpretable Neurological Disorder Identification via Multi-Domain Feature Fusion and Information Subgraph Awareness
records.abstract: EEG-based connectomes provide a noninvasive and cost-effective modality for neurological disorder identification, particularly for characterizing the complex patterns and connectivity of the brain. However, existing methods predominantly focus on global connectivity structures in a single domain, which inadequately address the interpretation of more intricate relational structures. In this study, we present a novel approach, i.e., Interpretable Neurological Disorder Identification (IntNDI) via Multi-Domain Feature Fusion and Information Subgraph Awareness to address these limitations. Specifically, we develop a multi-domain feature fusion strategy based on an iterative cross-attention mechanism to capture complementary temporal and frequency representations effectively. Building on this, we introduce an information-aware subgraph learning module that leverages an information-bottleneck theory and distillation regularization to extract compact, disorder-relevant subgraphs that highlight abnormal brain regions and connectivity patterns. Extensive experimental validation across three real-world datasets demonstrates that IntNDI outperforms state-of-the-art methods while providing more interpretable insights into underlying neurological abnormalities.

records.title: Learning Gamut-Aware Decomposition for Gain Map-Based Inverse Tone Mapping
records.abstract: The introduction of the gain map (GM) significantly improves high dynamic range (HDR) display compatibility, and inspires GM-based inverse tone mapping (ITM) methods that show superior performance. However, the inherent nature of GM restricts existing GM-based ITM methods to luminance recovery, hindering their ability to extend the color gamut. To address this limitation, we propose a gamut-aware decomposition strategy, which introduces the rectified GM (RGM) and the augmented quotient map (AQM), effectively decoupling luminance restoration and color conversion. To implement our strategy, we design a dual-branch network that incorporates global prior-guided attention and context-aware feature transform modules, collaboratively estimating the decomposed components by integrating global guidance with refined features. To facilitate further research along this line, we build a new dataset consisting of 2,000 high-quality data pairs. Both qualitative and quantitative results demonstrate that our method achieves leading performance.

records.title: SimInsert: Seamless Video Object Insertion via Regional Sparse Attention Fusion
records.abstract: Video object insertion requires ensuring spatio-temporal coherence and interactive realism, extending far beyond simple content placement. However, current approaches are often hindered by a reliance on explicit motion engineering or resource-intensive retraining, restricting their flexibility and generalization. To bridge this gap, we present \textit{SimInsert}, a training-free paradigm that efficiently decouples the task into intuitive single-frame editing and semantic motion description. By harnessing the robust generative priors of image-to-video diffusion models, SimInsert propagates edits temporally, strictly preserving background invariance while enabling plausible, text-driven interactions between the inserted object and the dynamic environment. Our approach hinges on non-invasive guidance mechanisms that enforce structural consistency, facilitate seamless boundary fusion, and counteract the fidelity drift that typically accumulates during the denoising trajectory. Extensive quantitative experiments validate our efficacy: SimInsert surpasses state-of-the-art methods with an 18.8\% gain in PSNR, 20.1\% in SSIM, and a 44.1\% decrease in LPIPS, offering a streamlined solution for high-fidelity video editing.

records.title: DCGLLM: LLM-Guided Dynamic Comorbidity Graph Learning for Personalized Risk Prediction
records.abstract: Predicting comorbidity progression is essential for personalized medicine, enabling tailored interventions and early risk prediction from electronic health records (EHR). However, most existing methods rely on static binary knowledge graphs, failing to capture the complex disease associations and their temporal evolution. To address this, we propose DCGLLM, a dynamic comorbidity graph learning framework guided by large language models (LLMs). DCGLLM first leverages a medical LLM to quantify evolving disease associations and constructs dynamic graphs that capture temporal variations across patient visits. Building on this, DCGLLM employs a spatio-temporal dynamic graph network that integrates LLM-guided knowledge priors with data-driven clinical observations. In this network, a dual-driven spatial attention layer captures spatial correlations between diseases within patient visits, while a temporal evolution layer models trajectory progression, reflecting dynamic disease associations over time. Finally, we design a cross-modal fusion module that combines these representations with patient visit sequence representations learned by an EHR encoder. Experiments on hypertension-to-diabetes prediction demonstrate the superiority of DCGLLM, surpassing the state-of-the-art AUPRC scores on MIMIC-III by 4.54% and on MIMIC-IV by 6.52%, highlighting its robustness against severe class imbalance and data sparsity.

records.title: Accident-Induced Traffic Congestion Prediction Based on Multi-Source Data
records.abstract: Urban expressways are critical for urban mobility, yet their efficiency is frequently disrupted by accident-induced congestion—a non-recurrent, event-driven phenomenon that con- ventional forecasting approaches struggle to capture. Analysis of large-scale user-generated content from Amap reveals that only 6.8% of traffic accidents on Shenzhen’s urban expressways lead to congestion, posing a severely imbalanced prediction challenge. We formulate this as a binary, event-level classification task and identify road structural complexity as a key yet underexplored predictive factor, annotating real-world expressway segments using a dedicated OpenStreetMap-based tool. To integrate het- erogeneous inputs—including spatial, temporal, road structural complexity, and meteorological features—we propose TACP-Net, a multi-branch deep learning framework featuring attention- based feature interaction and adaptive gated fusion. Focal Loss is adopted to address the long-tailed data distribution without oversampling. Experiments on real-world Shenzhen expressway data demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, validating both the predictive value of road structural complexity and the robustness of the multi-source fusion architecture for intelligent traffic incident response.

records.title: SPCA: Semantic Signal Preservation and Focus Alignment for Multimodal Recommendation
records.abstract: The multimodal recommendation has gained increasing attention due to its ability to effectively integrate various modal information. However, such approaches face two limitations: i) Semantic signal modeling in graph learning becomes distorted due to its excessive association with item popularity; ii) Inconsistent semantic focus across modalities to describe the same item will interfere with the representation modeling. To address such issues, we propose a novel Semantic Signal Preservation and Focus Alignment (SPCA) learning framework. Specifically, SPCA initially unifies multimodal semantic information into textual content. It then constructs local consensus networks among items in the semantic signal preservation module to resist erosion of popularity bias. Furthermore, SPCA incorporates the principal component alignment module to achieve cross-modal semantic focus alignment and single-modal principal component enhancement, based on feature correlation matrix decomposition and singular value truncation. Our empirical analysis conducted on three real-world datasets shows that SPCA significantly exceeds the performance of state-of-the-art baselines.

records.title: From Errors to Insights: Bi-Level Modeling of Programming Learning Dynamics
records.abstract: In traditional knowledge tracing (KT), a student’s repeated incorrect attempts on the same question are typically interpreted either as independent events or as evidence of stalled learning. However, in programming knowledge tracing (PKT), the interactive, iterative, and feedback-driven nature of coding tasks means that repeated attempts often signal active question solving and incremental progress. To examine how modeling this nuanced process influences PKT performance, we propose a bi-level programming knowledge tracing model (BIPKT) that jointly tracks students’ global conceptual understanding and their local, question-level learning. Our model further incorporates programming-specific feedback from compilers and automated testing systems at both levels. Experiments on real-world programming logs from major online coding platforms show that BIPKT more accurately captures fine-grained learning dynamics than (i) KT baselines that treat programming like non-interactive tasks and (ii) PKT baselines that overlook the detailed structure of repeated attempts on the same question. Both the implementation of the BIPKT model and the programming dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/iecc-lab/BIPKT.

records.title: Robust Registration via Structural Discrepancy and Pivot-Guided Matching
records.abstract: Point cloud registration under low overlap and heavy clutter remains challenging due to ambiguous correspondences and weak geometric constraints. We propose an overlap-aware two-stage framework built upon a Local-Global Geometry-Aware Transformer (LGT). Unlike existing geometry-aware Transformers that primarily focus on intra-cloud consistency, LGT injects dynamic metric-aware biases into self-attention to preserve spatial consistency and introduces a structure discrepancy bias in cross-attention to suppress non-overlapping regions. We further design a Two-Stage Spatial Consistency Matching strategy. At the sparse stage, a pivot-based second-order dual consistency formulation enables robust superpoint matching. At the dense stage, a superpoint-guided graph Transformer refines point-level correspondences by enforcing global spatial coherence. Experiments on KITTI, nuScenes, ModelNet40, and 3DMatch demonstrate state-of-the-art performance. Notably, on 3DLoMatch (overlap below 30 percent), our method improves recall from 80.4 to 83.2 percent, yielding a 2.8 point gain over the previous best approach.

records.title: Sample-Importance Gated Uncertainty Suppression for Facial Expression Recognition
records.abstract: In-the-wild facial expression data are often corrupted by ambiguous expressions, compression artifacts, and inconsistent annotations, which hinder reliable training. Label distribution learning can enrich supervision through dynamic fusion, yet its initial estimates are easily polluted by mislabeled samples and existing schemes rarely weigh sample credibility. We propose SIA-Net (Sample Importance-Aware Net) that injects sample importance into every stage to suppress uncertainty. A self-attention block assigns an importance weight to each image. A rank-regularization loss keeps a measurable margin between high- and low-confidence groups. A relabeling module corrects suspicious labels before each update. The importance scores act as gates that instantly balance sample-specific and class-level distributions. SIA-Net achieves 91.33\%, 66.26\% and 61.02\% accuracy on RAF-DB, AffectNet and SFEW, respectively, confirming its ability to reduce uncertainty and stabilize early training.

records.title: EviCal: Numerical-Driven Evidence Retrieval for Interpretable Calibration in Multimodal Forecasting
records.abstract: Multimodal time series forecasting leverages text to handle regime shifts invisible to numerical history. However, existing text-conditioned fusion often employs indiscriminate feature injection, which risks amplifying noise and disrupting temporal dynamics when semantics are misaligned. To address this, we propose EviCal, a numerical-driven framework that unifies active evidence retrieval and logic-based calibration. It utilizes internal numerical states to actively query external semantic evidence, integrating retrieved evidence via the bounded contextual modulator acting as a cognitive safety valve. Instead of passive fusion, EviCal employs explicit amplitude constraints to adaptively silence uninformative text while selectively amplifying regime-relevant evidence, thereby preserving the stability of the numerical backbone. This design inherently exposes interpretable attention signals. On the Time-MMD benchmark, our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in 23/35 settings, reducing MSE by approximately 15% over unimodal backbones. Mechanistic analyses further validate the model's ability to align temporal-semantic features and suppress misleading text through gate collapse.

records.title: Tigr100k: A Benchmark for Graded Relevance and Fine-Grained Text-to-Image Retrieval in Compositional Queries
records.abstract: Despite the remarkable success of CLIP models in text-to-image retrieval, their performance remains suboptimal when confronted with complex queries encompassing multiple subjects, attributes, or relations. Existing benchmarks and prevailing metrics, like R@k, are fundamentally insufficient, as they treat relevance as a binary state and fail to capture the nuanced ranking quality required for complex search results. To address this critical evaluative gap, we introduce Tigr100k, a novel and robust benchmark dataset specifically designed for rigorous complex query evaluation. Tigr100k surpasses existing resources by comprising 1,044 bilingual complex query pairs and images annotated with fine-grained, multi-level relevance grading (highly, moderately, and irrelevant). Crucially, we couple Tigr100k with hierarchical evaluation metrics that enable a comprehensive assessment of both result coverage and ranking quality. To validate the superior discrimination power of this benchmark, we propose CsdCLIP, an efficient, training-free, and plug-and-play framework. By decomposing complex queries into multiple logical sub-queries for compositional retrieval, CsdCLIP establishes a strong zero-shot baseline. Extensive experiments across multiple CLIP variants using CsdCLIP not only demonstrate significant performance gains, but also confirm the critical value of Tigr100k and its metrics in discerning and accurately measuring true compositional capabilities. Our code and dataset are available at https://github.com/Syqinx/Tigr100k.

records.title: FedMatrioska: All-in-One Self-Adaptation Personalized Federated Learning via Neural Architecture Search
records.abstract: Personalized Federated Learning (PFL) addresses non-IID heterogeneity in federated settings. Recent NAS-based PFL methods automate per-client architectures, yet most still enforce a rigid shared/personalized partition and are largely confined to CNN-centric search spaces. Moreover, personalized parameters are typically optimized only on local data, which can hinder generalization and convergence. For Vision Transformers (ViTs), performance may even fall behind non-personalized baselines. We propose \textbf{FedMatrioska}, a NAS-based PFL framework tailored for ViTs. Instead of pre-defining a shared/personal split, FedMatrioska adopts a hierarchical nested sampling space that learns layer-wise partitioning on the fly, enabling each client to benefit from both global and local knowledge without manual delineation. FedMatrioska further introduces client-adaptive search-space pruning to progressively restrict feasible architectures, reducing memory usage and search cost. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FedMatrioska consistently outperforms baselines and generalizes well to unseen clients for practical deployment under heterogeneous constraints.

records.title: VoidFormer: Mitigating Attention Distortion for Multimodal Learning Under Missing Modality
records.abstract: Deploying pretrained multimodal models in scenarios with missing modalities often leads to significant performance degradation caused by attention distortion. To address this, we propose VoidFormer, a novel parameter-efficient framework designed to enhance robustness against incomplete data. VoidFormer introduces two lightweight modules: a Global Attention Calibrator for holistic concept understanding and a Local Detail Compensator for fine-grained modeling. By employing a novel alignment loss, these components collaboratively rectify attention distributions to align with complete-modality scenarios. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our framework significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods across diverse modalities and backbone architectures, effectively maintaining high performance even under severe missing rates.

records.title: Knowledge-Refined Dual Context-Aware Network for Partially Relevant Video Retrieval
records.abstract: Retrieving partially relevant segments from untrimmed videos remains difficult due to two persistent challenges: the mismatch in information density between text and video segments, and limited attention mechanisms that overlook semantic focus and event correlations. We present KDC-Net, a Knowledge-Refined Dual Context-Aware Network that tackles these issues from both textual and visual perspectives. On the text side, a Hierarchical Semantic Aggregation module captures and adaptively fuses multi-scale phrase cues to enrich query semantics. On the video side, a Dynamic Temporal Attention mechanism employs relative positional encoding and adaptive temporal windows to highlight key events with local temporal coherence. Additionally, a dynamic CLIP-based distillation strategy, enhanced with temporal-continuity-aware refinement, ensures segment-aware and objective-aligned knowledge transfer. Experiments on PRVR benchmarks show that KDC-Net consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, especially under low moment-to-video ratios.

records.title: Visual Set Program Synthesizer
records.abstract: A user pointing their phone at a supermarket shelf and asking “Which soda has the least sugar?” poses a difficult challenge for current visual AI assistants. Such queries require not only object recognition, but explicit set-based reasoning such as filtering, comparison, and aggregation. Standard end-to-end MLLMs often fail at these tasks because they lack an explicit mechanism for compositional logic. We propose treating visual reasoning as Visual Program Synthesis, where the model first generates a symbolic program that is executed by a separate engine grounded in visual scenes. We also introduce Set-VQA, a new benchmark designed specifically for evaluating set-based visual reasoning. Experiments show that our approach significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on complex reasoning tasks, producing more systematic and transparent behavior while substantially improving answer accuracy. These results demonstrate that program-driven reasoning provides a principled alternative to black-box visual-language inference.

records.title: KD-Hash: CLIP-Distillation Guided Feature Calibration for Long-Tailed Image Hashing
records.abstract: Visual-Language Models (VLMs) like CLIP have advanced hashing-based image retrieval via knowledge distillation. However, we observe that existing distillation methods yield marginal gains under imbalanced long-tailed distributions. Our analysis identifies the primary bottleneck as representation entanglement between head and tail classes, which compromises hash code discriminability. To address this, we propose KD-Hash, a generic Knowledge Distillation Hashing framework for long-tailed scenarios. KD-Hash introduces a Feature Reweighting Post Operation (FRPO) that recalibrates learned features using adaptive scaling factors derived from their relationship with the CLIP space, thereby aligning skewed distributions with the generalizable CLIP manifold. Additionally, a Geometric Structure Consistency (GSC) loss minimizes the Gromov-Wasserstein distance between hash and CLIP feature spaces, preserving intrinsic relational structures and transferring underlying semantic knowledge. As a plug-and-play framework, KD-Hash can be seamlessly integrated into existing hashing methods. Extensive experiments demonstrate that KD-Hash achieves significant and consistent performance gains across both majority and minority classes.

records.title: Bridging Semantic Gaps: A Framework for Heterogeneous Graph Learning with Missing Edges
records.abstract: Heterogeneous graphs, by integrating diverse node types and semantic edge relations, have recently attracted significant academic attention. However, real-world graph data often suffer from missing edges, which undermines structural integrity and compromises the reliability of downstream reasoning tasks. Existing methods commonly rely on multi-view learning or teacher-student distillation to handle edge incompleteness, but they generally face three fundamental limitations : (i) insufficient cross-view knowledge transfer; (ii) sensitivity to the input view order; and (iii) poor dynamic task adaptability. To address these issues, we propose a novel framework, which integrates hierarchical 3D graph convolutional network with dual-end teacher-student strategy. Our framework employs order-invariant multi-view modeling to robustly capture multi-source semantics, eliminating the dependency, and establishes a bidirectional cross-view knowledge transfer mechanism to effectively bridge semantic gaps caused by missing information. Extensive experiments on four benchmarks demonstrate that our proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in both effectiveness and robustness.

records.title: From Explanation to Retrieval: Robust Adaptation of Large Multimodal Models for Multimodal Sarcasm Detection
records.abstract: Multimodal sarcasm detection (MMSD) targets sarcasm in text-image pairs and remains a key challenge in multimodal domains. Although large multimodal models (LMMs) exhibit strong generalization in MMSD, they often struggle with subtly expressed sarcasm, where intent is implicit and not overtly signaled. Such failures arise from (1) limited contextual grounding and (2) weak intent modeling, which lead models to rely on superficial correlations while overlooking subtle pragmatic cues. To this end, we propose LMM-TCF, a two-stage fine-tuning framework comprising Explanation-Augmented Fine-tuning and Retrieval-Augmented Fine-tuning. In Stage 1, the model learns to imitate teacher-provided explanations that highlight sarcasm-relevant cues grounded in cross-modal context. An explanation consistency loss encourages discriminative explanations by guiding a lightweight discriminator to recover labels from generated content. In stage 2, we introduce recency-aware retrieval contrastive learning, which retrieves semantically similar but label-different samples to form contrastive pairs. By incorporating temporal recency into the sampling process, the model learns to focus on semantically similar samples from evolving contexts, helping it track subtle intent shifts and reduce reliance on superficial correlations. Extensive experiments indicate that LMM-TCF achieves competitive in-domain results and strong out-of-domain generalization.

records.title: HiSA: Hierarchical Semantic Abstraction for Fine-Grained Text-Based Person Re-identification
records.abstract: Text-based Person Re-identification (TPReID) aims to retrieve pedestrian images from large-scale galleries using natural language descriptions. While existing methods have advanced cross-modal retrieval, two critical limitations remain: (1) textual descriptions are often coarse-grained and neglect the hierarchical structure of attributes, limiting the capture of fine-grained visual and text details; (2) textual descriptions generated by Vision--Language Models (VLMs) often contain semantically vacuous words (e.g., “with”, “the”) that lack visual grounding, which can lead to semantic drift in joint embedding spaces. To address these issues, we propose a Hierarchical Semantic Abstraction (HiSA) framework with two key components. The Masked Hierarchical Attribute Prediction (MHAP) module leverages VLMs guided attribute masking to construct structured semantic representations, increasing information density and alleviating semantic drift. Hierarchical Semantic Contrastive Loss (HSCL) enforces multi-scale attribute-image-text correlations in a unified space, boosting intra-class cohesion and inter-class distinction to mitigate semantic drift. Extensive experiments on CUHK-PEDES, ICFG-PEDES, and RSTPReid benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, achieving Rank-1 accuracy improvements of 1.09%, 1.77%, and 2.07% respectively.

records.title: Not All Samples Are Created Equal: MMI-Aware Valuation and Differentiated Augmentation for Image-Text Retrieval
records.abstract: Image--text retrieval (ITR) is a fundamental task in vision--language understanding, enabling cross-modal search by learning aligned representations between images and texts. In practice, most ITR systems rely on contrastive learning, which assumes equal contributions from all training samples, while overlooking the inherent heterogeneity in semantic consistency, ambiguity, and alignment difficulty across multimodal data. To address this limitation, we propose MiVDO, an information-theoretic framework for Multimodal Mutual Information (MMI)-based Valuation, Differentiated augmentation, and Optimization. MiVDO evaluates each sample’s training value by jointly modeling MMI and InfoNCE loss, forming a two-dimensional signal space that characterizes four distinct sample types and enables precision-targeted, differentiated augmentation driven by Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). Furthermore, we introduce an MMI-aware contrastive objective that adaptively prioritizes low-MMI, high-loss samples, which we identify as the most informative region for refining cross-modal alignment. By unifying valuation, augmentation, and optimization into a single framework, MiVDO achieves more effective and data-efficient representation learning. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate that MiVDO consistently outperforms existing contrastive learning frameworks. The code and datasets are provided in the supplements.

records.title: ANN-SNN Conversion with Unevenness Error Suppression by Triple Phase Inference
records.abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) are considered as energy-efficient and biologically plausible networks due to their emulation of spiking mechanism of neurons. One of effective way to obtain high-performance SNN is conversion from ANN. However, the conversion loss is evitable, which is severe under ultra low time-steps. In our work, we adopt a two-stage conversion framework employing search-finetuning strategy to obtain the tailored ANN, which ensuring the model adaptive to quantized-value domain without training from scratch. By establishing the occurrence model of unevenness error and analyzing the occurrence of conversion errors, we propose two metrics, ratio of information (RI) and information completeness (IC) to measure the state of neuron during inference. Based on them, we propose the triple-phase inference to preventing these errors. The experimental results show that the conversion method achieves state-of-the-art performance on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet datasets at ultra low time-steps.

records.title: MaskRecipe: Learning Context-Aware Masking for Cross-Modal Recipe Retrieval
records.abstract: Cross-modal recipe retrieval is challenged by the representational asymmetry between verbose procedural texts and visually rich food images. This issue persists even in recent approaches leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs), where generated descriptions may introduce redundant noise and hinder fine-grained alignment. To address this problem, we propose MaskRecipe, a framework that adapts the Masked Language Modeling (MLM) paradigm for discriminative cross-modal alignment. MaskRecipe introduces two key components. First, a Dual Masking Mechanism (DMM) combines length-adaptive masking for recipes with semantic-guided masking for LLM-generated descriptions, encouraging masked tokens to query relevant visual cues. Second, a Dynamic Difficulty Loss (DDL) jointly models MLM reconstruction difficulty and cross-modal similarity disagreement to emphasize challenging training samples. Extensive experiments on the Recipe1M dataset demonstrate that MaskRecipe achieves state-of-the-art performance, validating its effectiveness for fine-grained recipe–image retrieval.

records.title: Bridging Information Asymmetry: Canonical Domain Guided Multi-modal Multi-platform Person Re-Identification
records.abstract: Multi-modal Multi-platform Person Re-Identification (MP-ReID) addresses the dual heterogeneity of modalities and platforms but suffers from severe information asymmetry across domains. Specifically, the high-fidelity canonical domain, Ground-RGB, provides significantly richer visual details than constrained domains that undergo spectrum- or platform-induced degradation, such as UAV-Thermal. To bridge this gap, we propose CDG-ReID, a framework that leverages the canonical domain to guide the calibration and alignment of constrained domain representations. We construct an Asymmetric Adaptation Unified Backbone (AAUB) with a differentiated routing strategy: it preserves generic knowledge for canonical domain inputs via a pass-through path while adaptively calibrating constrained domain features using parallel adapters. Furthermore, we introduce a Dual-Anchor Canonical Domain Guidance mechanism, enforcing alignment with both the noise-free Canonical Semantic Anchor (CSA) and the teacher-derived Canonical Visual Anchor (CVA). Experiments demonstrate that CDG-ReID effectively unifies heterogeneous features and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

records.title: CMFENet: A Cognition-driven Network for Missing Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
records.abstract: In recent years, Multimodal Sentiment Analysis (MSA) has become a research hotspot in artiffcial intelligence due to its wide applications in intelligent interaction scenarios. However, existing methods still face practically difﬁcult in balancing modality-speciffc representation and cross-modal collaborative modeling, particularly under missing modality conditions where the model’s discriminative capacity and generalization ability are often severely compromised. To advance multimodal sentiment analysis under random modality features missing, we propose CMFENet, a cognition-driven multi-stage feature enhancement network. The key insight of CMFENet is to reconstruct and derive multimodal sentiment representations by simulating the staged cognitive processing of human emotions, which leverages prior "memories'' from complete modalities to calibrate incomplete modalities. On this basis, we develop a lightweight three-stage sentiment analysis architecture to mitigate modal conflicts and suppress modality bias for accurate sentiment analysis. Furthermore, to mitigate performance degradation caused by random modality features missing, we incorporate cross-view reconstruction and consistency constraints to bolster the stability of sentiment cognition. Experiments demonstrate that CMFENet consistently excels in performance, efficiency, and interpretability.

records.title: DualMatch: Exploiting Dual-Confidence for Semi-Supervised Speaker Diarization
records.abstract: Semi-supervised learning (SSL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for speaker diarization by exploiting unlabeled audio to reduce annotation costs. However, existing SSL methods typically rely on a single high-confidence threshold to filter pseudo-labels, which neglects informative cues embedded in low-confidence non-speech segments and increases the risk of propagating noisy labels. To address these limitations, we propose DualMatch, an SSL framework that leverages both high-confidence and low-confidence predictions to balance pseudo-label quantity and quality. At its core, a dual-difference dynamic weighting mechanism assesses pseudo-label reliability by modeling both temporal consistency and bidirectional confidence variation. Furthermore, a unified training paradigm that integrates SSL and contrastive learning enhances discriminative representations between speech and non-speech embeddings. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DualMatch achieves an average performance improvement of 14.14% over state-of-the-art (SOTA) SSL methods in diarization error rate (DER) and approaches the performance of fully supervised learning.

records.title: Multimodal Generative Recommendation with Hypercomplex Tokens
records.abstract: Generative recommendation reformulates the recommendation task as a sequence-to-sequence generation problem, where generative models predict items by autoregressively generating discrete codes. These codes are typically obtained by quantizing item embeddings into compact representations. However, we identify two critical challenges in existing methods: 1) Current quantization methods typically compress all features into a single-component vector space, where different modality attributes tend to interfere with each other; 2) The autoregressive generation process operates solely on discrete token sequences, lacking explicit semantic guidance from continuous multimodal features. To address these issues, we propose HyperGR, a novel framework that seamlessly integrates hypercomplex representation learning with multimodal generative recommendation. Specifically, HyperGR consists of two key modules: a Hypercomplex-VAE, which encodes multimodal item features into structured, multi-component hypercomplex codes; and a generative recommender, which predicts target item codes under the guidance of continuous multimodal preferences. Extensive experiments on three datasets demonstrate that HyperGR consistently outperforms both traditional and state-of-the-art methods. The implementation code is publicly available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/HyperGR-6B40.

records.title: Diffusing with Clarity: Hierarchical Disentanglement for Multimodal Recommendation
records.abstract: Achieving clarity in representation is essential for effective multimodal recommendation, where user preferences must be extracted from the complex interactions between visual, textual, and auditory signals. Existing diffusion-based models fail to explicitly separate modality-invariant user intent from modality-specific content, which results in semantic confusion and instability in the generated representations. To address these challenges, we propose HDDA-Diff, a novel framework that leverages Hierarchical Disentangled Diffusion to ensure stable and semantically consistent multimodal recommendations. HDDA-Diff incorporates two key components: the Hierarchical Disentangled Representation (HDR) module, which structures semantic information into a shared common space and distinct modality-specific subspaces, and the Dynamic Semantic Alignment (DAS) mechanism, which continuously aligns these spaces throughout the diffusion process. This approach guarantees that the generated representations remain both stable and semantically consistent across modalities. Extensive experiments on three real-world datasets demonstrate that HDDA-Diff outperforms state-of-the-art methods in recommendation accuracy, highlighting that clear semantic disentanglement is crucial for robust multimodal recommendation systems.

records.title: RKRG: Retrieval-Free Medical Report Generation via Graph-Conditioned Knowledge Distillation
records.abstract: Medical Report Generation (MRG) constitutes a crucial component of medical image analysis, requiring both precise lesion recognition and fluent semantic expression. Integrating knowledge graphs can further enhance the model’s ability to identify critical pathologies and understand their underlying relationships. However, traditional approaches based on external knowledge graphs suffer from the overhead of graph construction and complex retrieval networks. To address the above issues, we propose a retrieval-free and knowledge-augmented medical report generation framework based on knowledge-graph-conditioned distillation (RKRG). We design a region-aware label grounding to align visual regions with entity labels. Moreover, a graph simulator infers an implicit knowledge graph based on the attended visual regions and label information. Under a novel multi-modal knowledge distillation stage, we devise a supervisor and an implicit knowledge reasoner to obtain knowledge-enhanced features. Experiments demonstrate that this framework is particularly effective at distilling clinically meaningful knowledge and detecting rare abnormal findings.

records.title: MetaNAS: A Meta-Learning and Neural Architecture Search-Based Framework for Few-Shot Metal Surface Defect Segmentation
records.abstract: Deep learning models for industrial defect segmentation rely heavily on extensive annotated data, grappling with issues of scarcity, morphological diversity, and high labeling costs. While few-shot learning presents a potential solution, general-purpose networks often fail to adapt to the subtle texture variations, complex backgrounds, and scale differences inherent in such defects. To address these issues, we propose MetaNAS, a few-shot defect segmentation framework that deeply integrates neural architecture search (NAS) with meta-learning, aiming to automatically construct network architectures optimized for defect characteristics. A defect-oriented search space with specialized modules, and a two-stage search strategy is adopted to evolve the optimal network topology under extremely limited samples. To enhance feature discrimination and generalization, a contrastive learning loss and a learnable prototype modulation mechanism are introduced during training, forming a multi-task learning objective. This study provides an adaptive solution for defect detection with scarce data and validates the potential of NAS in specialized visual tasks.

records.title: SMPR-Gait: A Skeleton-Aware Multi-Modal Gait Recognition Network with Part-Relation Modeling
records.abstract: Gait recognition is a biometric technology for longdistance identity recognition from walking patterns, with significant practical value in public security and intelligent surveillance.In real scenarios, silhouette sequences are prone to occlusion and detection errors, while skeleton sequences suffer from missing keypoints and jitter, making a single modality unable to stably characterize gait appearance and structural information. records.title: Dual-R-DETR: Resolving Query Competition with Pairwise Routing in Transformer Decoders
records.abstract: Detection Transformers (DETR) formulate object detection as a set prediction problem and enable end-to-end training without post-processing. However, object queries in DETR interact through symmetric self-attention, which enforces uniform competition among all query pairs. This often leads to inefficient query dynamics, where multiple queries converge to the same object while others fail to explore alternative regions. We propose Dual-R-DETR, a competition-aware DETR framework that explicitly regulates query interactions via pairwise routing in transformer decoders. Dual-R-DETR distinguishes query-to-query relations as either competitive or cooperative based on appearance similarity, prediction confidence, and spatial geometry. It introduces two complementary routing behaviors: suppressor routing to attenuate interactions among queries targeting the same object, and delegator routing to encourage diversification across distinct regions. These behaviors are realized through lightweight, learnable low-rank biases injected into decoder self-attention, enabling asymmetric query interactions while preserving the standard attention formulation. To ensure inference efficiency, routing biases are applied only during training using a dual-branch strategy, and inference reverts to vanilla self-attention with no additional computational cost. Extensive experiments on COCO and Cityscapes demonstrate that Dual-R-DETR consistently improves multiple DETR variants, outperforming DINO by 1.7% mAP with a ResNet-50 backbone and achieving 57.6% mAP with Swin-L under comparable settings. Code will be available at this anonymous link.

records.title: Robust Low-Resolution Scene Text Recognition Through Iterative Cooperative Enhancement of Recovery and Recognition
records.abstract: Low-resolution text in natural scenes poses significant challenges to most existing text recognizers and hampers the effective extraction and utilization of scene information. In this paper, we propose a novel low-resolution scene text recognition network equipped with a cooperative enhancement mechanism, which effectively leverages the complementarity between text image super-resolution and recognition and thereby significantly improves the overall performance. Specifically, based on a multi-task feature learning backbone, the cross-task cooperative enhancement mechanism iteratively injects the visual and semantic text clues obtained from the recognition and recovery modules into each other across a series of enhancement stages. These mutual injections jointly enhance the performance of both modules and meanwhile effectively increase the discriminability of the shared features for both tasks. The experimental results show that the proposed network significantly improves the recognition accuracy of low-resolution scene text and achieves state-of-the-art performance on public datasets.

records.title: HCMF: Hierarchical Collaborative Multimodal Fusion for Longitudinal Functional Monitoring and Early Warning of Cognitive Impairment
records.abstract: Traditional cognitive assessment methods, limited by their static and fragmented nature, struggle to reflect the gradual decline of cognitive motor function in real-life situations. To address this deficiency, wearable technology is widely used to collect continuous gait features as functional biomarkers. However, existing single-gait methods offer limited representation and exhibit poor stability under noisy and small-sample conditions. Therefore, we propose a hierarchical collaborative multimodal fusion (HCMF) framework integrating gait features and clinical text for richer representations and improved assessment. HCMF uses a dual-expert mechanism: gait experts generate interpretable neuromotor representations under physiological constraints, while clinical experts extract structured features from sparse data. The modalities are then fused through low-rank dynamic graph attention and multipath negotiation, and aligned using orthogonality and consistency regularizers. records.title: Negation-Aware Robust Cross-Modal Alignment for Text-Based Person Search
records.abstract: Text-based person search (TBPS) aims to retrieve pedestrian images from natural language queries and plays an essential role in intelligent video surveillance. Although recent TBPS solutions have achieved great improvements in terms of retrieval performance, they still fail on queries involving negation, e.g., 'without black top'. The main reason is that current TBPS benchmarks contain almost exclusively affirmative descriptions, while providing no supervision for model to properly represent negation. To address above overlooked yet practically critical negation issue, we propose NARC, a two-stage Negation-Aware Robust Cross-modal alignments framework consisting of: 1) Negation-Aware Generation (NAG), a visually grounded caption synthesis pipeline that leverages a multi-modal large language model to produce negation descriptions and construct newly negation-aware benchmarks; and 2) Negation Transfer Distillation (NTD), a distillation strategy that transfers negation-related knowledge from a teacher trained on negation-aware benchmarks to a student for achieving more robust cross-modal alignments. Extensive experiments on the CUHK-PEDES, ICFG-PEDES, RSTPReid, and our newly constructed negation-aware benchmarks demonstrate that our NARC substantially enhances negation-aware cross-modal alignments while maintaining competitive performance on standard TBPS benchmarks.

records.title: GTIDD: A Novel Game Theory Framework for Imbalanced Disease Diagnosis
records.abstract: Class imbalance poses a significant obstacle to the development of reliable and robust disease diagnosis models, often resulting in biased learning behavior and suboptimal generalization, particularly for underrepresented yet clinically critical conditions. To address this challenge, we propose GTIDD, a Game Theory framework for Imbalanced Disease Diagnosis, which reformulates the training process as a multi-agent game. In this framework, each class acts as a competing agent, and sampling probabilities are adaptively adjusted based on inter-class interactions. GTIDD comprises two key components: a class contribution evaluation module that quantifies the influence of each class on model updates leveraging gradient statistics, and a game-driven sampling optimization module that dynamically adjusts sampling weights through inter-class competition to promote equitable learning. Extensive experiments on two public benchmarks and one in-house clinical dataset with pronounced class imbalance demonstrate that our method consistently surpasses state-of-the-art imbalance learning approaches.

records.title: Graph-Aware Logit Steering: A Plug-and-Play Paradigm for Graph Test-Time Adaptation
records.abstract: While Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) is pivotal for Graph Out-of-Distribution (OOD) generalization, the majority of existing methods remain trapped in a parameter-tuning paradigm. We argue that such paradigm suffers from a tripartite dilemma: catastrophic forgetting due to blind updates, computational overheads from backpropagation, and optimization instability on unlabeled data. In this work, we propose a fundamental shift from parameter tuning to explicit output distribution calibration. We introduce Graph-Aware Logit Steering (GALS), a gradient-free, plug-and-play inference module that decouples adaptation from training. Instead of risky parameter updates, GALS extracts a steering vector through the distributional discrepancy between the warm-up and pre-trained models, directly rectifying the logit distribution toward the target domain. Crucially, to handle graph-specific shifts, it incorporates Structure-Aware Denoising to enforce local consensus via homophily, and Dual-Granularity Confidence Constraints to establish a strict safety boundary against noise. Extensive experiments on numerous datasets demonstrate that GALS acts as a universal booster: it consistently improves various TTA baselines with negligible cost, effectively unlocking the latent potential of existing methods regardless of their convergence status.

records.title: SEVG: Semantic Excavation for Unsupervised Visual Grounding
records.abstract: Unsupervised visual grounding enables cross-modal region-text alignment using automatically generated pseudo-labels, which is critical for real-world applications such as human-computer interaction and robotic navigation. Existing methods rely on pre-trained vision-language models with rule-based composition strategies to generate pseudo-labels, yet neglect semantic sufficiency and linguistic naturalness. Naive attribute concatenation produces incoherent and unnatural descriptions, undermining deep cross-modal understanding. This paper proposes SEVG, a Semantic Excavation Framework for Visual Grounding. The Semantics-Coupled Pseudo-Label Generation module (SCPG) employs cross-modal semantic reinforcement and semantic correspondence constraint to generate coherent natural language descriptions with precise local semantics. During grounding, the Spatial-Semantic Collaborative Learning (SSCL) module jointly optimizes semantic understanding and spatial localization via semantic-guided feature refinement and spatial variation-aware constraints. Extensive experiments on five benchmarks demonstrate that SEVG achieves state-of-the-art performance in unsupervised visual grounding.

records.title: TURS: A Textual Uncertainty-aware Routing Strategy for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
records.abstract: Multimodal sentiment analysis aims to understand human affective states by integrating complementary signals from text, audio, and vision. However, existing approaches largely rely on static fusion strategies, applying a uniform process to all samples despite the inherent heterogeneity in modality uncertainty. This mismatch underscores the need for a dynamic routing mechanism that can customize multimodal fusion on a per-sample basis. This paper introduces the Textual Uncertainty-aware Routing Strategy (TURS), a dynamic fusion framework grounded in uncertainty estimation. TURS quantifies textual uncertainty via predictive variance and routes samples to specialized fusion pathways. For samples with varying Uncertainty levels, TURS employs distinct fusion routing strategies, dynamically adjusting the contributions of textual and non-textual modalities. We further propose a cross-route graph distillation mechanism to enhance knowledge sharing and generalization. Code and additional experimental details for TURS are available at the GitHub repository: https://github.com/Dikooo/TURS

records.title: Learning Discretization-Invariant Neural Operators via Latent Operator Bottlenecks
records.abstract: Neural operator learning seeks to approximate mappings between function spaces with generalization across spatial discretizations and geometries. However, existing approaches struggle to balance expressive global interactions with stable cross-resolution behavior. Graph-based methods rely on deep message passing to capture long-range dependencies, while transformer-based models introduce dense global attention with high computational cost and unstable information mixing. We propose LONet, a discretization-invariant neural operator architecture that represents global operator behavior through a compact set of Operator Latent Variables (OLVs). LONet follows an Encoder-Processor-Decoder paradigm, combining local graph propagation with global latent interaction. All long-range dependencies are routed through the OLVs, enforcing a structured low-dimensional constraint on global information flow. We show theoretically that this design induces a low-rank operator factorization and stabilizes long-range propagation. Experiments on diverse benchmarks with varying resolutions and geometry shifts demonstrate consistent improvements in accuracy and robustness over spectral, transformer-based, and graph-based baselines.

records.title: Multi-Modal Augmentation and Mutual Prompting for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation
records.abstract: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA) aims to transfer knowledge from a labeled source domain to an unlabeled target domain without direct access to target labels. However, existing methods struggle to extract sufficient information from limited unlabeled target data and often fail to capture domain-agnostic features when directly aligning source-target distributions. To address these issues, we propose MAMP, a framework that integrates multi-modal augmentation and mutual prompting. To enrich the semantic diversity of the training process, we introduce a multi-modal generative semantic expansion strategy. Specifically, this strategy jointly leverages CLIP and Stable Diffusion to obtain high-quality target samples. To prevent overfitting to source-specific styles, we introduce a mutual prompting mechanism. CoOp-optimized textual prompts are utilized as robust surrogates for raw source images, facilitating more efficient cross-domain alignment. Moreover, the combination of these two components leads to better domain adaptation performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MAMP achieves state-of-the-art performance on widely-used UDA benchmarks across different architectures.

records.title: AD-Reasoning: Multimodal Guideline-Guided Reasoning for Alzheimer’s Disease Diagnosis
records.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) diagnosis requires integrating neuroimaging with heterogeneous clinical evidence and reasoning under established criteria, yet most multimodal models remain opaque and weakly guideline-aligned. We present AD-Reasoning, a multimodal framework that couples structural MRI with six clinical modalities and a rule-based verifier to generate structured, NIA-AA-consistent diagnoses. AD-Reasoning combines modality-specific encoders, bidirectional cross-attention fusion, and reinforcement fine-tuning with verifiable rewards that enforce output format, guideline evidence coverage, and reasoning--decision consistency. We also release AD-MultiSense, a 10,378-visit multimodal QA dataset with guideline-validated rationales built from ADNI/AIBL. On AD-MultiSense, AD-Reasoning achieves state-of-the-art diagnostic accuracy and produces structured rationales that improve transparency over recent baselines, while providing transparent rationales.

records.title: FOCUS: Fused Observation of Channels for Unveiling Spectra
records.abstract: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) provides critical details for biology and agriculture, yet interpreting Vision Transformers (ViTs) on such high-dimensional data remains a challenge. Existing methods fail for two reasons: the computational cost of processing hundreds of bands is prohibitive, and models often suffer from ``attention collapse,'' where focus shifts to irrelevant tokens rather than meaningful spectral signals. We propose FOCUS, a framework that enables efficient spatial-spectral interpretability for frozen ViTs. Our method introduces two lightweight components: class-specific spectral prompts that anchor attention to relevant wavelength groups, and a learnable [SINK] token that actively filters out noisy attention. Unlike prior approaches, FOCUS generates 3D saliency maps in a single forward pass without requiring gradients or retraining the backbone. Experiments show that our method improves band-level IoU by 15\% and reduces attention collapse by 40\%. With less than 1\% parameter overhead, FOCUS makes interpretable HSI practical for real-world applications.

records.title: Query-guided Background-aware Learning for Fine-Grained Generalized Category Discovery
records.abstract: Generalized Category Discovery (GCD) aims to recognize both known and novel categories in unlabeled data by leveraging knowledge from labeled datasets. Recent studies reveal that self-supervised models often attend to task-irrelevant background regions, which is especially detrimental for fine-grained datasets with subtle inter-class differences. To address this, we propose Query-guided Background-aware Learning (QB-Learning), an efficient approach that can be seamlessly integrated into fine-grained GCD frameworks. QB-Learning comprises two components: Query-guided Feature Mining (QgFM), which learns query representations to extract fine-grained features and distinguish target regions from background clutter, and Background-aware Attention Suppression (BaAS), which leverages these features to suppress background attention and filter out task-irrelevant information. As a result, QB-Learning achieves semantic-aware background suppression, enabling the model to focus on discriminative regions, preserve meaningful foreground features, and consistently yield significant performance gains on fine-grained datasets.

records.title: Purify, Align, and Refine: Progressive Semantic Constraints for Multimodal NER
records.abstract: Multimodal Named Entity Recognition (MNER) aims to enhance entity extraction by incorporating visual cues, typically following a representation-alignment-fusion paradigm. However, prevailing attention-based approaches tend to overfit superficial statistical correlations by relying on spurious cross-modal co-occurrences. This makes them susceptible to cascading noise across all three stages: intra-modal noise, cross-modal misalignment, and entity-type ambiguity. To address these issues, we propose PAR-MNER, a novel framework that introduces progressive semantic constraints—instead of relying solely on attention networks—to actively Purify, Align, and Refine representations. Distinct from disjoint modular designs, our framework operates as a coherent pipeline: (1) Purify: We first distill task-relevant semantics and filter intra-modal noise using a Modality-specific Embedding Constraint based on the Information Bottleneck principle, ensuring that only clean signals enter the alignment stage. (2) Align: We then rectify cross-modal misalignment through a Cross-modal Alignment Constraint. By employing Optimal Transport with a novel filter bucket mechanism, we robustly calibrate text-image correspondence and effectively discard unaligned visual regions. (3) Refine: Finally, to sharpen decision boundaries, we impose a Multimodal Type Constraint via supervised contrastive learning, which resolves remaining entity-type ambiguities in the fused space. Extensive experiments on Twitter-2015 and Twitter-2017 demonstrate that our method consistently outperforming state-of-the-art baselines.

records.title: EU2-Geo: Cross-View Image Geo-Localization via Enhancing Unlabeled Data Utility
records.abstract: The supervised cross-view image geo-localization methods suffer from the high cost of labeling data. While existing few methods adopt pseudo-label mining to overcome this deficiency, they often assume the training samples are one-to-one matching, leading to insufficient recall and false negatives in real-world many-to-many matching scenarios. Therefore, we propose EU2-Geo, a novel cross-view image geo-localization method via enhancing unlabeled data utility. Firstly, a BEV-panorama fusion module is designed to reduce viewpoint discrepancy. Then, a dynamic gap-based strategy is developed to adaptively select multiple positives to improve recall. Furthermore, more accurate hard negatives are mined under the constraint of positive sample set and aggregated into a training batch to strengthen contrastive learning. Finally, a rank-weighted multi-positive contrastive loss is constructed to jointly leverage multiple positives and hard negatives. Experiments on CVUSA, CVACT, and VIGOR show that our method outperforms existing semi-supervised approaches and nearly matches state-of-the-art full supervised methods.

records.title: PGViM: Mitigating Memory Curse in Vision Mamba with Positional Grouping
records.abstract: State space models (SSMs) such as Mamba have recently emerged as efficient alternatives to attention for vision tasks, yet their performance degrades on high-resolution images as long recurrent scans cause severe gradient attenuation, commonly referred to as the memory curse. We propose Positionally Grouped Vision Mamba (PGViM), a non-hierarchical vision backbone that decouples global dependency modeling from full-resolution scanning. PGViM introduces a reversible positional grouping一ungrouping mechanism that aggregates dense spatial tokens into a compact set of learnable group tokens that serve as semantic summarizers for Mamba-scanning. Tailored rolespecific positional encoding schemes are used for spatial and group tokens to support this mechanism. Extensive experiments on image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation demonstrate that PGViM consistently improves gradient propagation and achieves a superior accuracy一efficiency trade-off compared to existing SSM-based vision models.

records.title: Multi-Perspective Subimage CLIP with Keyword Guidance for Remote Sensing Image-Text Retrieval
records.abstract: Abstract—Vision-Language Pre-training (VLP) models like CLIP have significantly advanced Remote Sensing Image-Text Retrieval (RSITR). However, existing methods predominantly rely on coarse-grained global alignment, which often overlooks the dense, multi-scale semantics inherent in overhead imagery. Moreover, adapting these heavy models via full fine-tuning incurs prohibitive computational costs and risks catastrophic forgetting. To address these challenges, we propose MPS-CLIP, a parameter-efficient framework designed to shift the retrieval paradigm from global matching to keyword-guided fine-grained alignment. Specifically, we leverage a Large Language Model (LLM) to extract core semantic keywords, guiding the Segment Anything Model (SamGeo) to generate semantically relevant sub-views. To efficiently adapt the frozen backbone, we introduce a Gated Global Attention (G2A) adapter, which captures global context and long-range dependencies with minimal overhead. Further-more, a Multi-View Representation (MVR) module aggregates these local cues into robust multi-perspective embeddings. The framework is optimized via a hybrid objective combining multi-view contrastive and weighted triplet losses, which dynami-cally selects maximum-response perspectives to suppress noise and enforce precise semantic matching. Extensive experiments on the RSICD and RSITMD benchmarks demonstrate that MPS-CLIP achieves state-of-the-art performance with 35.18% and 48.40% mean Recall (mR), respectively, significantly out-performing full fine-tuning baselines and recent competitive methods. Code is available in https://anonymous.4open.science/ r/ICME-4410-MPS-CLIP. Index Terms—remote sensing, cross-modal retrieval, vision-language pre-training, multi-view representation learning
