records.title: C-Mani: Conflict-aware Semi-supervised Multimodal Sentiment Analysis against Pseudo-label Sycophancy
records.abstract: Multimodal Sentiment Analysis (MSA) benefits from combining images and texts, yet in low-label regimes existing semi-supervised MSA methods largely inherit unimodal pseudo-labeling with a static confidence threshold. Such strategies fail to model cross-modal agreement/conflict, yielding over-confident but wrong pseudo-labels on conflicting samples, such as sarcastic text paired with positive imagery, and systematically biasing the decision boundary. We propose C-Mani, a conflict-aware semi-supervised framework for MSA. First, C-Mani generates conflict-aware pseudo-labels by integrating per-modality confidence with cross-modal consistency, and applies gated filtering and cleaning to suppress high-risk unlabeled samples. Next, it dynamically re-weights unlabeled samples based on agreement to reduce the influence of conflicts. Finally, it introduces a decoupled representation regularization to constrain shared and private representations and prevent error propagation. Experiments on three benchmarks show consistent gains over strong baselines, with up to 3.64 points improvement under extremely low-label settings.

records.title: CPAD: Constrained Prompt Learning for Few-Shot Anomaly Detection
records.abstract: Few-shot anomaly detection is pivotal for real-world applications characterized by severe data scarcity. Although prompt-based approaches have yielded promising results, they often overlook the specific contextual constraints within support samples. Consequently, the learned prompts often lack the discriminative power to accurately distinguish between normal and anomalous instances. To address this challenge, we propose CPAD, a novel Constrained Prompt learning framework for Anomaly Detection. CPAD imposes scene-conditional constraints during optimization, enabling the model to construct more effective boundaries between normal and abnormal concepts. Furthermore, we introduce a Logic-based Prompt Generation (LPG) mechanism. By leveraging the logical exclusion between normal and abnormal states, LPG synthesizes diverse prompts to enhance the model's generalization capabilities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CPAD significantly outperforms state-of-the-art prompt learning approaches across all evaluated datasets. Code will be released upon acceptance.

records.title: Dual Denoising U-Net Diffusion Model for End-to-End Image Composition
records.abstract: Real-scene image composition requires both realistic shadow generation and image harmonization. Existing diffusion-based approaches typically treat these as separate stages, leading to error accumulation. However, unifying them is non-trivial due to inherent gradient conflicts, where harmonization objectives often suppress generated shadows. To address this, we present DUDiffusion, an end-to-end framework featuring an interactive Dual Denoising U-Net. This architecture seamlessly integrates shadow generation and image harmonization within a unified latent feature space, ensuring semantic consistency across tasks. We introduce a decoupled training strategy to explicitly resolve task conflicts and a Hierarchical Feature Enhanced SG-Adapter to ensure texture-preserving shadow generation. Furthermore, we contribute a large-scale benchmark dataset, DESOBv2-DisH. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DUDiffusion effectively balances shadow realism and visual harmony, outperforming state-of-the-art two-stage approaches.

records.title: MP3: Mining Pure Pivot Patches for Robust Real-World Single Image Defocus Deblurring
records.abstract: Single Image Defocus Deblurring (SIDD) aims to restore an all-in-focus image from a partially defocused image. Early methods resort to designing complex dynamic blocks to enhance spatial awareness but their generalization performance is limited. Recently, prior-driven approaches leverage the defocus kernel prior to achieve promising results but still rely heavily on heuristic priors. In this paper, we rethink how to train a model that generalizes well from a data-quality perspective. Specifically, we find that not all patches contribute equally during training and aim to \underline{M}ine \underline{P}ure \underline{P}ivot \underline{P}atches (\textit{MP3}) that offers rich and clean learning signals for training a robust and generalizable model. To achieve this, we design a metric that quantifies the quality of patches by measuring the entropy-density decay and residual sparsity. Entropy-density decay is aimed at evaluating the richness of defocus cues (\textit{related to Pivot}) while residual sparsity is for evaluating whether a patch pair is aligned with the defocus degradation (\textit{related to Purity}). Additionally, a simple yet effective scale-recurrent neural network is adapted from existing methods by removing redundant activations and operations while emphasizing cross-scale selections. To further enhance robustness, we design a curriculum frequency learning paradigm to progressively guide the NN to learn from structures to details. Through extensive experiments, our method demonstrates strong generalization performance across different datasets.

records.title: FlowIR: Depth-driven Rectified Flow for Resolving Thermal Ambiguity in Infrared Super-Resolution
records.abstract: Distinguishing different heat sources in low-resolution infrared (IR) images is inherently difficult, as multiple thermal emitters often collapse into ambiguous and overlapping responses. Existing super-resolution methods hallucinate structures from such ambiguous 2D evidence, leading to thermal drift, boundary merging, and unreliable restoration under infrared degradations. We propose FlowIR, a depth-driven rectified flow framework that resolves thermal ambiguity by injecting 3D geometric cues into the generation process. Pseudo-3D depth lifting and depth-guided 3D convolutions disentangle overlapping foreground objects, while cluster-wise inter-attention suppresses cross-source feature contamination. A Thermal–Geometry Consistency Loss further enforces geometric alignment during refinement. Built upon a lightweight rectified flow backbone, FlowIR restores IR images in only a few steps, producing sharply separated, degradation-robust, and geometrically faithful high-resolution results.

records.title: Text-Guided Zero-Shot Image Dehazing
records.abstract: Zero-shot dehazing directly utilizes the input image without external datasets, offering a promising solution for real-world applications. The main challenge is extracting sufficient information from a hazy image, as haze significantly covers visual details. To address this issue, we propose a text-guided zero-shot image dehazing (TGZID) network, which is trained using only one hazy image and guided by haze-aware textual descriptions through self-supervised learning. A vision-language contrastive learning module aligns image and text representations in a multimodal embedding space. Positive (haze-free) and negative (hazy) descriptions are selected via a random sample screening algorithm. To better leverage multimodal semantic information, we further design a text-guided multiscale feature enhancement module, which incorporates edge attention blocks to refine feature fusion. To our knowledge, our approach is the first to implement vision-language guidance for zero-shot image dehazing. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art methods. The code is available at https://github.com/lizhangray/TGZID.

records.title: PMoE-Net:Prompt-Guided Heterogeneous Mixture-of-Experts for All-in-One Fundus Image Restoration
records.abstract: High-quality fundus images are crucial for the reliable diagnosis of retinal diseases, but real-world clinical imaging often suffers from complex and mixed degradations such as blurriness, artifacts, and uneven illumination. Existing methods typically rely on single-paradigm architectures (e.g., pure CNN or Transformer models), limiting their ability to address the spatially heterogeneous and compound degradations commonly found in real-world clinical data. To overcome these limitations, we present PMoE-Net, a prompt-guided fundus image restoration framework that integrates a heterogeneous mixture of experts, each expert specializing in a distinct task: Local Expert for detailed processing, Global Expert for long-range dependency modeling, and Frequency Expert for spectral domain analysis. The framework comprises dynamic soft-routing weight conditioning sub-expert networks based on input-specific degradation characteristics. Furthermore, a prompt-aware modulation strategy semantically aligns restoration operations with textual instructions, enabling controllable and fine-grained enhancement in diverse clinical scenarios. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PMoE-Net achieves superior performance under various degradation conditions, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods while providing interpretable and controllable restoration tailored to clinical requirements.

records.title: Self-supervised Single Image Deraining by Online Rainy/Clean Image Pair Synthesis
records.abstract: Deep learning techniques have been widely used for single image rain removal (SIRR) and achieved leading performance. However, they suffer from lacking various rainy/clean image pairs for training, and thus have limitations in either generality or practicality. In this paper, we propose a self-supervised learning framework, built on an unpaired one-sided image-to-image translation model, for single image deraining, which does not require any paired supervision. It synchronously performs rain streaks and image content disentanglement, rainy/clean image pair online synthesis and deraining model training with the self-generated paired supervision. Benefited from the sufficiently \textbf{various} rainy/clean image pairs synthesized online, the deraining model has both strong practicality and cross-dataset generality. Extensive experiments on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that the deraining model learned by our framework achieves significant improvement over state-of-the-art unsupervised SIRR methods and has much stronger cross-dataset generality than state-of-the-art supervised SIRR methods. Moreover, additional experiments on other image restoration tasks demonstrate the generalization of our self-supervised learning framework.

records.title: TempRetinex: Retinex-based Unsupervised Enhancement for Low-light Video Under Diverse Lighting Conditions
records.abstract: The acquisition of paired low-light video sequences remains challenging due to issues associated with poor temporal consistency, varying illumination characteristics and camera parameters. This has driven significant interest in unsupervised low-light enhancement approaches. In this context, we propose TempRetinex, an unsupervised Retinex-based video enhancement framework exploiting inter-frame correlations. We introduce Brightness Consistency Preprocessing (BCP) that explicitly aligns intensity distributions across exposures. BCP is shown to significantly improve model robustness to diverse lighting scenarios. Moreover, we propose a multiscale temporal consistency-aware loss and an occlusion-aware masking technique to enforce similarity between consecutive frames. We further incorporate a Reverse Inference (RI) strategy to refine temporally unstable frames and a Self-Ensemble (SE) mechanism to boost denoising across diverse textures. Experiments demonstrate that TempRetinex achieves state-of-the-art performance in perceptual quality. Code is available at https://github.com/liyinibristol/TempRetinex.

records.title: DunbarFL: Dynamic Cognitive Social Aggregation for Personalized Federated Learning
records.abstract: Personalized federated learning (PFL) enables client-specific models for heterogeneous visual data, yet its effectiveness is often limited by unreliable and poorly structured collaboration. In practice, heterogeneous optimization trajectories render uniform interactions ineffective, static or handcrafted collaboration structures fail to adapt to drifting visual distributions, and the absence of temporally-aware consistency control undermines robustness. Motivated by Dunbar’s cognitive limit theory, which states that individuals can maintain only a bounded number of stable relationships organized in layered social circles, we propose DunbarFL, a cognitively grounded framework for PFL. DunbarFL introduces a capacity-constrained dynamic collaboration graph that explicitly limits each client’s feasible interaction strength, organizes collaborators into layered relational circles with distinct influence levels, and refines collaboration through drift-aware consistency modulation. This design embeds a socio-cognitive inductive bias into federated collaboration, enabling selective, stable, and adaptive personalization. Extensive experiments show that DunbarFL improves both personalized and global accuracy over baselines, achieving up to 21.5% improvement in personalized accuracy under extreme non-IID settings.

records.title: WSRNet: Wavelet-Based Shadow Removal Network for Document Image Enhancement
records.abstract: Document shadow removal (DSR) is a challenging task, which aims to preserve the fine structural information of texts while eliminating shadows in the images. Observing that text details generally belong to high-frequency information, while shadows are mainly manifested as low-frequency components, we propose a novel shadow mask-free DSR network, i.e., Wavelet Shadow Removal Network (WSRNet), which combines spatial and frequency-domain information through simple convolution and wavelet transformation operations respectively. WSRNet is built upon an encoder-decoder archetecture, where the encoder composes of multiple Wavelet-domain Feature Extraction (WFE) blocks and the decoder consists of multiple Wavelet-domain Shadow Removal (WSR) blocks. WFE encodes images through wavelet convolutions, obtaining multi-domain document images feature representations from different receptive fields. A Document Mask Extraction (DME) module is proposed to aggregate wavelet-domain low-frequency information from WFE blocks and generates shadow masks in a unsupervised way. WSR turns the features back symmetrically to the image domain by repairing the different information in high and low frequency domain correspondingly with shadow mask guidance. In addition, we introduce a frequency-aware loss that emphasizes the text salient frequencies of document images. We conduct extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, and the results demonstrate that the proposed WSRNet significantly outperforms existing methods for DSR and also achieves remarkable performance for general image shadow removal task.

records.title: Draft with What the Target Knows: Hierarchical Intermediate Conditioning for Lossless VLM Acceleration
records.abstract: Vision Language Models (VLMs) enable many multimodal applications but face deployment constraints due to autoregressive latency and expensive cross-modal computation. While speculative decoding offers lossless acceleration via draft–verify pipelines, extending it to VLMs is difficult: visual inputs yield massive token sets and multi-token drafting suffers train–test mismatch because target-model intermediate states exist only for verified prefixes. We propose a VLM-oriented speculative decoding framework that aligns draft conditioning with inference-time target signals. We extract hierarchical intermediate representations from shallow, middle, and deep Transformer layers in a single pass and compress visual features with lightweight adapters, organizing them into depth-wise multimodal cues to condition the draft model. To respect the constraint that target features are only available for verified tokens, the draft model performs target-conditioned generation on verified prefixes and smoothly shifts to self-conditioned generation on unverified positions. A two-step unrolled training scheme simulates this transition, exposing the model to its own trajectories to reduce exposure bias and stabilize multi-token proposals under strict verification. Experiments show increased expected acceptance length, significantly improved decoding efficiency. achieving a 3.17$\times$ speedup on LLaVA-1.6 7B.

records.title: Unsupervised Spatio-temporal Coherence Learning for Noise Reduction in Time-resolved Velocity Fields of 4D Magnetic Resonance Flow Imaging
records.abstract: Four-dimensional phase-contrast magnetic resonance imaging (4D PC-MRI) provides a noninvasive approach to measure blood flow velocities and supports the diagnosis of cerebrovascular conditions. However, its performance in small and tortuous brain vessels is often degraded by inherent noise. To address this issue, we propose a novel unsupervised spatio-temporal denoising network (USTD-Net) for denoising 4D MR flow images, which learns spatio-temporal coherence in time-resolved 3D velocity fields without labeled data. Concretely, USTD-Net captures both inter- and intra-volume coherence and leverages spatio-temporal continuity implied by flow physics to remove global and local noise, enabling high-quality restoration of velocity vector fields. The resulting vectors exhibit improved temporal consistency and spatial smoothness, potentially enhancing downstream hemodynamic analysis. Extensive experiments verify that USTD-Net delivers robust denoising across a wide range of signal-to-noise ratios and generalizes well to diverse clinically acquired datasets without retraining.

records.title: Ambient2Hap: Rendering Haptic Feedback via Somatosensory Electrical Stimulation from Ambient Cues in Virtual Reality
records.abstract: Haptic feedback for immersive 360° video remains limited in its ability to convey ambient environmental effects. Electrical stimulation offers a compact and programmable alternative, yet methods for deriving stimulation cues directly from video content are still limited. This paper presents Ambient2Hap, a framework that detects ambient events in videos and maps them to somatosensory electrical stimulation on the upper body. We demonstrate two representative cases—rainfall as an instance of particle motion and bomb explosions as an instance of transient impacts—by estimating particle-motion intensity from visual cues and inferring explosion direction and strength from spatial audio. These cues are translated into time-varying stimulation patterns rendered through a wearable suit. A user study provides initial evidence that dynamic, content-aligned stimulation may improve perceived immersion relative to fixed or no feedback, although the advantage varies by scenario and dimension. We discuss design considerations and outline opportunities for integrating multimodal analysis with electrical stimulation in future immersive media systems.

records.title: Revisiting Event Guided Deblurring with State Space Model
records.abstract: Event guided motion deblurring has shown promising potential by leveraging asynchronous event streams to compensate for the severe information loss in blurred RGB frames. In this paper, we propose a novel event guided deblurring framework that explicitly models global motion information through state space models. We introduce modality specific encoders equipped with global state space modeling to capture long range motion dependencies from both RGB frames and event voxels, with a frequency aware dual branch design to disentangle low- and high-frequency information. A multi level fusion decoder progressively injects event guidance during reconstruction. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms state of the art approaches under various evaluation settings while maintaining favorable computational efficiency. The code and pre-trained model are available at: https://github.com/NikonD850/REGDSSM.

records.title: MapAgent: Trajectory-Constructed Memory-Augmented Planning for Mobile Task Automation
records.abstract: The recent advancement of autonomous agents powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) has shown significant potential for automating tasks on mobile devices through graphical user interfaces (GUIs). Despite initial progress, existing agents are limited to repetitive trial-and-error without learning from historical interactions. To address this, we propose MapAgent, a novel framework that augments task planning with memory constructed from past trajectories. First, we design a trajectory-based memory mechanism that converts previous task executions into a structured page-memory database, where each page encapsulates both interface layout and functional context as a compact snapshot. Then, a coarse-to-fine planning strategy retrieves relevant pages and injects them into an LLM-based planner to improve contextual awareness. The planned tasks are executed using a dual-LLM executor for reliable task execution. Evaluations on real-world mobile task datasets show that MapAgent significantly enhances task execution performance and adaptability.

records.title: OMIT-Net: Degradation-Adaptive Dynamic Routing for All-in-One Image Restoration
records.abstract: All-in-one image restoration aims to restore low-quality images affected by diverse and unknown degradations within a unified framework. However, the existing methods suffer from a rigid and redundant computation budget, as they rely on static and fixed network architectures to cope with varying restoration difficulties across different degradation types and intensities. To overcome this limitation, we propose OMIT-Net, a plug-and-play degradation-adaptive dynamic all-in-one image restoration network (\textit{i.e.,} OMIT-X), which effectively reduces computational complexity by adaptively skipping degradation-irrelevant layers while maintaining comparable restoration performance. Specifically, we introduce a lightweight router that adaptively determines whether to skip or execute each OMIT-X Layer, guided by loss functions that promote a consistent routing path for similar degradations and encourage diversity across different degradation types and intensities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed OMIT-Net exhibits high flexibility and effectiveness, reducing computational cost by approximately 25\% on average while achieving comparable image restoration performance. Code is available at \href{https://github.com/Brittany-Chen/OMIT-Net} {https://github.com/Brittany-Chen/OMIT-Net}.

records.title: PAWSS-Net:Position-Aware Wavelet Domain Fusion with Sequence Shuffle Attention for Text Image Super-Resolution
records.abstract: Text image super-resolution aims to recover clear character structures and readable content from low-quality images, which is critical for real-world text recognition. To address the coupled limitations in geometric deformation modeling, multi-scale feature interaction, and cross-modal fusion, this paper proposes the Position-Aware Wavelet Domain Fusion and Sequence Shuffle Attention Network. The model systematically tackles these issues through three key modules: the Dynamic Content-Aware Position Encoding Module effectively models geometric deformation; the Multi-Scale Attention with Fusion Sequence Shuffle Module enhances semantic-coherent feature interaction; and the Frequency-Guided Multimodal Fusion Module strengthens both details and semantic information in the wavelet domain. Evaluated on the TextZoom dataset, our method achieves recognition accuracies of 58.69%, 64.76% and 67.7% on CRNN, MORAN and ASTER classifiers, respectively, surpassing the state-of-the-art by approximately 3.7% on the Hard subset, with PSNR and SSIM reaching 21.83 dB and 0.7793. This work provides a strong reference for structure-sensitive vision tasks.

records.title: RRSSD: Radiometric-Response-Constrained Stripe Simulation and Destriping for Remote Sensing Imagery
records.abstract: Stripe noise significantly degrades the quality of pushbroom remote sensing images (RSIs) and hampers quantitative downstream applications. While deep learning-based destriping methods have shown promise, they often suffer from a reliance on unrealistic synthetic data and a lack of interpretability, failing to capture the complex non-linear radiometric response characteristics of real satellite detectors. To address these challenges, we propose RRSSD, a physics-guided framework that unifies realistic stripe simulation with a novel destriping network. Specifically, we revisit stripe formation through explicit detector-response modeling to construct a physically consistent training dataset. To bridge this gap, we propose RRSSD incorporating a Column Radiometric Prior and Visibility-Driven Gating to recover intrinsic details while enforcing column and radiometric consistency. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real GF-2/GF-7 datasets demonstrate that RRSSD outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving superior stripe removal and detail preservation. Code will be made publicly available upon acceptance.

records.title: Dual-Path Learning based on Frequency Structural Decoupling and Regional-Aware Fusion for Low-Light Image Super-Resolution
records.abstract: Low-light image super-resolution (LLISR) is essential for restoring fine visual details and perceptual quality under insufficient illumination conditions with ubiquitous low-resolution devices. Although pioneer methods achieve high performance on single tasks, they solve both tasks in a serial manner, which inevitably leads to artifact amplification, texture suppression, and structural degradation. To address this, we propose Decoupling then Perceive (DTP), a novel frequency-aware framework that explicitly separates luminance and texture into semantically independent components, enabling specialized modeling and coherent reconstruction. Specifically, to adaptively separate the input into low-frequency luminance and high-frequency texture subspaces, we propose a Frequency-aware Structural Decoupling (FSD) mechanism, which lays a solid foundation for targeted representation learning and reconstruction. Based on the decoupled representation, a Semantics-specific Dual-path Representation (SDR) learning strategy that performs targeted enhancement and reconstruction for each frequency component is further designed, facilitating robust luminance adjustment and fine-grained texture recovery. To promote structural consistency and perceptual alignment in the reconstructed output, building upon this dual-path modeling, we further introduce a Cross-frequency Semantic Recomposition (CSR) module that selectively integrates the decoupled representations. Extensive experiments on the most widely used LLISR benchmarks demonstrate the superiority of our DTP framework, improving +1.6% PSNR, +9.6% SSIM, and -48% LPIPS compared to the most state-of-the-art (SOTA) algorithm.

records.title: HSV-CFNet: Color-Space-Aware HSV Decoupling and Complementary Fusion for Low-Light Image Enhancement
records.abstract: Most deep low-light image enhancement methods operate in RGB space where luminance and chrominance are entangled, or treat decoupled color channels as generic tensors, often leading to color distortion and artifacts. To address this issue, we propose HSV-CFNet, a framework that incorporates color-space-aware inductive biases within a decouple–align–fuse paradigm in the HSV color space. Specifically, we design channel-specific representations that respect intrinsic geometric and structural properties, including trigonometric circular encoding for the non-Euclidean topology of Hue and gradient-guided refinement for the Value channel. To integrate these heterogeneous features, we introduce the Complementary Channel Collaborative Fusion (CCCF) module, which performs conditional statistical alignment before fusion to enable balanced cross-channel collaboration. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance with superior color fidelity.

records.title: FA²-Net: Learning Frequency-Asymmetric Channel Attention for Image Super-Resolution
records.abstract: Most frequency-based single image super-resolution (SISR) methods uniformly apply identical frequency manipulation to all feature channels and ultimately produce unsatisfying results. Notably, we observe that the response maps of different channels exhibit distinct structural and textural patterns, indicating that each channel tends to encode different aspects of the image—while existing SISR methods ignore this phenomenon, thereby suppressing channel-specific information. To address this issue, we apply hierarchical frequency bands to modulate the channel-specific information. Specifically, we propose FA²-Net, an asymmetric attention framework that performs both channel-wise and pixel-wise reasoning on the low-frequency and high-frequency bands, respectively. Its core Asymmetric Frequency Analysis Module (AFAM) decomposes features into frequency components and models their channel-wise and pixel-wise statistics, achieving cross-band selective enhancement through asymmetric low- and high-frequency processing. Building on AFAM, the Coarse-to-Fine Modulation Module (CFMM) employs the learned modulation parameters to progressively refine spatial features. Experiments show that FA²-Net surpasses recent state-of-the-art methods, especially on images with complex textures.

records.title: PSD-Net: Physics-Guided Spectral-Temporal Diffusion for Low-Dose PET Restoration
records.abstract: Low-dose Positron Emission Tomography (LDPET) involves a fundamental trade-off between radiation reduction and quantitative fidelity, where severe photon starvation induces structured bias beyond the Gaussian noise approximation. Although diffusion models show promise for perceptual restoration, their stochastic sampling often leads to anatomical hallucinations and radiometric inconsistency due to the lack of explicit physical grounding. We propose PSD-Net, a physics-guided spectral–temporal diffusion paradigm for robust LDPET restoration. Built on the observation that physical reliability in PET imaging is inherently frequency- and timestep-dependent, PSD-Net reformulates restoration as a frequency-disentangled residual generation process, separating deterministic low-frequency structural recovery from stochastic high-frequency texture synthesis. A spectral–temporal physical anchoring mechanism selectively enforces Poisson consistency on low-frequency components during signal-dominant diffusion stages, correcting quantitative bias without over-constraining noise-dominated regimes. Finally, a lightweight deterministic manifold projection module maps the generative output back to the quantitative activity domain (Bq/ml). Extensive experiments on clinical PET datasets demonstrate that PSD-Net consistently outperforms strong baselines across a wide range of dose levels, particularly under extreme low-dose conditions, achieving superior voxel-wise accuracy and structural fidelity with efficient inference.

records.title: MDIQA: Unified Image Quality Assessment for Multi-dimensional Evaluation and Restoration
records.abstract: Recent advancements in image quality assessment (IQA), driven by sophisticated deep neural network designs, have significantly improved the ability to approach human perceptions. However, most existing methods are obsessed with fitting the overall score, neglecting the fact that humans typically evaluate image quality from different dimensions before arriving at an overall quality assessment. To overcome this problem, we propose a multi-dimensional image quality assessment (MDIQA) framework. Specifically, we model image quality across various perceptual dimensions, including five technical and four aesthetic dimensions, to capture the multifaceted nature of human visual perception within distinct branches. Each branch of our MDIQA is initially trained under the guidance of a separate dimension, and the respective features are then amalgamated to generate the final IQA score. Additionally, when the MDIQA model is ready, we can deploy it for a flexible training of image restoration (IR) models, enabling the restoration results to better align with varying user preferences through the adjustment of perceptual dimension weights. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our MDIQA achieves superior performance and can be effectively and flexibly applied to image restoration tasks. The source code and pre-trained models will be released.

records.title: Gene Semantics Guided Multimodal Super-Resolution for Spatial Transcriptomics
records.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics provides critical insights into gene expression patterns at spatial scales. However, mainstream spatial transcriptomics technologies are constrained by spot-level resolution, which limits their ability to capture fine-grained tissue heterogeneity. As a result, reconstructing high-resolution spatial gene expression maps from low-resolution measurements has become a central research problem. Recent studies have explored spatial transcriptomics super-resolution by integrating histopathology images. Nevertheless, due to the morphological similarity of tissue structures, gene expression prediction based solely on visual cues often leads to over-smoothed results, hindering the model’s ability to recover genuine expression variability. To address these limitations, we propose Gene semantics guided multimodal super-resolution for Spatial Transcriptomics (GeneST), a novel framework that enhances spatial gene expression prediction by incorporating rich semantic knowledge from gene texts alongside histopathology images. Specifically, we curate a large-scale corpus of gene textual descriptions from knowledge bases, which capture fine-grained characteristics of spatial gene expression patterns. We then introduce a cross-modal alignment method between gene texts and histopathology images, thereby guiding the model toward more accurate and spatially detailed gene expression inference. Extensive experiments on eight datasets demonstrate that GeneST consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of prediction granularity and biological consistency. Our code will be released at https://github.com/anomity/GeneST.

records.title: A Retinex-Driven Data Fusion Network for Robust Shadow Removal via Illumination-Color Degradation Modeling
records.abstract: Shadow removal remains challenging due to the interference between diffuse reflection and direct lighting, as well as the complex coupling of texture and illumination. To tackle these issues, we introduce ICDM-SRNet, a Retinex-Driven Data Fusion Network for Robust Shadow Removal via Illumination-Color Degradation Modeling. ICDM-SRNet ingeniously blends physical priors with data-driven learning to establish a three-tier decoupled representation framework. Firstly, it features an intrinsic attribute subspace that meticulously preserves the inherent reflectance and geometric properties of the scene. Secondly, there is an illumination degradation subspace that precisely models the attenuation of illumination and the consequent local structural variations. Thirdly, a color degradation subspace is incorporated to capture the chromatic shifts induced by shadow occlusion. A dual-branch calibration module is integrated into the network, which adaptively compensates for these degradations within the latent space. Extensive experiments conducted on public datasets clearly demonstrate that ICDM-SRNet surpasses existing methods.

records.title: VisTAE: Visual-Text cAusal dEbiasing for Out-of-Distribution Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
records.abstract: Multimodal Sentiment Analysis (MSA) leverages language and vision to infer sentiment, but often suffers from spurious correlations—e.g., sentiment words or visual context spuriously associated with labels—hindering generalization to out-of-distribution (OOD) data. Existing methods try to fix this using counterfactual learning by removing the Natural Direct Effect (NDE), but they tend to over-correct, erasing both noise and useful sentimental cues. Our analysis shows sentiment words are not purely harmful—they also provide key sentimental signals, though they introduce two types of bias: (i)Label Co-occurrence Bias and (ii) Attention Over-emphasis Bias. We introduce VisTAE, a model-agnostic framework that inspired by causal reasoning to reduce bias without losing important sentiment information. In the textual branch, sentiment words are treated as proxies for confounders, and adjusted carefully to keep helpful signals. In the visual branch, we apply counterfactual reasoning to remove misleading context. The two debiased streams are then fused for final prediction. Experiments on MOSI and MOSEI show that VisTAE achieves strong out-of-distribution performance, outperforming previous state-of-the-art models by an average accuracy performance over 2.70\%.

records.title: Leveraging Fine-Grained Information and Noise Decoupling for Remote Sensing Change Detection
records.abstract: Change detection aims to identify remote sensing object changes by analyzing data between bitemporal image pairs. Due to the large temporal and spatial span of data collection in change detection image pairs, there is often a significant amount of task-specific and task-agnostic noise. Previous efforts have focused excessively on denoising, which has resulted in a great deal of loss of fine-grained information. In this paper, we revisit the importance of fine-grained features in change detection and propose a series of operations for Fine-grained Information compensation and Noise decOupling (FINO). First, context is utilized to compensate for fine-grained information in feature space. Next, a shape-aware and a brightness-aware module are designed to improve the capacity for representation learning. The shape-aware module guides the backbone for more precise shape estimation. It guides the backbone network in extracting shape features of change objects. The brightness-aware module learns an overall brightness estimation to improve the model's robustness to task-agnostic noise. Finally, a task-specific noise decoupling structure is designed to improve the model's ability to separate noise interference from feature similarity. With these training schemes, our proposed method achieves new state-of-the-art (SOTA) results in multiple change detection benchmarks. The code is available at https://github.com/Kane-Du/fino-cd.git.

records.title: Learning to Disentangle and Restore: Dual Frequency Decoupling for Image Deraining
records.abstract: Image deraining aims to remove rain streaks from degraded images. It is a challenging task in the spatial domain because the streaks are intricately entangled with diverse background textures. Though frequency-domain methods have shown promise for image deraining by exploiting spectral characteristics, they suffer from two critical limitations, \ie deteriorated frequency decoupling capability in dense rain regions and lack of adaptive mechanisms for diverse rain characteristics. To address these challenges, we propose a novel dual frequency decoupling network (DFDNet) that combines wavelet and Fourier transforms for rain-background disentanglement. Specifically, our method introduces a high-frequency aware spatial mix module (HASM) that integrates wavelet decomposition’s spatial-frequency localization with the Receptance Weighted Key Value (RWKV) architecture for efficient long-range dependency modeling. In addition, we propose a mixture of spatial-frequency experts module (MSFE) that dynamically balances spatial and frequency domain pathways. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms the existing approaches.

records.title: Noise-Resistant 3D Drone Trajectory Estimation via Acoustic Mode Decomposition
records.abstract: The rapid proliferation of low-altitude aircraft, particularly Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and drones, has intensified concerns regarding public safety and privacy, underscoring the urgent need for effective tracking solutions. While traditional detection systems rely on bulky and expensive multi-sensor arrays, acoustic-based methods offer a cost-effective alternative but often struggle in noisy environments. To address this, we introduce a novel framework for precise 3D UAV trajectory estimation using acoustic signals. A key innovation of our approach is the integration of Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD), which effectively isolates drone-specific characteristic frequencies from complex background noise. This process significantly enhances spectral feature quality before feeding into our architecture. We employ a dual-branch Mamba network to process temporal and enhanced spectral features, fusing them via residual cross-attention. Validation on MMAUD benchmarks confirms that our method not only achieves state-of-the-art accuracy but also demonstrates superior robustness in noisy environments compared to existing solutions.

records.title: Motion Semantics Guided Normalizing Flow for Privacy-Preserving Video Anomaly Detection
records.abstract: As embodied perception systems increasingly bridge digital and physical realms in interactive multimedia applications, the need for privacy-preserving approaches to understand human activities in physical environments has become paramount. Video anomaly detection is a critical task in such embodied multimedia systems for intelligent surveillance and forensic analysis. Skeleton-based approaches have emerged as a privacy-preserving alternative that processes physical world information through abstract human pose representations while discarding sensitive visual attributes such as identity and facial features. However, existing skeleton-based methods predominantly model continuous motion trajectories in a monolithic manner, failing to capture the hierarchical nature of human activities composed of discrete semantic primitives and fine-grained kinematic details, which leads to reduced discriminability when anomalies manifest at different abstraction levels. In this regard, we propose Motion Semantics Guided Normalizing Flow (MSG-Flow) that decomposes skeleton-based VAD into hierarchical motion semantics modeling. It employs vector quantized variational auto-encoder to discretize continuous motion into interpretable primitives, an autoregressive Transformer to model semantic-level temporal dependencies, and a conditional normalizing flow to capture detail-level pose variations. Extensive experiments on benchmarks (HR-ShanghaiTech & HR-UBnormal) demonstrate that MSG-Flow achieves state-of-the-art performance with 88.1% and 75.8% AUC respectively.

records.title: Leveraging Historical Interactions with Graph-Infused Attention for Object Interaction Anticipation
records.abstract: Short-term object interaction anticipation is a fundamental capability for proactive human-centric systems, requiring the joint prediction of future action categories, object locations, and time-to-contact from egocentric video. Existing methods are often limited by short temporal windows, overlooking the historical behavioral trajectories that define human intent. To address this, we propose Historical INteraction Transformer (HINT) to explicitly model historical interactions as a structured spatiotemporal graph. Our framework employs a dual-branch architecture that integrates local spatial-temporal features with a global interaction history. Central to our method is the Graph-Infused Attention (GIA) mechanism, which adaptively fuses global sequential dependencies with graph-guided relational cues to capture complex semantic and temporal dependencies across the interaction chain. Extensive experiments on Ego4D v1 and v2 benchmarks demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple metrics. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of our historical interaction modeling and Graph-Infused Attention.

records.title: PANDORA: Pixel-wise Attention Dissolution and Latent Guidance for Zero-Shot Object Removal
records.abstract: Removing objects from natural images is challenging due to difficulty of synthesizing semantically coherent content while preserving background integrity. Existing methods often rely on fine-tuning, prompt engineering, or inference-time optimization, yet still suffer from texture inconsistency, rigid artifacts, weak foreground–background disentanglement, and poor scalability for multi-object removal. We propose a novel zero-shot object removal framework, namely PANDORA, that operates directly on pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models, requiring no fine-tuning, prompts, or optimization. We propose Pixel-wise Attention Dissolution to remove object by nullifying the most correlated attention keys for masked pixels, effectively eliminating the object from self-attention flow and allowing background context to dominate reconstruction. We further introduce Localized Attentional Disentanglement Guidance to steer denoising toward latent manifolds favorable to clean object removal. Together, these components enable precise, non-rigid, prompt-free, and scalable multi-object erasure in a single pass. Experiments demonstrate superior visual fidelity and semantic plausibility compared to state-of-the-art methods. The project page is available at https://vdkhoi20.github.io/PANDORA.

records.title: DRaMI: Dialogue Relation-aware Multi-task with In-context Learning for Emotion Recognition in Multi-party Conversations
records.abstract: As an emerging research topic, the emotion recognition in multi-party conversations (ERMC) task garners significant attention from researchers. However, due to the unstructured nature and complicated emotional interactions among speakers within the entangled multi-party dialogues, the ERMC task presents substantial challenges. To tackle this issue, we propose a novel framework, called Dialogue Relation-aware Multi-task with In-context learning (DRaMI). Specifically, a transformer-based discourse parser is designed to extract links and the corresponding relation types between the Elementary Discourse Units (EDUs). With the extracted relations, dialogue discourse parsing task instruction-following data is constructed for instruction fine-tuning the Large Language Model (LLM) as the pre-trained model. Additionally, an efficient in-context learning (ICL) mechanism is applied to stably retrieve highly relevant examples across dual dimensions. Empirical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed DRaMI.

records.title: DUAL: Dual-modal Unified Adaptation for Label noise
records.abstract: Fine-tuning Vision-Language Models (VLMs) like CLIP on noisy datasets suffers from significant performance degradation. Traditional Learning with Noisy Labels (LNL) methods, limited by their single-modal nature, often fall into confirmation bias and fail to distinguish hard clean samples from noise due to reliance on self-generated supervision. To address this, we propose \textbf{D}ual-modal \textbf{U}nified \textbf{A}daptation for \textbf{L}abel noise (\textbf{DUAL}), a framework that leverages CLIP's dual-modal priors to calibrate the training process. DUAL integrates two key mechanisms: \textbf{C}umulative \textbf{N}eighbor \textbf{D}iscrepancy (\textbf{CND}), which exploits spatiotemporal geometric consistency to accurately identify hard samples, and \textbf{I}mage-\textbf{T}ext \textbf{R}elabeling (\textbf{ITR}), which utilizes frozen textual prototypes as invariant anchors to correct labels and break the confirmation bias loop. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world noisy datasets demonstrate that DUAL achieves state-of-the-art performance.

records.title: SenSE: Semantic-Aware High-Fidelity Universal Speech Enhancement
records.abstract: Generative Universal Speech Enhancement (USE) methods aim to leverage generative models to improve speech quality under various types of distortions. However, existing generative speech enhancement methods often suffer from semantic inconsistency in the generated outputs. Therefore, we propose SenSE, a novel two-stage generative universal speech enhancement framework, by modeling semantic priors with a language model, the flow-matching-based speech enhancement process is guided to generate semantically faithful speech, thereby effectively improving context fidelity. In addition, we introduce a dual-path masked conditioning training strategy that enables flow-matching-based enhancement to flexibly integrate multi-source conditioning signals from degraded speech, semantic tokens, and reference speech, thereby improving model flexibility and adaptability. Experimental results demonstrate that SenSE achieves state-of-the-art performance among generative speech enhancement models and exhibits a high performance ceiling, particularly under challenging distortion conditions. records.title: SVO-BiDeform: Structured Semantic Memory with Dual-Sampling for Dense Video Captioning
records.abstract: Dense video captioning aims to temporally localize and describe events in untrimmed videos. Current methods struggle with two critical challenges: capturing fine-grained visual semantics and reducing dependence on large-scale pretraining data. We propose SVO-BiDeform, a retrieval-augmented framework that leverages structured visual Subject-Verb-Object (SVO) prompts as semantic memory. Unlike sentence-level retrieval approaches, our compositional SVO representations enable flexible semantic composition and effective knowledge transfer across diverse video contexts. The framework incorporates a dual-sampling deformable attention mechanism that alternates between standard sampling for global temporal coverage and boundary-aware sampling for precise event localization. Experimental results on ActivityNet Captions and YouCook2 datasets validate the effectiveness of our approach, demonstrating competitive performance in caption generation quality and temporal localization precision without requiring large-scale pretraining data.

records.title: SIFCNet: Semantic–Illumination Fusion with Color Restoration for Low-Light Image Enhancement
records.abstract: Current low-light image enhancement methods still struggle to handle complex illumination, color distortions, and fine details restoration. We propose Semantic–Illumination Fusion with Color Restoration Network (SIFCNet), a low-light image enhancement network that jointly models semantic–illumination interactions and color restoration. SIFCNet adopts a Fusion-Guided Multi-Head Self-Attention (FG-MSA) mechanism, where Discrete Wavelet Transform-based stable low-frequency illumination features are fused with semantic features to build a channel-wise prior that modulates the value branch of attention, enabling brightness enhancement, noise suppression, colors and structure preservation. A Semantic–Color Restoration Module (SCRM) further eliminates color bias via global channel-wise additive offset estimation, while a semantic branch preserves textures and edges. Extensive experiments on seven benchmark datasets demonstrate that SIFCNet achieves superior quantitative results and visual quality, while requiring only 2.52M parameters and 7.27G FLOPs, thereby achieving a robust balance among brightness, structural details, color fidelity, and efficiency. records.title: Variable Responsibility-Based Redirected Walking for Supporting Non-forward Steps
records.abstract: In virtual reality (VR) applications, redirected walking (RDW) technique allows users to freely explore a large virtual world in a limited physical space. Currently, the non-forward steps are introduced into multi-user RDW, which requires RDW methods to deal with a more complex situation. Otherwise, it can result in more resets and lower user immersion for RDW tasks. To address this problem, we propose a variable responsibility-based redirected walking (VAR-RDW) method for supporting non-forward steps, which dynamically adjusts the user’s moving direction based on the relative position and velocity between users and obstacles. Furthermore, we present a novel point strategy based on variable responsibility. This strategy evaluates the user’s risk coefficient and guides the user to the free area. Our experiments demonstrate that our VAR-RDW provides a higher sense of immersion to users by minimizing the total resets, compared with the existing reactive multi-user RDW methods.

records.title: Evaluation Before Generation: A Paradigm for Robust Multimodal Sentiment Analysis with Missing Modalities
records.abstract: The missing-modality problem constitutes a fundamental challenge in multimodal sentiment analysis, critically compromising model accuracy and generalization stability in real-world applications. Current research predominantly enhances model robustness against missing modalities through independent prompt learning and pre-trained models. However, two key limitations persist: (1) the necessity of generating missing modalities lacks rigorous evaluation; (2) the structural dependencies among multimodal prompts and their global coherence remain insufficiently studied. To address these limitations, we propose a Prompt-based Missing Modality Adaptation framework (ProMMA). Specifically, a Missing Modality Evaluator (MME) is embedded at the data input stage to dynamically assess the importance of missing modalities via pretrained models and constructed pseudo-labels, thereby avoiding the generation of low-quality imputed data. Based on this, a Modality-invariant Prompt Disentanglement (MiPD) module disentangles shared prompts into modality-specific private prompts, enhancing data generation quality by capturing intrinsic local prompt correlations. Additionally, the Dynamic Prompt Weighting (DPW) module computes mutual information weights from cross-attention outputs, mitigating interference from missing modalities via adaptive prompt weighting. To propagate global prompt semantics, a Multi-level Prompt Dynamic Connection (MPDC) module integrates shared prompts with self-attention outputs via residual connections, leveraging the global prior of shared prompts to reinforce critical guidance features. Extensive experiments on three public MSA benchmarks (CMU-MOSI, CMU-MOSEI, and CH-SIMS) demonstrate that ProMMA maintains state-of-the-art accuracy and stability across diverse missing-modality scenarios. The code implementation of this work is publicly available on GitHub: https://github.com/rongfei-chen/ProMMA.

records.title: Scene-Aware Policy Optimization for VLA Fine-tuning in Robotic Manipulation
records.abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLA) have emerged as a promising paradigm for embodied AI. However, they often struggle with Out-Of-Distribution (OOD) scenes. While Reinforcement Learning (RL) offers a solution for fine-tuning, algorithms such as Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) often overlook the variance in task difficulty. We propose Scene-Aware PPO (SA-PPO), an RL fine-tuning framework guided by task-aligned multimodal complexity. Specifically, we introduce a Difficulty Head attached to the VLA backbone to decode scene complexity from deep multimodal features. The feedback mechanism of the framework dynamically aligns policy updates with the difficulty of the scene. Experiments on the modified SimplerEnv benchmark demonstrate that SA-PPO significantly outperforms standard PPO and other baselines with faster convergence, achieving a success rate of 96.88%. Our approach also maintains an average success rate of 83.55% outperforming prior methods in 15 diverse OOD scenarios including visual texture shifts, semantic variations, and unseen execution configurations.

records.title: Robust Incremental Learning via Prompt-Guided Expert Mixture
records.abstract: Incremental learning is a critical paradigm in Continual Learning (CL), aiming to adapt multimedia models to new tasks. The major challenge is a specific and more severe form of catastrophic forgetting, exacerbated by the fact that test samples lack explicit task identifiers. This condition makes preserving prior knowledge dramatically more difficult than in task-aware settings. In view of this problem, we propose Mixture of Prompt-Guided Experts (MPGE), a novel incremental learning framework for vision-language models (VLMs). The key novelty of this work lies in its utilization of Cognitive Anchors to guide the training of experts. Specifically, MPGE implements a selective protection mechanism called Memory Refinement to consolidate long-term memory, safeguarding important parameters. Experiments show MPGE attains superior average accuracies of 83.21% and 76.49% on CIFAR100 and iDomainNet benchmarks, which demonstrates the effectiveness of MPGE in adapting to incremental learning with only 1.44M trainable parameters.

records.title: Denoising-Evolution Generation for Pedestrian Trajectory to Balance Controllability and Realism
records.abstract: In this paper, we propose a pedestrian trajectory generation approach balancing controllability and realism in autonomous vehicle simulation testing (CoRe-Traj). Conventional works struggle to achieve this balance. This fails to satisfy precise intent execution and natural movement patterns, making it challenging to construct complex pedestrian-vehicle interaction scenarios in autonomous vehicle simulation testing. To address this issue, CoRe-Traj harmonizes micro-intentions represented by the pose with continuous-time latent evolution. More specifically, we design the fine-grained micro-intention representations to accurately map external control constraints. Additionally, we propose an implicit denoising evolution via neural differential equation, which models continuous condition dynamics in latent space to ensure trajectory realism. Evaluations on the nuScenes dataset demonstrate that CoRe-Traj outperforms previous methods, achieving an average reduction of control error by 8.1% and acceleration deviation by 12.1% across three control tasks. The results of generated pedestrian trajectories demonstrate a remarkable balance between controllability and realism.

records.title: Training-Free Overlap-Aware Compositional Denoising for Multi-Object Image Synthesis
records.abstract: Recent advances in diffusion models have substantially improved high-fidelity image synthesis. To enable precise spatial control, many existing methods incorporate layout-based conditions to guide object placement. However, generating multi-object scenes with correct instance attributes remains challenging, particularly when input conditions share overlapping regions. In this paper, we present a training-free approach that explicitly resolves overlap relationships during the diffusion denoising process. Based on linear denoising latent combination, our methods introduce a volume-rendering-inspired compositional mechanism that fuses intermediate latent generated from separate conditioned denoising process. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method produces semantically coherent scenes with accurate overlap order, outperforming existing approaches on multi-object layout-controlled image synthesis.

records.title: Bridging the Image–Text Gap in Blind Image Quality Assessment: A Comparative Study
records.abstract: Textual reasoning has recently been widely adopted in Blind Image Quality Assessment (BIQA). However, it remains unclear how textual information contributes to quality prediction and to what extent text can represent the score-related image contents. This work addresses these questions from an information-flow perspective by comparing existing BIQA models with three paradigms designed to learn the image–text–score relationship: Chain-of-Thought, Self-Consistency, and Autoencoder. Our experiments show that the score prediction performance of the existing model significantly drops when only textual information is used for prediction. Whereas the Chain-of-Thought paradigm introduces little improvement in BIQA performance, the Self-Consistency paradigm significantly reduces the gap between image- and text-conditioned predictions, narrowing the PLCC/SRCC difference to 0.02/0.03. The Autoencoder-like paradigm is less effective in closing the image–text gap, yet it reveals a direction for further optimization. These findings provide insights into how to improve the textual reasoning for BIQA and high-level vision tasks.

records.title: StructDiffGAN: Structure-Aware Adversarial Fine-Tuning for Real-World Super-Resolution
records.abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) have emerged as the mainstream approach for real-world image super-resolution (Real-ISR) tasks. However, the degraded features of low-resolution (LR) images cause their distributions to deviate from the natural image manifold. Guided solely by the learned generalized natural image prior, DMs generate trajectories toward high-probability regions of the natural image manifold rather than the target high-resolution (HR) manifold. This discrepancy leads to outputs that deviate from the content of HR images. To address this, we fine-tune diffusion models using adversarial training mechanisms to better suit Real-ISR tasks. By imposing adversarial constraints, we guide outputs toward the HR image manifold region to ensure content fidelity. Furthermore, we introduce a structure-aware discriminator to further constrain structural fidelity. It actually achieves a dual constraint of content and structure. The comprehensive experimental results show that our method can output results with higher fidelity.

records.title: LRFINet A Low-Rank Prior Guided Network for SAR RFI Suppression
records.abstract: Radio Frequency Interference (RFI) severely degrades Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imaging quality. Existing suppression methods often struggle with complex non-stationary interference or suffer from limited interpretability. To address this, we propose LRFINet, a physics-prior guided deep unfolding network. Unlike traditional Robust Principal Component Analysis (RPCA) solvers relying on iterative Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), we adopt a concept-wise unfolding strategy. Specifically, we employ a Transformer-based module to capture global low-rank correlations (replacing the nuclear norm), and a Channel Attention mechanism to act as an adaptive sparse proxy (replacing soft-thresholding). This architecture inherits the physical interpretability of matrix decomposition while avoiding the computational burden of explicit SVD. Experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that LRFINet outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both interference suppression and imaging fidelity.

records.title: Not All Noises Are Created Equally: Diffusion Noise Selection and Optimization
records.abstract: Diffusion models have become the dominant generative paradigm, yet the impact of initial noise quality remains under-explored. Existing approaches to noise selection often rely on external evaluators or lack generalization to standard text-to- image tasks. In this paper, we make three contributions. First, we show that generation quality strongly correlates with noise inversion stability, providing a principled metric for assessing initial noise quality. Second, we propose a noise-space optimization method that directly improves inversion stability without requiring extra evaluators or specialized prompts. Finally, ex- tensive experiments demonstrate that our noise selection and optimization methods significantly improve diffusion models such as SDXL and SDXL-Turbo. On DrawBench, our methods achieve human preference winning rates of up to 57% and 72.5% over the baselines, respectively.

records.title: VDNet: Hierarchical ViT-Gate-Denoising Network for Intestinal Polyp Segmentation
records.abstract: Accurate segmentation of intestinal polyps is crucial for early colorectal cancer detection and diagnosis, yet current computer-assisted techniques struggle with fundamental challenges. This task remains technically challenging due to three primary factors: low contrast at polyp boundaries, diverse morphological characteristics, and substantial variation in polyp sizes. To address these limitations, this paper introduces VDNet (Hierarchical ViT-Gate-Denoising Network), a novel architecture that integrates latent feature denoising, bidirectional gating mechanisms, and hierarchical multi-scale processing to systematically overcome these segmentation difficulties. Comprehensive evaluation on three benchmark datasets demonstrates VDNet's superior performance, achieving significant improvements over state-of-the-art approaches across all evaluation metrics. These improvements demonstrate VDNet's potential to enhance clinical decision-making during colonoscopy procedures and contribute to more effective colorectal cancer prevention.

records.title: Self-Adaptive Spectral Alignment Distillation for Weakly-Supervised Low-Light Semantic Segmentation
records.abstract: Weakly-supervised semantic segmentation under low-light conditions aims to achieve pixel-level classification using weakly annotated labels, such as image-level labels. However, such tasks face significant challenges due to the dual burden of degraded visual visibility and inherent limitations of weak supervision. These factors impede the network's ability to extract discriminative features, resulting in incomplete object regions and misclassification. To alleviate these issues, we propose a Self-Adaptive Spectral Alignment Distillation for Weakly-Supervised Low-Light Semantic Segmentation (SpecAlign) method that consists of a Spectral Alignment Distillation (SAD) and a Semantic-guided Adaptive Feature Enhancer (S-AFE) modules. Specifically, SAD disentangles spatial feature representations into frequency components to transfer robust structural and textural knowledge from normal-light features to their low-light counterparts, thereby establishing explicit and semantically rich supervision. To facilitate this process, the S-AFE acts as a learnable pre-processor that adaptively intensifies semantic regions and restores details before distillation. Extensive experimental results validate the effectiveness of our SpecAlign method, which achieves state-of-the-art performance on weakly-supervised semantic segmentation tasks under low-light conditions.

records.title: MSFET: Multi-Scale Fourier-Enhanced Transformer for Joint Image Dehazing and Deblurring
records.abstract: In critical visual scenarios such as autonomous driving and surveillance security, image dehazing tasks are often affected by factors such as high-speed motion of vehicles and targets, leading to combined degradation of haze and motion blur. However, existing methods typically handle image dehazing and deblurring tasks separately, neglecting the composite effect of these two degradation issues, which can easily cause error accumulation. In this paper, we propose a Multi-Scale Fourier-Enhanced Transformer (MSFET) for end-to-end joint processing of image dehazing and deblurring. For dehazing, we design a Dual-Domain Collaborative Filter (DDCF), which removes low-frequency haze components in the frequency domain. For deblurring, we propose a Direction-Guided Cross Attention (DGCA) module to reconstruct high-frequency details. In addition, we introduce a Frequency Feature Gate (FFG) to enable efficient feature interaction between DDCF and DGCA. Extensive experiments on various datasets demonstrate that MSFET significantly outperforms serial combinations of existing dehazing and deblurring models, as well as general-purpose image restoration networks.

records.title: Not All Regions Are Equal: Let Flow Attention on Difficult Region for Image Super-resolution
records.abstract: Rectified Flow demonstrates great potential as a novel generative modeling framework. However, existing methods overlook the reconstruction difficulty differences between flat and textured regions, leading to blurred detail recovery in textured regions while undesirable artifacts in flat regions. In this work, we propose a Difficulty-Aware region modeling with Rectified Flow (DARF) for single image super-resolution. Specifically, we constructs a probability flow field biased towards difficult regions and a difficulty-adaptive trajectory correction strategy is introduced to adaptively refine difficulty estimation, providing more precise control over the flow trajectory. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks show that DARF achieves state-of-the-art performance on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

records.title: FMPP: Flow-Matched Magnitude and Predictive Phase for One-Step Speech Enhancement
records.abstract: Diffusion models have shown great potential for speech enhancement, particularly in handling diverse distortions due to their strong generative capacity. However, compared with predictive models, they suffer from heavy computational overhead caused by multi-step inference, and still lag behind top-tier predictive models in denoising tasks. To bridge the gap between efficiency and quality, we propose FMPP, a one-step framework that combines the efficiency of predictive modeling with the generative power of flow matching. FMPP adopts a dual-branch design: a predictive branch estimates the complex spectra to provide phase information and guidance, while a generative branch employs flow matching to produce the clean magnitude spectrum in a single step. The final enhanced speech is obtained by combining the generated magnitude with the predicted phase. Extensive experiments on a variety of speech denoising benchmarks demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method over state-of-the-art baselines.

records.title: Real-Time Underwater Image Enhancement via Frequency-Guided Dual-Path Attention
records.abstract: Real-time underwater image enhancement (UIE) is crucial for mobile underwater photography and autonomous robotic systems, where practical deployment typically requires low latency and compact models under constrained computational resources. Recent ultra-lightweight CNNs based on structural re-parameterization meet these constraints but operate purely in the spatial domain, ignoring the frequency-sensitive nature of underwater degradation. To address this, we propose a lightweight UIE framework that integrates two key components: a Multi-Branch Reparameterizable Convolution with Fixed DCT Priors (MBRConv-DCT) that injects structured directional frequency priors during training, and a Frequency-Guided Dual-Path Attention (FGDPA) module that fuses spatial and spectral cues via a dual-path design for adaptive feature modulation. Both components are fully compatible with structural re-parameterization: the convolution branch introduces zero additional inference cost after re-parameterization, while the attention module incurs only a minimal computational overhead. Experiments show our model achieves state-of-the-art performance with only 4.23K parameters and 600+ FPS, outperforming much larger methods in both quantitative metrics and visual quality.

records.title: Slope-Guided Mamba and Angular-Refined Transformer for Light Field Super-Resolution
records.abstract: Light Field Super-Resolution (LFSR) necessitates accurate modeling of spatial-angular correlations while preserving intrinsic 4D ray coherence. However, maintaining such high-dimensional consistency remains challenging, primarily due to two inherent limitations in prevailing modeling paradigms. First, spatial and angular dimensions are often modeled in a decoupled manner, restricting early cross-dimensional interaction and leading to geometric inconsistencies. Moreover, although continuous sequence modeling paradigms show promise in representing epipolar structures, their rigid scanning mechanisms fundamentally conflict with epipolar geometry, limiting geometry-aware feature aggregation. To address these challenges, we propose a hybrid light field super-resolution network, termed SMART, which integrates a Slope-Guided Mamba and an Angular-Refined Transformer to effectively overcome these limitations. Specifically, we introduce an angular-modulated spatial module to bridge the decoupling gap, incorporating angular priors to strengthen spatial–angular correlation modeling. To mitigate the scan-geometry mismatch, we propose a manifold-aligned trajectory module that enables geometry-consistent sequence modeling along epipolar structures. Experiments on five benchmarks demonstrate that SMART achieves state-of-the-art performance, surpassing previous methods by 0.42 dB (PSNR) with significantly reduced artifacts.

records.title: FLSG-DR: Fragmented Lesion–Guided Grading for Diabetic Retinopathy
records.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) presents highly fragmented lesions, such as microaneurysms, hemorrhages, hard exudates and soft exudates, which differ fundamentally from the large and continuous abnormalities commonly seen in other medical imaging tasks. However, most existing DR grading methods—including anomaly-location–based approaches and text-guided classification—operate on coarse global or region-level cues, causing critical lesion evidence to be diluted or overwhelmed by irrelevant retinal structures. To address this inherent mismatch, we propose Fragmented Lesion–Guided Grading for Diabetic Retinopathy that explicitly extracts four fine-grained lesion types and incorporates their diagnostic semantics into the grading process. By leveraging fragmented lesion maps and lesion-aware semantic modulation, our method produces more accurate, interpretable, and clinically aligned severity predictions. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate the clear superiority of our approach over state-of-the-art methods.

records.title: MFMamba: Multi Frequency Mamba for Multi-Contrast MRI Super-Resolution
records.abstract: To improve the quality of Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) without increasing acquisition cost, multi-contrast MRI super-resolution (MCSR) is proposed to leverage information from a reference modality to reconstruct an SR image of the target modality. While Mamba performs well in super-resolution, applying it to MCSR faces two challenges: the absence of an explicit mechanism to capture cross-modality interactions, and the fragmentation of spatial context due to sequential scanning. To address these, we propose a Multi Frequency Mamba (MFMamba) method to exploit different types of frequency information. Specifically, to capture cross-modality complementary information, we perform cross-modality scanning in the amplitude domain, where different contrasts exhibit distinctive frequency characteristics. To preserve spatial and semantic structures, we further incorporate an attention module based on wavelet transforms and learnable semantic prompts, enabling effective modeling of multi-scale spatial patterns and high-level semantic information. Experiments on BraTS and fastMRI datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of MFMamba.

records.title: A Real-Time Dynamic Scene Deblurring Approach for Event Cameras
records.abstract: Event-assisted motion deblurring is often hindered by high computational costs and data redundancy when integrating asynchronous event streams with static images. In this paper, we propose DEGNet, an efficient RWKV-based framework employing a ``guide-then-select'' paradigm to prioritize motion-critical information. DEGNet utilizes dual Vision-RWKV encoders for feature extraction, followed by a Dynamic Edge Guidance Module (DEGM) that synthesizes a blur-aware spatial prior. This prior guides an event token selection strategy to filter redundant responses while preserving informative motion boundaries. Finally, a bidirectional RWKV-based module fuses refined tokens with image features to model long-range cross-modal dependencies with linear complexity. Experiments on GoPro and REBlur datasets show that DEGNet achieves state-of-the-art performance with superior inference efficiency, making it highly suitable for real-time deblurring applications.

records.title: FG-SGL: Fine-Grained Semantic Guidance Learning via Motion Process Decomposition for Micro-Gesture Recognition
records.abstract: Micro-gesture recognition (MGR) is challenging due to subtle inter-class variations. Existing methods rely on category- level supervision, which is insufficient for capturing subtle and localized motion differences. Thus, this paper proposes a Fine- Grained Semantic Guidance Learning (FG-SGL) framework that jointly integrates fine-grained and category-level semantics to guide vision–language models in perceiving local MG motions. FG-SA adopts fine-grained semantic cues to guide the learning of local motion features, while CP-A enhances the separability of MG features through category-level semantic guidance. To support fine-grained semantic guidance, this work constructs a fine-grained textual dataset that describes the dynamic process of MGs in four refined semantic dimensions. Furthermore, a Multi- Level Contrastive Optimization strategy is designed to jointly optimize both modules in a coarse-to-fine pattern. Experiments show that FG-SGL achieves competitive performance, validating the effectiveness of fine-grained semantic guidance for MGR.

records.title: FreqLock: Frequency-Locked Latent Diffusion for Unified Perceptual and Task-Driven Restoration
records.abstract: Robust recognition under adverse conditions remains challenging because restoration models optimized for perceptual fidelity can introduce artifacts that harm downstream tasks. While diffusion priors offer powerful generative capability, naively applying diffusion to degraded inputs that retain reliable low-frequency structure may cause over-generation and unstable semantics. We propose FreqLock, a unified framework for perceptual and task-driven image restoration built on a frozen latent diffusion backbone. FreqLock employs a Prototype-conditioned Fidelity Calibrator (PFC) to anchor reliable low-frequency structure via adaptive warm starts, and an Objective-aware Prompt Router (OPR) to steer the frozen backbone toward perceptual quality or recognition utility. Extensive experiments on classification and semantic segmentation demonstrate that FreqLock improves recognition robustness while maintaining strong perceptual quality with efficient sampling.

records.title: Preventing Dataset Misuse in Stable Diffusion for Multi-User Sharing
records.abstract: Text-to-image models, such as Stable Diffusion, have made significant progress in recent years, enabling users to generate realistic images based on existing images and textual descriptions. While this offers great convenience, it also raises concerns regarding copyright infringement. For instance, image creators often sell their works to multiple users, and malicious users may exploit these images to generate similar-style images without authorization. In this paper, we propose an effective protection strategy to address these issues. We analyze the limitations of existing solutions in multi-user sharing scenarios and design a framework to prevent unauthorized image usage in Stable Diffusion. This framework employs a user-specific, region-aware perturbation strategy with the principles of difference, continuity, and coverage. We validate the effectiveness of our method through extensive experiments, demonstrating its ability to protect against dataset misuse, as well as its harmlessness, transferability and robustness.
