records.title: FTAP-Net: Fourier Transform Amplitude Prior for Low-Light Image Enhancement
records.abstract: Low-light image enhancement (LLIE) is important for downstream low-light vision, but models trained on synthetic data often generalize poorly to real scenes because of the synthetic-to-real gap. Based on FTAP, we design a Fast Fourier Amplitude Convolution Module (FFACM) for Low2Normal enhancement and a Syn2Real training strategy based on low-frequency amplitude replacement. Experiments on 9 benchmarks show strong qualitative and quantitative performance, and downstream face anti-spoofing results further verify generalization.

records.title: A Dynamic Prognostic Prediction Method for Colorectal Cancer Liver Metastasis
records.abstract: Colorectal cancer liver metastasis (CRLM) exhibits high postoperative recurrence and pronounced prognostic heterogeneity, challenging individualized management. Existing prognostic approaches often rely on static representations from a single postoperative snapshot, and fail to jointly capture tumor spatial distribution, longitudinal disease dynamics, and multimodal clinical information, limiting predictive accuracy. We propose DyPro, a deep learning framework that infers postoperative latent trajectories via residual dynamic evolution. Starting from an initial patient representation, DyPro generates a 12-step sequence of trajectory snapshots through autoregressive residual updates and integrates them to predict recurrence and survival outcomes. On the MSKCC CRLM dataset, DyPro achieves strong discrimination under repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation, reaching a C-index of 0.755 for OS and 0.714 for DFS, with OS AUC@1y of 0.920 and OS IBS of 0.143. DyPro provides quantitative risk cues to support adjuvant therapy planning and follow-up scheduling.

records.title: Decoupling Semantics from Distortions: Multi-Scale Two-Stream Vision-Language Alignment for AI-Generated Image Quality Assessment
records.abstract: Existing vision-language model (VLM)-based AI-generated image quality assessment (AIGIQA) methods suffer from a fundamental \emph{semantic-distortion dimensional conflict}: monolithic representations optimized for semantic discrimination inherently entangle compositional understanding with low-level perceptual sensitivity, rendering them blind to fine-grained quality degradations. We introduce MST-CLIPIQA, a multi-scale two-stream framework that achieves hierarchical vision-language alignment through explicit representational decoupling. Our architecture leverages dual CLIP encoders with complementary patch granularities—coarse-grained streams capture global semantic coherence while fine-grained streams preserve textural signatures and artifact patterns. An information bottleneck-inspired gated fusion mechanism performs adaptive cross-scale distillation, with optional cross-attention enabling prompt-anchored correspondence evaluation when generation prompts are available. Extensive experiments across five benchmarks establish new state-of-the-art results, achieving average improvements of 1.11\% SRCC on quality and 2.35\% SRCC on text-image correspondence prediction, while maintaining efficiency with only $\sim$0.8M trainable parameters. Our project is available at \url{https://github.com/YMlinfeng/MST-CLIPIQA}.

records.title: Phy-ViT: Physics-Informed Vision Transformer for Non-Natural Spatio-Temporal Prediction
records.abstract: Forecasting multivariate geospatial environmental fields can be formulated as a non-natural video prediction problem, where each frame corresponds to a multi-channel physical field rather than a natural image. Unlike natural videos, such data exhibit weak visual texture, strong geospatial heterogeneity, cross-variable physical coupling, and long-range temporal dependencies. In this paper, we propose Phy-ViT, a physics-informed Vision Transformer for multivariate wind field forecasting. Given historical wind speed, wind direction, pressure, and temperature fields, Phy-ViT first converts wind observations into horizontal vector components and encodes local geospatial patches with a Physics-aware Patch Embedding (PaPE) module. It then improves cross-variable representation learning via Cross-modal Contrastive Alignment (CMCA) and models long-range dynamics with a Spatio-Temporal Memory Bottleneck (ST-MB). In addition, we introduce a physics-informed loss on the predicted wind vector field to encourage spatially coherent and physically plausible forecasts. Experiments on the NREL wind dataset show that Phy-ViT achieves stronger long-horizon performance than competitive baselines and consistently improves MSE and SMAPE across all evaluated horizons.

records.title: EGTM: Event-guided Efficient Video Turbulence Mitigation for Static Scene Restoration
records.abstract: Video turbulence mitigation (TM) aims to restore clean frames degraded by atmospheric turbulence. Existing state-of-the-art (SOTA) TM methods adopt high-capacity networks to disentangle turbulence cues between frames for lucky temporal fusion. Event cameras offer an alternative solution by capturing microsecond-level, turbulence-induced fluctuations explicitly, leading to (i) an event-lucky insight that showcases positive correlations between turbulence events and distortions. However, the non-stationary event noise hinders the exploitation of this insight for hand-craft lucky-imaging. We therefore (ii) propose a learnable event-guided lucky-imaging model, EGTM, that simultaneously filters noisy events and learns spatiotemporal turbulence-free guidance for reliable temporal fusion. Furthermore, to facilitate the research, we (iii) collect a real-world even-RGB turbulence dataset through a hybrid imaging system under controlled, static turbulence environment, on which our EGTM achieves SOTA performance with orders-of-magnitude gains in efficiency, establishing event-based sensing as a novel paradigm for lucky-imaging. Code and dataset will be released if accepted.

records.title: SGLCT: A Learnable Spectrum-Gated Linear Canonical Transform for Signal Recognition
records.abstract: Deep learning has become a powerful paradigm for wireless signal recognition, yet most existing architectures overlook the structured time–frequency behavior of signal waveforms and rely on fixed filters or generic attention mechanisms, limiting robustness under low SNR and complex channel impairments. This work proposes SGLCT, a Spectrum-Gated, learnable front-end that integrates a multi-branch Linear Canonical Transform (LCT) with a lightweight spectrum-gated enhancement module. By jointly learning LCT parameters and selectively amplifying informative spectral components, SGLCT produces adaptive and physically interpretable time–frequency representations. When inserted before diverse backbone networks, SGLCT consistently improves accuracy across RML-series datasets, particularly in low-SNR regimes, while incurring only modest computational overhead. These results establish SGLCT as a compact, generalizable, and noise-resilient front-end for robust signal recognition.

records.title: Low-Frame-Rate Speech Coding with Regularized Codebook Remapping and Dual-Branch Timbre Decoupling
records.abstract: Low-frame-rate neural speech codecs are crucial for efficient audio transmission and storage in resource-constrained multimedia applications. However, reducing frame rates typically leads to codebook underutilization and severe degradation in both time-frequency details and timbral fidelity. To defy this trade-off, we propose LFS-Codec, a streaming low-frame-rate speech codec enhanced by two orthogonal mechanisms. First, we introduce Parametric Linear Codebook Remapping (PLCR), which projects the codebook into a regularized embedding space with dynamic unfreezing strategies to maximize codebook utilization and refine semantic distillation. Second, we propose Dual-Branch Timbre Decoupling (DBTD), employing complementary timbre extractors and encoder-level feature subtraction to effectively disentangle content from speaker characteristics. Extensive experiments on LibriTTS and AISHELL-3 demonstrate that LFS-Codec achieves superior reconstruction quality, intelligibility, and speaker similarity at ultralow frame rates (12.5~fps) while maintaining low computational complexity (84 GMACs), significantly outperforming well-established baselines. The code is publicly available at: https://github.com/cqchen5/LFS-Codec.

records.title: Low-Complexity Vertex Optimization for G-PCC Trisoup Geometry Compression
records.abstract: The first generation of the Geometry-based Point Cloud Compression (G-PCC) standard, released in 2023, relies primarily on octree coding for geometry. While robust, octree representations become inefficient for dense, surface-like structures. To address this, ISO/IEC MPEG is developing the next-generation G-PCC standard that incorporates the Triangle Soup (TriSoup) coding tool, which models surface geometry using a collection of triangular patches. However, the TriSoup reconstruction operates on an edge-wise basis that often conflicts with local geometric fidelity, leading to inconsistent surface approximations. In this paper, we propose a node-wise distortion-driven vertex optimization framework. Guided by a theoretical analysis of the reconstruction error, we derive a low-complexity criterion based on local volumetric occupancy to selectively filter unsuitable edge vertices and merge redundant corner vertices. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves an average coding gain of 9.6% with negligible impact on runtime complexity. Notably, the core normative aspects of this method have been adopted into the ongoing MPEG G-PCC standardization.

records.title: Formalizing Heterogeneous Interaction Modeling for Multi-Agent Debate in Visual Geo-Localization
records.abstract: Visual geo-localization requires complex reasoning to infer image locations without GPS metadata. Traditional retrieval methods are limited by database quality while Large Vision Language Models often struggle with diverse scenes. Although existing multi-agent systems improve collaboration, they treat interactions uniformly and lack effective conflict resolution. We propose GraphGeo, a multi-agent debate framework based on heterogeneous graph neural networks for visual geo-localization. The framework models diverse debate relationships through typed edges and separates supportive collaboration, competitive argumentation and knowledge transfer. We introduce a dual-level debate mechanism combining node-level refinement and edge-level argumentation modeling. A cross-level topology refinement strategy enables co-evolution between graph structure and agent representations. Experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate GraphGeo outperforms single model and multi-agent baselines. The framework converts cognitive conflicts between agents into higher geo-localization accuracy through structured debate.

records.title: Multi-Stage Deformable Disentanglement and Scene-Joint Attention for Multi-View Pedestrian Detection
records.abstract: Multi-view pedestrian detection effectively addresses occlusion issues in single-view systems. However, existing methods focus primarily on mitigating projection distortions and optimizing fusion weights, lacking systematic disentanglement of task-related features. We propose MDSA, a task-driven framework integrating multi-stage deformable disentanglement and scene-joint attention. The Deformable Disentanglement Module (DDM) dynamically separates task-related features using channel-spatial dual-path attention, guided by a dual constraint loss through adversarial optimization. The Scene-Joint Attention (SJA) module generates geometry-free fusion weights by hierarchically modeling intra-view channel importance and inter-view semantic discrepancies, eliminating reliance on fixed camera configurations. Extensive experiments on WildTrack and MultiviewX demonstrate that MDSA achieves state-of-the-art performance, with plug-and-play generalizability across diverse scenarios.

records.title: ShadowFlow: Ambient-Light Driven Multi-View Optical Flow Sensing for Device-Free Localization
records.abstract: Camera-based tracking is widely used for embodied interaction and indoor navigation, but it raises privacy concerns and often fails under challenging illumination. This paper introduces \textit{ShadowFlow}, a multimedia sensing framework that leverages naturally occurring shadow dynamics under ambient indoor illumination for device-free localization of human users and embodied agents. Unlike conventional visible light positioning systems that require modulated emitters or structured light, ShadowFlow treats unmodulated illumination as a non-intrusive multi-view temporal signal and interprets the resulting spatiotemporal shadow variations as a low-resolution optical-flow field. We design a multi-view recurrent fusion network that extracts shadow-flow features and attention-enhanced temporal representations from wall and ceiling mounted photodiode (PD) arrays. A grayscale reconstruction module converts sparse PD readings into a differentiable brightness field, enabling an optical-flow estimator to capture subtle motion cues. The fused representation is then processed by a cross-scale attention mechanism and a recurrent decoder to infer continuous 2D position trajectories. We further outline a generalized PD deployment strategy that adapts to heterogeneous indoor geometries and illumination patterns, enabling scalable shadow-based sensing without explicit light-source calibration. Experiments over 927 minutes of recordings with 7 subjects in two room layouts show that ShadowFlow achieves a mean localization error of 2.35~cm while supporting real-time inference. These results demonstrate that ambient-light shadow flow is a viable privacy-preserving media signal for embodied localization and interaction, providing a camera-free alternative to traditional multimedia tracking systems.

records.title: Non-Depersonalized Dynamics Disentanglement for EEG Cross-Subject Emotion Recognition
records.abstract: Given the significant individual differences in electroencephalogram (EEG) signals related to emotion representation, cross-subject emotion recognition has garnered extensive attention. However, many existing cross-subject studies adopt depersonalized domain adaptation methods, leading to a deficiency of individualized emotion information. Moreover, subject distribution alignment eliminates distinguishing features, making the representation have less discriminative information in emotion classification. To address these issues, we propose a non-depersonalized disentanglement and reorganization (NDDR) framework for EEG emotion recognition. First, a subject-invariant feature disentanglement module dynamically separates representations into subject internally-invariant and mutually-invariant features, enabling targeted optimization of each component. Second, a feature reorganization module performs subject joint distribution alignment to maximize invariant information while improving generalization and emotion discrimination. Additionally, a spectral–spatial bi-attention module integrates spectral and spatial cues for bidirectional EEG representation extraction. Experiments on SEED and SEED-IV show that NDDR consistently outperforms recent state-of-the-art approaches in cross-subject emotion recognition.

records.title: AGAT-Seg: Anatomical Graph-Guided Anchor Attention for Two-Pass 3D Medical Image Segmentation
records.abstract: Accurate 3D medical image segmentation remains challenging for small organs, thin vessels, and lesions with weak contrast, where appearance-only models often miss targets or yield fragmented boundaries. We present AGAT-Seg, a lightweight two-pass refinement framework built on nnU-NetV2 that injects explicit anatomical structure via a calibrated anatomical graph and anchor-guided attention. Offline, a frozen large language model queried only with the task label list produces a sparse anatomical prior, which is calibrated with training-split spatial statistics to construct a task graph, partition labels into coherent subsets, and select one reliable anchor per subset. Online, Pass-1 generates a coarse prediction and Pass-2 refines difficult regions using graph-constrained attention expansion and attention-gated focus enhancement. Experiments report average DSC on AMOS22, MSD-Pancreas, and MSD-HepaticVessel and show consistent gains, especially on small and boundary-ambiguous structures.

records.title: Foundation Model Guided Uncertainty Weighting for Cross-Domain Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
records.abstract: Semi-supervised learning offers an effective solution to annotation scarcity for medical image segmentation, yet its performance deteriorates severely under multi-center domain shift. Distribution discrepancies amplify pseudo-label noise, causing existing confidence-based pseudo-label selection strategies to misinterpret high-confidence errors as reliable supervision. To address this challenge, we propose a Foundation-Model-guided Uncertainty-Adaptive Segmentation framework (FM-UAS). Specifically, we devise Uncertainty-Adaptive Weighting (UAW), which jointly models aleatoric uncertainty and two forms of epistemic uncertainty, captured through feature-level and output-level discrepancies between the teacher model and a domain-general foundation model. Furthermore, we introduce Structured Occlusion Mixing (SOM) to construct structurally challenging perturbations, further enhancing representation robustness under distribution shift. Extensive experiments on multi-center benchmarks demonstrate that FM-UAS consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods while incurring no additional inference overhead.

records.title: BiMoE: Brain-Inspired Experts for EEG-Dominant Affective State Recognition
records.abstract: Multimodal Sentiment Analysis (MSA) that integrates Electroencephalogram (EEG) with peripheral physiological signals (PPS) is crucial for the development of brain-computer interface (BCI) systems. However, existing methods encounter three major challenges: (1) overlooking the region-specific characteristics of affective processing by treating EEG signals as homogeneous; (2) treating EEG as a black-box input, which lacks interpretability into neural representations; (3) ineffective fusion of EEG features with complementary PPS features. To overcome these issues, we propose BiMoE, a novel brain-inspired mixture of experts framework. BiMoE partitions EEG signals in a brain-topology-aware manner, with each expert utilizing a dual-stream encoder to extract local and global spatiotemporal features. A dedicated expert handles PPS using multi-scale large-kernel convolutions. All experts are dynamically fused through adaptive routing and a joint loss function. Evaluated under strict subject-independent settings, BiMoE consistently surpasses state-of-the-art baselines across various affective dimensions. On the DEAP and DREAMER datasets, it yields average accuracy improvements of 0.87% to 5.19% in multimodal sentiment classification. The code is available at: https://github.com/HongyuZhu-s/BiMoE.

records.title: Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation with Graph Relation Consistency Regularization
records.abstract: Semi-supervised medical image segmentation seeks to leverage unlabeled data to alleviate the heavy reliance on costly expert annotations. Current approaches primarily draw supervisory signals from holistic features, failing to capture the fine-grained structural clues. In this paper, we propose MIS- GRCR, a novel semi-supervised segmentation method with graph relation consistency regularization. MIS-GRCR introduces a tri- branch supervision design that couples image-level, feature-level, and graph-level constraints. In addition to the perturbation holistic features, it builds relation graphs from perturbed latent space to calculate their structural consistency, yielding meaning ful supervisory information. More importantly, we design Node Loss and an Edge Loss to better enforce the coherence across the two relation graphs. Extensive experiments conducted on two challenging benchmarks, i.e., ACDC and ISIC, consistently demonstrate the superiority of MIS-GRCR on medical image segmentation over other state-of-the-art methods.

records.title: Chain Detail Retaining Network with Structured RetNet Modeling for Brain MRI Segmentation
records.abstract: Accurate MRI brain tumor segmentation is vital for clinical diagnosis but remains hampered by the progressive loss of fine structural details during hierarchical encoding. While existing CNN- and Transformer-based methods enhance semantic representation and global context modeling, they commonly rely on non-selective skip connections, resulting in unstable propagation of shallow anatomical cues and compromised delineation of thin boundaries and small lesions. To address this limitation, we propose CDR-Net, a lightweight segmentation framework that explicitly models detail consistency across encoder stages. CDR-Net introduces a chain-style detail propagation mechanism to stabilize structural information during downsampling, combined with a Feature Detail Filter that selectively extracts structurally informative regions. In addition, we incorporate a Swin-Cross Windowed RetNet module to provide efficient, direction-aware local–global modeling with linear computational complexity, without disrupting fine-grained structures. Experiments on the BraTS 2019 and BraTS 2023 benchmarks demonstrate that CDR-Net consistently improves boundary accuracy and small-lesion delineation while maintaining competitive segmentation performance and low computational cost.

records.title: MedDiff-FM: A Diffusion-based Foundation Model for Versatile Medical Image Applications
records.abstract: Diffusion models have achieved significant success in both natural and medical image domains. Previous medical studies typically focus on specific anatomies, applications, and limited datasets, resulting in isolated diffusion models. This paper introduces MedDiff-FM, a diffusion-based foundation model to address a broad spectrum of medical image tasks. MedDiff-FM leverages large-scale 3D CT images covering anatomical regions from head to abdomen to pre-train a diffusion foundation model and explore its capabilities across diverse application scenarios. MedDiff-FM performs multi-level integrated image processing, utilizes position embedding to establish multi-level spatial relationships, and incorporates region classes and anatomical structures to capture anatomical features. MedDiff-FM seamlessly handles several downstream tasks, including image denoising, anomaly detection, and image synthesis. MedDiff-FM is also capable of performing super-resolution, lesion generation, and lesion inpainting by rapidly fine-tuning. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of MedDiff-FM in addressing diverse medical tasks. The code will be released at https://github.com/YuriYu12/MedDiff-FM.

records.title: CoDiff: Towards Reliable Pseudo-Labels via Collaborative Difference Learning for Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
records.abstract: Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation offers a promising solution for the challenge of limited annotated data. While methods like Bidirectional Copy-Paste (BCP) have shown progress, they still face unreliable pseudo-labels generated by the Mean-Teacher framework, which propagate errors and impair model performance. To overcome this, we propose \textit{CoDiff}, an innovative framework that leverages collaborative difference learning to combat unreliable pseudo-labels. It embeds the same unlabeled image into different labeled contexts, thereby enforcing consistency regularization across two collaborative models. The core of CoDiff lies in its direct assessment of pseudo-label reliability at the feature level, which allows models to selectively assimilate knowledge from their counterparts, prioritizing learning from high-confidence regions and ultimately enhancing segmentation performance and robustness. Experiments on the LA, Pancreas-NIH, and ACDC datasets demonstrate that CoDiff consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in DSC and even surpasses fully supervised baselines on 3D datasets, highlighting its effectiveness and practical applicability in low-annotation regimes. The source code will be made publicly available upon acceptance.

records.title: Reversible Face Anonymization with Key-Controlled Latent Fusion
records.abstract: Face anonymization aims to protect users' biometric privacy while retaining the utility of face data in real applications. The key challenge is to provide strong anonymity without losing the ability to authenticate users or to trace misuse when necessary. In this paper, we propose Key-controlled Latent Fusion (KLF), a normalizing-flow-based framework that generates AIRE-Faces (Anonymized, Identifiable and REversible Faces). Each user is assigned a user-specific key, and KLF maps the original face to a consistent anonymized identity in a virtual space. The resulting AIRE-Faces are visually and statistically different from the original faces, can be directly recognized by standard face recognizers for authentication in the anonymized identity space, and still allow accurate reconstruction of the original faces when the key is available. KLF is built upon an invertible image--latent transformer and a key-conditioned latent fusion module, and is trained with a multi-task objective that jointly encourages anonymity, identifiability, reversibility and diversity. Experiments show that KLF achieves high protection rates, strong anonymized identity consistency and perfect reconstruction fidelity compared with advanced anonymization approaches, while maintaining high face detection rates and competitive visual quality.

records.title: Unified Face Attack Detection via Fine-Grained Semantic Guidance
records.abstract: The growing applications of facial recognition systems are accompanied by increasingly diverse security threats. Existing datasets lack detailed textual descriptions of forgery cues, leading most prior methods to treat face attack detection primarily as a visual recognition task. In this paper, building upon the large-scale MS-UFAD dataset which contains over 8 million attack images, we enrich each image with a fine-grained textual description of forgery cues. Furthermore, we propose a Dual Alignment Forgery Network(DAF-Net) to better leverage these textual information. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach extracts more generalizable and semantically meaningful forgery representations from attack images, outperforming both vision-only methods and approaches based on coarse-grained descriptions.

records.title: A Lightweight Multiscale Graph Convolutional Network for Robust Skeleton-based Abnormal Gait Recognition
records.abstract: Abnormal gait recognition is critical for early diagnosis and monitoring in clinical and home settings. Many skeleton-based methods require substantial computation and remain insensitive to subtle pathological motions, which limits real-time deployment on resource-constrained devices. This paper presents a lightweight multiscale graph convolutional network(LGMS-AGCN) for abnormal gait recognition. First, LGMS-AGCN integrates depthwise and group-based graph convolutions to reduce parameters and FLOPs. Second, a low-rank adaptive adjacency refinement module perturbs the physical skeleton graph to emphasize informative joint relationships with negligible cost. Third, a hybrid attention module focuses on discriminative joints and feature channels, while a lightweight multiscale temporal convolution branch models both local irregular steps and longer gait cycles, improving robustness to noise, missing joints, and frame drops. Experiments on a self-collected abnormal gait dataset and a public pathological gait benchmark show that LGMS-AGCN achieves higher accuracy and robustness than prior methods under lower computational budgets.

records.title: MV-RVE: Rayleigh-Constrained Multi-View Learning for Inter-VAE Feature Relationships
records.abstract: Multi-view learning aims to extract unified, discriminative features from complementary view-specific data by leveraging multi-source information. However, existing VAE-based methods overlook the intrinsic relationship between consistent and view-specific latent features, relying on indirect statistical constraints lacking explicit probabilistic characterization of feature spatial distributions—this severely limits the precision and robustness of consistent feature learning. To address this gap, we propose MV-RVE, a novel multi-view framework integrating three coupled innovations: a Rayleigh-constrained variational encoding mechanism that models latent features’ relative spatial relationship via Rayleigh-distributed posterior and prior distributions to impose explicit probabilistic clustering constraints; an Uncertainty-Aware Mixture of Experts (UMoE) module that calibrates view-specific uncertainty to ensure robust cross-view fusion, which is essential for Rayleigh-based modeling; and a cosine-scheduled curriculum learning strategy that dynamically balances consistency and view-specific loss weights to boost training stability and feature generalizability. Extensive experiments on four benchmarks demonstrate MV-RVE outperforms state-of-the-art methods in clustering and classification tasks.

records.title: From Detection to Correction: A Shadow-aware Illumination Consistency Framework for Medical Shadow Removal
records.abstract: Shadows cast by surgical instruments in vitreoretinal procedures obscure anatomy and hinder analysis. Existing natural image methods often fail due to complex illumination and structural similarities. We propose a two-stage detection-to-correction framework that unifies shadow localization and structural restoration. Our Shadow-aware Illumination Consistency Network (SICNet) integrates shadow-aware illumination calibration and edge-enhancement modules. A detection-guided strategy adapts LaMa to produce anatomically coherent, shadow-free results. We also construct the Fundus Instrument-Shadow Dataset, spanning animal, human, and external domains. Experiments demonstrate superior detection accuracy, strong cross-domain generalization, and clinically reliable shadow removal. Code is available at https://github.com/tkllndxn/shadow-remove.

records.title: Social Media Rumor Detection via Quantum Hybrid Neural Networks in Ball-Shaped Space
records.abstract: Multimodal rumor detection on social media faces two challenges: fragile semantic integrity caused by fragmentation of the event content, and performance bottleneck resulting from the loss of spatial relations between features during multimodal fusion. To address these, this paper proposes BLRQ-BV, a multimodal rumor detection framework based on quantum hybrid neural networks. The framework takes a rumor event as a sample, extracting quantum features via our Low-Discriminative-Information-Loss Quantum Hybrid Network, capturing sequential features using BiLSTM, extracting visual features with ResNet-18. These features are scaled, modulated, and then fused through the proposed Vector Composition of Ball‑Shaped Space method for final identification. Experiments demonstrate that BLRQ-BV achieves an average accuracy of 97.74%, outperforming state-of-the-art results by an average margin of 3.56%. This study offers an efficient rumor-detection solution and a quantum-fusion pathway.

records.title: LCM-UNet: A Laplacian frequency decoupling based hybrid state space model for medical image segmentation
records.abstract: Medical image segmentation requires capturing the global context while preserving fine boundaries and local textures. However, state space models often underrepresent boundary details and high-frequency cues. To address this, we propose a Laplacian frequency decoupling based network, named LCM-UNet. The method first decomposes the feature maps into complementary high- and low-frequency components. The multiscale depthwise convolution module (MSDC) then processes the high-frequency stream to model long range context, while the selective scan module (SS2D) refines the low-frequency stream to recover edges and textures. This enables parallel processing that maintains global consistency while preserving local details. Experiments are conducted on the Synapse, ISIC 2018 and ACDC datasets. The results show that LCM-UNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods while maintaining a low parameter count and FLOPs.

records.title: EmoFace: Emotion-Content Disentangled Speech-Driven 3D Talking Face Animation
records.abstract: The creation of increasingly vivid 3D talking face has become a hot topic in recent years. Currently, most speech-driven works focus on lip synchronisation but neglect to effectively capture the correlations between emotions and facial motions. To address this problem, we propose a two-stream network called EmoFace, which consists of an emotion branch and a content branch. EmoFace employs a novel Mesh Attention mechanism to analyse and fuse the emotion features and content features. Particularly, a newly designed spatio-temporal graph-based convolution, SpiralConv3D, is used in Mesh Attention to learn potential temporal and spatial feature dependencies between mesh vertices. In addition, to the best of our knowledge, it is the first time to introduce a new self-growing training scheme to dynamically adjust the ratio of groundtruth adopted in the 3D face animation task. Comprehensive quantitative and qualitative evaluations on our high-quality 3D emotional facial animation dataset, 3D-RAVDESS ($4.8863\times 10^{-5}$mm for LVE and $0.9509\times 10^{-5}$mm for EVE), together with the public dataset VOCASET ($2.8669\times 10^{-5}$mm for LVE and $0.4664\times 10^{-5}$mm for EVE), demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance.

records.title: Hemisphere-based Local Feature Fusion from Multimodal Imaging for Interpretable AD Diagnosis
records.abstract: Structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) and positron emission tomography (PET), as the most commonly used imaging modalities for clinical diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), provide structural and functional information of the brain, respectively. However, multimodal methods still face challenges in AD prediction due to pronounced inter-individual heterogeneity and subtle pathological changes in the imaging manifestations. To address this issue, this work proposed an end-to-end deep learning framework based on the neuroanatomical characteristics of bilateral brain symmetry and the asymmetric distribution of AD pathology. First, brain images are divided into 3D regional patches according to the left and right hemispheres, and the features are encoded via patch CNNs. Subsequently, multi-head attentions are employed to optimize the representation of these local features among brain patch regions in each of the hemispheres. Finally, we developed a Hemisphere-aware Cross Transformer that performs hierarchical feature fusion at both intermodal and interhemispheric levels. Compared to several deep learning models, our proposed network achieved significant improvements in both AD diagnosis and early AD prediction on the ADNI dataset. More importantly, our approach achieves a breakthrough in interpretability, providing critical insights for the exploration of AD patterns in multimodal brain imaging.

records.title: MP-Human: Multi-Prior Co-Optimization for Consistent Text-to-4D Human Generation
records.abstract: Generating high-quality dynamic 3D humans from text requires simultaneously modeling natural temporal motion and strict multi-view geometric consistency, a balance that remains challenging for existing methods. We propose MP-Human, a dual-stream co-optimization framework for text-driven 3D human animation that bridges implicit diffusion-based synthesis with explicit SMPL-X 3D priors to address this challenge. MP-Human combines the expressive capacity of diffusion models for detailed appearance and motion generation with the structural robustness of the SMPL-X parametric body model, enabling coherent human synthesis across time and viewpoints. At its core, a Pose-Constrained Motion Driving (PCMD) mechanism leverages SMPL-X 3D keypoints to spatiotemporally guide diffusion-based generation, synchronizing motion and appearance while enforcing geometric consistency without sacrificing motion diversity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MP-Human effectively reduces multi-view inconsistencies and Janus artifacts, producing high-fidelity, naturally animated, and fully animatable 3D mesh sequences. These results highlight the effectiveness and robustness of MP-Human for text-driven dynamic 3D human generation in interactive virtual environments.

records.title: VA-FastNavi-MARL: Real-Time Robot Control with Multimedia-Driven Meta-Reinforcement Learning
records.abstract: Interpreting dynamic, heterogeneous multimedia commands with real-time responsiveness is critical for Human-Robot Interaction. We present VA-FastNavi-MARL, a framework that aligns asynchronous audio-visual inputs into a unified latent representation. By treating diverse instructions as a distribution of navigable goals via Meta-Reinforcement Learning, our method enables rapid adaptation to unseen directives with negligible inference overhead. Unlike approaches bottlenecked by heavy sensory processing, our modality-agnostic stream ensures seamless, low-latency control. Validation on a multi-arm workspace confirms that VA-FastNavi-MARL significantly outperforms baselines in sample efficiency and maintains robust, real-time execution even under noisy multimedia streams.

records.title: SingingBot: An Avatar-Driven System for Robotic Face Singing Performance
records.abstract: Equipping robotic faces with singing capabilities is crucial for empathetic Human-Robot Interaction. However, existing robotic face driving research primarily focuses on conversations or mimicking static expressions, struggling to meet the high demands for continuous emotional expression and coherence in singing. To address this, we propose a novel avatar-driven framework for appealing robotic singing. We first leverage portrait video generation models embedded with extensive human priors to synthesize vivid singing avatars, providing reliable expression and emotion guidance. Subsequently, these facial features are transferred to the robot via semantic-oriented mapping functions that span a wide expression space. Furthermore, to quantitatively evaluate the emotional richness of robotic singing, we propose the Emotion Dynamic Range metric to measure the emotional breadth within the Valence-Arousal space, revealing that a broad emotional spectrum is crucial for appealing performances. Comprehensive experiments prove that our method achieves rich emotional expressions while maintaining lip-audio synchronization, significantly outperforming existing approaches.

records.title: Integrating Fine-Grained Audio-Visual Evidence for Robust Multimodal Emotion Reasoning
records.abstract: Multimodal emotion analysis is shifting from static classification to generative reasoning. Beyond simple label prediction, robust affective reasoning must synthesize fine-grained signals such as facial micro-expressions and prosodic which shifts to decode the latent causality within complex social contexts. However, current Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) face significant limitations in fine-grained perception, primarily due to data scarcity and insufficient cross-modal fusion. As a result, these models often exhibit unimodal dominance which leads to hallucinations in complex multimodal interactions, particularly when visual and acoustic cues are subtle, ambiguous, or even contradictory (e.g., in sarcasm scenery). To address this, we introduce SABER-LLM, a framework designed for robust multimodal reasoning. First, we construct SABER, a large-scale emotion reasoning dataset comprising 600K video clips, annotated with a novel six-dimensional schema that jointly captures audiovisual cues and causal logic. Second, we propose the structured evidence decomposition paradigm, which enforces a “perceive-then-reason” separation between evidence extraction and reasoning to alleviate unimodal dominance. The ability to perceive complex scenes is further reinforced by consistency-aware direct preference optimization, which explicitly encourages alignment among modalities under ambiguous or conflicting perceptual conditions. Experiments on EMER, EmoBench-M, and SABER-Test demonstrate that SABER-LLM significantly outperforms open-source baselines and achieves robustness competitive with closed-source models in decoding complex emotional dynamics. The dataset and model are available at \url{https://anonymous.4open.science/status/SABER-LLM-F3F1}.

records.title: Lightweight Gaze Correction via Synthetic Portrait Supervision and Temporal Fine-Tuning
records.abstract: Eye contact plays a vital role in human communication, yet it is often lost in video conferencing due to camera placement. While existing gaze redirection methods have shown promising results, they are typically too large or computationally intensive for real-time use on mobile devices. In this work, we propose MobileGazeFixer, a lightweight gaze redirection network designed for efficient deployment on mobile platforms. Our model integrates latent rotation transformation, progressive dense warping, and a spatial masked attention module to achieve high-quality gaze redirection. To address the lack of high-quality, pixel-aligned gaze datasets, we leverage the generative prior of a foundational portrait animation model to synthesize paired training data with varying gaze directions. Furthermore, we introduce a temporal finetuning strategy that exploits the inherent continuity in video sequences to improve temporal consistency in live video applications. Extensive experiments show that MobileGazeFixer keeps quantization performance close to the floating-point version while the inference costs 2.4 ms per frame on a Snapdragon 8 Elite with INT8 runtime.

records.title: Diffused Optimal Transport for Faithful Face Anti-Spoofing
records.abstract: In this paper, we propose a diffused optimal transport (DOT) for faithful anti-spoofing. Most methods primarily focus on attack generalization while overlooking slight attack biases in the frequency domain, which causes significant performance variations, particularly when dealing with textureless attacks. To address these issues, we treat different attack types as varying frequency degradations and reformulate the face anti-spoofing task into a super-resolution problem to assess the restoration quality. Our DOT framework integrates optimal transport (OT) theory with a diffusion model to iteratively recover unbiased bona fides from degraded attack samples. Specifically, OT first aligns varying attack distributions with genuine frequency distributions in the latent space of the diffusion process, mitigating spoof patterns through minimal-cost transport paths. A diffusion-based super-resolution network then reconstructs high-frequency details from unbiased features, ensuring the reliability of reconstruction. Ultimately, the frequency bias between the input face and the constructed “real” face can be treated as a faithful cue for the spoof feature learning. To this end, we conduct extensive experiments on four commonly used datasets to validate DOT. The experimental results demonstrate that DOT outperforms state-of-the-art competitors, showcasing the effectiveness of our method.

records.title: OT-MED: OT-Aligned Modality-Specific Emotion Dictionaries for Multimodal Emotion Recognition
records.abstract: Human emotions span linguistic, acoustic, and visual modalities, making multimodal signals vital for conversational emotion recognition. However, existing models emphasize feature extraction and fusion but overlook the semantic modeling of category representations, limiting their discriminative power. Moreover, instance-level alignment in existing methods captures only local interactions, limiting the modeling of global semantic consistency of categories across modalities. To address these limitations, we introduce a framework that integrates modality-specific Category Feature Dictionaries (CFDs) with an optimal transport (OT)–based alignment strategy. For each modality, a dedicated CFD is constructed to store discriminative, emotion-specific representations. To further enhance the diversity and semantic separability of these dictionary features, we incorporate a Rényi entropy–based regularization term. Furthermore, we design a cross-modal class-level alignment mechanism that leverages OT to structurally align category representations across modalities. Extensive experiments on IEMOCAP and MELD datasets demonstrate the superiority of our method.

records.title: TAMISeg: Text-Aligned Multi-scale Medical Image Segmentation with Semantic Encoder Distillation
records.abstract: Medical image segmentation remains challenging due to limited fine-grained annotations, complex anatomical structures, and image degradation from noise, low contrast, or illumination variation. We propose TAMISeg, a text-guided segmentation framework that incorporates clinical language prompts and semantic distillation as auxiliary semantic cues to enhance visual understanding and reduce reliance on pixel-level fine-grained annotations. TAMISeg integrates three core components: a consistency-aware encoder pretrained with strong perturbations for robust feature extraction, a semantic encoder distillation module with supervision from a frozen DINOv3 teacher to enhance semantic discriminability, and a scale-adaptive decoder that segments anatomical structures across different spatial scales. Experiments on the Kvasir-SEG, MosMedData+, and QaTa-COV19 datasets demonstrate that TAMISeg consistently outperforms existing uni-modal and multi-modal methods in both qualitative and quantitative evaluations. Code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/qczggaoqiang/TAMISeg.

records.title: P³-SAM: SAM with Perceptual Parallel Prompt for Few-Shot Strip Steel Surface Defect Segmentation
records.abstract: Few-shot semantic segmentation (FSS) of strip steel surface defects (S³D) has posed significant challenges distinct from natural scenes. Unlike natural images, S³D task exhibits unique characteristics including low local contrast, uneven illumination, and complex fine-grained texture patterns. Although recent methods based on Segment Anything Model (SAM) have shown promise in FSS on natural images by leveraging SAM's powerful pre-trained representations, these unique industrial characteristics of S³D images lead to performance drop when directly applying SAM to industrial defect scenarios. In this paper, we propose a novel Perceptual Parallel Prompt (P³) framework that empowers SAM, creating the P³-SAM model to address these challenges through two core strategies. First, we develop a Perceptual-Optimized Encoding (POE) strategy that enhances local contrast and preserves critical texture details for S³D segmentation. Second, we introduce the Parallel Prompt Generator (PPG) strategy that simultaneously generates both semantic and spatial prompts, enabling comprehensive guidance for SAM's decoder while maintaining robustness to feature variations. Extensive experiments on three few-shot S³D benchmarks demonstrate that P³-SAM achieves state-of-the-art performance, with particularly notable improvements of 12.00% in mIoU on Surface Defects-4i dataset.

records.title: FedPAF: Personalized Federated Learning via Prototype Alignment and Adaptive Fusion
records.abstract: Personalized federated learning (PFL) addresses statistical heterogeneity by learning client-specific models. Recent PFL methods leverage prototypes as semantic supervision for local training. However, under statistical heterogeneity, both prototype construction and utilization remain challenging: local prototypes learned in heterogeneous feature spaces exhibit semantic inconsistency, leading to semantically unstable global prototype construction, while relying solely on global prototypes fails to provide client-specific semantic supervision tied to local data distributions. In this paper, we propose FedPAF, a PFL method that improves prototype construction and utilization through projection-based prototype alignment and reliability-aware adaptive prototype fusion. FedPAF aligns heterogeneous local prototypes through a projection operator to enforce cross-client semantic consistency and stabilize global prototypes. It further adaptively integrates global and local prototypes based on behavioral and geometric reliability to mitigate feature-space mismatch, thereby combining shared and client-specific semantics for personalized training. Extensive experiments confirm that FedPAF achieves superior performance compared with state-of-the-art PFL methods.

records.title: LLM-Assisted Individual-Aware Modeling with Local–Global Graph Networks for Multimodal Emotion Recognition
records.abstract: Multimodal Emotion Recognition in Conversation (MERC) requires effective modeling of speaker-specific characteristics to improve generalization. Existing methods typically rely on discrete demographic attributes (e.g., gender, age, personality) integrated through multi-task learning or auxiliary information injection, which fail to construct nuanced individual representations. While recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) show potential inference ability for individual-aware emotion recognition, they are computationally prohibitive and data-hungry. To these ends, we propose LILG-MER, a framework that efficiently leverages LLM capabilities for individual modeling while maintaining computational tractability. GPT-4V generates behavioral profiles for the target speaker as compact individual-specific priors. A Local-Global Graph Network integrates these profiles with conversational context and cross-modal dependencies. To be robust toward inferior quality in LLM-generated descriptions, we introduce a hierarchical decision fusion strategy that enforces label-oriented feature alignment across modalities. Experiments on IEMOCAP, MELD, and EmoryNLP confirm LILG-MER outperforms baselines, capturing individual differences without overhead of full MLLM retraining.

records.title: Spectral-Spatial Orthogonal Decoupling for Unsupervised 3D Medical Image Registration
records.abstract: Accurate deformable registration of brain images is pivotal for neuroanalysis and clinical diagnosis. However, existing deep learning-based models often exhibit spectral bias, an inherent tendency to prioritize low-frequency global structures while neglecting high-frequency components, resulting in registered images with blurred anatomical boundaries and compromised local alignment. To address this issue, we propose the Spectral-Spatial Orthogonal Decoupling Network (S2OD-Net), a novel registration paradigm that harmonizes macroscopic alignment with fine-grained detail preservation. In S2OD-Nett, we employ a Convolution-Fourier Self-Attention (CFSA) module to explicitly model long-range topological dependencies in the spectral domain. Additionally, along with the global modeling, a Locality-Sensitive Convolution (LSConv3D) is supplemented to capture high-frequency edge features by injecting a priori constraints via 3D differential operators. S2OD-Net achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on IXI, LPBA40, and OASIS datasets, with Dice scores of 73.1%, 75.8% and 82.1%, respectively. Moreover, it maintains superior structural integrity with negligible topological folding. These results demonstrate the competitiveness and clinical potential of S2OD-Net. The code is available at https://github.com/tianzizan/SOD-Net.

records.title: Evaluating and Improving Explanation Coherence for Multimodal Emotion Recognition
records.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) achieve strong performance in Multimodal Emotion Recognition (MER), yet accurate predictions alone do not guarantee genuine emotional understanding. Explainable MER (EMER) extends MER by requiring natural language explanations, but such explanations are often redundant or inconsistent with predicted emotions, revealing deficiencies in emotional reasoning coherence. A key challenge is that coherence remains poorly defined and difficult to optimize systematically. In this work, we propose the Fine-Grained Coherence Evaluator (FG-CE), which operationalizes explanation coherence as a measurable and optimizable signal. FG-CE decomposes explanations into sentence-level units and identifies their functional role, modality grounding, and emotional consistency, producing interpretable coherence scores. Building upon FG-CE, we introduce Coherence-Aware EMER (CA-EMER), a unified optimization framework that integrates FG-CE into reinforcement learning and evaluator-guided rejection sampling, enabling coherence-aware self-improvement without additional human annotations. Experiments demonstrate that CA-EMER improves emotional explanation coherence while preserving emotion recognition performance and generalization.

records.title: Structure-enhanced Multimodal Medical Concept Quantization for Medication Recommendation
records.abstract: Multimodal medication recommendation leverages diverse medical concepts in Electronic Health Records (EHRs), modeling patient health conditions to support treatment decision-making. However, most existing approaches assign each medical concept an independent continuous embedding, resulting in limited parameter and memory efficiency. Although recent advances in vector quantization are promising for medical concept representation learning, semantic-only quantization often fails to distinguish clinically distinct concepts with similar textual descriptions, leading to code collision. To this end, we propose SCQMed, a structure-enhanced multimodal medical concept quantization framework that integrates complementary structural information from medical knowledge graphs. By learning compact and clinically discriminative quantized representations, SCQMed enables effective aggregation of multimodal patient longitudinal histories for medication recommendation. Experiments on two real-world EHR datasets show that SCQMed significantly improves medication recommendation effectiveness while reducing memory overhead and alleviating code collision.

records.title: CIMD: Cognitive Inspired Multi-perspective Descriptions for EEG-Image Alignment
records.abstract: Retrieving images from electroencephalogram (EEG) signals is crucial for advancing brain-computer interfaces (BCIs). Existing methods often use frozen pre-trained visual encoders to align EEG space with a generic visual space. However, such alignment fails to fully capture EEG-specific structure and the difficulty of bridging the modality gap between abstract EEG and visual stimuli. To address these challenges, we propose Cognitive Inspired Multi-perspective Descriptions (CIMD) for fine-grained alignment. Specifically, we first design the Cognitive-guided Multi-perspective Descriptions (CMD), which exploits EEG-related cognitive characteristics to construct global, color, and emotion questions, using a large multimodal model to generate cognition-inspired textual descriptions that act as semantic bridges and guide alignment between EEG and image. Second, to further achieve fine-grained alignment, we propose the Cognitive-driven Multimodal Alignment (CMA), which leverages these descriptions to fine-tune a large pre-trained model and construct a shared embedding space that unifies EEG, image, and text features. Finally, to preserve generalization while enhancing adaptability to cross-subject variability, we introduce a regularization strategy that constrains excessive drift during fine-tuning. Extensive experiments on the Things-EEG dataset demonstrate that CIMD achieves state-of-the-art performance on the challenging 200-way zero-shot retrieval task.

records.title: Early Prediction of Cybersickness from EEG in Immersive VR
records.abstract: Cybersickness remains a major obstacle to the widespread adoption of virtual reality (VR). While current mitigation strategies rely on real-time detection, these methods typically identify symptoms only after onset, leaving limited room for effective intervention. To address this, we introduce an early prediction framework based on electroencephalography (EEG) that forecasts symptom emergence given a short history of neural activity. Using a public dataset with continuous ratings, we propose, to the best of our knowledge, the first EEG-based formulation explicitly targeting early prediction in this domain. Furthermore, to overcome data scarcity, we benchmark the first application of EEG foundation models to cybersickness against strong task-specific architectures. Our experiments confirm that EEG signals contain precursor cues for future cybersickness and demonstrate that foundation models yield significantly more accurate and robust early predictors, highlighting their potential as generalizable backbones for proactive VR safety systems.

records.title: Modeling Emotion Hierarchy with Hyperbolic CLIP for Basic-Compound Facial Expression Recognition
records.abstract: In real-world scenarios, facial expressions often occur in basic and compound forms, and jointly recognizing them provides a comprehensive understanding of human emotions. However, intricate relations between basic emotions and their derived compound emotions lead to large inter-class similarity. To disentangle basic and compound emotions, we model emotion categories as a hierarchy and embed it in hyperbolic space, which is well-suited for hierarchical structures. First, we construct the emotion hierarchy based on the geometric properties of hyperbolic space. Second, we adapt contrastive language-image pretraining (CLIP) to hyperbolic space using a hyperbolic contrastive objective to implicitly capture hierarchical relationships. Third, we propose hierarchical-aware deep prompting to explicitly learn class-specific textual descriptors under the supervision of the emotion hierarchy. A two-stage training strategy is adopted for stable learning of visual and textual features. Extensive experiments on both in-the-lab and in-the-wild datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of our method.

records.title: PortraVec: Image-Based Portrait Vectorization with Text-Guided Manipulation
records.abstract: While portrait sketch generation is a special task in sketch synthesis, most existing methods are pixel-based, limiting their interpretability and editability. With the rise of vector generation techniques, representing sketches using vector elements may provide more flexible manipulation. However, due to the overlapping nature of vector graphics and the coarse detail modeling, existing vectorization methods struggle to capture facial integrity and fine-grained details, and lack semantic control. To address these issues, we propose PortraVec, a framework for converting pixel-based portrait images into vector sketches with text control. Specifically, we propose a two-stage image-guided generation module using Attention-aware Offset Sampling to capture face structure while correcting detail deviations, and a text-guided manipulation module based on Region-based Parameter Freezing to enable local semantic editing while maintaining global consistency. Experiments show that PortraVec achieves superior structural consistency, visual fidelity, and semantic controllability compared to state-of-the-art methods.

records.title: Uncertainty-Driven Adaptive Consistency Learning for Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
records.abstract: Semi-supervised medical image segmentation methods often neglect that uncertainty differs across anatomical structures, limiting their ability to learn from low-contrast or ambiguous regions. We propose Uncertainty-Driven Adaptive Consistency Learning (UACL), which integrates uncertainty into both supervised and unsupervised training. For labeled data, we propose an Uncertainty Representation Learner that explicitly captures prediction uncertainty and dynamically reweights the supervised loss, allowing the model to concentrate learning on structurally ambiguous or challenging regions. For unlabeled data, we introduce a Disagreement-Aware Consistency module that detects uncertain regions by measuring prediction disparities between two strongly augmented views. The model reinforces learning in these disagreement regions through additional consistency regularization. Experiments on the LA and ACDC datasets show that UACL outperforms representative baseline methods, particularly under low-label conditions, demonstrating the effectiveness of explicitly leveraging uncertainty.

records.title: Reliable Expert Collaboration under Structural Shifts for Multi-Source Domain Generalization in Medical Image Segmentation
records.abstract: Multi-source domain generalization is crucial for medical image segmentation in real-world clinical scenarios. Achieving strong performance in multi-source domain generalization requires effectively addressing distribution shifts across data from different sources. Owing to the ability of different expert networks to specialize in distinct data distributions and to be adaptively combined through gating mechanisms, Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) approaches demonstrate strong capabilities in handling domain shifts in multi-source domain generalization tasks. However, existing MoE methods often depend on fixed spatial priors and treat expert predictions as equally reliable, limiting effective expert collaboration under structural shifts in multi-source domain generalization. To address these limitations, we propose a novel Mixture-of-Experts framework with Dynamic Structural Attention and Hierarchical Gating Calibration (SCMoE). The framework consists of a dynamic structural attention mechanism (DSA) and a hierarchical gating calibration mechanism (HGC). The DSA enhances expert models' adaptability to structural shifts by adaptively modeling domain-specific spatial structures, while the HGC improves fusion stability through uncertainty-aware expert-level calibration and spatial–channel attention–based pixel-level calibration. Extensive experiments on the Fundus and Prostate datasets demonstrate the strong performance of SCMoE.

records.title: Behavior-driven Hypergraph Modeling for Accurate Cyberbullying Detection in Social Media
records.abstract: With the widespread adoption of social media and the growing complexity of online interactions, cyberbullying has increasingly exhibited characteristics such as group involvement, concealment, and coordinated behaviors. Most existing approaches model interactions by using linear sequences or binary graphs, which primarily capture simple local relationships but struggle to mimic multi-user coordinated attacks effectively. Moreover, these methods fail to model the relationship among group behaviors that naturally emerge during the evolution of cyberbullying. To address these challenges, we propose a Behavior-driven Hypergraph Model for Cyberbullying Detection (BeHM), which parses cyberbullying behaviors within media sessions at two complementary levels: coordinated interactions at the micro-level, and their relations at the macro-level. Then, BeHM adopts a three-stage framework to capture the features at the micro and macro levels. Experiments on two public sessionbased social media datasets demonstrate that BeHM consistently outperforms baselines, achieving an F1-score with improvements of up to 1.3% on Instagram and 2.8% on Vine, and validating its effectiveness in modeling complex group attacks and relationships among group behaviors.

records.title: Affect-OmniGPT: Synergizing Global-Local Visuals and Semantic Cues for Robust Emotion Recognition and Reasoning
records.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) facilitate open-ended emotion analysis but face two limitations: visual granularity mismatches, where holistic frames miss micro-expressions while face-only crops neglect context; and reasoning errors caused by subtitle reliance during non-verbal contradictions (e.g., sarcasm). To address these, we propose Affect-OmniGPT. This framework introduces a Multi-Expert Architecture with a Dual Visual Stream to process global frames and cropped facial sequences in parallel. Additionally, a Semantic-Enhanced Text Module augments lexical captions with Action Units estimated by OpenFace and acoustic tone descriptions produced by Qwen2-Audio. Evaluations on MER-UniBench, covering Sentiment Analysis, Basic Emotion Recognition, and Open-Vocabulary Emotion Recognition, demonstrate the method's effectiveness. Affect-OmniGPT achieves a state-of-the-art overall MER-UniBench score of 83.64 under the official evaluation protocol, outperforming the strongest baseline by 3.66 points. Code is available at https://github.com/ouyangjutian/Affect-OmniGPT.

records.title: Unrolling Graph-based Douglas-Rachford Algorithm for Image Interpolation with Informed Initialization
records.abstract: Conventional deep neural nets (DNNs) initialize network parameters at random and then optimize each one via stochastic gradient descent (SGD), resulting in substantial risk of poor-performing local minima. Focusing on image interpolation and leveraging a recent theorem that maps a (pseudo-)linear interpolator Θ to a directed graph filter that is a solution to a corresponding MAP problem with a graph shift variation (GSV) prior, we first initialize a directed graph adjacency matrix A given a known interpolator Θ, establishing a baseline performance. Then, towards further gain, we learn perturbation matrices P and P^(2) from data to augment A, whose restoration effects are implemented progressively via Douglas-Rachford (DR) iterations, which we unroll into a lightweight and interpretable neural net. Experiments on different image interpolation scenarios demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, while drastically reducing network parameters and inference complexity.

records.title: S2ED: From Story to Executable Descriptions for Consistency-Aware Story Illustration
records.abstract: Multi-frame story illustration requires long-horizon coherence beyond single-image text-to-image generation, including narrative decomposition and persistent character identity, layout, and affect across frames. We propose Story-to-Executable Descriptions (S2ED), a training-free, model-agnostic, prompt-layer framework that converts a full story into a sequence of explicit, editable executable descriptions for more consistent rendering. S2ED coordinates three agents to segment the narrative, ground canonical character attributes, and enrich spatial and affective cues, enabling interpretable prompt-carried state propagation and local edits to repair drift without retraining the generator. Experiments on Flintstones and Shakoo Maku show that S2ED improves sequence-level consistency and character fidelity over strong prompting, large-model planning, and a reference training-based method, under both automatic metrics and human judgments. We also deploy S2ED in an end-to-end story-to-storybook system for children's illustrated stories, with a supplementary video.

records.title: A Multi-Modal Emotion Recognition for Cross-Subject Brain-Computer Interfaces
records.abstract: Multi-modal emotion recognition remains challenging due to limitations in single-feature extraction, insufficient cross-modal fusion, and pronounced inter-subject variability. To address these issues, we propose a novel framework, namely the Multi-Modal Multi-View Neural Network (MMNN-EmotionNet). The proposed approach aims to learn comprehensive multi-view representations, enable effective semantic integration across modalities, and alleviate subject-dependent discrepancies, thereby improving both robustness and generalization performance in MER tasks. Specifically, data augmentation is first applied in the latent space to enhance feature diversity and model stability. Each modality is then decomposed into multiple views at the feature dimension level, where modality-specific encoders are designed to extract and aggregate discriminative affective representations across views. Furthermore, a cross-modal encoding network is introduced to facilitate deep interaction and integration of multi-modal information. To further reduce domain discrepancies, domain adaptation is incorporated to learn domain-invariant representations, projecting heterogeneous data into a unified feature space. Extensive evaluations on benchmark datasets demonstrate that MMNN-EmotionNet consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, highlighting its effectiveness and strong potential for practical Multi-modal emotion recognition applications.

records.title: HOT-Seg: Heterogeneous Orthogonal Triangulation for Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
records.abstract: Prevalent semi-supervised segmentation methods adopt Student-Teacher architectures but frequently suffer from model coupling. From a function space perspective, the fundamental premise is to leverage multiple functions to estimate the target segmentation function. However, constrained by structural homogeneity, these models tend to evolve along similar optimization trajectories, degenerating into collinear relationships that undermine multi-view supervision. To address this, we revisit semi-supervised learning via Function Space Triangulation and propose HOT-Seg. First, by integrating two networks with complementary structural characteristics, we construct a wide-baseline observation system, leveraging their distinct inductive biases for naturally complementary views. Furthermore, we introduce an explicit feature orthogonalization constraint to compel independent observation directions within the feature space. As a result, this mechanism averts homogenization collapse, maintaining a stable triangulation structure. Experiments on standard benchmarks show that HOT-Seg significantly outperforms existing methods, validating the effectiveness of our heterogeneous wide-baseline design and orthogonalization strategy.

records.title: Robust Brain Structure Characterization via Tensor Subspace Learning on Minimal Representative Subset
records.abstract: In high-dimensional neuroimaging, full-set learning often degrades tensor subspace estimation due to noise accumulation and solution deviation. We propose a Minimal Representative Subset Tensor Subspace Learning (MRS-TSL) strategy to investigate brain structure characteristic subspace stability. Our primary contribution is quantifiably demonstrating the high redundancy of dominant structural anatomy. Comprehensive subspace consistency analysis reveals that low-rank bases from approximately 5\% of samples exhibit high geometric alignment with full-cohort solutions. Furthermore, we analyze the optimization landscape, showing that minimal subsets mitigate noise-induced solution shifts inherent in full-set learning. Empirical evaluations on ADNI datasets confirm that this strategy yields robust features and provides a theoretical basis for efficient structural characterization in structured brain data.

records.title: Disambiguating Context for Visual Emotion Understanding via Affective Semantic Fields
records.abstract: Image emotion recognition is fundamentally challenged by the semantic-affective gap, where the semantic sparsity of visual features hinders fine-grained discrimination, and their contextual ambiguity leads to unreliable emotion mapping. To bridge this gap, this work reconceptualizes the task as contextual disambiguation within a structured semantic space. We introduce the Affective Semantic Field (ASF), a novel framework that formally models emotion as an interaction triad of visual stimuli, emotional semantics, and situational context. ASF is instantiated by leveraging Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) as affective diagnosticians, generating pre-disambiguated, high-density semantic descriptions to enrich visual input. Additionally, the Emotion-Prior Guided Attention (EPGA) mechanism is proposed, which innovatively injects structured affective knowledge from psychological lexicons as a differentiable prior into cross-modal fusion. This enables affective priming, shifting the fusion objective from general semantic alignment to emotion-aware affective alignment. To resolve potential conficts between local cues and global narrative, a hierarchical reasoning architecture is devised. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that our framework achieves state-of-the-art performance, with particularly improvements on emotionally ambiguous cases, validating its effectiveness in closing the semantic-affective gap.

records.title: Domain Incremental Learning for EEG Based Multimodal Emotion Recognition
records.abstract: Affective Computing leverages physiological signals like EEG and eye-tracking for multimodal emotion recognition, offering advantages such as anti-spoofing and broad applications in human-computer interaction and mental health. However, cross-subject generalization remains a critical challenge, as models suffer from performance degradation on new subjects due to individual variability and catastrophic forgetting—where fine-tuning erases prior knowledge. To address this, we propose a novel continual learning approach based on Domain-Incremental Learning (DIL). Our algorithm integrates dynamic data replay and knowledge distillation to preserve existing subject knowledge while adapting to new data, alongside a multi-prototype contrastive learning framework that enhances representational plasticity and stability. Experiments on SEED-IV and SEED-V datasets, involving sequential subject additions, demonstrate that our method significantly mitigates catastrophic forgetting and outperforms baseline models. These results validate the algorithm's efficacy in improving cross-subject generalization, highlighting its potential for scalable emotion recognition systems.

records.title: Perceptual Confidence-aware Learning for Digital Human Facial Quality Assessment under Action Topology Constraints
records.abstract: As core entities in the metaverse, digital humans serve as pivotal bridges connecting virtual and real worlds. However, current digital humans remain plagued by facial quality deficiencies, requiring effective digital human facial quality assessment methods to facilitate technological advancement. In this paper, we propose a perceptual confidence-aware digital human facial quality assessment framework under action topology constraints. Specifically, multidimensional asymmetric action unit topology graphs are first constructed for digital human sequences, modeling the temporal continuity of action unit intensity and the inherently directional nature of muscle synergy relationships through bidirectional cross-attention mechanisms. Subsequently, cross-validation information among similar samples is extracted using graph edit distance to construct auxiliary supervision neighbors. Similarity assessment is performed based on action-level topology graph calculations and feature-level multilayer perceptrons, achieving dual-level dynamic correction of supervision signals. Finally, we propose a perceptual confidence-aware learning strategy optimized via gradient descent to achieve adaptive confidence-based quality distribution learning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method is capable of achieving state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance for digital human facial quality assessment.

records.title: Mamba-Enhanced Implicit Motion Learning for Audio-Driven Portrait Animation
records.abstract: Audio-driven human motion video generation aims to synthesize realistic and temporally coherent human animations from a single static image, with applications in talking-head synthesis, co-speech gesture generation, and dynamic presentations. Moving beyond conventional keypoint-based methods that often struggle to capture subtle motion dynamics, We propose a novel implicit-motion framework for generating realistic and temporally coherent human motion videos from a single static image and audio. Our approach uses a two-stage pipeline that decouples motion prediction from rendering. The first stage integrates appearance priors and hierarchical depth cues into a region-aware attention mechanism to model latent motion features. The second stage employs a Mamba-enhanced diffusion model to directly predict these features from audio and the source image, enabling unsupervised learning of fine-grained motion patterns. This decoupled architecture enhances flexibility and efficiency. Trained on a new 380-hour high-quality dataset, our method outperforms prior work across multiple public benchmarks and our collected data in accuracy, naturalness, and temporal coherence, setting a new state-of-the-art.

records.title: PoWM: A Targeted Watermarking Method for Human Portraits
records.abstract: Digital watermarking is crucial for copyright protection, yet existing methods often overlook the unique characteristics of human portraits. These generalized algorithms treat all image regions with equal importance, which may inefficiently embed information in irrelevant backgrounds. To address this, we propose PoWM (Portrait Watermark Model), which leverages the latent space of a pre-trained Stable Diffusion Encoder to embed watermarks into the frequency domain of the representation within a user-defined foreground area. We introduce a two-stage optimization paradigm that incorporates a clamped edge-aware loss and an adaptive pixel-space refinement module to eliminate reconstruction artifacts while preserving fine details. Furthermore, we utilize a boundary-agnostic extraction strategy that decodes message bits from eroded regions to avoid semantically fragile boundaries. Experimental results demonstrate that PoWM significantly outperforms traditional and deep-learning-based baselines, achieving superior robustness against a wide range of attacks while maintaining excellent image fidelity.
