records.title: Enhancing Emotional Support via Context-Aware Multimodal Fusion and User-Centric Alignment
records.abstract: Multimodal Emotional Support Conversation (MESC) systems aim to alleviate user distress. Existing methods emphasize incomplete context modeling and response skillfulness, limiting the ability to capture users' emotional dynamics across turns and modalities, and to generate responses that align with user satisfaction. To address these issues, we propose MUSE, a novel framework that captures cross-turn Multimodal emotional dynamics and leverages User feedback to enhance Support Effectiveness. Specifically, MUSE captures cross-turn multimodal emotional dynamics through Context-Aware Multimodal Fusion (CAMF) by integrating modality-specific temporal representations into a unified turn-level embedding sequence, seamlessly injected into Large Language Models (LLMs). Building upon these emotional representations, we further introduce User-Centric Alignment (UCA) that incorporates explicit user feedback as a Reinforcement Learning (RL) reward to improve subjective support effectiveness. Experiments on the MESC benchmark demonstrate MUSE's effectiveness in fostering more emotionally appropriate and user-aligned responses.

records.title: A VR-Based Public Speaking Training Feedback Mechanism with Dynamic Adaptive Decision-Making and Personality-Oriented Regulation
records.abstract: Public speaking is an important interpersonal skill, yet many people face challenges due to anxiety and insufficient proficiency. Traditional training methods are resource-intensive and hard to organize, which has spurred the development of computer-driven training systems. However, existing training feedback mechanisms often lack effective adaptive strategies, resulting in rigid feedback that fails to provide precise and appropriate guidance and may lead to excessive cognitive load. To address these issues, we propose a public speaking training feedback method that enables dynamic feedback through multimodal data acquisition and processing, and regulates the feedback mechanism in a personality-oriented manner. This method is further implemented in a VR-based public speaking simulation system. An experimental study involving 30 participants demonstrates that the proposed system effectively enhances self-perception and overall public-speaking performance while reducing task load. This system provides an innovative and efficient solution for skill development, with substantial theoretical value and practical significance.

records.title: SAM-Supervised Feature-Level Enhancement for Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
records.abstract: Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation (SSMIS) has emerged as a crucial paradigm for medical image segmentation under annotation scarcity. However, existing semi-supervised segmentation methods suffer from confirmation bias, referring to the accumulation of errors from noisy pseudo-labels produced by the model itself. Recently, some approaches have incorporated the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to alleviate this issue; however, they are predominantly confined to the output level, leaving the rich dense supervisory information in SAM’s intermediate features underexplored. To address this limitation, we propose SAM-Supervised Feature-level Enhancement (SAM-SFE), which leverages SAM as an external supervisor to inject dense, reliable feature-level priors, effectively breaking the closed loop and thereby alleviating confirmation bias. Specifically, we design Local Affinity Distillation (LAD), which distills SAM’s local voxel-wise associations to supervise feature-level representations, thereby improving the geometric fidelity. Furthermore, we develop Tri-Perspective Contrastive Learning (TPCL), which leverages SAM to identify reliable hard negatives, forcing the model to learn more discriminative features. Extensive experiments on the BraTS2019, Pancreas-NIH, and LA datasets demonstrate that our method effectively outperforms state-of-the-art semi-supervised approaches.

records.title: M3R: Localized Rainfall Nowcasting with Meteorology-Informed MultiModal Attention
records.abstract: Accurate and timely rainfall nowcasting is crucial for disaster mitigation and water resource management. Despite recent advances in deep learning, precipitation prediction remains challenging due to limitations in effectively leveraging diverse multimedia data sources. We introduce M3R, a Meteorology-informed MultiModal attention-based architecture for direct Rainfall prediction that synergistically combines visual NEXRAD radar imagery with numerical Personal Weather Station (PWS) measurements, using a comprehensive pipeline for temporal alignment of heterogeneous meteorological data. With specialized multimodal attention mechanisms, M3R novelly leverages weather station time series as queries to selectively attend to spatial radar features, enabling focused extraction of precipitation signatures. Experimental results for three spatial areas of 100 km × 100 km centered at NEXRAD radar stations demonstrate that M3R outperforms existing approaches, achieving substantial improvements in accuracy, efficiency, and precipitation detection capabilities. Our work establishes new benchmarks for multimedia-based precipitation nowcasting and provides practical tools for operational weather prediction systems. The source code is available at https://github.com/Sanjeev97/M3Rain

records.title: TSMamba: Modeling Global Temporal-Spatial Dependencies and Adjacent Brain Interaction for EEG Emotion Recognition
records.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) has garnered significant attention in the field of Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs). However, existing methods often struggle to capture global temporal-spatial patterns and ignore the functional interactions between physically adjacent brain regions. In this paper, we propose TSMamba, a novel Mamba-based temporal-spatial dual-branch network tailored for EEG emotion recognition. Specifically, the temporal branch incorporates bi-directional scanning to enrich the global sequential modeling of EEG signals. For the spatial branch, we explicitly leverage the spatial topological priors of EEG electrodes and introduce a zigzag scanning scheme. This design maximizes the preservation of spatial adjacency during the scanning process, thereby facilitating inter-regional interactions. Moreover, TSMamba can capture global spatial associations through continuous cross-region scanning. Extensive experiments on three public emotion datasets demonstrate that our proposed approach achieves competitive or superior performance compared to state-of-the-art models.

records.title: Investigating Depression-Related Physio-Behavioral Signals in Immersive VR: A Cross-Environment Multimodal Analysis
records.abstract: Virtual Reality (VR) shows potential for mental health assessment, but the effectiveness and cross-environment consistency of depression-related unimodal data (gait, physiolog- ical signals, and speech features) remain largely unexplored in VR settings. This study innovatively evaluates the cross-environment consistency and detection feasibility of gait, physiological, and speech features in depressed patients. We developed an immersive VR platform closely replicating clinical settings and recruited 50 participants (24 depressed patients, 26 healthy controls) to perform identical conversation and walking tasks in both virtual and real environments. Analysis revealed that features collected in VR demonstrated high consistency with the real environment and could effectively distinguish depressed patients from healthy controls. These results confirm the reliability and promising potential of using VR-collected unimodal data for objective auxiliary depression detection.

records.title: ZebraShuffle Consistency Learning for Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
records.abstract: Semi-supervised medical image segmentation is a promising approach to supporting computer-aided clinical applications with limited manual annotations, where image perturbation is an important aspect in consistency learning. Despite convincing results achieved by existing patch-based perturbation methods, they suffer from the problem of discontinuity at edges of each patch along both horizontal and vertical directions. To address this, we propose ZebraShuffle, a novel strip-based perturbation method that partitions images into equal strips horizontally or vertically, which preserves structural continuity along the selected dimension. These strips are randomly shuffled and merged into perturbed images for consistency learning. By randomly alternating partition orientations, the model infers labels from both directions. We further extend ZebraShuffle consistency learning from single unlabeled images to unlabeled-unlabeled and labeled-unlabeled pairs for increased perturbation diversity and learning reliability. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms the state of the arts, with notable gains under extreme label scarcity.

records.title: NTM-CLIP: Natural to Medical CLIP with Dual Semantic Missing Contrastive Learning
records.abstract: Large-scale vision-language models (VLMs) provide powerful visual inference capabilities and present valuable opportunities for medical anomaly detection (AD). However, the complex and ambiguous features of medical images pose significant adaptation challenges. To address this, we propose NTM-CLIP, a method that effectively adapts the semantic generalization of natural VLMs to medical AD by incorporating specific medical knowledge to minimize ambiguity in medical images. Our approach introduces dual semantic missing contrastive learning, which integrates distinct semantic systems for guidance and utilizes both complete and partial semantic representations to reduce ambiguity and enhance fine-grained localization of anomalies. Additionally, we present an adaptive aggregation module that assigns different weights across stages to improve cross-modal feature alignment at various levels of abstraction, facilitating accurate anomaly classification (AC) and segmentation (AS). Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art AD approaches in both few-shot and zero-shot scenarios, showcasing robust generalization across multiple medical imaging modalities. Among these, under the few-shot (shots=4) setting, the AC task showed an average improvement of 14.95\% AUCs compared to CLIP.

records.title: Generalizable Sensor-Based Human Activity Recognition via Seasonal Style Projection and Trend Feature Disentanglement
records.abstract: Human Activity Recognition (HAR) with wearable sensors is widely used in sports, healthcare, and other fields, but its performance is affected by cross-subject distribution shift arising from individual style differences. This distribution shift significantly limits the generalization ability of existing HAR models. To address this challenge, we propose SPTD, a novel framework for generalizable HAR based on seasonal–trend decomposition. Raw sensor signals are decomposed into seasonal and trend components to provide a structured representation for domain-invariant feature learning. On this basis, we introduce two complementary modules: Seasonal Style Projection, which aligns diverse seasonal motion styles across domains, and Trend Feature Disentanglement, which isolates domain-invariant trends from domain-specific low-frequency artifacts. Experiments on three public datasets show that SPTD achieves competitive performance against state-of-the-art methods, with ablation studies validating the contribution of each component.

records.title: Towards Efficient Medical Image Segmentation via Collaborative Feature Enhancement and Inception GroupMamba
records.abstract: Modern healthcare multimedia systems increasinglyrely on robust and efficient medical image segmentation, par-ticularly when large-scale pretrained backbones are expectedto generalize across imaging modalities and clinical institutions.Recent Mamba-based and state-space-based segmenters offerlinear-complexity global modeling, but they often lack effectivemechanisms for selecting and reinforcing task-relevant features inthe presence of ambiguous anatomy and noise. They also struggleto incorporate multi-scale information without compromisinglong-range dependencies. To address these limitations, we proposeCEIGM-UNet, a lightweight U-shaped architecture built ontwo key components: a Collaborative Feature EnhancementLayer (CFEL) and a Modulated Inception Group MambaLayer (MIGML). CFEL enhances and propagates critical featuredistributions during decoding, while MIGML improves multi-scalerefinement and preserves a long-range dominant path throughchannel-wise allocation. On Synapse, CEIGM-UNet achieves aDice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 85.61% and a 95th percentileHausdorff Distance (HD95) of 10.00 mm. On the AutomatedCardiac Diagnosis Challenge (ACDC), it reaches 92.81% DSC and1.05 mm HD95. These results are obtained with fewer parametersand fewer floating-point operations (FLOPs) than competitivebaselines. records.title: Dual-Anchor Reward aware Reinforcement Learning for Medical Report Generation
records.abstract: Recent multimodal large language models have advanced medical report generation, yet practical deployment remains limited by weak visual grounding and the imbalance between image evidence and retrieved text. We propose Dual-Anchor Reward-Aligned Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), a retrieval-augmented framework that jointly optimizes evidence utilization and generation alignment. Our approach integrates CLIP-based retrieval with a Mistral-based generator and introduces a dual-anchor reward to explicitly coordinate image-grounded factuality and reference-guided coherence. Specifically, the Image-grounded Fidelity Reward (IFR) enforces consistency with visual evidence, while the Reference-guided Coherence Reward (RCR) improves clinical narrative quality under retrieved context. Experiments on MIMIC-CXR demonstrate consistent improvements, achieving state-of-the-art performance on METEOR, BLEU-1, BLEU-3, and BLEU-4, while remaining competitive on BLEU-2 and CIDEr.

records.title: DEFTalk: Dynamic Emotion Flow for Speech-Driven 3D Facial Animation
records.abstract: Current speech-driven 3D facial animation methods often assume a single and time-invariant emotion category for input sequences, overlooking natural prosodic fluctuations. This leads to stiff, mechanical expressions and notable distortion when processing sequences containing two distinct emotional states. To address these limitations, we propose DEFTalk, a novel framework designed to model Dynamic Emotion Flow as continuous and time-varying trajectories. Our approach focuses on the Flow-based Dynamic Emotion Embedding (Flow-DEE), with an Emotion Trajectory Predictor (ETP) to adaptively modulate static priors through residual learning for smooth and content-adaptive emotion trajectories. Furthermore, we introduce a dynamic consistency loss based on the Pearson Correlation Coefficient (PCC) to maximize the correlation between facial movement intensity and speech energy amplitude. Our experiments on the MEAD dataset with multiple speakers and diverse dynamic emotional evolutions show that DEFTalk significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in dynamic consistency and emotional realism, while ensuring precise lip-sync accuracy.

records.title: Collaborative Adaptive Curriculum for Progressive Knowledge Distillation
records.abstract: Recent advances in collaborative knowledge distillation have demonstrated cutting-edge performance for resource-constrained distributed multimedia learning scenarios. However, achieving such competitiveness requires addressing a fundamental mismatch: high-dimensional teacher knowledge complexity versus heterogeneous client learning capacities, which currently prohibits deployment in edge-based visual analytics systems. Drawing inspiration from curriculum learning principles, we introduce Federated Adaptive Progressive Distillation (FAPD), a consensus-driven framework that orchestrates adaptive knowledge transfer. FAPD hierarchically decomposes teacher features via PCA-based structuring, extracting principal components ordered by variance contribution to establish a natural visual knowledge hierarchy. Clients progressively receive knowledge of increasing complexity through dimension-adaptive projection matrices. Meanwhile, the server monitors network-wide learning stability by tracking global accuracy fluctuations across a temporal consensus window, advancing curriculum dimensionality only when collective consensus emerges. Consequently, FAPD provably adapts knowledge transfer pace while achieving superior convergence over fixed-complexity approaches. Extensive experiments on three datasets validate FAPD's effectiveness: it attains 3.64% accuracy improvement over FedAvg on CIFAR-10, demonstrates 2x faster convergence, and maintains robust performance under extreme data heterogeneity (α=0.1), outperforming baselines by over 4.5%.

records.title: FLaTEC: Frequency-disentangled Latent Triplanes for Efficient Compression of LiDAR Point Clouds
records.abstract: Point cloud compression methods jointly optimize bitrates and reconstruction distortion. However, balancing compression ratio and reconstruction quality is difficult because low-frequency and high-frequency components contribute differently at the same resolution. To address this, we propose FLaTEC, a frequency-aware compression model that enables high compression of a full scan. We first convert voxelized embeddings into triplane representations to reduce sparsity and storage requirements, and then introduce a frequency-disentangling technique that isolates compact low-frequency components while aggregating multi-scale high-frequency details. The decoupled low-frequency and high-frequency components are stored in binary format. During decoding, full-spectrum signals are progressively recovered via a modulation block. Our method achieves state-of-the-art rate-distortion performance and outperforms the standard codecs by 78\% and 94\% in BD-rate on both SemanticKITTI and Ford datasets. Our codes, models, and results will be released on GitHub.

records.title: LCSD: Real-Time Resource-Bounded Snow-Risk Mapping for Edge Autonomy
records.abstract: Snow-covered roads pose a multimedia perception challenge: onboard cameras face partial observability, low contrast and tight edge compute, while many vision models remain tuned to offline pixel metrics rather than control. We propose LCSD, an end-to-end, edge-native architecture that turns vehicle video streams into an affordance-level snow-risk map for real-time braking and trajectory adjustment. LCSD combines a Multi-Dimensional Perceptual Attention (MDPA) block to fuse directional and frequency cues, a Multi-Core Feature Fusion (MCFF) block to capture cross-scale context via multi-kernel pooling, and an Adaptive Sparse-Density Decoder (ASDD) for dynamic sparsification and adaptive convolution under latency constraints. Beyond pixel accuracy, LCSD outputs per-pixel confidence maps for risk-aware control and supports anytime refinement of high-risk regions. Experiments on diverse winter road datasets show that LCSD matches or surpasses Transformer and YOLO baselines while sustaining real-time performance on edge hardware.

records.title: HDMIBabelfish: Latency-Aware Real-Time Translation of Japanese Role-Playing Games on Edge Devices
records.abstract: Japanese role-playing games (JRPGs) often ship without English localization, leaving on-screen dialogue and menus inaccessible to many players. We present HDMIBabelfish, a real-time subtitle translation system that operates directly on HDMI gameplay streams and runs entirely on edge devices. The pipeline integrates text detection, tracking, OCR, neural machine translation, caching and rendering under a latency-aware multithreaded scheduling heuristic. A custom JRPG dataset is used to fine-tune a YOLOv11-nano detector, while a Marian OPUS model trained on JESC improves chrF by 6% on conversational subtitles. On NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX, the full system sustains 33.5 FPS with 14.9 ms mean latency. Although evaluated on Japanese-to-English JRPGs, the architecture is language-agnostic and preliminary tests on other Latin and CJK RPGs indicate broader applicability. The system is containerised with Docker for deployment on Jetson and PCs, and the full pipeline and models are publicly available as open-source artifacts.

records.title: Edge-Efficient Two-Stream Multimodal Architecture for Non-Intrusive Bathroom Fall Detection
records.abstract: Falls in wet bathroom environments are a major safety risk for seniors living alone. Recent work has shown that mmWave-only, vibration-only, and existing multimodal schemes, such as vibration-triggered radar activation, early feature concatenation, and decision-level score fusion, can support privacy-preserving, non-intrusive fall detection. However, these designs still treat motion and impact as loosely coupled streams, depending on coarse temporal alignment and amplitude thresholds, and do not explicitly encode the causal link between radar-observed collapse and floor impact or address timing drift, object drop confounders, and latency and energy constraints on low-power edge devices. To this end, we propose a two-stream architecture that encodes radar signals with a Motion--Mamba branch for long-range motion patterns and processes floor vibration with an Impact--Griffin branch that emphasizes impact transients and cross-axis coupling. Cross-conditioned fusion uses low-rank bilinear interaction and a Switch--MoE head to align motion and impact tokens and suppress object-drop confounders. The model keeps inference cost suitable for real-time execution on a Raspberry Pi 4B gateway. We construct a bathroom fall detection benchmark dataset with frame-level annotations, comprising more than 3 h of synchronized mmWave radar and triaxial vibration recordings across eight scenarios under running water, together with subject-independent training, validation, and test splits. On the test split, our model attains 96.1% accuracy, 94.8% precision, 88.0% recall, a 91.1% macro F1 score, and an AUC of 0.968. Compared with the strongest baseline, it improves accuracy by 2.0 percentage points and fall recall by 1.3 percentage points, while reducing latency from 35.9 ms to 15.8 ms and lowering energy per 2.56 s window from 14200 mJ to 10750 mJ on the Raspberry Pi 4B gateway.

records.title: Adaptive Prototypical Calibration for Federated Learning on Heterogeneous and Long-tailed Data
records.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training while preserving data privacy, yet it suffers from performance degradation and unfairness under non-IID and long-tailed data from clients, where local models overfit to dominant head classes. To address this important challenge, we propose FedAPC, a novel FL framework that can learn robust and equitable representations from non-IID and long-tailed data. First, we introduce a Reliable Prototype Adaptive Clustering (RPAC) mechanism that constructs client prototypes by using correctly classified samples weighted by prediction confidence, thereby mitigating bias propagation. Next, we employ an efficient Prototype Contrastive Learning (PCL) strategy with a prediction-guided negative prototype selection to enhance feature discriminability without prohibitive cost. To rectify skewed decision boundaries, we design a Bridge sample-based Classifier Calibration (BCC) method that generates diverse pseudo-features for tail classes by fusing features from confusing head-class samples and genuine tail samples. We formulate the aggregation of client models as an optimization problem based on their performance on a balanced prototype set. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets under heterogeneous FL scenarios demonstrate that FedAPC outperforms state-of-the-art methods while exhibiting improved generalization and fairness.

records.title: SAPA-KD: Structure-Aware Parameter Adaptation for Out-of-Distribution Knowledge Distillation
records.abstract: The domain shift between the teacher’s training data and the student’s deployment environment poses a critical challenge for Knowledge Distillation, known as the Out-of-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (OOD-KD) problem. Current OOD-KD methods predominantly align student data to the teacher domain for effective supervision, while overlooking the inherent source bias within the frozen teacher model. To address this, we propose SAPA-KD, a novel model-centric framework designed to explicitly align the teacher toward the student domain. Specifically, we construct an intermediate teacher through selective substructure parameter adaptation to effectively bridge the domain discrepancy. Furthermore, we design an uncertainty- guided parameter fusion strategy to robustly integrate the adapted knowledge. Extensive experiments across eight cross- domain settings demonstrate that SAPA-KD consistently outper- forms existing OOD-KD methods.

records.title: Two-Level Routing Grouped Mixture-of-Experts for Multi-Domain Continual Learning
records.abstract: Multi-domain continual learning faces challenges of catastrophic forgetting and forward forgetting when handling sequential tasks with distribution shifts and varying class sets. In this work, we propose a Two-level Routing Grouped Mixture-of-Experts (TRGE) method to address these issues. TRGE dynamically expands pre-trained CLIP with task-specific expert groups to mitigate catastrophic forgetting. Meanwhile, it maintains fixed group sizes with intra-group router to prevent routing overfitting, while inter-group router selects expert groups based on task identifiers and prototype distances for better collaboration. The task identifiers are obtained through Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) based on generated task semantic descriptions and the understanding of sampled images. To alleviate forward forgetting, we dynamically combine the outputs of frozen CLIP and TRGE adapters, leveraging both pre-trained knowledge and learned knowledge for the classification of unseen samples. Through extensive experiments across various settings, our method outperforms other advanced methods.

records.title: Diversifying the Multi-Teacher Knowledge via Sparse Mixture-of-Experts for Visual Encoder
records.abstract: Agglomerative visual models aim to unify the strengths of various visual encoders through multi-teacher distillation for enhanced performance across diverse tasks. However, current feature-aligned distillation approaches for agglomerative models frequently encounter a compromised trap: student models learn compromised features that overlook the unique contributions and inherent differences of individual teachers, limiting the overall performance of models. To mitigate this limitation, we propose a novel Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (SMoE) based framework for multi-teacher distillation. Within the framework, we introduce a teacher-aware loss as a regularization term to actively increase expert diversity, enabling the SMoE to capture specialized features tailored to each teacher's unique contributions. Extensive experiments have demonstrated the superior performance of our method across various large-scale vision tasks, validating its effectiveness in resolving the compromised trap and enhancing overall model performance.

records.title: Federated Partial Label Unlearning
records.abstract: Federated unlearning (FU) removes specified information from the global model in federated learning (FL). We move beyond fully supervised FU and study federated partial label unlearning, where each sample has only a candidate label set, not a single ground-truth label. This weak supervision creates two challenges: the target class membership of each sample is uncertain, and correlated labels make it hard to erase the target class without hurting utility. We propose FedPLU, an efficient framework for unlearning under partial labels. FedPLU first applies an unlearning projection to obtain a ``forgotten'' reference distribution, then measures probability shifts and uses a top-$k$ partitioning strategy to identify samples that likely belong to the unlearned class. A dual distribution distillation stage then suppresses the target class while preserving overall utility. We provide theoretical guarantees for the projection step and empirically show that FedPLU achieves effective, efficient unlearning on multimedia datasets.

records.title: UWNet: Dual-Path Network with Wavelet-features Transfer and Edge Supervision for Semi-Supervised Biological Microscopy Image Segmentation
records.abstract: Semi-supervised biological microscopy (BM) image segmentation is crucial for nanoscale analysis. However, few models focus on BM images' intrinsic frequency characteristics, while edge regions often suffer from high uncertainty, degrading segmentation performance. In this paper, we first analyze BM images' characteristics via the wavelet transform and discover high-frequency (HF) components ubiquitously present across BM images (e.g., details and textures), whereas low-frequency (LF) components structurally reveal segmentation targets' layout. To harness these properties, we propose UWNet, a dual-path framework with frequency-aware WNet and conventional UNet for consistency learning. Extra wavelet-based images are input into WNet to bring prior details and layout information. It also aligns with rich details and broad frequency information distributions by disentangling local and global feature flows. UNet is employed for inference against negative wavelet basis variations' effects. Meanwhile, we propose channel distillation to transfer frequency information from WNet to UNet’s redundant channels by analyzing feature channel correlations. Furthermore, deep edge supervision is applied to encoders to explicitly incorporate edge information. Extensive experiments show that UWNet outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) semi-supervised methods on three datasets, including both optical microscopy (OM) and electron microscopy (EM) images. Code is available at https://github.com/withNamer/UWNet.git.

records.title: Energy-Efficient Spiking Neural Networks for Enlarged Vestibular Aqueduct Detection
records.abstract: Enlarged Vestibular Aqueduct (EVA) is one of the most common congenital inner ear malformations leading to congenital Sensorineural Hearing Loss (SNHL). Its small size, blurred boundaries, and low contrast in temporal bone CT images make automated detection highly challenging. Existing deep learning-based approaches remain computationally intensive and are not well suited for resource-constrained deployment. To address these challenges, this study introduces Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) to EVA detection for the first time and adapts the SpikeYOLO architecture to medical imaging through domain adaptation, resulting in the EVA-SpikeYOLO model. We also constructed a clinical-grade dataset comprising 3,625 CT images, including 1,677 normal and 1,948 EVA images. Experimental results demonstrate that EVA-SpikeYOLO achieves 98.9% precision and 99.1% recall, outperforming conventional ANN-based detectors. Owing to the event-driven computational mechanism of SNNs, the model exhibits remarkable energy efficiency, requiring only 5.53 mJ per image inference, approximately half that of YOLOv8.

records.title: HieraCompress: Token-Efficient Document Compression for Hierarchical Retrieval
records.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is widely adopted to enhance the factual accuracy of large language models by incorporating external knowledge during inference. However, in long document scenarios, flat chunk based retrieval struggles to capture hierarchical semantic structure, leading to redundant retrieval results and inefficient context utilization. Recent tree-based RAG methods address this issue by organizing documents hierarchically, but often rely on recursive generative summarization, which introduces substantial computational overhead and potential semantic drift. In this work, we propose an efficient hierarchical semantic tree construction method for RAG without using generative summaries. Our approach combines semantic-aware chunking, Gaussian mixture clustering, and non generative token level compression based on token perplexity to build multilevel semantic representations of long documents. During retrieval, all tree nodes are flattened and ranked by semantic similarity to the query, and the top-k nodes are used as context for answer generation. Experimental results on long document question answering benchmarks show that, compared to baseline methods, our approach improves overall tree construction efficiency by $2.6\times$ while achieving approximately 3\% accuracy gain.

records.title: DASCO: Dual-Adapter Cross-Scale Collaboration for Federated Large–Small Models
records.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is a principled framework for collaborative model training under privacy constraints. With the popularity of large language models (LLMs), extending FL to support LLM training and adaptation is timely and necessary topic. In practical federated systems, however, two challenges remain largely underexplored. First, existing adapter-based FL methods typically rely on a single adaptation structure, making it difficult to simultaneously support global aggregation and client-level personalization. Second, in practice, client devices often exhibit substantial resource heterogeneity. This leads the coexistence of large and small language models within the same federated system, challenging effective collaboration within standard FL workflows. To address these challenges, we propose a new collaboration framework for federated learning with mixed-scale LLMs with two designs. First, we employ complementary serial and parallel adapters to decouple globally shared knowledge and client-specific personalization, coordinated via a lightweight alternating optimization strategy. Second, we design a cross-scale alignment mechanism to enable meaningful aggregation across heterogeneous model architectures while preserving the standard federated learning workflow. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate our consistent accuracy and efficiency improvement under non-IID data and mixed-scale model settings, outperforming several recent federated learning baselines.

records.title: MTLSI-Net: A Linear Semantic Interaction Network for Parameter-Efficient Multi-Task Dense Prediction
records.abstract: Multi-task dense prediction aims to perform multiple pixel-level tasks simultaneously. However, capturing global cross-task interactions remains non-trivial due to the quadratic complexity of standard self-attention on high-resolution features. To address this limitation, we propose a Multi-Task Linear Semantic Interaction Network (MTLSI-Net), which facilitates cross-task interaction through linear attention. Specifically, MTLSI-Net incorporates three key components: a Multi-Task Multi-scale Query Linear Fusion Block, which captures cross-task dependencies across multiple scales with linear complexity using a shared global context matrix; a Semantic Token Distiller that compresses redundant features into compact semantic tokens, distilling essential cross-task knowledge; and a Cross-Window Integrated attention Block that injects global semantics into local features via a dual-branch architecture, preserving both global consistency and spatial precision. These components collectively enable the network to capture comprehensive cross-task interactions at linear complexity with reduced parameters. Extensive experiments on NYUDv2 and PASCAL-Context demonstrate that MTLSI-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance, validating its effectiveness and efficiency in multi-task learning.

records.title: LEADE-Net: A Lightweight Edge-Attentive Dual-Enhanced Network for Efficient Medical Image Segmentation
records.abstract: Efficient and accurate medical image segmentation remains challenging due to inherent tissue complexities, ambiguous boundaries, and computational constraints. To address these issues, we propose LEADE-Net, a novel Lightweight Edge-Attentive Dual-Enhanced Network. Our innovative approach integrates a Dynamic Multi-Head Edge-Attention (DMEA) module, which adaptively leverages multi-source edge cues from a Laplacian pyramid to guide feature learning toward precise boundary delineation. Furthermore, a dual-enhancement strategy synergizes an Efficient Dual Attention (EDA) module for parallel channel-spatial refinement and an Adaptive Feature Selection Gate (AFSG) for dynamic feature filtering, enhancing the model's representational power with minimal overhead. Extensive experiments on four diverse public datasets show LEADE-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance, demonstrating an average Dice of 86.83% and IoU of 79.30%, with exceptional efficiency, utilizing only 2.42M parameters and 4.71G FLOPs. This balance of high accuracy and computational efficiency positions LEADE-Net as a promising and practical solution for resource-constrained clinical applications.

records.title: Data-Free Backdoor Mitigation via Benign Knowledge Transfer
records.abstract: Most existing backdoor mitigation methods require training or fine-tuning on clean data, an assumption that is often impractical in real-world scenarios where such data is inaccessible. While data-driven distillation has shown promising mitigation capabilities, data-free knowledge distillation (DFKD) may inherit backdoors from compromised teacher models. To address this, we propose Benign Knowledge Transfer (BKT), a data-free defense framework designed to prevent backdoor transfer. BKT first generates clean proxy data via a stochastic subnetwork disagreement regularization term. Using this proxy data, we employ a rectified distillation strategy that selectively distills the trustworthy components of the teacher’s predictions. We further instantiate BKT as a two-stage self-distillation process for effective backdoor erasing. Extensive experiments show that BKT outperforms existing data-free methods by a significant margin and achieves performance comparable to clean-data-driven approaches.

records.title: Unsupervised Industrial Anomaly Detection with Asymmetric Normalizing Flow Distillation
records.abstract: Unsupervised anomaly detection aims to identify defects in manufacturing using only normal samples for training. Existing teacher-student methods often suffer from limited anomaly sensitivity due to similar network architectures between teacher and student. We propose Asymmetric Normalizing Flow Distillation (ANFD), a novel framework that combines the strengths of normalizing flow and convolutional networks. The teacher network utilizes bijective normalizing flow with affine coupling layers to transform normal features into Gaussian-distributed representations. The student network implements a multi-scale architecture comprising base convolutional operations,FeatMergeBlock and Shuffled Channel Attention to learn discriminative feature embeddings. ANFD effectively integrates exact distribution modeling with efficient feature extraction, enhancing anomaly detection sensitivity in a fully unsupervised manner. Experiments on MVTec AD, BTAD and MPDD datasets demonstrate its superior performance.

records.title: Tessera: Efficient Serving for Visual Autoregressive Modeling via Proactive Staggered Scheduling
records.abstract: Visual Autoregressive (VAR) Modeling have emerged as a high-speed alternative to diffusion for image generation. However, serving VAR efficiently is challenging: unlike Large Language Models (LLMs) which decoding step produces exactly one token (O(1)), VAR inference is characterized by ``scale explosions" where token volume grows quadratically (O(N^2)) per iteration. This distinct resource profile causes existing serving systems to suffer from memory fragmentation and "sawtooth" compute utilization. We introduce Tessera, an efficient serving framework that exploits the deterministic nature of VAR to maximize throughput. Tessera implements proactive staggered scheduling, a mechanism that strategically delays and interleaves requests to balance memory-bound early scales with compute-bound late scales. To execute these heterogeneous workloads, we design a scale-aware continuous batching engine with globally fused attention kernels. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that Tessera achieves up to 2.01× higher throughput than state-of-the-art baselines like Orca and vLLM.

records.title: Token Contrastive Learning for Weakly-Supervised Remote Sensing Image Segmentation
records.abstract: Weakly supervised semantic segmentation (WSSS) aims to train high-performance segmentation models with only limited annotations. Existing methods typically adopt a multi-stage training framework based on ViT, they first generate a class activation map (CAM), followed by pseudo label extraction and supervised training. But ViT also introduce over-smoothing and background false activation problems. Due to the unique characteristics of RS images (e.g. foreground and background imbalance, large-scale variation, and boundary blurring), these problems will be further amplified, seriously affecting the quality of CAM and the accuracy of the segmentation results. In this light, an adaptive token contrastive learning scheme has been proposed in this paper. It has 2 core components, namely patch token semantic information optimization (PTSIO) and contrastive learning for weighted class token (CLWCT), which aim to optimize the quality of CAM and enhance feature expression, respectively. Extensive experiments have been conducted on mainstream RS datasets, where our model demonstrates appealing results over other popular methods.

records.title: Lightweight Annotation-Free Retinal Image Registration via Grid Self-Supervision and Keypoint Learning
records.abstract: Retinal image registration remains challenging in the presence of pathological changes or large deformations. Although learning-based keypoint detection and description methods have shown promise, most still rely on supervised or semi‑supervised frameworks that require costly pre‑annotated data and often employ parameter‑heavy architectures. To overcome these limitations, we propose an annotation-free and lightweight self‑supervised network for retinal image registration. Our method introduces a novel grid-based self-supervision strategy that automatically generates dense pseudo-labels, eliminating the need for any manual annotations or pre-trained label generators. These features are further used to refine keypoint localization via a novel offset prediction module. By integrating a streamlined U‑Net and distilling knowledge from an established detector, the network achieves a compact design with significantly fewer parameters. Extensive experimental evaluations demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods, particularly under large deformations and quality variations, while maintaining high computational efficiency. The results confirm that accurate, annotation‑free retinal image registration can be achieved with a lightweight and scalable model.

records.title: CA-HFP: Curvature-Aware Heterogeneous Federated Pruning with Model Reconstruction
records.abstract: Federated learning on heterogeneous edge devices requires personalized compression while preserving aggregation compatibility and stable convergence. We present Curvature-Aware Heterogeneous Federated Pruning (CA-HFP), a practical framework that enables each client perform structured, device-specific pruning guided by a curvature-informed significance score, and subsequently maps its compact submodel back into a common global parameter space via a lightweight reconstruction. We derive a convergence bound for federated optimization with multiple local SGD steps that explicitly accounts for local computation, data heterogeneity, and pruning-induced perturbations; from which a principled loss-based pruning criterion is derived. Extensive experiments on FMNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 using VGG and ResNet architectures under varying degrees of data heterogeneity demonstrate that CA-HFP preserves model accuracy while significantly reducing per-client computation and communication costs, outperforming standard federated training and existing pruning-based baselines.

records.title: Adaptive MLP Reduction for Efficient Large Vision Transformers
records.abstract: Large vision transformers present impressive scalability, as their performance can be well improved with increased model capacity. Nevertheless, their cumbersome parameters results in exorbitant computational and memory demands. By analyzing prevalent transformer structures, we find that multilayer perceptron (MLP) modules constitute the largest share of the model's parameters. In this paper, we propose an Adaptive MLP Reduction (AMR) method to substantially reduce the parameters of large vision transformers without obvious performance degradation. First, we adopt Taylor based method to evaluate neuron importance of MLP. However, the importance computation using one-hot cross entropy loss ignores the potential predictions on other categories, thus degrading the quality of the evaluated importance scores. To address this issue, we introduce label-free information entropy criterion to fully model the predictions of the original model for more accurate importance evaluation. Second, we rank the hidden neurons of MLP by the above importance scores and apply binary search algorithm to adaptively prune the ranked neurons according to the redundancy of different MLP modules, thereby avoiding the predefined compression ratio. Experimental results on several state-of-the-art large vision transformers, including CLIP and DINOv2, demonstrate that our method achieves roughly 40% parameter and FLOPs reduction in a near lossless manner. Moreover, when the models are not finetuned after pruning, our method outperforms other pruning methods by significantly large margin. The source code and trained weights are available at https://github.com/visresearch/AMP.

records.title: Distributed Predict-then-Coordinate Scheme for MAPF on Waypoint-based Maps
records.abstract: Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) is a core problem in multi-robot systems. While centralized solvers handle both grid-based and waypoint-based maps, they face scalability and communication bottlenecks. Existing distributed methods are mostly designed for grid maps with fixed action spaces and struggle with the irregular topology of waypoint-based maps. We propose a distributed planning framework tailored for waypoint-based topologies that couples learning-based prediction with decentralized coordination. A topology-aware spatio-temporal policy network operates on graph-structured observations to generate forward-looking, conflict-aware multi-step action intentions. Based on these predictions, a distributed priority coordination mechanism establishes dynamic priorities via local intent broadcasting and resolves conflicts online through local search. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves performance comparable to that of state-of-the-art centralized solvers.

records.title: FedDBK: Federated Learning on Heterogeneous and Long-Tailed Data via Dual-Branch Network and Knowledge Distillation
records.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) in practical scenarios frequently encounters the co-occurrence of data heterogeneity and long-tailed class distributions. Traditional heterogeneity-oriented methods often fail in such scenarios, as the aggregated global model becomes biased and performs poorly on minority classes. To address this issue, it is essential to consider data heterogeneity and class imbalance jointly. In this paper, we propose FedDBK, a novel framework that addresses the coupled challenges of data heterogeneity and long-tailed distributions through a dual-branch network and knowledge distillation. Specifically, we introduce a dual-branch network incorporating an auxiliary balanced classifier to rectify class imbalance. To further mitigate local drift induced by heterogeneity, we employ knowledge distillation to align and enhance the shared feature extractor, establishing a virtuous cycle between class balancing and feature alignment. Extensive experiments on benchmark long-tailed datasets demonstrate that FedDBK consistently outperforms state-of-the-art federated learning methods by up to 5.35% in classification accuracy, achieving robust performance under heterogeneous and long-tailed data settings.

records.title: Semi-Supervised Multilingual Text Detection: New Benchmark and Label-Efficient Approach
records.abstract: Scene text detection serves as a pivotal primitive for visual understanding, underpinning critical applications ranging from real-time translation to autonomous navigation. However, current advancements are disproportionately skewed toward high-resource languages, leaving complex low-resource scripts under-explored due to prohibitive annotation costs. While Semi-Supervised Learning offers a potential remedy, standard Mean Teacher paradigms struggle in this context, suffering from confirmation bias via static momentum and overfitting to noisy pseudo-labels. To bridge this gap, we first curate CET-8K, a challenging benchmark comprising 8,000 mixed-script images characterized by extreme aspect ratios and dense layouts. Building upon this, we propose GeoTeacher, a label-efficient framework tailored for robust multi-lingual detection. Specifically, we devise a Reliability-Gated Momentum mechanism to adaptively stabilize the teacher against drift, and a Decoupled Geometric Consistency strategy to enforce structural resilience against anisotropic perturbations. Additionally, a Masked Denoising Distillation module is introduced to focus representation learning strictly on informative text regions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GeoTeacher establishes a new state-of-the-art on CET-8K, achieving a substantial 2.0\% improvement in F-measure under the 30\% labeled data setting.

records.title: Counterfactual Contribution Alignment: An Adaptive Fusion Method for Multimodal Knowledge Graph Completion
records.abstract: Multimodal Knowledge Graph Completion (MMKGC) aims to improve link prediction by leveraging information from multiple modalities. However, existing fusion methods predominantly rely on statistical correlations (e.g., attention mechanisms) and often fail to differentiate valid signals from spurious ones, making models vulnerable to misleading and non-causal modalities in complex scenarios. To address this limitation, we propose the Counterfactual Contribution Alignment (CCA) framework. CCA introduces a causal-inference mechanism that estimates the marginal causal contribution of each modality through counterfactual interventions during training. Meanwhile, we design a Multi-Criteria Alignment Loss to enforce the alignment between the model’s fusion weights and the true contribution distribution, thereby improving reasoning robustness. Experimental results demonstrate that CCA achieves state-of-the-art performance on the large-scale open-domain MKG-W dataset, and delivers competitive results on DB15K and MKG-Y.

records.title: SpikefMRIformer: An Efficient Spiking Transformer for 4D fMRI Processing
records.abstract: Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) provides 4D spatiotemporal data essential for revealing brain dynamics and diagnosing neuropsychiatric disorders. However, existing deep learning methods are predominantly based on Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs), which face limitations in terms of temporal modeling efficiency and energy consumption in fMRI data processing. To address these challenges, we propose SpikefMRIformer, a Spiking Neural Network (SNN)-based model tailored for 4D fMRI recognition that leverages spike-driven properties to efficiently capture temporal dynamics. Central to SpikefMRIformer is a 4D Window-Spike Self-Attention mechanism, which employs temporally sparse weighting to capture subtle fMRI dynamics amidst consistent spatial structures, while enhancing spike sparsity to reduce energy consumption. Furthermore, the feature embedding and attention structures are optimized for fMRI spatial characteristics. Extensive experiments on multiple public datasets demonstrate that SpikefMRIformer outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both single-disease diagnosis and multi-disease recognition while significantly reducing parameter scales and theoretical energy consumption.

records.title: PriCL-Seg: Prior-Guided Continual Learning for Abdominal Organ Segmentation
records.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have introduced a flexible paradigm for generalizable organ segmentation. However, adapting VLMs to continual learning scenarios remains challenging due to the incremental nature of medical data, where distribution shifts between old and new data trigger catastrophic forgetting and cross-modal semantic drift. We propose PriCL-Seg, a VLM-driven and storage-free framework designed for continual abdominal organ segmentation. Central to our approach is a pseudo-label-guided knowledge replay mechanism that fuses three supervisory signals: predictions from the previous model, ground truth for new classes, and structural priors from the Segment Anything Model (SAM). This hybrid supervision ensures efficient knowledge distillation while preserving fine anatomical details. Additionally, to mitigate semantic ambiguity in text-guided segmentation, we introduce a Confidence-guided Filter Module (CFM) that dynamically suppresses low-confidence predictions, ensuring segmentation reliability. Extensive experiments on public abdominal datasets demonstrate that PriCL-Seg significantly outperforms continual learning baselines and effectively leverages the structural and semantic priors of VLMs.

records.title: HeLM: Heterogeneity-Aware Layer Merging for Stable Long-Term Continual Test-Time Adaptation
records.abstract: Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) enables models to adapt to test data streams, but aggressive self-training often causes catastrophic collapse. Departing from prior work that primarily blames noisy pseudo-labels, we identify layer-wise heterogeneity as a fundamental cause. We find that neural layers exhibit asymmetric sensitivities to distribution shifts. Consequently, uniform adaptation may trigger cascading failures, where low-level overfitting amplifies into high-level semantic corruption. To counter this, we propose Heterogeneity-Aware Layer Merging (HeLM) to regulate the stability–plasticity trade-off. By leveraging online Gram statistics, HeLM selectively re-anchors high-energy channels encoding invariant structural priors to the source model, while preserving plasticity in channels needing alignment. Additionally, we introduce Reliable Sample Distillation (RSD) to mitigate volatility. Recognizing that low entropy alone is insufficient for reliability, RSD identifies reliable informative samples via gradient stability across stochastic views. Experiments on diverse benchmarks showcase our method's remarkable long-term stability and robustness. Code is available at https://github.com/HeHuang2018/ICME2026.

records.title: Edge-guided Multi-Path Diffusion Network for Infrared Small Target Detection
records.abstract: Infrared small target detection is crucial for surveillance systems yet remains challenging due to dim, textureless targets submerged in heavy noise. Furthermore, repeated downsampling in deep networks inevitably degrades fine-grained edge information. To address these issues of low contrast and spatial loss, we propose the Edge-guided Multi-Path Diffusion Network (EMPD-Net). Inspired by physical diffusion, the Multi-path Diffusion Enhancement Module (MDEM) aggregates multi-scale directional differences to model target-background disparity, significantly boosting target saliency for precise localization. Complementarily, the Early Edge Module (EEM) fuses shallow features to extract high-frequency boundary priors under auxiliary supervision. These priors are then injected into deep layers via weighted residual connections, effectively counteracting spatial loss and refining target shapes. Experiments on SIRST, NUDT-SIRST, and IRSTD-1K demonstrate that EMPD-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance in both accuracy and shape preservation.

records.title: Elastic-Mamba: Efficient Handwritten Text Recognition via Differentiable Visual-Semantic Alignment
records.abstract: Handwritten Text Recognition (HTR) is pivotal for multimedia document analysis but faces significant challenges regarding visual-semantic length mismatch and the quadratic complexity of Transformer-based architectures. To address these issues, we propose Elastic-Mamba, a novel framework that harmonizes alignment flexibility with linear-complexity modeling. We introduce a Normalized Elastic Boundary Tokenizer (EBT) that performs differentiable, density-aware resampling to rectify feature sequences, ensuring optimal allocation of computational budget. To capture global context efficiently, we design a Parallel Bi-Mamba (P-BiM) encoder featuring hardware-friendly decou- pled scanning and cross-gated fusion. Furthermore, a Semantic- Guided Visual Correction (SGVC) module is integrated with an alignment-based teacher forcing strategy to mitigate error prop- agation. Extensive experiments on three benchmarks including IAM, LAM, and TiHTR demonstrate the strong effectiveness of Elastic-Mamba. It achieves significant performance gains, reducing CER and WER by 8.5% and 10.1% on IAM, 7.1% and 6.8% on LAM, and by 21.6% and 13.7% on the TiHTR dataset relative to state-of-the-art methods, consistently outperforming recent Transformer and Mamba-based models.

records.title: ASAG: Anatomical Structure-Aware Grading for Nasal Endoscopic Severity Assessment
records.abstract: Nasal endoscopy is an important procedure for diagnosing respiratory diseases such as adenoid hypertrophy and nasal septum deviation. However, existing grading methods for nasal endoscopic images often suffer from inconsistencies between anatomical descriptions and imaging features when dealing with morphologically similar structures such as the inferior turbinate and nasal septum, leading to unstable severity assessment. To address this, we propose Anatomical Structure-Aware Grading (ASAG), a severity assessment framework. ASAG employs an anatomy-aware mixture-of-experts to route image features to structure-specific experts according to learned anatomical preferences, producing disentangled structure-level representations. It further uses attribute-based text prompts to align visual features with clinical descriptions, and introduces a rank-aware ordinal loss to enforce correct severity progression across grades. Experiments on multiple datasets show that ASAG outperforms baseline methods, improving AUC and F1 scores by 11.3% and 17.5%, respectively. The framework not only enhances grading accuracy but also provides a new approach for assessing the severity of different nasal structures in clinical practice, with substantial potential to improve diagnostic and treatment decision-making.

records.title: Dynamic Cache-Prompt Synergy: Overcoming Distribution Shifts in Efficient Continual Learning
records.abstract: Continual Learning (CL) in multimedia settings aims to sequentially adapt models to new tasks, yet the major challenge has evolved from catastrophic forgetting to dynamic distribution shifts across tasks (inter-task) and within tasks (intra-task). To alleviate these problems, we propose to enhance Cache-Prompt Synergy for continual learning. On one hand, we unify external prompts (enriched by text-visual conditioning) and internal prompts (cross-modally conditioning across encoder layers) to dynamically capture task-specific features, mitigating inter-task distribution shifts. On the other hand, we propose a confidence-anchored adaptive cache mechanism leveraging positive/negative high-confidence samples to guide predictions, alleviating intra-task distribution shifts. Experiments show Dynamic Cache-Prompt Synergy (DCPS) achieves superior performance (88.6% on full-shot, 80.6% on few-shot) on multi-task incremental learning benchmark with only 0.9M trainable parameters. The source code of this work is available at https://github.com/222018321062044/DCPS.

records.title: DC-I2-World: Dynamic-Conditioned Intra–Inter Scene Tokenization for 4D World Modeling
records.abstract: Predicting future 4D scenes is crucial for autonomous driving systems, as it enables anticipatory reasoning about dynamic environments and supports safe decision-making. Although recent world models leverage intra-scene and inter-scene tokenization to efficiently encode spatial structures and temporal dynamics, they still lack explicit modeling of dynamic regions, which forces static background and moving objects to share the same representational burden. This results in ambiguous motion predictions and suboptimal temporal consistency. To address this, we propose DC-I2-World, a dynamically conditioned intra-/inter-scene tokenization framework that explicitly incorporates motion priors into 4D world modeling. By performing explicit motion prediction in a two-stage process, and integrating multiple tasks such as future dynamic masks, iterative flow fields, and trajectory prediction, the motion priors are encoded into the tokenization framework to accurately model evolving agents. Our approach imposes dynamic constraints during both tokenization and generation stages, focusing the model’s predictive capacity on regions of the scene that actually change over time. Extensive experiments on the nuScenes dataset demonstrate that, compared to the baseline I2-World, DC-I2-World achieves a 3.10% and 3.33% improvement in mIoU and IoU, respectively, while maintaining comparable computational efficiency.

records.title: MotifTokens: Compositional Artistic Creation via Visual Motif Tokenization
records.abstract: Text-to-image diffusion models have emerged as a powerful tool for artistic creation. However, prompt-only control often falls short of specifying fine-grained instance details and complex backgrounds, making reliable editing and recomposition difficult. Recent concept tokenization and multi-concept personalization move beyond pure text conditioning, but they often learn entangled representations, leading to identity leakage, attribute confusion, and unstable composition under compositional prompts. We propose MotifTokens, which decomposes a reference image into visual motifs instances and background) and represents each motif as an independent token for token-conditioned generation. We further introduce an Open-Vocabulary Compositional Prior Building (OCPB) module to construct a priorknowledge dataset by pairing VLM-derived motif captions with diverse theme and style prompts. MotifTokens is trained in two stages to promote motif decomposition: Stage I learns motif tokens in the text encoder, and Stage II fine-tunes the denoising U-Net with tokens fixed for stable composition. Experiments on multi-motif creation and editing show that MotifTokens enables more flexible recomposition, richer artistic variations, and more coherent aesthetics than strong baselines.

records.title: Preserving Novel Class Distributions for Open Set Domain Adaptation
records.abstract: Open Set Domain Adaptation (OSDA) transfers knowledge from a labeled source domain to an unlabeled target domain that contains both shared known classes and target-private novel classes. Most existing OSDA methods treat all novel classes as a single unknown class, neglecting their distinct distributions. Although recent CLIP-based approaches (e.g., AutoLabel) impose fine-grained pseudo supervision on target-private class, this process can be unstable without novel-class priors and may amplify pseudo-label noise under domain shift. Therefore, we propose a novel training scheme called Preserving Novel Class Distributions (PNCD) for OSDA. We introduce an entropy-based pseudo-labeling strategy with a per-class confidence memory bank that retains only high-quality target pseudo labels. Additionally, we filter out unknown-class samples whose distance to unknown-class prototype falls below a threshold in target training. This avoids forcing the samples of different novel classes to cluster tightly around the unknown-class prototype, helping to preserve the distribution of different novel classes. Furthermore, our framework incorporates CLIP and ActionCLIP backbones to enhance generalization and semantic alignment. The proposed PNCD achieves state-of-the-art results on image classification and action recognition tasks.

records.title: H-PFC: Heterogeneity-Aware Distributed Inference via Preset Partitioning and Frequency-Domain Co-Compression for Edge Multimedia Devices
records.abstract: Distributed inference offers an effective method to alleviate computational overload on heterogeneous edge multimedia devices while preserving data privacy by avoiding raw data offloading. However, practical deployment is fundamentally constrained by black-box inference engines that prohibit runtime model partitioning, as well as by excessive communication overhead when transmitting intermediate features. To address these challenges, this paper proposes H-PFC, a heterogeneityaware distributed inference framework that enables efficient edge–cloud collaboration through offline preset partitioning and lightweight online decision-making. Specifically, by jointly leveraging partition-aware collaborative model compression module and frequency domain feature compression scheme based on channel importance, H-PFC reduces both computation and communication costs without requiring runtime model modification. Experiments on ImageNet show that, with accuracy loss below 1.2%, H-PFC reduces local edge inference latency by 65.86% and distributed transmission data volume by 89.06%.

records.title: Dual Augmentation and CLIP Feature Alignment based Domain Generalization for LiDAR Semantic Segmentation
records.abstract: 3D LiDAR-based perception has achieved significant progress in autonomous driving. However, models trained in one domain often exhibit performance degradation in unseen domains. These phenomena primarily stem from dual distribution discrepancies across domains, involving sensor related variations and scenario induced shifts. To solve these problems, a density robust domain generalization approach is proposed. We generate point cloud data by resampling consecutive LiDAR frames under random LiDAR configurations, and mix data from different frames with different densities using LaserMix. Dual augmentation produces samples with mixed scenes and varying densities, while maintaining local semantic information, enabling the model to make consistent and confident semantic predictions. We further map features from original, resampled, and mixed data into a unified feature space based on CLIP embeddings of category names, encouraging the model to learn domain-agnostic and robust representations. Experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art domain generalization methods.

records.title: Towards Practical Universal Domain Adaptation via Multi-Modal learning and Uncertainty Estimation
records.abstract: Universal domain adaptation addresses domain shift under mismatched source and target label spaces, where unseen categories may appear in the target domain. Prior studies typically focus on either a single or multiple labeled domains in isolation. Directly aggregating multiple sources often introduces harmful interference, whereas methods designed exclusively for multi-source scenarios tend to sacrifice flexibility. We introduce a unified adaptation framework that combines multi-modal representations with uncertainty estimation to improve robustness under such mismatched label sets. By leveraging visual–textual features, the proposed method performs class-aware alignment through parameter-efficient fine-tuning and prompt-based adaptation. Source-domain images are further summarized into class-level prototypes, which are continuously updated to enhance target-domain discrimination. We present a new uncertainty estimation approach that classifies images as belonging to either known or unknown categories using a trainable threshold. Extensive experiments across diverse benchmarks show that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance under both single-source and multi-source settings. records.title: Taming Client Drift via Plug-and-Play Hamiltonian Dynamics in Federated Learning
records.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) faces significant challenges when dealing with Non-IID data, where the divergence between local and global objectives—often termed "Client Drift"—leads to unstable convergence and performance degradation. While momentum-based optimizers are standard in centralized training, they often exacerbate drift in FL by carrying historical inertia into conflicting directions. In this paper, we propose FedHdy, a novel aggregation strategy inspired by Hamiltonian dynamics. By viewing the global optimization process as a physical system, we identify that conflicting gradients in FL act as ``energy violations" that push the model uphill on the loss landscape. FedHdy addresses this by strictly masking conflicting updates while rescaling the remaining dimensions to maintain the system's total kinetic energy. This ``energy-conserving" mechanism effectively filters out noise induced by statistical heterogeneity without slowing down convergence. Extensive experiments on various benchmarks demonstrate that FedHdy significantly outperforms state-of-the-art FL optimizers, achieving faster convergence and higher accuracy in highly heterogeneous settings.

records.title: SO-LoRA: Sparse Orthogonal LoRA for Parameter-Efficient Continual Learning
records.abstract: Applying Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) to Continual Learning presents a structural dilemma: instantiating task-specific adapters leads to unsustainable linear parameter growth, while sharing adapters risks catastrophic forgetting due to gradient interference. In this work, we introduce Sparse Orthogonal LoRA (SO-LoRA), a novel framework that resolves this trade-off by reconceptualizing adaptation as the learning of sparse, evolving compositions over a fixed, universal orthogonal basis. Rather than isolating parameters or naively sharing them, SO-LoRA constrains all task-specific knowledge to a unified, stable subspace. This is achieved through a dual mechanism: group sparsity regularization minimizes interference by enforcing highly compact task representations, while a gradient-aware soft mask dynamically shields critical compositions to preserve accumulated knowledge. We analyze and demonstrate that our sparsity constraints explicitly bound the interference between task updates. Empirically, SO-LoRA outperforms existing methods across diverse benchmarks, particularly in long-sequence tasks, without increasing parameter complexity.

records.title: OpenSAI: A Distributed Cooperative Computing Platform for Supporting Edge Intelligence
records.abstract: Cooperative edge computing has emerged as a key paradigm for deploying distributed intelligence in dynamic environments, particularly for latency-sensitive multimedia applications such as real-time video analytics, augmented reality, and multi-view perception. However, existing systems grapple with several challenges: fluctuating network topologies, meeting task-specific Quality of Service (QoS) demands under resource constraints, and the heterogeneity of edge nodes. To address these issues, we introduce OpenSAI, a distributed cooperative computing platform that optimizes task execution via task decomposition, resource coordination, and dynamic configuration. OpenSAI adopts a three-layer architecture, with its core layer integrating three synergistic components. Specifically, the Computation Distribution Component partitions computational tasks into parallel subtasks based on operation-level dependencies, while the Cluster Management Component maintains a stable cooperative environment by monitoring node status and allocating subtasks via a greedy scheduling algorithm. Concurrently, the Adaptation Optimization Component enhances execution efficiency by adjusting task parameters in response to real-time resource fluctuations, thereby ensuring QoS compliance while preventing overload on resource-constrained nodes. Experimental results demonstrate that OpenSAI significantly reduces task latency while ensuring high reliability in heterogeneous and dynamic edge environments. Compared to state-of-the-art methods, OpenSAI exhibits a superior balance between efficiency, adaptability, and system stability.

records.title: Segmentation-Aware Region-Level Enhancement for Efficient Video Semantic Segmentation
records.abstract: Content-aware video enhancement has been increasingly adopted in edge–cloud collaborative video analytics systems to reduce bandwidth consumption while improving analysis accuracy. However, existing approaches are largely designed for object detection and rely on simple features such as object size or edges, which cannot be directly applied to video semantic segmentation due to its dense prediction and the absence of explicit regions of interest. In this paper, we propose SARE, a Segmentation-Aware Region-level Enhancement framework for efficient video semantic segmentation under constrained computation. Instead of performing uniform per-frame enhancement, SARE operates directly on decoder-accessible compressed-domain metadata to selectively enhance segmentation-critical regions. We first analyze enhancement sensitivity at the region level by exploiting decoder-accessible structural, residual, and motion cues, and identify regions that are most susceptible to enhancement-induced distortions without relying on explicit semantic labels. In particular, we design a region-adaptive enhancement strategy that selectively applies region-wise enhancement or motion-guided reuse according to the temporal stability of each region, avoiding redundant computation across frames. Based on the above analysis, we further introduce a lightweight scheduling strategy that regulates region reuse over time to reduce unnecessary re-enhancement, thereby improving system throughput while preserving semantic segmentation accuracy. Extensive experiments on both cloud and edge platforms demonstrate that SARE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art selective enhancement methods in the accuracy–efficiency trade-off, achieving up to 11.40% segmentation accuracy gain with 2.4x-24.4x throughput improvement, enabling practical deployment of video semantic segmentation on resource-constrained devices.

records.title: Overhauling Sample Weighting to Boost Heterogeneous Knowledge Distillation
records.abstract: Deep neural networks face an efficiency-accuracy trade-off issue when running on low-resource devices. Knowledge distillation (KD) mitigates this but struggles to reduce architectural mismatch in heterogeneous cases, e.g., Transformer teacher and CNN student. A critical, underexplored issue is how to utilize informative samples. Thus, we propose a convex gradient filtering module (CGF) to overhaul the sample weighting mechanism. CGF jointly considers sample information and architecture-aware inductive biases. However, this induces unexpected conflicting gradients to destabilize optimization, canceling out important knowledge. Here, a gradient filtering method is proposed to eliminate them, ensuring theoretical and empirical stability. Importantly, CGF is lightweight yet efficient. Integrating CGF with the One-for-All framework, we propose dynamic OFA (DOFA). DOFA achieves competitive accuracy against computationally expensive state-of-the-art methods on two benchmarks with minimal computational overhead.

records.title: EIMC:Efficient and Interpretable Multimodal Calibration Methodology
records.abstract: Multimodal machine learning has advanced remarkably, but its reliability and interpretability remain underexplored, hindering practical applications in critical fields like healthcare and finance. Through extensive empirical studies, we find that current multimodal classification methods exhibit unreliable prediction confidence. They often neglect individual modality effects during confidence estimation, and even make negative assessments of its contribution. This violates the original intention of fusing complementary information in multimodal learning. To address this, we propose an intuitive calibration principle: no modality's potential individual contribution should be negative. Based on this, we design a lightweight constrained algorithm—Efficient and Interpretable Multimodal Calibration Methodology (EIMC)—to calibrate existing methods' prediction confidence and enhance interpretability. This algorithm can be seamlessly integrated into existing models and demonstrates significant performance improvements across three core dimensions: prediction confidence calibration accuracy, classification performance and network robustness.

records.title: AIVD: Adaptive Edge-Cloud Collaboration for Accurate and Efficient Industrial Visual Detection
records.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) demonstrate exceptional capabilities in semantic understanding and visual reasoning, yet they still face challenges in precise object localization and resource-constrained edge-cloud deployment. To address this, this paper proposes the AIVD framework, which achieves unified precise localization and high-quality semantic generation through the collaboration between lightweight edge detectors and cloud-based MLLMs. To enhance the cloud MLLM's robustness against edge cropped-box noise and scenario variations, we design an efficient fine-tuning strategy with visual-semantic collaborative augmentation, significantly improving classification accuracy and semantic consistency. Furthermore, to maintain high throughput and low latency across heterogeneous edge devices and dynamic network conditions, we propose a heterogeneous resource-aware dynamic scheduling algorithm. Experimental results demonstrate that AIVD substantially reduces resource consumption while improving MLLM classification performance and semantic generation quality. The proposed scheduling strategy also achieves higher throughput and lower latency across diverse scenarios.
