records.title: From Theory to Practice: Explicit Shared Space Learning in Semi-Supervised Domain Adaptation
records.abstract: Domain adaptation (DA) aims to enhance the generalization ability of models in scenarios where labeled data in the target domain is scarce. In DA research, semi-supervised domain adaptation (SSDA) can utilize the labeled information in the target domain more effectively compared to unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA), thus achieving superior transfer performance and gaining widespread attention. Existing SSDA methods implicitly learn feature spaces in the process of aligning feature spaces between domains; however, the underlying mechanisms remain insufficiently explored. To address this issue, this paper first theoretically reveals the advantages of learning a shared feature space for enhancing transferability. Based on theoretical insights, we develop a framework to learn a shared space, which is implemented by a gating-driven enhancement mechanism. It is feasible to explicitly filter out inconsistent features across domains compared with existing methods. Extensive experimental results demonstrate the significant improvements of the proposed gating-driven enhancement mechanism on state-of-the-art SSDA models.

records.title: Better domain generalization: Spectral Stylization and Adaptive Aggregation in Federated Learning
records.abstract: Federated Domain Generalization (FDG) focuses on learning a global federated model from distributed clients, aiming to generalize well to unseen domains under privacy constraints. FDG is fundamentally challenged by the trade-off between acquiring diverse domain information to strengthen generalization and preserving privacy in federated learning. To address this challenge, we introduce FedSSDA, a novel framework that enhances generalization through efficient spectral stylization and adaptive aggregation. On each client, we enhance local data diversity with Domain-Aware Spectral Stylization (DASS), which augments local samples by injecting compact cross-domain low-frequency style vectors, thereby reducing privacy risk and communication cost compared with sharing high-dimensional features. On the server, Discrepancy-Aware Generalization Aggregation (DAGA) adaptively adjusts aggregation weights by jointly considering each client’s generalization gap and its similarity to others, ensuring the global model prioritizes contributions from informative and distinct domains. Extensive evaluations on multiple benchmark datasets show that FedSSDA achieves state-of-the-art performance.

records.title: Distilling Compact Memories via Grid-based Patch Sampling for Efficient Online Class-Incremental Learning
records.abstract: Online class-incremental learning aims to enable models to continuously adapt to new classes with limited access to past data, while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. Conventional replay-based methods address this challenge by maintaining a small memory buffer of previous samples and have shown competitive performance under memory constraints. To further improve replay efficiency, recent approaches leverage distilled data, but often incur significant computational overhead due to bi-level optimization. We introduce Grid-based Patch Sampling (GPS), a lightweight and effective strategy for distilling informative memory samples without relying on trainable models. GPS samples a subset of pixels from original images to generate compact low-resolution representations that preserve both semantic content and structural information. During replay, these representations are reassembled to support training and evaluation. Experiments on diverse benchmarks demonstrate that GPS consistently outperforms existing replay-based and distillation-based methods under strict memory budgets, while incurring negligible computational overhead.

records.title: Enhancing Visual Modality Emotion Recognition Based on Multimodal Knowledge Distillation
records.abstract: Multimodal emotion recognition has attracted increasing interest because combining heterogeneous data sources can substantially improve recognition accuracy. Nevertheless, in real-world scenarios, the practical deployment of multimodal systems is often constrained by the high cost and operational complexity of acquiring physiological signals such as EEG, which are considerably less accessible than visual data. To overcome these limitations, this work introduces a multimodal knowledge distillation framework for emotion recognition, where a powerful multimodal model serves as the teacher to guide a visual-only student model. To facilitate more effective knowledge transfer from the multimodal teacher to the unimodal student, we design a multimodal multi-guide distillation strategy. Specifically, multiple intermediate assistant models are incorporated to progressively bridge the performance gap between the teacher and the student, while a dense guidance scheme is employed to alleviate error propagation during the distillation process. Extensive experiments on several public emotion recognition benchmarks verify that the proposed approach consistently surpasses existing methods.

records.title: Continual Learning with Dynamic Domain Shifts
records.abstract: Standard continual learning (CL) benchmarks often overlook the severe continually distribution shifts and class imbalance prevalent in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we introduce continual learning with dynamic domain shifts (CL-DDS), a realistic setting where domains naturally alternate while retaining inherent distribution characteristics. This imposes dual challenges: catastrophic forgetting and dynamic distribution shifts. Empirically, we find existing methods exhibit significant instability in CL-DDS. Consequently, we propose a novel plug-and-play method to enhance model discriminability and stability. We first introduce an adaptive hierarchical calibration (AHC) module based on the effective number of samples to mitigate margin biases caused by dynamic distribution shifts and imbalance. Additionally, a domain knowledge stabilization (DKS) strategy is designed to enhance the model to simultaneously accommodate the batch normalization statistics of previous tasks and those of the current task. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of existing CL methods across CL-DDS scenarios.

records.title: FedPAKD: Federated Prototype Aggregation and Knowledge Distillation under Missing Modality
records.abstract: Federated learning enables privacy-preserving medical image analysis; however, multimodal segmentation remains particularly challenging when participating clients exhibit incomplete and heterogeneous modality availability. Most existing federated multimodal approaches rely on locally learned representations derived from partial observations, which limits effective semantic knowledge transfer across clients and often leads to unstable optimisation under severe modality imbalance. To overcome these challenges, we propose a semantic transfer framework for multimodal FL that explicitly addresses missing-modality scenarios. The proposed framework incorporates a prototype-centred distillation strategy to enable distribution-level semantic transfer from global class prototypes to modality-constrained clients, together with a modality separation mechanism that mitigates prototype collapse and cross-modality interference. The method is formulated within a unified optimisation framework and does not require architectural modifications or modality synthesis. Extensive experiments conducted on the BraTS2020 benchmark demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art federated multimodal methods across diverse missing-modality settings, thereby highlighting its robustness and effectiveness under heterogeneous modality distributions.

records.title: The Gradient-Model Dichotomy in Semi-Asynchronous Federated Learning
records.abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across distributed devices while preserving data privacy, but the performance gap between gradient-based (SGD) and model-based (Avg) aggregation strategies in semi-asynchronous FL (SAFL) remains unexplored. Through theoretical analysis, we attribute these disparities to gradient fluctuation and update staleness: gradient aggregation amplifies the fluctuation among gradients, yielding oscillations and occasional instability, whereas model aggregation averages over stale updates, slowing convergence and incurring accuracy loss. Extensive experiments on image and text workloads (536 trials over 100 GPU-days in total) validate this dichotomy: SAFL-SGD typically attains higher peak accuracy sooner but fluctuates markedly, while SAFL-Avg is steadier yet slower and consistently underperforms in final accuracy. We summarize these findings into practical guidelines for choosing gradient or model aggregation in communication-constrained edge training for multimedia applications.

records.title: VL-BEV: Object-level Distillation from VLM to BEV for Efficient Autonomous Driving
records.abstract: To address the lack of semantic reasoning in end-to-end autonomous driving, we propose VL-BEV, a universal asymmetric semantic distillation framework. We utilize a frozen Vision-Language Model (VLM) as an offline teacher to extract high-dimensional implicit "thought vectors". To bridge the granularity gap between modalities, we introduce Cascaded Compression Adapter (CCA) and Geometry-Aware Aggregation (GAA). These components align sparse object-level language features with dense BEV features, enhancing the original pipeline with rich semantic priors. Crucially, VL-BEV allows for zero-overhead inference by removing the VLM entirely during inference. Experiments on nuScenes demonstrate that VL-BEV seamlessly integrates with end-to-end models like UniAD and VAD, reducing average L2 errors by 16.5\% and 7\% respectively.

records.title: IntrinsicSign: Zero-Cost Traitor Tracing by Exploiting Inherent Model Bias in Federated Learning
records.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative training while preserving privacy, yet faces Intellectual Prop- erty (IP) theft risks from untrusted participants (“traitors”). Existing traitor tracing methods embed watermarks into model parameters but face a critical trade-off between traceability and model utility, constrained by limited parameter space and aggregation conflicts in large-scale federations. To overcome this, we present IntrinsicSign. Instead of injecting additional signals, IntrinsicSign introduces a novel paradigm by leveraging the inherent client drift induced by the data heterogeneity, which naturally accumulates in the model’s classifier layers. While typically viewed as a challenge to be mitigated, we leverage this model bias as a natural fingerprint via a zero-cost mechanism, complemented by a collaborative black-box protocol. This dual- module design unifies robust ownership verification and scalable tracing. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that In- trinsicSign significantly outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, maintaining exceptional fidelity in large-scale federations while exhibiting high traceability and robustness.

records.title: A Lightweight 2.5D Segmentation Model with Cross-Slice Contrastive Learning and Adaptive Attention
records.abstract: Accurate medical image segmentation is essential for clinical diagnosis, yet existing methods face significant tradeoffs: 2D models lack spatial consistency while 3D approaches are computationally intensive. To address this, we propose an innovative 2.5D segmentation model that integrates pixel-level cross-slice contrastive learning and an adaptive attention mechanism. Our architecture combines the efficiency of 2D methods with the spatial-consistency modeling of 3D approaches. Specifically, a multi-path encoder extracts features from central and adjacent slices. An adaptive cross-slice attention mechanism dynamically modulates feature responses, guiding focus toward structurally consistent regions and mitigating misjudgments due to single-slice information scarcity. Additionally, a spatially-aligned pixel-level contrastive loss enforces feature consistency across corresponding slice locations, enhancing discriminative capability. Experiments demonstrate that our method significantly improves spatial coherence and boundary accuracy in segmentation maps while maintaining low computational overhead, offering an effective balance between performance and efficiency for medical image Analysis.

records.title: Shapley-Guided Consensus Distillation on Multimodal Hateful Meme Detection
records.abstract: Detecting multimodal hateful memes is crucial to curbing the spread of hateful content in metaphor. While multimodal models strive to close the gap across different modalities, identifying implicit semantics remains difficult. Meanwhile, when humans interpret memes, they utilize their knowledge to understand metaphors and converse with others for additional insights. To emulate this cognitive process, we leverage a social simulator to generate the consensus understanding of a meme from MLLM-based agents. Although incorporating consensus as features enhances the detection model's performance, practical applications cannot accommodate the slow processing speed required for consensus generation. Thus, this study proposes a Shapley-Guided Consensus Distillation framework for multimodal hateful meme detection. The framework adopts a multi-agent consensus-driven detection model as the teacher and distills both feature-level and logit-level knowledge to a lightweight student model. To enhance consensus distillation, we propose a Shapley-guided mechanism that adaptively weights the consensus features of each sample based on their Shapley values. Experimental results on three hateful meme detection datasets show that our framework speeds up per-sample inference time from over 15 seconds to approximately 0.33 seconds while achieving performance comparable to that of the teacher model. In addition, the proposed method not only achieves up to a 2.9 percent increase in accuracy but also operates with an inference speed that is 10 times faster than that of the accuracy-leading model (ExplainHM).

records.title: Frontal Region Elevation Bias Across Various Non-Individualized Head-Related Transfer Functions
records.abstract: Binaural audio often employs generic or non-individualized head-related transfer functions (HRTFs) to accommodate a large portion of the population. However, inherent inaccuracies of non-individualized HRTFs often lead to poor externalization, front-back distinction, spectral coloration, and vertical localization. Further, some individuals may perceive a sound to be elevated despite originating on the horizontal plane. Previous studies have evaluated non-individualized HRTFs in comparison with measured, estimated, or otherwise individualized HRTFs, but very little work has been published comparing non-individualized HRTFs with each other, especially when evaluating elevation inaccuracies. This study investigates the presence of a perceived frontal region elevation bias across various non-individualized head-related transfer functions from multiple publicly available datasets published over the last 30 years in order to establish whether vertical localization errors are an inherent quality of non-individualized head-related transfer functions and to determine factors that may intensify this phenomenon.

records.title: Adaptive Interaction Knowledge Distillation for Egocentric Action Recognition
records.abstract: Egocentric action recognition critically depends on modeling fine-grained hand–object interaction cues. Existing methods largely fall into two categories: global modeling approaches that process the entire scene but lack semantic focus, and HOI-guided approaches that introduce interaction priors through prediction-level alignment. While the latter incorporates interaction awareness, its supervision remains indirect and fails to explicitly constrain intermediate representations, often allowing models to rely on background-driven shortcuts. In this work, we propose Adaptive Interaction Knowledge Distillation, a detector-free framework that enforces explicit feature-level spatial alignment for robust egocentric action recognition. Instead of aligning output predictions, we leverage HOI priors as a teacher to construct interaction-centric features, and introduce learnable queries to adaptively distill local interaction semantics from global spatiotemporal representations. A feature-level distillation objective explicitly guides the model to prioritize physically meaningful interaction regions while suppressing background context. Importantly, this supervision is applied only during training, enabling efficient and detector-free inference. Extensive experiments on EPIC-KITCHENS 100 and EGTEA Gaze+ demonstrate consistent improvements over strong baselines, validating the effectiveness of explicit feature-level spatial alignment for fine-grained egocentric action recognition.

records.title: TopCom: Fast Token Compression with Top-K Selection for Efficient Video Understanding
records.abstract: Recent advances in video large language models (Video-LLMs) demonstrate remarkable capabilities for comprehensive video understanding. However, videos with excessive frames easily lead to severe token redundancy, substantially degrading the inference efficiency of Video-LLMs. Most existing video token compression methods inadequately exploit video properties, resulting in suboptimal inference efficiency. To address these limitations, we propose TopCom, a training-free token pruning and merging framework designed for efficient Video-LLMs inference. Specifically, TopCom precedes LLMs and adopts a synergistic strategy to integrate inter-frame grouped pruning with intra-frame attention-based selection for efficient spatio-temporal token fusion, markedly reducing LLM input tokens while preserving strong performance. Experimental results on four widely-used video benchmarks show that by retaining only 25% of the visual tokens, our method slightly exceeds the baseline performance(+0.7%) on LLaVA-OneVision-7B, while reducing the TTFT to 41.1%, highlighting its practical advantages for efficient Video-LLM inference. Our code will be released to benefit the research community.

records.title: Internalizing Visual Retracing: Efficient Multimodal Hallucination Mitigation via Self-Generated Preference Optimization
records.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) frequently suffer from object existence hallucinations due to a phenomenon often referred to as visual ``amnesia," where the decoder progressively under-attends to visual features during autoregressive generation. Existing mitigation strategies face a dilemma: inference-time interventions incur high latency, while training-based methods rely on expensive, style-inconsistent external supervision. To resolve this, we propose SVR-DPO (Self-Visual-Retraced Direct Preference Optimization), a novel paradigm that internalizes inference-time visual retracing capabilities into the model's intrinsic intuition. SVR-DPO utilizes an offline, entropy-aware visual injection mechanism to generate high-fidelity ``positive" responses, pairing them with the model’s standard ``negative" outputs. By optimizing the model on these self-synthesized preference pairs, we distill the visual retracing capability into the model weights. Extensive experiments on POPE, CHAIR, and MME demonstrate that SVR-DPO achieves state-of-the-art hallucination mitigation performance without introducing inference-time overhead or relying on external teacher models, effectively unifying efficiency and accuracy.

records.title: HyperPriv-EPN: Hypergraph Learning with Privileged Knowledge for Ependymoma Prognosis
records.abstract: Preoperative prognosis of Ependymoma is critical for treatment planning but challenging due to the lack of semantic insights in MRI compared to post-operative surgical reports. Existing multimodal methods fail to leverage this privileged text data when it is unavailable during inference. To bridge this gap, we propose HyperPriv-EPN, a hypergraph-based Learning Using Privileged Information (LUPI) framework. We introduce a Severed Graph Strategy, utilizing a shared encoder to process both a Teacher graph (enriched with privileged post-surgery information) and a Student graph (restricted to pre-operation data). Through dual-stream distillation, the Student learns to hallucinate semantic community structures from visual features alone. Validated on a multi-center cohort of 311 patients, HyperPriv-EPN achieves state-of-the-art diagnostic accuracy and survival stratification. This effectively transfers expert knowledge to the preoperative setting, unlocking the value of historical post- operative data to guide the diagnosis of new patients without requiring text at inference.

records.title: Continuous Reinforcement Learning for Efficient Image Cropping with Aesthetic Awareness
records.abstract: Image cropping aims to identify visually appealing regions within images by removing extraneous content and improving composition. Existing approaches typically generate numerous candidate windows for evaluation, incurring substantial computational cost. While reinforcement learning methods reduce candidate enumeration, they remain constrained by fixed-step discrete action spaces that limit fine-grained adjustment and fail to cover arbitrary crop regions effectively. We propose a continuous-action reinforcement learning framework that integrates aesthetic assessment and visual saliency to guide the cropping process. Our model enables flexible window adjustment through continuous boundary prediction and learns effective cropping policies via carefully designed reward mechanisms. The framework constructs comprehensive state representations by fusing multi-scale visual features, saliency information, and historical actions, providing the agent with a rich environmental context for decision-making. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method achieves superior cropping accuracy (0.702 Avg IoU on FCD, 0.837 Top-1 Max IoU on HCD) while requiring significantly fewer steps (3.75 on average), validating both performance quality and computational efficiency for practical applications.

records.title: MLLMs-Semantic-Enhanced Diffusion Routing Network for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
records.abstract: Multimodal Sentiment Analysis aims to recognize human emotions by fusing linguistic, acoustic, and visual modalities. For samples with ambiguous overall emotional expression, subtle audio–visual cues often provide stronger discriminative power. Static fusion strategies fail to dynamically determine the importance of each modality for a given sample. This makes the system vulnerable to weak or noisy modalities. To address these challenges, we propose the MLLMs-Semantic-Enhanced Diffusion Routing Network (MSDR). We leverage a Multimodal Large Language Model to extract fine-grained non-linguistic cues from raw audio–video inputs, constructing an auxiliary semantic modality to support multimodal sentiment analysis. Furthermore, we construct a Prototype Similarity Routing (PSR) mechanism to achieve dynamic allocation of modality importance. We design a diffusion reconstruction module to effectively alleviate the loss of fine-grained information during dynamic fusion. Experiments on CMU-MOSI and CMU-MOSEI datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

records.title: Progressive Acquisition of Goals through Vision-Language Models
records.abstract: Natural language provides a compact and human-readable way to define tasks in reinforcement learning (RL). While leveraging linguistic instructions to derive rewards holds promise for building robots that learn from human input, this goal remains particularly difficult to achieve in visual settings. Current methods utilizing large, pretrained language models often depend on non-visual environment representations, demand excessive amounts of feedback, or produce imprecise and poorly structured reward functions. To address these issues, this paper introduces GoalLadder, a novel approach that uses vision-language models (VLMs) to train RL agents from a single language instruction in visual environments. The core idea of GoalLadder involves the incremental identification of intermediate states that mark progress toward task completion. By querying a VLM, the method recognizes states that signify advancement in the agent’s performance and orders them through pairwise comparisons. Diverging from previous techniques, GoalLadder does not take VLM feedback at face value; instead, it employs an ELO-based rating mechanism to rank candidate goal states, thereby mitigating the impact of unreliable VLM outputs. During training, the agent learns to minimize the distance—within a latent space trained on unlabeled visual data—to the highest-ranked goal. This design eliminates the typical dependence on copious and precise feedback for reward shaping. Experimental results show that GoalLadder achieves superior performance over existing alternatives in classic control and robotic manipulation environments, attaining an average final success rate of ∼95\%, compared to only ∼45\% for the strongest competitor.

records.title: Prompt-Guided Prefiltering for VLM Image Compression
records.abstract: The rapid progress of large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) has enabled a wide range of applications, such as image understanding and Visual Question Answering (VQA). Query images are often uploaded to the cloud, where VLMs are typically hosted, hence efficient image compression becomes crucial. However, traditional human-centric codecs are suboptimal in this setting because they preserve many task-irrelevant details. Existing Image Coding for Machines (ICM) methods also fall short, as they assume a fixed set of downstream tasks and cannot adapt to prompt-driven VLMs with an open-ended variety of objectives. We propose a lightweight, plug-and-play, prompt-guided prefiltering module to identify image regions most relevant to the text prompt, and consequently to the downstream task. The module preserves important details while smoothing out less relevant areas to improve compression efficiency. It is codec-agnostic and can be applied before conventional and learned encoders. Experiments on several VQA benchmarks show that our approach achieves a 25–50% average bitrate reduction while maintaining the same task accuracy. Our source code is available at https://github.com/bardia-az/pgp-vlm-compression.

records.title: ConsuEval: Evaluating Persona-Driven Consumer Populations with Large Language Models
records.abstract: Persona-driven consumer digital twins built with large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate decision behavior, yet there is still no standard framework to test whether such agents express coherent and differentiated personas. We introduce ConsuEval, a population-level simulation and evaluation framework based on decision outputs and reasoning traces: framing robustness, blueprint level discriminability measured by a Persona Sensitivity Index (PSI), that combines shifts in decisions and confidence, and thematic alignment between agent rationales and empirical review topics. We instantiate ConsuEval on 12,024,722 Amazon smartphone reviews, extracting 10 behavioral blueprints with BERTopic, instantiating 4,996 GPT 4o persona agents, and evaluating each agent under 21 controlled message stimuli. Experiments show that well specified personas remain stable under gain loss reframing, exhibit clear blueprint specific response gaps captured by the Persona Sensitivity Index, and generate rationales whose topic structure closely follows real consumer discourse, while ablations confirm that these effects depend on structured persona prompts and that the index is numerically stable across different confidence weightings.

records.title: Text and Metadata Matter: A Textual Enhanced Cascade Prediction Model Based on LLM
records.abstract: Cascade prediction aims to forecast the future scale of post propagation on social media, with applications such as product pricing and public opinion management. Existing approaches rely on sufficiently observed cascade sequences and overlook the intrinsic propagation potential encoded in the source post's text and metadata, such as publishing time and publisher profile. As a result, they are unreliable for early-stage forecasting and fail on those posts exhibiting similar initial sequences but ending with different scales. Despite the importance of post’s text and metadata for its propagation, they are often too noisy and heterogeneous to capture propagation potential by traditional feature engineering. To address these limitations, we propose a Textual Enhanced \textbf{Cas}cade Prediction Model based on \textbf{L}arge \textbf{L}anguage \textbf{M}odel (CasLLM) as a plug-and-play module to enhance traditional sequence-based models. Specifically, CasLLM utilizes LLMs to analyze the text and metadata of source posts, extracting key factors that influence propagation from three communication theory-based aspects: topic, content, and audience. To selectively extract meaningful insights from these factors, a Text-Factor Collaboration module is proposed for better textual representation. Furthermore, CasLLM integrates seamlessly with existing sequence-based models through multi-task learning for joint sequential and non-sequential prediction. Experiments on two real-world datasets demonstrate that CasLLM not only improves the performance of sequence-based models but also provides explicit interpretability. The source code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/CasLLM-2A2D/.

records.title: Graph-PiT: Enhancing Structural Coherence in Part-Based Image Synthesis via Graph Priors
records.abstract: Achieving fine-grained and structurally sound controllability is a cornerstone of advanced visual generation. Existing part-based frameworks treat user-provided parts as an unordered set and therefore ignore their intrinsic spatial and semantic relationships, which often results in compositions that lack structural integrity. To bridge this gap, we propose Graph-PiT, a framework that explicitly models the structural dependencies of visual components using a graph prior. Specifically, we represent visual parts as nodes and their spatial-semantic relationships as edges. At the heart of our method is a Hierarchical Graph Neural Network (HGNN) module that performs bidirectional message passing between coarse-grained part-level super-nodes and fine-grained IP+ token sub-nodes, refining part embeddings before they enter the generative pipeline. We also introduce a graph Laplacian smoothness loss and an edge-reconstruction loss so that adjacent parts acquire compatible, relation-aware embeddings. Quantitative experiments on controlled synthetic domains (character, product, indoor layout, and jigsaw), together with qualitative transfer to real web images, show that Graph-PiT improves structural coherence over vanilla PiT while remaining compatible with the original IP-Prior pipeline. Ablation experiments confirm that explicit relational reasoning is crucial for enforcing user-specified adjacency constraints. Our approach not only enhances the plausibility of generated concepts but also offers a scalable and interpretable mechanism for complex, multi-part image synthesis. The code is available at https://github.com/wolf-bailang/Graph-PiT.

records.title: FAS: Fast ANN-SNN Conversion for Spiking Multimodal Large Language Models
records.abstract: Spiking Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have emerged as a promising alternative to MLLMs in various scenarios. Existing methods for creating Spiking MLLMs, i.e., direct training and ANN-SNN conversion, often suffer from performance degradation and relatively high computational costs. To address these issues, we propose a novel Fast ANN-SNN conversion method (FAS) that transforms both MLLMs and LLMs into spiking counterparts in two stages. The first stage employs a full-parameter fine-tuning of pre-trained models, so it does not need any direct training from scratch. The second stage introduces a coarse-to-fine calibration method to reduce conversion errors and improve performance. Experiments on both language and vision–language tasks across four different model scales demonstrate that FAS achieves state-of-the-art performance while significantly reducing inference latency and computational costs. Notably, On PaliGemma-3B, FAS even impoves accuracy of 1.68% on the HallusionBench vision-language task, while largely reducing energy consumption.

records.title: ISED: A Large-scale Vision-language Dataset and Benchmark for Instruction-guided Sticker Editing
records.abstract: In recent years, advancements in vision-language models have propelled rapid progress in instruction-guided image editing. However, sticker editing—serving as a core tool for emotional expression in social media—poses unique challenges due to its diverse character appearances, abstract visual styles, and complex visual variations. To address these challenges, we construct ISED (Instruction-guided Sticker Editing Dataset), comprising over one million high-quality sticker editing pairs with fine-grained instructions. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first large-scale vision–language dataset specifically designed for instruction-guided sticker editing. Based on ISED, we introduce ISED-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark with 1,000 carefully curated samples covering diverse editing types. Furthermore, we develop ISED-Editor, a Diffusion Transformer model fine-tuned on ISED, which achieves strong performance on sticker-specific editing and serves as a solid baseline for future research. We hope this work can facilitate further advances in multimodal generation and intelligent sticker creation.

records.title: Humans or LLMs? Actively Inducing Hallucinations to Expose Agents in Social Networks
records.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly permeate social media ecosystems, amplifying risks related to automated manipulation, identity evasion, and fraud. As LLM agents can mimic human behavior and bypass real-name verification systems, distinguishing them from genuine users has become a critical requirement for platform governance and societal security. Existing detection approaches primarily rely on passive linguistic classifiers, but their effectiveness deteriorates as LLMs further converge toward human writing. In this paper, we propose HalluciTrap, an active identification framework that embeds natural-looking semantic decoys into interactions to induce model-specific hallucinations. These decoys exploit LLMs’ sensitivity to machine-interpretable adversarial suffixes, prompting controlled topic divergence that humans naturally ignore. To generate robust decoys, we design a gradient-guided two-stage beam search algorithm that first induces topic divergence and then refines the perturbations to trigger the desired hallucination. Experiments on Twitter data demonstrate that our method achieves a true positive rate above 0.95 with a false positive rate below 0.01 within 5 chat rounds, surpassing state-of-the-art baselines by 22.5-30.1% after multi-round interactions.

records.title: Road Rage Reasoning: Task Definition and a Vision-Language Model (VLM)-Based Framework
records.abstract: Road rage poses a great threat to road safety. Current digital interventions are post-response, relying on recognizing drivers' anger responses after road rage occurs. This leads to a major concern: Is it too late? To this end, we aim to break the Gross's emotion generation chain (Situation-Attention-Appraisal-Response) by focusing on situational causes rather than responses and propose the first: 1) Road Rage Reasoning task, 2) RoadRageBench, a real-world road rage footage dataset with rich annotations, 3) cons (e.g., insufficient visual reasoning) of mainstream VLMs via extensive experiments, and 4) enhanced VLM-based real-time reasoning framework coupling VLMs' strong visual representation with a MLP reasoning decoder. Our work constitutes the first step towards pre-response regulation in practice, which can be decoupled into two interdependent problems: road rage reasoning and reason-aware regulation (VLMs have been proven to excel at similar tasks like dialogue-based comforting). We provide the dataset and codes on GitHub to accelerate in-car regulation: https://github.com/RRR-Road-rage-reasoning/Road-Rage-Reasoning.

records.title: Constrained Prompt Enhancement for Improving Zero-Shot Generalization of Vision-Language Models
records.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) often suffer from semantic misalignment due to domain gaps between pre-training and downstream tasks. Existing adaptation methods face challenges with incomplete textual prompts and noisy visual prompts derived from random cropping. In this paper, we propose a novel Constrained Prompt Enhancement (CPE) method to improve visual-textual alignment by constructing comprehensive textual and compact visual prompts. Specifically, we introduce Topology-Guided Synonymous Semantic Generation (TGSSG), which leverages Large Language Models and topological analysis to curate robust semantic sets. Complementarily, Category-Agnostic Discriminative Region Selection (CADRS) utilizes activation maps to identify discriminative regions and filter visual noise. Furthermore, we employ set-to-set matching strategies based on Test-Time Adaptation and Optimal Transport to align these enhanced prompts. Extensive experiments on 10 zero-shot classification benchmarks, 5 out-of-distribution tasks, and 3 video datasets demonstrate that CPE achieves state-of-the-art performance.

records.title: FusDrag: Offset Attention-Enhanced Multimodal Fusion for Vehicle Drag Prediction
records.abstract: Intelligent surrogate modeling is increasingly essential for fast and data-efficient prediction of aerodynamic drag coefficients (Cd). However, point-cloud–only methods suffer from discontinuous sampling and sensitivity to geometric sparsity. We introduce FusDrag, a geometry-aware multimodal surrogate that integrates 3D point clouds and multi-view images for accurate Cd prediction. A curvature-aware adaptive sampling strategy prioritizes informative regions and is systematically evaluated across sampling scales. For multimodal fusion, FusDrag employs a Multimodal Feature Fusion Module to aggregate complementary 3D–2D structural cues. In addition, a Laplacian-guided offset attention mechanism suppresses redundant or noisy features while preserving salient aerodynamic geometry. Experiments on DrivAerNet++ and ShapeNet-EX show that FusDrag consistently surpasses state-of-the-art baselines, achieving up to 85% lower mean relative error. Beyond automotive aerodynamics, FusDrag offers a generalizable framework for multimodal 3D–2D representation learning in scientific simulation and physics-driven computational workflows.

records.title: Interpretable Traffic Responsibility from Dashcam Video via Legal Multi-Agent Reasoning
records.abstract: The widespread adoption of dashcams has made video evidence in traffic accidents increasingly abundant, yet transforming “what happened in the video” into “who is responsible under which legal provisions” still relies on human experts. Existing ego-view traffic accident studies mainly focus on perception and semantic understanding, while LLM-based legal methods are mostly built on textual case descriptions and rarely incorporate video evidence, leaving a clear gap between the two. We first propose C-TRAIL, a multimodal legal dataset that, under the Chinese traffic regulation system, explicitly aligns dashcam videos and textual descriptions with a closed set of responsibility modes and their corresponding Chinese traffic statutes. On this basis, we introduce a two-stage framework: (1) a traffic accident understanding module that generate textual video descriptions; and (2) a legal multi-agent framework that output responsibility modes, statute sets, and complete judgment reports. Experimental results on C-TRAIL and MM-AU show that our method outperforms general and legal LLMs, and existing agent-based approaches, while providing a transparent and interpretable legal reasoning process.

records.title: GRID: Jailbreaking Large Vision-Language Models via Grid-based Reconstructions for Intent Disguise
records.abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) introduce new attack surfaces due to their integration of visual inputs. Conventional jailbreak attacks typically embed malicious content directly in images or text, making them readily detectable by defense mechanisms. We propose GRID, a novel black-box jailbreak attack method that exploits LVLMs’ powerful cross-modal reasoning capabilities to circumvent safety alignment. GRID neutralizes the overt harmfulness of malicious queries through custom encryption and segmentation strategies, reassembling them into puzzle-like images comprising a content grid and an index grid. Paired with benign, fictional scenario prompts, this approach induces the model to decrypt and reconstruct the original malicious query, thereby generating targeted harmful outputs. Extensive experiments on advanced models---including GPT-4.1, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Claude-Sonnet-4---demonstrate that GRID achieves an average attack success rate exceeding 95\% across multiple safety benchmarks, with minimal refusal rates, exposing critical vulnerabilities in current LVLMs to sophisticated cross-modal inference-based attacks.

records.title: Training-Free Image Customization via Decoupling of Fidelity and Controllability
records.abstract: Recent advances in diffusion models have revolutionized image generation, enabling the customization and insertion of user-specified subjects into designated regions of existing images via text prompts. However, existing methods struggle to balance subject fidelity and text controllability due to the inherent conflict. In this paper, we propose a training-free framework for customized subject teleportation that explicitly decouples fidelity and controllability at both the task and condition levels. At the task level, we introduce two auxiliary subtasks: a fidelity-oriented reconstruction task and a controllability-oriented editing task, which are integrated via a novel attention-decoupled injection strategy. At the condition level, we decompose the conditional guidance in classifier-free guidance mechanisms into two components: text guidance for enhanced controllability and image guidance for improved fidelity. Furthermore, we design a novel cross-task guidance mechanism that provides fine-grained guidance from the editing task to the customization task. Notably, our method is training-free. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in both fidelity and controllability.

records.title: Progressive Video Condensation with MLLM Agent for Long-form Video Understanding
records.abstract: Understanding long videos requires extracting query-relevant information from long sequences under tight compute budgets. Existing text-then-LLM pipelines lose fine-grained visual cues, while video-based multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can keep visual details but are too frame-hungry and computationally expensive. In this work, we aim to harness MLLMs for efficient video understanding. We propose ProVCA, a progressive video condensation agent that iteratively locates key video frames at multiple granularities. ProVCA first adopts a segment localization module to identify the video segment relevant to the query, then a snippet selection module to select important snippets based on similarity, and finally a keyframe refinement module to pinpoint specific keyframes in those snippets. By progressively narrowing the scope from coarse segments to fine frames, ProVCA identifies a small set of keyframes for MLLM-based reasoning. ProVCA achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot accuracies of 69.3% on EgoSchema, 80.5% on NExT-QA, and 77.7% on IntentQA, while using fewer frames than previous training-free methods.

records.title: Scaling Dense Scene Graph Generation with MLLM
records.abstract: Weakly Supervised Scene Graph Generation (WSSGG) targets improving scene graph generation without scene graph annotations and recent works show promising results using caption supervision. Despite significant progress, existing methods face several key challenges which limit the overall performance: (1) limited scalability, (2) low graph precision and (3) incomplete scene graph. We propose SDSGG, a novel framework that integrates multiple MLLM-generated dense captions through a multi-stage reasoning and grounding pipeline to automatically construct precise, spatially-aligned scene graphs via cross-modal verification and graph merging. Our approach addresses the scalability and quality issues of previous weakly supervised methods, offering a more robust mechanism for extracting relationships from images. Extensive experiments on VG-150 and our proposed R-SGG benchmarks demonstrate that SDSGG significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art weakly supervised methods.

records.title: MoveIt: Instruction-guided Object Placement in Images with Relational Spatial References
records.abstract: By anchoring target objects to specific relational references, instruction-guided object placement with relational spatial references allows for finer spatial manipulation yet mandates a rigorous balance between precise positioning and background preservation. Despite its significance, existing open-weight models frequently fail on this task, showing spatial misplacement, background distortion, identity drift, and object hallucination—limitations largely rooted in the absence of high-fidelity training data with explicit spatial supervision. To address this gap, we introduce the first data-centric framework tailored for object relocation, built upon a hybrid dataset of 14,000 real and synthetic samples. Central to our pipeline is an automated curation system spanning data acquisition, compositionally rich synthesis, and cascaded filtering via structural verification and semantic evaluation, achieving high accuracy. We also establish a standardized and diverse benchmark with a hierarchical metric suite that aligns with human judgment at 90.8\%. Fine-tuning a FLUX.1-Kontext-dev backbone on our curated data yields MoveIt, an open-weight model that achieves state-of-the-art performance in instruction-guided object relocation.

records.title: Find the Cue: Towards Cue-Aware Audio-Visual Reasoning in MLLMs
records.abstract: “When receiving a question, humans intuitively seek hidden cues within the query—such as how, where, and what—to enrich their reasoning.” Motivated by this, we present a novel LLM-based pipeline, called LLaMA-Cue, to tackle challenging Audio-Visual Question Answering (AVQA). It divides the recognition paradigm into two steps: 1) Toolbox to Find the Cue Related to the Question: we deploy an off-the-shelf toolbox (including PANNs, the Recognize Anything Model (RAM), and GPT-3.5) to convert all question-related information into feature representations and plain text; 2) Injection of Generated Cue Knowledge: we first design an Association Block to learn coordinated audio-visual pairs. Then, a Cue Aggregator is proposed to incorporate textual knowledge into the audio-visual features. Finally, we fine-tune the LLM using LoRA while keeping the pretrained backbone weights frozen, enabling cue-aware reasoning at inference time. Results on two publicly available datasets containing multiple question-and-answer pairs (i.e., Music-AVQA and AVQA) demonstrate the effectiveness of our LLaMA-Cue model.Source code: https://github.com/Li-yaoer/LLaMA-Cue.

records.title: SepPrune: A Separator-based Pruning Framework for Efficient Multimodal Large Language Models
records.abstract: Owing to the any-res vision encoder structure, vision tokens in the latest Multimodal Large Language Models (MLMMs, Qwen2.5-VL and InternVL3) are more than before, hinder- ing efficiency and widespread applications. Although many vision token pruning methods have been proposed to al- leviate this issue, none of them are entirely satisfactory. Text-dependent approaches that rely on cross-modal atten- tion lack flexibility, cannot pre-prune before the prefill stage, while diversity-based methods incur substantial computa- tional overhead. When analyzing the attention scores of vi- sion and text tokens, we observed peaks at modality separator tokens (special tokens that separate visual and textual modal- ities), which implies separator tokens act as a bridge between different modalities. Inspired by this observation, we propose SepPrune, an efficient and plug-and-play vision token prun- ing method, which uses the separator token as a unified query to evaluate and select the most informative vision tokens. By reusing built-in parameters of the LLM itself as a projec- tion matrix, our method prunes vision tokens without altering the LLM architecture. Experiments on widely used Qwen2.5- VL-7B demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the- art results, retaining 96.3% of the original accuracy when dropping 80.2% of vision tokens.

records.title: PRCBench: Evaluating Text-Rich Visual Comprehension in MultiModal Large Language Models
records.abstract: Given the pervasive presence of text-rich visual content in natural scenes, it is crucial for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to possess the ability to understand such content. Textual information can assist models in comprehending visual content in an image, since textual and visual information share a strong semantic correlation derived from their common source. However, textual and visual information is coupled during training models, which results in models struggling to comprehend image content when there is a contradiction between textual and visual information. To evaluate the ability of MLLMs to decouple such homologous information, we propose PRCBench, a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate MLLMs' understanding of text-rich visual content through three tasks: Perception, Reasoning, and textual-visual Contradiction identification. Among these, the contradiction identification task specifically evaluates models' capacity to decouple textual and visual information. Specifically, we incorporate unrelated or semantically opposite textual cues into images to validate models' ability to discern semantic inconsistencies between textual and visual content. Besides, PRCBench also evaluates perception, reasoning capabilities. Compared to existing benchmarks, PRCBench offers a significantly larger dataset of evaluation images and associated questions, where each task includes both multiple-choice and open-ended formats. Furthermore, we conduct comprehensive evaluations of well-known MLLMs on PRCBench, and highlight their limitations in understanding text-rich visual content.

records.title: P$^2$HCT: Plug-and-Play Hierarchical C2F Transformer for Multi-Scale Feature Fusion
records.abstract: Feature fusion plays a pivotal role in achieving high performance in vision models, yet existing attention-based fusion techniques often suffer from substantial computational overhead and implementation complexity, particularly in resource-constrained settings. To address these limitations, we introduce the Plug-and-Play Hierarchical C2F Transformer (P$^2$HCT), a lightweight module that combines coarse-to-fine token selection with shared attention parameters to preserve spatial details while reducing inference cost. P$^2$HCT is trainable using coarse attention alone and can be seamlessly activated at inference to enhance accuracy without retraining. Integrated into real-time detectors such as YOLOv11-N/S/M, P$^2$HCT achieves mAP gains of 0.9%, 0.5%, and 0.4% on MS COCO with minimal latency increase. Similarly, embedding P$^2$HCT into ResNet-18/50/101 backbones improves ImageNet top-1 accuracy by 6.5%, 1.7%, and 1.0%, respectively. These results underscore P$^2$HCT’s effectiveness as a hardware-friendly and general-purpose enhancement for both detection and classification tasks.

records.title: AP-Attack: Attention-Disrupted Prompt-Guided Adversarial Attacks on Large Vision-Language Models
records.abstract: While Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) achieve state-of-the-art multimodal performance, their cross-modal integration expands the attack surface, leaving them prone to visual adversarial vulnerabilities. In this paper, we present Attention-Disrupted Prompt-Guided Attack (AP-Attack), a novel untargeted attack leveraging attention disruption and prompt-guided optimization to systematically break LVLMs. By disrupting attention mechanisms within the visual encoder and aligning perturbations with semantically critical regions indicated by prompt, AP-Attack consistently outperforms baselines on image captioning and VQA benchmarks. Furthermore, we discover a previously underexplored vulnerability: LVLMs generate semantically inconsistent outputs for the same adversarial image across repeated trials. Based on this, we introduce Semantic Consistency Guard (SCG), a lightweight defense detecting adversarial inputs with over 85% accuracy without requiring model access. Overall, this work provides a more comprehensive analysis of the adversarial threats faced by LVLMs and proposes a novel defense approach, offering new insights for building more reliable and secure large vision-language models.

records.title: ReVCT: Refining Vision-Correlated Tokens for Hallucination Mitigation in MLLMs
records.abstract: Despite the impressive capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), they exhibit a notable vulnerability to hallucinations, generating descriptions that are factually incorrect or misaligned with the visual evidence. Unlike text-only large models, MLLMs are susceptible to hallucination when insufficient attention is allocated to vision tokens during image-grounded text generation. This highlights the importance of constraining the decoding process with visual cues to enhance reliability. To this end, we propose Refining Vision-Correlated Tokens (ReVCT), a simple yet effective method for mitigating hallucinations in MLLMs. It operates through two stages: 1) Vision-Correlated Token Detection. The model identifies tokens whose generation is strongly correlated with visual content. This is achieved by analyzing the decoder’s internal attention patterns and tracking vision attention drift: a token is marked as vision-correlated if its attention to vision tokens exhibits a sharp increase relative to the previous token. 2) Vision-Enhanced Token Refinement. The detected vision-correlated tokens are refined via an additional vision-enhanced forward pass that reinforces their alignment with underlying visual features. By focusing refinement only on vision-correlated tokens, ReVCT effectively suppresses hallucinations without degrading linguistic quality. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that ReVCT consistently reduces hallucinations across MLLMs, achieving performance on par with state-of-the-art methods.

records.title: When Adaptation Fails: A Gradient-Based Diagnosis of Collapsed Gating in Vision-Language Prompt Learning
records.abstract: Adaptive prompting mechanisms have been proposed to enhance visual-language models by dynamically tailoring prompts to inputs. However, we systematically observe that adaptive gates and prompt-selection modules frequently collapse: they produce nearly constant outputs, contribute negligible gradient signals, and often degrade downstream performance compared to fixed prompts. To further explore this issue, we present a systematic diagnostic study to uncover the underlying causes and conditions of adaptation failure. Through controlled experiments across datasets and multiple prompt learning architectures, we identify and quantify two root causes: gradient magnitude imbalance (gate parameters receive gradients 2-3 orders smaller than prompts) and gate degradation (gating modules converge to trivial constant patterns). Our findings invite a re-examination of the prevailing trend of indiscriminately adding architectural complexity in parameter-efficient learning and delineate conditions under which adaptive prompting is—and is not—effective.

records.title: DFM: Difference Feature Modeling with Text-Guided Gated Contrastive Loss for Remote Sensing Image Change Captioning
records.abstract: The primary goal of Remote Sensing Image Change Captioning (RSICC) is to automatically generate descriptions of changes between remote sensing images captured at different time points. Existing models still rely on a single autoregressive generation paradigm, which tends to prioritize learning easily generated vocabulary over capturing discriminative differences between images. To address this, we reframe the training paradigm and propose a novel Difference Feature Modeling (DFM) framework. Specifically, we introduce a Text-guided Gated Contrastive Loss (TGCL) to guide the vision encoder to extract critical features from a text-modal perspective. Additionally, we incorporate a pre-trained Change Detection model to transfer stable change detection knowledge. In order to further enhance the representation, we design a Joint Feature Modeling (JFM) module to achieve the fusion of multi-scale difference representations, thereby capturing comprehensive spatiotemporal variations between multi-temporal images. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

records.title: Towards Training-Free Language-Guided Tracking: A Reasoning-Enhanced Framework with MLLMs
records.abstract: Language-guided tracking provides a user-friendly interface for human-computer interaction but faces challenges from initial grounding uncertainty and temporal semantic drift. We propose MAGTrack, a training-free framework that integrates Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to achieve robust tracking without spatial supervision. To balance performance and efficiency, MAGTrack employs an asynchronous updating strategy through two plug-and-play modules: the MLLM-based Grounding Module (MGM) for precise first-frame localization via joint reasoning, and the Text Refinement Module (TRM) which is adaptively triggered to align language with evolving visual contexts. By invoking MLLMs only when necessary, our framework enhances the stability of base trackers in complex scenes. Extensive experiments on four benchmarks—OTB99, TNL2K, LaSOT, and LaSOT$_{ext}$—demonstrate that MAGTrack achieves state-of-the-art performance in language-only settings, offering a practical solution for high-reliability multimedia applications.

records.title: Conscious Gaze: Adaptive Attention Mechanisms for Hallucination Mitigation in Vision-Language Models
records.abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) often exhibit text inertia, where attention drifts from visual evidence toward linguistic priors, resulting in object hallucinations. Existing decoding strategies intervene only at the output logits and thus cannot correct internal reasoning drift, while recent internal-control methods based on heuristic head suppression or global steering vectors lack principled grounding. We introduce Conscious Gaze (CG-VLM), a training-free, inference-time framework that converts game-theoretic interpretability into actionable decoding control. A Cognitive Demand Sensor built on Harsanyi interactions estimates instantaneous vision–text synergy and identifies moments when visual grounding is necessary. Conditioned on this signal, a Focused Consensus Induction module selectively reorients mid-layer attention toward visual tokens before collapse into text priors. CG-VLM achieves state-of-the-art results on POPE and CHAIR across InstructBLIP, LLaVA, Qwen-VL, and mPLUG, while preserving general capabilities, demonstrating that token-level sensing enables precise, context-aware intervention without compromising foundational knowledge.

records.title: META-IR: Meta-Introspective Reasoning for Adaptive Safety Alignment in LLM
records.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) remain vulnerable against jailbreak attacks and harmful-content prompts, particularly under adversarial distribution shifts where static alignment pipelines fail to generalize. Although introspective methods such as STAIR strengthen refusal consistency, they depend on fixed self-evaluation policies that cannot rapidly adapt to evolving manipulation strategies. To overcome these limitations this paper introduces META-IR, a meta-introspective reasoning framework that enhances safety alignment through meta-learning–driven adaptation. Its employs a dual-loop architecture: an inner introspective loop that performs structured risk analysis, self-assessment, and reflective correction via SI-MCTS, and an outer meta-learning loop that optimizes the introspection policy across diverse jailbreak task families to enable rapid generalization to unseen attacks. A dynamic jailbreak simulation module further exposes the model to progressively harder adversarial prompts, enabling continual self-improvement without human supervision. Experiments across multiple models (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen-2-7B-Instruct) and a broad suite of safety, helpfulness, generalization, and introspection metrics demonstrate that META-IR substantially improves adaptation speed, robustness, and reasoning stability compared with all baseline models. These results establish META-IR as an effective pathway toward building LLMs capable of sustained, adaptive safety alignment under dynamic and evolving threat environments.

records.title: Divide Image and Conquer Text: Unleashing Large Language Models for Fine-Grained Multimodal Fake News Detection
records.abstract: With the proliferation and diversification of multimodal fake news in social media, developing a fine-grained multimodal fake news detector has become a crucial problem. Although large language models perform well in the binary classification of real/fake news, they fail to address fine-grained detection because 1) the image forgery clues cannot be reasonably understood; 2) the multimodal manipulation evidence cannot be correctly reasoned. Considering that the detection of image manipulation and text manipulation relies on shallow perceptual information and deep semantic information respectively, we propose the DICT (Divide Image and Conquer Text) method. DICT first leverages a distortion-aware cross-modal reasoning module and a language-guided artifact grounding module to mine visual artifact traces, and then designs an image-to-text progressive prompting scheme to reason multimodal clues and predict veracity labels. Extensive experiments show that DICT significantly outperforms existing methods across various manipulation detection and grounding tasks. Notably, on the manipulated text grounding tasks, DICT surpasses the previous state-of-the-art by 27.86% respectively.

records.title: OracleAnalyser: Analysing Implicit Semantics of Oracle Bone Scripts through MLLMs with Post-training
records.abstract: With the advancement of artificial intelligence, research on oracle bone scripts has entered a new era. However, existing methods and benchmarks remain largely confined to recognition tasks, overlooking the equally crucial aspect of oracle bone analysis. In addition, we release both an oracle bone reasoning dataset and an oracle bone preference dataset, and further construct a new benchmark to evaluate models’ analytical capabilities for oracle bone scripts. Extensive experiments validate the superior analytical performance of OracleAnalyser, which achieves remarkable results with only 3B parameters, surpassing models with substantially larger scales.

records.title: FloorplanCoT: An LLM-based Chain-of-Thought Framework with RAG for Floorplan Generation
records.abstract: Automated floorplan generation from natural-language descriptions is challenging due to the gap between high-level semantic intent and low-level geometric realization. We propose FloorplanCoT, a retrieval-augmented chain-of-thought framework based on Large Language Models (LLMs) for text-driven floorplan generation. The LLM first infers a room-level topology from user input and retrieves representative layout cases via Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to provide geometry-aware priors. Guided by structured chain-of-thought reasoning, the model predicts parent-relative spatial attributes and room areas, producing executable bubble diagrams as intermediate representations. These bubble diagrams are then used to condition a Diffusion Transformer (DiT) for geometric realization, enabling the synthesis of complete and coherent floorplans. Experiments show that FloorplanCoT improves semantic controllability and geometric stability over baseline methods, demonstrating the effectiveness of combining retrieval-augmented reasoning with diffusion-based generation.

records.title: Rethinking Representation Adaptation for VLM-based Video Anomaly Detection
records.abstract: Weakly supervised video anomaly detection (WSVAD) has achieved remarkable success by leveraging features from large vision-language models (VLMs). However, how to best adapt these powerful, general-purpose features for the specific VAD task remains a critical question. We find the common two-stage paradigm of pre-training and fine-tuning is surprisingly sub-optimal, as it degrades the semantic integrity of VLM features. We propose ATLAS (Auxiliary Temporal Learning for Anomaly Supervision), a novel single-stage framework that recasts self-supervision as a lightweight auxiliary regularizer. By co-optimizing a temporal consistency objective with the main VAD objective, ATLAS learns robust temporal cues while preserving the rich VLM feature space. ATLAS demonstrates consistent performance improvements across four diverse benchmarks, establishing a new state-of-the-art of 88.19% AUC on UCF-Crime. Our work validates that for VLM adaptation, joint regularization is a more effective paradigm than sequential pre-training. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/ATLAS-AAAA.

records.title: Representation Calibration and Uncertainty Guidance for Class-Incremental Learning based on Vision Language Model
records.abstract: Class-incremental learning requires a learning system to continually learn knowledge of new classes and meanwhile try to preserve previously learned knowledge of old classes. As current state-of-the-art methods based on Vision-Language Models (VLMs) still suffer from the issue of differentiating classes across learning tasks. Here a novel VLM-based continual learning framework for image classification is proposed. In this framework, task-specific adapters are added to the pre-trained and frozen image encoder to learn new knowledge, and a novel cross-task representation calibration strategy based on a mixture of light-weight projectors is used to help better separate all learned classes in a unified feature space, alleviating class confusion across tasks. In addition, a novel inference strategy guided by prediction uncertainty is developed to more accurately select the most appropriate image feature for class prediction. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets under various settings demonstrate the superior performance of our method compared to existing ones.

records.title: Defer to Plan: Adaptive Multi-Agent Fusion for End-to-End V2X Driving
records.abstract: Vehicle-to-everything-aided autonomous driving (V2X-AD) significantly enhances driving performance through information sharing. However, existing collaborative perception methods only optimize module-level perception capabilities and fail to effectively serve the ultimate planning and control tasks. We propose an end-to-end collaborative driving system that directly optimizes planning task performance. The system employs MotionNetwork to fuse historical temporal information, utilizes attention mechanisms to efficiently compress spatial features into compact tokens, and adaptively fuses multi-agent features through an autoregressive decoder. Additionally, we introduce Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture to enhance the model's representation capacity for heterogeneous features. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves a driving score of 79.72, surpassing the state-of-the-art CoDriving baseline (77.15) by 3.33\% in closed-loop evaluation while maintaining communication efficiency.

records.title: Improving Long-Tail Detection via Layout–Instruction Conditioned Diffusion Synthesis
records.abstract: Synthetic data from diffusion models can improve object detection, but long-tail performance is still limited by scarce rare classes and inflexible conditioning (e.g., text-only or layout-only inputs). In this paper, we propose Tail-SD, a layout–instruction conditioned stable diffusion framework that supports text, layouts, or their hybrid, enabling controllable synthesis from boxes, masks, and/or prompts to better cover the long-tail objects. To train a single model across heterogeneous conditions, we introduce a multi-task cross-attention module and multi-task embedding tokens, improving generation quality and diversity. Extensive experiments on COCO and LVIS demonstrate that diffusion synthesis with hybrid conditioning consistently benefits detection, e.g., on LVIS val, it achieves +4.89% / +5.68% rare Box/Mask AP, highlighting strong potential for addressing long-tail challenges.

records.title: Auto-Slides: An Interactive Multi-Agent System for Creating and Customizing Research Presentations
records.abstract: The rapid progress of large language models (LLMs) has opened new opportunities for education. While learners can interact with academic papers through LLM-powered dialogue, limitations still exist: the lack of structured organization and the heavy reliance on text can impede systematic understanding and engagement with complex concepts. To address these challenges, we propose Auto-Slides, an LLM-driven system that converts research papers into pedagogically structured, multimodal slides (e.g., diagrams and tables). Drawing on cognitive science, it creates a presentation-oriented narrative and allows iterative refinement via an interactive editor to better match learners' knowledge level and goals. Auto-Slides further incorporates verification and knowledge retrieval mechanisms to ensure accuracy and contextual completeness. Through extensive user studies, Auto-Slides demonstrates strong learner acceptance, improved structural support for understanding, and expert-validated gains in narrative quality compared with conventional LLM-based reading. Our contributions lie in designing a multi-agent framework for transforming academic papers into pedagogically optimized slides and introducing interactive customization for personalized learning.

records.title: MARS: MLLM-Augmented Relation Semantics for Fine-grained Visual Privacy Understanding
records.abstract: Visual data are informative but inherently contain sensitive content, making fine-grained privacy understanding essential for user protection and human-centric AI. Most existing approaches primarily rely on visual features, while the role of object-level relation semantics in privacy understanding remains relatively underexplored. In this work, we propose MARS, a framework based on MLLM-Augmented Relation Semantics, which explores the incorporation of relation-aware semantics to support fine-grained visual privacy understanding. Specifically, subject-predicate-object triplets extracted from pretrained scene-graph generators serve as semantic anchors to prompt an MLLM to generate privacy-aware textual descriptions. These enriched relation representations are then integrated with image patch-level features via a fine-grained cross-modal fusion mechanism, enabling joint reasoning over visual regions and relation semantics. Experiments on fine-grained visual privacy datasets show that MARS consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in mAP, CF1, and OF1, indicating the potential of explicitly modeling relation semantics for privacy understanding.

records.title: RAW-VLM: Enabling Vision–Language Models to Understand RAW Images
records.abstract: RAW images preserve linear sensor measurements and camera-dependent statistics, which are crucial for com-putational photography and low-level vision tasks. With the widespread use of large vision–language models in multimodal understanding and interaction, extending their semantic under-standing and instruction-following ability to the RAW domain, so as to broaden the capability of computational photography and low-level vision tasks, is of great research value and practical interest. However, existing vision–language models are almost exclusively trained on RGB images processed by the ISP, and therefore exhibit suboptimal performance when directly applied to RAW images, which in turn hinders the development of RAW+VLM applications. To bridge this gap, we propose RAW-VLM, the ffrst approach designed to enhance the ability of native vision–language models to understand RAW images. We introduce a self-distillation task that transfers the model’s own understanding of RGB images to the RAW domain, and a camera parameter prediction task that strengthens its ability to model pixel-level patterns in RAW images. To overcome the scarcity of suitable RAW datasets, we apply an RGB-to-RAW procedure to existing VLM benchmarks and synthesize the ffrst large-scale RAW image VLM ffne-tuning dataset and test benchmark. We evaluate our method on multiple VLM backbones and benchmarks, and the experimental results show that it improves the understanding of RAW images to a level close to that on RGB images, while almost not affecting the original understanding of RGB images.

records.title: Training-Free ANN-to-SNN Conversion via Spatially-Aware Wasserstein Calibration
records.abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) provide an energy-efficient alternative to conventional neural networks, but ANN-to-SNN conversion often suffers from severe performance degradation under limited inference timesteps due to activation mismatch.To address this issue, we propose a fully training-free ANN-to-SNN conversion framework consisting of a distribution-level calibration module and a lightweight refinement module. The core component, Spatially-Aware Wasserstein Calibration (WPC), jointly determines firing thresholds and multi-spike capacities by minimizing a spatially-aware Wasserstein distance between ANN activations and their quantized SNN representations, enabling stable conversion under low-timestep and multi-spike settings. An optional Layer-wise Response Rescaling (LRR) module further compensates for residual response attenuation with negligible overhead.The proposed framework requires no retraining or architectural modification. On CIFAR-100 with ResNet-20, WPC achieves 81.68 accuracy at T=32, closely matching the ANN baseline. On ImageNet with ResNet-34, WPC reaches 74.68 accuracy at T=32, substantially outperforming representative training-free baselines under the same timestep budget. These results demonstrate that the proposed method provides an effective and practical solution for low-timestep, training-free ANN-to-SNN conversion.

records.title: ProtRLSearch: A Multi-Round Multimodal Protein Search Agent with Large Language Models Trained via Reinforcement Learning
records.abstract: Protein analysis tasks arising in healthcare settings often require accurate reasoning under protein sequence constraints, involving tasks such as functional interpretation of disease-related variants, protein-level analysis for clinical research, and similar scenarios. To address such tasks, search agents are introduced to search protein-related information, providing support for disease-related variant analysis and protein function reasoning in protein-centric inference. However, such search agents are mostly limited to single-round, text-only modality search, which prevents the protein sequence modality from being incorporated as a multimodal input into the search decision-making process. Meanwhile, their reliance on reinforcement learning (RL) supervision that focuses solely on the final answer results in a lack of search process constraints, making deviations in keyword selection and reasoning directions difficult to identify and correct in a timely manner. To address these limitations, we propose ProtRLSearch, a multi-round protein search agent trained with multi-dimensional reward based RL, which jointly leverages protein sequence and text as multimodal inputs during real-time search to produce high quality reports. To evaluate the ability of models to integrate protein sequence information and text-based multimodal inputs in realistic protein query settings, we construct ProtMCQs, a benchmark of 3,000 multiple choice questions (MCQs) organized into three difficulty levels. Experimental results show that ProtRLSearch improves accuracy from 35.7% to 86.9% on level 1, from 30.5% to 77.4% on level 2, and from 26.1% to 72.5% on level 3.

records.title: CineAGI: Character-Consistent Movie Creation through LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Modal Generation and Cross-Scene Integration
records.abstract: Automated movie creation requires coordinating multiple characters, modalities, and narrative elements across extended sequences---a challenge that existing end-to-end approaches struggle to address effectively. We present \textbf{CineAGI}, a hierarchical movie generation framework that decomposes this complex task through specialized multi-agent orchestration. Our framework employs three key innovations: (1) a multi-agent narrative synthesis module where specialized LLM agents collaboratively generate comprehensive cinematic blueprints with character profiles, scene descriptions, and cross-modal specifications; (2) a decoupled character-centric pipeline that maintains identity consistency through instance-level tracking and integration while enabling flexible multi-character composition; and (3) a hierarchical audio-visual synchronization mechanism ensuring frame-level alignment of dialogue, expressions, and music. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CineAGI achieves 40\% improvement in overall consistency, 4.4\% gain in subject consistency, 5.4\% enhancement in aesthetic quality, and 28.7\% higher character consistency compared to baselines. Our work establishes a principled foundation for automated long-form video generation that preserves narrative coherence and character authenticity.
