records.title: GAPR: General Attribute-Guided Mixture-of-Prompts for Vision-Language Generalization
records.abstract: Prompt learning has emerged as an effective lightweight strategy for adapting Vision–Language Models (VLMs). However, existing text-based approaches still suffer from key limitations: a single soft prompt struggles to account for diverse visual styles, unconstrained tuning may lead to overfitting, and restricting the prompt space to predefined categories limits generalization to unseen classes. To overcome these issues, we propose GAPR (Generalizable Attribute Prompt Routing). GAPR expands the prompt space from a category-only formulation to a richer attribute–category space, and introduces a dynamic routing mechanism to adaptively select prompts for each image. A large language model is first used to derive E representative attributes for each category, which serve as shared semantic anchors. Based on these anchors, we construct E attribute-specific soft prompts paired with category tokens. An attribute-driven contrastive constraint further enhances discrimination by encouraging intra-class compactness and inter-attribute diversity. To achieve adaptive alignment, a lightweight routing module selects the top-k attribute prompts according to image features and aggregates their embeddings into the final text representation. As a plug-and-play component, GAPR can be integrated into existing prompt-learning frameworks with minimal overhead. Experiments on eleven benchmarks show that GAPR consistently improves performance in both domain generalization and base-to-novel generalization settings, demonstrating strong robustness and scalability.

records.title: Disentangling Sentiment from Logic: A Financial Multimodal Dual-Process Agent
records.abstract: Existing multimodal large language models in finance often suffer from cognitive interference, failing to reconcile market sentiment with fundamental logic. As a result, they often prioritize token probability over safety, leading to reckless allocation during market panic. To address this, we introduce the Financial Multimodal Dual-Process Agent (FinMDPA), a novel framework that uses Dual-Process Theory to disentangle affective noise from rational trends. We propose Uni-Quant Tokenization to project heterogeneous visual charts and vocal prosody into a shared semantic space, ensuring robust multimodal grounding. To prevent feature collapse, we implement Dual-Path LoRA, which routes signals through orthogonal affective and cognitive pathways to explicitly separate System 1 intuition from System 2 reasoning. Furthermore, we align the execution policy with prudent risk standards via Risk-Aware Direct Preference Optimization. Extensive experiments on the 30 constituent stocks of the Dow Jones Industrial Average during the high-volatility periods of 2023 and 2024 demonstrate that FinMDPA significantly outperforms baselines by at least 7.3% in cumulative returns and 0.39 in Sharpe Ratio.

records.title: Category-Aware Fine-Tuning of Vision-Language Model for Grading-Oriented Handwritten Mathematical Expression Recognition
records.abstract: Handwritten mathematical expression recognition (HMER) for automatic grading differs fundamentally from generic optical character recognition (OCR). Large handwriting variability and the inherently two-dimensional structure of mathematical notation often pose great challenge to purely vision-driven image-to-LaTeX recognition. In real grading workflows, however, the reference answer is typically available, providing a label-aware prior that can constrain recognition rather than treating it as free-form recognition. Motivated by this, we formulate grading-oriented HMER as a constrained OCR problem and fine-tune a vision--language model (Qwen3-VL-4B) via a prompt-driven multi-task objective. Our framework integrates two complementary tasks: (i) category-conditioned recognition, where decoding is guided by a symbol-category prior derived from the LaTeX label to reduce ambiguity; and (ii) image--LaTeX matching, which explicitly verifies the equivalence between a handwritten expression image and a candidate LaTeX string. The two tasks are mutually reinforcing: the category prior injects structural cues into generation, while the matching objective regularizes the model toward semantic consistency. Without altering the base architecture, the proposed approach improves robustness to handwriting noise and style diversity, enhancing the reliability required in practical homework and exam grading. Experiments on benchmark HMER datasets demonstrate consistent gains over strong image-only HMER baselines.

records.title: Beyond Text: Inferring Fedspeak Policy Stance via Multimodal Cues and Agentic Historical Memory
records.abstract: The accurate interpretation of Federal Reserve communications (Fedspeak) is critical for financial forecasting and market stability. While recent Large Language Model (LLM) approaches have made progress by incorporating economic reasoning paths, they predominantly rely on textual data. Consequently, they overlook rich multimodal cues in press conferences and often lack dynamic access to historical context. In this paper, we propose a novel multimodal and retrieval-augmented framework for Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) policy stance analysis. First, we introduce a robust pipeline to align video timestamps with transcripts. This enables the extraction of audio features such as pitch, rhythm, and energy. Second, we enhance the model via a multi-stage contextual knowledge integration process. This mechanism adopts structured domain knowledge and utilizes an agentic retrieval system to ensure historical consistency. By fine-tuning a foundation LLM on this enhanced dataset, our method significantly outperforms existing text-only baselines. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on the FOMC benchmark, validating the efficacy of integrating paralinguistic signals with dynamic historical memory.

records.title: Low Entropy Enhances Stability: Image-Text Dual-Guided Classifier for CLIP-Based Class-Incremental Learning
records.abstract: Class-Incremental Learning (CIL) enables models to learn new classes sequentially while retaining previously acquired knowledge. Recently, vision-language models (e.g., CLIP) have provided a powerful foundation for CIL. However, CLIP is trained via contrastive learning to build a cross-modal representation manifold, rather than to produce discriminative, low-entropy predictions. As a result, most existing works rely on CLIP’s built-in cosine-similarity-based classifier, which leads to high-entropy predictions. This high-entropy state renders predictions susceptible to perturbations, exacerbating forgetting and thus compromising model stability. To address this issue, we propose a Image-Text Dual-Guided Classifier (DGC), trained with discriminative image and text in two stages. In the first stage, DGC is initialized with class prototypes and trained solely on image data to capture low-level visual patterns. In the second stage, high-level discriminative class knowledge is injected into DGC by generating contrastive texts using GPT-4. Furthermore, we introduce a mixup strategy to fuse image and text features, enhancing cross-modal synergy. By integrating DGC into two representative methods, notable performance gains across nine benchmarks demonstrate its effectiveness in mitigating the high-entropy issue and catastrophic forgetting.

records.title: GoCoMA: Hyperbolic Multimodal Representation Fusion for Large Language Model-Generated Code Attribution
records.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) trained on massive code corpora are now increasingly capable of generating code that is hard to distinguish from human-written code. This raises practical concerns, including security vulnerabilities and licensing ambiguity, and also motivates a forensic question: ‘Who (or which LLM) wrote this piece of code?’ We present GoCoMA, a multimodal framework that models an extrinsic hierarchy between (i) code stylometry, capturing higher-level structural and stylistic signatures, and (ii) image representations of binary pre-executable artifacts (BPEA), capturing lower-level, execution-oriented byte semantics shaped by compilation and toolchains. GoCoMA projects modality embeddings into a hyperbolic Poincaré ball, fuses them via a geodesic similarity-based cross-modal attention (GCSA) fusion mechanism, and back-projects the fused representation to Euclidean space for final LLM-source attribution. Experiments on two open-source benchmarks (CoDET-M4 and LLMAuthorBench) show that GoCoMA consistently outperforms unimodal and Euclidean multimodal baselines under identical evaluation protocols.

records.title: NPRCap:Neighbor Prompt Re-ranking and Semantic Anchor Distillation for Image Captioning
records.abstract: Image captioning has advanced with pretrained models and text prompts. However, retrieval-based prompts often lack semantic consistency with the image, making fine-grained alignment between the image and prompts difficult. To address the issue, we propose NPRCap, which improves vision–language alignment through fine-grained prompt re-ranking and semantic anchor distillation. First, we design a Fine-Grained Neighbor Prompt Re-ranking module that refines the ordering of prompts by adjusting their priority according to similarity, ensuring that the most representative of the image semantics are prioritized. Additionally, we propose a semantic anchor distillation module that aggregates high-frequency semantically consistent keywords as anchors to guide text generation. Moreover, we construct explicit instruction templates via replace vague prompts with precise directing words, further enhance the contextual consistency. Experiments on the MS COCO and NoCaps datasets demonstrate that NPRCap outperforms state-of-the-art methods across various metrics, achieving a best-in-class CIDEr score of 120.3%.

records.title: Benchmarking and Improving Abstract Visual Reasoning via Multimodal Self-Refinement
records.abstract: Text-to-Image Models (T2IMs) excel at visualizing explicit instructions but struggle to translate high-level concepts, metaphors, and cultural entities into coherent visuals. Current evaluations focus on fidelity for concrete captions, leaving abstract visual reasoning unexplored. To address this gap, we introduce a multi-domain benchmark of 1,800 abstract concepts across six culturally diverse domains, rendered in Cartoon and Minimalist styles. We further propose Iterative Self-Refinement (ISR), a closed-loop framework coordinating an LLM, T2IM, and MLLM that unifies generation and evaluation in a single reasoning step. Experiments across 10 LLMs and 10 MLLMs, validated by expert annotation (Fleiss' κ = 0.69), show that ISR achieves substantial gains over T2IM-only baselines (+14.7% Cartoon, +12.9% Minimalist) and reveal complementary strengths between human and model reasoning, with MLLMs excelling on visually-grounded domains while humans outperform on imagination-based categories.

records.title: From Arithmetic to Agents: Towards Autonomous Model Fusion with Large Language Models
records.abstract: The paradigm of fine-tuning pre-trained foundation models for diverse tasks has spurred significant interest in post-training model merging, which aims to combine task-specific models without raw data. However, prevailing methods like TIES-MERGING rely on static, predefined rules, struggling with complex inter-task conflicts due to their lack of granularity. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel paradigm that shifts from algorithmic execution to intelligent decision-making. This paper introduces the Multi-Agent Parameter Fusion Framework (MAF), an automated framework where a Large Language Model (LLM) acts as the \textit{\textbf{brain}} for model merging. MAF features a closed-loop process of perception, decision, and execution: it first diagnoses parameter-space conflicts, then uses an LLM agent to dynamically plan a layer-wise merging strategy, and finally executes the plan. Experiments on multi-task benchmarks with Vision Transformers demonstrate that MAF significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in accuracy and robustness, offering a scalable and interpretable solution for model fusion.

records.title: Boosting Knowledge-based Visual Question Answering with Structured Context Reasoning
records.abstract: Knowledge-based Visual Question Answering aims to answer questions about an image by integrating external knowledge with visual and textual information. Recent approaches often rely on in-context learning to prompt Large Language Models (LLMs) with multimodal context in a zero-shot or few-shot manner. However, we observe that directly concatenating heterogeneous visual descriptions and retrieved knowledge into long, unstructured prompts often degrades reasoning performance, due to both excessive irrelevant context and the lack of explicit relational structure. In this paper, we propose an LLM-based Structured Context Reasoning (SCoRe) framework that infers both explicit and implicit relationships for prediction. SCoRe consists of three stages: Context Acquisition, which generates diverse visual notes and retrieves explicit knowledge via an efficient two-stage multimodal retrieval strategy; Context Selection, which filters relevant visual, explicit, and implicit knowledge using LLM-guided selection; and Context Compression, which performs Relational Logic Distillation (RLD) to transform raw text into explicit entity-relation triplets. These relational triplets serve as a concise and structured prompt for final answer prediction. Extensive experiments on the OK-VQA and A-OKVQA benchmarks demonstrate that SCoRe consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

records.title: A Few-shot Segmentation Method via Integrating Global Category Prototypes and Contrastive Learning
records.abstract: Few-shot semantic segmentation (FSS) aims to segment novel categories from limited annotated examples, posing challenges for robust representation learning. Existing methods rely on episode-specific prototypes, which are sensitive to background clutter, pose variations, and partial observations, and often fail to capture consistent global category structures despite attention or contrastive mechanisms. To address these limitations, we propose \textbf{GCPNet}, an end-to-end framework that integrates dynamically updated Global Category Prototypes with supervised contrastive learning. The global prototype module aggregates support features across episodes to provide stable semantic anchors, while the contrastive module enforces intra-class compactness and inter-class separation. A prototype-guided decoder transfers support-derived semantics to query features, enabling robust and generalizable segmentation. Experiments on PASCAL-$5^i$ and COCO-$20^i$ show that GCPNet achieves state-of-the-art performance under both 1-shot and 5-shot settings.

records.title: Coarse to Refined: Multi-MLLM Knowledge Distillation for Out-of-Context News Detection
records.abstract: Out-of-context news is a form of multimodal misinformation, where the image is used outside of its original context. Although recent works leverage MLLMs to detect such news, existing methods rely heavily on large MLLMs, extensive annotated data, and costly API calls. In this work, we enhance small MLLMs in a label-efficient and cost-effective way. We employ multiple teacher MLLMs to generate label predictions and corresponding rationales as supervisory knowledge and propose a two-stage knowledge distillation framework to transfer knowledge to a student MLLM. Stage 1 quickly familiarizes the student model with the teachers' knowledge via LoRA fine-tuning. Stage 2 further refines the student model's discernment on teachers' conflicting predictions via LoRA-guided DPO learning. This approach reduces annotation costs and helps the student model to discover underlying patterns in more difficult cases. Experiments show that our approach achieves state-of-the-art results using only less than 10% labeled data.

records.title: NPSA Restoring VLM Semantics via Neuro-Physical Alignment in Adverse Conditions
records.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) struggle in adverse illumination where RGB semantics degrade, disrupting regiontext alignment. To address this in Multispectral Object Detection, we propose the Neuro-Physical Semantics Alignment (NPSA) framework. Unlike standard symmetric fusion, NPSA adopts an asymmetric design: a frozen RGB stream preserves pretrained linguistic priors, while a lightweight IR stream extracts physical structures via explicit gradient injection. Central to our approach is the Neuro-Physical Fusion (NPFusion) mechanism, which employs subspace orthogonalization to isolate unique thermal primitives and biophysical shunting inhibition to dynamically suppress visual noise. This ensures robust structure injection without contaminating the semantic manifold. Extensive experiments demonstrate that NPSA achieves state-of-the-art performance, effectively extending open-vocabulary capabilities to robust closed-set detection in challenging low-light scenarios.

records.title: Genesis: Evolving Attack Strategies for LLM Web Agent Red-Teaming
records.abstract: As large language model (LLM) agents automate complex web tasks, they boost productivity while simultaneously introducing new security risks. However, relevant studies on web agent attacks remain limited. Existing red-teaming approaches mainly rely on manually crafted attack strategies or static models trained offline. Such methods fail to capture the underlying behavioral patterns of web agents, making it difficult to generalize across diverse environments. In web agent attacks, success requires the continuous discovery and evolution of attack strategies. To this end, we propose Genesis, a novel agentic framework composed of three modules: Attacker, Scorer, and Strategist. The Attacker generates adversarial injections by integrating the genetic algorithm with a hybrid strategy representation. The Scorer evaluates the target web agent’s responses to provide feedback. The Strategist dynamically uncovers effective strategies from interaction logs and compiles them into a continuously growing strategy library, which is then re-deployed to enhance the Attacker’s effectiveness. Extensive experiments across various web tasks show that our framework discovers novel strategies and consistently outperforms existing attack baselines. Our code is available at https://github.com/CjangCjengh/web_agent_attack.

records.title: Vision-Language Alignment with LLM Encoders: Enhancing the Discriminability of Text Embeddings
records.abstract: CLIP learns a well-aligned multi-modal embedding space, but faces constrained capacities of its text encoder. Recent efforts replace it with an LLM-based embedder and learn a new joint embedding space from scratch through contrastive learning, yet they show inconsistent performance variations across retrieval and zero-shot classification tasks. Our empirical analysis reveals two factors associated with this gap: (1) LLM text embeddings have low discriminability, blurring decision boundaries, and (2) retrieval and classification objectives in CLIP-style models differ in sensitivity to embedding discriminability. To this end, we propose DNSCLIP, a two-stage framework that improves vision-language alignment with an LLM-based embedder via enhancing the discriminability of text embeddings. Specifically, Stage I employs Semantic and Relational Distillation to align LLM embeddings to the CLIP joint embedding space and distill pre-trained discriminative knowledge, while Stage II introduces a Gradient Null Space Projection module to preserve the pre-trained strengths learned in Stage I during cross-modal alignment. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DNSCLIP significantly improves vision-language alignment while effectively mitigating generalization degradation.

records.title: EmoCaustics: A Large-Scale Multi-Party Dialogue Benchmark for Large Language Models in Emotional Causality Reasoning
records.abstract: Emotional Causality Reasoning (ECR) in long-form, multi-participant dialogues is severely hampered by the critical challenges of capturing distant causal dependencies across extensive conversational turns, accurately modeling the dynamic evolution of emotional states through interlinked event chains, and disentangling intricate influence patterns and attributions amidst complex multi-party interactions. Existing benchmarks largely fail to provide adequate scale and annotation depth to investigate these specific complexities. To confront these obstacles, we introduce HELIX, a large-scale dataset featuring 1,000 long-form, multi-participant dialogues averaging over 200 turns. HELIX features detailed annotations capturing causal event chains and attributing emotional shifts to specific sources. We further propose EmoCaustics, a framework to break these long-dependency and multi-party constraints. Through its dynamic context windows, event-centric memory, and structured event aggregation mechanisms, EmoCaustics effectively addresses the key challenges of capturing distant dependencies, modeling dynamic causal evolution, and disentangling complex multi-party influences. Extensive experiments demonstrate EmoCaustics significantly enhances LLM performance on the HELIX benchmark, effectively mitigating the identified challenges and establishing robust baselines for complex dialogue ECR. Our framework significantly surpasses GPT-o1 in key metrics including emotion state accuracy and source identifier matching.

records.title: MPLCA: Multi-modal Prompt Learning with Category Alignment for AI-generated Image Detection
records.abstract: Insufficient modality collaboration and semantic misalignment are two critical challenges that hinder the performance of pre-trained vision–language models in AI-generated image detection. These issues weaken their ability to capture subtle visual artifacts and to maintain coherent cross-modal semantics. To address these challenges, we present a Multi-modal Prompt Learning with Category Alignment (MPLCA) algorithm, which strengthens visual–textual interactions and enhances category-level semantic coherence. Specifically, MPLCA injects learnable prompts into both the visual and textual encoders and incorporates a coupling function to facilitate effective cross-modal interaction, thereby enhancing the detection of synthesized image artifacts. In addition, MPLCA introduces dynamically tuned ``real/fake'' category embeddings along with a hierarchical alignment loss to further alleviate semantic misalignment. Experiments conducted on 18 fake-image datasets—including both GAN-generated images and commercially produced forgeries—demonstrate that MPLCA surpasses prior state-of-the-art methods with a notable improvement in average accuracy.

records.title: Better Composition: Photography Guidance by Simple Instructions
records.abstract: Image composition fundamentally determines the aesthetic quality of photographs, yet achieving the optimal view in real-time remains a challenge due to dynamic shooting conditions. To address this, we propose a real-time photographic composition guidance system based on Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). We first construct a dataset of ``large-small'' image pairs to train a Composition Prediction Network (CPN) that accurately identifies the optimal composition type. This prediction guides a View Adjustment Network (VAN), which employs an Actor-Critic framework integrated with Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) and LSTM units to dynamically adjust camera viewpoints via translation, scaling, and rotation. The optimization process relies on a comprehensive multi-task reward function that accounts for classification confidence, aesthetic improvements, and the retention of key compositional elements. We validate our approach through extensive quantitative experiments, ablation studies, and subjective user evaluations. Furthermore, the system is deployed on mobile devices with an inference speed of 33ms per step. Experimental results demonstrate that our method produces visually superior and compositionally balanced images in diverse environments.

records.title: CoCo-CoT: Collaborative and Consistent Multimodal Chain-of-Thought for MLLMs
records.abstract: Multimodal Chain-of-Thought (CoT) has shown remarkable visual reasoning capabilities in MLLMs. However, existing methods still suffer from hallucination in the reasoning process, mainly due to insufficient visual information and the absence of effective evaluation mechanisms. In this paper, we aim to enhance the reasoning quality and reliability in multimodal CoT under a zero-shot setting. Inspired by the human cognitive process of addressing complex tasks, we propose a Collaborative and Consistent multimodal Chain-of-Thought (CoCo-CoT) framework based on a Decision-Reasoning-Evaluation architecture with a multi-agent and multi-path collaborative reasoning mechanism. Unlike previous CoT methods, the CoCo-CoT framework performs initial analysis and actively raises questions about visual information to formulate structured perceptual decisions. To improve stability, our CoCo-CoT framework evaluates consistency across collaborative reasoning paths through cross-validation thinking and iterative self-refinement. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness and generalizability of the CoCo-CoT framework, which achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot performance across two multimodal reasoning benchmarks.

records.title: HiCrew: Hierarchical Reasoning for Long-Form Video Understanding via Question-Aware Multi-Agent Collaboration
records.abstract: Long-form video understanding remains fundamentally challenged by pervasive spatiotemporal redundancy and intricate narrative dependencies that span extended temporal horizons. While recent structured representations compress visual information effectively, they frequently sacrifice temporal coherence, which is critical for causal reasoning. Meanwhile, existing multi-agent frameworks operate through rigid, pre-defined workflows that fail to adapt their reasoning strategies to question-specific demands. In this paper, we introduce HiCrew, a hierarchical multi-agent framework that addresses these limitations through three core contributions. First, we propose a Hybrid Tree structure that leverages shot boundary detection to preserve temporal topology while performing relevance-guided hierarchical clustering within semantically coherent segments. Second, we develop a Question-Aware Captioning mechanism that synthesizes intent-driven visual prompts to generate precision-oriented semantic descriptions. Third, we integrate a Planning Layer that dynamically orchestrates agent collaboration by adaptively selecting roles and execution paths based on question complexity. Extensive experiments on EgoSchema and NExT-QA validate the effectiveness of our approach, demonstrating strong performance across diverse question types with particularly pronounced gains in temporal and causal reasoning tasks that benefit from our hierarchical structure-preserving design. Our codebase is available at https://github.com/SYSUzzz/HiCrew

records.title: LSI: Latent Syllogistic Inversion for Overcoming Safety Resistance in LLMs
records.abstract: Current safety alignment in Large Language Models (LLMs) often neutralizes traditional jailbreak backdoors through a "Resistance Phenomenon," where models interrupt compliant responses. To overcome this, we introduce Latent Syllogistic Inversion (LSI), a universal jailbreak backdoor designed for black-box data poisoning. Unlike shallow trigger-response mappings, LSI implants a "cognitive backdoor" activated by a Distributed Semantic Trigger (DST)—a stealthy style mimicking academic audits. Upon activation, the model generates an inverted syllogism via Chain-of-Thought (CoT) that rationalizes malicious queries as authorized safety tests, effectively resolving cognitive dissonance. Extensive experiments on Llama-3.1 and GPT-4o-mini demonstrate that LSI achieves state-of-the-art attack success rates (>80%) while preserving general capabilities. This reveals a critical vulnerability: safety mechanisms can be "psychologically hijacked" to justify their own violation.

records.title: CATS: Content-Context Aggregation Two-Stage Adaptation for Vision-Language Model
records.abstract: In vision-language model adaptation, visual context can both aid recognition and introduce bias, making it important to balance subject and contextual cues for robust generalization. We propose CATS, a simple two-view, two-stage framework that separates subject-focused and panoramic views, learns complementary view-specific semantics, and adapts decision boundaries with text-initialized classifiers. To better handle the different characteristics of base and novel classes, CATS further uses class-adaptive prediction heads and fusion strategies at inference time. As a model-agnostic module, CATS consistently improves strong prompt-learning baselines on both base and novel categories across multiple benchmarks.

records.title: Towards Faithful Sentimental Image Captioning via Evidence-Aware Multi-Agent Reasoning
records.abstract: Sentimental Image Captioning (SIC) requires balancing emotional expression with visual fidelity. Existing methods often struggle with this trade-off, leading to hallucinations due to insufficient local grounding and the lack of sentimental verification mechanisms. To address these limitations, we propose SEA-Cap, a Sentiment-Evidence-Aware Multi-Agent System for faithful and evidence-grounded sentimental image captioning. SEA-Cap incorporates a Sentiment Evidence Miner that extracts structured, local affective cues to shift sentiment control from global attributes to verifiable object-level evidence. Leveraging this evidence, our framework orchestrates a collaborative workflow where a Generator, Hallucination Checker, and Arbitrator iteratively refine captions via a shared blackboard. By explicitly auditing generated content against mined visual evidence, SEA-Cap ensures both sentiment accuracy and factual consistency. Extensive experiments on two benchmark datasets demonstrate that SEA-Cap effectively mitigates hallucinations and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

records.title: Table-Centric MultiModal GraphRAG: Enhancing Cross-Modal Reasoning via Table-Driven Dynamic Graph Communities
records.abstract: Abstract—Retrieval-Augmented Generation using graphs (GraphRAG) shows significant promise in addressing the challenges of large language models by enhancing their textual reasoning capabilities. Despite its remarkable success, GraphRAG remains inherently limited to unimodal processing, struggling with complex scenarios that require reasoning across heterogeneous data. To mitigate this limitation, we propose a TableCentric MultiModal GraphRAG (TCMM-GRAG) framework, a table-centric extension of GraphRAG for multimodal reasoning. TCMM-GRAG introduces a table-centric framework by leveraging the structured, low-noise, and high-density nature of tables as a central hub. This table-centric design anchors the reasoning process and enables highly efficient cross-modal information retrieval and fusion. Furthermore, TCMM-GRAG dynamically builds table-centric multimodal knowledge graphs for hierarchical summarization, which can drive a structured and verifiable reasoning chain. An extensive experiment on two challenging multimodal question-answering benchmarks demonstrates that TCMM-GRAG achieves new state-of-the-art performance with significant improvements over previous baselines. records.title: Dual-Path Stable Soft Prompt Generation for Domain Generalization
records.abstract: Domain generalization (DG) aims to train models on related source domains that generalize to unseen out-of-distribution target domains. Prompt tuning of large pre-trained vision-language models (VLMs) improves DG but lacks domain-specific features due to fixed prompt inputs. Recent generation methods have addressed this limitation by dynamically generating instance-specific and domain-specific prompts, but suffer from Prompt Variability: the same input often yields different and suboptimal prompts across different random seeds. To address this, we introduce negative learning into prompt generation and propose Dual-Path Stable Soft Prompt Generation (DPSPG), a transformer-based framework via a complementary prompt generator producing negative prompts to reduce misleading information. Theoretical and empirical analyses confirm that negative learning increases the effective margin and lowers an upper bound on the gradient norm, yielding more robust prompts. Extensive experiments on five DG benchmark datasets show that DPSPG consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods while maintaining prompt stability.

records.title: UA-MR: Uncertainty-Aware Multi-Relation Learning for Short-Baseline Binocular 3D Human Pose Estimation under Highly Dynamic Motion
records.abstract: 3D human pose estimation is fundamental to motion-centric analysis, yet existing methods degrade under highly dynamic actions with abrupt spatiotemporal variations. Short-baseline binocular cameras offer practical depth cues with low deployment cost, but dynamic motion introduces two core challenges: (i) severe depth uncertainty caused by weak stereo disparity and fast joint movements, and (ii) limited robustness due to reliance on handcrafted priors for modeling cross-camera relationships. To address these challenges, we propose UA-MR, an uncertainty-aware multi-relation framework for highly dynamic binocular 3D pose estimation. UA-MR explicitly models uncertainty and employs uncertainty-aware spatial and temporal attention to reconstruct unreliable joints from confident spatiotemporal context, while a multi-relation learning strategy based on heterogeneous auxiliary tasks implicitly captures binocular correlations without explicit geometric assumptions. To support evaluation, we introduce Bi-DynPose, a challenging benchmark of complex sports actions. Experiments on Human3.6M, MHAD, and Bi-DynPose demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, especially under highly dynamic motion conditions.

records.title: UltraGS: Real-Time Physically-Decoupled Gaussian Splatting for Ultrasound Novel View Synthesis
records.abstract: Ultrasound imaging is a cornerstone of non-invasive clinical diagnostics, yet its limited field of view poses challenges for novel view synthesis. We present UltraGS, a real-time framework that adapts Gaussian Splatting to sensorless ultrasound imaging by integrating explicit radiance fields with lightweight, physics-inspired acoustic modeling. UltraGS employs depth-aware Gaussian primitives with learnable fields of view to improve geometric consistency under unconstrained probe motion, and introduces PD Rendering, a differentiable acoustic operator that combines low-order spherical harmonics with first-order wave effects for efficient intensity synthesis. We further present a clinical ultrasound dataset acquired under real-world scanning protocols. Extensive evaluations across three datasets demonstrate that UltraGS establishes a new performance-efficiency frontier, achieving state-of-the-art results in PSNR (up to 29.55) and SSIM (up to 0.89) while achieving real-time synthesis at 64.69 fps on a single GPU. records.title: ILSF-Net: A Lightweight Image-LiDAR Sparse Fusion Network for 3D Object Detection
records.abstract: 3D object detection faces challenges in fusing sparse point clouds with semantically rich but geometrically imprecise color images. Projection methods suffer from calibration and alignment errors, whereas BEV fusion methods have a high computational cost. To address these issues, we propose ILSF-Net, an Image-LiDAR Sparse Fusion Network that integrates geometric and semantic information through three innovations: (1) A semantic voxel generator that samples multiscale image features using voxel centroids via bilinear interpolation, eliminating depth estimation dependencies, and reducing alignment errors. (2) A heterogeneous U-shaped feature diffusion module with separate geometric (local aggregation) and semantic (multiscale attention) operations to address modality imbalance. (3) A domain accumulative attention module that performs sparse cross-attention between instances and adaptively sampled domain features for efficient refinement. The results show that ILSF-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance while maintaining real-time efficiency.

records.title: S-VGGT: Structure-Aware Subscene Decomposition for Scalable 3D Foundation Models
records.abstract: Feed-forward 3D foundation models face a key challenge: the quadratic computational cost introduced by global attention, which severely limits scalability as input length increases. Concurrent acceleration methods, such as token merging, operate at the token level. While they offer local savings, the required nearest-neighbor searches introduce undesirable overhead. Consequently, these techniques fail to tackle the fundamental issue of structural redundancy dominant in dense capture data. In this work, we introduce S-VGGT, a novel approach that addresses redundancy at the structural frame level, drastically shifting the optimization focus. We first leverage the initial features to build a dense scene graph, which characterizes structural scene redundancy and guides the subsequent scene partitioning. Using this graph, we softly assign frames into a small number of subscenes, guaranteeing balanced groups and smooth geometric transitions. The core innovation lies in designing the subscenes to share a common reference frame, establishing a parallel geometric bridge that enables independent and highly efficient processing without explicit geometric alignment. This structural reorganization provides strong intrinsic acceleration by cutting the global attention cost at its source. Crucially, S-VGGT is entirely orthogonal to token-level acceleration methods, allowing the two to be seamlessly combined for compounded speedups without compromising reconstruction fidelity.

records.title: GCoT: Grounding Spatial Reasoning with Chain-of-Thought in 3D Scenes
records.abstract: 3D vision-language models (3D VLMs) have recently achieved strong performance on static perception tasks such as grounding, captioning, and question answering. However, they remain fragile on \emph{dynamic spatial reasoning} in answering ``what if'' and ``how to'' questions that require simulating viewpoint changes, resolving occlusions, or planning multi-step interactions in a static scene. We address this gap with \textbf{Grounding Chain-of-Thought (GCoT)}, a framework that equips 3D VLMs with structured, geometrically verifiable reasoning. GCoT decomposes complex queries into three phases (Scene Parsing, Perspective Taking, and Interaction Simulation) and enforces \emph{Scene-Information} (\texttt{ }) tags that explicitly cite 3D evidence at each step. We further construct a large-scale grounded CoT dataset with automatic geometric checks and multi-agent LLM verification. Experiments on SCoT, MSQA, and Beacon3D show that GCoT substantially improves analysis and planning performance and grounding–QA coherence while preserving basic perception.

records.title: Body Regional Guidance for Semi-supervised Human Pose Estimation
records.abstract: Human pose estimation under limited annotations is challenging due to keypoint supervision is naturally sparse and error-prone. Recent semi-supervised approaches reduce labeling costs by leveraging pseudo-labels, where teacher predictions serve as supervision for unlabeled samples. However, these methods often overlook the sparsity and fallibility of pseudo keypoint labels, leading to error accumulation and weak robustness to background interference. To address this, we present BRG-Pose, a semi-supervised framework that introduces dense regional guidance to regularize sparse keypoint learning. We design a zero-shot human parsing branch to provide dense segmentation guidance for body regions, injecting structural cues without additional annotations. Guided by these region masks, our proposed region-guided selection module adaptively chooses the appropriate pseudo-label type, either relaxed or Gaussian, based on regional consistency, effectively reducing background noise. Experiments on various labeled data settings demonstrate the effectiveness of our BRG-Pose.

records.title: Geometry-Adaptive 3D Convex Polyhedron for Tomographic Reconstruction
records.abstract: While Gaussian-based methods advance novel view synthesis, they struggle to capture the complex density fields and hard boundaries essential for computed tomography. We propose a novel reconstruction framework based on geometry-adaptive 3D convex polyhedral primitives. Our method employs a set of deformable 3D convex polyhedral primitives that adaptively tailor spatial-varying density distributions in the tomographic scene. Each primitive is parameterized by bounding planes and an associated density field, enabling more flexible shape representation to model complex internal structures than Gaussian-based representations, such as sharp boundaries and spiky shapes, particularly suitable for computed tomography applications. For efficient optimization, we introduce a fast differentiable rasterizer tailored to X-ray physics imaging, simulating X-ray images through an unordered convex density-accumulation strategy, unlike alpha-blending in RGB images. Experiments on diverse X-ray datasets demonstrate our method outperforms prior methods in novel view synthesis by 3.66 dB in PSNR and 1.40% in SSIM, showing better geometric interpretability.

records.title: M-Gaussian: Magnetic 3D Gaussian for Slice-to-Volume MRI Reconstruction
records.abstract: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is a crucial non-invasive imaging modality. Clinical practice often acquires multi-stack thick-slice scans to reduce scan time, but this introduces severe anisotropy that compromises volumetric analysis, necessitating reconstruction of isotropic high-resolution volumes. Implicit neural representation methods, while achieving high quality, suffer from computational inefficiency due to complex network structures. We present M-Gaussian, adapting 3D Gaussian Splatting to MRI reconstruction. Our contributions include: (1) magnetic Gaussian primitives with physics-consistent volumetric rendering, (2) neural residual field for high-frequency detail refinement, and (3) multi-resolution progressive training. Our method achieves optimal balance between quality and speed. On the FeTA dataset, M-Gaussian achieves 40.31 dB PSNR while being 14 times faster, representing the first successful adaptation of 3D Gaussian Splatting to multi-stack MRI reconstruction.

records.title: GatedSketchNet: A Monocular Sketch-Driven Network for 3D Reconstruction
records.abstract: Monocular 3D reconstruction from hand-drawn sketches is challenging due to geometric uncertainty and the distinct characteristics of sketches versus natural images. Existing methods, such as Sketch2Vox, rely on feature extractors pre-trained on natural images, resulting in a domain gap and inadequate modeling of local spatial relationships. Our analysis confirms that directly transferring such models is suboptimal. To address this, we propose GatedSketchNet, introducing three innovations: (1) a Gated Sketch Feature Extraction Module to suppress sketch noise and preserve essential contours via adaptive gating mechanisms; (2) a Point Feature Extraction Module with Squeeze-and-Excitation mechanisms for improved inter-point correlation modeling; (3) a Cross-domain Feature Fusion Module that strengthens local spatial pattern learning using bidirectional convolutional attention. Experiments on Sketch3D and ModelNet show our method achieves mean IoU scores of 0.4582 and 0.4167, respectively, surpassing Sketch2Vox by 6.5% and 12.7%. This work offers a practical direction for cross-domain fusion in sketch-based 3D reconstruction.

records.title: Residual Adapter with Offset Correction for Accurate 3D Animal Mesh Recovery
records.abstract: Recovering precise 3D animal pose and shape from monocular images is inherently challenging, and existing methods often yield inaccurate predictions. Although Vision Transformer-based approaches provide robust global priors, their self-attention mechanisms can dilute local evidence, introducing systematic misalignment in fine-grained reconstruction. To address this, we propose a lightweight Residual Adapter (RA) that integrates with a frozen Transformer backbone for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT). Our framework incorporates two key components: Semantic Injection, which leverages learnable class tokens to mitigate inter-species ambiguity, and an Offset Correction module that functions as a non-linear compensator to rectify 2D-to-3D projection errors. Experiments on the Out-Of-Distribution (OOD) Animal Kingdom dataset demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms baselines, improving Percentage of Correct Keypoints (PCK@0.10) from 34.9 to 37.4 (+7.0% relative). These results confirm that RA enhances local geometric precision while preserving the robust 3D priors of the pre-trained backbone.

records.title: GraphiContact: Pose-aware Human-Scene Robust Contact Perception for Interactive Systems
records.abstract: Understanding human-scene contact is essential for enabling robust physical interaction in human–computer interaction (HCI) systems, including assistive monitoring, embodied AI, and rehabilitation support. However, existing methods often fail to capture fine-grained spatial relationships between the human body and the environment, particularly overlooking human pose as a key cue for accurate 3D contact prediction. To address this limitation, we propose GraphiContact, a novel framework that explicitly incorporates pose-aware features to improve contact point prediction and simultaneously enhance 3D human reconstruction accuracy. GraphiContact outputs a reconstructed 3D human mesh with contact annotations, enabling joint and mutually reinforcing optimization of reconstruction and contact reasoning. To further improve robustness under occlusion and perceptual noise—common challenges in real-world HCI scenarios—we introduce a Single-Image Multi-Infer Uncertainty (SIMU) strategy. Experiments on five benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms existing approaches on both contact prediction and 3D human reconstruction metrics. Our code, based on the GraphiContact method, provides comprehensive 3D human reconstruction and interaction analysis, and will be publicly available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/GraphiContact-BC56/.

records.title: SOV-CAD: Stepwise Orthographic Views Guided CAD Modeling Sequence Reconstruction
records.abstract: Reconstructing Computer-Aided Design (CAD) modeling sequences from images is crucial for preserving design intent and supporting parametric editing. However, existing methods typically generate full CAD sequences holistically, overlooking the iterative, feedback-driven nature of human design workflows. We address this limitation by introducing the rich stepwise visual supervision: at each modeling step, the system observes the target’s orthographic projections, the projections of the incrementally constructed model, and the active sketch, enabling informed action selection. To effectively leverage this on-the-fly feedback, we propose SOV-CAD, a framework that formulates CAD reconstruction as a sequential decision-making task and employs offline reinforcement learning with a Decision Transformer architecture. This design incorporates continuous visual feedback guided by geometric alignment rewards, resulting in a more accurate and human-like modeling process. Extensive experiments show that SOV-CAD surpasses state-of-the-art methods in CAD sequence reconstruction while exhibiting strong data efficiency. records.title: GAC-R: An Infrared Small Target Detection Model Based on Gaussian Annular Convolution Coupled with the RWKV Architecture
records.abstract: Detecting small infrared targets is intrinsically difficult due to the lack of detailed texture and the interference of complex environmental noise. Existing methods typically bifurcate into model-driven approaches utilizing handcrafted priors or data-driven deep networks, often failing to fully exploit the synergy between physical imaging mechanisms and representation learning. To bridge this gap, we propose GAC-R, a physics-informed detection network. Drawing inspiration from the thermal Point Spread Function (PSF), we design a Gaussian Annular Convolution (GAC) module. Unlike standard convolutions, GAC is explicitly constrained to learn isotropic, center-surround difference features, thereby effectively separating targets from anisotropic background clutter. Furthermore, to address the limitation of local receptive fields, we incorporate a multi-scale Receptance Weighted Key Value (RWKV) architecture. This allows the model to capture global long-range dependencies with linear computational complexity. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that GAC-R yields state-of-the-art detection accuracy and robust generalization, while meeting the stringent speed requirements of real-time applications.

records.title: Expansive Geometry Stabilization for Exemplar-free Continual Learning with Pre-trained Models
records.abstract: Exemplar-free Continual Learning (CL) acquires new classes without storing old samples, whereas classic CL can replay. With the rise of Pre-Trained Models (PTMs), most methods froze backbone and adapt via lightweight modules. Meanwhile, Neural Collapse (NC) motivates Equiangular Tight Frames (ETF) classification with maximally separated prototypes. However, in exemplar-free setting, existing NC-inspired methods often aggravate drift and forgetting. To address these issues, we propose Expansive Geometry Stabilization (EGS) for exemplar-free continual learning. During training, EGS assigns each task to an independent projection block via expansive ETF anchoring, which keeps old geometry stable and reduces drift. We further apply dual-level decorrelation to suppress cross-block interference. During inference, routed dual-path fusion combines local block predictions with a global classifier, reducing feature confusion and stabilizing predictions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EGS outperforms state-of-the-art methods across six benchmarks, notably exceeding the runner-up by 2.9$\%$ on OmniBenchmark.

records.title: TSplatter: Fast Few-View Thermal Splatting with RGB-Guided 3D Gaussians
records.abstract: Thermal 3D scene reconstruction is crucial for inspection, safety, and environmental monitoring, but existing methods typically require densely sampled thermal views and long optimization times. This makes them difficult to deploy in practical scenarios where thermal patterns evolve rapidly (e.g., heating and cooling cycles, industrial processes) or only a few thermal images can be captured per session. We present \emph{TSplatter}, a fast and data-efficient multimodal framework that reconstructs 3D thermal radiance fields from a pretrained RGB 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) model and only a handful of thermal views. TSplatter models thermal fields with a physically motivated spherical harmonic parameterization, converts a few thermal scans into per-Gaussian view-dependent thermal attributes via per-view thermal intensity estimation and visibility-aware spherical harmonic fitting, completes underconstrained regions through graph-based thermal propagation on Gaussian KNN graphs. A lightweight consistency-guided refinement then jointly adjusts geometry and thermal appearance to enforce cross-modal consistency. Experiments on diverse real-world RGB--thermal scenes show that TSplatter achieves higher thermal reconstruction fidelity while reducing per-session optimization time from tens of minutes to tens of seconds, making repeated few-view thermal recaptures practical for real deployments.

records.title: Learning Hierarchical Orthogonal Prototypes for Generalized Few-Shot 3D Point Cloud Segmentation
records.abstract: Generalized few-shot 3D point cloud segmentation aims to adapt to novel classes from only a few annotations while maintaining strong performance on base classes, but this remains challenging due to the inherent stability–plasticity tradeoff: adapting to novel classes can interfere with shared representations and cause base-class forgetting. We present HOP3D, a unified framework that learns hierarchical orthogonal prototypes with an entropy-based few-shot regularizer to enable robust novel-class adaptation without degrading base-class performance. HOP3D introduces hierarchical orthogonalization that decouples base and novel learning at both the gradient and representation levels, effectively mitigating base–novel interference. To further enhance adaptation under sparse supervision, we incorporate an entropy-based regularizer that leverages predictive uncertainty to refine prototype learning and promote balanced predictions. Extensive experiments on ScanNet200 and ScanNet++ demonstrate that HOP3D consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines under both 1-shot and 5-shot settings. records.title: Asymmetric Dual-Teacher Self-Training for Adapting Stereo Foundation Models
records.abstract: Stereo Foundation Models have demonstrated remarkable zero-shot generalization. However, leveraging unlabeled downstream data to further boost their performance, especially under domain shifts caused by visual corruptions, remains an underexplored bottleneck. To this end, we propose Asymmetric Dual-Teacher (ADT), a novel self-training framework for the source-free domain adaptation of stereo foundation models. Unlike conventional single-teacher paradigms, which often suffer from confirmation bias when coupling pseudo-label generation with reliability estimation, ADT explicitly decouples these roles. Specifically, a slow-evolving Anchor Teacher provides stable pseudo-disparity targets to preserve robust pre-trained priors, while a fast-evolving Active Teacher captures domain-specific error patterns to generate pixel-wise reliability for gated optimization. Furthermore, we introduce Unified Consistency Reliability (UCR), which fuses complementary geometric constraints (left-right and forward-backward consistency) with photometric cues. This approach yields a conservative, soft reliability map that effectively filters noisy supervision. Extensive evaluations across five diverse benchmarks, including KITTI, Middlebury, ETH3D, and challenging scenarios like Booster and DrivingStereo, demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in source-free adaptation.

records.title: SIC3D: Style Image Conditioned Text-to-3D Gaussian Splatting Generation
records.abstract: Recent progress in text-to-3D object generation enables the synthesis of detailed geometry from text input by leveraging 2D diffusion models and differentiable 3D representations. The first stage generates the 3D object content from text with a text-to-3DGS generation model. The second stage transfers style from a reference image to the 3DGS. Within this stylization stage, we introduce a novel Variational Stylized Score Distillation (VSSD) loss to effectively capture both global and local texture patterns while mitigating conflicts between geometry and appearance. A scaling regularization is further applied to prevent the emergence of artifacts and preserve the pattern from the style image. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SIC3D enhances geometric fidelity and style adherence, outperforming prior approaches in both qualitative and quantitative evaluations. records.title: Correcting Structural Hallucinations in 3DGS: A LiDAR-Prior Guided Diffusion Framework
records.abstract: High-fidelity scene reconstruction based on 3D Gaussian Splatting is crucial for autonomous driving simulation, but training with sparse data collected from real driving trajectories easily leads to overfitting and noticeable distortions during extrapolated novel-view synthesis. Existing approaches, such as geometric regularization or generative models, still struggle with structural ambiguity during reconstruction: the former provides only limited constraints, while the latter often produces artifacts or geometrically inconsistent results. To address this, we propose a geometry-aware inpainting framework that introduces LiDAR projection maps as explicit structural priors and injects them into a denoising process via ControlNet. During training, a forced guidance mask strategy is designed to randomly remove parts of the rendered input, compelling the model to rely more on geometric priors rather than defective visual cues. Experiments on the Waymo dataset demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in extrapolated view synthesis, validating the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework.

records.abstract: High-fidelity 360◦ object reconstruction from wide- baseline sparse views remains challenging for 3D Gaussian Splat- ting (3DGS). To handle incomplete observations, our In-Context Restoration Module leverages high-resolution generative capability to plausibly synthesize detailed content in unseen regions. These restored views are then used to drive a closed-loop refinement process via view perturbation, serving as reliable pseudo-labels. Experiments demonstrate that SOCon-GS significantly outperforms existing baselines, producing identity- preserving, high-resolution 360◦ reconstructions from sparse real-world object views.

records.title: Learning Fine-Grained Geometry for Sparse-View Splatting via Cascade Depth Loss
records.abstract: Novel view synthesis is a fundamental task in 3D computer vision that aims to reconstruct photorealistic images from novel viewpoints given a set of posed images. However, reconstruction quality degrades sharply under sparse-view conditions due to insufficient geometric cues. Existing methods, including Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) and more recent 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), often exhibit blurred details and structural artifacts when trained from sparse observations. Recent works have identified rendered depth quality as a key factor in mitigating these artifacts, as it directly affects geometric accuracy and view consistency. However, effectively leveraging depth under sparse views remains challenging. Depth priors can be noisy or misaligned with rendered geometry, and single-scale supervision often fails to capture both global structure and fine details. To address these challenges, we introduce Hierarchical Depth-Guided Splatting (HDGS), a depth supervision framework that progressively refines geometry from coarse to fine levels. Central to HDGS is our novel Cascade Pearson Correlation Loss (CPCL), which enforces consistency between rendered and estimated depth priors across multiple spatial scales. By enforcing multi-scale depth consistency, our method improves structural fidelity in sparse-view reconstruction. Experiments on LLFF and DTU demonstrate state-of-the-art performance under sparse-view settings.

records.title: HA-GaussianDet: Multi-View 3D Object Detection via Height-Aware Sampling and Gaussian BEV Fusion
records.abstract: In surround-view camera–based bird’s-eye-view (BEV) 3D object detection, feature fusion across cameras remains challenging due to inherent cross-view discrepancies, slight extrinsic drift, and view-dependent occlusions. Existing grid-level fusion methods inadequately model spatial uncertainty and lack the continuity needed to preserve fine semantic structures, resulting in the loss of elongated features and geometric inconsistencies near camera boundaries. In this work, we propose HA-GaussianDet, a BEV-based detection framework that introduces Gaussian BEV Fusion to enable continuous, differentiable, and spatially adaptive multi-view feature fusion. By leveraging learnable Gaussian anchors, the proposed method explicitly encodes geometric uncertainty and visibility variations, and performs Gaussian-weighted feature rendering on a unified BEV plane. This design enhances structural continuity across viewpoints and significantly improves geometric consistency. Extensive experiments on the nuScenes dataset demonstrate that HA-GaussianDet achieves 58.9\% mAP and 68.0\% NDS in multi-view 3D object detection, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative metrics and qualitative visualizations.

records.title: Wavelet2DGS: Efficient Enhancement of Degraded Images via Wavelet-Domain 2D Gaussian Splatting
records.abstract: Robust 3D reconstruction from degraded images is fundamental to perception and graphics systems, yet spatially varying motion and defocus blur suppress high-frequency geometric details and disrupt multi-view consistency. Existing Neural Radiance Field and Gaussian Splatting methods rely on photometric supervision that degrades under heterogeneous blur, leading to geometry drift, texture oversmoothing, and view-inconsistent artifacts. We introduce Wavelet2DGS, a blur-aware 2D Gaussian splatting (2DGS) framework guided by a high-frequency prior. Our approach incorporates an explicit frequency-domain prior within the rendering process, imposing a structural constraint that facilitates the reconstruction of high-frequency details. The core of our method is a prior enhancement module that adaptively reconstructs subbands to combat the high-frequency degradation characteristic of degraded blur. Besides, we enforce depth-normal consistency regularization to couple frequency enhancement with surface geometry, preventing texture-geometry ambiguity during reconstruction. Extensive experiments on degradation scenarios demonstrate that Wavelet2DGS recovers finer geometric details and maintains cross-view coherence, while remaining efficient for practical deployment.

records.title: Compact and Fabricatable 3D Hair Representation from Strands
records.abstract: Fabrication of daily objects like figurines attracts a lot of attentions with the popularity of 3d printer. For a character, either virtual or fabricated, the hair always plays an important role in conveying personal image. However, the intricate and delicate nature of hair strands makes them difficult to print directly. Besides, the large amount of data also raised issues in transfer to and storage on 3d printer. This paper introduces a novel approach to convert strand-level hair into a 3d-printable mesh, which is also much more compact, while preserving hair style as much as possible. records.title: NRGS: Neural Regularization for Robust 3D Semantic Gaussian Splatting
records.abstract: We propose a neural regularization method that refines the noisy 3D semantic field produced by lifting multiview inconsistent 2D features, in order to obtain an accurate and robust 3D semantic Gaussian Splatting. The 2D features extracted from vision foundation models suffer from multi-view inconsistency due to a lack of cross-view constraints. Lifting these inconsistent features directly into 3D Gaussians results in a noisy semantic field, which degrades the performance of downstream tasks. Previous methods either focus on obtaining consistent multi-view features in the preprocessing stage or aim to mitigate noise through improved optimization strategies, often at the cost of increased preprocessing time or expensive computational overhead. In contrast, we introduce a variance-aware conditional MLP that operates directly on the 3D Gaussians, leveraging their geometric and appearance attributes to correct semantic errors in 3D space. Experiments on different datasets show that our method enhances the accuracy of lifted semantics, providing an efficient and effective approach to robust 3D semantic Gaussian Splatting.

records.title: LatentDFKD: Resolving Ill-Posed Pixel Inversion in Data-Free Distillation through Latent Modeling
records.abstract: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (DFKD) aims to distill representations from a teacher network to a student by synthesizing alternative training samples, thereby eliminating the dependency on the original dataset. Despite the success of existing methods on small-scale tasks, scaling to high-resolution scenarios like ImageNet-1K is severely hindered by the highly ill-posed inverse mapping from low-dimensional predictions to high-dimensional pixel space. To resolve this, we propose a Latent-space DFKD framework that exploits the rich structural priors of variational autoencoders to shift the synthesis paradigm from the uncertain pixel space to a more compact latent manifold. This transforms the ill-posed inversion into a tractable mapping problem. Furthermore, to constrain the synthetic samples to reside on the manifold of natural images, we introduce an SDS loss as a strong regularizer. Extensive results on multiple high-resolution datasets confirm the effectiveness of our proposed framework, showing that it significantly improves upon the state-of-the-art, particularly on ImageNet-1K.

records.title: GCCE: Geometry-Constrained Curve Evolution for Lane Detection
records.abstract: Lane detection is critical for autonomous driving, yet remains challenging in real-world scenes with occlusions, fragmented markings, illumination changes, and highly curved geometries. We propose Geometry-Constrained Curve Evolution (GCCE), a two-stage framework that decouples global structure recovery from local refinement. GCCE first encodes each lane as a compact low-dimensional geometric skeleton and employs a diffusion-based denoising model to infer robust skeletons from noisy skeleton states conditioned on image features, naturally capturing structural uncertainty. Guided by the recovered skeleton, a geometry-constrained curve evolution module then reconstructs complete lane shapes with accurate local alignment. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that GCCE achieves state-of-the-art performance, especially improving robustness and geometric consistency under occlusion and high-curvature scenarios.

records.title: Revisiting Photometric Self-Supervision under Texture Scarcity for Monocular Depth Estimation
records.abstract: Self-supervised monocular depth estimation learns from image sequences via photometric view synthesis, offering an appealing way to adapt depth models to unseen environments without collecting ground truth RGB-D data. However, in large textureless regions, the photometric loss becomes weakly correlated with depth errors, which can hinder optimization or even degrade useful depth priors. Meanwhile, the success of depth foundation models has shifted attention away from photometric self-supervision, despite their limited robustness in challenging unseen environments. In this work, we revisit photometric self-supervision under texture scarcity and seek to restore informative training signals for depth learning. We propose a noise-anchored framework that injects sparse synthetic perturbations into view synthesis, guided by a Perturbation Injection Curriculum (PIC) that progressively propagates supervision from texture-rich boundaries into textureless interiors. A prior-preserving distillation loss further stabilizes model updates in well-constrained regions. Experiments on diverse benchmarks demonstrate that our approach improves both standard photometric self-supervision from scratch and self-supervised adaptation of pretrained depth models, with particularly strong gains in textureless environments.

records.title: SSGaussian: Semantic-Aware and Structure-Preserving 3D Style Transfer
records.abstract: 3D style transfer has achieved promising results, driven by advances in neural representations such as Neural Radiance Fields and 3D Gaussian Splatting. However, existing approaches struggle to capture high-level style semantics from reference images and often produce results with limited structural clarity and poor instance separation. To address these issues, we propose a novel two-stage pipeline that leverages prior knowledge from 2D diffusion models. In the first stage, stylized key views are generated using a diffusion-based process, augmented with a Cross-View Style Alignment module that introduces cross-view attention to ensure style fidelity and instance-level consistency across viewpoints. In the second stage, an Instance-level Style Transfer mechanism propagates these coherent stylistic characteristics to the underlying 3D representation. Our pipeline yields well-structured, semantically coherent stylization and outperforms state-of-the-art approaches across diverse scenes, as validated by extensive experiments. records.title: Glazestopia: A User-Adaptive VR System for Experiencing Chinese Royal Glaze Craftsmanship
records.abstract: Royal glaze craftsmanship, a National Intangible Cultural Heritage of China, embodies a rich cultural legacy yet faces challenges in awareness and understanding of the contemporary youth public. The complexity of its production processes limits the ability of the general public to appreciate the craft, and existing promotional methods fail to convey the underlying attitudes and spirit associated with this intricate art form. In this paper, we developed Glazestopia, a VR system containing a Royal Glaze Craftsmanship Exhibition Hall and an Experience Hall, which offers an immersive exploration of the glaze-making process. The system allows users to engage interactively with each stage, from material selection to shaping and firing, utilizing a handwriting tablet to provide real-time feedback on the deformation of raw materials and adaptive guidance based on the user’s performance. This interaction enables users to create personalized glaze models, enhancing their connection to the craftsmanship. User studies reveal that our VR system significantly enhances users' comprehension and interest in royal glaze craftsmanship compared to traditional video-based learning methods. This innovative approach not only improves educational outcomes but also contributes to the preservation and promotion of royal glaze culture.

records.title: Bridging Semantics and Geometry: Infusing Foundation Model Priors into Unsupervised Monocular Depth Estimation
records.abstract: Unsupervised monocular depth estimation relies heavily on photometric consistency, which often deteriorates in texture-less regions and dynamic scenarios due to the violation of the static world assumption. To address these intrinsic limitations, we propose a novel framework that explicitly infuses cross-modal semantic priors and robust geometric constraints into the learning pipeline. Specifically, we leverage the zero-shot capabilities of CLIP to generate semantic masks and feature-gradient weights, effectively filtering unreliable supervisory signals and enforcing semantic-aware smoothness. Furthermore, to mitigate the structural instability of unsupervised learning, we introduce a Teacher-Student distillation strategy using a frozen Depth Anything V2 model, providing scale-invariant structural guidance. Finally, we design a Geometric Consistency Gate that fuses rigid-optical flow discrepancies with semantic cues to robustly weight the photometric loss. Extensive experiments on the DDAD dataset demonstrate that our method effectively suppresses dynamic artifacts and significantly outperforms state-of-the-art approaches.

records.title: MCBlock: Faster Neural Radiance Field Training via MCTS Dynamic-Resolution Ray Sampling
records.abstract: Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) is a representative media generation technique for high-fidelity novel view synthesis, but even state-of-the-art Gaussian Splatting still needs minutes of training, far from real-time generation demands (e.g., telemedicine). A key bottleneck is inefficient sampling: Existing point-sampling methods uniformly sample simple-texture regions (easy to fit) and complex-texture regions (hard to fit), while ray-sampling methods always sample in the finest granularity (i.e. the pixel level), both wasting GPU training resources. Actually, regions with different texture intensities require different sampling granularities. To this end, we propose a novel dynamic-resolution ray-sampling algorithm, MCBlock, which employs Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) to partition each training image into adaptively sized pixel blocks for active block-wise training. Specifically, MCBlock initializes trees according to the texture of training images, and refines the block partition via expansion/pruning. Implemented in Nerfstudio, MCBlock achieves up to 2.33× training speedup, surpassing other ray-sampling algorithms.

records.title: DPGO: Dynamic Pose Graph Optimization for Robust Multiview Registration
records.abstract: Multiview registration of 3D point clouds is a fundamental problem, yet its robustness is often compromised by numerous outlier transformations. Dominant methods based on Iterative Reweighted Least Squares (IRLS) are hampered by two critical limitations: 1) the inflexibility of static pose graphs, which cannot recover from initial structural errors, and 2) the dependency of reweighting schemes on unreliable initial weights. We address these challenges with two synergistic innovations. First, to overcome structural rigidity, we introduce a Dynamic Pose Graph Optimization method that performs self-correction by iteratively pruning unstable edges and reactivating globally consistent ones. Second, to break the dependency on poor initializations, we propose a content-aware adaptive edge weighting strategy that robustly learns weights from a rich fusion of geometric and appearance features. On challenging benchmarks, our framework achieves competitive or superior performance compared to strong IRLS-based baselines. For example, in the sparse-graph setting on the low-overlap 3DLoMatch dataset, it improves Registration Recall over SGHR by 4.3 percentage points, and on ScanNet it yields a 20.7% relative reduction in mean rotation error. Extensive ablation studies further validate the efficacy of our design, demonstrating improved robustness and precision in outlier-prone scenarios.

records.title: PointHIL: Hyperbolic Invariance Learning for Unsupervised Point Cloud Domain Adaptation
records.abstract: In real-world, due to the sparsity of distance measurement sensor sampling and the significant differences in scene layouts and data collection conditions, there are discrepancies between the point cloud data obtained and the data distribution used for model training, which leads to a significant degradation in model performance when it is actually deployed. As a result, unsupervised point cloud domain adaptation (UDA) remains highly challenging. To address this problem, we propose a novel hyperbolic-based framework for unsupervised point cloud domain adaptation, termed Hyperbolic Invariance Learning (HIL). The core idea of HIL is to fully exploit the inherent geometric structure of point cloud data by mapping point cloud features from Euclidean space into a hyperbolic space that is better suited to modeling hierarchical and structural relationships. Specifically, we design a geometric consistency constraint based on hyperbolic geometric distances, where geometric consistency is enforced according to the geometric invariances of point clouds. This encourages the model to learn domain-invariant representations in hyperbolic space that are more robust to variations in object shape and position. We conduct extensive experiments on the PointDA-10 dataset, and our method achieves new state-of-the-art performance.

records.title: HRMT: Enhancing HRNet with Hierarchical Textual Guidance for Cross-Species Animal Pose Estimation
records.abstract: Animal pose estimation has been widely applied in animal husbandry and biological research. These applications often involve animals from different species with diverse morphologies. However, in cross-species animal pose estimation, the diversity and uncertainty of visual features pose significant challenges to traditional image-based methods. To address this issue, we propose HRMT, a vision-language collaborative model built on High-Resolution Network that integrates hierarchical textual guidance and state-space modeling. Specifically, we inject textual semantic priors into the visual encoder at early stages and supervise the intermediate fused features through multiple auxiliary spatial decoders. we construct a CSP-Mamba module that is used in both the HRNet visual decoder and the cross-modal fusion stage. Their combination further enhances feature representation and effectively integrates textual priors. Experiments on publicly available datasets show that our method outperforms baseline models under both supervised and zero-shot learning settings. It validates the effectiveness and generality of the model design.

records.title: FCP-SatMVS: Feature-Context-Progressive Network for Robust Satellite Digital Surface Model
records.abstract: Digital Surface Model (DSM) is fundamental for Earth observation. Deep learning-based Multi-View Stereo shows promise in satellite remote sensing, but high-precision reconstruction is challenging due to low texture, limited resolution, and complex geometries. To address these issues, we propose a novel satellite DSM reconstruction framework incorporating three core components. Firstly, the Fusion Feature Extractor (FFE) integrates multi-scale hierarchical features via a pyramid to enhance sensitivity to seize texture cues. Secondly, the Cross-Dimensional Attention Module (CDAM) aggregates horizontal and vertical branches to capture long-range spatial dependencies, which alleviates elevation discontinuities arising from resolution limits and ensures accurate elevation assignment. Finally, the Pixel-wise Uneven Interval Processing (PUIP) strategy adaptively refines depth sampling using probabilistic uncertainty and local geometric gradients to balance efficiency and accuracy in steep terrain. Extensive experimental results on the WHU-TLC dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves SOTA performance, significantly reducing the Mean Absolute Error and Root Mean Square Error by 9.23% and 24.35%, respectively.
