records.title: Leveraging SAM for Generalized Few-Shot 3D Volumetric Segmentation: A Cross-View Propagation Approach
records.abstract: Few-shot segmentation (FSS) enables learning from limited examples, but existing 3D FSS methods often require domain-specific meta-training and may struggle under large structural variations. In this work, we propose Cross-View Propagation with Segment Anything Models (CVP-SAM), a training-free and generalized framework for 3D few-shot volumetric segmentation that repurposes the spatiotemporal segmentation capability of the video foundation models SAM~2 and SAM~3. We reinterpret cross-instance structural differences as temporal deformations in a virtual video, enabling robust label transfer via SAM’s built-in tracking and memory mechanisms. Our approach features three key components: (1) Entropy- and Uniformity-Aware Support Optimization, which selects informative support slices by balancing structural uncertainty (via entropy) and spatial coverage; (2) a Virtual Video Bridge that interleaves support and query slices into hybrid sequences for memory-based feature alignment; and (3) Orthogonal Geometric Scouting, a registration-free coarse-to-fine localization strategy using global feature matching across orthogonal views. Experiments on medical and semiconductor 3D volumes show our model-agnostic method achieves state-of-the-art performance with only 5 support slices, demonstrating strong generalization across diverse 3D vision tasks.

records.title: Long-Horizon On-Road Navigation with Visual Map Guidance
records.abstract: Traditional long-horizon point-goal on-road navi- gation typically employs a two-stage pipeline with global path planning followed by local behavior decision making. However, this approach relies on topological maps, which are inherently prone to information latency and incompleteness. Consequently, in regions susceptible to frequent road condition changes or in unstructured areas, pre-planned paths prove unsuitable. To address these challenges, we propose a novel task coordinating a global visual map with local observations for navigation, in which the former provides road network layout for optimal routing and the latter assesses real-time feasibility. To facilitate this research, we contribute a large-scale multimodal dataset with comprehensive types of routes, building upon which, we design an architecture based on a multimodal large language model, achieving a single- stage, end-to-end framework. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms conventional approaches, reaching state-of-the-art performance.

records.title: PointRFT: Explicit Reinforcement Fine-tuning for Point Cloud Perception
records.abstract: Understanding spatial dynamics and semantics in point cloud is fundamental for comprehensive 3D comprehension. While reinforcement learning algorithms such as Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) have recently achieved remarkable breakthroughs in large language models by incentivizing reasoning capabilities through strategic reward design, their potential remains largely unexplored in the 3D perception domain. This naturally raises a pivotal question: Can RL-based methods effectively empower 3D point cloud fine-tuning? In this paper, we propose PointRFT, the first reinforcement fine-tuning paradigm tailored specifically for point cloud representation learning. We select three prevalent 3D foundation models and devise specialized accuracy reward and dispersion reward functions to stabilize training and mitigate distribution shifts. Through comprehensive few-shot classification experiments comparing distinct training paradigms, we demonstrate that PointRFT consistently outperforms vanilla supervised fine-tuning (SFT) across diverse benchmarks. Furthermore, when organically integrated into a hybrid Pretraining-SFT-RFT paradigm, the representational capacity of point cloud foundation models is substantially unleashed, achieving state-of-the-art performance particularly under data-scarce scenarios.

records.title: PhysLayer: Language-Guided Layered Animation with Depth-Aware Physics
records.abstract: Existing image-to-video generation methods often produce physically implausible motions and lack precise control over object dynamics. While prior approaches have incorporated physics simulators, they remain confined to 2D planar motions and fail to capture depth-aware spatial interactions. We introduce PhysLayer, a novel framework enabling language-guided, depth-aware layered animation of static images. PhysLayer consists of three key components: First, a language-guided scene understanding module that utilizes vision foundation models to decompose scenes into depth-based layers by analyzing object composition, material properties, and physical parameters. Second, a depth-aware layered physics simulation that extends 2D rigid-body dynamics with depth motion and perspective-consistent scaling, enabling more realistic object interactions without requiring full 3D reconstruction. Third, a physics-guided video synthesis module that integrates simulated trajectories with scene-aware relighting for temporally coherent results. Experimental results demonstrate improvements in CLIP-Similarity (+2.2\%), FID score (+9.3\%), and Motion-FID (+3\%), with human evaluation showing enhanced physical plausibility (+24\%) and text-video alignment (+35\%). Our approach provides a practical balance between physical realism and computational efficiency for controllable image animation.

records.title: Topology-Constrained Inter-Frame Mesh Registration for V-DMC
records.abstract: Video-based Dynamic Mesh Coding (V-DMC) is currently being standardized as the emerging framework for dynamic mesh compression, where inter-frame mesh registration plays a crucial role in motion prediction and rate–distortion performance. However, the registration methods used in V-DMC rely primarily on Euclidean nearest-neighbor matching, which often leads to cross-face mismatches and degraded inter-frame deformation quality. This paper proposes a topology-constrained inter-frame mesh registration method that derives robust face-level correspondence regions between the decimated mesh and the original input mesh by jointly tracing vertex merges during decimation and exploiting intermediate mapping meshes. These regions are used as constraints during registration, jointly with vertex-distance minimization, to prevent mismatches and improve alignment accuracy. Integrated into the V-DMC pipeline, the proposed method enhances the stability of inter-frame mesh deformation and yields competitive BD-rate performance on the latest V-DMC CTC tracked sequences. This method has been adopted into the V-DMC reference software.

records.title: Reconstruct High Quality Facial Geometry and Reflectance Details in One Shot
records.abstract: We propose a novel single-shot system for high quality facial geometry and reflectance reconstruction using entry-level consumer DSLR cameras and sequential flash illumination. Our method captures multi-view images under varying lighting conditions within a sub-blink interval, effectively mitigating motion artifacts. By leveraging differentiable rendering and traditional color space analysis, we disentangle diffuse and specular reflections without polarization filters, thereby reducing hardware complexity and light loss. A two-stage optimization strategy first reconstructs coarse geometry and diffuse albedo from specular-invariant components, then refines detailed normal map and specular parameters through photometric constraints. Experimental results demonstrate pore-level geometric details and realistic reflectance recovery, achieving state-of-the-art performance compared to existing methods. The system's low-cost setup and computational efficiency make it practical for applications in digital humans, AR/VR, and entertainment.

records.abstract: Affordance learning is fundamental for embodied agents to interact with the physical world. To support this task, we present AffordPart3D, a large-scale dataset comprising over 25,000 language-part pairs across 216 diverse 3D scenes. We further conduct a systematic exploration of the design space for this task, and based on the resulting insights, propose a multi-granular representation that integrates object-level context with part-aware cues, enabling more precise and interpretable affordance understanding in complex 3D scenes.

records.title: CoMER-TSCL: Reshaping Decoder Geometry for HMER via Token-Level Supervised Contrastive Learning
records.abstract: Transformer-based architectures have revolutionized Handwritten Mathematical Expression Recognition (HMER) by enabling superior global dependency modeling. However, despite their dominance, these models remain vulnerable to Structural Drift in complex expressions, primarily due to latent feature ambiguity. To address this, we propose CoMER-TSCL, a framework incorporating Token-Level Supervised Contrastive Learning to explicitly regularize the decoding trajectory. Diverging from standard non-linear projection heads, we introduce a novel Identity Projection strategy. This design enforces linear discriminability directly on the decoder's latent manifold, strictly aligning with the autoregressive generation objective. Crucially, this auxiliary module is discarded during inference, ensuring zero additional inference cost. Experiments demonstrate that CoMER-TSCL achieves state-of-the-art performance on CROHME 2014 and 2016, outperforming the baseline by an absolute margin of 4.16\% on CROHME 2014, while exhibiting superior robustness on structurally complex sequences.

records.title: Towards Accurate Single Panoramic 3D Detection: A Semantic Gaussian Centric Approach
records.abstract: Three-dimensional object detection in panoramic imagery is crucial for comprehensive scene understanding, yet accurately mapping 2D features to 3D remains a significant challenge. Prevailing methods often project 2D features onto discrete 3D grids, which break geometric continuity and limit representation efficiency. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes PanoGSDet, a monocular panoramic 3D detection framework built upon continuous semantic 3D Gaussian representations. The proposed framework comprises a panoramic depth estimation component and a semantic Gaussian component. The panoramic depth estimation component extracts the equirectangular semantic and depth features from the monocular panorama input. The semantic Gaussian component includes a semantic Gaussian lifting module that projects spherical features into 3D semantic Gaussians, a semantic Gaussian optimization module that refines these semantic Gaussians, and a Gaussian guided prediction head that generates 3D bounding boxes from optimized Gaussian representations. Extensive experiments on the Structured3D dataset demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing methods.

records.title: Exploring Modality Invariance: A Cross-Modal Framework for 3D Representation Learning
records.abstract: Existing scene-level 3D self-supervised methods predominantly focus on learning representations from point clouds only, leading to inherent constraints such as overfitting to local geometric patterns (e.g., surface normals and height biases). To address this, we propose EMI, a cross-modal framework that exploits modality invariance between point clouds and RGB-D frames. Three key innovations form a shared representation space by integrating intrinsic properties from point clouds and semantic priors from visual foundation models: Masked Color Reconstruction applies cross masking to occlude continuous scene textures, forcing the backbone to infer missing color information from local context; Superpoint Guided Distillation partitions the scene into superpoints via graph-cut, capturing explicit geometry and serving as units for cross-modal distillation; Cross-View Feature Restriction generates augmented views to provide correspondences, constraining the network to learn augmentation-invariant features. Extensive experiments on major benchmarks, evaluated under linear probing, data efficiency and supervised finetuning protocols, underscore EMI's superior generalizability.

records.title: Progressive Camera Learning for Unsupervised Visible-Infrared Person Re-Identification
records.abstract: Unsupervised visible–infrared person re-identification (US-VI-ReID) aims to match individuals across modalities without annotations. Existing methods rely on global clustering across visible and infrared cameras. However, this approach overlooks camera-specific domain discrepancies and often results in severe identity splitting particularly in visible cameras, which led to suboptimal clustering results and incorrect mapping of cross-modal relationships. To address these issues, we propose a straightforward yet effective Progressive Camera Learning (PCL) framework which incorporates Progressive Camera Alignment (PCA), Camera-aware Adversarial Learning (CAL) and Hierarchical Collaborative Contrastive Learning (HCCL) Module. Specifically, PCA progressively incorporates local visible domains to calibrate the global feature space and yield more compact clusters. CAL further adopts adversarial optimization to suppress camera-specific cues and learn camera-invariant features. Moreover, HCCL performs hierarchical collaborative contrastive learning to strengthen identity consistency across modalities. Extensive experiments conducted on the publicly available SYSU-MM01 and RegDB datasets demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method.

records.title: Comprehend and See Clearly: Monocular Semantic Occupancy Prediction via Semantic Anchoring and Frequency Refinement
records.abstract: Reconstructing dense 3D geometry from a single image is challenging, as it requires recovering both global layouts and fine-grained details. We observe that existing methods are limited by a mixture of uncertainties: semantic existence in texture-less regions, geometric orientation of planar surfaces, and boundary localization at structural edges. To address these issues, we propose LFOcc, a framework based on Cognitive–Structural–Spectral decomposition. Specifically, we use VLM-based Semantic Guidance (VLSG) to link visual features to high-level concepts, reducing existence ambiguity in texture-less areas. Building on this, the Surface Normal Supervision Mechanism (SNSM) serves as a semantic-adaptive geometric prior: it utilizes semantic-guided supervision to enforce Manhattan-consistent geometry on planar structures while preserving object topology. In addition, Learnable Wavelet Boundary Enhancement (LWBE) tackles localization uncertainty by separating and recovering high-frequency boundary components in the spectral domain. Experiments on NYUv2 and Occ-ScanNet show that LFOcc achieves state-of-the-art performance. Our code will be publicly available at https://github.com/zj-png/LFOCC/tree/main.

records.title: MODE-NVS: Free-Form Motion Deblurring for Novel View Synthesis
records.abstract: Novel view synthesis is a pivotal challenge in the field of 3D vision, experiencing significant progress driven by the advent of neural rendering. However, when the input images are unordered and blurry due to shaking during data acquisition, existing solutions often presuppose uniform camera motion through linear or cubic interpolation, which leads to performance declines under arbitrary camera paths and varying velocities during exposure. To tackle this challenge, we introduce MODE-NVS, a motion-aware learning framework designed to maximize imaging process freedom. On the one hand, MODE-NVS redefines motion blur modeling by developing motion-aware blur kernels that account for velocity changes. On the other hand, it utilizes a learning-based interpolation approach to represent the camera's dynamic motion trajectory and inter-frame temporal associations. Furthermore, we incorporate a high frequency depth regularization to improve the consistency of multi-view imaging. We performed extensive experiments on both public and custom real-world datasets. These experimental results indicate that MODE-NVS sets a new benchmark in novel view synthesis by providing an average PSNR enhancement of 1.5dB to 2dB.

records.title: Active 3D Gaussian Splatting via Quality-Aware Adaptive Octree Representation
records.abstract: Active mapping with high-fidelity 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is often still guided by coverage-oriented objectives and uniform NBV sampling, which overexplores free space and fails to trigger revisits for already mapped but low-fidelity surfaces. We propose an octree-guided active 3DGS framework that couples exploration with quality-aware refinement. The method maintains an adaptive octree whose nodes accumulate rendering residuals and multi-view consistency cues from differentiable 3DGS mapping, yielding compact reliability statistics. An octree-aware NBV planner balances frontier expansion with revisiting low-fidelity hotspots, while GPU-parallel voxel projection enables efficient occupancy and frontier reasoning. On the Replica indoor benchmark, our system achieves millimeter-level geometric accuracy with 99% coverage and improves novel-view fidelity over baselines.

records.title: HydraMamba: Hybrid Dimensional Refinement Architecture with Mamba for LiDAR-based 3D Object Detection
records.abstract: Current LiDAR-based 3D detection paradigms face a fundamental trade-off, sparse convolution is restricted by local receptive fields, while Transformer architectures incur prohibitive quadratic computational costs. Although State Space Models (SSMs) like Mamba offer linear complexity, their direct application to point clouds fractures local geometric topology and fails to address orientation-aware dependencies. We introduce HydraMamba, a hierarchical architecture that synthesizes the global modeling utility of Mamba with the local inductive bias of sparse convolution. Central to this architecture is the Hydra Block, which employs a Local-Global Gate to adaptively fuse features, complemented by Axial-Aware Aggregation and Content-Aware Merging to preserve structural integrity. Benchmarking on the KITTI dataset confirms HydraMamba establishes a new performance standard with 85.2% mAP, surpassing Mamba baselines by 13.8% while maintaining real-time efficiency on consumer hardware.

records.title: Refined Dynamic Scene Reconstruction via Global Structure-enhanced 4D Gaussian Splatting
records.abstract: Dynamic scene reconstruction aims to reconstruct time-varying 3D scenes from images with known camera poses and timestamps, enabling high-fidelity rendering from arbitrary viewpoints and time instances. As a representative method, 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) is commonly used to address this task and achieves superior performance. However, 4DGS still faces two main challenges: it relies on discrete point-wise modeling of Gaussian primitives, leading to insufficient global structural awareness and spatially inconsistent deformations. Moreover, heavy reliance on pixel-space supervision limits fine-grained detail recovery and often causes temporal flickering. To this end, we propose a GS-4DGS method, namely Global Structure-enhanced 4D Gaussian Splatting, which captures spatial dependencies among Gaussian primitives via graph attention-based global modeling and incorporates Spatio-Temporal-Frequency regularization to enhance high-frequency details reconstruction and temporal stability. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GS-4DGS consistently outperforms existing methods in reconstruction quality and temporal coherence.

records.title: Hierarchical Feature Alignment 3D Scene Graph for Dynamic Environment Navigation
records.abstract: 3D scene graph (3DSG) provides a lightweight and structured representation for robotic navigation. However, existing 3DSG methods encounter several challenges in dynamic environments, limiting their effectiveness for navigation. Insufficient robustness to motion interference causes dynamic objects to be misidentified as static nodes, affecting the construction of navigable space. Inadequate hierarchical scene representation results in a large search space, reducing the efficiency of large-scale navigation. Limited geometric–semantic consistency leads to unreliable language grounding and incorrect navigation target selection. To address these issues, we propose HFA-3DSG, a Hierarchical Feature Alignment 3D Scene Graph for dynamic environment navigation. First, Uncertainty Map Guided Dynamic Filtering is employed to remove dynamic objects and recover stable scenes. Second, Spatial Field-guided Scene Decomposition is introduced to enable reliable hierarchical partitioning. Finally, Pixel-ray Confidence Driven Feature Alignment achieves accurate object-level geometric-semantic consistency. By organizing multi-level scene elements into a hierarchical graph, HFA-3DSG enables robust navigation in dynamic environments. Experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance of our method in room segmentation, object-level semantics, and navigation tasks, along with strong robustness to dynamic environments.

records.title: Wavelet-Guided Color-Field Stability Modeling for 3D Gaussian Splatting Compression
records.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables fast, high-quality novel view synthesis but suffers from unreliable SfM colors and the lack of visually grounded, spatially adaptive density control. These issues cause color shifts, redundant Gaussians in low-texture regions, and incorrect merging of chromatically inconsistent surfaces. We observe that both problems originate from the absence of a unified description of multi-scale visual stability. To this end, we propose a wavelet color field–guided Joint Stability Field that integrates low-frequency color consistency, high-frequency texture complexity, and structural variation into a unified stability estimate. The low-frequency component provides a robust and view-consistent color estimate for Gaussian color initialization, mitigating SfM-induced noise. The resulting stability field yields a continuous estimate of local representational demand. It is used to guide point-cloud simplification as well as to adaptively regulate Gaussian splitting and pruning during training. Experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that our method significantly improves model compactness while preserving rendering quality.

records.title: Occupancy-Map–Aware Metrics for 3D Gaussian Splatting: Toward More Reliable Objective Quality Evaluation
records.abstract: Objective quality assessment of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) content is commonly performed by rendering evaluation view(s) and applying full-frame 2D image metrics such as Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM). However, when rendered views contain regions with no contribution from the 3DGS representation, e.g., background around object silhouettes, or uncovered parts of a scene due to limited view coverage, these low-information pixels can dominate full-frame averaging and yield overly optimistic scores. To address this issue, we propose Occupancy-Map--aware metrics (OM-PSNR and OM-SSIM), which restrict quality computation to occupied pixels using a binary occupancy mask obtained during renderering process. To avoid discarding artifacts that change visible support, we adopt a union pooling strategy that treats a pixel as valid if it is occupied in either the reference or distorted view. Analytical modeling establishes the dependence of metric deviation on occupancy rate, and experiments confirm the predicted relationship. Across multiple objects and distortion types, OM-PSNR removes about 5.8dB of background-induced bias on average, while OM-SSIM reduces overestimation by roughly 0.08 absolute points. Additional zoom-factor experiments show that OM-metrics remain stable under varying view coverage, validating their robustness. The proposed methods have been adopted in the MPEG Joint Exploration Experiment (JEE6.8) Common Test Conditions for Gaussian Splat Coding (GSC) and are integrated into the official evaluation software for standardized 3DGS quality assessment.

records.title: Cross-Modal Learning for Spike Image Reconstruction
records.abstract: Spike cameras, with their ability to capture light intensity at ultra-high temporal resolutions, are exceptionally suited for recording high-speed dynamic scenes. However, fluctuations in spike intervals under constant lighting due to noise in the camera pose significant challenges in reconstructing clear images from spike sequences. While existing methods attempt to model spatial-temporal correlations to mitigate this noise, their performance is frequently constrained by the domain gap between simulated and real-world noise. In this paper, we reframe this challenge and propose a novel cross-modal learning framework that synergistically couples spike image reconstruction with an auxiliary image denoising task. Our method employs a dual-branch architecture where, in addition to the primary reconstruction branch, a denoising branch is trained on a dataset created by applying diverse degradations to the ground-truth images. Crucially, we introduce a mutual information loss to align the feature representations of both modalities. This forces the reconstruction network to learn robust noise and structural priors from the denoising task, effectively enhancing its generalization capability without requiring any additional data. Extensive experiments on both simulated and real-world datasets demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance.

records.title: ContextFormer: Object-Centric 3D Spatial Priors for Robust Zero-Shot Navigation
records.abstract: Zero-shot object navigation (ZSON) requires agents to locate novel targets in unfamiliar environments without task-specific training. Existing LLM-based methods offer semantic priors but suffer from a grounding gap in 3D spatial reasoning. Map-based learning methods tend to overfit to absolute coordinates and generalize poorly. We propose ContextFormer, a plug-and-play 3D Scene Context Transformer designed to inject environment- and target-agnostic spatial priors into existing navigation policies. We introduce a two-stage learning framework. First, we employ 3D relative spatial attention with geometric bias to encode semantic co-occurrences and geometric layouts through a self-supervised Masked Object Prediction task, disentangling priors from specific scenes. Second, a target-aware cross-attention module transforms these generic priors into task-specific inference signals, predicting target existence even under occlusion. Experiments demonstrate that ContextFormer boosts state-of-the-art baselines, achieving a 4.0% relative gain in Success Rate on HM3D and 3.2% on MP3D. Specifically, in severe occlusion scenarios, our method improves SR by 16.7% and SPL by 11.6%.

records.title: TrioCL: Structured Alignment of Geometry and Language for 3D Object Grounding via Progressive Curriculum Framework
records.abstract: 3D object grounding has wide application in robotics and computer vision, which aims to understand complex spatial relationships within point clouds based on natural language queries. However, existing methods typically adopt a holistic training paradigm, forcing the model to simultaneously align noisy geometric features with linguistic compositionality from scratch. We argue that this "cold-start" alignment strategy often leads to optimization instability and brittle representations that overfit to scene-specific biases. To this end, we propose TrioCL, a Structured Alignment framework that reformulates 3D grounding as a progressive denoising process. Unlike standard approaches, TrioCL decouples the cross-modal learning complexity along three orthogonal dimensions: (1) Object-Level: It transitions from explicit semantic anchors (ground-truth features) to implicit geometric cues (raw point clouds), stabilizing early-stage visual-semantic correspondence; (2) Language-Level: It progresses from attribute-dominant queries to relation-rich descriptions, enabling hierarchical parsing of spatial constraints; and (3) Optimization-Level: It employs dynamic loss modulation to synchronize training focus with data complexity. Extensive experiments on three public benchmarks (Nr3D, Sr3D, and ScanRefer) demonstrate that TrioCL consistently outperforms strong baselines, offering a general and robust training strategy for 3D vision-languag grounding tasks.

records.title: ISPhy3D: Incremental Semantic-Physical 3D Reconstruction from a Single Image
records.abstract: While recent strides in 3D generation have achieved impressive visual fidelity, ensuring the physical plausibility required for Embodied AI and VR/AR remains a critical challenge. We address this with ISPhy3D, a training-free framework for Incremental Semantic-Physical 3D reconstruction from a single image. Specifically, our framework proceeds in three distinct stages: (1) Semantic Perception, where a VLM parses the scene into a topological dependency graph to dictate a physically grounded generation sequence; (2) Occlusion-Aware Geometric Initialization, which employs generative in-painting to restore occluded regions and utilizes a robust coarse-to-fine alignment strategy to estimate 6-DoF poses from visual depth and point clouds; and (3) Incremental Physics-Aware Assembly, where objects are sequentially refined using a novel Native SDF-based differentiable optimization loop. By enforcing hierarchical physical constraints within a frozen environment, ISPhy3D effectively resolves inter-penetration and floating artifacts. Experiments on the 3D-FRONT dataset demonstrate that ISPhy3D significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving superior geometric accuracy and physical consistency suitable for downstream simulation.

records.title: VersaGauss: A Versatile Framework for Generating Multiphase Dynamics with 3D Gaussians
records.abstract: Recent progress has been made in 3D Gaussian representation for reconstruction, generation, and physical simulation. However, current approaches mainly concentrate on physics-based dynamic generation of solid objects and only handle single-phase collision interactions. We introduce VersaGauss, a unified framework for generation, simulation, and rendering that supports versatile physics-based dynamic generation, particularly for multiphase interactions. Our system takes a few images as input and produces a realistic, physics-driven 3D dynamic scene with multiple objects. To optimize the Gaussian kernel distribution, we develop a particle pruning algorithm. We also propose the Coupled Multiphase Point Method (CMPM) to effectively model and generate multiphase interactions. Additionally, harmonic interpolation within CMPM and a Gaussian evolution strategy are introduced to achieve realistic fluid rendering. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our framework can simulate interactions among various materials such as fluid, rubber, sand, snow, and others. Code is available at https://github.com/Elowen-surj/VersaGauss.

records.title: HDAL: Hierarchical Disentanglement and Depth-Aware Learning for Multi-Modal Rumor Detection
records.abstract: Multi-modal rumor detection demands reasoning over potentially conflicting evidence where text may appear credible while images are manipulated, or propagation patterns seem anomalous yet content appears normal. This fundamental challenge exposes critical gaps in existing approaches: coarse-grained fusion averages away fine-grained modality-specific conflicts that rumors exploit, while graph-based propagation models ignore the hierarchical nature of diffusion where credibility systematically degrades across depth. We propose Hierarchical Disentanglement and Depth-Aware Learning (HDAL), advancing multi-modal rumor detection through hierarchical learning paradigm. Our framework preserves shared semantics via contrastive alignment while isolating modality-specific nuances through adversarial decoupling, captures credibility evolution in propagation trees via temporal decay attention and structural constraints, and adaptively synthesizes heterogeneous evidence through cross-space fusion. Experiments validate substantial performance gains over strong baselines, with systematic ablations confirming the effectiveness of hierarchical learning.

records.title: Effects of Takeover Request Modalities on Autonomous Driving under Varying Workload: A VR-based Pilot Study
records.abstract: Level 3 autonomous driving enables drivers to engage in non-driving related tasks during driving activities, only needing to take over when prompted by the autonomous driving system. The takeover requests, being crucial for the transition between non-driving and driving tasks, may affect takeover performance differently under various workload levels. To investigate this issue, this study developed a virtual reality autonomous driving simulation platform integrating motion capture technology to examine visual, auditory, and vibratory takeover modalities under varying workload levels induced by n-back tasks. Results indicate that the effectiveness of prompt varies by workload: while no significant differences occurred under low workload, visual and auditory prompts excelled at medium levels, and auditory prompts proved most effective under high workload. Furthermore, usability and satisfaction surveys showed no significant differences among prompt types. Finally, The VR simulation platform demonstrated strong general presence, spatial presence, and user involvement, validating its effectiveness for immersive autonomous driving research.

records.title: Distractor-Masked Adversarial Meta-Learning for Robust Few-Shot Object Detection
records.abstract: Few-shot object detection (FSOD) offers great practical utility. Meta-learning is a promising strategy, yet its success depends on a robust meta-detector. To address this, we advance a distractor-masked FSOD framework, dubbed Adversarial Meta-Learning (AML). To begin with, we put forward MaskResNet, a masked meta-encoder with Non-RoI masking, to concentrate on extracting support features within the regions of interest (RoI). To address the overfitting challenge arising from MaskResNet, we propose two adversarial autoencoders. We incorporate gaussian noise and random masking to increase feature diversity, generate latent features with an encoder, and reconstruct features with a decoder. A discriminator is utilized to distinguish the latent data (fake) from random gaussian features (real). We leverage adversarial learning between real and fake features to boost autoencoder's generation and discriminator's performance. Sufficient experiments on PASCAL VOC and MS COCO obviously proved that AML outshines similar meta-learning FSOD frameworks.

records.title: Synth-to-Segment: Defect Segmentation in Low-Data Regime with Synthetic Defects
records.abstract: Industrial anomaly detection is crucial for product quality, yet the scarcity and diversity of defective samples in real manufacturing environments hinder the development of reliable segmentation models. Recently, diffusion-based approaches have been introduced to generate synthetic defects from limited data, offering a promising way to expand training samples without manual annotation. However, the visual fidelity of these anomalies varies significantly, and low-quality samples may even degrade model performance. Moreover, real and synthetic anomalies often exhibit noticeable distribution discrepancies in feature space, making their joint training difficult to optimize and limiting the benefits of synthetic data when used alongside real samples. To address these issues, we propose Synth-to-Segment, a training pipeline designed to reliably exploit diffusion-generated anomalies for defect segmentation. We introduce Unsupervised Quality-Guided Selection (UQS) to filter low-quality synthetic anomalies, ensuring high-fidelity samples are retained for training. Besides, for integrating real and synthetic defects, we design Heterogeneous Anomalous Mosaic (HAM), which can compose heterogeneous anomalies in a way that preserves defect authenticity while enriching contextual diversity. Extensive experiments on four benchmarks demonstrate consistent performance gains, validating the effectiveness of our approach.

records.title: Expert–Generalist Collaborative Active Constrained Learning Based on the Hartley Operator for Pancreatic Tumor Segmentation
records.abstract: Pancreatic cancer is one of the most aggressive and lethal malignancies of the digestive system. Accurate delineation of the Gross Tumor Volume (GTV) is crucial for effective radiotherapy and treatment planning. In recent years, significant advancements have been achieved in GTV segmentation. Nevertheless, manual annotation of medical images remains a time-consuming and costly process that necessitates the expertise of experienced clinical specialists. Furthermore, the pancreas is situated deep within the abdominal cavity and exhibits similar tissue density to adjacent organs, leading to ambiguous and indistinct boundaries. To address this challenge, we propose an expert-generalist collaborative active constrained learning paradigm, through which a segmentation algorithm for pancreatic tumors is developed under an extremely limited (constrained) annotation budget, where the data is essentially unlabeled. In addition, the Hartley transform is incorporated into the encoder to capture structural representations in the frequency domain, thereby enhancing the model’s sensitivity to the indistinct boundaries of the pancreas. Extensive experiments on our self-collected pancreatic tumor dataset and a publicly available MRI dataset show that our model has superior performance over the state-of-the-art segmentation methods, and achieves even better results than the fully supervised segmentation methods.

records.title: Triple Domain Perception Convolution for Robust and Efficient Underwater Object Detection
records.abstract: Underwater object detection is challenged by severe image degradation and the presence of small targets, which lead to feature loss, noise interference, and reduced perception accuracy. Existing enhancement-based or multi-scale fusion methods only partially address these issues, as they overlook the spectral characteristics of underwater noise and the semantic–spatial misalignment within deep networks. To address these challenges, we propose Triple Domain Perception Convolution (TDP-Conv), a tri-domain feature modeling module that integrates spatial–semantic complementarity and spatial–frequency collaboration to enhance robustness and small-object representation. Building upon TDP-Conv, we further develop a lightweight detector family, TDP-YOLO, by embedding TDP-Conv into YOLOv8 and removing redundant components. Extensive experiments on TrashCan and UTDAC2020 demonstrate that TDP-YOLO consistently achieves a superior accuracy–efficiency tradeoff compared with both general-purpose detectors and underwater-specific models. The code is available here: https://github.com/18322306208/TDP-YOLO/

records.title: Pseudo-label generation strategy for semi-supervised arbitrary-oriented object detection via RIoU-aware
records.abstract: Arbitrary-oriented Object Detection (AOOD) has garnered significant attention in the fields of re mote sensing and aerial image due to its ability to perform fine-grained detection. However, manually annotating oriented bounding boxes (OBB) is time-consuming and costly. To address this challenge, semi-supervised arbitrary-oriented object detection (Semi-AOOD) has been introduced, significantly reducing the need for extensive OBB annotations. Despite the advantages of existing methods, we ob serve that their generated pseudo-labels often introduce substantial background noise. These low-quality pseudo-labels lack accurate localization information for unsupervised training, which degrades the over all model performance. In response, we propose a high-quality pseudo-label generation strategy (HPG). Specifically, we design a hybrid metric of the regression and classification quality of prediction OBB to f ilter for high-quality pseudo-labels during the pseudo-label generation phase. To quantify the regression quality, we propose a Regression Quality Prediction (RQP) branch to predict Rotated Intersection over Union (RIoU) scores. Additionally, we introduce an improved binary cross entropy loss named Candidate Class (CC) loss to mitigate the interference of redundant category information. Based on the above core components (HPG and CC loss), we develop an RIoU-aware semi-supervised arbitrary-oriented object detector named RA-SOOD. Extensive experiments on the DOTA-v1.5 dataset show that RA-SOOD achieves state-of-the-art performance without extra computational overhead.

records.title: DVP: Dynamic Visual Prompting for Open-World Continual Object Detection
records.abstract: Open-World Continual Object Detection (OW-COD) aims to enable detectors to continuously learn new categories from few-shot data while preserving performance on previously learned categories and maintaining open-world generalization to unseen objects. State-of-the-art methods, such as MR-GDINO, mitigate catastrophic forgetting by retrieving task-specific LoRA parameters. However, these methods primarily focus on model adaptation while overlooking the data distribution discrepancies among different categories, leading to suboptimal recognition performance on seen categories. To address this issue, we propose a novel OW-COD method based on a Dynamic Visual Prompting (DVP) mechanism. Specifically, we introduce a retrievable visual prompt. By directly modifying the input pixels, the new category data can be adapted to the pre-trained model, thereby alleviating the problem of the model forgetting the categories it has seen from the perspective of data.Furthermore, to fully explore the potential of visual prompting in OW-COD, we investigate various visual prompting designs, all of which achieve competitive performance. Extensive experiments on the OW-COD benchmark show that our method outperforms the existing state-of-the-art methods.

records.title: FR-DETR: Frequency and Recurrent Feature Refinement for Robust Object Detection under Adverse Weather
records.abstract: Object detection under adverse weather remains challenging due to severe visual degradations and domain shifts. Existing enhancer-based approaches attempt to improve detection by cascading an enhancer with a detector, but they introduce redundant feature extraction and incur high computational cost with limited accuracy gains when paired with SOTA detectors. We propose FR-DETR, a detector-centric framework that refines features rather than images, focusing enhancement on regions of interest and leveraging frequency-domain cues. Specifically, we design (I) a Frequency Refinement Module that dynamically separates and reweights low- and high-frequency components to improve foreground-background discrimination, and (II) a Recurrent Focus Refinement Module (RFRM) that iteratively refines features using coarse predictions as guidance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FR-DETR achieves superior detection accuracy under adverse weather while being significantly more computationally efficient than enhancer-based methods.

records.title: Dual-Level Alignment: Bridging Feature and Task Gaps in Remote Sensing Small Object Detection
records.abstract: One-stage object detectors often suffer from feature misalignment in FPN-based multi-scale fusion and conflicting optimization gradients between the localization and classification tasks. Small objects often occupy few pixels, even slight misalignment leading to significant performance drops. To address this issue, we propose the Dual-Level Alignment Network (DLANet), a unified one-stage detector designed to bridge alignment gaps at both the feature level and task level. At the feature level, we propose a Spatial-Semantic Alignment FPN (S$^2$A-FPN) that integrates a Spatial Recalibration Alignment (SRA) module to mitigate location shifts and resolution-induced degradation, and a Semantic Perception Alignment (SPA) module to enhance cross-level semantic consistency. At the task level, we propose a Dynamic Task-aware Alignment (DTA) module that adaptively aligns and balances feature representations between two tasks through learnable feature gating and interaction mechanisms. Extensive experiments on four challenging aerial image datasets, including AI-TODv1, DOTA-v1.0, DIOR and DIOR-R, demonstrate that DLANet significantly outperforms state-of-the-art detectors, particularly in scenarios with dense and small objects.

records.title: A Dual-Imbalance Rectified Framework for Tiny Object Detection
records.abstract: Tiny Object Detection (TOD) remains a formidable challenge due to weak feature representations and severe background clutter. While DETR-like paradigms have shown promise, they suffer from two critical bottlenecks: semantic-geometric imbalance, where downsampling dilutes semantics while ignoring stable edge cues, and scale-induced supervision imbalance, where standard matching costs favor large objects, leaving tiny objects insufficiently supervised. To mitigate these issues, we propose DIRF, a dual-imbalance rectified framework for tiny object detection. Specifically, we introduce a Contextual-Edge Fusion Module (CEFM) and a Boundary-Guided Module (BGM) to leverage object edges as explicit auxiliary supervision for sharper localization. Furthermore, we design an Area-Guided Hungarian Matching (AGHM) strategy that incorporates scale penalties into the loss function, ensuring equitable supervision for tiny objects. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing models, validating the effectiveness ofthe proposed method.

records.title: Semantic-Guided Dual-Granularity Memory Network for Video Camouflaged Object Detection
records.abstract: Video camouflaged object detection (VCOD) is highly challenging, as targets closely resemble their surroundings and motion cues are often unstable. Zoom-based methods can make camouflaged regions more visible, but their enlargement schemes usually retain large amounts of background and rely on coarse, manually designed scaling rules, limiting fine-grained segmentation. We propose a semantic-guided dual-granularity memory framework for robust VCOD. In an offline stage, a language model and a grounding model generate semantically guided focus regions without additional pixel-level annotations. During training, a global memory branch aggregates temporal context from full frames, while a semantic enhancement branch focuses on the enlarged focus regions to refine object details and boundaries. A lightweight gating unit adaptively fuses the two branches. Experiments on multiple VCOD benchmarks demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches, especially for small objects and heavily occluded targets.

records.title: Navigating the Unknown: Continual Test-Time Adaptation for Unknown-Aware Object Detection
records.abstract: Existing continual test-time adaptation frameworks operate under a restrictive closed-set assumption, presuming all objects belong to known training categories. This limitation renders them fragile in open-world scenarios where novel, unknown objects inevitably appear. In this paper, we introduce the Continual Test-Time Adaptive Unknown-aware Object Detection setting, where models must maintain performance on both unknown and known classes under continuous domain shifts. We identify two primary challenges in this setting: the ambiguity of unknowns, where parts of known objects are misclassified as unknown, and the suppression of foregrounds, where valid objects missed by the teacher model are erroneously suppressed as background. Therefore, we propose Unknown-Aware Adaptation (UAA), which incorporates IoU-based Unknown Awareness (IUA) to geometrically distinguish true unknowns from object fragments, and a Foreground Elimination Strategy (FES) that leverages the source model to recover missed detections, preventing the suppression of valid foregrounds. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UAA significantly outperforms baselines, offering robust unknown identification without compromising known-class stability.

records.title: Prompt-Guided Mixture-of-Experts Unlocks CLIP's Potential for Generalized Deepfake Detection and Segmentation
records.abstract: Currently, vision–language models such as CLIP have been widely applied across various domains. However, because their cross-modal knowledge is misaligned with the skills required for deepfake face detection, their potential in this area remains underexplored. In this paper, we show that by fine-tuning CLIP’s text prompts and introducing two lightweight modules, we can fully unleash CLIP’s highly generalizable detection and forgery region segmentation capabilities. Specifically, we first introduce a LoRA-based Mixture-of-Experts adapter (LoME) to fine-tune CLIP’s vision encoder. Then, we incorporate a relatively lightweight convolutional network, the Vision Prompt and Segmentation Module(ViPS), which both guides the router within LoME and, under the supervision of the CLIP vision encoder, performs generalized forgery region segmentation. Experimental results demonstrate that our enhanced CLIP sets new state-of-the-art benchmarks across several datasets, notably achieving roughly a 10% gain over previous methods on the challenging DFDC dataset. Moreover, the fine-tuned model also exhibits strong performance on the forgery region segmentation task.

records.title: Seeing the Unseen: Geometric Priors-driven Method for Cross-view Object Geo-localization
records.abstract: Cross-view object geo-localization (CVOGL) is pivotal for locating ground or drone-view object with overhead satellite imagery. However, existing approaches suffer from two fundamental limitations: the referential ambiguity of point-based user inputs and the loss of fine-grained topology during structure-agnostic feature fusion. To address these challenges, we propose StructGeo, a unified framework that enforces geometric consistency from input to interaction. First, to resolve the input ambiguity, we introduce a Shape Prompt (SP) mechanism. Instead of relying on vague coordinates, SP leverages segmentation foundation models to transform point prompts into explicit geometric masks, providing shape-aware priors for the query. Second, to preserve structural integrity during cross-view alignment, we design the Geometric Structure Perception Fusion Module (GSPFM). By integrating an axial strip modeling strategy, GSPFM effectively captures and aligns the topological details of targets between varying viewpoints. Extensive experiments on the CVOGL and VIGOR-Building benchmarks demonstrate that StructGeo significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, particularly in localizing targets with prominent axial characteristics. Our codes are available at https://github.com/Mech-Who/StructGeo.

records.title: Rethinking Out-of-Distribution Detection through the Lens of Model Generalization
records.abstract: We posit that a model’s ability to detect out-of-distribution (OOD) samples arises from learning a clear and consistent classification logic. This logic does not need to originate from ground-truth (GT) labels; any coherent, learnable rule derived from the data’s inherent structure can suffice. The decisive factor for OOD performance is how well the model generalizes this logic. Our key observation reveals that the performance ceiling in challenging OOD tasks is not solely due to distribution shift, but is fundamentally constrained by the model’s failure to generalize on the in-distribution (ID) task itself. Guided by this principle, we adopt an unsupervised framework that trains classifiers on pseudo-labels to form a learnable classification logic. A central feature of our approach is using the model’s generalization ability on the ID task as a direct criterion for hyperparameter selection. Experiments demonstrate that this generalization-driven strategy consistently outperforms existing unsupervised methods, highlighting a strong and direct link between generalization and effective OOD detection.

records.title: From Extractor to Perceiver: Text-Aware Adapter in CLIP for Zero-Shot Referring Image Segmentation
records.abstract: Existing CLIP-based Referring Image Segmentation (RIS) methods frequently suffer from feature misalignment due to the independent operation of image and text encoders. To mitigate this, we propose a novel Adapter in CLIP framework facilitating fine-grained multi-modal interaction directly within the image encoder. Our dual-branch architecture integrates Local and Global Adapters. Specifically, the Local Adapter exploits SAM masks via gated fusion to achieve precise region-aware alignment. Complementing this, the Global Adapter employs variance-based enhancement and robust similarity estimation to preserve resilient global context, ensuring robustness against low-quality inputs. This architecture effectively transforms the image encoder from a passive feature extractor into an active, text-aware perceiver. Extensive experiments on three benchmarks demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, validating the efficacy of deep internal feature adaptation.

records.title: Spatially Constrained Self-Supervised Contrastive Learning and Adaptive Slicing-Aided Inference for SAR Ship Detection
records.abstract: Ship detection in synthetic-aperture radar (SAR) imagery is essential for maritime monitoring, yet multi-scale variations, sea clutter, and speckle frequently cause missed detections of small vessels and false alarms. Annotated data are scarce, further limiting supervised learning. To this end, we propose SC-SAR, which integrates spatially constrained self-supervised contrastive learning (SC2L) with heatmap-driven adaptive slicing-aided inference (HASI) to improve detection under low-label regimes. SC2L pretrains the encoder on unlabeled data by contrasting neighboring and distant patches to model spatial statistics; the resulting representations exhibit strong transferability under limited annotations, while requiring substantially less pretraining time and GPU resources. HASI converts the first full-image inference into an uncertainty heatmap that fuses spatial proximity, scale, and confidence cues, then performs targeted re-detection on low-confidence regions and merges the results, recovering small vessels and refining localization without architectural changes. Extensive experiments on two public datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of SC-SAR. Notably, an average precision AP_s of 66.9% is achieved on the SSDD dataset for small-ship detection.

records.title: TEAR of the SUNSET: A Benchmark for Road Detection in Off-Road Environment
records.abstract: Recent advances in autonomous driving technology have enabled its mature deployment in structured urban scenarios that rely on standardized artificial markers for perception. However, this reliance limits its applicability in unstructured environments. Semi-structured environments are a subset of unstructured environments characterized by the absence of artificial road markings but the presence of road traces. To address road detection in such environments, this work proposes a dedicated benchmark. We design a novel road representation that models the road edge lines using higher-order Bézier curves. Meanwhile, we construct the annotated SUNSET dataset, tailored for road detection tasks in such environments. Furthermore, we present TEAR, an end-to-end road detection method which employs an Interconvertible Dual-Instance decoder to decouple road and line instances. We also design a Hierarchical Bipartite Matching strategy for instance association.The experimental results demonstrate that TEAR achieves excellent performance on the proposed benchmark.

records.title: Weakly Supervised Incremental Segmentation via Semantic Anchors and Spatial Arbitration
records.abstract: —Weakly Incremental Learning for Semantic Segmentation (WILSS) suffers from the continuous introduction of noisy supervision, which progressively corrupts class-level representations, leading to severe feature drift and semantic corruption, thereby causing newly learned classes to overwrite old ones. To address these issues, we propose an adrift-resilient WILSS approach, named SASA, designed to stabilize semantic learning via Semantic Anchors and Spatial Arbitration. Specifically, at the representation level, we introduce semantic anchors of learnable tokens as rigid class-level references to preserve long-term semantic identity. Complementary to this, an elastic residual adaptation facilitates controlled, instance-specific refinement, ensuring a stable yet flexible learning trajectory. At the supervision level, we develop a Spatial Label Arbitration mechanism that performs geometry-aware decisions to directly filter unreliable signals and enforce a strict “one object, one class” constraint. By synergistically stabilizing representations and improving supervision reliability, SASA effectively mitigates feature drift under weak supervision. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, particularly in challenging multi-step incremental settings. The code is available at https://github.com/ZhonggaiWang/SASA.

records.title: HF-MoE: Unifying Image and Feature Level Morphing Detection via Hierarchical Frequency Mixture of Experts
records.abstract: Face morphing attacks have evolved from image-level blending to feature-level generation, posing severe generalization challenges. To address this challenge, it is essential to uncover shared anomalies across existing methods. We identify that the key to a unified detection strategy lies in the shared linear interpolation operation. Theoretically, while linear in the spatial domain, this operation induces specific frequency anomalies: spectral contraction in magnitude and anomalous nonlinearity in phase. The former results in an abnormal reduction of high-frequency energy, while the latter disrupts natural phase congruency, introducing structural artifacts. Guided by this insight, we propose HF-MoE, a Hierarchical Frequency Mixture of Experts framework. By leveraging learnable spectral experts to adaptively disentangle magnitude and phase irregularities across hierarchical levels, our framework effectively captures multi-scale spectral artifacts, thereby significantly boosting generalization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that HF-MoE achieves state-of-the-art performance against diverse attacks, including graphics-based morphing, StyleGAN, and Diffusion models.

records.title: E-PriorDet: Exploiting Exposure Consistency for Night-Time Object Detection
records.abstract: Low-light object detection is challenged by uneven illumination and glare-induced degradations, where conventional detectors struggle to balance target enhancement and highlight suppression. We propose Exposure-PriorDetector (E-PriorDet), a novel framework that leverages Cross-Exposure Consistency Prior (CECP) to extract illumination-invariant structural cues from randomly simulated exposure variants and inject them into early backbone layers for robust feature learning. A Cross-Exposure Consistency-driven Training Strategy further enforces prediction consistency across exposure pairs, improving exposure generalization. In addition, a lightweight PiE-Mapper module adaptively expands the dynamic range of inputs during end-to-end training. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent improvements across different detectors.

records.title: HARMONIAD:HARMONIZINGLOCALSTRUCTURESANDGLOBALSEMANTICSFOR ANOMALYDETECTION
records.abstract: Anomaly detection is crucial in industrial product quality inspection. Failing to detect tiny defects often leads to serious consequences. Existing methods face a structure–semantics trade-off: structure-oriented models (such as frequency-based filters) are noise-sensitive, while semantics-oriented models (such as CLIP-based encoders) often miss fine details. To address this, we propose HarmoniAD, a frequency-guided dual-branch framework. Features are first extracted by the CLIP image encoder, then transformed into the frequency domain, and finally decoupled into high- and low-frequency paths for complementary modeling of structure and semantics. The high-frequency branch is equipped with a fine-grained structural attention Module (FSAM) to enhance textures and edges for detecting small anomalies, while the low-frequency branch uses a global structural context module (GSCM) to capture long-range dependencies and preserve semantic consistency. Together, these branches balance fine detail and global semantics. HarmoniAD further adopts a multi-class joint training strategy, and experiments on MVTec-AD, VisA, and BTAD show state-of-the-art performance with both sensitivity and robustness.

records.title: FreqDINO: Frequency-Aware Adaptation of Vision Transformers for AI-Generated Content Detection
records.abstract: AI-generated content (AIGC) detection has become increasingly critical as modern generative models rapidly evolve, producing synthetic images that closely resemble real photographs, challenging both human perception and current forensic systems. Traditional detection methods typically rely on handcrafted features or architectures tailored to specific generative mechanisms, which often suffer from poor generalization. While recent methods leveraging pre-trained foundation models have shown promising generalization, their lack of effective fine-tuning for downstream forensic tasks limits their detection capabilities. To overcome these limitations, we propose FreqDINO, a frequency-aware adaptation framework built upon the powerful DINOv3 vision foundation model. Unlike most existing methods that only use the foundation model for feature extraction, our approach introduces two modules for model fine-tuning to better adapt to forensic tasks: DWTAdapter, which refines intermediate representations through wavelet-based attention to capture multi-scale frequency cues, and WLoRA, a wavelet-driven low-rank adaptation mechanism that enables parameter-efficient and frequency-sensitive fine-tuning. Additionally, by integrating feature representations from various stages of DINO, our method allows the model to acquire more comprehensive features for AIGC detection. Extensive experiments across diverse datasets demonstrate that FreqDINO achieves state-of-the-art performance in AIGC detection. Moreover, thorough ablation studies further validate the effectiveness and complementary roles of the proposed modules.

records.title: WinPrompter: Delving into Visual Prompt Tuning for Object Detection with Plain Vision Transformers
records.abstract: While Visual Prompt Tuning (VPT) excels in image classification, applying its static and globally-shared prompts to object detection with plain Vision Transformers (e.g., ViTDet) often degrades performance. We identify this failure stems from a task discrepancy: detection demands precise local discriminability, whereas standard VPT imposes a uniform effect across semantically diverse windows. Moreover, its token concatenation strategy disrupts the spatial geometry crucial for detection. To address these limitations, We propose WinPrompter, a context-aware framework for window-based visual prompt tuning, grounded in the principles of contextual adaptability and intrinsic feature injection. WinPrompter replaces static prompts with a Context-Aware Guidance module, which tailors prompts for each window and injects them into corresponding features via element-wise summation. Furthermore, a Dual-Path Robust Training strategy is introduced to regularize prompt learning against spurious channel-wise correlation. Extensive experiments show that WinPrompter outperforms state-of-the-art Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning methods and full fine-tuning with negligible parameter overhead.

records.title: CrossMDD:Fine-Grained Disentanglement for Multimodal Cross-Domain Deception Detection
records.abstract: Multimodal deception detection aims to analyze the linguistic content and behavioral cues (such as facial expressions and speech prosody) of individuals in videos to identify deceptive intent, holding significant importance for financial security and social media governance. However, existing methods typically treat deception as an anomaly detection task, prompting models to learn its typical features followed by simplistic fusion. This approach overlooks the individual differences in deceptive behavior and the cross-modal semantic gaps among different features. To address these issues, we propose a disentangled representation learning framework designed to isolate domain-invariant features within deceptive behaviors, thereby mitigating individual variations. Specifically, we explicitly disentangle the extracted audio and visual features into distinct components, utilize a Graph Neural Network (GNN) to capture common cross-domain cues of deception, and constrain the distances between homogeneous and heterogeneous features via different regularization loss functions. Furthermore, to capture modal inconsistencies inherent in deceptive acts (such as confident speech co-occurring with nervous vocal tremors), we design a Cross-modal Conflict Verification(CCV) mechanism, enhancing the model's discriminative and generalization capabilities. Evaluated on the fusion dataset proposed for MMDD 2025(The 1st Multimodal Deception Detection Competition), our method outperforms top-ranked approaches from the competition across key metrics, validating its effectiveness.

records.title: VIGIL: Vision-Language Industrial Grounding for Few-shot Defect Detection
records.abstract: Few-shot defect detection poses substantial challenges due to the scarcity of anomalous data samples. While numerous works have been proposed to utilize multi-modal data to improve detection accuracy and generalization ability under data-scarcity scenarios, these methods often underperform in this domain due to significant domain shifts and a lack of specialized terminology, limiting their applicability in real-world scenarios. We introduce VIGIL, a specialized framework adapting Grounding DINO for few-shot industrial defect detection. VIGIL integrates an image-conditioned NanoVLM text encoder, fine-tuned on synthetic industrial VQA data to bridge the semantic gap. To enhance localization, we propose class-wise chunking with positive token mapping for precise contrastive supervision and a scale-aware text–visual fusion module that dynamically handles extreme scale variations. Furthermore, a semantic regularization loss anchors image-conditioned embeddings to offline prototypes, mitigating overfitting in few-shot regimes. Extensive experiments on seven industrial datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over strong text-prompted grounding baselines across 1-, 5-, and 10-shot settings.

records.title: DAFR: Detail-Aware Feature Recomposition for Domain Generalized Semantic Segmentation
records.abstract: Despite recent progress, Domain Generalized Semantic Segmentation (DGSS) remains challenging due to severe distribution shifts across unseen domains. Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) provide strong semantic representations, yet their fixed-resolution outputs and deep abstraction often suppress fine-grained local details crucial for accurate segmentation. Existing approaches typically rely on naive interpolation to construct multi-scale features, which cannot recover lost spatial information and may propagate domain-specific artifacts. We identify feature scaling as a critical yet underexplored bottleneck in VFM-based DGSS pipelines and propose Detail-Aware Feature Recomposition (DAFR), a query-driven feature refinement framework that reconstructs high-resolution representations by integrating raw-image details with coarse VFM features via cross-attention. In addition, we adopt a lightweight In-Batch Mosaic augmentation to introduce scale diversity during training. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent improvements in cross-domain generalization with relatively limited computational and parameter overhead.

records.title: JMI-FDWNet: A Frequency-Decoupled Wavelet Network via Joint Mutual Information for Remote Sensing Change Detection
records.abstract: Remote sensing change detection (RSCD) aims to identify surface change regions between satellite bitemporal images. Existing deep learning-based remote sensing change detection models face several challenges, such as failing to preserve high-frequency details and subtle small-scale alterations, exhibiting limitations in distinguishing pseudo-change, and neglecting frequency domain properties where fixed filters introduce directional ambiguity and redundancy. To address these challenges, we propose JMI-FDWNet, a novel framework that integrates Multi-frequency Domain Wavelet Interaction Transformation (MDWIT) to perform frequency domain decoupling and differencing, thereby mitigating global illumination variations and high-frequency noise. The model further incorporates a Sub-band Specific Attention mechanism to enhance discriminative frequency features and a Joint Distribution Mutual Information (JDMI) module to reduce directional feature confusion and cross-sub-band redundancy. Experimental results on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that JMI-FDWNet achieves state-of-the-art performance.

records.title: Semantic-Aware Interruption Detection in Spoken Dialogue Systems: Benchmark, Metric, and Model
records.abstract: Achieving natural full-duplex interaction in spoken dialogue systems (SDS) remains a challenge due to the difficulty of accurately detecting user interruptions. Current solutions are polarized between "trigger-happy" VAD-based methods that misinterpret backchannels and robust end-to-end models that exhibit unacceptable response delays. Moreover, the absence of real-world benchmarks and holistic metrics hinders progress in the field. This paper presents a comprehensive framework to overcome these limitations. We first introduce SID-Bench, the first benchmark for semantic-aware interruption detection built entirely from real-world human dialogues. To provide a rigorous assessment of the responsiveness-robustness trade-off, we propose the Average Penalty Time (APT) metric, which assigns a temporal cost to both false alarms and late responses. Building on this framework, we design an LLM-based detection model optimized through a novel training paradigm to capture subtle semantic cues of intent. Experimental results show that our model significantly outperforms mainstream baselines, achieving a nearly threefold reduction in APT. By successfully resolving the long-standing tension between speed and stability, our work establishes a new state-of-the-art for intelligent interruption handling in SDS. To facilitate future research, SID-Bench and the associated code will be made publicly available upon acceptance at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/SID-bench-1B9B/.

records.title: HA-DETR: Hardness-Aware Object Detection with Hybrid Assignment for Aerial Imagery
records.abstract: Object detection in aerial imagery remains challenging due to the difficulty of capturing small objects within dense distributions. Although DEtection TRansformer (DETR)-like detectors provide an elegant end-to-end paradigm, they struggle with UAV imagery due to the sparse one-to-one supervision that limits positive sample signals and the weak local feature perception for small objects. To address these issues, we propose HA-DETR, a Hardness-Aware DETR with Hybrid Assignment. HA-DETR introduces a Hardness-Aware Collaborative Supervision mechanism, where a hardness prediction branch utilizes the results of Hungarian matching to guide a one-to-many supervision branch, enhancing the learning of difficult and easily overlooked objects without increasing the number of queries. In addition, an Adaptive Amplification and Fusion Encoder selectively strengthens and fuses multi-level features to improve local discrimination. Experiments show that HA-DETR improves over the baseline by up to 3.0 AP on VisDrone and 2.5 AP on UAVDT.

records.title: Trinity-RepNet: Multi-Expert Feature Co-Guidance and Frequency Calibration for Efficient UAV Object Detection
records.abstract: UAV object detection faces severe challenges from scale variation, cluttered backgrounds, and dense small targets under strict computational constraints. To resolve the inherent efficiency-accuracy paradox, we propose Trinity-RepNet, a "training-heavy, inference-light" framework. To enhance collaborative representation learning, three RepViT experts are co-optimized via a Trinity Co-Guidance Mechanism, using P2P-VICReg loss to enforce inter-expert orthogonality and non-degenerate feature variance. Complementarily, a Frequency-Domain Calibration (FDC) branch decomposes predicted density maps via FFT to provide spectral supervision, actively suppressing high-frequency noise while preserving global context. For efficient deployment, we employ additive parameter fusion to structurally consolidate these experts into a single backbone. This achieves Zero-Cost Inference—merging multi-expert intelligence into single-model latency. Empirically, Trinity-RepNet breaks the conventional size-accuracy correlation on the VisDrone benchmark, delivering large-model level accuracy of 48.5% AP50 with only 8.0M parameters at a real-time speed of 102 FPS.

records.title: Adversarial Training for Object Detection via Curriculum Learning
records.abstract: Adversarial Training (AT) is the most effective method for enhancing the adversarial robustness of deep neural networks. However, its high training cost has hindered its application in computationally intensive tasks such as object detection. Existing methods employ a free replay mechanism to reduce the cost of adversarial training on object detectors, but the speed improvement inevitably leads to a degradation in recognition accuracy. Moreover, using adversarial examples with excessively high attack strength in the early training stages may cause the model to struggle with convergence. To address these issues, this paper proposes a curriculum learning based adversarial training method for object detection, enhancing the detector's robustness through a progressive learning strategy integrated into Free Adversarial Training (FreeAT) pipeline. Specifically, we design dynamic replay and a dynamic perturbation budget that increase linearly with training epochs. This strategy synthesizes adversarial examples with lower attack strength in the early stages and harder, high-intensity adversarial examples in the later stages, thereby achieving an improved trade-off between clean accuracy and adversarial robustness. Furthermore, compared to existing algorithms, we provide a more detailed convergence guarantee for the proposed method under the assumption of non-convex smoothness. Extensive experiments on the PASCAL VOC object detection dataset validate the effectiveness of the proposed method compared to existing state-of-the-art adversarial training methods.

records.title: Beyond Hierarchy: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Fine-Grained Vehicle Semantic Grounding in Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
records.abstract: Open-vocabulary object detection (OVOD) is commonly evaluated using coarse-grained categories and aggregate detection metrics, leaving its fine-grained semantic capability largely unexamined. In practice, fine-grained semantics often span non-hierarchical dimensions, characterized by identity-based attributes in passenger cars and appearance-based variations in trucks, which are not adequately captured by existing benchmarks. As a result, the impact of fine-grained supervision on open-vocabulary behavior and semantic drift remains unclear. To address this issue, we propose a diagnostic evaluation framework, together with the newly constructed FG-Truck dataset, to probe fine-grained semantic sensitivity through controlled positive and negative caption perturbations. The framework employs dataset-aware caption designs tailored to identity-based and appearance-based vehicle semantics. By introducing a Fusion-Based Fine-Grained Hit Assessment (FGA), we reveal a consistent trade-off between closed-set specialization and open-vocabulary generalization not reflected by conventional evaluation protocols, offering a diagnostic tool to guide future OVOD model development under fine-grained supervision.To address this issue, we propose a diagnostic evaluation framework that probes fine-grained semantic sensitivity through controlled positive and negative caption perturbations. By analyzing model responses under both zero-shot and fine-tuned settings, and introducing a fusion-based fine-grained hit assessment, we reveal a consistent trade-off between closed-set specialization and open-vocabulary generalization that is not reflected by conventional evaluation protocols.

records.title: Frequency-Aware Disentanglement for Dense and Tiny Object Detection in UAV Imagery
records.abstract: Object detection in UAV imagery faces two critical challenges: the feature degradation of tiny objects and the instance ambiguity in dense scenes. We propose DroneDEIM,a lightweight framework designed to mitigate these issues via frequency-aware refinement. Our first contribution, the Frequency-Aware SPPF (FA-SPPF), utilizes a spectral-energy proxy to selectively amplify high-frequency signals, rescuing tiny objects from feature suppression. Second, we introduce the Instance-Disentanglement Module (IDM), which employs Query-Aware Channel Modulation (QACM) to isolate target features within the channel manifold, resolving overlap ambiguity. DroneDEIM is evaluated on four diverse benchmarks:VisDrone2019, HIT-UAV (thermal), CoDrone, and CARPK (dense counting). Results demonstrate state-of-the-art performance (46.5% AP50 on VisDrone) with only 7.6M parameters and 80.5 FPS. Our model provides a robust and efficient solution across various aerial scenarios, maintaining a superior balance between detection accuracy and real-time deployment feasibility.
