records.title: MonoLSPF: Large-kernel Spatial Parallel Feature Fusion Framework for Monocular 3D Object Detection
records.abstract: Monocular 3D object detection is a critical task in autonomous driving, which captures 3D properties of objects, including dimensions and orientation, through a single RGB camera. However, a common challenge is that monocular cameras cannot capture depth information. This paper introduces an innovative monocular 3D object detection method: a Large-kernel Spatial Parallel Feature Fusion Framework for Monocular 3D Object Detection (MonoLSPF). The core innovation of this framework lies in the design of the Large-Kernel Spatial Parallel Feature Fusion Module (LSPF) and the Nested Orthogonal Multi-scale Shuffle Module (NOMS). The LSPF module achieves pixel-level global relationship modeling through depth-wise separable large-kernel convolutions, obtaining an approximate global receptive field while maintaining the translation equivariance of convolutions. This module employs multi-scale feature extraction with adaptive representation, multi-dimensional attention enhancement mechanisms, and hierarchical feature fusion strategies. The NOMS module comprises three core components: grouped nested processor, orthogonal fusion unit, and adaptive feature shuffler, which effectively addresses the information isolation problem caused by grouping operations through constructing feature pyramids and dual-branch parallel processing architecture. We evaluated our method on the KITTI 3D object detection benchmark, where MonoLSPF surpassed SOTA monocular 3D detection models in car and cyclist detection, achieving $19.51\%$ \text{AP}_{\text{3D}}.

records.title: YOLO-EPMD: A Weed Detection Method for Cotton Fields Based on Balanced Perception and Dual-Branch Detection Heads
records.abstract: Precise detection of weeds in farmland, as a core component of smart agricultural management, holds significant importance for achieving intelligent regulation of crop growth conditions. Addressing challenges in real-world farmland scenarios,such as complex spatial weed distribution and significant target size variations,this paper proposes YOLO-EPMD, a weed detection model tailored for complex cotton field environments. This model employs a multidimensional balanced perception attention network (Enhanced Pyramid Module with Dynamic Scale Perception, EPMD) to resolve class imbalance and en hance small object detection; introduces EPConv convolutions to strengthen small object feature representation; and incorporates a Dual-Branch Matching Head (DBMH) to enhance detection capabilities. We constructed the proprietary Cotton_Weeds14 dataset, comprising 5876 images of 14 weed species across various growth stages and scenarios. Results demonstrate that YOLO-EPMD achieves a 3.3% improvement in mean average precision at 50% (mAP50) on the custom dataset and a 0.8% gain on the public CottonWeedDet12 dataset.

records.title: Ship30: Benchmarking Fine-grained Out-of-distribution Ship Detection
records.abstract: Due to the rapid development of the maritime industry, the categories of ships are constantly increasing, and the existing classification system is difficult to cover all the ships that appear in real scenarios. Moreover, the high similarity between different ship categories further leads to missed ship inspections. To address these issues, we construct Ship30, a benchmark of ships containing 30 categories and 8,964 annotated images. Moreover, we introduce a novel fine-grained OOD ship detection framework, Text-guided Refinement for ID and OOD ENTities(TRIDENT). TRIDENT expand label space by using existing ID labels or a few ID images and enhances ID category discrimination by optimizing text embedding with image semantics.Then, OOD text representation and optimized ID text representation were integrated to calculate similarity and define scores. Experiments on multiple datasets consistently outperforms state-ofthe-art approaches, achieving average improvements of 10.42% in FPR95 and 5.37% in AUROC. Moreover, our method can achieve millisecond-level ship detection, reaching the practical application level.

records.title: Disentangle Before You Fuse: Uncertainty-Aware Visible–Infrared Aerial Object Detection
records.abstract: Visible-infrared aerial object detection is challenged by modality complementarity collapses, often caused by co-located low illumination visible inputs and spurious infrared signals such as thermally confusable patterns and ghosting artifacts. Existing multimodal fusion methods frequently entangle classes, mistakenly linking misleading infrared responses with true visible instances, leading to false positives. To mitigate this, we propose DiBI-Net, a Hierarchical Category Disentangling-before-Interaction Mechanism designed to decouple inter-class confusion and address co-located modality uncertainties. Central to this is the Vision-Language Hierarchical Category Disentangler (VL-HCD), which first separates features into category-aware components using auxiliary semantic segmentation, and then projects each instance into a class-specific subspace guided by text embeddings to enhance semantic alignment. For cross-modal interaction, we introduce the Local-to-Global Cross-Modal Compensator (LoG), which identifies category-specific modality discrepancies via a prototype-guided residual block and aggregates global intra-class cues for robust compensation. Our approach explicitly disentangles semantic confusion before fusion, yielding reliable and state-of-the-art performances on DroneVehicle and VEDAI benchmarks.

records.title: Fragment-Aware Two-Stage Object Detection
records.abstract: Current object detection algorithms lack an explicit supervisory signal indicating that a proposal, while belonging to the correct object category, captures only a small portion of the object. We address this issue with a fragment-aware object detector built around a notion of purity, a box-level coverage measure that quantifies the fraction of object pixels inside a proposal. Fragment proposals are defined as high purity, low Intersection over Union (IoU) boxes that depict only part of the object. Our framework formally characterizes fragments via purity and IoU, uses a label-assignment rule that ignores fragment proposals during training, and adds a purity head that calibrates detection scores at inference. The resulting detector improves accuracy and predictive reliability and is more robust to synthetic fragment-like annotation noise than a Faster R-CNN baseline.

records.title: Hierarchical Relational Reasoning and Text-Guided Human-Object-Human Interaction Detection
records.abstract: Human-object-human interactions (HOHI) are critical for fine-grained video understanding in domains such as daily activity analysis, embodied AI, and assistive systems. However, existing interaction detection methods struggle to model the multi-agent relational complexity inherent in HOHI. We propose HRTG, a hierarchical relation reasoning and text-guided framework that jointly captures first-order human-object and second-order human-object-human relations, enabling more reliable recognition of complex interaction patterns. A text-guided enhancement module further integrates natural language semantics to distinguish visually similar actions. To support the evaluation, we introduce HOH-DailyLife, a dataset with fine-grained HOHI annotations in everyday scenarios. Extensive experiments show that HRTG achieves superior accuracy and consistent performance compared to state-of-the-art approaches, thus improving the model’s ability to understand complex interaction behaviors.

records.title: Focus on Driver Perception Preference: General Threat Object Detection in the Open World
records.abstract: Autonomous driving is a typical open-world scenario where perception systems are expected to detect threat objects, especially unknown ones that fall outside predefined categories. While open-vocabulary detection models offer promising solutions by leveraging semantic priors from large-scale pretraining, their reliance on explicit category prompts conflicts with threat object detection. Threats are context-dependent rather than category-defined, and predefining categories for all unforeseen hazards is impractical. To address this issue, we focus on driver perception preferences and propose a general threat object detection framework, which unifies diverse threats under a single "threat" embedding, moving beyond exhaustive category enumeration. To provide explicit supervision, we design a fully automated annotation pipeline termed Semantic-Geometry Dual-Branch Labeling (SGDBL). This pipeline combines context-aware semantic reasoning via multimodal large language models (MLLMs) with class-agnostic object localization through monocular geometry estimation (MGE). The resulting pseudo-labels are then combined with ground-truth annotations to fine-tune the model using parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT). Extensive experiments on CODA dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, achieving a 12.1% improvement in unknown AP over the previous state-of-the-art.

records.title: NeCo-CD: Neighborhood Relational Propagation and Contrastive Learning for Semi-Supervised Change Detection
records.abstract: Semi-supervised remote sensing change detection (RSCD) leverages unlabeled images to mitigate annotation scarcity. However, existing methods often treat change detection as independent pixel-wise classification, overlooking local context and rich semantic relations across bi-temporal image pairs, limiting the ability to exploit unlabeled data. To address these, we propose \textbf{NeCo-CD}, a semi-supervised CD framework that enhances unlabeled-data utilization by jointly modeling neighborhood pixel relations and global semantic discrimination. First, we propose the \textbf{Neighborhood Relational Propagation (NeRP)} module, which shows that modeling correlations within the neighborhood is essential as a spatial prior, and demonstrates squared Euclidean distance as an effective correlation measure in our method. Second, we introduce contrastive learning with the \textbf{Neighborhood Entropy Selection (NES)} anchor selection strategy. NES measures neighborhood uncertainty instead of single-pixel confidence, and adaptively mines informative anchors to enhance category-level discriminability across bi-temporal image pairs. Experiments on LEVIR-CD and WHU-CD demonstrate that NeCo-CD achieves state-of-the-art performance in most settings.

records.title: Object-aware Low-Rank Adaptation for Domain Incremental Object Detection
records.abstract: Domain incremental object detection has attracted increasing attention for its ability to perform object detection across a sequence of domains. Although this ability enables the model to adapt to the ever-changing real world, it also causes the model to forget previously acquired knowledge. Existing methods mostly alleviate forgetting by maintaining the stability of important features from old domains. However, features learned by these works may include domain-specific non-object features, which can exacerbate the plasticity–stability dilemma due to domain shifts. To address this, we propose Object-Aware Low-Rank Adaptation (OA-LoRA), a rehearsal-free domain incremental object detection method. Specifically, we first design an Object-aware Gradient Correction (OAGC) module, which learns object features by correcting the gradients through cross-domain gradient similarity. Second, to mitigate catastrophic forgetting of learned features, we devise a Feature Similarity-based Domain Selection (FSDS) module, which leverages pre-trained knowledge to select parameters corresponding to the sample’s domain. Extensive experiments on the Pascal VOC and Cityscapes series datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of OA-LoRA.

records.title: BRG-Bokeh: Boundary-Refined 3DGS Segmentation for Multi-View Consistent Bokeh
records.abstract: Generating consistent bokeh effects for foreground objects in 3D scenes across multiple viewpoints poses a significant challenge for single-image bokeh methods, due to inconsistent focus target localization and prominent boundary artifacts. To address these challenges, we propose a novel framework that integrates depth-regularized scene reconstruction and boundary-refined 3D segmentation to learn a 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) representation. Specifically, we leverage Depth Anything v3 to generate monocular depth maps and SAM3 to produce text-prompt-driven masks, which respectively serve as ground truth for depth estimation and segmentation. This allows the learned 3DGS to simultaneously generate RGB images, depth maps, and spatially consistent masks of the target object across multiple views. Furthermore, we develop a multi-view consistent bokeh rendering method that reassigns depth values to pixels within the in-focus object and applies dual-band Gaussian smoothing to mitigate edge artifacts. Comprehensive experiments on segmentation and bokeh datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms 3D segmentation methods and single-image bokeh methods. Notably, our method realizes flexible, natural, and multi-view consistent bokeh rendering, providing a promising solution for scenarios requiring highly precise and coherent defocus effects across multiple viewpoints.

records.title: Conditional Edge Diffusion Model for Weakly-Supervised Salient Object Detection
records.abstract: Weakly-supervised Salient Object Detection (WSOD) approaches provide a cost-effective alternative to pixel-level supervision. However, existing methods rely on sparse cues and semantic segmentation frameworks, which still suffer from low-quality pseudo-labels, blurred boundaries and unstable predictions. To alleviate these challenges, we propose a novel generative framework—Conditional Edge Diffusion Model with SAM-based Pseudo-Label Optimization (SAM-CEDiff), which exploits the iterative refinement capability of diffusion models to enhance WSOD performance. Specifically, an Uncertainty Guided Prompt Enhancer (UGPE) is designed to improve SAM-generated pseudo-labels under enhanced prompts. In addition, an Edge Auxiliary Attention Module (EAAM) is integrated into the conditional diffusion process to explicitly leverage edge information for boundary refinement. Furthermore, we propose an Adaptive Noise Scheduling Strategy (ANSS) to dynamically adjust noise levels across diffusion time steps, improving the robustness and fine-grained representation capability of our model. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art WSOD approaches and attains competitive performance compared to some fully-supervised methods.

records.title: Modality-Specific Hierarchical Enhancement for RGB-D Camouflaged Object Detection
records.abstract: Camouflaged object detection (COD) is challenging due to high target-background similarity, and recent methods address this by complementarily using RGB-D texture and geometry cues. However, RGB-D COD methods still underutilize modality-specific cues, which limits fusion quality. We believe this is because RGB and depth features are fused directly after backbone extraction without modality-specific enhancement. To address this limitation, we propose MHENet, an RGB-D COD framework that performs modality-specific hierarchical enhancement and adaptive fusion of RGB and depth features. Specifically, we introduce a Texture Hierarchical Enhancement Module (THEM) to amplify subtle texture variations by extracting high-frequency information and a Geometry Hierarchical Enhancement Module (GHEM) to enhance geometric structures via learnable gradient extraction, while preserving cross-scale semantic consistency. Finally, an Adaptive Dynamic Fusion Module (ADFM) adaptively fuses the enhanced texture and geometry features with spatially varying weights. Experiments on four benchmarks demonstrate that MHENet surpasses 16 state-of-the-art methods qualitatively and quantitatively. Code is available at https://github.com/afdsgh/MHENet.

records.title: STAR-Det: Pseudo-Label Adaptive and Reassignment Learning for Self-Training Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
records.abstract: Open-vocabulary object detection employs self-training methods to learn the generalization capabilities of VLM, thereby overcoming the category limitations inherent in conventional supervised learning approaches. However, recent works have directly replaced manually annotated ground truth labels with pseudo labels generated by VLM, without conducting deeper analysis on the impact of pseudo labels on training. In this paper, a novel self-training framework named STAR-Det addresses the limitations of existing methods from the generation and use of pseudo labels. Most pseudo labels were correctly classified by VLM, while they were not entirely beneficial for training the current detector. To address this challenges, we innovatively fuse the prediction scores from current detectors with the classification scores from VLM to select suitable pseudo labels. These pseudo labels are not only novel objects but also beneficial to the detector. Meanwhile, STAR-Det integrates a two-branch detection head that masks the ground truth box to reassign pseudo labels. This effectively resolves the issue of novel class labels being obscured in real-world environments. Extensive experiments demonstrate the module we propose achieves the new state of the arts in 49.6 APnovel and 26.4 APr on the OV-COCO and OV-LVIS benchmarks.

records.title: Generalizable Detection of AI Generated Images with Large Models and Fuzzy Decision Tree
records.abstract: The malicious use and widespread dissemination of AI-generated images pose a serious threat to the authenticity of digital content. Existing detection methods exploit low-level artifacts left by common manipulation steps within the generation pipeline, but they often lack generalization due to model-specific overfitting. Recently, researchers have resorted to Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) for AIGC detection, leveraging their high-level semantic reasoning and broad generalization capabilities. While promising, MLLMs lack the fine-grained perceptual sensitivity to subtle generation artifacts, making them inadequate as standalone detectors. To address this issue, we propose a novel AI-generated image detection framework that synergistically integrates lightweight artifact-aware detectors with MLLMs via a fuzzy decision tree. The decision tree treats the outputs of basic detectors as fuzzy membership values, enabling adaptive fusion of complementary cues from semantic and perceptual perspectives. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and strong generalization across diverse generative models.

records.title: ABC-LandSeg: A landslide segmentation framework based on adaptive feature selection and boundary correction
records.abstract: Landslides, characterized by their sudden onset and destructive impact, pose substantial challenges to disaster prevention and mitigation. In remote sensing imagery, their pronounced multi-scale variability and ambiguous boundaries often hinder the effectiveness of conventional segmentation models. To address these issues, we present ABC-LandSeg, a semantic segmentation framework equipped with adaptive feature selection and boundary correction. The framework incorporates three key components: (1) AMS that constructs multiscale features from fixed-scale transformer layers by grouping and adaptively weighting them to improve spatial-scale perception; (2)CSCI that enables lightweight bidirectional fusion between high-level semantic features and low-level details; (3)BUC that enhances delineation of ambiguous edges through uncertainty-guided correction. Extensive experiments on the CAS and Bijie landslide datasets demonstrate that ABC-LandSeg achieves state-ofthe-art performance, surpassing representative CNN-based and Transformer-based baselines by up to 1.8% in mIoU and 1.85% in Dice, while maintaining excellent efficiency and robustness. Index Terms—Landslide segmentation, adaptive multi-scale processing, boundary refinement

records.title: Modality Trust Graph: Uncertainty-Aware Manifold Rectification for Multimodal Salient Object Detection
records.abstract: Multimodal salient object detection (MSOD) aims to combine RGB images with auxiliary modalities to predict salient objects. In practice, auxiliary sensors are often unreliable, while existing fusion models still assume all modalities are equally trustworthy at every pixel, causing noisy signals to be propagated and amplified. We propose a Modality Trust Graph (MTG) that turns fusion into uncertainty-aware, trustworthy inference. First, we build Saliency Manifold References (SMRs) by clustering salient-region features from the training set into stable semantic anchors. At inference, multimodal features and SMRs are modeled as graph nodes, and pixel-wise uncertainty maps dynamically gate edge weights, weakening unreliable modalities and rectifying features along the saliency manifold. The calibrated representations are decoded into saliency maps under joint saliency and uncertainty losses. Experiments on several RGB-D and RGB-T benchmarks show that MTG consistently improves robustness and accuracy, especially under degraded auxiliary modalities.

records.title: Aligning Spectral Properties with Inductive Biases for Robust Multi-Modal Salient Object Detection
records.abstract: Existing Multi-modal Salient Object Detection (MSOD) methods often overlook the misalignment between visual spectral properties and network inductive biases. To address this, we propose the Spectral-State Synergy Network, which adheres to the principle of Spectral-Inductive Bias Alignment. We introduce a Spectral-State Synergistic Block that employs a learnable soft spectral mask to decouple frequency components. Specifically, low-frequency global structures are routed to State Space Models for isomorphic long-range modeling, while high-frequency local details are processed by CNNs to preserve edge sharpness. Furthermore, to handle noise in auxiliary modalities, we construct a Sparse Prototype Manifold to extract semantic priors, guiding an Uncertainty-Aware Spectral Arbiter for robust fusion. Our method effectively unifies physical attributes with architectural strengths, achieving superior robustness.

records.title: TG-WSPIS: Multi-Granular Text-Guided Weakly Supervised Pathology Image Segmentation
records.abstract: The high cost of pixel-level annotations has brought increasing attention to weakly supervised pathological image segmentation. However, conventional weak supervision approaches based on image-level labels often fail to capture the heterogeneity of cellular distributions, leading to incomplete supervision. To address this limitation, we propose TG-WSPIS, a text-guided weakly supervised pathological image segmentation paradigm that replaces traditional image-level labels with textual supervision. To bridge the visual-textual semantic gap, TG-WSPIS introduces a soft-alignment multimodal cell consensus algorithm and a unidirectional Gaussian mutual information-based collaborative learning mechanism, enabling more effective cross-modal alignment and improving segmentation performance. Specifically, we design three types of textual captions for each cell type in every image: global proportion, spatial distribution, and their fused representation, which are mapped into a unified multimodal semantic space. A newly proposed Pathology Multimodal Cell Consensus (PMCC) algorithm quantifies the semantic consistency between pathological images and textual descriptions. The framework further incorporates three caption-alignment branches and employs mutual learning to integrate cross-granularity knowledge. In addition, we construct two benchmark datasets, BCSS-T3G and WSSS4LUAD-T3G, to support comprehensive evaluation on the proposed TG-WSPIS task. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves superior segmentation performance across multiple metrics, confirming the effectiveness of text-guided weak supervision with multi-granular alignment. The dataset and source code will be released at: https://github.com/alp789/TG-WSPIS.

records.title: Multi-Granularity Inconsistency Learning for Partial Audio Forgery Detection and Localization
records.abstract: Partial audio forgery manipulates specific audio frames to alter the original semantic content, posing significant challenges to detection and localization. Most existing detection methods rely on intra-frame artifacts, overlooking acoustic inconsistencies at other granularities. In this work, we conduct systematic analyses on widely used datasets and identify three complementary inconsistencies induced by partial tampering: intra-frame spectral inconsistency, inter-frame loudness inconsistency, and boundary timestamps discontinuities. Motivated by these findings, we propose MGITracer, a multi-granularity inconsistency learning framework that jointly models three inconsistency patterns for robust partial forgery detection and localization. MGITracer integrates two complementary components: a Frame-based Feature Aggregation Module that captures both intra-frame artifacts and inter-frame inconsistencies, and a Boundary-based Multi-scale Discrepancy Perception Module that characterizes boundary context across multiple temporal windows to detect abrupt transitions at tampering boundaries. Extensive experiments on three datasets demonstrate our method achieves a state-of-the-art performance in both Partial Forgery Detection and Temporal Forgery Localization.

records.title: ASG-Net:Manifold-Consistent Asymmetric Fusion via VLM Priors for RGB-Infrared Object Detection
records.abstract: Adapting Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to multispectral object detection is impeded by the semantic-structural gap between infrared (IR) modalities and RGB-centric pre-training manifolds. Conventional symmetric fusion overlooks this disparity, causing feature contamination where thermal noise disrupts VLM alignment. To address this, we propose ASG-Net, an asymmetric framework that repurposes IR as a conditional structural prompt. We introduce a Structure-Aware Thermal Prompter (STP) for manifold alignment and a Semantic-Guided Denoising Fusion (SGDF) mechanism. Crucially, a frozen VLM acts as a semantic anchor, utilizing tri-modal arbitration to inject structural cues only when validated by semantic consensus, effectively suppressing background clutter. Extensive experiments on LLVIP and DroneVehicle demonstrate that ASG-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance. Notably, on the LLVIP benchmark, it achieves 96.9% mAP50 and surpasses the runner-up method by a significant margin of 5.0% in mAP.

records.title: Amplify Uncertainty Feature for Weakly-Supervised Semantic Segmentation
records.abstract: Weakly-Supervised Semantic Segmentation relying on Class Activation Maps (CAMs) often overlooks the modeling of uncertainty regions in CAMs, which inherently limits their capability to identify complete object extents. A novel Amplify Uncertainty Feature (AUF) method is proposed that amplifies the representation of uncertainty regions while preserving discriminative features of salient areas. Specifically, AUF explicitly amplifies features in uncertainty regions through feature perturbation, enabling uncertainty features to align with semantic information without erasing critical visual evidence. Moreover, an Uncertainty Region Constraint (URC) loss is designed to minimize over-reliance on uncertainty regions, ensuring a balance between uncertainty exploration and discriminative feature retention. Ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of AUF and URC, improving CAM quality (72.8% mIoU on VOC and 42.5% on COCO) and pseudo-label accuracy (71.0% mIoU on VOC and 44.8% on COCO). AUF further achieves 74.7% mIoU on the PASCAL VOC 2012 validation set (74.5% on test) and 44.1% mIoU on the MS COCO 2014 validation set, demonstrating superior performance.

records.title: DARC: Difficulty-Aware Adaptive Routing with Multi-Model Collaboration for Efficient Object Detection
records.abstract: Object detection in complex real-world scenes requires balancing computational efficiency and detection accuracy across inputs of varying difficulty. Lightweight detectors enable fast inference but often perform poorly on complex samples, while vision-language models(VLM) offer stronger representational capacity yet incur substantially higher computational costs. To address this challenge, we propose DARC, a difficulty-aware adaptive routing framework with multi-model collaboration for efficient object detection. First, a lightweight-driven dynamic routing mechanism uses low-cost predictive cues from the lightweight detector to evaluate input difficulty. Second, a structured and parameter-efficient fine-tuning approach improves the VLM’s performance on routed hard samples. It freezes pre-trained backbone parameters and injects low-rank adaptations into attention modules. Extensive experiments on the COCO and DAWN datasets show that DARC improves detection efficiency while maintaining accuracy. It reduces inference time by over 62% and lowers power consumption by more than 50% in complex scene distributions.

records.title: Reliability-Guided Dual-View Multimodal Graph Learning for Social Bot Detection
records.abstract: Social bot detection is increasingly challenged by heterogeneous relations, noisy or adversarial connectivity, and limited supervision on real-world social platforms. Existing graph-based detectors can be brittle under heterophily and injected interactions, where unreliable edges contaminate message passing and distort node representations. We propose ReDBot, a reliability-guided dual-view multimodal graph learning framework for robust social bot detection. ReDBot first encodes multimodal user attributes into unified node representations, and then jointly learns from two complementary views: (i) a Structure-Denoising Branch that estimates relation-aware edge reliability without edge-level supervision and performs robust multi-relational aggregation with a Multi-Granularity Relational Graph Transformer, and (ii) a Raw-Graph Context Branch that operates on the original graph to preserve weak ties and broader relational context that may be attenuated by denoising. We further introduce a unified objective that combines uncertainty-aware multi-branch supervision with reliability-guided contrastive regularization to stabilize training under class imbalance and noisy topology. Experiments on TwiBot-20 and MGTAB show that ReDBot achieves best or highly competitive performance across metrics, demonstrating strong robustness and generalization.

records.title: PCFR: Progressive Cross-Domain Feature Reconstruction for Weakly-Supervised Object Segmentation in Hazy Remote Sensing Imagery
records.abstract: Weakly supervised object segmentation (WSOS) in hazy remote sensing imagery (RSI) suffers from inherent multidimensional degradations: visual suppression that erodes feature discriminability, severe data imbalance leading to the ``stochastic absence" of rare classes under batch constraints, and atmospheric scattering that causes ``attention bleeding" and structural ambiguity. To surmount these coupled challenges, we propose Progressive Cross-domain Feature Reconstruction (PCFR), a unified framework that systematically restores integrity across three domains. Specifically, we introduce the Saliency-Encoded Differentiated Dehazing (SEDD) module, which utilizes a task-discriminative prior to reconcile background suppression with foreground fidelity. To address data scarcity, we devise the Memory-Augmented Distribution Rectification (MADR) strategy, employing a ``store-and-inject" mechanism to decouple semantic injection from batch-wise sampling. Furthermore, the Geometric-Coherent Contextual Refinement (GCCR) module incorporates region-level geometric priors to robustly regulate context propagation, enforcing boundary consistency even in low-contrast conditions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PCFR significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, establishing a robust baseline for semantic learning in complex hazy environments.

records.title: Token-Space Masking via VQ-GAN Inversion for Defending Against Adversarial Patch Attacks in Object Detection
records.abstract: Adversarial patch attacks pose a significant threat to deep learning-based object detectors due to their ease of implementation. Among various defense strategies, defending by locating and eliminating adversarial patches is one of the most practical for deployed detectors, as it preserves the original inference pipeline without requiring architectural modifications or retraining of the detectors. In this paper, a training-free defense method is proposed by utilizing a reconstruction-based generative model, VQ-GAN. Comprehensive studies are conducted to demonstrate that the token space of VQ-GAN exhibits strong spatial and semantic correspondence with the original image. Building on these insights, token-space masking is proposed a technique to eliminate the adversarial patches to overcome the limitations of pixel-space masking in certain conditions. Experimental results on the INRIA pedestrian dataset show that the proposed method outperforms existing locating and eliminating defenses and achieves improved performance against perturbation-like adversarial patch attacks in pedestrian detection.

records.title: Enhancing Event-based Object Detection with Monocular Normal Maps
records.abstract: Object detection in autonomous driving is frequently compromised by complex illumination. While event cameras offer a robust solution, they are susceptible to sudden contrast changes such as reflections which often trigger dense, misleading event signals. To overcome this, we leverage RGB-derived surface normal maps as explicit geometric constraints. Crucially, even when RGB degrades, they preserve low-frequency structural priors that effectively assist in event-based detection. Consequently, we present NRE-Net, a trimodal framework that integrates structural priors from surface Normal maps, appearance context from RGB images, and high-frequency dynamics from Events. The Adaptive Dual-stream Fusion Module (ADFM) first aligns geometric and appearance cues, followed by the Event-modality Aware Fusion Module (EAFM) which selectively integrates event dynamics. Extensive evaluations on DSEC-Det-sub and PKU-DAVIS-SOD demonstrate that incorporating geometric priors yields an additional 3.0% AP50 gain over dual-modal baselines, while our approach consistently outperforms fusion methods such as SFNet (+2.7%) and SODFormer (+7.1%).

records.title: Label Decoder: Synthesizing Object Detection Data from Diffusion Feature under Limited Labeled Data
records.abstract: Object detection models rely on large-scale labeled datasets to achieve high accuracy, while such data is costly and time-consuming to collect. Existing object detection data synthesis methods either require additional layout information for conditioning or object detectors pretrained with large-scale datasets, which are unavailable in data-scarce scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose \textbf{Label Decoder}, a framework that decodes object detection annotations from intermediate features of the diffusion model, with only a small amount of labeled data. A joint data- and model-level learning strategy is designed to mitigate the gap between real-synthetic features and enhance annotation quality. Furthermore, we introduce a two-stage LLM-based prompt construction approach to generate diverse training data for downstream detection models. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that our method produces high-quality annotations and substantially improves detection performance in data-scarce scenarios.

records.title: SynSeg: Feature Synergy for Multi-Category Contrastive Learning in End-to-End Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation
records.abstract: Semantic segmentation in open-vocabulary scenarios presents significant challenges due to the wide range and granularity of semantic categories. Existing weakly-supervised methods often rely on category-specific supervision and ill-suited feature construction methods for contrastive learning, leading to semantic misalignment and poor performance. In this work, we introduce a novel weakly-supervised approach, SynSeg, to address the challenges. SynSeg performs Multi-Category Contrastive Learning (MCCL) as a stronger training signal which robustly injecting intra- and inter-category knowledge during training. We also propose a new feature reconstruction framework named Feature Synergy Structure (FSS). FSS reconstructs discriminative features for contrastive learning through prior fusion and semantic-activation-map enhancement, effectively avoiding the foreground bias introduced by the visual encoder. Furthermore, SynSeg is a lightweight end-to-end solution capable for real-time inference. In general, SynSeg effectively improves the abilities in semantic localization and discrimination under weak supervision in an efficient manner. Extensive experiments on benchmarks demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance, with mIoU score gains ranging from 0.6% up to 8.9% across all reported benchmarks.

records.title: DRPFNet: Dual-domain Residual Progressive Fusion Network for RGB-Thermal Object Detection
records.abstract: RGB-thermal (RGB-T) object detection aims to fuse complementary information from visible and thermal modalities to achieve robust detection under varying illumination and weather conditions. Current methods typically employ attention mechanisms or transformers to perform cross-modal fusion independently at each feature scale, directly combining RGB and thermal features in the spatial domain. However, they still face significant limitations: cross-level knowledge inheritance caused by independent fusion at each scale, suppressing noise continuously due to the lack of bidirectional optimization, and information degradation induced by the absence of frequency-spatial collaboration. To address these issues, we propose DRPFNet, a Dual-domain Residual Progressive Fusion Network that constructs a unified information flow optimization system from three synergistic levels: structure, feature, and enhancement. At the structural level, we establish cross-scale propagation through bottom-up knowledge accumulation and bidirectional enhancement, ensuring smooth information flow. At the feature level, we collaboratively extract RGB high-frequency edges and thermal low-frequency structures via frequency band separation and edge guidance, guaranteeing representation quality. At the enhancement level, we enhance foreground-background discrimination through edge-guided dual-domain refinement, achieving precise object localization. Extensive experiments on two public RGB-T datasets demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance with competitive efficiency, validating the effectiveness of this hierarchical collaborative strategy.

records.title: FabricEyes-ACD: A Large-Scale Dataset for Reference-Based Anomaly Change Detection in Textiles
records.abstract: Detecting logical anomalies—defects that violate design constraints rather than local texture statistics—remains a formidable challenge in industrial vision. While recent benchmarks address logical violations in discrete object arrangements, they overlook Continuous Pattern Verification, where anomalies manifest as valid textures appearing in invalid topological contexts (e.g., misaligned patterns on textiles). To bridge this gap, we make three contributions. First, we formalize Anomaly Change Detection (ACD), a problem setting that reframes inspection as reference-based logical verification. Unlike traditional Anomaly Detection (AD) or Change Detection (CD), ACD targets open-set defects by verifying a target against an aligned reference without category-specific training. Second, we introduce FabricEyes-ACD, a large-scale dataset collected from real production lines. It contains 21,056 mechanically aligned image pairs across over 160 product categories, specifically curated to capture complex logical violations in continuous surfaces. Third, we propose ACDClip, a CLIP-based benchmark that leverages reference-target alignment for effective detection under one-shot constraints. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ACDClip significantly outperforms state-of-the-art AD and CD methods, establishing a strong baseline for future research. The dataset and code will be publicly available.

records.title: Multi-scale Structural Alignment for Cross-view Object Geo-localization
records.abstract: Cross-view object geo-localization aims to locate a query object within a geo-referenced aerial image, but the task remains highly challenging due to drastic viewpoint discrepancies and scale variations. Existing approaches predominantly rely on appearance-level semantic matching, which often suffers from spatial misalignment when visual structures vary significantly across views. To address this limitation, we propose MSA-Geo, a cross-view object geo-localization framework enhanced by a Multi-scale Structural Alignment Module (MS-SAM). Unlike prior arts, MS-SAM explicitly aggregates structural cues from multiple feature scales to align representations across viewpoints. By injecting hierarchical spatial information, our method improves structural reasoning, leading to more robust correspondences despite extreme view variations. Experimental results further show that MSA-Geo exhibits strong cross-domain robustness. When trained on the ground-to-satellite task (G→S) and evaluated on the drone-to-satellite task (D→S), it surpasses the current state of the art by 9.46\% in acc@0.25 and 10.38\% in acc@0.5, underscoring the importance of multi-scale structural alignment in cross-view matching.

records.title: SSCA-Net: Spatial-Semantic Alignment for Farmland Remote Sensing Segmentation
records.abstract: Existing vision–language approaches for farmland segmentation often suffer from insufficient cross-modal semantic alignment and weakened language constraints during decoding, which results in blurred boundaries and prediction drift. To address these issues, this paper proposes SSCA-Net, a farmland-oriented vision–language segmentation framework that establishes a unified semantic constraint throughout the entire pipeline from representation formation to decision inference. Specifically, SSCA-Net introduces a structured cross-modal alignment strategy at the representation level and a semantically conditioned decoding mechanism, thereby strengthening the discriminative correspondence between textual semantics and spatial structures while converting language-derived semantic priors into effective spatial constraints. Experiments on the FIT vision–language farmland segmentation benchmark across three distinct regions, as well as multiple vision-based farmland segmentation datasets, demonstrate that SSCA-Net consistently outperforms existing methods in both segmentation accuracy and generalization ability. Furthermore, extensive ablation studies validate the necessity and complementary contributions of the proposed components.

records.title: Learning from Coarse Labels: Content-adaptive Graph Inference for Weakly Supervised Hyperspectral Target Detection
records.abstract: Learning from coarse labels is a fundamental challenge for hyperspectral target detection (HTD), since acquiring precise target spectra or pixel-level annotations is expensive and often impractical in real-world scenarios. This paper presents CAG-Net, a weakly supervised framework that enables pixel-wise hyperspectral target detection using only region-level supervision. The key idea is to progressively reduce label ambiguity through content-adaptive graph inference. Specifically, CAG-Net alternates between target candidate inference and detector optimization within an iterative EM-style learning scheme. During the E-step, region-specific graph structures are constructed to exploit spatial and contextual relationships, allowing potential target locations to be uncovered under weak supervision. During the M-step, the inferred target candidates are used to update a discriminative detector. This alternating process facilitates a gradual transition from coarse regional cues to refined target predictions. Experiments on two real-world hyperspectral datasets demonstrate that CAG-Net consistently outperforms representative weakly supervised baselines, validating its effectiveness under limited supervision.

records.title: M$^2$-MoE: Joint Manifold and Message-Passing Mixture of Experts for Graph Fraud Detection
records.abstract: Graph-based fraud detection is essential for safeguarding multimedia platforms and social networks, where rich multi-modal content and user interactions naturally form complex graphs. Most existing methods address geometric heterogeneity (non-Euclidean embeddings) and architectural heterogeneity (adaptive message passing) separately, overlooking their interdependence. Our empirical analysis reveals two findings: different nodes exhibit distinct preferences for geometry and message-passing architecture, and these preferences are coupled at the node level. Specifically, hierarchical fraud patterns favor hyperbolic geometry with multi-hop aggregation, while dense collusive clusters prefer Euclidean space with smoothing filters. A globally fixed manifold or a single architecture cannot accommodate such coupled heterogeneity. To this end, we propose M$^2$-MoE (Manifold $\times$ Message-passing Mixture of Experts), which jointly routes geometry and architecture per node. A Collaborative Context Module and cross-feedback allow the two routing processes to co-adapt. Experiments on four public fraud benchmarks show consistent gains over strong baselines, with improvements of up to 4.45 AUC points.

records.title: Robust Visual Reasoning via Corrective Drawing and Anchor Guided Reinforcement
records.abstract: Vision Language Models (VLMs) treat images as static context, which limits visual reasoning. Although visual tools have been introduced to enhance interaction, two critical challenges remain. Firstly, high-level plans often fail to translate into precise actions, causing tool failures and collapsing reasoning. Secondly, Reinforcement Learning (RL) for this interactive process suffers severe reward sparsity because binary outcomes ignore valuable intermediate steps in failed trajectories. We introduce Corrective Drawing-based Chain-of-Thought (CD-CoT), which models reasoning as a Think-Draw-Observe-Correct loop, supported by a correction module that stabilizes execution. We further propose Anchor Guided Reinforcement (AGR) for RL, which uses successful trajectories as anchors to evaluate and reward effective actions within failed trajectories. Experiments show that our method significantly improves performance on visual grounding and multimodal reasoning benchmarks. More importantly, it enables the model to acquire high-value visual manipulation strategies.

records.title: VocoMark: Watermarking the Voice to Defend Against Cloning
records.abstract: With the rapid development of voice cloning technologies, the security risks posed by highly realistic spoofed speech are becoming increasingly severe. Actively embedding adversarial watermarks into speech provides an effective means of restricting misuse; however, existing approaches often suffer from low generation efficiency and limited transferability across different models. To address these challenges, we propose VocoMark, an adversarial audio watermarking framework designed for efficient generation and robust generalization across diverse systems. VocoMark introduces a learnable watermark initialization network that generates structured initial watermarks. Sensitive region analysis across multiple voice cloning models is used to guide the watermark toward jointly vulnerable spectral regions, enabling stronger transferability under a limited watermark budget. Based on this initialization, the watermark is further refined through adversarial training, ensuring imperceptibility while providing strong protection against cloning attempts. Experimental results demonstrate that VocoMark achieves strong defensive performance on a wide range of cloning systems, generalizes well to unseen models, and substantially reduces watermark generation overhead.

records.title: AR-DiffHTG: Autoregressive-Conditional Diffusion for Structurally Coherent Handwritten Text Generation
records.abstract: Handwritten Text Generation (HTG) aims to synthesize visually realistic and stylistically diverse images from arbitrary text. While Diffusion Models excel in texture synthesis, they often suffer from structural collapse and attention drift in variable-length text scenarios due to the lack of effective structural constraints. To address these challenges, we propose AR-DiffHTG, an Autoregressive-Conditional Diffusion framework designed for Structurally Coherent generation. First, we introduce an Autoregressive Character Planner to explicitly model the sequential dependencies of handwriting, providing a global structural prior. Second, we propose an Explicit Character Query Alignment mechanism, which enforces precise slot-wise mapping between character positions and image regions via learnable character queries. Under this dual constraint, the diffusion model focuses on high-frequency texture rendering, achieving decoupled generation of structure and detail. Experimental results demonstrate that AR-DiffHTG significantly outperforms state-of-the-art approaches on standard benchmarks in terms of FID and Geometric Score.

records.title: Scene-Consistent Video Generation for Robust 3D Human Pose Estimation
records.abstract: Deep learning models for 3D human pose estimation often generalize poorly to new environments and camera settings, largely because they are trained with clean 2D keypoints but deployed with noisy detector outputs. We address this challenge with a controllable video synthesis framework that systematically varies poses, scenes, and viewpoints to generate diverse human motion sequences. Unlike conventional methods that only augment skeletal data, our approach generates RGB sequences to obtain detector-produced 2D keypoints for training, aligning the training inputs with real inference-time detections. The videos are generated offline and introduce no inference-time overhead. This integration of video modality helps bridge the gap between idealized 2D pose inputs and real-world detection noise. We explore different combinations of ideal and real-world 2D inputs during training and evaluation, showing that while ideal conditions yield the best theoretical accuracy, using real-world detections leads to significantly stronger robustness and generalization. Experiments across multiple benchmarks, including corrupted 2D inputs, show that scene-diverse synthetic videos consistently improve robustness and generalization in 3D human pose estimation.

records.title: MMEDIT: A Unified Framework for Multi-Type Audio Editing via Audio Language Model
records.abstract: Text-guided audio editing requires modifying specific acoustic events while strictly preserving non-target content. Despite recent progress, existing approaches remain fundamentally limited: training-free methods often suffer from signal degradation due to diffusion inversion. Training-based methods exhibit better generation quality but remain severely constrained by the scarcity of high-quality paired data and task formulations that cover only a narrow subset of editing operations. Moreover, standard architectures in this paradigm often decouple text and audio processing, limiting the model's ability to align instructions with specific acoustic contexts. To overcome these constraints, we propose \textbf{MMEdit}, an ALM-driven framework for unified audio editing. We systematically extend task definitions to cover a comprehensive range of operations, including addition, replacement, removal, reordering, and attribute modification. Furthermore, we construct a scalable synthesis pipeline to generate large-scale paired data with fine-grained event-level annotations. To capture complex editing semantics, we integrate Qwen2-Audio encoder with an MMDiT-based generator, achieving precise cross-modal alignment and localized editing. Experiments demonstrate that our approach delivers superior editing localization accuracy, robust instruction following, and high fidelity in non-edited regions.

records.title: P-Flow: Multi-Objective Optimization for Conflict-Free Few-Step Generative Modeling
records.abstract: Few-step generative models, particularly MeanFlow, have made significant strides in bridging the quality-efficiency gap inherent in multi-step diffusion models. However, they suffer from inherent optimization conflicts between trajectory flow matching ($\Ltfm$) and trajectory consistency ($\Ltcc$) objectives. Recent analyses reveal that these conflicts manifest as negative gradient correlations, leading to slow convergence, excessive computational overhead from necessary surrogate losses, and suboptimal trade-offs between generation quality and sampling speed. To address this, we propose \textbf{P-Flow}, a multi-objective optimization framework that reinterprets MeanFlow's conflicting objectives as a Pareto optimization problem. P-Flow unifies conflicting loss terms under a weighted Pareto front formulation, adaptively balances their contributions via a dynamic weight scheduler based on gradient similarity, and eliminates reliance on inefficient border-case supervision. We theoretically motivate that P-Flow's objective converges to a set of non-dominated solutions, where improvements in one objective do not degrade another. Extensive experiments on ImageNet-1K $256\times256$ demonstrate that P-Flow outperforms state-of-the-art methods across key metrics: our largest P-Flow-XL/2+ model achieves FID scores of 2.41 (1-NFE) and 1.98 (2-NFE), with 35\% reduced training computation compared to MeanFlow.

records.title: LoRA-Hash: Unveiling Model Identity from Heavy-Tailed Weight Distributions
records.abstract: The explosive adoption of Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) for text-to-image (T2I) generative models has precipitated a surge in unauthorized model replication. Existing copyright protection mechanisms struggle to address the following challenges: inference-based methods are computationally prohibitive for platforms with a large scale of LoRAs, while traditional model hashing fails to capture the unique heavy-tailed statistics of LoRA weights. In this paper, we propose LoRA-Hash, a lightweight parameter-level hashing framework tailored for robust plagiarism detection. Our approach is grounded in the ''Sparsity Hypothesis" which posits that model identity is encoded in sparse extremum parameters rather than diffuse global distributions. LoRA-Hash constructs compact binary signatures by extracting bidirectional local extremums across weight segments, with provable error rate. Extensive experiments on a benchmark of 6,000 real-world adapters demonstrate that LoRA-Hash significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving a detection AUC of 1.0 with 118ms latency under the open-set scenario. These results confirm it as a scalable and efficient solution for protecting community-shared LoRAs.

records.title: Vivid4D: High Fidelity Text to 4D Generation via Dual Branch Adapter
records.abstract: We introduce Vivid4D, a novel end-to-end text-to-4D diffusion framework designed to generate realistic, controllable four-dimensional (4D) content from natural language prompts. Vivid4D leverages hierarchical text–4D conditioning and decouples foreground and background modeling through specialized spherical and diagonal adapter modules. By expanding text into structured scene attributes and routing these cues into spatial, inter-frame, and 3D-attention layers, Vivid4D improves semantic alignment, temporal consistency, and geometric coherence. The framework's key contributions include a Text–4D Alignment mechanism, a progressive weighted-fusion training schedule, and the incorporation of multi-view and multi-frame outputs with robust motion smoothness. Empirical results demonstrate superior consistency and fidelity, with Vivid4D outperforming state-of-the-art models across multiple metrics.

records.title: PyraMotion: Coarse-to-Fine Full-Body Motion Generation with Body–Hand Coherence
records.abstract: Virtual character animation requires the generation of coherent full-body motions with accurate details. Most of the previous works focus on localized motions, such as body or hand motions. When extending these methods to full-body motion with both body and hands, two major issues often arise: 1) body and hand motions may be poorly coherent, sometimes exhibiting implausible joint configurations; and 2) motion details may be inaccurate, such as when performing grasping actions, there may be incorrect grasping timing. To address these issues, we propose PyraMotion, a pyramid-like coarse-to-fine full-body motion generation model. First, to jointly model global body movements and fine-grained hand details, we design a pyramid motion tokenizer that represents full-body motions as multi-granularity motion tokens. Then, to ensure temporal consistency, we leverage a large language model to generate coarse-grained motion plans. Next, to further enrich motion details, we introduce a mask-based infill model to refine the motion plans. Experimental results show that PyraMotion achieves state-of-the-art generation quality. It improves the best baseline 15% in terms of R-Precision@3 and reduces 25% in terms of FID. In addition, our method achieves the best performance in motion coherence-related metrics. The proposed framework bridges body coherence and fine-grained hand details, establishing new standards for text-to-motion generation.

records.title: FontCrafter: One-shot Font Generation with Structural Integrity and Style Enhancement
records.abstract: Few-shot Font Generation (FFG) aims to generate stylized font images using a single character image and a few style reference images. Although existing methods have achieved promising results, the stylized characters often exhibit broken structures and noticeable discrepancies between the reference styles. To address these issues, we propose a novel method, FontCrafter, designed to generate structure-preserving and style-consistent font images through a two-stage process. In the first stage, we introduce a Content Preserved Module (CPM) which focuses on the global structure while progressively learning style features. In the second stage, we design a Style Enhanced Module (SEM) to enhance the style details. We also incorporate a Style Space Discrimination Loss to effectively distinguish similar styles and widen the distance across different styles. Extensive experiments show that the proposed FontCrafter outperforms existing state-of-the-art FFG models in both quantitative metrics and qualitative results. Furthermore, our model delivers impressive results in cross-language scenarios, such as Chinese-to-Korean and Chinese-to-Japanese.

records.title: 3Dcon: Subject-Based Personalized 3D Consistency Control with Diffusion Priors
records.abstract: The growing demand for high-quality 3D content in animation and gaming highlights the need for generation methods that ensure both structural consistency and precise control. However, existing approaches often fail to preserve a subject’s geometry and texture after manipulation, especially in complex 3D scenes. We present 3Dcon, an innovative subject-driven 3D generation framework that incorporates subject features into the diffusion prior distribution for achieving desired control. Specifically, we obtain semantically meaningful text and image alignment cues through the Image Prompt Adapter (IPA) for robust 2D-to-3D conversion. Meanwhile, Multi-view Adaptation (MA) improves cross-view consistency by selecting the best view with LLM scoring. Additionally, the proposed Conditional Constraints (CC) are designed to guide geometry and texture generation to maintain consistency. To validate the effectiveness of our method, we conducted extensive qualitative and quantitative experiments demonstrating that 3Dcon outperforms existing methods in 3D generation tasks. Our approach provides a practical and powerful tool for 3D content creation, offering significant utility to artists and developers

records.title: Training-Free High-Resolution Image Generation via Optimized Attention Computation
records.abstract: Diffusion models have achieved remarkable success in image generation. However, due to computational constraints, they are typically trained at relatively low resolutions. Directly applying pre-trained models to generate images beyond the training resolution often leads to severe repetitive patterns and disordered structures. To address this issue, we propose a novel training-free method that enhances the quality of high-resolution images generated by pre-trained models through optimized attention computation. First, we propose a \textbf{Dilated Convolution-Guided Attention (DCGA)} module to refine the original attention map. Unlike existing approaches, our method preserves the value features extracted from the original convolutional layers while using attention maps derived from dilated convolutional features to guide subsequent self-attention computation. This design reduces repetitive patterns while maintaining the integrity of the extracted features. Second, we introduce a \textbf{Dilated Sampling Attention (DSA)} mechanism to constrain the scale of attention computation. Specifically, DSA restricts attention computation to the training resolution that is the optimal scale for inference, while preserving global awareness, thereby further improving performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in generating high-quality, high-resolution images.

records.title: A Preliminary Study on GPT-Image Generation Model for Image Restoration
records.abstract: Recent advances in OpenAI's GPT-series (e.g., GPT-4o, GPT-5) multimodal models equipped with GPT-Image generation capabilities have shown remarkable abilities in producing visually compelling images. In this work, we investigate its potential impact on the image restoration community. We provide, to the best of our knowledge, the first comprehensive study across diverse restoration scenarios. We observe that while the restoration results generated by GPT-Image models are often perceptually pleasant, they tend to lack pixel-level structural fidelity compared with ground-truth references. Typical deviations include changes in image geometry, object positions or counts, and even modifications in perspective. Beyond empirical observations, we demonstrate that GPT-restored images can serve as strong visual priors, significantly boosting the performance of existing restoration networks across multiple tasks. This study not only provides practical insights and a baseline framework for incorporating GPT-based generative priors into restoration pipelines, but also highlights new opportunities for bridging image generation models and restoration tasks. Our GPT-restored results are publicly available at https://github.com/noxsine/GPT_Restoration

records.title: FPGA: Fast Prior-based Gaussian Avatar
records.abstract: Photorealistic 3D head avatar reconstruction from monocular video demands high fidelity, computational efficiency, and temporal stability. While 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables real-time rendering, existing dynamic methods suffer from slow convergence and fail to robustly integrate necessary priors for detailed reconstruction.We propose FPGA, a novel two-stage prior-driven framework designed to accelerate training and elevate quality by strategically fusing input information. Our core innovation lies in the synergistic integration of the FLAME parametric mesh model for geometric constraints with DINOv2 semantic features for rich pixel-space understanding. In Stage I, we fuse these priors to establish a stable, detail-aware geometric foundation and produce a refined mesh. In Stage II, 3D Gaussians are initialized from this refined mesh and optimized using a Gaussian decoder augmented by our novel DINO-guided 3D spatial modulation mechanism. This mechanism projects semantic DINO features onto the 3D Gaussians, enabling efficient and semantically-aware refinement of high-frequency details.Our framework achieves robust and rapid convergence, significantly accelerating optimization process. Extensive experiments demonstrate FPGA achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction quality with faster training while supporting real-time rendering at 60 FPS.

records.title: Structure–Detail Decoupled 3D Shape Generation under Multimodal Conditions
records.abstract: Generating 3D shapes with consistent structures and rich geometric details under multimodal conditions remains a challenging task. Existing methods usually model global structure and local geometric details within a unified latent space, ignoring their inherent differences in semantic hierarchy and generative stability, which often leads to structural degradation and topological instability during diffusion-based generation. To address this issue, we propose a multimodal structure–detail decoupled 3D shape generation framework, which explicitly learns disentangled structural and detailed latent representations in a continuous implicit space. A structure-prior-constrained two-stage generation strategy is further introduced to progressively refine local geometric details while keeping the structural latent fixed. In addition, we design a cross-modal structural alignment mechanism to explicitly align image-, sketch-, and text-based conditions with 3D structural latents. Experimental results demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms existing approaches in terms of structural consistency, geometric detail quality, and multimodal semantic alignment, validating its effectiveness and strong generalization capability.

records.title: CMAE: Contrastive Manifold Autoencoder for Efficient Latent Diffusion
records.abstract: Latent Diffusion Models (LDMs) excel in image synthesis but are limited by VAE-based latent spaces that lose high-frequency details and lack semantic structure. We propose \textbf{Contrastive Manifold Autoencoder (CMAE)}, a novel framework for learning high-resolution, semantically structured latent spaces optimized for diffusion-based generation. CMAE introduces three key innovations: a hybrid encoder combining frozen self-supervised features with trainable residual refinement; a \textbf{Hybrid Guided Upsampling (HGU)} mechanism that increases latent resolution from $16^2$ to $64^2$ via image-conditioned upsampling; and a contrastive manifold alignment with stable L1+LPIPS objective, eliminating the need for adversarial training. Extensive experiments on ImageNet demonstrate that CMAE significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving superior reconstruction quality (\textbf{+4.24~dB PSNR}, \textbf{58\% lower LPIPS} vs. SVG) and enabling efficient few-step diffusion sampling with \textbf{23\% lower gFID}. CMAE provides a principled pathway toward high-fidelity, semantically coherent visual generation. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/Jaywalk18/CMAE-Contrastive-Manifold-Autoencoder}.

records.title: SOYO: A Tuning-Free Approach for Video Style Morphing via Style-Adaptive Interpolation in Diffusion Models
records.abstract: While video stylization has achieved remarkable progress, existing methods are predominantly limited to static, single-style transfer. In this paper, we formally define a novel task: Video Style Morphing, which necessitates seamless and coherent evolution between distinct artistic styles over time. Current approaches fail to handle such dynamic transitions, resulting in abrupt shifts and structural discontinuities. To address this, we present SOYO, a tuning-free diffusion framework tailored for this task. We introduce a dual-style fusion mechanism where Attention Injection maintains structural layouts while Adaptive Instance Normalization (AdaIN) modulates global color tones, effectively decoupling structure from appearance to ensure consistency. Furthermore, we propose an Adaptive Style Distance Mapping (ASDM) to harmonize transition pacing against perceptual non-linearity. Experiments on our newly constructed SOYO-Test benchmark demonstrate SOYO's superiority in this new domain.

records.title: FREE-Edit: Using Editing-aware Injection in Rectified Flow Models for Zero-shot Image-Driven Video Editing
records.abstract: Image-driven video editing aims to propagate edit contents from the modified first frame to the remaining frames. Existing methods usually invert the source video to noise using a pre-trained image-to-video (I2V) model and then guide the sampling process using the edited first frame. Generally, a popular choice for maintaining motion and layout from the source video is intervening in the denoising process by injecting attention during reconstruction. However, such injection often leads to unsatisfactory results, where excessive injection leads to conflicting semantics with the source video while insufficient injection brings limited source representation. Recognizing this, we propose an Editing-awaRE (REE) injection method to modulate the injection intensity of each token. Specifically, we first compute the pixel difference between the source and edited first frame to form a corresponding editing mask. Next, we track the editing area throughout the entire video by using optical flow to warp the first-frame mask. Then, editing-aware feature injection intensity for each token is generated accordingly, where injection is not conducted in editing areas. Building upon REE injection, we further propose a zero-shot image-driven video editing framework with recent-emerging rectified-Flow models, dubbed FREE-Edit. Without fine-tuning or training, our FREE-Edit demonstrates effectiveness in various image-driven video editing scenarios, showing its capability to produce higher-quality outputs compared with existing techniques. records.title: Disentangled Semantic and Rhythmic Modeling for Co-Speech Gesture Generation
records.abstract: Abstract—Generating lifelike co-speech gestures is essential for creating expressive digital avatars. While lip movements are strictly synchronized with phonetics, body gestures exhibit a complex dependency on semantic context and speech rhythm. To address this, we propose a novel framework that disentangles rhythmic and semantic cues for adaptive integration. Specifically, we extract content features using a pre-trained speech encoder while deriving rhythmic representations from audio amplitude and onset. To align these modalities, we introduce a Speech-Text FiLM module that modulates semantic features with rhythmic patterns, ensuring the generated motion is both semantically meaningful and rhythmically synchronized. Furthermore, we combine Self-Attention with a State Space Model to capture long-range dependencies efficiently. Experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms existing baselines, generating co- speech gestures with significantly improved realism, diversity, and rhythmic consistency.

records.title: Attention-guided Evidence Grounding for Spoken Question Answering
records.abstract: Spoken Question Answering (Spoken QA) presents a challenging cross-modal problem: effectively aligning acoustic queries with textual knowledge while avoiding the latency and error propagation inherent in cascaded ASR-based systems. In this paper, we introduce Attention-guided Evidence Grounding (AEG), a novel end-to-end framework that leverages the internal cross-modal attention of Speech Large Language Models (SpeechLLMs) to explicitly locate and ground key evidence in the model’s latent space. To address the diffuse attention distribution in pre-trained models, we propose Learning to Focus on Evidence (LFE), a supervised fine-tuning paradigm that calibrates the model's attention mechanism to distinguish query-relevant segments from irrelevant context. Experiments on SQuAD, HotpotQA, and MuSiQue demonstrate that AEG reduces hallucinations and achieves strong efficiency gains, outperforming large-scale cascaded baselines (Whisper-Large-v3 + Reranker) while reducing inference latency by approximately 62%.

records.title: CardioManifold: Direct Pathological PCG Synthesis via Cyclic-Mamba and Phase-Preserving Manifold Diffusion
records.abstract: The data starvation paradox in pathological Phonocardiogram (PCG) analysis significantly impedes the development of robust AI diagnostics. Existing Latent Diffusion Models (LDMs) suffer from a critical Phase-Fidelity Trade-off, where lossy VAE compression obscures the high-frequency phase relationships essential for characterizing subtle murmurs. To bridge this gap, we present \textbf{CardioManifold}, a novel framework that approaches synthesis via diffusion directly on the Complex STFT Manifold. This Back to Basics' paradigm preserves strict bijectivity between representation and waveform, significantly mitigating reconstruction artifacts. Furthermore, we introduce a Cyclic-Mamba backbone equipped with Polar-Cycle Embeddings, enabling the efficient modeling of long-range cardiac rhythms with linear complexity O(N). CardioManifold achieves a state-of-the-art Fréchet Audio Distance (FAD) of 8.8 on PhysioNet datasets, surpassing hierarchical latent baselines by 9.2% and demonstrating superior validity in downstream clinical diagnosis.

records.title: Text-Guided Local Image Editing via Anchor-SAM Masks and Stepwise Latent Fusion
records.abstract: Diffusion-based image editing has achieved remarkable progress, yet precise text-guided local editing remains challenging because existing methods often modify irrelevant regions or require manually provided masks. In this paper, we present a training-free framework for text-guided local image editing that combines automatic region localization with explicit locality-constrained diffusion guidance. Our method first generates candidate object-centric masks using a DINO-attention-to-anchor pipeline together with the Segment Anything Model (SAM), and then selects the final mask in an instruction-aware manner by matching candidate masked regions with the noun phrase of the editing instruction. Based on the selected mask, we introduce a mask-gated guidance formulation that applies editing increments only inside the target region while reverting to unconditional prediction outside the mask, thereby improving background preservation by construction. To better combine global instruction following and local attribute refinement, we further perform stepwise latent fusion between InstructPix2Pix and MagicBrush throughout the reverse diffusion process. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach achieves high editing accuracy and visual fidelity, with results closely aligning with user intent.

records.title: Linear Multi-granular Body Modeling for Text-Driven Motion Generation
records.abstract: Text-to-motion generation is a rapidly growing field at the nexus of multimodal learning and computer graphics, enabling flexible and cost-effective applications in gaming, animation, robotics, and virtual reality. Existing part-aware pipelines typically split the body into segments and then recover whole-body coordination via attention-based fusion, which incurs quadratic complexity and fails to model part-level and whole-body cues simultaneously. Moreover, we observe that naively stacking spatial and temporal modules accumulates redundant features, thereby requiring deeper networks to achieve competitive fidelity. To address these issues, we propose HiSTF Mamba, a linear-time framework composed of Dual-Spatial Mamba,Bi-Temporal Mamba, and the Dynamic Spatiotemporal Fusion Module (DSFM). Dual-Spatial Mamba performs parallel part-based and whole-based modeling to simultaneously capture local joint dynamics and global coordination. Bi-Temporal Mamba employs bidirectional scanning to encode both short-term motion details and long-term dependencies. DSFM further removes redundancy and extracts complementary temporal information before fusing it with spatial features, yielding an expressive spatiotemporal representation. Extensive experiments on HumanML3D and KIT-ML demonstrate that HiSTF Mamba improves generation fidelity and semantic alignment while requiring substantially fewer parameters than existing segment-based architectures.

records.title: RA-VAR: Reference Attention for Efficient Controllable Visual Autoregressive T2I Generation
records.abstract: Text-to-image generation with visual autoregressive (VAR) models has achieved impressive fidelity and efficiency, yet enabling precise and flexible control within VAR paradigm remains underexplored. To bridge this gap, we introduce RA-VAR, an efficient framework designed to achieve high-fidelity, controllable generation upon advanced VAR models. The core design of RA-VAR is the Reference Attention module, which efficiently integrates conditional information. Different from standard multi-modal attention, Reference Attention removes unnecessary image-to-condition attention, reducing computational cost while stabilizing control injection. In addition, it strategically emphasizes parameter reuse and employs a zero-initialized linear projection to ensure that control signals are incorporated effectively without disrupting the generative capability of the base model. Extensive experiments show that RA-VAR delivers high-quality generation and precise control while attaining superior efficiency over diffusion-based methods, making it a practical solution for controllable text-to-image generation within the visual autoregressive paradigm. records.title: Reflection Generation for Composite Image Using Diffusion Model
records.abstract: Image composition involves inserting a foreground object into the background while synthesizing environment-consistent effects such as shadows and reflections. Although shadow generation has been extensively studied, reflection generation remains largely underexplored. In this work, we focus on reflection generation. We inject the prior information of reflection placement and reflection appearance into foundation diffusion model. We also divide reflections into two types and adopt type-aware model design. To support training, we construct the first large-scale object reflection dataset DEROBA. Experiments demonstrate that our method generates reflections that are physically coherent and visually realistic, establishing a new benchmark for reflection generation.
