records.title: SwinRobo: A Lightweight Multimodal Diffusion Model for Robotic Manipulation
records.abstract: Language-conditioned robotic manipulation enables robots to interpret multimodal inputs and execute actions from natural language instructions. However, achieving this capability remains challenging, as existing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) frameworks face two key limitations: reliance on large-scale pretraining and the use of only RGB input, which limits both efficiency and robustness. To address these limitations, we propose SwinRobo, a lightweight multimodal diffusion policy. Our approach integrates RGB and depth data via a bidirectional cross-attention fusion module, significantly improving spatial and semantic understanding. For action generation, we employ a Swin-UNet-1D-based conditional diffusion network that effectively captures both local dynamics and global temporal dependencies, ensuring stable and coherent control. On the CALVIN benchmark, SwinRobo achieves state-of-the-art performance in imitation learning and zero-shot generalization, despite using only 225M parameters and requiring no additional pretraining. Together, these contributions yield a compact and robust solution for adaptive multimodal robotic manipulation.

records.title: StegaDPM: Decoupled Image Steganography via Probability Flow Trajectory Matching}
records.abstract: With the exponential growth of digital media transmission, ensuring secure and covert communication has emerged as a critical imperative in information security. Steganography aims to conceal the very existence of communication by embedding data into digital media. Traditional methods are often betrayed by pixel-level artifacts, recent generative paradigms suffer from a structural coupling between the secret payload and the stego, leading to detectable semantic deviations. In this paper, we propose StegaDPM, a training-free steganographic framework that achieves payload-stego decoupling by leveraging the reversible generative priors of diffusion models. We treat steganography as an exact trajectory matching problem within the probability flow Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE). By ensuring that the stego-latent precisely follows the model’s learned probability flow, StegaDPM minimizes the discretization drift that plagues latent-based embedding. We project secret images into the standard Gaussian latent space via orthogonal transformations, maintaining the statistical integrity of the noise manifold. During extraction, we reformulate the recovery of the secret payload as a constrained posterior sampling task, enabling high-fidelity reconstruction without auxiliary optimization or fine-tuning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that StegaDPM outperforms existing methods in both security and visual quality when the embedding is aligned with the generative trajectory of diffusion models.

records.title: SPDiff: Enhancing Diffusion Models for Scalable Periodic Image Generation
records.abstract: Periodic images have broad applications including texture synthesis, pattern design, and panoramic scene generation. Recent progress in diffusion-based image generation enables high-quality image synthesis. However, existing models exhibit inherent spatial biases that prevent them from producing periodic output simply through prompts like "periodic". Moreover, creating high-resolution images or images with unusual aspect ratios often leads to loss of periodic structure and visual degradation. This paper proposes a novel SPDiff framework that enhances diffusion models for scalable periodic image generation. To enable periodic image synthesis at different high resolutions, we introduce Cross-Subimage Splice-and-Focus, a training-free approach that combines overlapped tiling with a refined attention strategy. We further incorporate a RandomShift mechanism to explicitly break spatial biases, thus improving image naturalness. Additionally, we develop a Periodic Expansion Pipeline (PEP) to produce large periodic units from a reference image. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our framework enables scalable periodic generation with high visual quality.

records.title: GenHash: A Diffusion-Based Generative Framework for Image Hashing
records.abstract: Deep image hashing encodes high-dimensional images into compact binary codes for efficient large-scale retrieval. However, predominant methods adhere to a discriminative learning paradigm, directly optimizing a deterministic mapping from images to hash codes.Such approaches require relaxing the binary constraint during training, thereby introducing significant quantization errors and degrading retrieval accuracy. To address this limitation, we propose GenHash, a generative framework reformulating hash learning as a conditional denoising diffusion process. Instead of optimizing a deterministic mapping, our model progressively constructs hash representations within a continuous hash-center space, strictly guided by hierarchical semantic cues. This generative paradigm allows GenHash to explicitly learn the conditional distribution of hash codes, effectively bridging the quantization gap while maintaining semantic consistency and discriminability.We have conducted comprehensive experiments on four widely used datasets: CIFAR-10, ImageNet, NUS-WIDE, and MS~COCO. Extensive experiments validate the superiority of the proposed generative paradigm, demonstrating that GenHash significantly outperforms state-of-the-art discriminative methods and maintains robust semantic consistency.

records.title: QRStego: Diffusion Steganography for Robust Visual Encoding in Standard QR Codes
records.abstract: With the surge of multimedia in the big-data era, securing high-capacity visual transmission against detection and distortion remains a key challenge. Steganography serves as a secure means of communication by embedding data within a cover to hide the existence of the concealed data. However, it often falls short in robustness against degradation and malicious attacks. While QR codes provide a standardized, error-resilient container with inherent error-correction capabilities, their limited capacity constrains high redundancy image embedding. To address these limitations, we present a novel steganography framework that merges ultra-compact semantic compression with robust QR communication (QRStego). By distilling high-resolution images into compact binary codes via a training-free discrete diffusion process, we preserve essential semantics while reducing data volume. These codes are then embedded into standard QR structures, preserving scanability and error correction. The embedded content can be recovered under typical channel disturbances without complex decryption and retraining. We achieve high-capacity data embedding while fully complying with the structural standards of QR codes. Extensive experiments show that our approach unites high-capacity embedding with strict structural compliance, enabling robust and stealthy transmission of visual intelligence in real-world applications.

records.title: Active Defense against Generative Steganography via Pixel-Level Deep Reinforcement Learning
records.abstract: Generative steganography hides secret messages in the latent space of deep generative models, achieving high concealment and robustness that challenge conventional passive detection. However, most active defense methods are not designed for the specific embedding mechanisms of generative steganography, resulting in limited effectiveness. To address this limitation, we propose DGStegRL, a deep reinforcement learning framework for active defense against generative steganography. DGStegRL formulates steganography destruction as a pixel-level decision process and jointly optimizes hidden information disruption and visual quality preservation within a unified Actor--Critic framework. An adaptive reward function guided by image texture complexity dynamically balances perturbation strength and visual fidelity. Extensive experiments show that DGStegRL achieves optimal or near-optimal destruction performance across diverse generative steganography schemes, while consistently delivering superior image quality.

records.title: Towards Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection via Contrastive Diffusion Inversion
records.abstract: AI-generated images increasingly threaten digital forensics. Existing methods struggle to capture subtle off-manifold deviations. Unlike prior passive forensic methods, CRAFI actively induces controlled generative collapse for AI-generated inputs while maintaining real image fidelity. By applying contrastive reconstruction loss and stage-wise DDIM adaptation, CRAFI engineers asymmetric generative dynamics, and class-guided latent perturbation steers forgeries into engineered collapse regions, producing predictable, distinctive artifacts. Experiments across multiple generative architectures demonstrate its effectiveness and cross-model robustness.

records.title: UniSign: Continuous Sign Language Synthesis via Multi-Conditioned Diffusion
records.abstract: Generating long, continuous sign pose sequences guided by textual descriptions is challenging due to the need to preserve semantic fidelity for each description while ensuring seamless transitions between isolated signs. Prior approaches often produce abrupt transitions, require predefined transition durations, or introduce computational overhead through additional processing steps. We propose UniSign, a novel diffusion-based model that generates seamless continuous sign pose sequences without any post-processing or additional denoising steps. Our approach introduces two key techniques. First, Scheduled Positional Encoding strategically combines absolute and relative positional encoding during denoising. Absolute encoding in early stages establishes global semantic coherence of isolated signs, while relative encoding in later stages promotes smooth, realistic transitions across sign boundaries. Second, to address the training-inference mismatch when multiple conditions must coexist at inference, we propose Query-Conditioned Pose Attention, which injects conditions only into queries while using noisy poses as keys and values, enabling seamless transitions to emerge without explicit supervision. Experiments on the WLASL2000 benchmark demonstrate that UniSign outperforms the baseline method in accuracy, realism, and transition smoothness.

records.title: TM-CAD: Tree-Structured Mamba for Hierarchical Parametric CAD Generation
records.abstract: Generative modeling of parametric Computer-Aided Design (CAD) programs remains challenging due to the complex hierarchical dependencies among geometric primitives and operations. While transformer-based methods have achieved notable progress, they flatten CAD sequences into linear token streams, disrupting the natural tree topology that governs sketch-extrusion relationships. We propose TM-CAD, an end-to-end framework for hierarchy-aware CAD generation. Our method encodes CAD programs as a four-level hierarchical tree, where each solid comprises multiple extrusions, each extrusion contains one sketch, and each sketch consists of closed loops, thereby preserving geometric and topological dependencies. A lightweight T-Mamba block generates layer-conditioned state-space matrices to fuse global and local features with linear complexity. We further introduce two masking strategies: Child-Mask for unconditional generation and Parent-Mask for conditional sketch-to-extrusion inference. Experiments on the DeepCAD benchmark demonstrate that TM-CAD achieves state-of-the-art performance in generation accuracy and computational efficiency.

records.title: Diffusion-Guided Semantic Consistency for Multimodal Heterogeneity
records.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is severely challenged by non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) client data, a problem that degrades global model performance, especially in multimodal perception settings. Conventional methods often fail to address the underlying semantic discrepancies between clients, leading to suboptimal performance for multimedia systems requiring robust perception. To overcome this, we introduce SemanticFL, a novel framework that leverages the rich semantic representations of pre-trained diffusion models to provide privacy-preserving guidance for local training. Our approach leverages multi-layer semantic representations from the pre-trained Stable Diffusion model (including VAE-encoded latents and U-Net hierarchical features) to create a shared semantic space that aligns heterogeneous clients, facilitated by an efficient client-server architecture that offloads heavy computation to the server. A unified consistency mechanism, employing cross-modal contrastive learning, further stabilizes convergence. We conduct extensive experiments on benchmarks including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and TinyImageNet under diverse heterogeneity scenarios. Our results demonstrate that SemanticFL surpasses existing federated learning approaches, achieving accuracy gains of up to 5.49% over FedAvg, validating its effectiveness in learning robust models from heterogeneous and multimodal data for perception tasks.

records.title: A High-Quality Benchmark and A MoE-Corrected Diffusion Model for Mural Image Restoration
records.abstract: Mural image restoration aims to recover the intact image from a damaged mural. Despite significant progress has been made in mural image restoration, we note that most existing methods are often developed for simple or isolated degradation settings and fail to generalize across real-world mural restoration scenes. How to effectively model complex and coupled degradations within a diffusion-based framework is crucial for mural image restoration. In this paper, we propose MurDiff, a mixture-of-experts (MoE)-corrected diffusion model designed to achieve faithful and high-fidelity mural image restoration. To better enhance model generalization, we construct a high-quality dataset named HQ-Mural, which simulates realistic coupled degradation phenomena by modeling 3D physical degradation and 2D imaging degradation. Furthermore, we develop an effective MoE corrector network to extract degradation information and guide the diffusion process, thereby enabling faithful structural restoration under real-world degradation conditions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art models on both proposed and public datasets.

records.title: Digital Twin Logic Synthesis via Multi-Source PLC Code Generation
records.abstract: Programmable logic controller (PLC) programming is fundamental to maintaining the logical fidelity of Digital Twin systems, involving heterogeneous information sources. In the Industrial Metaverse, the synchronization between virtual visualization and physical execution logic remains a critical challenge. From a multi-source perspective, this task requires aligning unstructured text with rigid program representations. We propose a multi-source PLC code generation framework that integrates retrieval based contextual enrichment with symbolic static-analysis feedback. Given only a small set of examples, the method retrieves relevant PLC code and documentation to provide cross-modal context, employs structured templates to ground generation, and incorporates static-analysis signals to iteratively correct syntactic and semantic inconsistencies. Experiments on Siemens Structured Control Language (SCL) show consistent improvements in compilation success and functional correctness over retrieval-only and few-shot baselines, offering a reliable solution for the behavioral execution layer of complex industrial multimedia environments. Our data collection scripts and retrieval corpus are publicly available at https://github.com/GongJialian/Industrial-PLC-Dataset

records.title: Noise is Message: Generative Watermarking via Discrete Diffusion Models
records.abstract: The rapid proliferation of diffusion-based generative models has revolutionized visual content creation. This accessibility escalates the risks of intellectual property infringement and the propagation of unauthorized content, which necessitates robust mechanisms for provenance verification. Invisible watermarking stands as a cornerstone for protecting copyright and establishing provenance in the AI-generated content. It often demands computationally prohibitive retraining and can degrade semantic consistency, introducing artifacts that undermine the very generative models it aims to protect. In this paper, we present a training-free watermarking framework. By defining the watermark as a timestep-dependent noise vector from a discrete codebook, we replace standard Gaussian noise with a semantic container that is statistically indistinguishable from natural sampling noise. This approach weaves watermarking into image semantics during generation, enabling precise extraction via the inverse diffusion trajectory. Extensive evaluations show that our method maintains high image quality while offering greater payload capacity and robustness to perturbations.

records.title: Segmentation-Guided Real Hair Removal based on Simulated Hair Generation
records.abstract: Hair interference within dermoscopic images usually obscures critical lesion details, dramatically affecting the results of automatic lesion analysis and diagnosis. Hair removal aims to eliminate hairs in dermatological images while restoring hidden lesion information to assist subsequent tasks. However, traditional dehairing approaches typically either inadequately or excessively remove hair, leading to the loss of vital lesion details. Besides, deep learning models are hampered by the scarcity of the ground truth without hair, which imposes a substantial challenge for supervised hair removal. In this work, we aim to address these issues through a hair removal framework that is pretrained with simulated hair data and then fine-tuned with hair segmentation guidance. We first developed a novel hair simulation approach using Bézier curves to synthesize realistic hair disturbances in lesion images, which is adopted to generate synthetic images with hair interference for model pretraining. Meanwhile, we devise a meticulous strategy to bridge the gap between synthetic and real hairy samples by adapting knowledge from a hair segmentation model, significantly boosting the performance of hair removal on real-world instances. Extensive experiments illustrate the efficacy and robustness of our framework, as well as its superiority over existing hair removal methods.

records.title: HandFirst-SLG: Two-Stage Pose-Guided Hand-Optimized Sign Language Generation
records.abstract: Sign language video generation is critical for facilitating communication accessibility for the deaf community, yet existing methods often suffer from distorted hand gestures, limiting their practical utility. To address this, we propose HandFirst-SLG, a novel pose-guided two-stage framework for high-fidelity sign language synthesis. Stage 1 employs a HandGenerator to decouple hand synthesis with precise gesture control. Stage 2 integrates hand images to synthesize body movements while maintaining temporal coherence via motion modules. Evaluated on three datasets, our method outperforms general pose-guided frameworks and achieves significant improvements in hand gesture accuracy compared to state-of-the-art sign language models on the C4A dataset. This work advances pose-guided sign language generation by providing a robust solution for generating high-fidelity sign language videos with accurate hand gestures, which is essential for effective communication aids for the deaf community. records.title: MusicKV: Training-Free Music Editing via Vital Layer Selection and Time-Varying Key-Value Injection
records.abstract: Text-to-music generation is shifting from UNet architectures to Diffusion Transformers (DiTs), but training-free editing remains challenging because homogeneous DiT blocks lack the bottlenecks that enable feature injection in UNets. In this work, we study the internal mechanisms of music DiTs under the premise that not all layers and diffusion timesteps contribute equally to structural coherence. Through layer-wise probing, we show that a sparse subset of self-attention layers acts as the primary carrier of musical form. Leveraging this insight, we propose MusicKV, a training-free editing framework for DiTs with three components: (1) vital layer selection, which identifies a compact set of structure-critical self-attention layers; (2) key–value (KV) Injection, which strengthens edits while better preserving content; and (3) a time-varying injection schedule, which adapts injection strength over diffusion steps to match the coarse-to-fine generative process. Experiments show that MusicKV effectively decouples content from style and significantly outperforms baselines in the trade-off between fidelity and editability. Code and audio demos are available at https://musickv2026.github.io/MusicKV2026.

records.title: PCMG: Psychology-driven Personality-consistent Text-to-Motion Generation
records.abstract: Text-to-motion generation is crucial in applications such as animation, gaming and virtual reality. However, existing methods prioritize semantic fidelity while overlooking psychological consistency, often producing motions that are semantically correct but lack distinguishable individuality. To address this issue, we propose PCMG, a psychology-driven text-to-motion generation framework. PCMG is designed to bridge the semantic gap between abstract personality traits and concrete kinematics. Our core insight is to decouple personality injection into two stages: personality integration and kinematic refinement. In the personality integration stage, OCEAN ControlNet (OCEAN-CN) adopts a dual-branch architecture with residual feature fusion to inject psychological priors without disrupting semantic integrity. In the kinematic refinement stage, Laban-Guidance (Laban-Gd) provides psychophysically-grounded control by applying Laban Movement Analysis–based analytic gradient guidance to steer joint rotations during sampling. To support this task, we construct MoOCEAN, a dataset of text–personality–motion triplets. Extensive experiments and perceptual studies demonstrate that PCMG outperforms state-of-the-art methods, generating realistic motions with distinct, human-perceivable personality traits.

records.title: From Part to Whole: 3D Generative World Model with an Adaptive Structural Hierarchy
records.abstract: Single-image 3D generation lies at the core of vision-to-graphics models in the real world, yet achieving reliable generalization across diverse semantic categories and highly variable structural complexity under sparse supervision remains a fundamental challenge. Existing approaches typically monolithic or assume a fixed part count, including recent part-aware models such as PartCrafter, which still require a labor-intensive user-specified part count. Such designs easily lead to overfitting or missing structural components, and limited compositional generalization when encountering novel object layouts. To this end, this paper rethinks single-image 3D generation as learning an adaptive part–whole hierarchy in the flexible 3D latent space. We present a novel part-to-whole world model that autonomously discovers latent structural slots (i.e., parts of objects) by inferring soft and compositional masks directly from image tokens. Specifically, an adaptive slot-gating mechanism dynamically determines the slot-wise activation probabilities and smoothly consolidates redundant slots within different objects, ensuring that the emergent structure remains compact yet expressive across categories. Each distilled slot is then aligned to a learnable, class-agnostic prototype bank, enabling powerful cross-category shape sharing and denoising through universal geometric prototypes in the real world. To further refine structure and appearance, a lightweight 3D denoiser is introduced to reconstruct geometry and appearance via unified diffusion, RGB, and silhouette objectives, with multi-view diffusion guidance for keeping multi-view consistency. Experiments on Objarverse and 3D-Front datasets show consistent gains in cross-category transfer, part-count extrapolation, and robustness under occlusion and appearance shifts, and ablations confirm complementary benefits of the prototype bank for shape-prior sharing and of slot-gating for structural adaptation.

records.title: TIM-Seg: Text-Driven Interactive Model for Multi-Organ Segmentation in Abdominal CT
records.abstract: Precise abdominal multi-organ segmentation from Computed Tomography (CT) is crucial in medical image analysis, aiding in disease diagnosis, treatment planning, and post-operative evaluation. Existing segmentation methods typically rely on pure visual features or sparse geometric cues, such as clicks or bounding boxes, while neglecting the anatomical guidance embedded in medical texts. This anatomical knowledge is essential for distinguishing complex and morphologically similar abdominal organ structures. To address this, we propose a Text-driven Interactive Multi-organ Segmentation framework (TIM-Seg), which integrates abdominal CT images with organ-level textual descriptions. TIM-Seg introduces a dual-stage image-text fusion mechanism: the Text-Image Fusion Module (TIFM) for multi-scale cross-modal feature alignment, and the Text-Aware Module (TAM), which integrates textual semantics into visual feature reconstruction for fine-grained anatomical guidance. In addition, a category discrimination mechanism based on learnable organ-specific class tokens enhances organ-level separability and improves segmentation reliability for morphologically similar and low-contrast structures in abdominal CT images. Experiments on three abdominal multi-organ datasets show that TIM-Seg outperforms state-of-the-art automatic and interactive segmentation methods, especially in segmenting low-contrast and challenging organs, demonstrating the effectiveness of leveraging language priors for medical image segmentation.

records.title: FreqStyler: Decoupled Arbitrary Image Style Transfer via Dual-Domain Guidance
records.abstract: Although recent diffusion-based methods have demonstrated impressive results, balancing robust style injection with faithful content preservation remains challenging. We introduce FreqStyler, a novel framework leveraging dual-domain adapters for optimization-free arbitrary style transfer. FreqStyler effectively decouples style and content via two complementary modules. Specifically, the Spectral Feature Enhancer (SFE) enhances style fidelity by utilizing a novel cross-gated coordinate attention mechanism combined with a frequency-domain gate. Complementarily, the Structural Anchor Guidance (SAG) module preserves complex structural details by guiding deep semantic features with shallow spatial cues. Furthermore, we introduce a zero-shot post-processing module to replace complex latent preprocessing, effectively mitigating color and luminance discrepancies to ensure faithful color reproduction without compromising structural integrity. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that FreqStyler achieves a superior balance between content preservation and stylistic texture transfer, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art approaches.

records.title: Towards Efficient Background Preservation in Text-Guided Image Editing via Hybrid Exact Inversion Sampling
records.abstract: Recent advancements in text-guided image editing grapple with the trade-off between inference efficiency and structural fidelity. While the emerging Bidirectional Explicit Linear Multi-step (BELM) sampler achieves exact inversion without costly optimization, we identify a critical problem when applying it to attention-based editing: the violation of trajectory smoothness introduces severe numerical instability, manifesting as high-frequency colorful artifacts. To this end, we propose a framework that reconciles high-order solver precision with low-order robustness. Specifically, we introduce a Hybrid Trajectory Strategy that leverages BELM for structural anchoring in early stages while switching to a robust first-order solver to absorb attention-induced discontinuities in the final steps. Furthermore, we apply Source-Guided Rectification that injects trajectory constraints from the source image, effectively bridging the semantic gap induced by asymmetric Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG). Experiments demonstrate that our method eliminates numerical artifacts and yields superior structural preservation, achieving high-fidelity editing with negligible computational overhead.

records.title: CLSSDiff: Temporal Knowledge Graph Reasoning with Generative Diffusion Prior
records.abstract: Temporal Knowledge Graph Reasoning (TKGR) is pivotal for analyzing dynamic event evolution in multimedia streams. However, existing deterministic approaches struggle with two critical challenges: the data sparsity inherent in high-frequency event streams and the aleatoric uncertainty of future events. To bridge this gap, we propose CLSSDiff (Conditional Latent Semantic Saliency Diffusion), a novel generative framework. Specifically, we treat event forecasting as a conditional generation process, introducing a Generative Uncertainty Modeling module to capture the stochastic nature of evolving facts within the latent space. To mitigate sparsity, we design a Semantic Structure Augmentation mechanism that enriches long-tail entity representations by mining latent global neighbors. Furthermore, an Adaptive Temporal Saliency module is employed to filter historical noise. Extensive experiments on four benchmarks, including the large-scale event-centric GDELT dataset, demonstrate that CLSSDiff achieves state-of-the-art performance, showing particular superiority in forecasting unseen and sparse events.

records.title: Region-Aware Optimization for Multi-Person Hand Generation in Text-to-Image Synthesis
records.abstract: Despite recent advances in text-to-image synthesis, generating realistic human hands remains a persistent challenge due to their complex articulation and high structural sensitivity, particularly in images containing multiple individuals. To address this, we propose Region-Aware Group Relative Policy Optimization (RA-GRPO), a reinforcement learning framework that directly enhances a diffusion model’s hand-generation capability by localizing policy optimization to hand regions. Specifically, our approach introduces a spatially masked reward mechanism that aligns region-specific rewards with corresponding latent transition probabilities, enabling targeted anatomical refinement while preserving global image quality. To provide a reliable supervision signal, we design a Keypoint Confidence Reward (KCR) based on hand pose estimation, which quantitatively evaluates the structural correctness of generated hands. Additionally, we construct a multi-person hand gesture dataset, MultiHand-11K, to facilitate model training and evaluation. Extensive experiments on both single-person and multi-person benchmarks demonstrate that our RA-GRPO significantly improves hand realism and anatomical accuracy, outperforming prior fine-tuning and post-processing methods, without degrading overall image fidelity. The dataset will be available at https://github.com/cxy205/MultiHand-11K.

records.title: CausalDreamer: Temporal Image Generation through Causal Intervention Attention with Identity Preservation
records.abstract: Text-to-image diffusion models generate photorealistic images but are not designed to produce temporally ordered image sequences that depict how events unfold while preserving subject identity. We introduce CausalDreamer, a framework for temporal image sequence generation that models semantic state progression through causal-inspired, intervention-guided diffusion attention. Trained on CausalLite10K, a text-only dataset of 10,000 curated cause--effect pairs, a lightweight 1.3M-parameter adapter learns effect progression patterns in CLIP embedding space. A causal-inspired intervention mechanism modulates Stable Diffusion cross-attention to enable discrete temporal state transitions while maintaining identity consistency. Given a single cause description, CausalDreamer retrieves temporally ordered effects and generates progressive image sequences. Across 190 scenarios, CausalDreamer achieves a favorable identity-diversity balance, delivering $4.7x higher semantic diversity than strong baselines while maintaining positive temporal ordering and cause-effect alignment. Unlike video diffusion models emphasizing smooth motion, CausalDreamer focuses on ordered semantic state transitions in image sequences.

records.title: SafeCtrl: Region-Aware Safety Control for Text-to-Image Diffusion via Detect-Then-Suppress
records.abstract: The widespread deployment of text-to-image diffusion models is significantly challenged by the generation of visually harmful content, such as sexually explicit content, violence, and horror imagery. Common safety interventions, ranging from input filtering to model concept erasure, often suffer from two critical limitations: (1) a severe trade-off between safety and context preservation, where removing unsafe concepts degrades the fidelity of the safe content, and (2) vulnerability to adversarial attacks, where safety mechanisms are easily bypassed. To address these challenges, we propose SafeCtrl, a Region-Aware safety control framework operating on a Detect-Then-Suppress paradigm. Unlike global safety interventions, SafeCtrl first employs an attention-guided Detect module to precisely localize specific risk regions. Subsequently, a localized Suppress module, optimized via image-level Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), neutralizes harmful semantics only within the detected areas, effectively transforming unsafe objects into safe alternatives while leaving the surrounding context intact. Extensive experiments across multiple risk categories demonstrate that SafeCtrl achieves a superior trade-off between safety and fidelity compared to state-of-the-art methods. Crucially, our approach exhibits improved resilience against adversarial prompt attacks, offering a precise and robust solution for responsible generation.

records.title: R$^3$D: Regional-guided Residual Radar Diffusion
records.abstract: Millimeter-wave radar enables robust environment perception in autonomous systems under adverse conditions yet suffers from sparse, noisy point clouds with low angular resolution. Existing diffusion-based radar enhancement methods either incur high learning complexity by modeling full LiDAR distributions or fail to prioritize critical structures due to uniform regional processing. To address these issues, we propose R³D, a regional-guided residual radar diffusion framework that integrates residual diffusion modeling—focusing on the concentrated LiDAR-radar residual encoding complementary high-frequency details to reduce learning difficulty—and $\sigma$-adaptive regional guidance—leveraging radar-specific signal properties to generate attention maps and applying lightweight guidance only in low-noise stages to avoid gradient imbalance while refining key regions. Extensive experiments on the ColoRadar dataset demonstrate that R$^3$D outperforms state-of-the-art methods, providing a practical solution for radar perception enhancement. records.title: Chain-of-Thought Guided Autoregressive Diffusion Models for Whole-body Human-Object Interaction Generation
records.abstract: Human-object interaction (HOI) generation aims to synthesize realistic human motions and dynamic object movements given textual descriptions. Whereas existing methods focus on either body or hand motions, they struggle with the whole-body human motions, especially when handling small objects. In this work, we tackle the challenge of synthesizing holistic and continuous human-object interactions for manipulating handheld objects, including unseen objects. Our key insight is that HOI can be presented by Chain-of-Thought (CoT), which defines interactions as flexible combinations of semantic primitives. However, such representations can lead to inherent distribution gaps between primitives. To overcome this issue, we introduce a diffusion-based autoregressive model conditioned on a frame-wise monitor to generate continuous and long-term motions. Finally, a contact-guided refiner is employed to correct implausible finger motions. By integrating these components, our proposed framework, CoT-HOI, is able to synthesize arbitrary-length full-body HOIs with dexterous finger movements, which breaks down the complexity of HOIs using CoT. Experiments on HIMO and GRAB-Pri datasets verify our method’s effectiveness.

records.title: Hybrid-Order Solver for Sparse Diffusion Acceleration
records.abstract: Sparse attention has emerged as a promising approach to accelerate diffusion transformers, yet a critical inefficiency remains unexplored: existing methods uniformly apply first-order Euler methods regardless of step type---squandering precise gradients at dense steps while remaining vulnerable to approximation errors at sparse steps. We identify this fundamental Solver-Sparsity Mismatch in sparse diffusion acceleration and propose Hybrid-Order Solver: a principled strategy that aligns solver order with computational precision by applying second-order Heun methods at dense (full-attention) steps and first-order Euler methods at sparse steps. On FLUX-dev with 2,000 MS-COCO samples, our training-free approach achieves 60.1% MSE reduction, +4.12 dB PSNR improvement, and state-of-the-art CLIP Score of 31.63, surpassing TeaCache and Chipmunk while maintaining ~2x speedup with only 20% additional network evaluations. Trajectory analysis further validates that our adherence is 35-41% closer to optimal ODE solutions, demonstrating that precision alignment is the key to recovering quality in sparse diffusion acceleration.

records.title: Controllable Shape-Guided Point Cloud Generation with Collaborative Diffusion
records.abstract: Existing diffusion-based methods for 3D point cloud synthesis demonstrate strong generative capabilities but suffer from underdeveloped underlying 3D prior models. To address this limitation, we propose ShapeDiff, a diffusion-based prior model that decomposes shapes into latent primitives for enhanced controllability. This framework supports unconditional generation, shape completion, and cross-modal synthesis. Specifically, we first encode point clouds into sparse latent structures enriched with shape semantics using a vector-quantized variational autoencoder (VQ-VAE). Critically, unlike prior work optimizing dense point clouds directly, we introduce two time-dependent adaptive encoders – derived from transformer and CNN architectures – trained jointly in latent space to model global positions and fine-grained feature distributions. Operating in this sparse domain substantially accelerates training convergence while enabling explicit control over both high-level topology and granular geometry. We validate ShapeDiff as a model-agnostic framework compatible with standard diffusion architectures. Extensive benchmarking confirms that ShapeDiff achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse 3D generation tasks, surpassing existing methods in training efficiency and structural controllability.

records.title: DiffGuard: Physically Constrained Diffusion for Fine-Grained Biomechanical Anomaly Detection
records.abstract: Skeleton-based Video Anomaly Detection (SVAD) is pivotal for surveillance and healthcare, yet existing methods focusing on coarse security events fail to diagnose fine-grained biomechanical deviations. To bridge this gap, we propose DiffGuard, a novel coarse-to-fine framework. It innovatively decouples detection: Stage I employs a lightweight Kinetic-Aware Contrastive Support Vector Data Description (SVDD) for efficient screening, while Stage II activates a Biomechanics-Conditioned Diffusion Refiner for precise diagnosis of suspicious samples. Crucially, we inject explicit physical constraints (e.g., velocity limits) into the diffusion process to ensure kinematic consistency. Furthermore, we introduce FitError, a synchronized quad-view benchmark comprising 25 exercises with over 50 specific error types. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DiffGuard achieves state-of-the-art performance, effectively balancing inference efficiency with diagnostic granularity.

records.title: Multi-organ Metabolic Coupling in Alzheimer's Disease Revealed by Total-Body PET/CT Imaging
records.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is increasingly viewed as a systemic disorder, yet the quantitative coupling between peripheral metabolism and neurodegeneration remains poorly defined. We integrated whole-body and brain 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography in 95 subjects (66 patients with AD and 29 normal controls). Utilizing TotalSegmentator and brain atlas, we extracted standardized uptake value ratio (SUVR) for 114 peripheral organs and SUVR for 166 brain regions. Covariate-adjusted body-brain interaction networks were constructed using ANCOVA and path analysis. AD patients exhibited widespread cerebral hypometabolism and significant metabolic alterations in the liver, pancreas, and gastrointestinal tract. Path analysis identified anatomically specific pathways, notably a negative effect of liver metabolism on the cuneus (|β|=0.39–0.43) and significant gallbladder/colon-thalamic associations (p<0.001). This study characterizes a systemic body-brain metabolic network in AD, revealing heterogeneous coupling between peripheral organs and specific brain regions. These interaction hubs provide a novel framework for systemic diagnosis and multimodal interventions.

records.title: Accelerating Multi-Condition T2I Generation via Adaptive Condition Offloading and Pruning
records.abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) generation using multiple conditions enables fine-grained user control on the generated image. Yet, incorporating multi-condition inputs incurs substantial computation and communication overhead, due to additional preprocessing subtasks and control optimizations. It hence leads to unacceptable generation latency. In this paper, we propose an end-edge collaborative system design to accelerate multi-condition T2I generation through adaptive condition offloading and pruning. Extensive offline profiling reveal that, different conditions exhibit significant diversity in computation and communication costs. To this end, we propose a Subtask Manager that jointly optimizes condition inference offloading and bandwidth allocation using a heuristic algorithm, balancing local and edge execution delays to minimize overall preprocessing latency. Then, we design a lightweight feature-driven Conditioning Scale Estimator that evaluates the contribution of each condition by analyzing its feature activation strength and overlap with other conditions. This allows adaptive conditioning scale selection and pruning of insignificant conditions, thereby accelerating the denoising process. Extensive experimental results show that our system reduces latency by nearly 25% and improves 6% average generation quality, outperforming other benchmarks.

records.title: Holistic Co-Hyperbolic-Wavelet Learning for Head Avatars
records.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), with its advantages of real-time capability and high-quality rendering, has brought a new paradigm to high-fidelity facial reconstruction. Existing methods introduce parameterized model, e.g. 3DMM, to deform Gaussian mixtures, but 3DGS over-relies on covariance optimization for geometric adaptation, while 3DMM fails to model nonlinear facial motion deformations. This limits the modeling of highfrequency details and complex geometries in facial animation. To address this, we propose a novel hyperbolic collaborative learning approach based for head avatars based on Gaussian splatting. For nonlinear facial modeling, we integrate hyperbolic space learning and wavelet domain constraint learning: the former captures inherent hierarchical topologies in facial movements, and the latter models high-frequency details, enhancing reconstruction fidelity through collaborative learning. Additionally, leveraging 3DGS’s end-to-end nature and unique covariance matrix optimization, we adopt an optimization algorithm with adaptive momentum coefficients to find flat minima, ensuring fast convergence while avoiding local overfitting. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method performs state-of-the-art reconstruction on benchmark datasets. Our code will be made public.

records.title: AudioMoG: Guiding Audio Generation with Mixture-of-Guidance
records.abstract: The design of diffusion-based audio generation systems has been investigated from diverse perspectives, such as data space, network architecture, and conditioning techniques, while most of these innovations require model re-training. In sampling, classifier-free guidance (CFG) has been uniformly adopted to enhance generation quality by strengthening condition alignment. However, CFG often compromises diversity, resulting in suboptimal performance. Although the recent autoguidance (AG) method proposes another direction of guidance that maintains diversity, its direct application in audio generation has so far underperformed CFG. In this work, we introduce AudioMoG, an improved sampling method that enhances text-to-audio (T2A) and video-to-audio (V2A) generation quality without requiring extensive training resources. We start with an analysis of both CFG and AG, examining their respective advantages and limitations for guiding diffusion models. Building upon our insights, we introduce a mixture-of-guidance framework that integrates diverse guidance signals with their interaction terms (e.g., the unconditional bad version of the model) to maximize cumulative advantages. Experiments show that, given the same inference speed, our approach consistently outperforms single guidance in T2A generation across sampling steps, concurrently showing advantages in V2A, text-to-music (T2M), and image generation. Demo samples are available at: audiomog.github.io.

records.title: PhysAgent3D: Physically Plausible Video Generation via 3D-Aware VLM Agentic Planning
records.abstract: Recently, the physical plausibility of synthesized videos has attracted increasing attention in video diffusion research. However, existing techniques fail to reconcile the fundamental disparity between 2D pixel generation and the physical laws of the 3D world, thus leading to physical distortions. To bridge this gap, we propose PhysAgent3D, which integrates single-image 3D reconstruction with VLM agentic reasoning to inject explicit spatial priors into the diffusion process. Leveraging the extensive world knowledge of VLMs, our framework incorporates an agentic physical planning module via executable code reasoning to perform more feasible motion planning with reconstructed 3D models, thereby enhancing the spatial perception and understanding of the VLM. Consequently, our method can generate video content that exhibits superior fidelity to the input text prompt while adhering to real-world physical dynamics. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms baseline models in various metrics.

records.title: OctantAvatar: Disentangled and Inertia-Aware Gaussian Avatars via Vectorized Atlas Mapping
records.abstract: Reconstructing animatable human avatars with complex, dynamic clothing remains a significant challenge. Existing methods often struggle with appearance ambiguities and feature collisions in planar representations. To address this, we propose OctantAvatar, featuring a novel disentangled representation and a generative animation mechanism. Specifically, we design an Orthant-based Disentangled Representation that leverages human body symmetry to partition the canonical space, effectively mitigating projection aliasing on feature planes. This representation is implemented efficiently by a branch-free Vectorized Atlas Mapping. For animation, we present a generative Inertia-Aware Gating Network that learns to synthesize appearance features for novel poses. The proposed model learns a continuous dynamics manifold by interpolating from a reference bank, conditioned on both pose and inertia. Experiments on challenging benchmarks demonstrate that our OctantAvatar significantly outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in rendering intricate clothing and ensuring smooth, robust animation.

records.title: Parameterized Temporal Gaussian Flow for Animatable Human Avatar
records.abstract: In recent years, 3D human avatar reconstruction based on 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has attracted significant research interest due to high rendering efficiency. However, most existing methods rely on MLPs to regress non-rigid deformations. The failure to disentangle genuine high-frequency physical details from temporally irregular noise results in attenuated dynamic variations and the emergence of non-physical artifacts. To alleviate this limitation, we propose a parameterized temporal trajectory for Gaussian primitive, which constrains frame-wise non-rigid deformations to evolve as a smooth temporal process, suppressing temporal noise while preserving fine-grained garment dynamics. In addition, we adopt a 6D rotation residual representation to improve stability in highly articulated regions and propose a local structural consistency regularization to stabilize geometry and appearance evolution. Experimental results demonstrate that our method enables stable reconstruction with reduced training time while supporting real-time rendering at 234 FPS.

records.title: PhyRPR: Training-Free Physics-Constrained Video Generation
records.abstract: Recent diffusion-based video generation models can synthesize visually plausible videos, yet they often struggle to satisfy physical constraints. A key reason is that most existing approaches remain single-stage: they entangle high-level physical understanding with low-level visual synthesis, making it hard to generate content that require explicit physical reasoning. To address this limitation, we propose a training-free three-stage pipeline,\textit{PhyRPR}:\textit{Phy\uline{R}eason}--\textit{Phy\uline{P}lan}--\textit{Phy\uline{R}efine}, which decouples physical understanding from visual synthesis. Specifically, \textit{PhyReason} uses a large multimodal model for physical state reasoning and an image generator for keyframe synthesis; \textit{PhyPlan} deterministically synthesizes a controllable coarse motion scaffold; and \textit{PhyRefine} injects this scaffold into diffusion sampling via a latent fusion strategy to refine appearance while preserving the planned dynamics. This staged design enables explicit physical control during generation. Extensive experiments under physics constraints show that our method consistently improves physical plausibility and motion controllability.

records.title: FFSynth: Fast Flow Matching for Efficient 3D Indoor Scene Synthesis
records.abstract: High-quality 3D indoor scene synthesis is an important research direction in computer vision and is increasingly influential in creative industries. Advances in generative technology have heightened the demand for methods that combine realism with efficient generation. Although diffusion-based scene generators are promising, they typically require expensive iterative sampling, leading to long inference times, and the resulting layouts may deviate from the underlying floor geometry. We propose FFSynth, a fast and high-fidelity framework based on a Flow Matching denoising paradigm. By conditioning on floor-plan information, FFSynth better aligns generated furniture layouts with user-specified room structures, while incorporating a Flow-Inversion Guided Structural Regularization (FIGSR) strategy to ensure structurally plausible furniture placements. Using an existing model to form noisy–target training pairs, we adopt rectified flow to streamline generation, accelerating sampling while preserving quality. Experiments on 3D-FRONT demonstrate improved layout plausibility and scene realism, while effectively supporting indoor scene synthesis and related downstream tasks.

records.title: DSCI-GAN: Dynamic Segmentation and Component-style Guided Facial Image Inpainting
records.abstract: Reference-guided face inpainting addresses user demand for personalized image restoration. However, existing methods often require multiple iterations to transfer styles from multiple reference images, leading to error accumulation and semantic distortion. Additionally, they frequently underperform in repairing irregular, large-scale missing regions due to insufficient utilization of contextual information. To address these limitations, we present DSCI-GAN, a novel facial inpainting framework based on Dynamic Segmentation and Component-level style guided Inpainting (DSCI). This approach enables the extraction of distinct facial component styles from multiple reference images within a single forward pass. Furthermore, we propose a Multi-branch Dilated Gated Module (MDGM) to capture long-range dependencies and improves robustness under complex occlusions. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of our method. Compared with state-of-the-art techniques, DSCI-GAN reduces the FID by 8.28% at mask ratios of 0.5-0.6, while achieving fine-grained control over image style.

records.title: PRG-Flow: Parallel Rectification Gating and Cross-Scale Fusion for Online Video Editing
records.abstract: Real-time video editing faces a critical dilemma between inference speed and temporal consistency, as causal constraints often lead to severe error propagation. To address this, we propose PRG-Flow, a novel training-free online framework that bridges the gap between efficiency and quality. We introduce Flow-Gated Semantic Rectification (FGSR) to explicitly correct historical feature misalignment and Cross-Scale Temporal Fusion (CSTF) to inject structural priors for smooth transitions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PRG-Flow matches the visual fidelity of heavy offline methods while running at 5.26 FPS, significantly outperforming existing online baselines. Furthermore, we validate our method in a downstream application by deploying it as a style transfer engine in a 3D simulation platform. The successful execution of vision-based navigation tasks verifies that PRG-Flow preserves essential scene geometry, thereby effectively enhancing the robustness evaluation of embodied agents.

records.title: Human Multi-View Synthesis from a Single-View Model: Transferred Body and Region Representations
records.abstract: Generating multi-view human images from a single view is a complex and significant challenge. Although recent advancements in multi-view object generation have shown impressive results with diffusion models, novel view synthesis for humans remains constrained by the limited availability of 3D human datasets. Consequently, many existing models struggle to produce realistic human body shapes or capture fine-grained facial details accurately. To address these issues, we propose an innovative framework that leverages transferred body and facial representations for multi-view human synthesis. Specifically, we use a single-view model pre-trained on a large-scale human dataset to develop a multi-view body representation, aiming to extend the 2D knowledge of the single-view model to a multi-view diffusion model. Additionally, to enhance the model's detail restoration capability, we integrate transferred multimodal facial features into our trained human diffusion model. Experimental evaluations on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms the current state-of-the-art methods, achieving superior performance in multi-view human synthesis.

records.title: HG-Mamba: Heuristic-Guided State Space Model for Laparoscopic Image Desmoking
records.abstract: Developing smoke removal algorithms for laparoscopic surgery is crucial for enhancing surgical visibility and supporting accurate intraoperative decision-making. While Mamba, a state space model (SSM), shows strong potential in visual tasks by balancing global receptive fields with efficiency, its sequential state transitions restrict spatial correlation modeling and its feed-forward layers lack frequency modeling, hindering effective removal of complex surgical smoke.To overcome these limitations, we propose Heuristic-Guided Mamba (HG-Mamba), which enhances Mamba through spatial and frequency domain improvements. HG-Mamba introduces a Heuristic-Guided SSM (HG-SSM) that performs input-guided dynamic sampling and flexible state fusion for adaptive spatial context modeling, and a Frequency Refine FFN (FR-FFN) that applies multi-band frequency decomposition with adaptive weighting to strengthen frequency representations. By combining spatial adaptability with frequency-aware refinement, HG-Mamba becomes an effective backbone for surgical smoke removal.Extensive experiments demonstrate that HG-Mamba outperforms state-of-the-art methods on both synthetic and real-world smoke/smokeless datasets. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/ShiweiWu98/HG-Mamba.

records.title: SDFD: Physics-Based Source-Driven Flare Dataset and Decoupled Dual-Reconstruction Network
records.abstract: Nighttime flare suppression is hindered by the scarcity of high-fidelity paired data and architectures that neglect local flare characteristics. We propose a unified framework addressing both challenges. First, we introduce the Source-Driven Flare Dataset (SDFD). By modeling physical patterns from real-world flares, SDFD utilizes actual light sources within scenes to drive the generation of 15,000 physically consistent image pairs, effectively narrowing the synthetic-to-real domain gap. Second, we propose the Flare-Decoupled Dual-Reconstruction Network (FD$^2$R-Net). Its Glare-Aware Dual-Decoder decouples flare perception from background restoration, facilitated by our Asymmetric Dual-Stream Modulation (ADSM), which employs differentiated modulation strategies to optimize information flow. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, validating the superiority of our source-driven synthesis and task-decoupled design.

records.title: YWave-Mamba: A Y-Channel Guided Hybrid-Domain State Space Model for Underwater Image Enhancement
records.abstract: Underwater images suffer from degradation characterized by color distortion and loss of texture details. Existing methods often process these coupled factors holistically, leading to limited restoration accuracy. To address this, we propose YWave-Mamba, a Y-channel guided hybrid-domain state space model. We first employ Discrete Wavelet Transform to decouple degradation features into low-frequency and high-frequency components. For the low-frequency component, reconsidering the relationship between amplitude and phase in the Fourier domain, we design an Amplitude-Phase Cross Attention Module to cooperatively restore amplitude and phase. For high-frequency components, we design a mamba-net to process the Y-channel in YCbCr space to provide robust structural priors, and introduce a High-Frequency State Space Module to reconstruct directional textures via linear-complexity global modeling. Extensive experiments demonstrate that YWave-Mamba achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance.

records.title: Causal Source-Free Domain Adaptation for Low-Light Image Enhancement
records.abstract: To address the performance degradation caused by domain shifts, while adhering to data privacy constraints that preclude source data access, we propose a novel Causal Source-free Domain adaptation for Low-light image enhancement (CSDL) method. Operating within a teacher-student framework, CSDL employs two core interventions to mitigate source domain bias. Specifically, the illuminance intervention module utilizes contrast adjustment and global deviation correction to perform de-confounding on inaccurate illuminance estimates. Simultaneously, the content relationship intervention module applies pixel-level and patch-level expansions based on do-operations to eliminate the influence of unobservable source content relationships. Experiments across six transfer scenarios with three methods demonstrate that CSDL significantly enhances source domain model performance, achieving an improvement of up to 2.39 dB.

records.title: STMG-DUN: A Spatio-Temporal Memory-Guided Deep Unfolding Network for Sparse-View CT Reconstruction
records.abstract: Sparse-view Computed Tomography (CT) imaging reduces the radiation dose by decreasing the number of projection views, thereby mitigating the risk of radiation exposure to patients. However, the process introduces severe streaking artifacts and degrades image quality. To tackle the aforementioned challenge, a novel Spatio-Temporal Memory-Guided Deep Unfolding Network (STMG-DUN) is proposed, which combines the framework of Proximal Gradient Descent (PGD) with the powerful nonlinear modeling capability of Deep Learning (DL). Specifically, STMG-DUN unfolds the iterative reconstruction process into multiple stages. Each stage comprises a Gated Memory-Guided Gradient Descent Module (GMGM) and a Multi-scale Feature-Guided Proximal Mapping Module (MFGM). The GMGM innovatively introduces a gating mechanism to generate a content-aware and history-dependent dynamic adaptive step size (DASS). The MFGM integrates multi-scale perception with an attention mechanism, leveraging local multi-scale context information to fuse global long-range dependency. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that the STMG-DUN framework significantly outperforms many state-of-the-art methods.

records.title: Enhancing Image Quality Assessment Ability of LMMs via Retrieval-Augmented Generation
records.abstract: Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) have recently shown remarkable promise in low-level visual perception tasks, particularly in Image Quality Assessment (IQA), demonstrating strong zero-shot capability. However, achieving state-of-the-art performance often requires computationally expensive fine-tuning methods, which aim to align the distribution of quality-related token in output with image quality levels. Inspired by recent training-free works for LMM, we introduce IQARAG, a novel, training-free framework that enhances LMMs' IQA ability. IQARAG leverages Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to retrieve some semantically similar but quality-variant reference images with corresponding Mean Opinion Scores (MOSs) for input image. These retrieved images and input image are integrated into a specific prompt. Retrieved images provide the LMM with a visual perception anchor for IQA task. IQARAG contains three key phases: Retrieval Feature Extraction, Image Retrieval, and Integration & Quality Score Generation. Extensive experiments across multiple diverse IQA datasets, including KADID, KonIQ, LIVE Challenge, and SPAQ, demonstrate that the proposed IQARAG effectively boosts the IQA performance of LMMs, offering a resource-efficient alternative to fine-tuning for quality assessment.

records.title: A Smooth Decoupling Strategy based on Shared Prior for Compressed Image Super-Resolution
records.abstract: With the explosive growth of images, image compression and downsampling play an important role in reducing transmission and storage overhead, yet inevitably introduce artifacts and information loss. For Compressed Image Super-Resolution (CSR), most end-to-end methods overlook that downsampling-induced blur further exacerbates information loss during the quantization process, while cascaded frameworks suffer from high training costs and error accumulation. In this work, we analyze these degradation mechanisms and propose DiffCSR, a single network that facilitates task decoupling by employing two task-specific LoRAs based on shared diffusion priors. Furthermore, we introduce Progressive Structure Modulation (PSM) to enhance fidelity and structural consistency across the two-stage process. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of DiffCSR across diverse compression methods, validating its potential for addressing the coupled CSR task.

records.title: M^2TS: Nighttime Image Deraining via Macro-to-Micro Teacher-Student
records.abstract: Existing nighttime image deraining methods rely on synthetic data due to scarce real-world pairs, yet inherent synthetic-to-real domain gaps cripple performance on real-world data. This paper proposes Macro-to-Micro Teacher-Student (M^2TS), a nighttime image deraining framework that removes rain streaks at two levels: coarse (Macro Teacher-Student, Macro-TS) and fine-grained (Micro Teacher-Student, Micro-TS), by leveraging real-world unlabeled rain images for learning. Macro-TS exploits vision foundation models (VFMs) to extract rain-robust semantic features and enforces semantic consistency to suppress coarse artifacts while preserving structure. Guided by Macro-TS, Micro-TS further removes fine-grained streaks via pixel-level optimization using pseudo pairs generated by the teachers. Both qualitative and quantitative results demonstrate the state-of-the-art performance of our method, achieving an 16\% improvement in the BRISQUE score over previous methods on real-world nighttime images.

records.title: Prompt-Guided Semantic Refinement for Cross-Weather Driving Saliency Adaptation
records.abstract: Adverse weather conditions pose significant challenges to robust saliency prediction due to pronounced domain shifts in appearance and scene structure. Existing approaches often rely on coarse global feature alignment, which fails to capture fine-grained spatial and stylistic variations. In this work, we propose a prompt-guided adaptation framework for cross-weather driving saliency prediction, leveraging scene structural priors to refine semantic representations. The framework introduces a Prompt-Guided Structure-Aware Normalization module (PGSAN) that encodes scene structure distributions into channel-wise style modulation, together with a mask-guided backbone that effectively fuses structure-aware cues with deep semantic features. Extensive experiments across diverse adverse weather conditions demonstrate strong cross-domain generalization and accurate localization of critical regions in complex driving scenes.

records.title: DCDformer: All-in-One Weather Restoration with Cross-Scale Linear Log-Normal Attention
records.abstract: All-in-One weather image restoration aims to recover images degraded by diverse adverse weather conditions. Many unified methods rely on a global conditioning signal, which can be suboptimal when degradations vary spatially within an image. We propose a degradation-conditioned dyadic Transformer (DCDformer) that performs region-aware processing via two complementary streams. The alignment-centric stream adopts deformable attention to capture locally structured degradations. The cross-scale stream introduces Cross-Scale Linear Log-Normal Attention, which applies degradation-conditioned temperature/bias modulation and cross-scale key/value augmentation to improve long-range context modeling with linear complexity. To couple the two streams, a Degradation-Conditioned Router (DCR) produces a pixel-wise routing map to adaptively integrate the two streams without explicit weather labels, and a Dyadic Confidence Modulator (DCM) further applies confidence-based weighting to the multi-stage integration of paired features. Experiments on WeatherBench, RESIDE-SOTS, and Test2800 demonstrate improvements over unified baselines.

records.title: Wavelet-Domain Haze-Aware Disentangled Learning for Non-Uniform Haze Removal in Remote Sensing Imagery
records.abstract: Non-uniform haze removal in remote sensing imagery (RSI) remains challenging due to spatially varying degradation patterns and the entanglement between global structure distortion and local texture attenuation. In this paper, we propose a Wavelet-Domain Haze-Aware Disentangled Learning (WHDL) framework. Unlike spatial-domain methods that struggle with entangled features, WHDL adopts a frequency-disentangled divide-and-conquer strategy to map the degraded scene into orthogonal frequency subspaces, enabling the targeted decoupling of large-scale illumination distortion from fine-grained texture corruption. Specifically, we design a Band-Aware Dual-Stream Haze Analyzer to extract subband-distinct, spatially-variant conditions. Under this guidance, we introduce a Haze-Aware Disentangled Modulation mechanism, where a Spatially-Variant Illumination Rectifier (SIR) and a Spatially-Variant Texture Router (STR) execute coarse-grained structural rectification and fine-grained texture recovery in low- and high-frequency subbands, respectively. Furthermore, we propose a Multi-Granularity Decoupled Supervision scheme that transcends traditional spatial-only constraints. By imposing specific fidelity goals on global reconstruction, structure, and texture, this scheme enforces coherent restoration across different semantic granularities. Extensive experiments demonstrate WHDL's quantitative and visual superiority under non-uniform haze conditions.

records.title: A Multi-stage Collaborative Robustness Enhancement Method for Face Recognition Models
records.abstract: As a common multimedia-based identity authentication technology, face recognition remains vulnerable to malicious inputs, posing significant challenges to its safe deployment. Existing defenses cannot simultaneously guarantee the legitimacy of model inputs and the intrinsic robustness of the model, and thus suffer from limited applicability and generalization. Meanwhile, the distinctive network architecture, task characteristics, and application risks of face recognition call for specialized defense designs. To this end, we propose a data–model collaborative robustness enhancement framework that employs a reusable lightweight encoder module to build a multi-stage defense pipeline, ranging from architectural hardening to malicious sample interception and post-purification re-recognition. Experimental results show that the proposed method substantially improves robustness against diverse malicious inputs with only minor model fine-tuning and is applicable to both verification and identification scenarios.

records.title: PhysioMamba: Physics-Informed ST-Mamba Diffusion for Controllable Echocardiogram Synthesis
records.abstract: High-fidelity and clinically controllable echocardiogram synthesis remains constrained by privacy regulations and data scarcity. Existing studies mainly focus on data-driven generative processes, lacking modeling of the underlying physical mechanisms of cardiac motion, which leads to limited physiological consistency. In addition, existing models are often computationally complex, constraining their potential for clinical application. We propose the PhysioMamba framework, which integrates differentiable physics priors, linear-time state space modeling, and agentic reasoning. A cardiac simulator is introduced to reproduce realistic heartbeat dynamics and provide physical priors, while the ST-Mamba-UNet achieves linear complexity backbone. Two agents work synergistically to ensure physiological consistency of the results through an active correction mechanism. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PhysioMamba achieves a Fr\'echet Video Distance of 5.85 and an Ejection Fraction Mean Absolute Error of 3.1%, significantly outperforming leading multimodal (HeartBeat) and latent diffusion (EchoFlow) baselines. By bridging physical simulation with generative AI, PhysioMamba paves the way for trustworthy medical digital twins.

records.title: Text-Guided Optimal Transport for Aerial-Ground Person Re-Identification
records.abstract: The significant viewpoint discrepancy between ground and aerial cameras presents a fundamental challenge in Aerial-Ground Person Re-Identification (AGPReID), where dramatic appearance variations severely hinder cross-view identity matching. Existing methods typically rely on attribute learning or viewpoint decoupling, but they struggle to cope with extreme viewpoint diversity and often underutilize discriminative local features. To address these issues, we propose a novel Text-guided Optimal Transport (TOT) framework that leverages structured textual descriptions as view-invariant semantic anchors to bridge the cross-view domain gap. Specifically, we build a three-stream framework with shared CLIP backbone to encode ground and aerial images together with textual descriptions. Then, we introduce an Optimal Transport Alignment (OTA) module formulates local feature matching as an optimal transport problem to obtain a cost-efficient mapping between ground and aerial feature distributions under textual guidance. Meanwhile, a Global Consensus Fusion (GCF) module enforces global consistency across the visual and textual streams to obtain unified, view-invariant identity representations. Extensive experiments on multiple AGPReID benchmarks demonstrate our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance.

records.title: MIIG: Multi-Instance Interaction Generation in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
records.abstract: Existing text-to-image diffusion models often face challenges in spatial localization and semantic understanding of interactions. To address these issues, we propose MIIG (Multi-Instance Interaction Generation), a novel generative framework for interaction control. Our core innovation is introducing action masks as visual conditions that precisely define interaction regions. MIIG employs a feature-decoupling architecture with two pathways: an Instance Attention Module that leverages bounding boxes to anchor the location of instances, and an Interact Attention Module that extracts visual details of interaction from action masks. Subsequently, these two independent feature streams are dynamically integrated via timestep-gated fusion. Furthermore, we design an LLM Pipeline and vector database for flexible inference. Experiments on the HICO-DET and V-COCO interaction datasets show that MIIG outperforms existing methods across multiple metrics. Particularly on rare interactions, MIIG achieves 3.66% improvement, demonstrating superior generalization capabilities. Project is available at https://github.com/13549425112/MIIG.

records.title: MPDU: Momentum-Preserving Diffusion Unrolling via Explicit Subspace Decoupling for Compressed Sensing
records.abstract: The convergence of generative modeling and data compression is reshaping the landscape of Compressed Sensing (CS), promising a new era of Physics-Generative Synergy. However, achieving this synergy is hindered by a fundamental conflict: forcing generative models to directly satisfy physical measurements often leads to Manifold Deviation, where high-frequency semantic textures are corrupted by low-frequency physical corrections. To resolve this, we propose MPDU, a Momentum-Preserving Diffusion Unrolling framework. Unlike existing hybrids that entangle physical and generative updates, MPDU introduces Explicit Subspace Decoupling. By analytically decomposing the diffusion state into a deterministic Signal Subspace and a stochastic Generative Subspace, we enforce physical fidelity strictly on the signal anchor while preserving the generative momentum in the noise residual. Furthermore, we construct a Spatiotemporal Physical Adapter (STPA) and a Deep Chronological Feature Flux (DCFF) to bridge the semantic gap and prevent the forgetting of high-frequency cues. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MPDU achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction quality at ultra-low sampling rates, outperforming standard diffusion solvers in both efficiency and fidelity.

records.title: Patch Knowledge Transfer for Efficient AI-Generated Image Quality Assessment
records.abstract: With the rapid advancement of image generation technologies, perceptual quality assessment of AI-generated images has emerged as a crucial research direction in computer vision. The core challenge of this task lies in achieving efficient quality assessment for massive generated images. Current mainstream approaches exhibit two key limitations: 1) Methods employing complex feature extraction strategies, while improving performance, incur prohibitive computational costs that hinder real-time inference; 2) Simple image scaling-based solutions, despite their computational efficiency, demonstrate significantly inferior assessment accuracy. To address this critical issue, we propose Patch Knowledge Transfer (PKT), a knowledge distillation-based optimization framework that achieves synergistic optimization of visual representation capability and inference efficiency through an innovative multi-level knowledge transfer mechanism. Specifically, we design a dual-model architecture: a teacher model with local-global hybrid processing provides high-quality supervision signals, while a student model relying solely on global processing efficiently inherits the teacher's representation capacity through multi-level supervision. Extensive experiments conducted on 4 AIGIQA databases demonstrate that the PKT framework enables the student model to maintain performance comparable to the teacher while reducing computational costs by 67.7\%. Furthermore, compared to existing methods, our approach achieves a superior balance between model efficiency and assessment accuracy.

records.title: SemIR: Degradation Distinguishability in Diffusion Semantic Space for All-in-One Image Restoration
records.abstract: All-in-One Image Restoration (AiOIR) aims to effectively recover high-quality clean images from images with various degradation types and levels. The challenge of AiOIR lies in the joint requirement to estimate the degradation type and restore the image. In this paper, we explore the properties of various degraded images in the semantic latent space of frozen pre-trained diffusion models and propose a Semantic features-guided Image Restoration framework SemIR to achieve end-to-end and effective AiOIR. Specifically, we first reveal that the latent representations of different types of degraded images in the diffusion semantic space are degradation-distinguishable. Based on the findings, we design a Distinguishable Degradation Integration Module and an Adaptive Degradation Learning Module to integrate the degradation representations from the diffusion latent space into the image restoration network. Our method effectively leverages the informative representations derived from the pre-trained diffusion model, avoiding the need for additional training of degradation encoders or extensive parameter learning. Comprehensive experiments verify that the proposed modules can be integrated into other unified and multi-task restoration networks, outperforming existing AiOIR methods.
