records.title: MeloCodec: Harnessing Melodic Priors for High-Fidelity Singing Voice Representation
records.abstract: Neural audio codecs serve as fundamental tokenizers for LLM-based audio generation. While semantic priors are widely exploited to enhance linguistic intelligibility, the integration of explicit acoustic priors remains underexplored, limiting synthesis fidelity in frequency-sensitive domains. To address this gap, we introduce MeloCodec, a novel framework designed to effectively incorporate melodic priors—a critical form of acoustic information for singing. To address the optimization instability typically caused by the direct fusion of such explicit priors, we propose a ``Tokenize-then-Fuse'' paradigm that pre-trains a discrete melodic branch to lock in structures before feature fusion. To robustly realize this paradigm, we further propose a robust two-stage training strategy, which prevents codebook collapse and ensures stable convergence. Experiments show that MeloCodec outperforms baselines in singing voice representation, improving pitch consistency and enabling controllable pitch manipulation with minimal timbre degradation. Audio samples are available at \url{https://anonymous.4open.science/api/repo/melocodec_demo-60EC/file/demo.html?v=42c197c7}.

records.title: CityGen: Structure-Guided City-Style Synthesis for Cross-City Autonomous Driving
records.abstract: Autonomous driving systems are commonly trained and evaluated within limited geographic regions, which hinders their scalability when deployed in new cities. However, significant domain shifts in appearance, road topology, and traffic patterns often cause severe performance degradation under cross-city deployment. Existing approaches based on domain adaptation, data augmentation, or synthetic data generation typically rely on labeled target data, city-specific annotations, or task-specific designs, limiting their scalability and effectiveness for holistic evaluation. In this paper, we introduce CityTransfer-Bench, a geographically disjoint benchmark for evaluating cross-city generalization across perception, segmentation, and planning, and propose CityGen, a diffusion-based generative framework that performs zero-label city adaptation via HD-map–conditioned synthesis guided by city-level visual prompts. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CityGen consistently improves cross-city robustness across multiple tasks, establishing a scalable and label-efficient foundation for generalizable autonomous driving.

records.title: Phase-Shifted Temporal Fusion and Spectral Guidance for Diffusion Super-Resolution
records.abstract: Image super-resolution via diffusion models fundamentally operates as a coarse-to-fine spectral evolution. However, existing methods suffer from a Static-Dynamic Mismatch by applying fixed conditioning to this dynamic process, while also neglecting spectral fidelity. To address this, we propose PTSG-Diff (Phase-shifted Temporal Fusion and Spectral Guidance). First, Phase-Temporal Fusion (PT-Fusion) introduces a Dynamic Soft-Gating Mechanism, decomposing timesteps into phase-shifted tokens to align features with evolving structural-to-textural demands. Second, the Spectral Guidance Network (SG-Net) employs Orthogonal Frequency Decomposition to resolve spectral deficits by enforcing joint consistency across noise, pixel, and decoupled Fourier domains. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PTSG-Diff outperforms competing diffusion-based and flow-based methods in both spatial accuracy and perceptual realism.

records.title: Phy-Traffic: Physics-Informed Synthetic Data Generation for Rare Traffic Events via Logic-Constrained LLMs
records.abstract: Data scarcity within rare-event traffic scenarios constitutes a primary bottleneck for developing robust Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS), necessitating advanced synthetic data generation. Although generative models capture statistical distributions, they frequently lack kinematic consistency; meanwhile, direct synthesis via Large Language Models (LLMs) often yields numerical hallucinations. To resolve this, we present Phy-Traffic, a physics-informed framework that decouples synthesis into semantic logic formulation and deterministic numerical execution. Phy-Traffic utilizes a collaborative multi-LLM paradigm featuring three specialized agents: a Physics-Aware Generator for logic-driven perturbation, a Logic Auditor for physical validity enforcement, and a Reflective Optimizer for iterative refinement. We unify these agents under an end-to-end Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) pipeline, facilitating autonomous alignment with complex physical constraints. Empirical evaluations indicate that Phy-Traffic achieves over 90% distributional fidelity and a 24.2% improvement in rare-event classification, validating its efficacy for safety-critical autonomous applications.

records.title: ORSIFlow: Saliency-Guided Rectified Flow for Optical Remote Sensing Salient Object Detection
records.abstract: Optical Remote Sensing Image Salient Object Detection (ORSI-SOD) remains challenging due to complex backgrounds, low contrast, irregular object shapes, and large variations in object scale. Existing discriminative methods directly regress saliency maps, while recent diffusion-based generative approaches suffer from stochastic sampling and high computational cost. In this paper, we propose ORSIFlow, a saliency-guided rectified flow framework that reformulates ORSI-SOD as a deterministic latent flow generation problem. ORSIFlow performs saliency mask generation in a compact latent space constructed by a frozen variational autoencoder, enabling efficient inference with only a few steps. To enhance saliency awareness, we design a Salient Feature Discriminator for global semantic discrimination and a Salient Feature Calibrator for precise boundary refinement. Extensive experiments on multiple public benchmarks show that ORSIFlow achieves state-of-the-art performance with significantly improved efficiency.

records.title: Closed-Loop Diffusion Purification via Semantic Consistency
records.abstract: Diffusion-based adversarial purification faces a robustness-fidelity bottleneck, where increasing noise to resist adaptive attacks causes severe semantic drift. We address this via a novel Closed-loop Semantic Consistency framework. By treating the diffusion path as a stochastic reference and enforcing feature alignment, our method acts as a semantic anchor to prevent generative deviations. Theoretically, we prove that high-dimensional stochasticity induces gradient decorrelation, effectively disrupting adaptive attack alignment. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving a superior balance between robustness and fidelity.

records.title: DriveGen3D: Boosting Feed-Forward Driving Scene Generation with Efficient Video Diffusion
records.abstract: We present DriveGen3D, a novel framework for generating high-quality and highly controllable dynamic 3D driving scenes that addresses critical limitations in existing methodologies. Current approaches to driving scene synthesis either suffer from prohibitive computational demands for extended temporal generation, focus exclusively on prolonged video synthesis without 3D representation, or restrict themselves to static single-scene reconstruction. Our work bridges this methodological gap by integrating accelerated long-term video generation with large-scale dynamic scene reconstruction through multimodal conditional control. DriveGen3D introduces a unified pipeline consisting of two specialized components: FastDrive-DiT, an efficient video diffusion transformer for high-resolution, temporally coherent video synthesis under text and Bird's-Eye-View (BEV) layout guidance; and FastRecon3D, a feed-forward module that rapidly builds 3D Gaussian representations across time, ensuring spatial-temporal consistency. DriveGen3D enable the generation of long driving videos (up to $800\times424$ at $12$ FPS) and corresponding 3D scenes, achieving state-of-the-art results while maintaining efficiency.

records.title: DINO-GFSA: Geo-Localization via Semantic Gated Fusion and Mamba-based Sequential Aggregation
records.abstract: Cross-view geo-localization (CVGL) is critical for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) self-positioning and target localization in GNSS-denied environments. However, acquiring robust semantics while preserving fine-grained spatial details remains challenging. To address this, we propose DINO-GFSA, a framework leveraging a LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) adapted DINOv3 (ViT-L) backbone for parameter-efficient, high-capacity representation. Crucially, we introduce a Semantic Gated Residual Fusion module, which utilizes high-level semantics to selectively calibrate and integrate low-level spatial cues, effectively bridging the semantic gap. Furthermore, a Mamba-based Sequential Aggregation Head is designed to capture long-range spatial dependencies with linear complexity. Experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on University-1652 and DenseUAV benchmarks, notably surpassing the previous best on DenseUAV by 3.48% on Recall@1. These results validate DINO-GFSA as a generalized, robust solution for UAV CVGL.

records.title: Robust Embodied Perception in Dynamic Environments via Disentangled Weight Fusion
records.abstract: Embodied perception systems face severe challenges of dynamic environment distribution drift when they continuously interact in open physical spaces. However, the existing domain incremental awareness methods often rely on the domain id obtained in advance during the testing phase, which limits their practicability in unknown interaction scenarios. At the same time, the model often overfits to the context-specific perceptual noise, which leads to insufficient generalization ability and catastrophic forgetting. To address these limitations, we propose a domain-id and exemplar-free incremental learning framework for embodied multimedia systems, which aims to achieve robust continuous environment adaptation. This method designs a disentangled representation mechanism to remove non-essential environmental style interference, and guide the model to focus on extracting semantic intrinsic features shared across scenes, thereby eliminating perceptual uncertainty and improving generalization. We further use the weight fusion strategy to dynamically integrate the old and new environment knowledge in the parameter space, so as to ensure that the model adapts to the new distribution without storing historical data and maximally retains the discrimination ability of the old environment. Extensive experiments on multiple standard benchmark datasets show that the proposed method significantly reduces catastrophic forgetting in a completely exemplar-free and domain-id free setting, and its accuracy is better than the existing state-of-the-art methods.

records.title: Modality Dominance-Aware Optimization for Embodied RGB–Infrared Perception
records.abstract: RGB–Infrared (RGB–IR) multimodal perception is fundamental to embodied multimedia systems operating in complex physical environments. Although recent cross-modal fusion methods have advanced RGB–IR detection, the optimization dynamics caused by asymmetric modality characteristics remain underexplored. In practice, disparities in information density and feature quality introduce persistent optimization bias, leading training to overemphasize a dominant modality and hindering effective fusion. To quantify this phenomenon, we propose the Modality Dominance Index (MDI), which measures modality dominance by jointly modeling feature entropy and gradient contribution. Based on MDI, we develop a Modality Dominance-Aware Cross-modal Learning (MDACL) framework that regulates cross-modal optimization. MDACL incorporates Hierarchical Cross-modal Guidance (HCG) to enhance feature alignment and Adversarial Equilibrium Regularization (AER) to balance optimization dynamics during fusion. Extensive experiments on three RGB–IR benchmarks demonstrate that MDACL effectively mitigates optimization bias and achieves SOTA performance.

records.title: Hand3R: Online 4D Hand-Scene Reconstruction in the Wild
records.abstract: For Embodied AI, jointly reconstructing dynamic hands and the dense scene context is crucial for understanding physical interaction. However, most existing methods recover isolated hands in local coordinates, overlooking the surrounding 3D environment. To address this, we present Hand3R, the first online framework for joint 4D hand-scene reconstruction from monocular video. Hand3R synergizes a pre-trained hand expert with a 4D scene foundation model via a scene-aware visual prompting mechanism. By injecting high-fidelity hand priors into a persistent scene memory, our approach enables simultaneous reconstruction of accurate hand meshes and dense metric-scale scene geometry in a single forward pass. Experiments demonstrate that Hand3R bypasses the reliance on offline optimization and delivers competitive performance in both local hand reconstruction and global positioning.

records.title: PAWFU: Progressive Adaptive Weighted Fusion with Uncertainty-Aware for Multimodal Emotion Recognition in Conversation
records.abstract: Multimodal Emotion Recognition in Conversation (MERC) is challenging due to the subtle and ambiguous nature of emotional expressions. Typically, text modality offer stronger and more learnable affective signals in conversation, leading model to a bias preference for textual branch, and then deactivating the attention's dynamic properties. Moreover, some existing frameworks adopt text-dominated design strategies that capitalize on textual advantage but marginalize acoustic and visual modalities. Recent studies on dynamic adaptation fusion attempt to mitigate such imbalance, but they lack the quantification and proper utilization of uncertainty. Inspired by cognitive science, we employ uncertainty metrics to simulate the difficulty of inferring human emotions. Thus, we propose PAWFU, which quantifies emotional ambiguity and enhances multimodal reliability. It comprises three components: (1) a Unimodal Feature Processing (UFP) module which handles distribution alignment and contextual interaction; (2) a Bidirectional Progressive Attention (BPA) module which is responsible for iterative cross-modal fusion; and (3) a Uncertainty-aware Dynamic Weighting (UDW) module which adjusts contribution of each fusion path. Experiments on IEMOCAP and MELD demonstrate improved weighted F1 scores, confirming PAWFU’s ability to preserve textual strengths while adaptively enhancing the role of non-textual modalities.

records.title: GeoMag: Geometric-Aware Video Motion Magnification via State Space Model
records.abstract: Video Motion Magnification (VMM) reveals imperceptible dynamics but often suffers from structural inconsistencies under complex geometric transformations. Existing learning-based methods generally face a trade-off between the limited global context of CNNs and the high computational cost of Transformers. In addition, current training protocols, largely dominated by simple linear motion, fail to capture the geometric and imaging complexities encountered in realworld videos. To address these issues, we propose GeoMag, a geometric-aware VMM framework built upon State Space Models to achieve globally consistent motion amplification with linear complexity. We further construct Geo-200K, a large-scale synthetic dataset that introduces rich geometric transformations together with sensor-realistic degradations, improving the diversity and realism of training signals. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmarks show that GeoMag consistently outperforms prior methods in visual fidelity and computational efficiency, while producing fewer artifacts and better structural consistency. The source code is available at https://github.com/scottHankcheng/GeoMag

records.title: Learning Where to Attend: A Sparse Dynamic Gate Transformer for Efficient Image Deraining
records.abstract: Image deraining aims to reconstruct high-quality scenes from degradations caused by rain streaks and raindrops. Although recent Transformers enhance long-range modeling, they rely on inefficient attention (dense or fixed sparse), wasting computation on rain-irrelevant regions and introducing noisy interactions. To address these issues, we propose a Sparse Dynamic Gate Transformer (SDGformer), which learns where to attend by coupling content-adaptive sparse attention with local structure refinement. Specifically, a Dynamic Gate Operator (DGO) predicts input-dependent attention sparsity and scope, allocating computation to rain-degraded regions on demand. Built on DGO, Sparse Gate Self-Attention (SGSA) captures global dependencies with dynamic sparsity, while a parallel Local Group Convolution Enhancer (LGCE) sharpens edges and textures by reweighting local feature groups. Moreover, a Mixed-scale Frequency Feed-forward Network (MFFN) integrates multi-scale spatial features with complementary frequency cues to restore fine details. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SDGformer achieves state-of-the-art performance on eight benchmark datasets and generalizes well to other image restoration tasks.

records.title: CLP-OPaint: Progressive Dual-Branch Outpainting with Patch Smoothing for Chinese Landscapes
records.abstract: Outpainting Chinese landscape paintings requires simultaneously preserving macroscopic structure and microscopic brushwork, a cross-scale challenge where existing methods often fail. To address this, we propose CLP-OPaint, a novel progressive framework tailored for Chinese landscape painting outpainting. We introduce a Three-Stage Progressive Training Strategy to guide the model from coarse layout to fine texture via curriculum learning. Furthermore, a Dual-Branch Decoder is designed to explicitly decouple structure and texture generation, while a U-Net Patch Smoothing Module (UPSM) eliminates boundary artifacts. Extensive experiments on our curated CLP-9k dataset and public benchmarks demonstrate that CLP-OPaint significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both visual quality and quantitative metrics.

records.title: Facial-VGR: Visual-Grounding Enhanced Reasoning for Facial Emotion Analysis
records.abstract: Facial-emotion analysis (FEA) benefits from pairing expression labels with explicit evidence, yet the recent works leave the fine-grained spatial link between described Action Units (AUs) and their true facial locations under-constrained, which limits reliability. The state-of-the-art results demonstrate that visually verifiable reinforcement learning can markedly enhance the faithfulness of multimodal reasoning in FEA. records.title: UDKF: A Unified Dual-stream Knowledge Fusion Framework for Few-shot Defect Classification
records.abstract: Few-Shot Defect Classification (FSDC) enables efficient defect recognition with limited samples, yet current methods face two key limitations: the absence of a unified framework that effectively integrates Vision-Language Model (VLM) priors with domain-specific defect features, and the lack of a cross-material generalizable architecture under a single training paradigm. To address this, we propose a Unified Dual-stream Knowledge Fusion framework (UDKF). Its core comprises: 1) Collaborative Multivariate Attention (CMA), enhancing defect representation while preserving VLM generalization via multi-aspect attention and cross-modal alignment; 2) Learnable Feature Correlation (LFC), constructing a multi-view feature memory bank and achieving precise defect matching through few-shot fine-tuning; 3) Dynamic Weight Fusion (DWF), adaptively fusing dual-stream outputs with object-aware weighting for robust decision integration. Experiments on three challenging benchmarks demonstrate that UDKF achieves state-of-the-art performance in both defect semantic understanding and cross-material recognition tasks.

records.title: Separate-Layered Alignment Framework for Multi-Modal Manipulation Detecting and Grounding
records.abstract: The rapid rise of generative models has intensified the threat of multi-modal media manipulation. Existing multi-modal manipulation detection methods tend to rely on precise alignment of global semantics, resulting in missing manipulation traces hidden in local details and causing global and local inconsistencies. To address this issue, we propose a Separate-Layered Alignment Framework (SLAF) that incorporates Layer Mask Alignment (LMA) and Dynamic Gating Aggregation Block (DGAB). LMA first employs a lightweight segmentation module to extract foreground and background layer features from image embeddings, and then interacts with text tokens to achieve fine-grained visual–textual alignment. Additionally, DGAB adaptively assigns gating weights to suppress noise and emphasize reliable manipulation cues. Experiments on $\mathrm{DGM}^4$ and $\mathrm{DGM}^4+$ dataset show that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in manipulation detection and grounding tasks, demonstrating its effectiveness in cross-modal semantic reasoning.

records.title: MonoGCC: Monocular 3D Object Detection with Geometric Consistency Constraints
records.abstract: Monocular 3D object detection faces the inherent ill-posed challenge of depth loss during perspective projection. Existing Transformer-based methods often overlook strict geometric consistency between physical dimensions and visual appearances, leading to significant scale drift. To address this, we propose MonoGCC, a novel end-to-end framework integrating Geometric Consistency Constraints. Specifically, we introduce a Dual-Geometry architecture with a parallel height branch, leveraging the intra-class stability of physical height for robust geometric reasoning. Crucially, we design a differentiable Geometric Consistency Module that utilizes pinhole-derived geometric depth to dynamically calibrate regression depth via a self-supervised consistency loss. This mechanism effectively reduces the solution space by enforcing physical projection laws. Experiments on the KITTI benchmark demonstrate that MonoGCC achieves state-of-the-art performance on the Car category using only monocular images, significantly outperforming baselines without relying on extra modalities like LiDAR or CAD models.

records.title: SIM: Intra-Group Member Differentiation via Social Interaction Modeling for Group Re-Identification
records.abstract: Group Re-identification (G-ReID) aims to associate group images containing the same members across different camera views. A critical challenge lies in capturing the dynamic variations in group topology and member composition, which are often non-uniform among individuals. Inspired by principles from social psychology, we observe a phenomenon of member differentiation: core members tend to maintain stable positions within the group, whereas peripheral members are prone to significant displacement or may even fade out from the view. To exploit this prior, we propose a novel Social Interaction Modeling (SIM) method, which conceptualizes each group as a social interaction field to mine discriminative and robust features. Specifically, we construct a Social Interaction Calculation Module (SICM) to quantify member differentiation within these fields. By deconstructing member differentiation into identity and position differentiation, we introduce a Social Prior Attention Mechanism (SPAM) and a Social Layout Variation Module (SLVM) to explicitly model identity differentiation and position differentiation, respectively. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets validate the superiority of SIM over state-of-the-art methods. Our code and supplementary materials are released at https://github.com/VinceKuo13/SIM.

records.title: Task- and Motion-Specific Representations for Unified Micro-Expression Analysis
records.abstract: Micro-expression (ME) analysis aims to spot and recognize subtle facial motions, yet remains challenging due to divergent representation requirements between spotting and recognition, as well as significant macro-motion interference (e.g., macro-expressions and global movements). Existing methods often adopt a shared-representation design for spotting and recognition, making it difficult to capture their different preferences over multi-scale temporal granularities; moreover, they typically lack effective mechanisms to suppress macro-motion noise. To address these issues, we propose a method that learns task- and motion-specific representations for joint spotting and recognition. First, we model micro-expression dynamics with a multi-scale, difference-enhanced temporal representation and allow spotting and recognition to independently emphasize the most suitable temporal scales via task-conditioned weighting. Second, we introduce a macro-motion suppression mechanism that leverages global, low-frequency motion cues to down-weight responses dominated by macro motions in spotting. Experimental results on SAMMLV and CAS(ME)3 show that our method outperforms recent state-of-the-art methods, achieving relative STRS gains of 9.35% and 5.87%, respectively.

records.title: Bridging the Semantic Gap: Unified Cross-Modal Representation and Image-Specific Description for Blind Image Quality Assessment
records.abstract: Blind Image Quality Assessment (BIQA) aims to accurately evaluate image quality without access to reference images. With the emergence of Vision-Language Models (VLMs), several VLM-based BIQA methods have been proposed. However, most of these approaches rely on coarse-grained cross-modal alignment, which hinders effective vision–language correspondence and results in limited performance. In this work, we propose a novel multimodal BIQA framework, termed Uni2Ref-IQA, that addresses these limitations by introducing two key components: the Q-CMA module, which establishes fine-grained cross-modal correspondence through a shared low-rank subspace, and the VDTR module, which leverages hierarchical visual features and region-aware attention to generate image-specific text embeddings for more accurate quality prediction. In addition, we introduce a novel loss function that jointly models the distributional characteristics of subjective quality scores and preserves their relative ranking, combining both objectives of distribution regression and ranking consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our proposed method achieves competitive performance and robust generalization across diverse datasets.

records.title: Fine-Grained Vehicle Localization: A Sensor-Adaptive Contrastive Learning Framework
records.abstract: Fine-grained acoustic lane localization faces significant challenges arising from severe environmental noise and domain shifts caused by heterogeneous sensor deployments. To address this, we propose HySCL (Hybrid Sensor-Invariant Contrastive Learning), a robust framework designed to extract sensor-independent representations. HySCL integrates Energy Guided Input Processing to prioritize informative segments and simulate distortion. Meanwhile, a Sensor-Adaptive Hybrid Backbone is introduced, which employs a dynamic feature calibration mechanism to effectively compensate for the distribution shifts induced by variations in sensor deployment locations and hardware conditions. Furthermore, we introduce a Dual-Path Collaborative Optimization paradigm, synergizing hierarchical inference with contrastive learning to enforce intra-class compactness while stripping sensor-specific bias. Experiments on our newly constructed and open-sourced multi-location roadside acoustic dataset demonstrate that HySCL achieves state-of-the-art performance and superior generalization across disparate sensors. records.title: DREAM: Distribution-aware Re-sampling with Equiangular Alignment Mechanism for Long-Tailed Semi-Supervised Learning
records.abstract: Standard semi-supervised learning (SSL) often fails in real-world settings where data invariably exhibits long-tailed class distributions. This challenging long-tailed semi-supervised learning (LTSSL) problem causes models to develop a severe bias towards majority classes, a situation exacerbated by the unknown distribution of the unlabeled data. Re-sampling is a potent strategy for class imbalance and can serve as a plug-and-play component with other approaches. Its direct application to LTSSL is fraught with difficulties, including inaccurate distribution estimation, inefficient sample utilization, and a tendency to degrade the quality of learned feature representations. To overcome these obstacles, we propose a Distribution-aware Re-sampling with Equiangular Alignment Mechanism (DREAM). First, it employs a normalized weighted geometric mean approximation for robust estimation of the true class distribution. Second, it introduces a joint re-sampling strategy to improve sample utilization based on the estimated distribution. Finally, it incorporates an extended equiangular alignment mechanism, which regularizes the final-layer representations towards an optimal simplex equiangular tight frame geometry, enforcing maximal class separability. Extensive experiments on $4$ benchmarks demonstrate that DREAM achieves state-of-the-art performance. Furthermore, its modular design allows it to function as a plug-and-play component, consistently enhancing various LTSSL algorithms with limited additional overhead.

records.title: Deep Multi-View Clustering with Size-Constrained Embedding and Graph Amendment
records.abstract: Deep multi-view clustering integrates representation learning and structure fusion to exploit complementary information from multiple views. However, existing methods often suffer from collapsed or highly imbalanced cluster assignments due to the absence of explicit size constraints, and they frequently ignore the consistency between learned embeddings and constructed similarity graphs. To address these issues, we propose SCEGA, a size-constrained deep multi-view clustering framework with adaptive neighbors amendment. SCEGA adopts a self-attention–based graph encoder followed by a feed-forward network to learn deep spectral embeddings, which are jointly regularized by a graph reconstruction objective and a differentiable size constraint to control cluster cardinalities. To ensure strict feasibility, the continuous embeddings are further projected onto a size-constrained indicator matrix, which provides cluster-level guidance for refining adaptive neighbors in each view. The refined graphs are iteratively fed back to improve embedding–graph consistency. Extensive experiments on eight benchmark datasets demonstrate that SCEGA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art multi-view clustering methods.

records.title: DRIM-Net: Dual-Representation Inconsistency Modeling for Generalizable Deepfake Detection
records.abstract: The rapid advancement of deepfake technology poses significant challenges to the generalization of detection models. While existing methods often rely on single-representation learning or suboptimal multi-branch fusion, they frequently fail to sufficiently exploit the intrinsic discrepancies between structural and textural representations that are highly indicative of forgeries. To address this limitation, we propose a dual-representation inconsistency modeling framework for generalizable deepfake detection. First, we construct complementary structural and textural perspectives by combining a DINOv3-based transformer branch with a CNN-based branch. Second, we design a dual-representation contrastive module that explicitly models and amplifies structural–textural inconsistencies via local contrastive attention, transforming these inconsistencies into discriminative forgery cues instead of simply aggregating features. Third, we introduce an inconsistency-guided frequency perception (IFP) module that embeds Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) components into the network, enabling end-to-end enhancement of high-frequency responses and improving sensitivity to fine-grained forgery cues. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of detection accuracy and cross-dataset generalization.

records.title: Customized Semantic Target Alignment with Boundary Uncertainty for Source-free Domain Adaptation
records.abstract: Source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) aims to transfer knowledge using only a well-learned source model and unlabeled target data. Recent state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods primarily leverage local neighborhood structures for consistency learning. However, these methods often overlook the risk of neighborhood semantic contamination, where geometric proximity fails to ensure semantic consistency due to domain shift. Consequently, samples near decision boundaries are misled by inter-class neighbors, leading to error propagation through parameter updates. To address this, we propose CSTA, a customized learning framework. We first introduce a novel Boundary Uncertainty Score that integrates prediction uncertainty and inherent cluster structure to adaptively distinguish susceptible boundary samples from stable core samples. Furthermore, we establish a dual-branch alignment mechanism to provide robust supervision for boundary samples and enhance stability for core ones. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate that CSTA achieves SOTA performance, surpassing the representative neighborhood baseline NRC by 4.3%. Moreover, it can be integrated into existing SFDA methods to yield further improvements.

records.title: Beyond Forced Modality Balance: Intrinsic Information Budgets for Multimodal Learning
records.abstract: Multimodal models tend to converge to a dominant-modality solution, where a stronger, faster-converging modality overshadows weaker ones. This modality imbalance causes suboptimal performance. Existing methods attempt to balance different modalities by reweighting gradients or losses. However, they overlook the fact that each modality has a finite information capacity. In this work, we propose IIBalance, a multimodal learning framework that aligns the modality contributions with Intrinsic Information Budgets(IIB). We propose a task-grounded estimator of each modality’s IIB, transforming its capacity into a global prior over modality contributions. Anchored by the highest-budget modality, we design a prototype-based relative alignment mechanism that corrects semantic drift only when weaker modalities deviate from their budgeted potential, rather than forcing imitation. During inference, we propose a probabilistic gating module that integrates the global budgets with sample-level uncertainty to generate calibrated fusion weights. Experiments on three representative benchmarks demonstrate that IIBalance consistently outperforms state-of-the-art balancing methods and achieves better utilization of complementary modality cues.

records.title: Uncertainty-Aware Prompt Learning for Multi-Label Recognition with Incomplete Annotations
records.abstract: Multi-label image recognition typically assumes exhaustive annotations, whereas real-world datasets such as MS-COCO and PASCAL VOC often contain missing or incorrect labels. Treating unlabeled categories as negatives introduces false-negative supervision, leading to degraded performance under partial annotations. To address this issue, we propose Uncertainty-Guided Context Optimization (UncertaintyCoOp), a prompt learning framework that explicitly models prediction uncertainty for partial-label multi-label recognition. UncertaintyCoOp consists of three components: (1) an entropy-confidence hybrid uncertainty estimator capturing epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty, (2) an uncertainty-guided prompt fusion mechanism combining positive, negative, and uncertain prompts, and (3) an uncertainty-aware loss with a momentum-updated teacher to ensure stable optimization under noisy supervision. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate that UncertaintyCoOp achieves competitive performance while consistently enhancing robustness under partial annotations.

records.title: Reliability-Aware Distillation: Mitigating Teacher Overconfidence in Class-Incremental Learning
records.abstract: Knowledge Distillation is widely used to alleviate catastrophic forgetting in Class-Incremental Learning (CIL). However, it suffers from a critical limitation: the teacher model tends to overconfidently misclassify unseen samples as old classes. Unlike existing works that focus on rectifying erroneous responses, we identify that this overconfidence induces issues in distinct dimensions: sample-level unreliability and class-level distortion. To tackle these issues, we propose Reliability-Aware Distillation (RAD), a novel framework that comprises two decoupled yet complementary components specifically tailored to resolve these issues. Reliability-aware Weighting Distillation introduces an unreliability metric to dynamically adjust the distillation weights, effectively suppressing the impact of unreliable sample-level responses. In parallel, Structure-Consistent Distillation preserves the inter-class relational structure by encouraging stable and consistent response patterns across classes. Extensive experiments on multiple CIL benchmarks demonstrate that RAD achieves state-of-the-art performance, yielding an average improvement of 8.1% in Final Average Accuracy. Its plug-and-play property is further demonstrated through seamless integration with several mainstream methods. Our code is available at https://github.com/marksunspace/RAD-2026.git.

records.title: H-SAGE: Holistic Speaker-Aware Guided Experts for MoE-based Multi-Talker ASR
records.abstract: Multi-talker Automatic Speech Recognition (MTASR) faces significant challenges in accurately transcribing overlapping speech, particularly under complex high-overlap conditions. While recent Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) approaches have shown promise, they typically rely on frame-independent routing that leads to temporal myopia, and depend solely on the downstream ASR objective, which results in implicit and ungrounded representation learning. To address these limitations, we propose Holistic Speaker-Aware Guided Experts (H-SAGE) for MoE-based MTASR. Specifically, we introduce a Speaker-Aware Global Encoder to capture long-term dependencies, supervised by an auxiliary Overlap-Aware Loss that explicitly guides the model to discern acoustic states. Furthermore, we design a Holistic Gating Mechanism to arbitrate expert selection by jointly evaluating global context and local details. Experiments on LibriSpeechMix demonstrate that H-SAGE achieves consistent improvements over strong baselines, particularly in complex scenarios, validating that explicit acoustic guidance effectively enhances expert collaboration. Our code can be found at https://github.com/NKU-HLT/H-SAGE.

records.title: Joint Logits Purification and Feature Supplement for CLIP-based Few-shot Learning
records.abstract: While CLIP demonstrates strong potential for few-shot learning (FSL), we identify two inherent limitations stemming from its pretraining objective: (1) inter-class logits confusion caused by cross-modal similarity dominance, which blurs decision boundaries, and (2) underutilization of multi-layer visual features, resulting in a lack of fine-grained discriminative cues. To address these issues, we propose LPFS, a framework that synergistically integrates Logits Purification (LP) and Feature Supplement (FS). The LP module decouples image features into text-preference and vision-preference components, establishing a cleaner basis for modeling, and then refines the logits via lightweight adapters. The FS module aggregates intermediate visual features to supplement the logits with fine-grained information. An adaptive logits fusion strategy dynamically combines both enhancements, significantly boosting CLIP's performance in few-shot classification. Extensive experiments on 11 FSL datasets and 4 out-of-distribution benchmarks demonstrate that LPFS consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance. Our code is available at https://github.com/YvoGao/LPFS.

records.title: Causal Routing and Imbalanced Learning for Robust Multimodal Learning with Missing Modalities
records.abstract: Multimodal Sentiment Analysis (MSA) may encounter uncertain modality missing caused by unavoidable factors such as sensor damage or privacy concerns. Existing incomplete multimodal learning methods tend to focus on data imputation or cross-modal joint representation learning. However, in real-world applications, spurious correlations between incomplete data and labels may lead to a significant degradation in model performance, which is often overlooked. To this end, we propose a novel CAusal Routing and imbalanced Learning (CARL) framework that overcomes spurious correlations in dynamic data missingness scenarios from a causal perspective. Specifically, causal relationships are introduced at the intra-modality expert level to guide the router in selecting causal experts, while bias-variance-aware imbalanced learning is employed at the modality fusion level to adaptively calibrate modality contributions across arbitrary combinations. Extensive experiments on multimodal benchmark datasets demonstrate that our CARL outperforms the state-of-the-art significantly.

records.title: FedBST: Bilateral Self-Training for Unsupervised Federated Classification
records.abstract: Unsupervised federated learning with Vision-Language Models (e.g., CLIP) offers a promising solution for label-free classification, yet its performance often degrades under severe non-IID shifts. A pioneering method, FedCoPL, typically relies on self-training strategies that exclusively prioritize high-confidence predictions for pseudo-labeling. However, this selective approach neglects the information of ambiguous samples (often referred to as ``waist" samples), leading to the underutilization of data and biased decision boundaries. To address this limitation, we propose FedBST, a bilateral self-training framework that effectively exploits both high-confidence and ambiguous data. Specifically, for local optimization, we introduce uncertainty-aware confidence penalization (UACP). UACP targets ambiguous samples by penalizing overconfident predictions to implicitly promote higher uncertainty, thereby preventing erroneous pseudo-labeling. At inference, we employ a visual-text ensemble strategy. This approach aggregates uncertainty-aware local visual prototypes and ensembles them with textual prototypes, achieving lightweight adaptation to local distributions via prototype-based calibration. Experiments demonstrate that FedBST achieves consistent improvements over existing methods with standard federated aggregation protocols.

records.title: MIRAGE: Multimodal Priors Meet Residual Pretraining for Graph-level Anomaly Detection
records.abstract: Graph-level Anomaly Detection (GLAD) is critical for securing multimedia ecosystems modeled as complex graphs. However, existing methods typically face two fundamental limitations: blind feature search due to a semantic vacuum, which necessitates computationally expensive search for optimal receptive fields, and the underutilization of inter-graph structural dependencies due to the independent and identically distributed assumption. To address these challenges, we propose a Multimodal Priors Meet Residual Pretraining for Graph-level Anomaly Detection framework called MIRAGE. First, we introduce a LLM-weighted Residual Pretraining module that leverages Large Language Models to provide a semantic warm start for feature importance, facilitating efficient multi-scale fusion via an asymmetric residual projection that accelerates convergence. Second, we employ a Structural Similarity Finetuning strategy that refines decision boundaries by exploiting latent inter-graph manifold structures through confidence-aware neighbor aggregation. Extensive experiments on four real-world datasets demonstrate that MIRAGE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in detection accuracy while reducing training time by over 40%.

records.title: Weakly Supervised Infrared Small Target Recognition Based on Causal Representation Learning
records.abstract: While existing infrared small target detection methods have achieved considerable progress in localization, the classification of infrared small targets remains largely unexplored, leaving a critical gap between detection and actionable recognition in real-world infrared scenarios. To bridge this gap, we present a weakly supervised infrared small target recognition framework based on causal representation learning, which, to our knowledge, represents the first systematic study on infrared small target classification. The framework constructs independent foreground and background branches to suppress clutter interference while focusing on discriminative target regions. To further eliminate non-causal feature interference, we introduce a sequential causal feature selection module operating across both spatial and channel dimensions. Furthermore, we provide category-level annotations for three widely-used infrared small target benchmarks, establishing the first classification-oriented evaluation protocol for this task. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and generalization capability of the proposed method under complex background conditions.

records.title: Occlusion-Aware Panoptic Segmentation with Joint Position Embedding and Occlusion-Level Attention
records.abstract: Panoptic segmentation in complex scenes remains challenging because of occlusions, yet modern approaches often neglect occlusion modelling. In this paper, we propose Position Embedding Modulation with Occlusion-Level Attention (PEMOLA), a novel occlusion-aware module that can be seamlessly integrated into transformer-based panoptic segmentation. To obtain occlusion cues, we train an occlusion classifier on the COCO-OLAC dataset. The classifier derives the occlusion-level attention, which serves as spatial guidance, while the occlusion labels are encoded into a learnable embedding to produce channel-wise weights. Through joint modulation, PEMOLA elegantly introduces the occlusion priors into the position embedding, thereby improving the occlusion modelling. We further annotate the Cityscapes dataset with occlusion levels, termed Cityscapes Occlusion Labels for All Computer Vision Tasks (Cityscapes-OLAC), following the same labelling protocol as COCO-OLAC, to evaluate the cross-dataset generalisation ability of PEMOLA. Extensive experiments on COCO-OLAC and Cityscapes-OLAC demonstrate that PEMOLA consistently improves panoptic segmentation quality while introducing minimal computational overhead. These results highlight the importance of occlusion modelling, where incorporating occlusion-level attention helps deliver robust panoptic segmentation under occlusion.

records.title: Zero-shot Concept Bottleneck Models
records.abstract: Concept bottleneck models (CBMs) are inherently interpretable and intervenable neural network models, which explain their final class label prediction via intermediate predictions of high-level semantic concepts. However, they require target task training to learn input-to-concept and concept-to-class mappings, which necessitates collecting target datasets and significant training resources. In this paper, we present zero-shot concept bottleneck models (Z-CBMs), which predict concepts and labels in a fully zero-shot manner without additional training of neural networks. Z-CBMs leverage a large-scale concept bank, comprising millions of vocabulary extracted from the web, to describe diverse inputs across various domains. For the input-to-concept mapping, we introduce concept retrieval, which dynamically identifies input-related concepts through cross-modal search within the concept bank. In the concept-to-class inference, we apply concept regression to select essential concepts from the retrieved concepts by sparse linear regression. Experiments demonstrate that our Z-CBMs provide interpretable and intervenable concepts without any additional training.

records.title: Dynamic Visual-semantic Alignment for Zero-shot Learning with Ambiguous Labels
records.abstract: Zero-shot learning (ZSL) aims to recognize unseen classes without visual instances. However, existing methods usually assume clean labels, overlooking real-world label noise and ambiguity, which degrades performance. To bridge this gap, we propose the Dynamic Visual-semantic Alignment (DVSA), a robust ZSL framework for learning from ambiguous labels. DVSA uses a bidirectional visual–semantic alignment module with attention to mutually calibrate visual features and attribute prototypes, and a contrastive optimization grounded in Mutual Information (MI) at the attribute level to strengthen discriminative, semantically consistent attributes. In addition, a dynamic label disambiguation mechanism iteratively corrects noisy supervision while preserving semantic consistency, narrowing the instance-label gap, and improving generalization. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks verify that DVSA achieves stronger performance under ambiguous supervision.

records.title: Hyperspherical Incomplete Multi-View Clustering with Spherical Sliced-Wasserstein Coherence
records.abstract: Incomplete multi-view clustering (IMVC) aims to discover shared cluster structure from partially observed multi-view data. Most deep IMVC models adopt Euclidean latent spaces with Gaussian priors and Gaussian-based fusion, which is mismatched to directional representations and tends to become overconfident under missing or imbalanced views. We propose Hyperspherical Incomplete Multi-View Clustering (HIMVC), a variational IMVC framework with a shared hyperspherical latent space. HIMVC places a von Mises–Fisher (vMF) mixture prior to model shared cluster structure and lets each view-specific encoder output a vMF posterior. A vMF Product-of-Experts aggregates the available posteriors into a joint latent distribution, where concentration parameters serve as reliability indicators and enable robust fusion under missing views. To promote cross-view agreement while preserving spherical geometry, we introduce a spherical sliced-Wasserstein coherence scheme that aligns the aggregated posterior with view-specific posteriors along geodesic optimal transport on the sphere. This design yields latent representations that are clustering-friendly and coherent across incomplete views. Extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets demonstrate that HIMVC consistently achieves robust and competitive clustering performance compared with state-of-the-art IMVC approaches.

records.title: Collaborative Geometry-Semantic Learning: An Online Multi-View Hyper-Clustering Framework for Long-Tailed Recognition
records.abstract: Long-tailed recognition remains a fundamental challenge due to severe class imbalance, which frequently causes feature space collapse for minority classes. Existing solutions either re-balance the loss or decouple the learning process, yet they often fail to construct a feature space that is both geometrically uniform and semantically discriminative. In this paper, we propose CoLT (Collaborative Learning for Long-Tailed Recognition), a unified framework that first integrates Online Multi-View Hyper-Clustering with Supervised Semantic Guidance. Specifically, we enforce an equipartition constraint to reshape the feature space and prevent tail collapse, while supervised signals act as semantic anchors to rectify clustering bias. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CoLT achieves competitive performance across multiple benchmarks, including CIFAR-100-LT and ImageNet-LT. The source code is available at https://github.com/xtliu07/CoLT-ICME2026.

records.title: SynergyReID: Bridging Modalities via Semantic Prototypes and Consistency Priors for Multi-Modal Object Re-Identification
records.abstract: Multi-modal object Re-Identification (ReID) aims to retrieve objects by leveraging complementary cues from RGB, Near-Infrared (NIR) and Thermal Infrared (TIR) images. However, existing methods aggregate visual tokens indiscriminately, allowing background clutter and modality noise to obscure identity-relevant cues. To address this issue, we propose SynergyReID, which performs text-guided token purification and consistency-prior complementary fusion for trustworthy multi-modal object ReID. Specifically, we first propose a Semantic Prototype-Guided Cross-Modal Token Selection (SPCTS) to construct text-derived semantic prototypes as anchors and select identity-relevant visual tokens via collaborative scoring across intra-modal, cross-modal and textual cues. Afterwards, we propose a Consistency-Prior Driven Complementary Fusion (CPDCF) to jointly emphasize cross-modal consensus and preserve modality-specific salient details. With these two modules, our framework first purifies intra-modal features and then adaptively fuses complementary information, yielding more robust multi-modal representations under complex scenarios. Extensive experiments on three multi-modal object ReID benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of our proposed method. The code will be released at https://github.com/maxingan2412/ICME2026-SynergyReID.

records.title: Region-adaptive Regularization with Hierarchical Prompts for Few-shot OOD Detection
records.abstract: Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection is challenging in intelligent diagnosis of diseases based on medical images, especially in few-shot scenarios where the scarcity of labeled samples makes the task even more difficult. Recently developed methods make use of local features from image regions for effective few-shot OOD detection, but still fail to fully utilize local image regions. Here, we propose a novel framework based on Region-Adaptive regularization with Hierarchical Prompts (RAHP), tailored for medical few-shot OOD detection. The framework uses an adaptive adjustment mechanism for the CLIP similarity threshold to categorize image regions into three types, where a unique regularization is employed for each type. To better align CLIP text embeddings with global and local visual features, we propose hierarchical prompts that incorporate both global and local prompts, enabling the extraction of text embeddings at different granularities. Experiments on two medical OOD benchmarks demonstrate the superiority of our RAHP, achieving new SOTA performance. The code is available via https://github.com/prion502/RAHP.

records.title: Incremental Prototype-Guided Frequency-Aware Anomaly Synthesis for Multi-Class Industrial Anomaly Detection
records.abstract: Unified multi-class anomaly detection often overfits when modeling feature distributions across categories. Recent work introduces synthesized anomalies, but existing methods mainly operate in feature space with texture-dependent priors and fixed noise, producing redundant samples that poorly match real defects. We propose a frequency-aware adaptive anomaly synthesis (FaaS) strategy with incremental prototype guidance for unified multi-class anomaly detection. FaaS generates feature-level anomalies without explicit spatial texture cues via three components: incremental prototype adaptation (IPA), high-frequency perception resampling (FPR), and a multiscale heterogeneous reconstruction (MHR) subnet. IPA progressively refines class prototypes and tightens intra-class distributions through local feature-bias alignment. FPR adapts the scale and intensity of synthesized anomalies according to high-frequency discrepancies between inputs and prototypes. MHR further sharpens reconstruction-based decision boundaries across scales and orientations. Experiments on four public industrial benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art performance.

records.title: Semantic–Emotional Resonance Embedding: A Semi-Supervised Paradigm for Cross-Lingual Speech Emotion Recognition
records.abstract: Cross-lingual Speech Emotion Recognition (CLSER) aims to identify emotional states in unseen languages. However, existing methods heavily rely on semantic synchrony of complete labels and static feature stability, hindering low-resource languages from reaching high-resource performance. To address this, we propose a semi-supervised framework based on Semantic–Emotional Resonance Embedding (SERE), a cross-lingual dynamic feature paradigm that requires neither target language labels nor translation alignment. Specifically, SERE constructs an emotion-semantic structure using a small number of labeled samples. It learns human emotional experiences through an Instantaneous Resonance Field (IRF), enabling unlabeled samples to self-organize into this structure. This achieves semi-supervised semantic guidance and structural discovery. Additionally, we design a Triple-Resonance Interaction Chain (TRIC) loss to enable the model to reinforce the interaction and embedding capabilities between labeled and unlabeled samples during emotional highlights. Extensive experiments across multiple languages demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, requiring only 5-shot labeling in the source language.

records.title: CANet:Cross-Modal Anchor Network for Multimodal Industrial Anomaly Detection
records.abstract: Multimodal anomaly detection that jointly exploits RGB appearance and 3D geometry is crucial for robust industrial inspection. The key difficulty lies in modeling the joint distribution of normal appearance and shape: existing methods either maintain large, separate memory banks for each modality or rely on shallow feature concatenation, both of which fail to enforce cross-modal consistency and are vulnerable to contextual anomalies. We propose CANet, a memory-bank-free Cross-Modal Anchor Network that represents multimodal normality via a compact set of learnable cross-modal anchors. A Cross-Modal Anchor Generator (CAG) refines a small set of anchor tokens by attending to RGB and 3D features extracted by a shared frozen ViT encoder, yielding a sample-specific set of cross-modal anchors that each encode a valid "appearance-geometry" concept. Two lightweight decoders then perform Anchor-Guided Reconstruction (AGR) for RGB and 3D respectively: features are reconstructed as convex combinations of anchors via cross-attention, which explicitly constrains reconstructions to the learned normal subspace. To regularize the anchor space, we introduce an Anchor Usage Entropy (AUE) term that encourages balanced anchor utilization and prevents representational collapse, and a Cross-Modal Assignment Consistency loss that aligns anchor assignments between modalities. CANet is trained end-to-end on normal data only. Extensive experiments on two challenging benchmarks, MVTec 3D-AD and Eyecandies, show that CANet establishes new state-of-the-art performance in both image-level detection and pixel-level localization while being over 50x faster and markedly more memory-efficient than memory-bank baselines.

records.title: ADORE: Adversarial Diverse Representation for Robust Few-Shot Anomaly Detection
records.abstract: Few-shot anomaly detection (FSAD) for industrial inspection is challenging due to the scarcity of normal samples and the large intra-class variation of normal appearances. Reconstruction-based FSAD methods often suffer from a prototype collapse phenomenon in low-data regimes: the model tends to reconstruct an averaged normal pattern, resulting in over-smoothed reconstructions and false alarms on fine-grained normal structures. Meanwhile, overly expressive decoders may memorize identity mappings and undesirably reconstruct anomalies. We propose ADORE, a reconstruction framework that learns a set of diverse normal prototypes and leverages them as a prior to guide reconstruction. Specifically, ADORE (i) learns mutually diverse prototypes with a clustering-and-repulsion objective and a coverage regularizer to avoid inactive prototypes; (ii) introduces an inverse-mapping generalization module to reduce trivial copy behavior; and (iii) applies a prototype-similarity prior to modulate reconstruction, encouraging faithful reconstruction for normal-like regions while suppressing anomalous ones. Experiments on MVTec-AD, VisA, and Real-IAD demonstrate that ADORE improves both image-level detection and pixel-level localization under 1-shot and 2-shot settings, achieving state-of-the-art performance with sharper reconstructions and fewer false positives.

records.title: PROSE: Prototype-Guided Semantic Experts for Weakly-Paired IHC Stain Translation
records.abstract: Weakly-paired stain translation (H&E to IHC) is fundamentally challenged by spatial misalignment between adjacent tissue sections, which often trigger optimization instability and structural hallucinations. To address these issues, we introduce PROSE, a robust framework that reformulates the translation task as a projection onto learnable semantic prototypes rather than relying on rigid instance matching. Specifically, we devise an Uncertainty-Gated Expert Routing mechanism to filter misalignment noise via entropy-based gating and dynamically select reliable prototypes. This is coupled with a Manifold Projection that aligns generated representations with these prototypes to ensure pathological consistency. Furthermore, we incorporate Dispersive Regularization to prevent feature collapse and maintain discriminative staining gradations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PROSE significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving superior fidelity in both tissue morphology and staining details.

records.title: Cascade-Free Mandarin Visual Speech Recognition via Semantic-Guided Cross-Representation Alignment
records.abstract: Chinese mandarin visual speech recognition(VSR) is a task that has advanced in recent years, yet still lags behind the performance on non-tonal languages such as English. One primary challenge arises from the tonal nature of Mandarin, which limits the effectiveness of conventional sequence-to-sequence modeling approaches. To alleviate this issue, existing Chinese VSR systems commonly incorporate intermediate representations, most notably pinyin, within cascade architectures to enhance recognition accuracy. While beneficial, in these cascaded designs, the subsequent stage during inference depends on the output of the preceding stage, leading to error accumulation and increased inference latency. To address these limitations, we propose a cascade-free architecture based on multitask learning that jointly integrates multiple intermediate representations, including phoneme and viseme, to better exploit contextual information. The proposed semantic-guided local contrastive loss temporally aligns the features, enabling on-demand activation during inference, thereby providing a trade-off between inference efficiency and performance while mitigating error accumulation caused by projection and re-embedding. Experiments conducted on publicly available datasets demonstrate that our method achieves superior recognition performance.

records.title: Self-Supervised Learning Using Contrastive and Masking Representation Fusion for EEG Visual Classification
records.abstract: EEG-based visual decoding has garnered considerable attention in brain-computer interfaces (BCIs). While many studies have concentrated on utilizing deep learning models, a significant gap remains in the development of effective algorithms for EEG visual decoding. In this study, we introduce self-supervised pre-training methods for EEG visual classification by implementing two pre-training tasks: contrastive learning with data augmentation and masked signal modeling, utilizing a hybrid EEG model and a transformer model as pre-training encoders. During the fine-tuning phase for downstream tasks, we combined features from the two self-supervised tasks through a feature fusion module, which were then processed by a multilayer perceptron (MLP) for classification. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art classification performance on four classification tasks across three datasets. Ablation experiments confirmed that self-supervised learning significantly improved performance in the four classification tasks by 3.62%, 5.08%, 3.20%, and an impressive 18.00%.

records.title: Time- and Frequency-Domain Target Recognition in Diverse Acoustic Environments
records.abstract: Achieving high-precision Acoustic Target Recognition (ATR) for different acoustic media, such as air and water, remains a fundamental challenge due to distinct propagation characteristics and noise interference. We propose DAMFN, a novel Dynamic Attention-based Multi-representations Fusion Network that jointly learns from raw waveforms (in the time domain) and spectrograms (in the frequency domain) via a cross-domain-aware strategy. DAMFN integrates specific representation and soft Mixture-of-Experts encoders to capture unique and shared features from the time and frequency domains. A hierarchical fusion mechanism combining cross-domain attention and gated fusion further reduces redundancy while enhancing task-relevant information. Experiments on diverse datasets, including environmental sounds (ESC-10/50) and underwater recordings (Watkins-4, ShipsEar), demonstrate that DAMFN achieves competitive performance with only 2.48M parameters, while maintaining robustness under low signal-to-noise ratio levels (e.g., -5 dB). Ablation studies confirm the contribution of each component, validating DAMFN as an effective solution for ATR in multiple acoustic scenarios.

records.title: PRGCD: Probabilistic Representation Learning for Generalized Category Discovery
records.abstract: Generalized Category Discovery (GCD) aims to classify unlabeled images from both known and novel categories, leveraging partially labeled data. Existing methods predominantly rely on deterministic contrastive learning, which represents each sample as a single point embedding and measures similarity through point-to-point distances. We argue that this paradigm is inherently limited, as it provides only one degree of freedom for optimization. In this paper, we propose PRGCD, a novel framework that models each sample as a Gaussian distribution parameterized by mean and variance. We adopt the 2-Wasserstein distance for distribution-level similarity, which naturally decomposes into location and spread terms, enabling dual consistency enforcement. Based on this formulation, we design Wasserstein Unsupervised Contrastive (WUC) loss and Wasserstein Supervised Contrastive (WSC) loss for representation learning, along with a distribution calibration loss to prevent posterior collapse. Extensive experiments on six benchmarks demonstrate that PRGCD achieves state-of-the-art performance. The code will be open-sourced upon acceptance.

records.title: FlowContrast: Few-Shot Multimedia Traffic Representation Learning in LEO Satellite Networks
records.abstract: Although the adoption of encryption protocols is essential for ensuring data privacy, it introduces significant challenges for traffic classification on the Internet, particularly in low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks such as Starlink, where fluctuating RTT, burst jitter, and reordering frequently distort flow patterns. Meanwhile, modern Internet traffic is dominated by multimedia applications (video streaming, social media, audio services), whose burst structures and temporal dynamics differ significantly from conventional terrestrial flows. To address encrypted traffic classification, prior deep learning approaches rely on large labeled datasets and are primarily tailored for terrestrial networks, limiting their generalizability under satellite-specific dynamics. To close this gap, we propose FlowContrast, a framework that combines self-supervised contrastive pre-training with few-shot learning, tailored for satellite multimedia traffic. FlowContrast applies domain-aware augmentations directly on raw flows, simulating satellite-induced perturbations before flow-to-image conversion, preserving temporal dependencies and packet-level semantics. Using massive unlabeled traffic, FlowContrast learns transferable representations adapted with minimal labeled samples. We also release SMA40, the first publicly available dataset of Starlink multimedia applications traffic. Experiments on multiple benchmarks show FlowContrast consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving superior cross-domain generalization with reduced label dependency. The SMA40 dataset will be released to facilitate future research.

records.title: WaveKD: A Unified Frequency-Aware Distillation Framework for SAR Ship Recognition
records.abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks have achieved remarkable progress in ship recognition from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery, yet they suffer from two limitations: (1) high computational and memory costs on resource-constrained platforms, and (2) compact models' inability to capture high-frequency details critical for fine-grained recognition. To address these limitations, we propose WaveKD, a frequency-aware knowledge distillation framework. The framework is built upon the proposed Centered Semantic Similarity (CSS), a principled distance metric that is invariant to scalar affine and orthogonal transformations, which provides a robust foundation for teacher-student alignment. Based on this, the discrete wavelet transform decomposes features into multiple frequency bands, and high-frequency semantics are distilled through two modules: Frequency Semantic Alignment (FSA) for instance-level transfer and Class Attention Transfer (CAT) for preserving class-specific discriminative textures. Extensive experiments on several benchmarks demonstrate that WaveKD consistently outperforms state-of-the-art distillation methods in both detection and classification tasks across diverse backbones.

records.title: Define-to-Detect: Towards Robust and Generalizable Text-Guided Open-World VAD
records.abstract: Traditional video anomaly detection (VAD) under closed-set settings fails to handle variable anomalies (anomaly expansion and anomaly drift) in real-world scenarios. To address these issues, open-world VAD has emerged as a new task, but existing methods still struggle with inadequate dynamic anomaly modeling, limited scene generalization, and imprecise temporal anomaly localization. Therefore, we propose Define-to-Detect (D2D), a text-guided anomaly detection framework with strong generalization and localization capabilities. Firstly, we introduce dynamic anomaly definition sampling, explicitly modeling diverse anomaly definitions and constructing a robust mapping from visual content and dynamic anomaly definitions to anomaly scores. Secondly, with the support of text-conditioned settings, we leverage pretraining on multiple large-scale external temporal localization datasets to enhance generalization and localization capabilities. Finally, we design a text-guided uncertainty-aware loss to maintain robust temporal localization under dynamic anomalies. Extensive cross-domain experiments on four datasets demonstrate that D2D achieves state-of-the-art performance in open-world settings.

records.title: LGSSR: Language-Grounded Spatial State Representation for Vision and Language Navigation
records.abstract: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) requires agents to travel in complex 3D scenes following the linguistic instructions. Prevailing VLN approaches primarily rely on 2D observations while overlooking the effect of 3D environment priors given the complex spatial layouts and nontrivial instruction-to-action transformations. To this end, we introduce a Language-Grounded Spatial State Representation (LGSSR), which aggregates 3D state features through neural rendering from the Language-Grounded Feature Field (LG-FF). Specifically, a 3D field encoder is pre-trained in two stages to generate dense spatial representations for the LG-FF. The pre-training process further enhances the spatial representation capabilities of LG-FF through image rendering and enables LG-FF with multi-granularity language grounding attributes via cross-modal contrastive learning. Moreover, we design an Interlaced Feature Aggregation Module (IFAM), which interactively fuses 2D features and 3D LGSSR within the existing navigation framework. Extensive experiments on the R2R and R2R-CE benchmarks demonstrate the competitive performance of our method.

records.title: FSA-PAD: Few-Shot Alignment for Face Presentation Attack Detection on Unseen Cameras
records.abstract: In recent years, existing methods for face presentation attack detection (PAD) often struggle to adapt to diverse scenarios, particularly when samples from different cameras significantly differ from training data in terms of image quality and color distribution. To address these limitations and enhance model adaptability, we propose a novel few-shot alignment-based detection method using meta-learning. Unlike traditional fine-tuning, our approach aligns the source domain model for different cameras by centralizing the features of both the source and target domains within the feature spaces of image quality, texture classification, and depth maps. This alignment mechanism is crucial for overcoming challenges posed by varying image qualities and camera-specific features, ensuring better generalization to unseen cameras. Extensive experimental analysis on four public face spoofing databases (Idiap Replay-Attack, CASIA-MFSD, OULU-NPU, and MSU-MFSD) demonstrates that our proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art techniques, offering promising performance across various camera types.

records.title: MinEMIL: Minority-aware MIL for Fine-Grained Whole Slide Image Classification
records.abstract: Traditional lymph node metastasis classification methods primarily focus on binary classification and fail to meet the clinical demand for fine-grained four-class categorization, including Negative, Isolated Tumor Cells (ITC), Micro-metastasis, and Macro-metastasis. Minority lesion types, such as ITC and micro-metastasis, occupy only small regions within whole-slide images, resulting in insufficient discriminative features. Consequently, existing approaches tend to be biased toward majority classes during classification. To address this challenge, we propose a novel framework, termed MinEMIL, for robust four-class WSI classification. MinEMIL integrates a prompt–guided prototype generator, an information-guided feature filtering mechanism, and a teacher–student training strategy. By filtering out low-informativeness redundant features while synthesizing prototype features, MinEMIL effectively alleviates the feature sparsity issue of minority classes. Furthermore, we introduce a fully annotated four-class lymph node metastasis dataset, NIMM, and conduct extensive evaluations on both NIMM and the public CAMELYON17 dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that MinEMIL significantly outperforms baseline methods, with particularly pronounced improvements in recognizing ITC and micro-metastasis lesions.

records.title: Learning Resolution-Invariant Representations for Multi-Resolution Fine-Grained Image Classification
records.abstract: Fine-grained image classification relies on subtle visual details that are easily degraded by resolution changes. Existing fine-grained image classification methods assume a fixed input resolution, while real-world scenarios produce diverse resolutions due to varying sensors or viewing conditions. To address this gap, we tackle the more practical problem of multi-resolution fine-grained image classification. We introduce an end-to-end framework that processes multi-resolution images. In this work, we train a single backbone across multiple resolutions through progressive canonical-resolution alignment. We further introduce mixed-resolution patch training to enhance robustness to resolution variations. Experiments on three benchmarks show that our method enables a single unified model to achieve superior performance across all resolutions with fewer parameters.

records.title: Structured Error-Aware Self-Refinement for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Semantic Segmentation
records.abstract: Cross-domain few-shot semantic segmentation typically relies on binary foreground-background prototypes, which suffer from limited expressiveness, especially under significant domain shifts. To address this, we propose a two-stage selfcalibration framework based on structured error decomposition that enables more robust cross-domain prototype learning. The framework leverages a divided prototype representation and performs self-adaptive prototype calibration on the support side via error decomposition, reconstructing global prototypes with improved cross-domain robustness. On the query side, calibrations are applied to uncertain regions. Through the cooperative interaction between the support and query sides, the method forms a losed-loop adaptive prototype optimization process,enhancing both global representation and the capability to discriminate uncertain regions. Extensive experiments on four cross-domain benchmarks (DeepGlobe, ISIC, Chest X-ray, and FSS-1000) show that our method consistently outperforms the baseline in both 1-shot and 5-shot settings.

records.title: Reliable Pseudo-label Enhanced Contrastive Incomplete Multi-View Clustering with Latent Graph
records.abstract: Incomplete Multi-View Clustering(IMVC) focuses on the challenge of leveraging information from multiple data sources or perspectives with the missing data and has attracted significant attention. However, existing methods do not make full use of the learned pseudo-labels, divide clustering and imputation into two separate stages, which result in the suboptimal clustering results. To overcome these challenges, we propose a novel Reliable Pseudo-label Enhanced Contrastive Incomplete Multi-View Clustering with Latent Graph (PECIMVC) framework. Specifically, it firstly captures the embedded features of each view via the view-specific deep autoencoders. Then, the clustering pseudo-labels with high-confidence are incorporated to guide the latent graph refinement, contrastive learning process and the imputation of missing data. At the end of each step, the clustering probability will be updated based on the optimized sample features and used for the next optimization. Experimental results on several representative datasets demonstrate that PECIMVC outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of clustering accuracy and robustness.
