records.title: Prototype-guided and Attention-enhanced Multi-instance Learning for Whole Slide Image Classification
records.abstract: Whole-slide image (WSI) classification is one of the most critical research areas in pathological diagnosis, facing major challenges including high computational costs due to gigapixel resolution and classification difficulties caused by spurious correlations. Multi-instance learning (MIL) is a popular framework for WSI classification, treating each WSI as a bag. Existing methods typically employ global prototype extraction or global bag graph construction to address these issues but may introduce noisy information. To tackle this, we propose the prototype-guided and attention-enhanced multi-instance learning (ProtoMIL) framework, featuring two core modules. The clustering-based prototype construction (CBPC) module mines informative hidden features and generates customized instance prototypes through feature scaling. The cross-attention enhancement (CAE) module fuses prototypes with global bag information to produce more discriminative bag representations. Additionally, CBPC and CAE form a plug-and-play module. All hyperparameters and configuration settings remain consistent with those of the baseline methods, eliminating the need for any additional modifications or recalibrations. Experimental evaluations on CAM16, BRACS and HER2 datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly improves the performance of existing MIL algorithms.

records.title: CAVIN: Concept-Aware View Imputation Network for Incomplete Multi-View Clustering
records.abstract: Incomplete multi-view clustering suffers from missing views. Prior methods rely on a universal transformation network, ignoring semantic diversity and causing confused, imprecise representations. Inspired by human cognitive completion, we design the Concept-Aware View Imputation Network (CAVIN), which discovers concepts in a coarse-to-fine manner and learns concept-specific transformation networks to capture cross-view relations per semantic category. An adaptive concept-matching mechanism aligns incomplete samples to the right concept, enabling consistent imputation under high missing rates. Experiments on four benchmarks show CAVIN consistently surpasses state-of-the-art methods.

records.title: Disentangling Hardness from Noise: An Uncertainty-Driven Model-Agnostic Framework for Long-Tailed Remote Sensing Classification
records.abstract: Long-Tailed distributions are pervasive in remote sensing due to the inherently imbalanced occurrence of grounded objects. However, a critical challenge remains largely overlooked, i.e., disentangling hard tail data samples from noisy ambiguous ones. Conventional methods often indiscriminately emphasize all low-confidence samples, leading to overfitting on noisy data. To bridge this gap, building upon Evidential Deep Learning, we propose a model-agnostic uncertainty-aware framework termed DUAL, which dynamically disentangles prediction uncertainty into Epistemic Uncertainty (EU) and Aleatoric Uncertainty (AU). Specifically, we introduce EU as an indicator of sample scarcity to guide a reweighting strategy for hard-to-learn tail samples, while leveraging AU to quantify data ambiguity, employing an adaptive label smoothing mechanism to suppress the impact of noise. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets across various backbones demonstrate the effectiveness and generalization of our framework, surpassing strong baselines such as TGN and SADE. Ablation studies provide further insights into the crucial choices of our design. Our code is publicly open at Github.

records.title: Light Through Shadow: Single-Stage Shadow Removal via Luminance-Color Embedding
records.abstract: Shadows induce coupled degradations in illumination, color, and texture, making single-image shadow removal highly ambiguous. Existing methods typically rely on explicit masks or multi-stage pipelines, yet shadows are essentially an illumination problem where lighting variations provide natural cues for localization. We propose LithSSR, a single-stage, mask-free framework that uses intrinsic luminance information to detect illumination discrepancies without explicit boundary prediction. Luminance and color priors are embedded into the encoder through spatial and channel-wise modulation. The luminance prior guides implicit shadow localization without mask supervision, after which the color prior restores color constancy and fine textures under luminance guidance. Extensive experiments on SRD, ISTD, and ISTD+ benchmarks demonstrate that LithSSR achieves state-of-the-art performance in both quantitative metrics and visual quality while maintaining a compact single-stage design.

records.title: AMT-ReID: Content-Adaptive Fusion and Relation Mining for Asymmetric Vehicle Re-identification
records.abstract: Most existing vehicle re-identification methods rely solely on single-image visual features, often failing to capture fine-grained semantic details crucial for distinguishing similar vehicles. Thus, exploiting textual descriptions for complementary semantic guidance is necessary. In this paper, we propose AMT-ReID, a Transformer-based framework that bridges modality gaps. It employs Content-Adaptive Gated Fusion to dynamically incorporate textual semantics into visual representations. Furthermore, we introduce Asymmetric Feature Alignment to adapt unimodal gallery features to the multimodal space, enabling robust asymmetric retrieval. Extensive experiments demonstrate our method's superiority. Particularly, on the challenging VeRi-776 dataset, AMT-ReID achieves 92.1\% mAP, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art methods.

records.title: Enhancing Synergy of Features and Logits: A Joint Fine-Tuning for Few-Shot CLIP Alignment
records.abstract: Leveraging its strong transferability and generalization performance, CLIP has become a foundation for many parameter fine-tuning approaches in few-shot classification. However, many of these fine-tuning approaches typically only modify the shallow parts of the model and cannot effectively address the semantic inconsistency between image features and text prototypes, leading to inter-class confusion in few-shot regimes. To address this issue, we propose ESFL-CLIP (Enhancing Synergy of Features and Logits for CLIP), a parameter-efficient joint fine-tuning alignment framework. ESFL-CLIP operates with frozen semantic anchors and conducts unified optimization under dual-head supervision. Furthermore, ESFL-CLIP enforces consistency between the two prediction heads via InfoNCE regularization in the logit space, while simultaneously aligning features with their corresponding prototypes to reshape the feature geometry. This prototype-aware feature alignment alleviates instability caused by feature–prototype mismatch. Experimental results show that ESFL-CLIP significantly improves classification performance and effectively alleviates predictive ambiguity.

records.title: Prototype-Graph Synergistic Enhancement Network for Zero-Shot Sketch-Based Image Retrieval
records.abstract: Although Zero-Shot Sketch-Based Image Retrieval (ZS-SBIR) based on prompt learning have made progress, they still face the challenges of large visual intra-class variance and insufficient fine-grained alignment between modalities. To this end, we propose a Prototype-Graph Synergistic Enhancement Network, called PGSEN. Specifically, we first propose the Prototype-Guided Feature Enhancer (PGFE), which dynamically learns category-specific visual prototypes through momentum update mechanism, enhancing the visual features and reducing intra-class variance. Next, we design the Graph Attention Fusion Module (GAFM), which constructs visual and text features as graph nodes, dynamically builds a sparse adjacency matrix based on semantic similarity, and uses graph attention networks to promote cross-modal information propagation, achieving deeper inter-modal alignment. Finally, extensive experiments are conducted on three benchmark datasets. The experimental results demonstrate that compared with the existing ZS-SBIR methods, our proposed PGSEN has superior performance.

records.title: From Model Patterns to Abstract Semantics in Compositional Zero-Shot Learning
records.abstract: Compositional Zero Shot Learning aims to recognize unseen compositions by recombining learned primitives. Recent methods rely on vision language models and attempt to explicitly model contextual variations of primitives through multiple representations. However, such approaches are limited by fixed variant capacity and competition between abstract and concrete semantics. In this work, we present a new perspective that views primitive variations as the context-driven activation of concrete visual cues rather than independent entities. Based on it, we propose CLEAR, a CLoze-style rEAsoning-based Re-ranking framework inspired by human perceptual processes. CLEAR extracts conditional variants from the primitive candidate set in a coarse-to-fine manner, performs cloze-style reasoning to infer high-level semantics, and re-ranks predictions to correct biases toward salient concrete primitives. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CLEAR consistently improves the Base Model and outperforms state-of-the-art methods on the challenging C-GQA and MIT-States datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/buptLwz/CLEAR.

records.title: HiCAE: A Hierarchical Cross-Attention Expert Framework for Multimodal Retinal Disease Classification
records.abstract: Integrating multiple imaging modalities, such as Color Fundus Photography (CFP) and Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT), enables exploitation of complementary information for retinal disease diagnosis. Although Vision Transformer (ViT) has been widely applied in medical image analysis, existing ViT-based multimodal methods struggle with fine-grained intra-modality feature extraction and effective cross-modal fusion, limiting their ability to capture discriminative lesion features and improve diagnostic accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose a Hierarchical Cross-Attention Expert framework (HiCAE) for multimodal retinal disease classification. HiCAE introduces a Hierarchical Multi-Level Token Fusion (HMLTF) module to enhance single-modality semantic representations by leveraging multi-depth ViT tokens, and a Modality-Aware Adaptive Expert Routing (MAAER) module to enable dynamic cross-modal feature interaction and fusion. Extensive experiments demonstrate that HiCAE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUROC) improvements of 1.37%–4.25% across three multimodal retinal datasets. The source code is available at GitHub https://github.com/zycl2001/HiCAE.

records.title: Content-Adaptive Multiresolution Grids for Neural Image Representation
records.abstract: Multiresolution hash encoding enables fast fitting of neural implicit representations but allocates uniform storage regardless of local signal complexity. We propose Content-Adaptive Sparse Grids (AGRID), which replace hash tables with explicit sparse grids that allocate vertices based on image gradient magnitude. Coarse levels remain dense to capture global structure, while fine levels become sparse, placing features only where high-frequency content exists. On DIV2K, Kodak, and Tecnick benchmarks, AGRID achieves 2–3 dB higher PSNR than Instant-NGP at equal or lower storage, demonstrating that content-adaptive allocation significantly improves representation quality for multiresolution neural fields.

records.title: Multi-Scale Prototype-Guided Dynamic Convolution for Multimodal Image Registration
records.abstract: Multimodal medical image registration aims for accurate spatial alignment across distinct modalities. However, inter-modality discrepancies, limited cross-modal representation of static convolutions, and insufficient contextual modeling constrain performance under large deformations. To tackle this, we propose a novel framework integrating Self-organizing Prototype Alignment (SPA) and Multi-level Modality Feature Dynamic Modulation (MDM) modules, which synergistically mitigate modality discrepancies and enhance cross-modal feature consistency. Additionally, a Scale–Context Flow Generator (SCFG) incorporates multi-scale contextual information to improve alignment accuracy under large deformations. Extensive experiments on brain and abdominal datasets show our framework outperforms state-of-the-art methods in accuracy.

records.title: SPOT: Structured Part-Attribute Optimal Transport for Zero-Shot Fine-grained Recognition
records.abstract: In recent years, foundation vision language models (VLMs) like Contrastive Language Image Pre-training (CLIP) have been widely adopted for zero-shot setting as they provide better generalization capability. However, VLMs like CLIP struggle in challenging scenario of fine-grained visual classification where classes share global appearance but differ in localized parts. We propose Structured Part-Attribute Optimal Transport (SPOT), a framework that strengthens zero-shot VLMs by explicitly using evidence from semantic object parts and their attributes. SPOT follows a two-stage design: a global CLIP stage first selects a small set of candidate classes, and a part-guided stage then performs attribute-aware alignment between detected parts and LLM-generated part--attribute prompts via structured optimal transport with a dustbin, yielding a structured set-to-set score that rewards coverage of all relevant attributes and suppresses redundant regions. This structured pipeline suppresses the redundant regions and emphasizes more on fine grained cues achieving around 1-2\% improvement over state-of-the-art zero-shot methods on benchmark fine-grained datasets.

records.title: Semantic Prototype Learning for Cross-Domain Activity Recognition
records.abstract: Real-world deployment of people-centric activity recognition in distributed multimedia systems, critical for applications like intelligent transportation and edge-cloud computing, is hindered by domain shifts and failures to detect anomalous behaviors. Traditional models often ignore the rich semantic relationships between activities, limiting their robustness and generalization across heterogeneous edge devices. To address this, we propose SemanticAnchor-VAE, a semantic prototype learning framework that integrates pre-trained text encoders with variational autoencoders for robust anomaly detection in cross-domain multimedia activity recognition. Specifically, our anchors are class prototypes derived from a SentenceTransformer, which effectively bridge the modality gap between sensor data and high-level textual concepts. Our dual-pronged approach detects anomalies by measuring both sensor reconstruction quality and deviation from semantic anchors in the latent space, enabled by a multi-scale convolutional architecture that captures complex temporal dynamics. Extensive experiments on three publicly available real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of SemanticAnchor-VAE, achieving up to 1.63% accuracy gains over state-of-the-art methods and validating the contribution of each component for robust cross-domain activity recognition.

records.title: SGT-Aug: Semantic-Guided Tail Augmentation for Long-Tailed Multi-Label Classification
records.abstract: Multi-label image classification aims to recognize multiple labels associated with a single image. Typically, label frequencies of real-world data often follow a severe long-tailed distribution, posing two key challenges: label co-occurrence and class imbalance. To address these challenges, we propose a new framework called Semantic-Guided Tail Augmentation (SGT-Aug), which merely augments representations for tail classes through a Semantic-Guided Co-occurrence Decoupling module and an Adaptive Tail Augmentation module. Firstly, SGT-Aug utilizes semantic-guided cross-attention to localize and decouple tail-class foregrounds from their co-occurring head-class contexts. Then, it designs a tail-exclusive augmentation method that generates tail samples by mixing the decoupled tail foregrounds with diverse backgrounds, which mitigates class imbalance without introducing head labels. Extensive experiments on the VOC-LT and COCO-LT benchmarks demonstrate that SGT-Aug effectively augments tail-class representations without compromising feature learning for head classes.

records.title: SG-CLIP: Segmentation-Guided CLIP with Adaptive Prototype-Aware Fusion for Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection
records.abstract: CLIP-based zero-shot anomaly detection has made rapid progress, yet it often suffers from a feature-granularity mismatch between global image-level classification and local pixel-level segmentation, leading to semantic bias and inconsistent predictions. We propose SG-CLIP, a segmentation-guided CLIP adaptation framework that aligns global decisions with multi-scale local evidence. The Adaptive and Prototype-aware Hierarchical Fusion module adaptively selects informative regions from multi-scale patch features and injects discriminative local anomaly semantics into the global representation. We further introduce a Segmentation-Classification Consistency Loss, where the segmentation branch is used as a fine-grained teacher to calibrate the classifier in probability space. Experiments on seven industrial and medical benchmarks show that SG-CLIP narrows the granularity gap and improves decision consistency, achieving state-of-the-art detection accuracy and strong cross-domain generalization.

records.title: CLIP-based Positive-Negative Visual Encoders for Open-set Single-source Domain Generalization
records.abstract: Open-Set Single-source Domain Generalization (OS-SDG) aims at transferring models trained by only a single-source domain to unseen target domains under both domain and category shifts. Existing OS-SDG methods are developed based on only the visual modality, without fully utilizing the complementary textual modality with rich semantics. Despite the success of related works on CLIP-based Out-Of-Distribution (OOD) detection, they rely on generic negative text prompts and thus struggle to capture visual cues under domain shifts. In this paper, we propose to learn positive-negative Dual Visual encoders in a CLIP-based framework (DV-CLIP) for OS-SDG. In DV-CLIP, class-discriminative and class-irrelevant visual features of each image are extracted by the positive and negative encoders respectively to improve unknown-class detection. Our method mitigates domain shift by injecting style features within each image into learnable prompts to obtain instance-adaptive text features. In addition, we incorporate adversarial style perturbations to learn domain-agnostic prompts for more robust feature learning. Extensive experiments on four benchmarks demonstrate that DV-CLIP achieves substantial improvements over state-of-the-art methods for OS-SDG.

records.title: HiFuseNet: Hierarchical Fusion Network for Multimodal Molecular Representation Learning
records.abstract: Molecular representation learning plays a crucial role in molecular science. Existing approaches primarily rely on Simplified Molecular Input Line Entry System (SMILES) sequences and molecular graphs to model complex molecular structures. However, they often treat different modalities and structural levels in a parallel or statically fused manner, limiting their ability to model hierarchical molecular semantics and contextual importance. To bridge this gap, we propose HiFuseNet, a Hierarchical Fusion Network that unifies multimodal molecular representations through a hierarchical message interaction mechanism, enabling intra-level refinement and cross-level semantic interaction from fine-grained local structures to global molecular context. HiFuseNet features a two-stage fusion strategy, where a intra-modal fusion module refines features within SMILES sequence, followed by a hierarchical cross-modal fusion module that adaptively aggregates atom-, motif-, and sequence-level representations to produce unified, context-aware molecular embeddings. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that HiFuseNet consistently outperforms existing methods in downstream molecular property prediction tasks.

records.title: Gaussian Diffusion Classifiers: An Efficient and Strong Baseline for Zero-Shot Generative Classification
records.abstract: Large diffusion models have become mainstream generative models in both academia and industrial AIGC applications. Recent studies have explored their potential as zero- shot classifiers. However, existing diffusion-based classifiers suffer from extremely slow inference (e.g.,∼1000 seconds per image on ImageNet), which severely limits their practical use. In this paper, we propose an embarrassingly simple and efficient zero- shot Gaussian Diffusion Classifier (GDC) based on pretrained text-to-image diffusion models and DINOv2. GDC significantly outperforms prior zero-shot diffusion-based classifiers on Im- ageNet by over 10 percentage points (61.40% → 71.44%), while achieving over 30, 000× speedup in single-image inference time (1000 → 0.03 seconds). Moreover, GDC provides a probabilistic interpretation of classification results. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GDC achieves competitive zero- shot performance across multiple datasets and naturally benefits from stronger diffusion models. To our knowledge, GDC is the first zero-shot diffusion-based classifier that achieves both high accuracy and practical efficiency.

records.title: Few-shot Class-incremental Audio Classification using Fixed Non-negative Orthogonal Classifier
records.abstract: Few-shot class-incremental audio classification aims to simulate real-world scenarios in which a deployed model must continually adapt to novel classes with only a limited number of samples. Most existing FCAC methods adopt a decoupled training strategy with an extensible prototype-based classifier, whose performance critically depends on strong inter-class separability and intra-class compactness. To address this challenge, we propose a novel FCAC framework that integrates three key components: (1) an extensible fixed non-negative orthogonal classifier that anchors features of different classes to mutually orthogonal directions, thereby enhancing inter-class separability; (2) a semantic-guided virtual learning strategy that introduces virtual samples during the base session to effectively promote intra-class compactness; and (3) a memory replay scheme that preserves and replays a small number of samples per class to maintain both inter-class separability and intra-class compactness throughout incremental sessions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing baselines in terms of both average accuracy and comprehensive performance score.

records.title: MoE-SSPL: Balanced Mixture-of-Experts and Semantic-Structure Pseudo-Labeling for Weakly Supervised Video Anomaly Detection
records.abstract: Weakly supervised video anomaly detection (WS-VAD) localizes abnormal snippets using only video-level labels, but is often hindered by dominant multi-modal normal patterns, MIL bias toward a few high-scoring snippets, and noisy scores that cause false alarms. We enhance a strong MIL baseline with two complementary modules: (i) a lightweight mixture-of-experts routing block with load-balancing regularization to encourage specialization for diverse normal behaviors and rare long-tailed anomalies; and (ii) a semantic-structure guided pseudo-labeling strategy that derives reliable snippet supervision via clustering structure and vision–text semantic consistency. These modules reinforce each other: diversified representations stabilize pseudo labels, while refined pseudo labels provide cleaner constraints to further improve expert specialization and suppress spurious normal responses. Experiments show strong results with fewer false alarms: 98.41 AUC (ShanghaiTech), 90.67 AUC (UCF-Crime), and 87.56 AP (XD-Violence). Prompts are used only in training.

records.title: Subspace Combination Convolutional Network For Image Classification
records.abstract: In computer vision, researchers have sought to develop convolutional neural networks (CNNs) that emulate the dynamic receptive field mechanisms of the biological visual cortex. Prior approaches often relied on multi-branch architectures to achieve this, but incurred high computational costs, thus hindering an optimal balance between performance and efficiency. To address this, we propose Subspace Combination Convolution (SCC), a novel single-branch method for nonlinear feature extraction, drawing inspiration from established principles. SCC decomposes a single convolutional kernel to capture diverse feature subspaces, preserving the benefits of a single kernel while enabling multi-scale receptive field acquisition. Evaluations on ImageNet and CIFAR demonstrate that SCC achieves significantly higher accuracy than standard convolutional blocks under comparable computational costs. Statistical analyses further reveal that our network yields more desirable output distributions than traditional convolutional blocks that employ explicit activation functions. Code and experimental results are available at: github.com/Raven-Z-china/SCCNet.

records.title: DMC-GC: A Multi-View Anchor Clustering Method Based on Geometric Alignment and Dual-Matrix Collaboration
records.abstract: Abstract—Multi-view clustering aims to fuse information from different views to enhance clustering performance. However, existing anchor-based methods often suffer from geometric distortion in anchor representations and overly simplistic information fusion mechanisms. We propose DMC-GC, a multi-view anchor clustering method based on geometric alignment and dual-matrix collaboration, which achieves efficient and robust multi-view clustering through geometric centroid regularization and dual- matrix collaborative optimization. Specifically, at the geometric representation level, we propose a global-mean-guided geometric alignment constraint that aligns anchors with the data centroid of each view. It effectively mitigates representation drift and establishes a stable geometric foundation for cross-view fusion. At the information fusion level, we design an iterative dual-matrix collaborative optimization mechanism that dynamically optimizes the consensus matrix and view-specific matrices, promoting cross-view consistency and complementary information fusion through deep bidirectional interactions. Experimental results on benchmark datasets validate the effectiveness and superiority of the DMC-GC algorithm. Index Terms—Multi-view Clustering, Anchor Learning, Geometric Alignment, Dual-Matrix Collaboration

records.title: Unifying VLM-Guided Flow Matching and Spectral Anomaly Detection for Interpretable Veterinary Diagnosis
records.abstract: Automatic diagnosis of canine pneumothorax is challenged by data scarcity and the need for trustworthy models. To address this, we first introduce a public, pixel-level annotated dataset to facilitate research. We then propose a novel diagnostic paradigm that reframes the task as a synergistic process of signal localization and spectral detection. For localization, our method employs a Vision-Language Model (VLM) to guide an iterative Flow Matching process, which progressively refines segmentation masks to achieve superior boundary accuracy. For detection, the segmented mask is used to isolate features from the suspected lesion. We then apply Random Matrix Theory (RMT), a departure from traditional classifiers, to analyze these features. This approach models healthy tissue as predictable random noise and identifies pneumothorax by detecting statistically significant outlier eigenvalues that represent a non-random pathological signal. The high-fidelity localization from Flow Matching is crucial for purifying the signal, thus maximizing the sensitivity of our RMT detector. This synergy of generative segmentation and first-principles statistical analysis yields a highly accurate and interpretable diagnostic system (source code is available at: https://github.com/Pu-Wang-alt/Canine-pneumothorax).

records.title: FMCL: Fuzzy Membership-Guided Contrastive Learning for Multi-view Clustering
records.abstract: Multi-view clustering can explore complementary information from multiple views and has attracted increasing attention. Contrastive learning has become a dominant paradigm for learning view-invariant representations. However, existing methods treat all negative pairs equally, where they ignore that samples from the same cluster may be incorrectly pushed apart, known as the false negative problem. To address this issue, we propose a fuzzy membership-guided contrastive learning method (FMCL) for multi-view clustering. It learns soft cluster assignments via a shared clustering head based on Student's t-distribution, and computes membership agreement scores to dynamically weight negative pairs. Samples with high membership agreement receive lower negative weights, thus mitigating the false negative problem. Furthermore, we design a dual-level contrastive module at both instance and cluster levels for comprehensive cross-view alignment. Experimental results on benchmark datasets show that FMCL outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

records.title: scDCAN: Genetic-Prior Aware Single-Cell Representation Learning with Decoupled Cell-Gene Attention Networks
records.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis is often hindered by technical noise, sparsity, and a lack of functional context. While existing methods incorporate biological priors via Graph Neural Network (GNN) or dual-stream Variational Autoencoder (VAE) structures, they suffer from architectural bottlenecks: GNN forces all cells to share a single, static topology constraint, ignoring cell-type-specific gene interactions and leading to representation over-smoothing, whereas VAE-based knowledge integration relies on shallow interactions that fail to capture deep, context-aware signals. To address these gaps, we propose scDCAN (Genetic-Prior Aware Single-Cell Representation Learning with Decoupled Cell-Gene Attention Networks). We decouple gene embeddings into static topological identities and adaptive expression profiles. Specifically, scDCAN utilizes cell states as queries to prioritize gene importance based on their identities, while leveraging genes' adaptive profiles to reconstruct cell-specific expression. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that scDCAN learns biologically meaningful cell-gene representations and outperforms state-of-the-art methods in cell clustering, gene function identification, and spatial gene expression imputation.

records.title: ReMAP-AD: Relation-guided Multi-scale Adaptive Prompting for Anomaly Detection
records.abstract: Zero-shot anomaly detection (Zero-Shot AD) using vision-language models has attracted increasing attention due to the scarcity and diversity of defective samples in real-world scenarios. However, existing vision-language models (VLMs) struggle to derive spatially consistent anomaly localization solely from global image–text alignment. To bridge this gap, we present ReMAP-AD, which explicitly models patch-semantic relational grounding by converting local visual evidence into instance-adaptive textual prompts. Specifically, our framework integrates: Class-Agnostic Universal Prompt Learning (CAUPL) to construct transferable normality and abnormality prototypes; Multi-Scale Relational Refinement (MSRR), which enriches patch-level representations with hierarchical structural cues; and Semantic-Guided Relational Prompting (SGRP), which embeds patch-semantic relational information into semantic-driven prompts. Comprehensive evaluations on industrial and medical benchmarks show that ReMAP-AD attains state-of-the-art or competitive results in both zero-shot and few-shot settings, all while maintaining a completely frozen CLIP backbone. The code is available at https://github.com/lhy0525/ReMAP.

records.title: Decoupled Spectral-Spatial Graph Learning with Low-Frequency Priors for Multi-View Clustering
records.abstract: Multi-view Clustering (MVC) has emerged as a pivotal paradigm for integrating heterogeneous data representations. However, graph-based approaches often suffer from oversmoothing due to reliance on static topologies and rigid low-pass priors, which suppress discriminative high-frequency details. To address this, we propose a Dynamic Graph Learning framework with Prior-Constrained Spectral Filtering. Unlike static approaches, we introduce a curriculum-based evolution strategy that synergizes spatial expansion with spectral filtering. Specifically, we impose a strict low-pass constraint initially for robustness. As the spatial neighborhood expands to capture global structures, the learned filters adaptively evolve beyond this constraint to recover informative mid-frequency details essential for cluster boundaries. This mechanism effectively balances noise suppression with structural refinement. Extensive experiments on eight benchmarks demonstrate that our method mitigates oversmoothing and yields superior performance compared to state-of-the-art baselines. records.title: LogAD-Glass: Logical Anomaly Detection in Industrial Glass with Consistency-Aware Reasoning
records.abstract: Anomaly detection for industrial glass faces two challenges: structural anomalies (e.g., scratches) are difficult to localize due to glass transparency and background interference. Logical anomalies (e.g., incorrect hole counts) exhibit no distinguishable appearance differences from normal samples. Since appearance-based methods lack the ability to verify images against manufacturing requirements, logical anomalies are difficult to identify. Moreover, hidden contamination in training set hinders unsupervised learning. We propose a unified framework for detecting structural and logical anomalies. Training Set Purification filters contaminated samples through cross-model consensus to stabilize pattern learning. Prompt-guided Semantic Segmentation performs prompt-guided localization, followed by box-guided high-precision segmentation and semantic fusion to produce precise instance-level semantic segmentation. Logical Consistency Constraint evaluates instance-level attributes against predefined manufacturing rules, enabling reliable logical anomaly detection. Experimental results on benchmarks demonstrate improvements over existing methods.

records.title: Attribute-Guidance and Size-Aware Learning for Fine-Grained Blood Cell Classification
records.abstract: The fine-grained classification of blood cells is impeded by substantial intra-class heterogeneity and nuanced inter-class distinctions. Prevalent methodologies are typically bifurcated: they are either vision-centric, thereby neglecting discriminative cellular attributes, or dependent on attribute prediction, which is susceptible to error propagation and representational sparsity. To address these limitations, we introduce a hybrid framework augmented by a Vision-Language Model (VLM) that integrates textual attribute guidance and morphological size cues. Specifically, our architecture synthesizes visual features with VLM-encoded categorical attributes and instance-level metrics via an adaptive fusion mechanism. Empirical evaluations across two datasets, including a newly curated large-scale corpus comprising 329,000 images spanning 47 categories, substantiate that our approach outperforms existing general-purpose and specialized fine-grained classification approaches. The implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/CVIU-CSU/AGSA.

records.title: SIM-GCN: Learning Symmetry-Interactive Attention and Multi-Semantic Prototypes for Skeleton-Based Action Recognition
records.abstract: Despite the success of Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) in skeleton-based action recognition, learning discriminative representations for fine-grained and similar actions remains challenging. Existing methods often overlook dynamic body symmetry, fail to filter noisy correlations, and entangle multi-level semantics. To address these limitations, we propose SIM-GCN. First, a Dynamic Symmetry Interaction (DSI) module is introduced to explicitly model bilateral synergistic dynamics within skeleton sequences, enhancing sensitivity to subtle motion patterns. Second, we design an Uncertainty-weighted Graph Attention (U-GAT) mechanism, which dynamically reweights noisy connections based on feature uncertainty to ensure reliable fusion. Finally, a Structured Prototypical Decoupled Contrastive Learning (SPDCL) strategy is proposed to align features across joint, part, and global hierarchies, maximizing intra-class compactness. Extensive experiments on NTU RGB+D, NTU RGB+D 120, and NW-UCLA demonstrate that SIM-GCN achieves state-of-the-art performance, particularly in distinguishing kinetically ambiguous actions.

records.title: Dynamic Dual Alignment Learning Framework for Long-Tailed Visual Classification
records.abstract: Deep neural networks suffer from biased learning problems on long-tailed data, leading to degraded recognition accuracy for tail classes. Although dual-branch mixed augmentation architectures show potential in this task, we identify an inherent semantic misalignment problem, manifested as semantic divergence between different augmented views and semantic blindness across different task branches within the same view. To address this, we propose a Dynamic Dual Alignment Learning (DDAL) framework consisting of Prototype-Guided Semantic Alignment (PGSA) and Cross-Branch Feature Alignment (CBFA). PGSA utilizes the weight matrix of the rebalanced classification head as dynamic class prototypes to inject high-level semantic information into the contrastive branch, thus alleviating semantic blindness. CBFA enhances feature consistency by guiding multi-level features from different augmented views to approach each other. Furthermore, we introduce an effective-area-aware reweighting strategy that dynamically adjusts loss weights based on the actual distribution range of classes in the feature space, providing balanced supervision signals. Experiments on multiple long-tailed benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10-LT, CIFAR-100-LT, ImageNet-LT, and Places-LT, demonstrate the superiority of DDAL compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

records.title: PAL-Net: Jitter Activated Learnable Temporal Pyramid Pooling for Latency Robust EEG Object Classification
records.abstract: With the development of brain computer interface technology, visual object classification based on electroencephalogram (EEG) signals has become a significant research direction. However, the significant latency jitter inherent in event-related potentials results in the temporal misalignment of discriminative features, which severely constrains the performance of traditional models relying on fixed temporal windows. To address this challenge, we propose the Physiology-Aware Learning Network (PAL-Net). We first introduce a learnable temporal pyramid pooling (L-TPP) module, which employs a soft binning mechanism to dynamically optimize integration boundaries, thereby flexibly localizing temporally shifted key waveforms. Furthermore, a physiologically consistent data augmentation strategy simulating temporal jitter is introduced to explicitly activate the L-TPP, compelling it to learn robust boundaries for misaligned waveforms. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method exhibits superior robustness and achieves state-of-the-art performance on two public EEG datasets.

records.title: FPGM: Factorized Prototype Gating for Domain Generalization in Emotion Recognition across Subjects and Sleep States
records.abstract: Emotion recognition based on electroencephalography (EEG) and eye movements has attracted increasing attention due to high temporal resolution. However, real-world deployment faces distribution shifts across subjects and recording sessions, and sleep state variation can further aggravate this shift. Existing methods often rely on feature alignment or domain invariance, but struggle with multi-source shifts. We propose the Factorized Prototype Gating Module (FPGM) for multi-source domain generalization, treating each subject-state pair as a source domain. FPGM factorizes each class prototype into a global prototype, a subject bias from shared archetype bases, and a sleep-state bias. A gating network composes sample-wise prototypes and is optimized with prototype matching, intra-class smoothing, and bias regularization. On SEED-SD, FPGM improves the backbone baseline by 1.92% in the multi-state cross-subject setting and reaches 86.67% accuracy with the adapter-augmented backbone, enhancing robustness to sleep state shifts.

records.title: Hyperbolic Prototype Routing for Rehearsal-Free Class-Incremental Learning
records.abstract: Class-Incremental Learning (CIL) aims to continually learn new classes while preserving prior knowledge. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) with pre-trained models (PTMs) has recently shown promise, enabling CIL with minimal parameter updates. However, existing approaches still suffer from catastrophic forgetting due to cumulative interference across tasks and suboptimal module-sample matching during inference. We propose \underline{Hy}perbolic \underline{P}rototype \underline{Ro}uting (HyPro), a rehearsal-free framework that exploits hyperbolic geometry for continual learning. First, we allocate a dedicated \textbf{LoRA-Expert} module for each incremental task, enabling isolated representation learning and eliminating cross-task interference. Second, to enhance module-sample matching, we introduce a HyPro mechanism that projects features onto a Poincaré ball and performs geodesic nearest-prototype matching, yielding exponentially larger decision margins and more reliable task-level discrimination. Extensive experiments on standard CIL and Few-Shot CIL (FSCIL) benchmarks show that HyPro consistently improves average and final-stage accuracy over strong baselines. We will release our code to support future research.

records.title: HGCAF: Heterogeneous Graph Convolutional Attention-based Facial-Motion Feature Fusion for Epilepsy Classification
records.abstract: Epilepsy poses a major diagnostic challenge due to its sudden onset and diverse visual manifestations, particularly in pediatric patients with subtle symptoms. Video-based seizure classification is further complicated by the transient nature of seizures and the subtle co-occurrence of motor spasms and facial expressions. To address these challenges, we propose HGCAF, a principled framework that formulates seizure detection as a cross-modal representation alignment problem. By constructing a heterogeneous spatio-temporal graph, we explicitly model the complex dependencies between sparse skeletal structures and dense facial feature spaces. A multi-scale spatial–semantic attention mechanism is introduced to bridge the resolution gap between modalities, complemented by a modality-consistent regularization that encourages cross-modal semantic consistency. Extensive evaluations on clinically annotated pediatric datasets demonstrate that HGCAF achieves an F1 score of 0.9616 and an accuracy of 0.9583 in binary classification, and an F1 score of 0.8586 with an accuracy of 0.8587 in ternary classification, consistently outperforming strong baselines.

records.title: MSA-MER: 4D Micro-Expression Recognition Based on Multi-View Symmetry-Driven Attention
records.abstract: Facial micro-expression recognition is a challenging task due to the subtle changes in micro-expression motions. However, most existing methods primarily rely on single-view 2D video data, which poses critical bottlenecks, including limited views, data scarcity, and sensitivity to illumination. To address these issues, we propose a novel 4D micro-expression recognition framework, MSA-MER, based on multi-view symmetry-driven attention. Firstly, we construct a hybrid parallel architecture integrated with frontal-view feature extraction with side-view symmetric interaction to exploit spatiotemporal complementarity. Secondly, we design a Symmetry-driven Attention (SDA) module to translate facial biological symmetry into geometric priors and to recover the lack of features via cross-view interaction. Furthermore, we introduce a Bilateral-Guided strategy (B-Guided) that employs a dual-source mechanism to optimize attention weights, effectively overcoming unilateral bias. Extensive experiments on the 4DME dataset verify that the multi-view approach significantly improves 4D micro-expression recognition.

records.title: Dynamic Sub-Prototype Refinement Network for Few-Shot Learning
records.abstract: Few-shot Learning (FSL) aims to recognize novel categories using only a limited number of labeled samples per class. The scarcity of training data presents significant challenges to model generalization, as existing single-prototype methods are not only vulnerable to interference from sample bias but also inadequate for modeling intra-class diversity. To address this issue, a novel attribute-level Dynamic Sub-Prototype Refinement Network (DSP-Net) is proposed in this paper. The method consists of two core modules: the Cross-Set Attribute Selection (CSAS) module and the Dynamic Sub-Prototype Refinement (DSPR) module. The CSAS module selects attribute representations across different sets, enabling the model to focus on discriminative attributes, thereby mitigating prototype bias and enhancing inter-class separability. The DSPR module dynamically refines multiple sub-prototypes per class, addressing the challenges of significant intra-class diversity. Experiments on four benchmark datasets show that DSP-Net outperforms state-of-the-art methods under various settings.

records.title: Heterophily-Aware Graph Anomaly Detection via Local-Global Structural Perspective
records.abstract: Unsupervised graph anomaly detection (GAD) has been widely adopted in diverse real-world applications. Targeting anomalies that camouflage themselves by connecting to normal nodes, existing approaches primarily emphasize attribute-level heterophily between nodes and their neighbors. However, such methods predominantly rely on attribute information and suffer from the misclassification of low-homophily normal nodes as anomalies. To address this limitation, we propose AHGAD, which integrates local and global structural perspectives to capture universal graph anomaly patterns through three components: 1) Anomaly Property-based Attribute Augmentation, which cap tures local structural anomaly by identifying degree-coreness mismatches; 2) Heterophily-aware Graph Encoder, which adap tively leverages features from different neighborhood ranges to handle varying levels of homophily; 3) Graph Context-guided Anomaly Scoring, which introduces a novel anomaly mining approach from a global perspective. Extensive experiments on five benchmark datasets demonstrate that AHGAD significantly outperforms state-of-the-art competitors, showcasing its superior effectiveness and robustness.

records.title: OpenAVS: Open-vocabulary Audio-Visual Segmentation with Message Relay Agents
records.abstract: Audio-visual segmentation (AVS) aims to separate sounding objects in videos by predicting pixel-level masks conditioned on audio signals. However, in real-world scenarios, the scarcity of labeled data poses significant challenges. Existing methods primarily focus on closed-set scenarios and direct audio-visual alignment, which limits their generalization ability. In this paper, we propose OpenAVS, a novel training-free multi-agent framework that reformulates Open-vocabulary AVS as a textual reasoning loop that effectively and flexibly aligns multi-modal signals via natural language message relaying. Our method seamlessly connects foundation model based specialized autonomous agents and handles AVS through three main stages: 1) Perception: Multimedia Agents receive audio and visual streams and convert raw signals into textual descriptions. 2) Understanding: Translation Agent receives textual multimedia descriptions, performs abstraction and digestion, aligns multi-modal representations within the textual semantic space, and then translates them into instruction prompts for segmentation. 3) Execution: Segmentation Agent processes these instruction prompts to generate pixel-level masks. The Translation Agent is a key component of our framework, enabling effective knowledge transfer from general-purpose foundation models to AVS through task-specific prompt design. Moreover, it reduces noise the textual descriptions generated by the Multimedia Agents by enforcing prompt-wise, model-wise, and temporal consistency. Comprehensive experiments on four benchmark datasets demonstrate the superior performance of our method. It surpasses existing methods by 4.95% in mIoU and 2.99% in F-score on the AVSBench dataset, and a significant gain of 12.8% in mIoU on the zero-shot V3 dataset.

records.title: Connecting Generation with Compression: Unified Generative Coding with Semantic Guidance
records.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) raises growing interest in compressing generative images. However, existing practices typically separate generation and compression processes, due to their intrinsic opposing entropy increase and decrease, leading to ineffective processing and leaving room for further optimization in generative image compression. To address this issue, this paper proposes a generation-with-compression paradigm that jointly optimizes both processes with a Holistic Entropy Constraint, preventing meaningless signal entropy increase and narrowing the gap between generation and compression distributions bidirectionally. Specifically, a Unified Generative Compression Network is designed from three perspectives to achieve optimization for such a constraint. First, at the architecture level, a compression-aware diffusion framework is designed, which incorporates rate constraints during the generation training, enabling compression-aware image generation with lower signal entropy. Then, on the model design end, a semantic attention guided mechanism is employed, which dynamically allocates bitrates at the regional level, ensuring the preservation of critical structural and semantic features within the image. Finally, for the representation space, the proposed joint generative compression framework integrates an adaptive latent compression network into a generative model that enables a joint optimization at the unified latent space to minimize information loss and computational overhead. Extensive experiments validate the superiority of our method to existing compression techniques. Our project is publicly available at: https://ellisonkuang.github.io/UGCN.github.io/.

records.title: Robust Zero-shot Brain Visual Decoding via Consistency Refining and Mining
records.abstract: Recently, zero-shot brain-to-visual decoding has attracted considerable interest for recognizing novel visual concepts from neural signals. However, existing methods suffer from brain-image noisy correspondences induced by attention fluctuation, physiological noise, and signal acquisition interference. Unlike traditional cross-modal tasks, brain signal degradation is pervasive and inevitable, making standard contrastive learning vulnerable to false positives. To address this, we propose SEmantic Consistency Refining and Mining (SECRM), a quality-aware framework that distinguishes signal quality from semantic difficulty. SECRM dynamically partitions samples into quality tiers using collaborative assessment, then applies differentiated learning strategies. For high/medium-quality samples, it refines reliable correspondences through contrastive learning; for low/medium-quality samples, it relies solely on mining semantic consistency from negative pools via neighborhood-based soft supervision. Extensive experiments on 200-way zero-shot retrieval on the THINGS-EEG and THINGS-MEG datasets demonstrate gains of +2.0\% and +4.4\% over state-of-the-art methods, respectively. Additionally, the framework exhibit broad compatibility various different brain encoder architectures.

records.title: Reactivating Ambiguous Regions for Breast Ultrasound Image Segmentation
records.abstract: Breast ultrasound images often contain ambiguous regions caused by blurry boundaries and degraded textures. These regions yield prediction probabilities near 0.5, producing weak gradients and poor learnability. While recent methods address them via reweighting, sampling, or contrastive learning, they often fail to truly activate ambiguous regions during optimization, leading to under-trained representations and degraded lesion boundaries. To tackle this, we propose a two-stage Decoupled Learning Network (DLNet). Stage I introduces AAR, which dynamically replaces confident areas with ambiguous patches to perturb stable contexts and strengthen gradient flow. Stage II freezes the encoder to preserve ambiguity-aware features and performs structural recovery in the decoder with two modules: Ambiguity-Aware Semantic Alignment (ASA) for deep–shallow consistency and Ambiguity-Focused Boundary Restoration (ABR) for boundary refinement via multi-scale filtering. Experiments demonstrate that DLNet achieves state-of-the-art results, with clear gains on ambiguous-region segmentation.

records.title: Beyond Concatenation: Harmonized Multimodal Knowledge Graph Representation via Gram-Based Geometric Fusion
records.abstract: Multimodal entity representations are crucial for downstream tasks such as multimodal question answering. However, embeddings of the same entity from different modalities often diverge — manifesting as modality-wise directional conflicts that can severely distort an entity's multimodal semantics. Existing approaches typically rely on contrastive objectives to pull modality pairs closer and thereby reduce semantic interference. In this work, we propose an alternative fusion strategy, GraCon, a contrastive learning method driven by Gram-matrix volume minimization. Unlike pairwise comparison-based objectives, GraCon treats modality embeddings as the vertices of a polytope and enforces a global geometric constraint by minimizing that polytope’s volume; this jointly harmonizes multimodal semantics and mitigates interference. Building on GraCon, we present HarmoKG, a unified framework for multimodal knowledge-graph representation learning. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets show that HarmoKG consistently outperforms 16 state-of-the-art baselines on link prediction and triple-classification tasks (e.g., +5.7% MRR and +5.8% Hits@10 on MKG-W).

records.title: D²Feat: Dual Distillation for Semantic and Geometric Local Feature Learning
records.abstract: Convolution-based feature descriptors remain widely adopted in many downstream tasks for their resource efficiency and ease of deployment. Recently, transformer-based feature matchers and their underlying self-supervised visual encoders have achieved remarkable progress in feature matching, redefining the frontier of visual correspondence learning. Motivated by these advances, we propose D²Feat, a dual-distillation framework that injects the strengths of both self-supervised visual encoders and transformer-based matchers into a compact convolutional backbone. Specifically, we distill semantically rich but spatially coarse representations from self-supervised encoders at early stages, and later distill geometrically precise features from transformer-based feature matchers. Furthermore, we introduce a lightweight Fine-grained Perceiver Module (FPM) that integrates the distilled features in a bypass manner with minimal computational overhead. Our dual-stage distillation strategy ensures stable convergence and consistent optimization behavior across training stages. Extensive experiments on MegaDepth, ScanNet, and HPatches demonstrate that D²Feat achieves outstanding performance.

records.title: Beyond the Unknown: Extrapolating Semantic from Seed Classes to Open World
records.abstract: Open world learning holds great promise for addressing the real-world challenge arising from the continuously emerging novel instances which are unseen during training. However, existing approaches tend to treat these novel instances as an undifferentiated unknown class neglecting their intrinsic affinities with known classes. To address these limitations, we propose open-world extrapolator (OWE), a novel framework that leverages likelihood-guided feature synthesis to extrapolate semantics from limited seed classes. Specifically, we utilize a normalizing flow model with a mixed conditional Gaussian distribution to synthesize diverse visual features, which are then integrated with prompt learning to establish extrapolated semantic anchors. These anchors help construct a holistic decision boundary for super classes. By pushing novel instances away from the entire super class distribution instead of just seed classes, our method effectively reduces the confusion between novel and unseen objects. Extensive experiments on benchmarks like CODA demonstrate that our OWE significantly outperforms prior approaches in achieving the fine-grained detection of novel instances, enabling robust interaction in real world.

records.title: ModalImmune: Immunity Driven Unlearning via Self Destructive Training
records.abstract: Multimodal systems are vulnerable to partial or complete loss of input channels at deployment, which undermines reliability in real-world settings. This paper presents ModalImmune, a training framework that enforces modality immunity by intentionally and controllably collapsing selected modality information during training so the model learns joint representations that are robust to destructive modality influence. The framework combines a spectrum-adaptive collapse regularizer, an information-gain guided controller for targeted interventions, curvature-aware gradient masking to stabilize destructive updates, and a certified Neumann-truncated hyper-gradient procedure for automatic meta-parameter adaptation. Empirical evaluation on standard multimodal benchmarks demonstrates that ModalImmune improves resilience to modality removal and corruption while retaining convergence stability and reconstruction capacity.

records.title: Synergistic Prompting: Regularizing Encoders and Distilling Prototypes for WSSS
records.abstract: The application of Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) has advanced Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation (WSSS), yet its effectiveness is fundamentally constrained by the modality gap between vision and text spaces. This gap prevents text-derived prototypes from accurately corresponding to pixel-level visual features, leading to incomplete object activations and erroneous localization on co-occurring backgrounds. To mitigate this gap, we propose a novel framework, SyMA (Synergistic Modality Alignment), that learns a more faithful vision-centric prototype through a synergistic process of dual-modality adaptation and prototype distillation. First, we introduce Dual-Modality Prompt Regularization, which adapts the frozen CLIP encoders. Learnable visual prompts are injected to regularize the vision encoder’s internal attention mechanism, suppressing feature-level artifacts. Concurrently, learnable textual prompts purify the semantic space by explicitly modeling and separating object concepts from their surrounding contexts. Second, we propose a Visual Consistency Distillation module. This module treats the initial, text-guided localization map as a weak signal and refines it by aggregating cues from parallel local affinity and global structural-dependency pathways, effectively distilling a final map driven by pure visual evidence. Extensive experiments show that our framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on the PASCAL VOC 2012 and MS COCO 2014 benchmarks, validating the effectiveness of our approach in bridging the modality gap for WSSS.

records.title: Spatial-Semantic Hypergraph Attention Learning for Survival Prediction on Whole Slide Images
records.abstract: Accurate survival prediction from whole-slide histopathology images (WSIs) remains challenging due to the inability of existing methods to jointly model spatial tissue architecture and semantic feature hierarchies effectively. Current approaches either impose rigid graph structures that oversimplify tissue topology or rely on attention mechanisms lacking explicit geometric constraints, limiting their prognostic accuracy. We propose S2HGAL, a hierarchical framework that combines graph-based and attention-based learning through three key components: (a) a dual-graph representation learning module consisting of a spatial graph that preserves tissue topology alongside a semantic hypergraph to capture higher-order feature affinities, (b) intra- and cross-modal transformer modules facilitating bidirectional information flow within and between the spatial and semantic subspaces among the patches, and finally, (c) an inter-patch attention module for enhanced dynamic slide-level aggregation. Evaluated on 4 different TCGA cohorts, our method achieves state-of-the-art performance with an average C-index of 0.7629, outperforming all SOTA method significantly. Kaplan–Meier survival analysis shows that our approach effectively separates patients into high- and low-risk groups, achieving a statistically significant and clinically meaningful distinction. The framework advances WSI analysis by unifying spatial-semantic learning with interpretable global aggregation, offering a principled approach for computational pathology.

records.title: NMCSE: Noise-Robust Multi-Modal Coupling Signal Estimation Method via Optimal Transport for Cardiovascular Disease Detection
records.abstract: The coupling signal is a latent process that links electrical excitation in the electrocardiogram (ECG) to mechanical activity reflected in the phonocardiogram (PCG), providing an informative representation for cardiovascular disease (CVD) analysis in noisy wearable settings. Existing estimation methods are highly noise-sensitive, often producing distorted reconstructions and unreliable coupling estimates. We propose Noise-Robust Multi-Modal Coupling Signal Estimation (NMCSE), which reformulates coupling-signal estimation as an optimal-transport-based distribution-matching problem. By jointly aligning amplitude statistics and temporal structure, NMCSE reduces the noise amplification inherent in deconvolution-based approaches and enables stable recovery of the coupling signal. Experiments on PhysioNet/CinC 2016 with hospital ambient noise and on EPHNOGRAM with motion-induced noise show consistent improvements in reconstruction error, spectral coherence, and intra-state consistency at low signal-to-noise ratios. Using the estimated coupling signal as an additional modality further improves balanced accuracy and F1-score over strong ECG--PCG fusion baselines, demonstrating its value as an interpretable and discriminative representation for multi-modal CVD screening.

records.title: Improving Adversarial Transferability on Vision Transformers via Attention and Feature Disruption
records.abstract: Adversarial examples pose serious security threats to deep learning models, making the study of their generation essential for evaluating and improving model robustness. Although Vision Transformers (ViTs) have become a dominant architecture, their robustness under adversarial threats remains a critical concern. To address the high cost of query-based black-box attacks, we focus on improving transferability, which enables efficient evaluation across models without repeated adversarial examples generation. In this paper, we propose JAFDA (Joint Attention and Feature Disruption based Attack), a novel method that enhances adversarial transferability. Specifically, JAFDA integrates multi-scale attention manipulation with reverse targeting strategies and disrupts feature representations through a cosine distance loss. Experiments on ImageNet demonstrate that JAFDA outperforms existing methods, achieving an average improvement of 8.3% in attack success rate across diverse black-box ViTs while also improving transferability to CNNs by 5.7% on average. Code is available at: https://github.com/lingyu700/JAFDA.

records.title: GSFA-ICM: Image Compression for Machines via Gated Spatial-Frequency Adaptation
records.abstract: Image Compression for Machines (ICM) aims to compress images to support machine vision tasks instead of human vision systems. However, its practical application is limited by the high training costs of existing paradigms. To address this challenge, inspired by Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT), we propose a lightweight Gated Spatial-Frequency Adapter (GSFA) to repurpose pre-trained base codecs by updating only the GSFA, thereby significantly reducing training costs. Specifically, to minimize task-irrelevant spatial redundancy, we introduce a Spatial-Context Adapter (SCA) that employs a hierarchical learning mechanism to exploit context and align semantics between the codec and machine vision tasks. For efficient task-relevant frequency representation, the Frequency-Spectrum Adapter (FSA) is introduced to synergize FFT-based and Wavelet-based adaptations, effectively disentangling global-local frequency components. Finally, the Gated Fusion Adapter (GFA) dynamically balances the influence of spatial and frequency adaptation. Moreover, the GSFA is plug-and-play and compatible with multiple existing neural image compression models. Experiments demonstrate that our framework saves more than 20% of parameters compared to existing SOTA methods while maintaining competitive rate-task performance in image classification, object detection, and instance segmentation.

records.title: Multimodal Just Noticeable Difference Estimation via Audio-Visual Fusion
records.abstract: With the continuous expansion of multimedia content, audio and video have become integral components of information presentation. However, existing just noticeable distortion (JND) research predominantly focuses on the visual channel, with insufficient consideration given to the impact of audio characteristics on overall perception. Therefore, this paper proposes a multimodal JND estimation model tailored for audio-visual content. Specifically, we map audio signals into saliency to drive visual perception, thereby integrating visual and auditory channels. We model auditory JND as a modulation matrix across both spatial and temporal domains, combining it with existing spatio-temporal visual JND models to achieve an audio-visual multimodal JND framework. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model exhibits superior subjective quality compared to several typical models and possesses excellent noise masking capabilities.

records.title: Neural Video Compression with Intra-Guided Context Modulation
records.abstract: Neural video compression (NVC) methods have made significant advances in recent years. Most advanced conditional-coding-based NVC frameworks employ temporal context modeling to eliminate temporal redundancy. However, existing context modeling schemes mainly rely on mining the temporally propagated context from inter-frame reference information, while neglecting the pivotal intra-frame reference information of the current coding frame for the conditional coding paradigm. In this paper, we address this limitation by modulating the temporal context in two steps. Specifically, first, we propose an intra-guided temporal context refinement method, in which intra-frame reference information from the current frame is explicitly exploited to modulate the temporal context, yielding a more accurate context for efficient contextual coding. Second, to further utilize the intra-frame information, we propose the hyper-modulated prior modeling, where the temporal prior is further modulated by the hyperprior to derive a more accurate prior for entropy modeling, enabling more precise probability estimation. Experimental results demonstrate that our codec can achieve 27.4% bitrate reduction over the traditional video codec H.266/VVC, and obtain 12.6% bitrate saving compared to the previous state-of-the-art neural video codec DCVC-FM.

records.title: Harmonized Tabular-Image Fusion via Gradient-Aligned Alternating Learning
records.abstract: Multimodal tabular-image fusion is an emerging task that has received increasing attention in various domains. However, existing methods may be hindered by gradient conflicts between modalities, misleading the optimization of the unimodal learner. In this paper, we propose a novel Gradient-Aligned Alternating Learning (GAAL) paradigm to address this issue by aligning modality gradients. Specifically, GAAL adopts an alternating unimodal learning and shared classifier to decouple the multimodal gradient and facilitate interaction. Furthermore, we design uncertainty-based cross-modal gradient surgery to selectively align cross-modal gradients, thereby steering the shared parameters to benefit all modalities. As a result, GAAL can provide effective unimodal assistance and help boost the overall fusion performance. Empirical experiments on widely used datasets reveal the superiority of our method through comparison with various state-of-the-art (SoTA) tabular-image fusion baselines and test-time tabular missing baselines. The source code is available at https://github.com/njustkmg/ICME26-GAAL.

records.title: Towards Implicitly Accurate Touch: Understanding and Modeling Moving Target Selection in Vibration Environments
records.abstract: With touchscreens increasingly integrated into vehicles, cabins, and cockpits, understanding and facilitating user interaction in dynamic environments has become an important research topic. While many existing studies focus on user performance in static tasks under dynamic conditions, relatively little attention has been paid to dynamic tasks such as moving target selection. This paper investigates pointing performance in moving target selection under varying levels of vibration, aiming to reveal how vibration affects user interaction with moving targets. We propose a vibration-aware Ternary-Gaussian model to predict pointing uncertainty. Compared to the baseline model, our approach reduces the mean Wasserstein distance by 56.33%. Furthermore, based on this model, we implement an implicit assistance technique in a real-world in-vehicle scenario, improving selection accuracy by 56.32%, which demonstrates the practical effectiveness of the proposed method. This work advances the understanding of moving target selection in vibration environments and provides modeling and design insights that can inform future research on dynamic touch interaction.

records.title: Dual-Stream Swin Transformers for Multimodal Behavior Inference via Eye Movements
records.abstract: Human eye movements provide critical behavioral cues for tasks such as disease screening and identity recognition. Existing eye-tracking-based classification methods typically focus on fixation-based feature extraction followed by averaging or temporal fusion of visual scene features, rather than modeling gaze patterns. As a result, the final features for classification in these methods fail to capture complex dynamic gaze patterns and discriminative eye-tracking details, such as saccade amplitude and direction and the global spatial positioning and sequential distribution of gaze transitions. To address these challenges, we propose a balanced dual-stream Transformer architecture that jointly models visual scene content and gaze dynamics. Specifically, the framework integrates a hierarchical 2D Swin Transformer encoder for spatial scene semantics with a Swin-inspired 1D temporal encoder, which combines windowed self-attention, shift-based cross-window interactions, and hierarchical merging to capture essential multi-scale temporal gaze dynamics. The two encoders are designed with matching depth and feature dimensionality, ensuring stable optimization and providing an effective mechanism to integrate the representation of dynamic gaze patterns with global visual scene embeddings. After encoding, the visual and gaze embeddings are fused via parameter-free element-wise addition, a strategy that outperforms other common fusion approaches due to the structurally aligned dual-stream design. Extensive experiments across five datasets and four classification tasks demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms traditional CNN+RNN and Transformer-based baselines, achieving strong subject-level performance and robust behavioral discrimination. Our source code is available at \url{https://github.com/RobertTang0/GazeImageFusionModel-ICME2026}.

records.title: PartMatch: Part-Aware Pseudo-Labeling for Fine-Grained Semi-Supervised Learning
records.abstract: Fine-grained visual classification (FGVC) is characterized by subtle inter-class differences that are often localized in small, discriminative object parts. While Vision Transformers (ViTs) naturally highlight such regions through their attention mechanisms, existing semi-supervised learning (SSL) methods rely solely on global pseudo-labels, which may be highly unstable for fine-grained categories. In this work, we introduce PartMatch, a part-aware semi-supervised framework that integrates TransFG-style part token extraction into the FreeMatch paradigm. Our method constructs entropy-weighted part-level predictions, fuses them with global weak-view predictions via a reliability-aware combination, and enforces part--global consistency through a KL regularization loss. This design stabilizes pseudo-labels, reduces ambiguity among visually similar classes, and improves the effectiveness of unlabeled data in FGVC. We evaluate PartMatch on multiple fine-grained benchmarks, including CUB-200-2011, Stanford Dogs, NABirds, and iNaturalist18. Across 1%, 10%, and 25% labeled-data settings, PartMatch consistently achieves superior performance over strong semi-supervised baselines. Visualizations further reveal that part tokens remain stable under strong augmentations, leading to clearer feature clusters and more reliable pseudo-labeling. Our approach is simple, lightweight, and compatible with mainstream SSL frameworks, offering a new direction for fine-grained SSL.

records.title: HiGCD: History-Anchored Hierarchical Relevance Induction for Generalized Category Discovery
records.abstract: Generalized Category Discovery (GCD) requires recognizing known categories while discovering novel ones. Previous methods typically enforce strict geometric separation between different clusters. Although shaping a clear decision boundary, they often neglect the latent hierarchical semantic relevance among categories. To address this, we propose HiGCD, an approach that leverages prediction ambiguity to uncover these intrinsic structures. Specifically, we introduce Reliability- Gated Historical Consistency (RHC) to stabilize known-class representations for semantic exploration. Building on this stable foundation, Hierarchical Semantic Regularization (HSR) trans- lates the relevance of different categories encoded in prediction confusion patterns into soft semantic constraints to shape mean- ingful representation space. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of HiGCD on known- class retention and novel-class discovery. The visualization and ablation studies further clarify proposed modules for better interpretability. Code is available at: https://github.com/HITORI111/HiGCD.

records.title: Curvilinear Geometric Partitioning Mode for Video Coding
records.abstract: Geometric partitioning has received intensive attention during the development of video coding standards. The existing geometric partitioning mode (GPM) in Versatile Video Coding (VVC) employs a set of predefined straight lines as the partitioning candidates. However, in natural videos, the moving objects usually exhibit complex, non-linear contours, resulting in motion boundaries that are difficult to represent compactly using the straight-line partitioning. To address this limitation, this paper propose a curvilinear geometric partitioning mode (CGPM). In CGPM, Bézier parametric curves are introduced to provide more flexible partitions that better align with object contours. The curves are represented using a three-control point (CP) formulation, with the existing GPM syntax reused to signal the two endpoint CPs. A decoder-side derivation scheme is further developed to obtain the intermediate CP and reconstruct the complete curvilinear partitioning without incurring significant signaling overhead. Experimental results demonstrate that CGPM achieves average BD-rate reductions of 0.29% and 0.15% compared to VTM-23.0 under low-delay B (LDB) and random access (RA) configurations, respectively, with a marginal increase in decoder complexity.

records.title: SongFormer: Scaling Music Structure Analysis with Heterogeneous Supervision
records.abstract: Music structure analysis (MSA) underpins music understanding and controllable generation, yet progress has been limited by small, inconsistent corpora. We present SongFormer, a scalable framework that learns from heterogeneous supervision. SongFormer (i) fuses short- and long-window self-supervised learning representations to capture both fine-grained and long-range dependencies, and (ii) introduces a learned source embedding to enable training with partial, noisy, and schema-mismatched labels. To support scaling and fair evaluation, we release SongFormDB, the largest MSA corpus to date (over 14k songs spanning languages and genres), and SongFormBench, a 300-song expert-verified benchmark. On SongFormBench, SongFormer sets a new state of the art in strict boundary detection (HR.5F) and achieves the highest functional label accuracy, while remaining computationally efficient; it surpasses strong baselines and Gemini 2.5 Pro on these metrics and remains competitive under relaxed tolerance (HR3F). Code, datasets, and model are open-sourced at https://github.com/ASLP-lab/SongFormer.
