records.title: AGGC-QA: A Novel Quality Assessment Database for AI-Generated Game Characters
records.abstract: Game character (GC) design is a fundamental component of game development and has traditionally depended heavily on designers’ professional expertise and creative experience. With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), text-to-image (T2I) models have emerged as efficient and scalable solutions for AI-generated game characters (AGGCs) design. However, the lack of explicit human control in generative processes often leads to various visual distortions and semantic inconsistencies, which can adversely affect player experience. To systematically investigate and evaluate the quality issues inherent in current T2I models for AGGC design, we select 7 representative T2I methods and construct a novel AGGC Quality Assessment (AGGC-QA) dataset. Specifically, based on 80 GC prompts, a total of 560 AGGCs are generated. Two different tasks are considered, designing derivative works based on existing GCs and designing entirely original GCs, to comprehensively assess the AGGC design capabilities of T2I models under different creative constraints. Subjective evaluation experiments conducted with multiple participants reveal notable limitations in current T2I models for AGGC design, with clear performance disparities. To establish objective evaluation baselines, 14 quality assessment algorithms are applied to the AGGC-QA dataset. The experimental results demonstrate that existing objective assessment methods struggle to reliably capture perceptual quality. These findings highlight the pressing need for more effective and robust quality assessment algorithms tailored specifically to AGGC design.

records.title: DEOF: Dual-Expert Orthogonal Fusion for Universal Deepfake Detection
records.abstract: Rapid advancements in deepfakes blur the boundary between real and forged images, challenging digital authenticity. Existing methods often rely on a single feature space and struggle to capture high-level semantics and fine-grained artifacts.To address this issue, we propose a Dual-Expert Orthogonal Fusion (DEOF) framework. We utilize a frozen CLIP as the semantic expert and design a Frequency-Spatial Decoupling and Recomposition module (FSD-R), combined with ResNet-50, as the artifact expert, which captures both local texture artifacts and global generative patterns via DWT and FFT. To prevent semantic and artifact information from interfering with each other, we design a Semantic Purification Module (SPM) that utilizes SVD-based orthogonal projection to eliminate semantic interference from artifact features. Purified artifact features are then integrated with CLIP mid-layer features via cross-attention. Experiments show that DEOF achieves superior performance across 22 distinct generative models, demonstrating robust cross-generator generalization.

records.title: Texture-Aware Non-Separable Transform Set Selection for Inter-Prediction Residuals in Video Coding Beyond VVC
records.abstract: Non-separable transforms in video coding beyond VVC deliver notable gains for directional residuals. For inter residuals, transform set selection is guided by whole-block texture analysis. However, inter residual energy is often spatially concentrated, and global HoG extracted from the prediction may be dominated by residual-inactive regions, thereby masking the direction most relevant to transform coding. To enhance transform--residual alignment, we propose a texture-aware scheme that localizes a salient region by maximizing prediction-gradient energy and derives the dominant direction from local texture. On this basis, two strategies are developed: (i) gradient-saliency single transform set selection (GS-STSS) that switches between global and local cues, and (ii) global--local enhanced multiple transform set selection (GL-EMTSS) for GPM blocks that refines the second candidate using local texture, thereby enhancing MTSS expressiveness. Experiments on ECM-16.1 under LDB demonstrate consistent coding-efficiency improvements for both strategies, with marginal runtime overhead.

records.title: TokTic: Alleviating Multimodal Hallucinations via Token-Intervention Decoding
records.abstract: Despite significant progress, Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are prone to generating responses that are inaccurate and inconsistent with the content of the images, a phenomenon referred to as ``hallucination." To mitigate this issue, we introduce token-intervention decoding (TokTic), a simple yet effective solution that can alleviate hallucinations in a training-free manner. TokTic consists of a token pruning strategy and a token replacement strategy. The proposed token pruning strategy seeks to reduce the negative impact of irrelevant image and text tokens in the current decoding step, thereby encouraging MLLMs to focus on relevant multimodal contexts. On the other hand, the proposed token replacement strategy aims to mitigate the object co-occurrence-induced hallucinations by replacing the generated object token with embeddings of its neighboring tokens. We conducted extensive experiments on several benchmarks, and the evaluation demonstrates that TokTic can effectively alleviate multimodal hallucinations.

records.title: Frequency-Conformer for Automatic Piano Transcription
records.abstract: Automated piano transcription remains challenging due to the intricate harmonic structures and temporal dependencies of musical signals. Recent methods increasingly adopt Transformers but often fail to fully exploit the synergy between CNNs and attention mechanisms. To address this, we propose Frequency-Conformer (F-Conformer), a hierarchical framework designed for robust feature learning. Our approach features a Convolution and Attention Double Branching (CADB) module that concurrently captures fine-grained local spectral textures and long-range temporal dependencies. Furthermore, a Cross-task Semantic Guidance (CSG) mechanism is introduced to refine feature fusion by leveraging inherent semantic correlations between different transcription sub-tasks. Experimental results on the MAESTRO dataset demonstrate that F-Conformer achieves state-of-the-art performance with F1 scores of 98.06% (Onset), 91.17% (Offset), and 89.80% (Velocity), while significantly reducing parameter complexity and computational overhead compared to existing sequential models.

records.title: NFAuR-5.1: A Benchmark for Visually Guided 5.1-Channel Audio Reconstruction
records.abstract: Immersive media relies heavily on accurate collaboration between visual and spatial audio. However, while visual rendering has advanced to dynamic 4D scenes, a significant gap remains in high-quality spatial audio resources and reconstruction methods, especially for the widely adopted 5.1-channel audio. To this end, we construct the NFAuR-5.1 benchmark, which is the first benchmark for visually guided 5.1-channel audio reconstruction from normal-field-of-view (NFOV) video, to the best of our knowledge. It encompasses the FSV-5.1 dataset and the NFAuR-5.1-Base baseline model. Our constructed FSV-5.1 dataset comprises 2,604 high-quality film-source video clips covering cartoon, science fiction, literary, musicals, and documentary, each providing an original 5.1 channel mixed audio and six isolated audio tracks. Further, our proposed NFAuR-5.1-Base integrates feature extraction, audio-visual fusion, and audio post-processing modules to reconstruct 5.1-channel audio from mono input for NFOV videos. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed NFAuR-5.1-Base is effective in 5.1-channel audio reconstruction for NFOV videos on our FSV-5.1 dataset.

records.title: STGV: Spatio-Temproal Hash Encoding for Gaussian-based Video Representation
records.abstract: 2D Gaussian Splatting (2DGS) has recently become a promising paradigm for high-quality video representation. However, existing methods employ content-agnostic or spatio-temporal feature overlapping embeddings to predict canonical Gaussian primitive deformations, which entangles static and dynamic components in videos and prevents modeling their distinct properties effectively. These result in inaccurate predictions for spatio-temporal deformations and unsatisfactory representation quality. To address these problems, this paper proposes a Spatio-Temporal hash encoding framework for Gaussian-based Video representation (STGV). By decomposing video features into learnable 2D spatial and 3D temporal hash encodings, STGV effectively facilitates the learning of motion patterns for dynamic components while maintaining background details for static elements.In addition, we construct a more stable and consistent initial canonical Gaussian representation through a key frame canonical initialization strategy, preventing from feature overlapping and a structurally incoherent geometry representation. Experimental results demonstrate that our method attains better video representation quality (+0.98 PSNR) against other Gaussian-based methods and achieves competitive performance in downstream video tasks.

records.title: Graph-Guided Adaptive Channel Elimination for KV Cache Compression
records.abstract: Large Language Models have revolutionized natural language processing, achieving unprecedented success across a vast range of tasks. However, their practical application in long-context scenarios is severely hampered by the formidable memory footprint of the Key-Value cache. While channel pruning has emerged as a promising compression strategy, existing methods evaluate channel importance in isolation, fundamentally ignoring the inter-channel interactions that collectively dictate model performance. This oversight leads to suboptimal pruning decisions. To address this, we introduce \textbf{GRACE} (\textbf{GR}aph-guided \textbf{A}daptive \textbf{C}hannel \textbf{E}limination), a novel framework that reframes KV cache compression as a graph-based optimization problem. GRACE models channels as nodes and their interactions as weighted edges, enabling the identification of a near-optimal channel subset for pruning by minimizing the reconstruction error of the attention weight matrix. Furthermore, GRACE incorporates an adaptive protection mechanism that shields salient key channels from removal, ensuring a robust autoregressive decoding process. Extensive experiments show that GRACE can reduce KV cache size by 60\% with negligible performance degradation, consistently outperforming the state-of-the-art method.

records.title: ModuLoRA: A Modular Scheduling Framework for Multi-Tenant LoRA-Based LLM Inference in Multimedia Services
records.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in AI-driven multimedia and content generation services, where scalable multi-tenant inference under shared GPU resources is critical. Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) enables parameter-efficient customization, but existing multi-tenant LoRA inference systems struggle to handle heterogeneous online and offline workloads due to insufficient scheduling adaptability, resulting in inefficient adapter management, suboptimal batching, and degraded quality of service. This paper presents ModuLoRA, a modular and adaptive scheduling framework for multi-tenant LoRA-based LLM inference. ModuLoRA integrates dynamic priority scheduling, adapter-aware scheduling, and feedback-driven adaptive batch control within a unified scheduler to jointly optimize latency, throughput, and GPU utilization. We implement ModuLoRA on a production-grade LLM serving platform and evaluate it using diverse mixed workloads. Experimental results demonstrate that ModuLoRA substantially reduces tail latency and improves GPU utilization compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

records.title: FedDMLA: A Dynamic Multi-factor Layered Federated Aggregation Mechanism for Non-IID ECG Signal Diagnosis
records.abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) analysis is critical for cardiovascular disease diagnosis; however, strict privacy regulations hinder centralized data collection. While federated learning provides a promising solution, its performance is often affected by the heterogeneity of data across different institutions, particularly Non-IID data and long-tailed distributions. To address these challenges, we propose FedDMLA, a dynamic layered aggregation framework that evaluates client updates across three dimensions—directional alignment, update magnitude, and convergence quality—to compute reliable contribution scores. These scores guide layered aggregation through asymmetric weighting of shallow feature extractors, deep representation blocks, and classification heads, effectively balancing model stability and plasticity. Additionally, we incorporate an adaptive sparse communication strategy that balances communication efficiency and model performance through parameter sparsification and stochastic recovery mechanisms. Experiments on large-scale multi-center ECG benchmarks demonstrate that FedDMLA significantly improves global generalization ability, diagnostic accuracy, and robustness, while reducing computational and communication costs.

records.title: An Edge-aware Prompt-enhanced SAM for Ultrasound Image Segmentation
records.abstract: Ultrasound image segmentation is essential for delineating anatomical structures and lesions, providing the foundation for accurate diagnosis. While the Segment Anything Model (SAM) has demonstrated remarkable success on natural images, its performance on ultrasound data is often hindered by poor boundary delineation. To address this limitation, we propose EP-SAM, an edge-aware and prompt-enhanced adaptation of SAM. Specifically, we leverage multi-block feature extraction from the image encoder to enrich coarse-to-fine semantic representations, while edge-aware supervision of the image encoder improves robustness to contour ambiguity and speckle noise. By integrating these complementary cues, EP-SAM generates high-quality prompts that effectively guide the model toward target regions of interest. Experimental results on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that EP-SAM consistently outperforms existing SAM-based methods.

records.title: Proto-Context: VLM-Enhanced Prototypes for Continuous Video Scene Graph Generation
records.abstract: Video Scene Graph Generation methods currently have achieved promising performance. However, they suffer from semantic ambiguity in local representations and temporal discontinuity, resulting in inconsistent predictions. Vision-Language Models have achieved notable success in capturing global semantics. In this paper, we propose a novel framework Proto-Context, termed Prototype and Context-based Video Scene Graph Generation. The main idea is to exploit global semantic reasoning and explicit temporal modeling to generate robust scene graphs. Proto-Context includes VLM-Driven Semantic Feature Modulation, Temporal Manifold Evolution via Prototypes, and a Progressive Temporal Inference Curriculum. The Modulation module recalibrates visual features using global intents to resolve ambiguity. The Manifold Evolution aligns latent trajectories with semantic prototypes to ensure temporal smoothness. The Curriculum strategy facilitates causal reasoning by progressively masking temporal inputs. Extensive experiments on the Action Genome dataset demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches.

records.title: ES-Net: Early-Split Model For Fine-Grained Music Source Separation Beyond Four Stems
records.abstract: Music source separation becomes increasingly challenging as the number of target stems grows beyond the standard four, due to stronger spectral overlap and low-energy stems that are easily masked. While late-split architectures remain effective in a four-stem setting, our analysis shows that they become limiting in fine-grained settings with five or six stems, where more stem-specific modeling is required. To address this, we adopt an early-split strategy to build ES-Net, by providing each stem with a stem-specific feature before decoding. We further propose a Selective Fusion module tailored for the early-split framework that adaptively integrates skip connections with stem-specific features to enhance spectral reconstruction. Our study provides the first clear evidence that early-split strategy offers distinct advantages specifically in the fine-grained (five– or six-stem) settings, offering new guidance for the design of multi-stem music separation networks. Experiments on the six-stem MoisesDB dataset show that ES-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance with an average SDR of 8.0 dB, with notable improvements on low-energy stems.

records.title: ADINFN: Adaptive Dual-Branch Implicit Neural Fusion Network for Multispectral and Hyperspectral Image Fusion
records.abstract: Multispectral and hyperspectral image fusion (MHIF) aims to reconstruct high-resolution hyperspectral images (HR-HSI) by leveraging the spectral richness of hyperspectral images and the spatial details of multispectral images. Recently, Implicit Neural Representation (INR) has gained attention as a novel paradigm for modeling spatial or spectral details with high fidelity. However, existing INR-based methods are limited by local and static receptive fields. To address these challenges, we propose the Adaptive Dual-Branch Implicit Neural Fusion Network (ADINFN) with two parallel branches for spatial and spectral domains. The spatial branch employs an attention-guided INR network within an adaptive window for continuous fine-grained reconstruction. Concurrently, the spectral branch leverages Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to first aggregate global high-frequency details, followed by an INR network within an adaptive window for amplitude enhancement. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets show that ADINFN outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in fusion performance.

records.title: DS-JSCC: Diffusion-Driven Semantic Joint Source-Channel Coding for Video Transmission
records.abstract: The transition from bit-centric to semantic-centric paradigms in future wireless systems requires video transmission schemes that preserve high-level meaning rather than merely pixel-wise fidelity. Existing deep joint source-channel coding (Deep JSCC) methods provide graceful degradation under noisy channels but still suffer from severe blur and semantic inconsistency at low SNRs, and they lack generative capability when information is irreversibly lost. In this paper, we propose DS-JSCC, a diffusion-driven semantic-aware Deep JSCC framework for wireless video transmission. DS-JSCC integrates a latent diffusion generative model with a multi-frame JSCC backbone, semantic guidance from CLIP features, and an SNR-guided adaptive noise scheduling strategy, forming a generative semantic communication system. Experiments on multiple video benchmarks and simulated wireless channels show that DS-JSCC outperforms state-of-the-art Deep JSCC methods by up to 3.2 dB PSNR and about 15% LPIPS reduction at low SNR, while improving CLIP-based semantic similarity by around 10%. These results highlight the potential of diffusion-based generative models for robust semantic video communications.

records.title: DSD: Dual Self-Distillation for Robust Audio Tagging
records.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) is pivotal for enhancing the performance and compressibility of audio classification models. However, conventional KD typically relies on pre-training large-scale teacher models, significantly increasing training complexity and computational cost. In this paper, we propose a Dual Self-Distillation (DSD) framework tailored for Audio Tagging. This framework enables efficient knowledge transfer during the fine-tuning of pre-trained Vision Transformers (ViT) without external teachers, solely by harnessing the model’s internal potential. Specifically, to exploit internal representations, we introduce Hierarchical Intra-Layer Self-Distillation. This mechanism appends auxiliary classifiers to intermediate layers, utilizing deep semantic features and ground-truth labels to supervise shallow layers. Simultaneously, to improve robustness, we employ Evolutionary Mask-Consistency Distillation. This strategy combines the Mean Teacher mechanism with masked data augmentation, leveraging smoothed historical parameters to guide current training. Experiments on the DCASE 2025 Task 4 dataset demonstrate that DSD boosts baseline accuracy from 51.54% to 61.05%, verifying its effectiveness.

records.title: Boundary-Uncertainty Guided Image-Video Fusion Network to Predict Extrathyroidal Extension Using Preoperative Dual-View CEUS Video
records.abstract: Preoperative prediction of extrathyroidal extension (ETE) using ultrasound (US) and contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) is crucial for thyroid cancer staging and treatment planning. Most existing deep learning methods emphasize semantic features while neglecting subtle boundaries and peritumoral tissue features essential for assessing ETE. To address this, we propose a new boundary-uncertainty guided image-video fusion network (BGIFN) to extract dynamic features related to peritumoral tissues from straightened boundary area (SBA) sequences. This network integrates an uncertainty-guided static branch for extracting boundary-anatomical related features from US images with a clinical knowledge-driven dynamic branch that processes CEUS videos, their SBA sequences and CEUS TI-RADS clinical features to establish a dynamic global-local (perfusion-peritumoral) feature space. These static and dynamic features are fused using bidirectional cross-attention aligned with clinical reasoning. Experiments on 434 dual-view CEUS videos demonstrate that BGIFN achieves an AUC of 0.751, outperforming state-of-the-art methods and improving AUC, Accuracy, and F1 by 13.4%, 11.5%, and 22.9%, respectively, compared to a senior radiologist.

records.title: Learning to Reason Robustly: Entropy-Aware Noise-Augmented Policy Optimization for Large Audio Language Models
records.abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) boosts LLMs’ reasoning abilities but faces two key challenges when applied to audio reasoning tasks. Models tend to overfit superficial acoustic patterns and fail under perturbations, while policies suffer from entropy collapse and converge prematurely. We propose EAPO (Entropy-Aware Noise-Augmented Policy Optimization), which integrates dynamic noise injection for acoustic augmentation within the RL training and sequence-level entropy-aware advantage shaping for response exploration. EAPO achieves state-of-the-art on MMAU among Qwen2-Audio variants, outperforming the previous best Audio-Thinker by 1.6%, and maintains competitive performance on both benchmarks with Qwen2.5-Omni, all using fewer than 10k samples without auxiliary reward models. This demonstrates that entropy-aware advantage shaping and dynamic augmentation enable effective audio reasoning under limited resources.

records.title: PromptMask: A Controllable Text-Driven Masking Framework for Self-Supervised Visual Pretraining
records.abstract: The scarcity of annotations in medical imaging limits the training of robust vision models. Masked image modeling (MIM) alleviates this, but random high-ratio masking is often inefficient and poorly aligned with task semantics. We propose PromptMask, a controllable text-driven masking framework that uses a vision–language model to localize semantically relevant regions from prompts and applies region-specific masking ratios to reduce background redundancy. This simple control mechanism improves semantic alignment and enables effective pretraining under substantially lower masking ratios. Extensive experiments show that our method: (1) consistently surpasses MIM baselines on classification, detection, and instance segmentation, with gains of up to +3.1 in classification accuracy, +1.3 in BoxAP, and +1.1 in MaskAP; (2) generalizes robustly across modalities with diverse anatomical structures and imaging characteristics; and (3) achieves higher performance with 40% masking than prior methods with 70% masking, demonstrating improved pretraining efficiency.

records.title: PACD-Net: Permutation-Aware Collaborative Decoding with Spectral-Temporal Refinement for Scene Text Recognition
records.abstract: Scene text recognition remains challenging due to diverse visual variations and insufficient exploitation of linguistic priors. We propose PACD-Net, a novel framework that addresses these limitations through three key innovations: (1) Spectral-Temporal Feature Refinement (STFR) that enhances visual features in both frequency and sequential domains; (2) Position-Guided Cross-Modal Alignment (PGCA) that adaptively fuses visual and semantic information based on positional characteristics; and (3) Permutation-Aware Collaborative Decoding (PACD) that synergistically combines autoregressive (AR), non-autoregressive (NAR), and iterative refinement paradigms. Extensive experiments on seven benchmarks demonstrate that PACD-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance with 91.6% average accuracy, outperforming previous methods by 1.4% while maintaining real-time inference speed.

records.title: SPG-Codec:Exploring the Role and Boundaries of Semantic Priors in Ultra-Low-Bitrate Neural Speech Coding
records.abstract: Conventional neural speech codecs suffer from severe intelligibility degradation at ultra-low bitrates, where the bottleneck transitions from acoustic distortion to semantic loss. To address this issue, this paper conducts a systematic investigation into the role and fundamental limits of integrating frozen semantic priors – specifically HuBERT and Whisper – into neural speech coding. We introduce and quantitatively validate a novel Semantic Retirement phenomenon: while semantic constraints reduce the Word Error Rate (WER) by up to over 10 percent at 1.5 kbps, their benefits rapidly diminish beyond 6 kbps, indicating a practical capacity boundary. We further uncover a clear trade-off between different prior types: acoustic-rich priors (HuBERT) better preserve prosodic and timbral details, whereas high-level linguistic priors (Whisper) effectively suppress phonetic hallucinations in noisy environments (reducing hallucination rates by 26 percent) and substantially narrow the generalization gap for unseen speakers. Building on these findings, we propose a bitrate-aware regulation strategy that dynamically adjusts prior strength to optimize the trade-off between semantic consistency and perceptual naturalness. Extensive experimental evaluations confirm that our approach achieves competitive intelligibility and noise robustness compared to existing baselines, offering a principled pathway toward ultra-low-bitrate generative speech coding.

records.title: Certainty is Safety: A Multimodal Synergistic RL Framework using Quantified Uncertainty for Robust Low-Altitude Navigation
records.abstract: Robust autonomous navigation in low-altitude scenarios requires efficient processing of heterogeneous multimodal data under stringent on-board computational constraints. Addressing the persistent exploration–safety dilemma in such resource-limited environments, we propose a Cognizant Reinforcement Learning framework that couples quantified policy uncertainty with both safety and exploration. A lightweight concatenation fusion backbone encodes proprioception, goal intent, geometric perception, and dynamic entities, while a Beta policy provides an explicit single-pass uncertainty signal from its distribution concentration, without the overhead of heavy ensembles. This unified signal drives a synergistic loop: (1) an Uncertainty-Gated Safety Shield that ensures robustness against dynamic obstacles, and (2) an epistemic-driven intrinsic motivation for adaptive exploration. Furthermore, we employ Safety Distillation to internalize constraints into the neural policy, enabling efficient inference on edge devices. Simulations show a 97.3% success rate with a 2.7% collision rate, validating the framework as a resource-aware, robust solution for embodied aerial decision-making.

records.title: Cross-Domain Device-Free Fingerprinting Localization Using LoRa Antenna-Array
records.abstract: LoRa technology demonstrates considerable potential for long-range, device-free fingerprint-based localization. However, owing to its narrowband nature, the received signal contains limited spatial feature information, which readily leads to fingerprint ambiguity in long-range localization scenarios. Moreover, environmental changes (e.g., opening a window) alter location fingerprints, resulting in degraded localization performance when fingerprints constructed in the original environment are applied to a new environment. To address these challenges, we first employ a multi-antenna receiver array to construct high-dimensional fingerprints by fusing amplitude ratios and phase differences, thereby substantially enhancing spatial discriminability. Second, we propose an unsupervised cross-domain localization framework. The proposed framework incorporates hybrid contrastive learning to strengthen feature representations and leverages multi-layer feature alignment and domain-adversarial learning to extract robust, domain-invariant features, enabling accurate localization in the target domain. Extensive experiments conducted in diverse scenarios, including a conference room, a long corridor, and a hall, demonstrate superior generalization capabilities, achieving 90% cross-domain localization accuracy even within a 45 m corridor.

records.title: STAR: Mitigating Cascading Errors in Spatial Reasoning via Turn-point Alignment and Segment-level DPO
records.abstract: Structured spatial navigation is a core benchmark for Large Language Models (LLMs) spatial reasoning. Existing paradigms like Visualization-of-Thought (VoT) are prone to cascading errors in complex topologies. To solve this, we propose STAR, a two-stage framework grounded on topological anchors, and introduce the RedMaze-23K dataset with human-inspired turnpoint annotations. The first stage uses supervised fine-tuning to help models internalize spatial semantics and prune redundant paths. The second adopts Spatial-aware Segment-level Direct Preference Optimization (SDPO) to refine self-correction in long horizon navigation. Experiments show STAR achieves state-of the-art performance among open-source models: its 32B variant outperforms DeepSeek-V3 (29.27% vs. 25.00%) and reaches 82.4% of GPT-4’s performance.

records.title: AV-CrossMamba: Multi-Modal Cross-Mamba Modeling for Audio-Visual Speech Separation
records.abstract: Existing convolutional speech separation models mainly capture short-range structure and struggle to represent long temporal context. Recurrent and self-attention–based models extend the modeling range, but their computation and memory cost grow quickly with sequence length. To address these limitations, we propose a novel method called AV-CrossMamba, a dual-path framework that applies selective state modeling in both intra- and inter-chunk pathways. Specifically, the AV-CrossMamba consists of two key modules including the IntraMamba and the InterMamba. The IntraMamba employs bidirectional Mamba modules to update audio temporal states for intra-chunks, and uses bottleneck attention and depthwise separable convolutions to enhance local modeling. The InterMamba fuses visual cues through bidirectional gating, gated refinement, and bidirectional Mamba stacks, enabling temporally consistent and noise robust modulation of audio states. Extensive experiments on VoxCeleb2 and LRS2 benchmark show that our method consistently improves separation quality under both short and long utterances. The AV-CrossMamba achieves superior performance to the Transformer-based counterparts, especially on the long-duration and challenging VoxCeleb2 benchmark.

records.title: Image Complexity Assessment via Detail-Semantics Synergy Network
records.abstract: The perception of image complexity by human visual system (HVS) relies on the synergism between low-level structural details and high-level semantic information. However, existing methods for image complexity assessment (ICA) often prioritize semantic content, ignoring fine-grained visual patterns. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel model to explicitly emulate the dual-pathway processing mechanisms of the HVS, which is termed as detail-semantics synergy network (DSSN). DSSN features a sparse grouping attention (SGA) module that captures primitive visual patterns via sparse self-attention coupled with cross-block interactions. Besides, a guide fusion (GF) strategy is employed to integrate these details with high-level semantics, simulating HVS cognition. Furthermore, we introduce entropy-based heatmaps to visualize the spatial contributions of visual patterns. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DSSN achieves superior alignment with human perception and consistently exceeds existing methods.

records.title: Learning Collaborative Solutions with Multi-Level Priors for Snapshot Compressive Imaging
records.abstract: Deep unfolding networks (DUNs) have demonstrated strong potential for snapshot compressive imaging (SCI). However, most existing approaches are limited to a single-solution inference paradigm with a fixed prior, restricting their ability to exploit diverse and complementary priors for complex SCI reconstruction. In this paper, we propose a novel Multi-Solution Collaborative Deep Unfolding Network with Multi-Level Priors (MS-DUN) for SCI reconstruction, which jointly learns and exploits both intra-solution priors and inter-solution priors within an end-to-end unfolding framework. For intra-solution priors, we introduce learnable gradient and step-size maps for spatially adaptive descent, together with a spectral–spatial prior module embedded in the proximal operator to capture intrinsic structural information within each solution branch. For inter-solution priors, we design a cross-solution collaborative mechanism that dynamically aggregates and refines features across multiple solution branches, enabling mutual guidance between global semantics and fine-grained details to exploit solution diversity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed MS-DUN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art HSI reconstruction methods in terms of reconstruction accuracy, robustness, and generalization.

records.title: Geometry-Aligned Sketch Representation Learning via Line-Jet Masked Autoencoding
records.abstract: Sketch representation learning is becoming increasingly important for a wide range of applications, such as drawing-based psychological analysis. However, mainstream image representation learning methods are not tailored to sparse, geometry-dominated sketches, and tend to bias the learned representations toward texture and appearance rather than stroke geometry. To this end, we propose Line-Jet Masked Autoencoder (LJ-MAE), which reconstructs a geometric field deterministically computed from Gaussian scale-space derivatives. This field encodes stroke saliency with gradient magnitude, stroke orientation with a half-turn periodic encoding, and stroke bending with bounded level-line curvature. It enables geometry-aligned masked reconstruction over the sketch manifold without relying on vector strokes, skeletonization, or graph construction. Extensive experiments and ablation studies on TU-Berlin, QuickDraw, TUB-Scene, and the domain-specific HTP dataset demonstrate the superiority of our proposed method.

records.title: ArticuSim: Articulation-Aware Modeling from a Single Image for Simulation
records.abstract: Modeling articulated objects from a single image remains extremely challenging, due to the complex kinematic constraints and topological structures. Current paradigms often suffer from coarse-grained attribute modeling and the inherent feature aliasing problem in serial architectures. Furthermore, existing methods rarely produce the actionable dynamic parameters essential for physical simulation. To address these limitations, we present ArticuSim, an end-to-end single-view framework for articulated object modeling, featuring Attribute-Aware Attention (AAA), a Disentangled Attention Mechanism (DAM), and Simulation-Ready Representation (SRR). AAA explicitly captures hierarchical dependencies among articulation attributes, while DAM parallelizes heterogeneous feature processing to mitigate interference and improve representation fidelity. Crucially, our pipeline automatically generates simulation-ready representations, bridging the gap between visual reconstruction and physical application. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ArticuSim outperforms state-of-the-art methods in geometric and articulation estimation while directly supporting downstream robotic manipulation tasks.

records.title: BUS-IT: An Image-text Pairing Dataset for Semantic Segmentation of Breast Ultrasound Tumor
records.abstract: Textual modality is indispensable for enabling segmentation models to learn semantically meaningful representations of lesions. However, existing breast tumor segmentation datasets generally lack high-quality textual modality annotations, which severely hinders the development of multimodal segmentation. records.title: SAEFRig: An Automatic Rigging Model Based on Structure-Aware Encoding and Fusion
records.abstract: Automatic skeletal rigging is a crucial task in 3D animation, aiming to generate skeletal structures and skinning weights for three-dimensional character models to enable realistic motion control. To address this, this paper proposes SAEFRig, a three‑stage automatic rigging framework. The method transforms unordered point clouds into structurally ordered representations via Structure‑Aware Encoding (SAE), and employs a Multi‑Skeleton Fusion (MSF) module to integrate complementary information from skeleton estimation and skinning weight prediction, progressively refining the rigging outcome. Experiments conducted on datasets such as Mixamo and VRoid (including their extended versions Mixamo+ and VRoid+) demonstrate that SAEFRig outperforms existing methods in both skeleton generation and skinning weight prediction, exhibiting stronger robustness and accuracy especially under non‑standard poses.

records.title: Multimodal Emotion Recognition under Modality Uncertainty
records.abstract: Multimodal emotion recognition utilizes complementary information from visual, textual, and acoustic cues. However, real-world scenarios often suffer from missing modalities and uneven modality contributions, leading to suboptimal fusion. In this paper, we propose a multimodal fusion framework that effectively handles missing modalities and modality weighting through adaptive mechanisms. Our approach integrates Uncertainty-Aware Modality Dropout (UAMD), which dynamically drops unreliable modalities based on prediction confidence during training, to regulate the contribution of each modality at the sample level, Tri-directional Cross-Modal Attention to capture rich pairwise interactions, and Self-Attention Fusion to refine the joint representation. Additionally, we propose a novel auxiliary loss function that encourages balanced modality utilization while aligning uncertainty with modality concentration. Extensive experiments on the MELD and IEMOCAP datasets demonstrate superior performance over state-of-the-art methods, particularly under missing modality conditions.

records.title: A Lightweight Residual Check for Stabilizing Adaptive Loop Filter in Video Coding
records.abstract: The adaptive loop filter (ALF) is an efficient coding tool in video coding, designed to minimize the mean squared error (MSE) between original and reconstructed images. By analyzing the Wiener-Hopf equations solving process, which utilizes Cholesky decomposition, this paper identifies and addresses a critical numerical instability that severely degrades ALF's performance. This issue is particularly pronounced when encoding screen content at low quantization parameters (QPs), where the autocorrelation matrix becomes highly ill-conditioned. Cholesky decomposition of these ill-conditioned matrices, stored in single-precision floating-point, leads to significant errors, resulting in inaccurate filter coefficients and severe visual artifacts. To address this issue, we propose a lightweight and effective solution: a residual check performed after the decomposition to detect instability and discard the resulting unreliable coefficients. Experimental results show that, based on the Beyond Versatile Video Coding (VVC) test model, the Enhanced Compression Model (ECM), the proposed method achieves BD-rate reductions of 0.09% for class F sequences and 0.72% for class text and graphics with motion (TGM) sequences on luma component under the all intra (AI) configuration. The proposed design guarantees a more stable ALF in video coding. Owing to its coding performance and zero memory overhead, the proposed approach has been adopted by the latest ECM.

records.title: Robust Generative Audio Quality Assessment: Disentangling Quality from Spurious Correlations
records.abstract: The rapid proliferation of AI-Generated Content (AIGC) has necessitated robust metrics for perceptual quality assessment. However, automatic Mean Opinion Score (MOS) prediction models are often compromised by data scarcity, predisposing them to learn spurious correlations—such as dataset-specific acoustic signatures—rather than generalized quality features. To address this, we leverage domain adversarial training (DAT) to disentangle true quality perception from these nuisance factors. Unlike prior works that rely on static domain priors, we systematically investigate domain definition strategies ranging from explicit metadata-driven labels to implicit data-driven clusters. Our findings reveal that there is no "one-size-fits-all" domain definition; instead, the optimal strategy is highly dependent on the specific MOS aspect being evaluated. Experimental results demonstrate that our aspect-specific domain strategy effectively mitigates acoustic biases, significantly improving correlation with human ratings and achieving superior generalization on unseen generative scenarios.

records.title: Hierarchical Multi-Agent Video Trimming via Reflective Semantic Planning
records.abstract: Automated video trimming remains challenging due to the semantic gap between raw footage and narrative intent, combined with the computational cost of multimodal processing. Existing methods either perform isolated highlight detection without narrative coherence or rely on exhaustive visual token consumption. In this paper, we present ChatTrimming, a hierarchical multi-agent framework that achieves efficient natural-language-driven video trimming through reflective semantic planning. Our approach constructs shot-based hierarchical representations that preserve temporal topology while enabling text-based reasoning. A Director Agent generates structured narrative scripts, which are mapped to footage through novel reflective semantic matching that resolves shot allocation conflicts via ranked retrieval with intelligent fallback. Quality optimization employs sliding-window assessment across five aesthetic dimensions. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art zero-shot performance: 87.0% mAP on YouTube Highlights surpasses both zero-shot and supervised methods, while 65.7% on TVSum exceeds all zero-shot approaches, requiring only 1% of the token cost of recent agent-based methods.

records.title: CCE-SR: Luma-Guided Cross-Component Enhancement for Chroma Reconstruction in Neural Video Coding
records.abstract: Neural Network-based Video Coding (NNVC) leverages deep learning techniques to improve coding efficiency. Decoder-side super-resolution (SR) is commonly used for resampling-based video coding in NNVC. However, in YUV420 format, chroma components (UV) are downsampled and further degraded during resampling, causing severe information loss at low bitrates. The existing SR methods always treat the UV components in the same way as the luma (Y) component, which makes it extremely difficult to recover the chromatic details from sparse sampling. To address this issue, we propose an SR model called CCE-SR, integrated with a luma-guided Cross-Component Enhancement (CCE) module that utilizes a cross-component attention mechanism to improve the UV reconstruction by applying the structural constraints of the Y component. The initially reconstructed UV is then enhanced through attention-based refinement blocks, thereby capturing the channel-wise and long-range spatial dependencies within the UV components. Experimental results show that our method achieves BD-rate savings of -3.39% and -3.26% for the U and V under the random access (RA) configuration compared with NNVC-13.0. Compared with VTM-11.0, our method achieves BD-rate savings of -2.57%, -1.02%, and -0.17% for the Y, U, and V, respectively.

records.title: SABER: A Semantic-Aligned Brain Network Analysis Framework via Multi-scale Hypergraphs
records.abstract: Effective brain disease diagnosis requires the synergy of brain connectivity patterns and high-level semantic knowledge. Existing methods, however, largely treat semantics from large language models (LLMs) as auxiliary features or supervision, limiting their direct role in decision-making and constraining classification stability and robustness. To overcome this, we propose a semantic-aligned brain network framework that actively integrates LLM-derived semantics into the prediction process. Specifically, ROI-level semantics are first incorporated via global self-attention to enrich node representations and provide whole-brain context. Multi-scale hypergraphs are then constructed to explicitly model functional subnetworks and multi-ROI interactions, addressing the locality limitations of traditional GNNs and capturing high-order dependencies. Finally, a decision-level semantic alignment mechanism selectively injects patient-specific textual embeddings into graph representations, enabling semantics to directly guide predictions without perturbing the underlying network structure. Experiments on public brain network datasets ABIDE and ADHD-200 demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, enhanced stability, and improved interpretability, particularly in small-sample settings.

records.title: When Meaning Isn't Literal: Exploring Idiomatic Meaning Across Languages and Modalities
records.abstract: Idiomatic reasoning deeply intertwined with metaphor and culture remains a blind spot for contemporary language models, whose progress skews toward surface-level lexical and semantic cues. For instance, the Bengali idiom আঙ্গুর ফল টক (angur fol tok, "grapes are sour"): it encodes denial-driven rationalization, yet Naïve models latch onto the literal fox-and-grape imagery. Addressing this oversight, we present "Mediom," a multilingual, multimodal idiom corpus of 3,533 Hindi, Bengali, and Thai idioms, each paired with gold-standard explanations, cross-lingual translations, and carefully aligned text-image representations. We benchmark both large language models (textual reasoning) and vision language models (figurative disambiguation) on Mediom, exposing systematic failures in metaphor comprehension. To mitigate these gaps, we propose "HIDE," a Hinting-based Idiom Explanation framework that leverages error-feedback retrieval and targeted diagnostic cues for iterative reasoning refinement. Collectively, Mediom and HIDE establish a rigorous test bed and methodology for culturally grounded, multimodal idiom understanding embedded with reasoning hints in next-generation AI systems.

records.title: SEEC: Segmentation-Assisted Multi-Entropy Models for Learned Lossless Image Compression
records.abstract: Recently, learned image compression has attracted considerable attention due to its superior performance over traditional methods. However, most existing approaches employ a single entropy model to estimate the probability distribution of pixel values across the entire image, which limits their ability to capture the diverse statistical characteristics of different semantic regions. To overcome this limitation, we propose Segmentation-Assisted Multi-Entropy Models for Lossless Image Compression (SEEC). Our framework utilizes semantic segmentation to guide the selection and adaptation of multiple entropy models, enabling more accurate probability distribution estimation for distinct semantic regions. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that SEEC achieves state-of-the-art compression ratios while introducing only minimal encoding and decoding latency. With superior performance, the proposed model also supports Regions of Interest (ROIs) coding condition on the provided segmentation mask. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/chunbaobao/SEEC}.

records.title: StyleSpeaker: Fine-Grained Style Modeling for Speech-Driven 3D Facial Animation
records.abstract: Speech-driven 3D facial animation aims to generate expressive and temporally coherent facial motions from speech signals. Speech predominantly dictates the coarse motion trends of the lip region, while specific styles determine the details of lip motion and the overall facial expressions. Prior works lack fine-grained learning in style modeling, which reduce the accuracy of synthesized motions and hamper the adaptation capability to unseen speakers. To address this, we propose a novel framework, StyleSpeaker, which utilize a style encoder to capture speakers' styles from facial motions. The styles are then integrated into the coarse motion features via a style infusion module, which employs a set of style primitives to learn fine-grained style representation. Hence, StyleSpeaker possesses robust style modeling capability for seen speakers and can rapidly adapt to unseen speakers without fine-tuning. Extensive qualitative and quantitative experiments on three public datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches.

records.title: MindHub: Towards Cross-Subject 3D Decoding via Subject-Invariant EEG Embeddings
records.abstract: Decoding human vision from brain activity is critical for understanding the cognitive processes. Although recent research has achieved significant success in 2D visual decoding, 3D decoding from Electroencephalogram (EEG) remains three main challenges: (1) the scarcity of paired EEG-3D datasets and noise in EEG signals, (2) individual differences across subjects, and (3) the inherent difficulty of reversing from 1D EEG to 3D objects. To address above issues, we propose a new decoding framework named MindHub for cross-subject EEG-to-3D decoding. Specifically, a Dual-branch Spatial-Temporal and Frequency (DSTF) encoder is first designed for subject-specific representations, while a Mixture of Experts-Decoupler (MoE-D) is then introduced to couple these features with individual differences and subject-invariant features. Additionally, a two-stage Cross-Subject Adversarial Adaptation (CSAA) method is proposed to mitigate individual differences and facilitate generalized feature representations. In the inference stage, a Cross-Subject Memory Elicitation (CSME) mechanism is proposed to transfer cross-subject knowledge and enhance decoding performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MindHub achieves state-of-the-art performance in the per-subject-per-model paradigm and comparable performance in cross-subject scenarios.

records.title: Semantics Communication with Scene Graph for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
records.abstract: Communication of teammates in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is a way of exchanging local observation information. Current communication works mainly focus on exchanging observation data or encoding features, whose knowledge is complete but overlapped, from camera or lidar sensors. Redundant knowledge creates stress on communication bandwidth with part of key information being buried. Faced with that, we propose Scene Semantics Communication MARL (SCMAC), which dynamically selects agents for semantic information exchange, improving their comprehension of multi-agent scenes to foster cooperation. First, the scene state is semantically modeled through a priori knowledge, and the scene graph is employed to express semantic information that is hidden in the original sensory data. Second, semantic information fusion is conducted after spatial topology being used in selecting communication agents. Third, cooperative strategies are learned under shared reward conditions through centralized training and decentralized execution paradigm. Experiments indicate that our method outperforms baselines in various cooperative tasks.

records.title: SMDP: Source-aware Music Deepfake Detection via Disentangled Perception and State Space Fusion
records.abstract: With the rapid advancement of deep generative models, verifying the authenticity of multimedia content faces unprecedented challenges. Existing audio deepfake detection methods predominantly target the speech domain, with limited research dedicated to music deepfake detection and lacking source-aware capabilities to address diverse music synthesis techniques. This paper presents SMDP, a novel framework for robust music deepfake detection that adopts a source-aware design philosophy by processing different components of the music through multiple specialized modules to achieve complete perception. Specifically, SMDP leverages prompt-tuned encoders specialized for speech and music to capture vocal and instrumental patterns, while incorporating frequency-domain features for representation enhancement. The framework adopts a disentangled perception strategy by analyzing instrumental and vocal features separately, then strategically integrates them through a multi-level cross-fusion mechanism. Extensive evaluations on widely used benchmarks demonstrate that SMDP consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in music deepfake detection.

records.title: GAANet: Global-guided Asymmetric Attention Network for Audio-Visual Speech Separation
records.abstract: Multi-scale design is crucial for efficient audio-visual speech separation, yet effectively modeling multiscale information for audio-visual feature fusion remains challenging. We argue that the limited capacity of existing approaches primarily arises from: 1) treating features from different modalities in the same manner, and 2) overlooking the role of global features. To address these issues, we propose a Global-guided Asymmetric Attention Network (GAANet). Our model introduces two core innovations: first, an asymmetric multi-scale fusion framework that allows audio and visual streams to extract and interact with features at their respective optimal temporal resolutions, removing the need for symmetric temporal downsampling; second, a global-guided attention mechanism that compresses each modality into a compact global token with a temporal dimension of one, which then provides high-level semantic cues to guide both intra- and inter-modal fusion across scales. Experiments on LRS2 and VoxCeleb2 demonstrate that GAANet achieves state-of-the-art performance, reaching 16.5 dB SI-SNRi on LRS2 and 14.0 dB on VoxCeleb2, while maintaining a lightweight computational profile with only 3.3M parameters and 19.8G MACs. These results highlight the strong potential of asymmetric temporal modeling and global guidance for efficient and robust multimodal fusion. The source code is publicly accessible at \url{https://github.com/redizzy/GAANet}.

records.title: ACFormer: Agent-based Communication Transformer for Audio-Visual Segmentation
records.abstract: Audio-visual segmentation (AVS) aims to identify and segment sound-producing objects by jointly exploiting visual and auditory cues. However, most existing methods treat each frame independently and fail to capture temporal dependencies, which limits segmentation performance in dynamic scenes. To address this issue, we propose ACFormer, an efficient audio-visual segmentation framework with inter-frame interaction. First, the Audio-to-Visual Attention module (A2VA) injects audio-guided saliency into visual features to highlight sound-related regions. Then, the Multi-Scale Agent Generator (MSAG) produces high-level semantic agents through hierarchical pooling, reducing low-level noise and yielding more compact, semantically consistent agents for efficient inter-frame communication. Finally, the Inter-Frame Agent-based Communication module (IFAC) performs lightweight agent-level interaction, avoiding the computational burden of full-feature operations. Experiments on benchmark datasets show that ACFormer achieves state-of-the-art performance on MS3 and AVSS datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness.

records.title: Low-Light Image Enhancement via Shared Encoding and Brightness-Aware Hybrid Loss
records.abstract: Low-Light Image Enhancement (LLIE) is a critical upstream task for robust high-level vision applications in challenging lighting conditions. LLIE methods often suffer from high computational overhead due to redundant feature extraction in independent color–intensity pathways. To address this, we propose an architecturally-efficient enhancement network operating in the HVI color space. We introduce a shared encoder with an asymmetric dual-head decoder that unifies early-stage feature extraction, significantly reducing architectural redundancy while maintaining high representational capacity. Furthermore, we develop a multi-scale brightness-aware hybrid loss that dynamically balances pixel-level, structural, perceptual, and edge constraints according to brightness distribution divergence, enabling robust supervision across diverse lighting conditions. Extensive experiments on eight benchmark demonstrate that our method achieves competitive enhancement quality with only 0.55M parameters and 6.73G FLOPs, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in both efficiency and effectiveness. The code is released at https://github.com/Shili-Ma/LightCIDNet.

records.title: Self-Learning Surprise Detection in Spatial Audio for Viewport-Aware 360-Video Streaming
records.abstract: Adaptive streaming of 360-degree video relies on viewport prediction to allocate bandwidth efficiently. Current approaches predominantly use visual saliency or historical gaze patterns, neglecting the role of spatial audio in guiding user attention. This paper presents a self-learning framework for detecting ``surprising'' auditory events, moments that deviate from learned temporal expectations, and demonstrates their utility for viewport prediction. The proposed architecture combines SE(3)-equivariant graph neural networks with recurrent temporal modeling, trained via a dual self-supervised objective. A key feature is the natural modeling of temporal attention decay: surprise is high at event onset but diminishes as the listener adapts. Experiments on the AVTrack360 dataset show that integrating audio surprise with visual cues reduces bitrate waste by up to 18\% compared to visual-only methods.

records.title: S^2-MAE: Spatial Speech Masked Autoencoders for Multi-Channel Speech Representation Learning
records.abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) has substantially ad- vanced speech processing by leveraging large-scale unlabeled data. However, most existing SSL frameworks are designed for mono speech, which is suboptimal for in-the-wild multi-channel speech due to their limited ability to model spatial cues. In this paper, we propose the spatial speech masked autoencoders (S^2-MAE), a multi-channel SSL framework for learning spatially informed speech representations. S^2-MAE introduces a spatially aware multi-dimensional masking strategy that jointly operates across time, frequency, and microphone array dimensions, with frequency-dependent masking ratios to account for heterogeneous information distributions. In addition, multi-level acoustic consistency losses are employed to enhance representation learning across complementary acoustic dimensions. Experiments on multi-channel speech separation and direction-of-arrival estimation demonstrate that S2-MAE consistently outperforms several representative mono-channel SSL models, highlighting the advantages of native multi-channel pre-training for spatial speech representation learning.

records.title: TA-AVIS: Temporal Alignment for Audio-Visual Instance Segmentation
records.abstract: Audio-Visual Instance Segmentation (AVIS) leverages audio-visual information to localize, segment and track sounding objects in videos, with valuable applications in video content analysis, human-computer interaction, intelligent surveillance and autonomous driving. Existing methods cannot solve two key audio-visual temporal alignment problems in long videos: short-term synchronization deviation and long-term identity drift. We propose TA-AVIS, an AVIS framework for audio-visual temporal alignment. We design the Audio-Visual Alignment Encoder (AVAE) to encode long-term audio temporal context and relieve short-term misalignment; propose the Video Instance-Guided Query (VIGQ) to initialize queries using visual priors for avoiding identity drift; and build the Hierarchical Audio-Visual Collaborative Decoder (HAVAD) to enforce temporal consistency verification in decoding. Experiments on AVISeg show TA-AVIS surpasses the baseline in mAP, HOTA, FSLA under various settings, with significant improvements in complex multi-soundsource scenes.

records.title: RAP-INR: A Rate-Adaptive Linear Positional Encoding–Based Implicit Neural Representation for Point Cloud Attribute Compression
records.abstract: Implicit Neural Representation (INR) leverages coordinate-based neural networks to represent complex signals. While positional encoding and specialized activation functions are typically employed to mitigate spectral bias and capture high-frequency components, existing INR-based point cloud compression (PCC) methods often introduce excessive redun- dancy. Such ineffective encoding dimensions interfere with the network’s ability to learn signal patterns. Furthermore, conventional activation functions struggle to fit intricate point cloud attributes, necessitating learnable alternatives. To ad- dress these challenges, we propose RAP-INR, which features Rate-Adaptive Linear Positional Encoding tailored to point cloud distributions. Additionally, we integrate multi-scale KAN (Kolmogorov-Arnold Network) activation functions to better characterize high-frequency details. Compression efficiency is further enhanced through piecewise quantization of network weights. Experimental results demonstrate that RAP-PCC achieves a 33.98% BD-Rate (Y) saving relative to PICO and a 6.97% saving compared to the latest G-PCC v31 standard.

records.title: Mitigating Density Imbalance in 3D Gaussian Splatting for Few-Shot Reconstruction
records.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) provides high-quality and real-time rendering for novel view synthesis; however, it often produces artifacts and blurry results under sparse-view settings. We find that sparse observations lead to uneven spatial constraints during optimization, exacerbating density imbalance, which subsequently gives rise to inaccurate Gaussians. To address this, we adopt a two-stage strategy that improves the density distribution. In preprocessing, we densify sparse distant regions of the SfM point cloud via a depth- and density-aware strategy. During training, we use two coupled 3DGS models for co-regularization and guide Gaussian updates with periodically rendered density maps, which are segmented into sparse, dense, and high-gradient regions to reflect different types of density errors. We then apply region-specific update rules—densification, reset, and perturbation—to progressively correct the imbalance. Experiments on LLFF, Mip-NeRF360, and DTU demonstrate the superiority of our approach.

records.title: Few-Shot Identity Adaptation for 3D Talking Heads via Global Gaussian Field
records.abstract: Reconstruction and rendering-based talking head synthesis methods achieve high-quality results with strong identity preservation but are limited by their dependence on identity-specific models. Each new identity requires training from scratch, incurring high computational costs and reduced scalability compared to generative model-based approaches. To overcome this limitation, we propose FIAG, a novel 3D speaking head synthesis framework that enables efficient identity-specific adaptation using only a few training footage. FIAG incorporates Global Gaussian Field, which enables the representation of multiple identities within a shared field while effectively mitigating severe identity conflicts through adaptive identity embedding, and Universal Motion Field, which captures the common motion dynamics across diverse identities. Benefiting from the shared facial structure information encoded in the Global Gaussian Field and the general motion priors learned in the Universal Motion Field, our framework enables rapid adaptation from canonical identity representations to specific ones with minimal data. Extensive comparative and ablation experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches, validating both the effectiveness and generalizability of the proposed framework.

records.title: SRP-Talker: Realistic Person-specific Talking Head Synthesis via Semantics-consistent Reconstruction Priors
records.abstract: Realistic person-specific 3D talking head synthesis is pivotal for digital avatars. While 3DGS-based methods offer superior rendering efficiency, they frequently suffer from person-specific audio-lip misalignment caused by insufficient pixel-level supervision and visual artifacts arising from decoupled modeling strategies. To address these limitations, we present SRP-Talker, a novel framework incorporating semantic-consistent reconstruction priors to regularize audio-driven generation. Our pipeline operates in three stages: (1) Semantic-Consistent Reconstruction: We establish a reference model via Gaussian Grouping to capture fine-grained facial semantics, providing explicit structural priors. (2) Reconstruction-Guided Motion Alignment: To resolve motion ambiguity, we constrain audio-driven deformations by aligning them with deterministic motion priors from the reference model, enforcing topology-preserving constraints for precise articulation. (3) Semantic-Guided Refinement: We introduce a semantic-aware inpainting module leveraging projected semantic masks as structural conditions to eliminate artifacts and enhance boundary naturalness. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in both lip-synchronization accuracy and photorealistic visual quality.

records.title: Why Learn What Physics Already Knows? Realizing Agile mmWave-based Human Pose Estimation via Physics-Guided Preprocessing
records.abstract: We revisit millimeter-wave (mmWave) human pose estimation (HPE) from a signal preprocessing perspective. A single mmWave frame provides structured dimensions that map directly to human geometry and motion: range, angle, and Doppler, offering pose-aligned cues that are not explicitly present in RGB images. However, recent mmWave-based HPE systems require more parameters and compute resources yet yield lower estimation accuracy than vision baselines. We attribute this to preprocessing modules: most systems rely on data-driven modules to estimate phenomena that are already well-defined by mmWave sensing physics, whereas human pose could be captured more efficiently with explicit physical priors. To this end, we introduce processing modules that explicitly model mmWave's inter-dimensional correlations and human kinematics. Our design (1) couples range and angle to preserve Spatial human structure, (2) leverages Doppler to retain human motion continuity, and (3) applies multi-scale fusion aligned with the human body. A lightweight MLP is involved as the regressor. In experiments, this framework reduces the number of parameters by 55.7–88.9\% on the HPE task relative to existing mmWave baselines while maintaining competitive accuracy. Meanwhile, its lightweight nature enables real-time Raspberry Pi deployment. Code and deployment artifacts will be released upon acceptance.

records.title: VDM: A Visibility-Driven Diffusion Model for Single-View 3D Point Cloud Reconstruction
records.abstract: Recent advances show strong potential for conditional diffusion models in single-view 3D point cloud reconstruction, yet effectively leveraging single-view image information for conditional control remains challenging. In this paper, we present a visibility-driven diffusion model (VDM) that significantly enhances reconstruction quality. VDM first selects key points through farthest point sampling and constructs a sub-point cloud within a defined radius. At its core lies a visibility-driven image–point cloud fusion module, which uses the camera pose aligned with the input image to divide the sub-point cloud into visible and invisible regions and fuse each with corresponding image features. This design stabilizes conditional guidance during the denoising process and leads to more accurate and reliable point clouds. Compared with existing state-of-the-art methods, our VDM is able to effectively reconstruct complex real-world images into 3D point clouds and demonstrates significant improvement on synthetic benchmarks. The code is available at https://github.com/fei1lee/VDM.

records.title: Decoupling Geometry and Appearance for Cross-Domain Crowd Counting
records.abstract: Crowd counting is a pivotal task in computer vision with extensive real-world applications. However, existing methods suffer from severe performance degradation when deployed across domains, primarily due to drastic variations in imaging conditions and camera perspectives. To address this, we analyze the domain gap from a generative perspective, identifying that cross-domain discrepancies mainly stem from two dimensions: appearance style variations and geometric projection differences. Building on this insight, we propose a novel framework, the Decoupling Crowd Counting Network (DCCNet), which explicitly decouples these factors to enhance cross-domain transferability. Specifically, DCCNet leverages the zero-shot capabilities of DepthAnything to inject robust geometric priors, effectively modeling perspective changes and scale variations to mitigate counting biases caused by geometric misalignment. Simultaneously, we introduce a dual-stream training paradigm to extract appearance style-invariant feature representations, ensuring robustness against appearance shifts. Extensive experiments on multiple cross-domain settings show that DCCNet consistently achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance. The code is available at https://github.com/Jason-Mar1/DCCNet.

records.title: VeloGauss: Learning Physically Consistent Gaussian Velocity Fields from Videos
records.abstract: In this paper, we aim to jointly model the geometry, appearance, and physical information of 3D scenes solely from dynamic multi-view videos, without relying on any physical priors. Existing works typically employ physical losses merely as soft constraints or integrate physical simulations into neural networks; however, these approaches often fail to effectively learn complex motion physics. Although modeling velocity fields holds the potential to capture authentic physical information, due to the lack of appropriate physical constraints, current methods are unable to correctly learn the interaction mechanisms between rigid and non-rigid particles. To address this, we propose VeloGauss, designed to learn the physical properties of complex dynamic 3D scenes without physical priors. Our method learns the velocity field for each Gaussian particle by introducing a Physics Code and a Particle Dynamics System, and ultimately incorporates Global Physical Constraints to ensure the physical consistency of the scene. Extensive experiments on four public datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms achieves state-of-the-art performance in both Novel View Interpolation and Future Frame Extrapolation tasks. To adhere to the principles of Double-Blind Review, we anonymously provide the code at https://github.com/DustSettled/VeloGauss

records.title: PartClick: Click-Guided Interactive 3D Part Segmentation
records.abstract: 3D part segmentation is fundamental to understanding and manipulating 3D objects. However, the high cost of 3D annotation leads to data scarcity, preventing models from large-scale training and hindering existing methods from balancing efficiency and accuracy. We present PartClick, a 3D interactive part segmentation framework. PartClick requires only a single forward during inference, significantly improving runtime compared to previous methods. We propose a pre-segmentation mechanism and a 3D Iterative Training Strategy (3DITS) that enable our method to achieve accurate segmentation and controllability with limited training data. Experiments show that PartClick achieves up to 12\% higher accuracy than other recent part-segmentation methods and enables controllable segmentation at arbitrary precision. Meanwhile, PartClick delivers orders of magnitude faster inference speed, achieving 100× speedup over SAMPart3D and enabling real-time interactive segmentation with millisecond-level latency.

records.title: Rethinking Depth-Aware Learning for Weakly Supervised Camouflaged Object Detection
records.abstract: Camouflaged object detection (COD) aims to segment objects that are visually indistinguishable from their surroundings, while most existing approaches rely on expensive pixel-level annotations. To reduce annotation burden, weakly supervised COD (WSCOD) has gained attention, but its performance is limited by sparse supervision and single-modality RGB cue, leading to inaccurate localization and blurred boundaries. In this paper, we rethink WSCOD from a depth-aware learning perspective and leverage depth cues derived from RGB images using a Depth Anything model to alleviate camouflage ambiguity without requiring extra depth inputs. Specifically, RGB and depth are processed in parallel by a dual-modal complementary network (DCLNet) with cross-modal interaction and feature fusion. A depth-aware pseudo-label generator (DPG) provides high-quality supervision by integrating semantic priors, geometric cues, and sparse localization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, validating the effectiveness of depth-aware learning for WSCOD. The code and results are available at https://github.com/zZxinyi/DCLNet.

records.title: Training-Free Semantic-Level Dynamic Reconstruction Based on Hierarchical Attention
records.abstract: Temporal multi-view dynamic reconstruction suffers from degraded performance due to inconsistent matching between dynamic objects and static backgrounds. Existing methods rely on motion separation but often produce imprecise dynamic masks and underutilize semantic information. Meanwhile, Vision-Language Models (VLMs), while rich in semantics, struggle with pixel-level accuracy and multi-view consistency for dynamic-static separation. To address these challenges, we propose a training-free framework for semantic-level dynamic reconstruction in multi-view videos. Specifically, coarse-grained dynamic masks are generated by hierarchically aggregating latent dynamic cues from the intermediate layers and temporal windows of a feedforward reconstruction network, and then refined via VLM-assisted segmentation, where the VLM solely removes noise and background without explicitly inferring object motion. We further use the refined masks to suppress dynamic attention in intermediate layers, enhancing static scene reconstruction and camera pose estimation, while supporting downstream tasks such as dynamic object editing. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in semantic dynamic object separation and static scene reconstruction across diverse scenarios.

records.title: A Versatile Rate-Distortion Optimized RAHT Coding Layer for 3D Gaussian Splatting
records.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) offers breakthrough rendering efficiency, yet its massive storage overhead hinders practical deployment. To enable standardized transmission, MPEG is actively investigating the adaptation of legacy video and point cloud coding standards for a fast-track 3DGS compression solution. Focusing on the Geometry-based Point Cloud Compression (G-PCC) pathway, the Region Adaptive Hierarchical Transform (RAHT) serves as the primary tool for compressing the high-dimensional attributes that constitute the bulk of 3DGS data. However, the legacy RAHT design relies on uniform quantization and limited fixed-point precision, which constrains its effectiveness for high-dynamic-range 3DGS attributes. In this paper, we propose a standard-compatible, rate-distortion optimized (RDO) RAHT framework. We first introduce a configurable precision extension to reduce numerical errors, and then derive a rate–distortion model that allocates bits according to the hierarchical contribution of RAHT layers. Experimental results show that our method achieves an average BD-rate gain of 37.87% over existing G-PCC RAHT. Moreover, the proposed method is able to serve as an effective training-free transform layer to enhance other 3DGS compression pipelines.

records.title: DEHOI: A Depth-Enhanced Vision-Language Model for Egocentric Hand-Object Interaction Understanding
records.abstract: Egocentric hand-object interaction (HOI) understanding is a fundamental problem for embodied intelligence, as it directly reflects how humans perceive and manipulate objects in the physical world. Recent Vision Language Models (VLMs) have achieved remarkable progress in multimodal reasoning and open-vocabulary understanding. However, their performance remains limited in egocentric settings due to the unique challenges of first-person data, including severe motion blur, frequent occlusions by hands, small manipulated objects, and cluttered backgrounds. As a result, RGB-only models often rely on language priors rather than reliable visual evidence for interaction reasoning. In this work, we propose DEHOI, a depth-enhanced Vision Language Model for egocentric HOI understanding. By incorporating depth information as an explicit geometric cue, DEHOI provides complementary spatial information that helps disambiguate foreground interactions from background clutter. We design an effective depth integration strategy that selectively leverages depth to guide visual reasoning while maintaining compatibility with pretrained VLMs. Extensive experiments on egocentric HOI benchmarks show that DEHOI consistently improves object recognition, localization, and interaction reasoning over strong RGB-based baselines, especially for interaction-centric tasks.
