records.title: Boosting Neural Video Codec via Scale-Driven Online Flow Refinement
records.abstract: Although state-of-the-art neural video codecs (NVCs) have achieved remarkable performance, they suffer from limited generalization when encountering complex motion patterns unseen during training. To bridge this domain gap without the expensive cost of online fine-tuning, we propose a Training-Free Scale-Driven Online Flow Refinement (SOFR) method. Serving as a plug-and-play module, SOFR integrates motion information from coarse and fine scales and dynamically fuses them according to warping accuracy, effectively rectifying motion estimation errors with negligible computational overhead. Furthermore, we design a rate-aware strategy that selects different dynamic fusion strategies according to bitrate modes, and employs a reliability check based on warping error to ensure robustness. Extensive experiments on the USTC-TD dataset verify the effectiveness and generalization of SOFR across various NVC frameworks, including DCVC-SDD, DCVC-FM, and EHVC. Notably, it brings an average of 2.84% and 4.05% bitrate savings in terms of PSNR and MS-SSIM, respectively, to DCVC-FM with negligible coding time increase. Our code is available at https://github.com/SunnyMass/SOFR.

records.title: DCVC-MB: Neural B-Frame Video Compression using State Space Models
records.abstract: In this paper we propose DCVC-Mamba (DCVC-MB), a neural video codec framework for B-frame coding. Our approach incorporates an IBP frame strategy for low-delay B-frame coding, a spatio-temporal fusion model based on state-space models for bidirectional temporal prediction, and an entropy-aware skipping mechanism that selectively omits coding certain latents to reduce entropy coding times. In addition to our model contributions we also implement two inference-time strategies that enhance compression performance. Experimental evaluation shows that DCVC-MB compares favorably to existing NVCs and traditional codecs. The method demonstrates BD-rate reductions of up to 8.98% on average compared to prior neural video codecs, and improvements of up to 30.45% and 1.81% over the VTM-19.0-LDP and VTM-19.0-RA(Inter-GoP=16) benchmarks, respectively, contributing to advances in neural video compression.

records.title: Video Compression with Hierarchical Temporal Neural Representation
records.abstract: Video compression has recently benefited from implicit neural representations (INRs), which model videos as continuous functions. INRs offer compact storage and flexible reconstruction, providing a promising alternative to traditional codecs. However, most existing INR-based methods treat the temporal dimension as an independent input, limiting their ability to capture complex temporal dependencies. To address this, we propose a Hierarchical Temporal Neural Representation for Videos, TeNeRV. TeNeRV integrates short- and long-term dependencies through two key components. First, an Inter-Frame Feature Fusion (IFF) module aggregates features from adjacent frames, enforcing local temporal coherence and capturing fine-grained motion. Second, a GoP-Adaptive Modulation (GAM) mechanism partitions videos into Groups-of-Pictures and learns group-specific priors. The mechanism modulates network parameters, enabling adaptive representations across different GoPs. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TeNeRV consistently outperforms existing INR-based methods in rate-distortion performance, validating the effectiveness of our proposed approach.

records.title: Improving Gaze Fidelity in Generative Face Video Coding with Pupil Position Signaling
records.abstract: Generative Face Video Coding (GFVC) techniques achieve ultra-low bitrates by transmitting a few static 2D image(s), known as base picture(s), that are animated through a generative process using compact facial features to reconstruct a full animation, yet generated eye gaze often fails because pupil motion is not explicitly signaled. This paper presents a standardized pupil position signaling mechanism carried in the Generative Enhancement Face Video (GEFV) Supplemental Enhancement Information (SEI). The design comprises: (i) a normalized eye-local coordinate system; (ii) predictive sign–magnitude residual coding with a configurable precision factor; and (iii) an adaptive presence index that selectively omits left/right pupil updates when gaze motion is negligible. To keep the approach applicable to any GFVC backbone, we implement a proof-of-concept as a decoder-side post-processing module that uses the standardized pupil coordinates to redirect gaze, without modifying the underlying generative model. The resulting bitstream is generator-agnostic and can co-exist with other GEFV tools (e.g., background/chroma-key fusion). Experiments on the JVET GFVC reference software with several GFVC methods show that pupil SEI incurs only a minor bitrate overhead (typically about 0.4–2% at QP=22) while reducing gaze-trajectory errors by roughly 10–20% and improving perceived eye contact. The adaptive presence index further reduces pupil-signaling overhead by up to about 50% with negligible impact on quality. The proposed syntax has already been adopted in the current Versatile Supplemental Enhancement Information for coded video bitstreams (VSEI) standard (Rec.ITU-T H.274,|,ISO/IEC 23002-7).

records.title: FlipGuard: Defending Large Language Models Against Quantization-Conditioned Backdoor Attacks
records.abstract: Model quantization is essential for the efficient deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs), but introduces a critical vulnerability: Quantization-Conditioned Backdoor (QCB) attacks. In these attacks, malicious behaviors remain dormant in full-precision models and activate only after specific quantization distortions, bypassing standard security audits. To mitigate this, we introduce FlipGuard, a proactive defense framework that selectively perturbs model weights prior to quantization. By breaking the adversary’s precise alignment between weight patterns and quantization boundaries, FlipGuard suppresses backdoor activation without requiring access to training data or trigger samples. We further propose the Defense Effectiveness Ratio (DER), a unified metric to jointly evaluate security gains, utility preservation, and computational cost. Extensive experiments across seven LLMs (including StarCoder and LLaMA-family models) and three quantization schemes (INT8, FP4, NF4) demonstrate that FlipGuard effectively neutralizes QCBs across three scenarios, i.e., vulnerable code generation, content injection, and over-refusal, achieving high security with negligible performance degradation.

records.title: Embedding Densification via Recursive Adversarial Noise for Sparse Malware API Sequences
records.abstract: The ubiquity of intelligent media systems has rendered them prime vectors for cyberattacks. In recent years, large language model (LLM)–driven tools have democratized malware creation and obfuscation. The obfuscation process often strips away API context. Existing classifiers struggle with such raw sequences due to inherent sparsity stemming from their non-continuous, non-linguistic structure and repetitive patterns. To address this, we propose EDEN (Embedding Densification), a framework that injects guidance signals into the latent space to bolster feature representation. These signals are derived from adversarial perturbations but are repurposed as distributional transformation to map the sparse latent distribution to a denser and more discriminative one. EDEN introduces a Recursive Noise Inference Model (NIM) that approximates these label-dependent perturbations, eliminating the need for labels during inference. Experiments on benchmark datasets show that our method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques. Notably, EDEN boosts the BiLSTM baseline from 56.28\% to 82.68\% accuracy on MalAPI2019, surpassing fully fine-tuned CodeBERT. These results suggest representation-level densification is more crucial than token-to-token dependency modeling in sparse API sequences.

records.title: Multi-view Enhanced Adversarial Camouflage Attack against Monocular Depth Estimation
records.abstract: Monocular depth estimation (MDE) models, widely used in 3D reconstruction and autonomous driving applications, are susceptible to adversarial camouflage attacks. Existing methods rely on optimizing a local texture seed and transferring it to physical objects to disrupt depth perception, which face two challenges: local textures may misalign in real-world deployment, and direct optimization of high-resolution global textures suffers from inefficient pixel updates and multi-view gradient conflicts. To address these problems, we propose a Multi-view Enhanced Adversarial Camouflage (MEAC) attack that improves optimization efficiency and ensures robustness across viewpoints and distances. Specifically, the MEAC enhances efficiency by initializing from low-resolution global textures and applying a progressive upscaling strategy (Pups) to preserve texture coherence. Furthermore, we introduce multi-gradient projection descent (MGPD) to mitigate gradient conflicts from different angles. Numerous experiments show that MEAC achieves an average absolute distance error of 9.51 meters across six different MDE models in simulation under diverse viewpoints and distances, while maintaining great real-world attack performance.

records.title: AgentStudio: Multi-Agent Video Generation for Product Storytelling via Structured Role-Based Collaboration
records.abstract: Creating engaging product videos demands sophisticated storytelling, visual consistency, and brand identity preservation, yet manual production remains prohibitively costly and time-intensive. Existing automated video generation methods lack narrative depth and struggle to maintain product fidelity while crafting compelling stories. We present AgentStudio, a multi-agent collaborative framework for automated product advertisement video generation that transforms product images and brief textual descriptions into coherent narrative-driven videos. AgentStudio employs a blackboard architecture orchestrating seven specialized agent roles through structured debate mechanisms. The pipeline begins with visual profile extraction and creative concept proposal, followed by three-act narrative generation tailored to target audiences. An Art Director defines unified visual themes and compositional strategies for cross-shot consistency, while Technical Advisors and User Representatives iteratively refine narratives through debate-consensus loops until quality thresholds are met. The Photographer executes production through a customized dual-pathway synthesis approach: text-to-video generation for narrative scenes with identity-preserving conditioning, and image-to-image refinement followed by controlled animation for product close-ups. Final assembly enforces color harmony, lighting consistency, and seamless transitions across scenes. Comprehensive evaluation on 10 diverse products demonstrates that AgentStudio achieves 68.1% preference over single-model baselines and 62.7% preference over ablated variants without debate, with 50% higher motion density, 19.6% lower color incoherence, and substantially superior narrative quality compared to existing automated methods.

records.title: GenShield: Robust Watermarking against CFA-Display Aliasing via Generative Adversarial Mining
records.abstract: Robust watermarking against screen-shooting is critical for tracing data leakage through the ``analog hole.'' However, current methods suffer from a severe simulation-to-reality gap, typically relying on simplistic parametric heuristics or limited real-world captures that fail to cover the long-tail distribution of non-stationary Moir\'e aliasing. In this paper, we propose \textbf{GenShield}, a novel framework that bridges this gap by modeling distortions via a high-dimensional continuous manifold. Unlike prior arts limited by bounded datasets, we leverage Latent Diffusion Models (LDMs) to construct a \emph{Synthesized Aliasing Manifold}, enabling infinite sampling of realistic artifacts to cover rare ``corner cases'' in frequency collisions. We further introduce \textbf{Manifold-based Adversarial Mining (MAM)}, a strategy that efficiently serves as a hard example mining strategy on the aliasing manifold. Instead of random augmentation, MAM actively retrieves ``worst-case'' distortion patterns to optimize encoder robustness against fatal frequency collapses. Our simulator incorporates a physically grounded Photometric Response Alignment Network (PRAN) that ensures gradient stability while mimicking device-specific photometric shifts. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GenShield significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in bit recovery accuracy and exhibits superior cross-display generalization.

records.title: Rethinking Gradient-based Adversarial Attacks on Point Cloud Classification
records.abstract: Gradient-based adversarial attacks are widely used to evaluate the robustness of 3D point cloud classifiers, yet they often rely on uniform update rules that neglect point-wise heterogeneity, leading to perceptible perturbations. We propose two complementary strategies to improve both the effectiveness and imperceptibility of the attack. \textbf{WAAttack} employs weighted gradients to dynamically adjust per-point perturbation magnitudes and uses an adaptive step size strategy to regulate the global perturbation scale. \textbf{SubAttack} partitions the point cloud into subsets and, at each iteration, perturbs only those combinations with high adversarial efficacy and low perceptual saliency. Together, these methods offer a principled refinement of gradient-based attacks for 3D point clouds. Extensive experiments show that our approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in generating highly imperceptible adversarial examples. The code is available at https://github.com/chenjun0326/WA_SubAttack.

records.title: Screenshot Document Image Tampering Localization with Layout Conditioning Diffusion Model
records.abstract: Locating tampered regions in screenshot documents is a significant forensic challenge due to the subtle nature of tampering traces. Unlike scanned documents exhibiting detectable physical distortions, screenshots retain an undistorted background, forcing forensic analysis to rely on subpixel font rendering features within text regions. However, these features are subtle, vary across devices and platforms, and are often overlooked by methods designed for scanned documents. To address this, we propose a novel layout-conditioning diffusion model (LayoutDiff) to model rendering artifacts across diverse environments. Additionally, we introduce a residual-based tampering localization network (ResTL) to detect subtle rendering inconsistencies by analyzing residuals between original and restored images. We validate our method using a dataset of 7,200 diverse screenshot samples. Experiments show it significantly outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods in detecting tampering traces, with ResTL achieving an F1 score of 0.634 (3.94% improvement over the second-best) under the cross-platform Windows to Mac protocol.

records.title: Semantic-Preserving Prompt Hijacking: A Black-Box Adversarial Attack on Auto-Prompt Optimization
records.abstract: LLMs increasingly integrate auto-suggestion optimization modules, enabling them to rewrite and display user input before generating the final response. While this design aims to enhance transparency and trust, its process of autonomously selecting a single ``best" result from multiple candidate solutions allows attackers to hijack this optimization process by inducing subtle, imperceptible semantic shifts. To address this, we propose a semantic preservation hijacking attack method based on black-box conditions—Adaptive Greedy Local Search. This method hierarchically decomposes the input text, masks key language units, and dynamically adjusts candidate replacement words at predefined semantic checkpoints. This maximizes the deviation between the model output and the original intent while strictly maintaining semantic similarity to the original text. Experimental results on commercial and open-source LLM demonstrate that, under the same semantic similarity constraints, this method achieves a higher attack success rate than existing attack methods in over 2400 test cases. Code is available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/EDA5G6S8.

records.title: Non-contrastive Self-supervised Adversarial Training via Cluster Label Prediction
records.abstract: Recent studies have shown that integrating adversarial training into self-supervised learning (SSL) can significantly enhance model robustness. Non-contrastive self-supervised adversarial training (self-AT) exhibits superior efficiency compared to contrastive methods, yet its robustness remains inferior. This gap arises because non-contrastive self-AT models often lack effective and diverse optimization directions for adversarial learning. To address this problem, we propose CPLACL, a novel self-AT method using cluster-based pseudo-labels. By clustering features from a warm-up model, CPLACL calculates loss based on pseudo-labels to provide effective and diverse optimization directions for adversarial learning. To stabilize the training process, we propose a momentum-based update strategy for cluster centers, which ensures the consistency of pseudo-labels assigned to each sample throughout the training. Extensive experiments show that CPLACL significantly improves the robustness of non-contrastive self-AT methods and outperforms state-of-the-art self-AT methods. Especially, CPLACL improves robustness under Auto-Attack by 16.25% compared to SOTA methods on the CIFAR-10 dataset. Our code and appendix are available in the supplementary material.

records.title: Block Complexity Adaptive Secret Sharing for Reversible Data Hiding in Encrypted Images
records.abstract: Cloud outsourcing of images and video requires visual confidentiality and reversible data embedding. Existing reversible data hiding in encrypted images either relies on a single encrypted carrier, creating a single point of failure, or adopts secret sharing with limited capacity and coupled image recovery. This work presents a random coefficient feedback secret sharing framework that produces multiple encrypted shares with block adaptive representation. The scheme reserves space in sixteen bit containers, embeds secret and auxiliary data under secondary encryption, and supports separable extraction and lossless image reconstruction. Experiments on images and datasets show higher effective embedding rates than prior schemes. The generated shares exhibit near ideal entropy and differential statistics, and the cover image is recovered without distortion. Analysis further confirms strong key sensitivity and robustness to statistical and differential attacks. The framework offers a robust, capacity-efficient solution for secure multimedia storage and forensics in semi-honest cloud environments.

records.title: DisMoE: Can Distillation-Driven Frame-Level Mixture-of-Experts Enable Robust Micro-Expression Recognition
records.abstract: Micro-expression recognition (MER) aims to detect genuine emotions through subtle and transient facial movements. However, existing methods depend on apex annotations and precise prior knowledge, while failing to capture comprehensive temporal dynamics. To overcome these limitations, we propose a Distillation-Driven Mixture of Frame-Level Experts (DisMoE) framework, in which a Dynamic Interval Sampling (DIS) strategy is introduced to adaptively select temporal subsequences, thereby eliminating reliance on apex annotations and enhancing temporal robustness. A Continuous Attention (CA) block further refines emotion-relevant spatial cues and facilitates the modeling of temporal features. In parallel, the Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) dynamically fuses motion cues from multiple frame-level experts via a router network, while a Frame-level Distillation (FD) mechanism transfers complementary knowledge across frames to reinforce temporal coherence and discriminability. Extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets (CASME II, SAMM, SMIC-HS, and CAS(ME)$^3$) demonstrate that DisMoE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both accuracy and robustness. The code will be released upon acceptance.

records.title: EIB-Net: Entropy-Guided Information Bottleneck for Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection
records.abstract: The proliferation of photorealistic AI-generated images demands robust detection methods that generalize across diverse generative models. While existing approaches target manipulation-based forgeries with local artifacts, generation-based images (e.g., from diffusion models) lack such traces, posing a fundamental challenge. We observe that generative models prioritize global semantics at the expense of local texture fidelity, making low-texture regions key indicators of synthetic origin. To exploit this, we propose EIB-Net, an Entropy-guided Information Bottleneck Network. EIB-Net introduces a novel Image Entropy (IE) metric to automatically select the most informative (lowest-entropy) patch, then processes it with a Variational Information Bottleneck (VIB) to learn compact, generalizable features. Extensive experiments on DIFF, DiffusionForensics, and GenImage benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art performance: EIB-Net achieves 85.7\% accuracy using only 2\% of training data, outperforming full-image baselines by over 15\%, and maintains robust cross-generator generalization (83.5\% average accuracy on GenImage). Furthermore, our entropy-guided patch selection (EGPL) consistently enhances diverse backbones (CNNs and Transformers), proving its practical value for data-efficient detection.

records.title: EffeCFFD: Exemplar-free Federated Continual Face Forgery Detection
records.abstract: As rapidly-evolving face forgery techniques pose serious threats to society and individuals, most existing forgery detection models rely on closed-set offline training, suffering from a significant degradation in generalization performance when facing new forgery attacks. Although continual learning may be adopted to improve adaptability to new forgeries, most methods rely on sample replay to mitigate forgetting. These approaches encounter severe privacy leakage risks and storage bottlenecks in distributed scenarios where multi-party data cannot be shared. To address these challenges, we propose an exemplar-free federated continual face forgery detection framework (EffeCFFD). Instead of storing any historical samples, this framework maintains a globally shared universal adversarial perturbations pool to generate pseudo-forged samples that approximate the distribution of historical forgeries. Furthermore, a multi-level knowledge distillation strategy is incorporated to effectively prevent the forgetting of previous knowledge. We conducted extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets, including FFpp, CDF, WildDeepfake and DFDC. Under privacy constraints, the EffeCFFD significantly alleviates catastrophic forgetting and achieves state-of-the-art performance on cross-dataset generalization.

records.title: SAFE-DF: Early Explanation Injection for Explainable Deepfake Detection
records.abstract: Explainable face forgery detection is urgent for trustworthy face forgery detection. However, current explainable methods based on Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are plagued by a semantic gap. This stems from the late-stage injection of explanation abilities, where visual features are optimized for classification but lack forensic semantic alignment. To address the misalignment, we propose SAFE-DF (Semantic Alignment for Forgery Explanation), a novel framework that shifts the paradigm to Early Explanation Injection. Specifically, SAFE-DF incorporates an explanation-guided detector augmented with learnable forgery prompts, enabling the explicit extraction of multi-grained forensic tokens. Furthermore, we enforce semantic consistency during the feature extraction phase via a forgery text-image contrastive loss, ensuring that visual representations are pre-aligned with linguistic concepts before reaching the LLM. Extensive experiments on the DD-VQA dataset demonstrate that SAFE-DF achieves state-of-the-art performance in explanation quality while preserving high detection accuracy.

records.title: DUAP: Dual-task Universal Adversarial Perturbations Against Voice Control Systems
records.abstract: Modern Voice Control Systems (VCS) rely on the collaboration of Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and Speaker Recognition (SR) for secure interaction. However, prior adversarial attacks typically target these tasks in isolation, overlooking the coupled decision pipeline in real-world scenarios. Consequently, single-task attacks often fail to pose a practical threat. To fill this gap, we first utilize gradient analysis to reveal that ASR and SR exhibit no inherent conflicts. Building on this, we propose Dual-task Universal Adversarial Perturbation (DUAP). Specifically, DUAP employs a targeted surrogate objective to effectively disrupt ASR transcription and introduces a Dynamic Normalized Ensemble (DNE) strategy to enhance transferability across diverse SR models. Furthermore, we incorporate psychoacoustic masking to ensure perturbation imperceptibility. Extensive evaluations across five ASR and six SR models demonstrate that DUAP achieves high simultaneous attack success rates and superior imperceptibility, significantly outperforming existing single-task baselines.

records.title: User-Defined Visual Privacy Preserving via Vision–Language Region Anonymization
records.abstract: The increasing circulation of multimedia content has amplified concerns over visual privacy, particularly in scenarios where users wish to conceal nuanced, context-dependent information rather than fixed object categories. Addressing such personalized privacy demands requires identifying semantically sensitive regions and anonymizing them without compromising downstream utility. In this paper, we present UVPP, a user-defined visual privacy preserving framework that reformulates privacy protection as a vision–language alignment problem. Natural-language prompts are used to express user privacy intent, while a generalized privacy distance (GPD) quantifies the semantic affinity between textual descriptions and visual content. This metric guides both the localization of privacy-relevant regions and a fully differentiable anonymization process based on permutation rearrangement, enabling targeted concealment without injecting noise or disrupting global image structure. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UVPP achieves a superior privacy-utility trade-off compared to state-of-the-art baselines, exhibiting strong robustness against reconstruction and membership inference attacks.

records.title: Flatness-aware Transferable Adversarial Attacks on SAR Image Recognition
records.abstract: With the wide application of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) in Synthetic Aperture Radar Automatic Target Recognition (SAR-ATR), the vulnerability of SAR deep recognition models has raised security concerns. Adversarial examples, which introduce imperceptible perturbations to inputs, can significantly degrade the performance of DNNs. While existing gradient-based methods show promise in improving adversarial transferability, they suffer from gradient confusion due to coherent noise and a lack of tailored design for SAR images. In this work, we address these issues by introducing the concept of flat maxima and propose a novel Flatness-Aware Maximization (FAM) attack. Our method crafts SAR adversarial examples by maximizing loss within a local neighborhood using a ``max-min" optimization framework. By theoretical derivation and employing Taylor expansion, we approximate flat perturbations for both amplitude and phase. Additionally, we enhance robustness by sampling and averaging gradients to reduce variance and effectively explore the neighborhood space. Extensive experiments on the widely used MSTAR dataset demonstrate that our method significantly enhances the transferability of gradient-based attacks. Furthermore, FAM's performance is further boosted when combined with input transformation attack techniques.

records.title: AIPA: Adaptive Invisible Partitioned Backdoor Attack
records.abstract: Data poisoning–based backdoor attacks pose a significant security threat to deep neural networks (DNNs), as malicious behaviors can be implanted without accessing the training process. However, existing approaches often struggle to simultaneously achieve visual imperceptibility and robustness against state-of-the-art defenses. In this work, we examine the role of trigger diversity and propose an Adaptive Invisible Partitioned Backdoor Attack (AIPA). AIPA employs a discrete particle swarm optimization (DPSO) strategy to generate partition-specific, visually imperceptible triggers embedded into fine-grained victim class partitions. In addition, a lightweight local pixel displacement mechanism combined with adversarial augmentation is used to construct stealthy poisoned datasets. Experimental results show that AIPA achieves an attack success rate of 98.78% on MNIST while preserving 99.27% benign accuracy, and maintains an ASR of 39.55%–47.13% under mainstream detection and mitigation defenses.

records.title: PMBAC: Physical Multi-Modal Backdoor-Adversarial Collaborative Attack
records.abstract: Backdoor and adversarial attacks are two major threats to deep neural networks. Prior work typically treats them separately and evaluates them mainly in single-modal settings, leaving their interaction in cross-modal physical scenarios underexplored. In this paper, we propose a physical-world multi-modal backdoor–adversarial collaborative attack (PMBAC) with two key innovations. First, we introduce a multi-modal trigger localization algorithm that combines pose-derived anatomical priors with Bayesian optimization to identify detector-sensitive yet physically feasible placements, outperforming static template matching in accuracy, adaptability, and robustness. Second, we couple backdoor implantation with modality-aligned adversarial perturbations via micro-composite triggers and lightweight adversarial camouflage, posing additional challenges to single-attack detectors. Experiments in both digital and physical domains show strong performance, achieving 93.7% and 90.4% attack success rates in visible light and thermal infrared physical settings.

records.title: Mitigating Complexity-Induced Bias in Membership Inference Attacks for Diffusion Models
records.abstract: Driven by rising privacy concerns regarding diffusion models, researchers have increasingly investigated membership inference attacks (MIAs). Existing score-based attacks typically assume that decision scores solely reflect the model’s memorization of a given sample. However, our analysis reveals that decision scores reflect not only the model’s memorization but also a systematic, complexity-induced bias. To mitigate this bias, we propose Dual-Model with Entropy Augmentation (DME), which leverages a pre-trained model to estimate this bias and applies entropy-based weighting to adaptively calibrate the strength of the correction. Experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate that DME achieves average improvements of up to 10.9% in AUC and 13.6% in ASR over three baselines, with particularly pronounced advantages in low–false-positive rate (low-FPR) regimes.

records.title: Knowledge Priors for Identity-Disentangled Open-Set Privacy-Preserving Video FER
records.abstract: Facial expression recognition (FER) relies on facial data that inherently expose identity and thus raise significant privacy concerns. Current privacy-preserving methods typically fail in realistic open-set video settings where identities are unknown, and identity labels are unavailable. We propose a two-stage framework for video-based privacy-preserving FER in challenging open-set settings that requires no identity labels at any stage. To decouple privacy and utility, we first train an identity-suppression network using intra- and inter-video knowledge priors derived from real-world videos without identity labels. This network anonymizes identity while preserving expressive cues. A subsequent denoising module restores expression-related information and helps recover FER performance. Furthermore, we introduce a falsification-based validation method that uses recognition priors to rigorously evaluate privacy robustness without requiring annotated identity labels. Experiments on three video datasets demonstrate that our method effectively protects privacy while maintaining FER accuracy comparable to identity-supervised baselines.

records.title: Band-Attention Modulation Network for Robust Face Forgery Detection
records.abstract: Face forgery detection faces critical challenges in generalizing to unseen manipulation techniques and remaining robust under image compression, which often obscures subtle artifacts. While frequency-domain analysis has shown promise, existing methods typically rely on fixed filters or coarse band separation, lacking the adaptability to learn task-specific spectral cues. To address this, we propose the Band-Attention Modulation Network (BAM-Net), a novel framework that pioneers learnable, fine-grained modulation of frequency components for forgery detection. At its core is the Band-Attention Modulation (BAM) mechanism, which transforms an image into its Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) spectrogram and learns to dynamically reweight frequency bands along anti-diagonals. This process effectively enhances forgery-related spectral signatures while suppressing less informative ones, simulating an adaptive “inverse compression” that counters information loss. The modulated frequency information is then fused with the spatial domain to guide a lightweight yet effective spatial backbone equipped with distance-decayed attention for comprehensive feature extraction. Extensive experiments on FaceForensics++, Celeb-DF, and DFDC datasets demonstrate that BAM-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance. More importantly, it exhibits exceptional generalization in cross-dataset, cross-compression, and cross-manipulation scenarios, underscoring the vital role of adaptive frequency band modulation in building robust forgery detectors.

records.title: Feature-Aligned Speech Watermarking for Robustness to Reconstruction Distortions
records.abstract: Audio watermarking aims to embed identifiable information into audio while remaining imperceptible. Existing methods adopt high-fidelity, low-energy designs to preserve perceptual quality, but the resulting watermarks lack robustness under suppression by speech reconstruction models. Improving robustness is challenging due to the inherent robustness–fidelity trade-off in existing designs, where increasing watermark energy improves robustness but reduces fidelity. To address this problem, we propose a feature-aligned watermarking method that aligns the watermark with the original speech feature distribution, allowing higher watermark energy to improve robustness while preserving imperceptibility. We use a pretrained speech codec to generate a pseudo-speech watermark and fuse it into the spectrogram of the input audio, with VAD loss and perceptual losses guiding embedding within voiced regions. Experiments show that our method maintains imperceptibility comparable to existing approaches while substantially improving robustness under both seen and unseen speech reconstruction models.

records.title: Simulated Annealing Iterative Fast Gradient Sign Method for Generating Adversarial Examples
records.abstract: Deep learning models are susceptible to adversarial examples generated by introducing imperceptible perturbations to benign inputs. Existing methods often generate effective adversarial examples by iteratively updating input examples along the gradient, following a greedy strategy. However, such methods overlook the impact of saddle points and local minima within the loss landscape on the generation of adversarial examples, which undermines the transferability of adversarial examples. To address this problem, we reconsider the generation of adversarial examples as a search problem within the neighborhood of the real example. Inspired by the effectiveness of heuristic search methods in finding global optima, we propose the Simulated Annealing Iterative Fast Gradient Sign Method (SAI-FGSM), which leverages the principle of thermal annealing and the Metropolis-Hastings acceptance criterion to escape local minima and saddle points, thereby increasing the probability of discovering global optima. Experimental results demonstrate that SAI-FGSM achieves superior performance in black-box attacks.

records.title: Debias-VG: Mitigating Visual Saliency and Correlation Biases for Robust Visual Grounding
records.abstract: Visual grounding, which localizes objects in images based on natural language descriptions, plays a critical role in multimodal understanding. Despite advances in multimodal fusion, existing approaches often suffer from inherent biases that limit their robustness. Specifically, two key issues persist: (1) visual saliency bias, where pretrained visual encoders disproportionately focus on salient regions, injecting biased features into fusion stages; and (2) correlation bias, wherein models tend to exploit spurious statistical correlations rather than causal relationships during fusion. To address these shortcomings, we propose Debias-VG, a novel debiasing framework that introduces a Multi-view Information Bottleneck to suppress saliency noise while enhancing query-relevant visual cues, and employs causal intervention via information minimization to identify and mitigate latent confounders. Together, these mechanisms promote clearer visual representation and more causally grounded reasoning. Extensive evaluations across five benchmarks confirm the effectiveness and robustness of our approach.

records.title: Interpretable Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning via Adversarial Feature Stabilization
records.abstract: Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning (FSCIL) faces the critical challenges of decision boundary drift and catastrophic forgetting. Although multimodal models like CLIP exhibit robust zero-shot transferability, their raw features often lack the stability and interpretability required for high-trust applications, and their fine-tuning performance frequently trails that of supervised pre-trained models. To leverage CLIP’s semantic alignment properties for enhanced interpretability, we propose Adversarial Feature Stabilization for FSCIL (AFS-FSCIL). Our core innovation is an adversarial feature stabilization technique, incorporating sparsity-induced regularization within the CLIP image encoder. This approach compels the encoder to focus on core semantic features, yielding object-centric saliency maps that intrinsically enhance feature interpretability. Concurrently, we introduce a Visual Instance-Filtered Text (VIFT) mechanism, which leverages stabilized image features to distill category descriptions generated by Visual Large Language Models (VLLMs), effectively capturing intra-class semantic diversity. This study represents the first systematic exploration of CLIP's potential for interpretability within the FSCIL paradigm. Our research demonstrates that this interpretability-driven stabilization achieves a superior balance between interpretability and performance, establishing a promising direction for high-trust incremental learning systems.

records.title: Directed Adversarial Training: Directing Robustness Optimization for Priority Classes
records.abstract: In practical scenarios, classes in classification tasks are rarely of equal priority—some classes exhibit higher priority than others. While researchers have addressed this in clean accuracy optimization (e.g., cost-sensitive learning), the robustness of high-priority classes similarly deserves more attention. However, to date, conventional adversarial training methods treat all classes equally without accounting for their inherent disparities. This paper proposes Directed Adversarial Training (DAT) framework for the directed robustness optimization of priority classes. Firstly, we theoretically demonstrate that targeted adversarial training implicitly shifts the model’s decision boundary toward the attack target class, thereby creating a trade-off between the robustness of source and target classes. Leveraging this insight, we then introduce a sampling mechanism that inversely correlates the selection probability of target classes with their priority levels. The training dataset generated in this way can reduce the degree to which priority classes are affected during adversarial training. Finally, we incorporate class-aware loss weighting and perturbation margins as complementary reweighting mechanisms. Experimental results on benchmark datasets show that our method effectively improves both the robustness and accuracy of task-specified high-priority classes without significantly sacrificing the classifier’s global performance.

records.title: An Integrated Defense Framework with Nested FGSM-Augmented Adversarial Training and Disruption-Based FGSM-T Purification
records.abstract: Existing adversarial defense methods face inherent trade-offs between robustness, clean accuracy, and generalization. Adversarial training improves robustness to specific attacks but often sacrifices clean accuracy and generalization, while inference-time purification methods rely heavily on attack priors and may distort semantics under strong perturbations. To address these issues, we propose NATDP, an integrated defense framework that combines nested FGSM--augmented adversarial training with disruption-based adaptive test-time purification. During training, nested FGSM-enhanced adversarial training explicitly models nested attack behaviors, inducing robust overfitting to FGSM-related perturbations and improving generalization to iterative attacks. At inference time, a two-stage purification strategy is employed: a small-perturbation yet strong attack first disrupts latent adversarial structures, followed by FGSM-T--based directional purification to recover discriminative features. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and SVHN demonstrate that NATDP significantly enhances robustness against diverse adversarial attacks while maintaining competitive clean accuracy.

records.title: Employing Progressive Cross-Modal Consistency Checking to Detect Video Fake News
records.abstract: Fake news videos increasingly disseminate misinformation by recombining authentic multimedia fragments, making each modality appear locally plausible in isolation. Their falsity often emerges only when spatial cues, temporal structure, and cross-modal semantics are examined jointly, resulting in locally plausible yet globally unsupported evidence patterns. However, existing approaches typically rely on static one-shot fusion or single-round alignment, which struggle to capture fine-grained inconsistencies and tend to dilute structural temporal anomalies under real-world editing and contextual manipulation. To address the above issue, we propose a novel framework ProgCheck, a progressive inconsistency checking framework that establishes global references and iteratively aggregates spatial, temporal, and cross-modal evidence. ProgCheck progressively refines local visual cues against global context, explicitly highlights structural temporal breaks through anomaly-aware modeling, and calibrates cross-modal semantics via a vision-anchored multi-round propagation module to suppress spurious surface-level consistency. Experimental results on FMNV and FakeTT datasets demonstrate that ProgCheck achieves state-of-the-art performance.

records.title: MAF-Det: Motion-Aware Forgery Cue Perception for AI-Generated Video Detection
records.abstract: The rapid development of AI-generated videos poses growing privacy and economic risks, creating an urgent need for effective detection. Existing methods struggle to capture fine-grained forgery cues, as subtle high-frequency anomalies are often dominated by low-frequency components, while localized artifacts are easily obscured by background content. To address these issues, we propose To address these issues, we propose MAF-Det, a motion-aware framework featuring: 1) a Frequency-domain Motion-aware Adapter (FMA), which disentangles motion features into decoupled HF and LF components to explicitly model frequency-specific anomalies; and 2) a Motion-guided Key Object Focusing (MOF) strategy that isolates suspicious frames and suppresses background noise to highlight discriminative regions. Extensive experiments on 10 benchmarks show state-of-the-art performance, with an average gain of 2.19% using only 17.75M parameters. Our method excels particularly in detecting physically implausible motions and anatomical deformations.

records.title: IEDN: Efficient Input Enhancement for Adversarial Defense via Feature-Enhanced Loss
records.abstract: Adversarial attacks pose a serious threat to the security of deep neural networks. Existing defense methods, such as adversarial training and input reconstruction, often suffer from high training costs or inference latency, which hinders their practical deployment in real-world scenarios. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an efficient single-step input enhancement method. Our approach is grounded in the key finding that beneficial adversarial perturbations generated with true labels as targets can enhance the model's confidence in those labels. Based on this insight, we design an Input Enhanced Defense Network named IEDN, which learns to produce such perturbations through Feature-Enhanced Loss. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet demonstrate that our method maintains high clean accuracy while significantly improving robustness, with additional advantages in cross-model transferability and low training/inference costs, making it well-suited for practical deployment.

records.title: GA-LMGNet: A Geometric Algebra-Based Learnable Metric Graph Network for Robust Point Cloud Feature Detection
records.abstract: Industrial point clouds contain sharp edges and fine geometric transitions that are essential for inspection and robotic perception. However, most existing Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based detectors rely on fixed Euclidean metrics, leading to unstable neighborhoods under anisotropic curvature and limited robustness to rotations. To address these limitations, we propose Geometric Algebra-based Learnable Metric Graph Network (GA-LMGNet), a geometric-algebra-based graph network that unifies adaptive metric learning, orientation-aware GA edge encoding, and information-preserving aggregation.GA-LMGNet achieves up to +3.7% F1 improvement over state-of-the-art edge-aware baselines on the ABC dataset, while showing promising qualitative generalization on real industrial scans. These results demonstrate that coupling geometric algebra with learnable metrics enables more stable and rotation-consistent local geometric encoding.

records.title: Cache-Guided Test-Time Purification for Robust Zero-Shot Adapted Vision-Language Models
records.abstract: Cache-based adaptation facilitates efficient zero-shot transfer for Vision-Language Models (VLMs) yet severely exacerbates adversarial vulnerability. To mitigate this, we propose Cache-Guided Test-Time Purification (CG-TTP), an inference-stage defense governed by a “Break-and-Guide” paradigm. CG-TTP destabilizes the local stagnation of adversarial samples via counterattacks and leverages the adapter’s key-value cache as a robust semantic anchor to rectify feature alignment. Extensive experiments across 10 datasets demonstrate a superior robustness-accuracy trade-off: CG-TTP achieves an average Robust Accuracy of 54.82% while elevating Clean Accuracy to 72.70%. This establishes the zero-shot cache as a dual-purpose asset for both recognition capability and geometric defense.

records.title: Cross-Domain Representation Learning with State Space Model for Deepfake Detection
records.abstract: The rapid advancements in deepfake face forgery have reduced visual artifacts, challenging conventional single-domain detection methods. Existing approaches often isolate spatial and frequency features, neglecting their inherent synergy and local-global dependencies. To address this, we propose CRL-Mamba, a dual-stream state space model framework that jointly learns spatial and frequency representations through multi-stage interactions. Our method enhances cross-domain learning via frequency guidance, which hierarchically captures subtle artifacts in the DCT domain using a spectral attention mechanism and an adaptive filter to amplify high-frequency cues. A frequency enhancement gate then converts refined spectral features into spatial attention maps, recalibrating spatial focus toward forgery-sensitive regions. Experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that CRL-Mamba achieves state-of-the-art performance and strong generalization.

records.title: LaMF: Latent Multi-Level Fusion for Transferable Facial Privacy Protection
records.abstract: The widespread deployment of deep face recognition (FR) systems has raised privacy concerns, prompting the introduction of adversarial examples to shield personal images from unauthorized identification. However, current diffusion-based approaches typically neglect the rich target identity priors embedded within the generation process, resulting in suboptimal compromises between protection capability and visual realism. To overcome this limitation, we propose Latent Multi-Level Fusion (LaMF), a novel diffusion-based method that actively harnesses internal generative representations by embedding target identity information into both diffusion guidance signals via Unconditional Embedding Fusion and internal spatial representation via Structural Attention Blending. We further enforce the Structural Attention Blending via a Dual-Pressure mechanism, which combines Hybrid Structural Alignment and Post-Loss Attention Replacement to ensure rigorous feature consistency. Extensive evaluations confirm that our method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in protection efficacy while maintaining high visual imperceptibility.

records.title: MCIForensics: A Multi-Scale Contrastive Interaction Network for Image Forgery Localization
records.abstract: Modern image forgery techniques have achieved unprecedented levels of photorealism, substantially increasing the difficulty of reliable forgery detection. To address this challenge, we present MCIForensics, a Multi-Scale Contrastive Interactive framework for fine-grained image forgery localization. Unlike existing approaches that rely primarily on bottleneck-layer representations, MCIForensics employs a U-Net–inspired architecture augmented with Dense Self-Attention and Multi-Scale Interaction modules to effectively capture, refine, and fuse both high-level semantics and subtle texture cues across hierarchical stages. To further enhance discriminability, we introduce a task-specific contrastive learning strategy that constructs hard samples tailored to the characteristics of forgery localization, thereby improving the model’s ability to distinguish authentic from manipulated regions. In addition, we design a boundary-aware hybrid loss to strengthen supervision over structural and edge-level forgery signals. Extensive experiments conducted on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that MCIForensics consistently improves localization accuracy and achieves state-of-the-art performance compared with existing methods.

records.title: FedDV: Robust Federated Learning against Noisy Labels via Dual-View Augmentation
records.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables privacy-preserving distributed training. However, practical deployments are hindered by poor data quality, specifically label noise stemming from annotation errors. Such corruption induces biased updates, severely degrading global model generalization. Existing defenses prioritize noise filtering or robust aggregation but often fail to capture intrinsic features, resulting in fragile representations susceptible to memorizing noisy labels. To address this, we propose FedDV, a robust framework leveraging dual-view augmentation to enforce representation invariance. Additionally, we employ a collaborative correction strategy utilizing the disagreement between global and local models for label rectification, integrated with logit adjustment to mitigate class imbalance. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100 and Clothing1M demonstrate the superiority of FedDV, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods by 4.79% on CIFAR-100 under challenging non-IID and severe noise scenarios.

records.title: Modality-Advantage Conceptual Preservation for Robust Multimodal Violence Detection with Missing Modality
records.abstract: Multimodal Violence Detection (MVD) inevitably encounters the modality-missing problem in real-world applications, rendering models unreliable. However, existing anti-missingness strategies suffer from two fundamental limitations: feature-reconstructed methods encounter the ill-posed problem of mapping one-to-many concepts, resulting in semantic ambiguity, while robustness-enhanced methods risk miscorrelation due to the blind-alignment problem when discriminative cues are absent. To this end, we propose a novel yet practical framework termed Modality-Advantage Conceptual Preservation (M-ACP), shifting the paradigm from low-level feature recovery to high-level conceptual consistency preserving. Specifically, guided by modality advantage, a metric quantifying the information gain of missing modalities, M-ACP integrates two synergistic modules. Advantage-Driven Concept Rectification (ADCR) anchors student predictions to stable violence prototypes to resolve semantic ambiguity, while Advantage-Aware Feature Regularization (AAFR) employs dynamic contrastive learning to maintain structural integrity, enforcing strict constraints only when necessary. Extensive experiments on the XD-Violence dataset demonstrate that M-ACP significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, establishing a new standard for robust MVD.

records.title: VFACamou: View-Fused Adversarial Camouflage for Environment-Adaptive Physical Evasion
records.abstract: Adversarial camouflage in the physical world remains highly challenging, particularly under UAV reconnaissance where targets undergo continuous geometric changes and extreme illumination variations. Existing methods either optimize 2D digital perturbations that fail to generalize to dynamic viewpoints or produce visually unnatural textures that cannot be deployed in real scenarios. Therefore, we propose VFACamou, an end-to-end framework for adversarial camouflage generation that automatically produces wearable adversarial patterns and maintains stable attack performance in real physical environments with changing viewpoints, poses, and lighting conditions.Our method integrates UV-volume rendering with a diffusion-based texture generator, enabling consistent appearance under varying scales, poses, and lighting conditions. To ensure environmental realism, we propose an illumination–color consistency estimator that extracts dominant background attributes and guides a natural texture loss to align the generated UV texture with the surrounding environment. A multi-scale dynamic training strategy further enhances robustness against viewpoint shifts and body deformation. Extensive experiments across multiple mainstream detectors demonstrate that VFACamou achieves strong and stable physical attack performance while maintaining high perceptual naturalness, reducing human detection rates without introducing unnatural artifacts.

records.title: RDM-AE: Learning Non-disruptive Noise for Generalizable Adversarial Training
records.abstract: Deep Neural Networks (‌DNN‌s) are easily affected by gradient attack noise, resulting in adversarial samples with a high success rate of attacks. Adversarial training boosts the robustness of DNN‌s but faces challenges in generalization. In this paper, we propose a Robust Defensive Model-AutoEncoder (RDM-AE) to approximate a clean image and purify an adversarial image at the same time, transforming adversarial noise into non-disruptive noise with a Knowledge-Augmented loss. Unlike conventional autoencoders that solely focus on feature enhancement, we propose a novel Local-Semantic Normalization module to enhance encoding/decoding capabilities for noise detection. To improve the robustness of RDM-AE with adversarial augmentation, a Dynamic Stochastic Adversarial Sample Generation module is implemented. Experimental results demonstrate that our RDM-AE performs better than previous state-of-the-art approaches on the small dataset CIFAR-10, especially achieving effective generalization of robustness across different model architectures and attack scenarios on the large dataset ImageNet.

records.title: Prompt-Learning-based Rebalancing for Dual-Imbalanced Multimodal Fake News Detection
records.abstract: In practice, multimodal fake news detection (MFND) suffers from modality and class imbalance. The dominant modality suppresses other modalities during training and fake-news samples are typically much fewer than real ones, together resulting in an ill-defined decision boundary. Recent work has attempted to address both types of imbalance via prototype learning, which makes it difficult to capture finegrained cues. To overcome these limitations, we propose PLR, a Prompt-Learning-based Rebalancing framework for Dual Imbalanced MFND. Specifically, PLR contains three components: a Prompt Learning-based Modality Rebalance module (PLMR) injects learnable modality-specific prompts to boost weak modalities and prevent modality collapse. Class-Biased Self-Attention blocks (CBSA) introduce class-aware prompts and reweight token attention to highlight minority evidence while suppressing majority interference, and a Mamba-based Cross-Modal Fusion (MCMF) module uses a lightweight 1D Mamba backbone for efficient cross-modal fusion. Extensive experiments on benchmark MFND datasets show that PLR outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods.

records.title: FUDefense: Towards Robust Recovery from Poisoning Attacks in Federated Learning
records.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is vulnerable to poisoning attacks. While federated unlearning (FU) can remove harmful data, existing methods fail to prevent malicious poisoning from persisting across subsequent rounds. To address this gap, we propose FUDefense, a lightweight plug-and-play framework that enhances history-aware FU pipelines through dual-stage client selection,thereby mitigating both direct and indirect forms of adversarial contamination without reliance on an auxiliary clean dataset. Parameter-wise hypothesis testing identifies and filters suspicious checkpoints by detecting gradient deviations from trusted global models, and the Q-learning agent dynamically selects optimal participants based on long-term utility simultaneously. Theoretically, we prove that FUDefense reduces residual bias, ensures Lyapunov stability, and preserves linear convergence. Experiments on three FU benchmarks demonstrate robustness against trimming and backdoor attacks, achieving up to 12% accuracy improvement and 68% faster recovery compared to state-of-the-art methods.

records.title: A Frequency-Aware Lightweight Network for Robust Nuclei Segmentation and Classification on Challenging Histologies
records.abstract: Current nuclei instance segmentation and classification methods based on deep learning typically involve a large number of parameters and face challenges when processing morphologically complex tissues (such as adrenal glands and stomach) and weak nuclei (such as inflammation and death). We argue that the key to efficient and robust modeling lies in expanding the receptive field while reducing parameters through smarter feature representation. Then, we propose Lightweight Wavelet KeyPoint Network (LWPNet), a novel lightweight network built on a frequency-aware paradigm. LWPNet introduces a Wavelet Transfer Conv Mixer (WTCM) block that replaces large-kernel convolutions with wavelet transforms, explicitly expanding the receptive field at minimal computational cost to capture multi-scale spectral features. Furthermore, a Frequency Scale-Aware Coordinate Aggregation (FSACA) module is designed to enhance high-frequency boundary details while incorporating precise spatial coordinates, ensuring accurate localization. Evaluated on the PanNuke, Kumar, and CoNSeP datasets, LWPNet reduces parameters by 81\% and excels in these challenging cases, achieving gains of 4.3\% mPQ on stomach tissue.

records.title: Unsupervised Cross-Domain Anomaly Detection in Aerospace Sensor Time Series via Adversarial Contrastive Representation Learning
records.abstract: Labeled anomalies are scarce in aerospace multivariate sensor time-series data, and distribution shifts (e.g., platform and operating-condition changes) hinder reliable detection. Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) can leverage labeled anomalies from a related source domain to adapt to an unlabeled target domain, but performance often degrades when target anomalies are novel and do not align with source anomaly categories. We propose Adversarial Contrastive Representation Learning (ACRL), which integrates contrastive learning with UDA to improve transfer to unseen anomaly types. First, we introduce a lightweight adaptive time-series network as a feature extractor, addressing practical limitations of Transformer-based models for aerospace sensor data, such as sensitivity to noise, computational overhead, and overfitting on small datasets. Second, we propose an anomaly injection strategy to improve generalization to unseen anomalies. Third, our objective combines supervised contrastive learning on the source domain with a self-supervised triplet loss on the target domain, encouraging domain-invariant yet discriminative representations and improving robustness under adversarial training. Finally, we develop an entropy-guided centroid classifier (ECC) to better capture transferable normality boundaries learned from the source domain. Experiments on multiple real-world aerospace sensor time series datasets show that ACRL reduces reliance on labeled anomalies and improves source-to-target knowledge transfer under domain shift, achieving substantial improvements over state-of-the-art baselines in F1, precision, recall, and AUPR.

records.title: DeepLocBench: A Unified and Standardized Benchmark for Deepfake Localization
records.abstract: Pixel-level deepfake localization is pivotal for forensic interpretability, yet the field is hindered by fragmented evaluation protocols and metrics that fail to account for foreground bias in authentic samples. To bridge this gap, we introduce DeepLocBench, a standardized benchmark that unifies data preprocessing, multi-paradigm training, and evaluation. Crucially, we propose the Semantically-Refined Difference Map (SRDM), which leverages semantic segmentation priors to suppress compression artifacts, automatically generating high-fidelity supervision signals to address the scarcity of pixel-level annotations. We conduct a systematic evaluation of 10 state-of-the-art methods on DeepLocBench. The results reveal critical insights: 1) an inherent optimization conflict between detection and localization objectives in multi-task learning, 2) a severe generalization gap when transferring to unseen generative mechanisms, such as diffusion models, and 3) a precision-robustness trade-off, where frequency-dependent methods falter under video compression. DeepLocBench provides a reproducible platform to foster more generalizable and robust forensic techniques.

records.title: Dual-Path Attentive Fusion with Vision–Language Guidance under Adversarial Perturbations
records.abstract: Infrared–visible (IR–VI) fusion is increasingly adopted in safety-critical perception, yet two challenges remain: (i) small perturbations can induce cross-modal artifacts that propagate through fusion backbones; and (ii) most text-guided pipelines use language only as shallow conditioning, leading to limited controllability and degraded stability under domain shift. We propose a robust and controllable IR–VI fusion framework with three components: Dual-Path Attentive Coupling (DPAC), Vision–Language Affine-and-Gated Modulation (VLAGM), and Hierarchical Cross-Modal Contrastive Alignment (HCCA). DPAC decomposes cross-modal interactions into promotive and suppressive dependencies, amplifying salient cues while actively inhibiting background correlations to mitigate artifact propagation. VLAGM transforms embeddings from a frozen vision–language encoder into feature-wise affine calibration and spatial gating priors, enabling prompt-steerable fusion. HCCA aligns IR/VI representations across scales via patch-level contrastive learning with memory-efficient token-pair sampling. Experiments on text-annotated benchmarks and cross-dataset evaluations show improved fusion quality, stronger prompt controllability, and enhanced robustness under adversarial perturbations.

records.title: AnyBreak: Towards Jailbreaking Any T2I Model for Any Concept
records.abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) models have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in image generation and editing, yet this progress has also introduced significant security risks. Prior work has shown that adversarial prompt can induce the generation of Not-Safe-For-Work (NSFW) content, including pornographic, violent, and graphic imagery. However, such attacks are typically mitigated by prompt filters and often rely on white-box assumptions. In this paper, we propose AnyBreak, a novel jailbreak framework that constructs adversarial images via multi-scale progressive semantic alignment. During the generation process, these adversarial images steer the generation trajectory in latent space towards unsafe data manifolds, enabling cross-modal transfer of malicious concepts from the text modality to the image modality. AnyBreak operates using only clean textual prompts and adversarial images at inference time, and can jailbreak any T2I models towards any malicious concepts in a fully black-box setting. We further introduce AnyBreak-V, an enhanced variant that incorporates a compensation term to bypass post-hoc safety checkers. Extensive experiments demonstrate that AnyBreak achieves high attack success rates while preserving visual fidelity and semantic consistency with the input prompts under black-box and clean-text constraints. Our findings reveal that existing T2I defense leave critical cross-modal attack surfaces insufficiently addressed. The code is available at \href{https://github.com/luqi-glory/AnyBreak}{GitHub}.

records.title: Unveiling and Breaking Feature Traps in Unlearnable Examples
records.abstract: Unlearnable Examples (UEs) aim to protect data privacy by injecting imperceptible perturbations that mislead models into learning shortcut features. In this paper, we unveil a critical feature trap mechanism: while models initially capture both semantic and perturbation features, the shallow layers rapidly become dominated by perturbations, suppressing the learning of essential image semantics. Based on this insight, we propose Progressive Staged Training (PST), a self-adaptive framework designed to circumvent UEs by strategically mitigating the feature trap across different training phases. Extensive experiments on CIFAR and ImageNet demonstrate that PST consistently restores model performance across various architectures, effectively defeating state-of-the-art UE methods. Our findings reveal that existing UEs provide a false sense of privacy and establish a robust baseline for evaluating the true security of future data-masking techniques.

records.title: DEFT: Deformation-Guided Efficient Fusion for Real-Time Deepfake Detection
records.abstract: Real-time deepfake detection is crucial for video-call scenarios, where delayed or offline analysis cannot prevent ongoing fraud or impersonation. In such settings, detection must operate on streaming video under strict latency and resource constraints. However, many existing methods rely on computationally heavy models or process all video frames, making them inefficient for real-time deployment, while lightweight approaches often sacrifice accuracy or robustness due to their reliance on single-frame or single-domain cues. Moreover, forgery artifacts are unevenly distributed across frames and tend to become more pronounced under natural facial deformations, yet this property is often overlooked. Motivated by this observation, we find that natural facial expressions can act as a passive challenge that exposes forgery artifacts. Based on this insight, we propose DEFT, a real-time deepfake detection framework. DEFT selects Key Deformation Frames (KDFs) based on facial deformation cues and fuses spatial, gradient, and frequency-domain features through a lightweight cross-attention network. Experiments demonstrate that DEFT achieves strong detection accuracy and generalization while maintaining real-time efficiency.

records.title: CloneGuard: Robust Watermarking via Parallel Stream Weight Cloning
records.abstract: With the advancement of AIGC, watermarking is crucial for copyright protection. However, existing high-fidelity methods face a dilemma: VAE-based approaches suffer from reconstruction blur, while RAE-based pipelines are sensitive to additive noise. To address this, we propose CloneGuard. Unlike traditional noise injection, our Parallel Stream Weight Cloning mechanism initializes the watermark stream from the host decoder to synthesize semantically aligned texture residuals. Additionally, we integrate a Wavelet-Flow Decoder to eliminate the grid artifacts inherent in Vision Transformers. Experiments demonstrate that CloneGuard achieves state-of-the-art visual fidelity and robustness against geometric distortions, establishing a new paradigm of endogenous texture synthesis.

records.title: Simplicity-Oriented Semantic-Agnostic Learning for Generalized AI-Generated Image Detection
records.abstract: Images synthesized by diffusion models and GANs have reached a level of realism that poses severe security challenges. Previous approaches attempted to address this by employing VLM to extract semantic features, or by analyzing common procedural traces inherited from generative pipelines. However, existing AI-generated image detection approaches still face significant generalization challenges, particularly exhibiting limited capability in detecting images produced by unseen generators. To address this issue, we first analyze the properties of patches with different complexity levels. We observe that while forgery traces are distributed throughout the entire image, classifier trained on simple patches, which contain minimal semantic information, demonstrate the strongest generalization ability. Building on this insight, we design a simplicity-oriented framework for detecting generated images. The proposed method not only learns intrinsic and universal forgery artifacts from simple patches, but also adaptively acquires richer supplementary signals from other regions. Our method surpasses current state-of-the-art models in cross-generator evaluation involving 17 Diffusions and 15 GANs. Extensive experiments further validate the effectiveness and generalization capability of out method in extracting universal manipulation traces.

records.title: CALM: Cross-lingual Adaptation for Low-resource Lipreading via Language-specific Viseme Modulation
records.abstract: Lipreading for low-resource languages remains challenging due to data scarcity. While conventional methods such as data augmentation or direct distillation introduce complexity or fail to address inter-lingual conflicts, we propose CALM—a novel framework for cross‑lingual adaptation via language‑specific viseme modulation. Our multi-phase strategy transfers universal viseme knowledge from high-resource languages and integrates target language-specific viseme patterns through an adapter-enhanced cross-attention mechanism. This design facilitates seamless knowledge integration, further strengthened by unidirectional distillation that promotes mutual refinement between the backbone and expert modules, leading to substantial performance gains in low‑resource lipreading. Evaluated on CMLR, the largest sentence-level Mandarin lipreading dataset, our method achieves a character error rate (CER) of 8.53%, surpassing baselines and attaining state-of-the-art results to our knowledge. These findings confirm that our approach effectively alleviates inter-lingual conflicts and improves fine-grained knowledge transfer, laying a groundwork for future cross-lingual and multilingual lipreading research. Code will be made public to foster future research.

records.title: ViTAlign: Region-Aligned Patch Views and Routed Adapters for Deepfake Detection
records.abstract: Face forgery detection remains challenging under cross-dataset and cross-manipulation shifts. Existing CNN-based detectors and large pretrained ViTs often rely on a single global representation, underutilizing the pronounced spatial locality of forgery artifacts across facial regions. We propose ViTAlign, a parameter-efficient framework that aligns coarse facial-region priors with the native ViT patch grid for robust detection. Using a frozen DINOv2 backbone, ViTAlign reshapes patch tokens into an H_p × W_p grid and derives three region-aligned views: a global CLS view, a central pooled window capturing interior inconsistencies, and a peripheral pooled complement emphasizing boundary and context artifacts. The views are supervised individually and fused at inference to exploit complementary regional evidence. To further inject task-specific capacity with minimal overhead, we insert routed multi-expert low-rank adapters into selected transformer projections while keeping all backbone parameters fixed. Extensive experiments on FF++ and multiple unseen benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements in cross-dataset and cross-manipulation generalization.

records.title: PSC-LDP: Pixel-Semantic Conditional Latent Diffusion for Adversarial Purification
records.abstract: Despite the remarkable success of deep learning, its vulnerability to adversarial perturbations fundamentally compromises model reliability. While adversarial purification offers defensive potential through perturbation removal, current methods suffer from significant limitations: (1) pixel-domain distortions (defensive noise, artifacts, structural loss) degrade clean-sample performance; (2) feature-domain semantic degradation from insufficient high-level guidance constrains adversarial robustness. To overcome these dual-domain limitations, we pioneer the integration of conditional latent diffusion into adversarial purification, proposing Pixel-Semantic Conditional Latent Diffusion Purification (PSC-LDP). Leverages pre-trained LDM as generative backbone, establishing the first defense paradigm operating in compressed latent space for efficiency and fidelity preservation. To address the problem of pixel-domain distortion, we propose a Pixel Level Conditional Module (PCM) that unlocks structural alignment via ControlNet and cross-attention, injecting low-level features into latent representations to eliminate defensive perturbations and recover high-frequency details. For the challenge of feature semantic degradation, we propose a Real-time Semantic Conditional Module (RSCM) that obtains classification information by decoding intermediate latents and then injects high-level semantics through CLIP, thereby dynamically rectifying semantic drift during generation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PSC-LDP achieves state-of-the-art adversarial robustness while inducing negligible degradation in clean samples. This work establishes a new paradigm for high-fidelity, semantics-aware adversarial purification.

records.title: LoCC: Detection and Localization of Lip-Syncing Deepfakes via Counterfactual Frame Consistency
records.abstract: Lip-syncing deepfakes are among the most challenging forms of manipulated media because their artifacts are localized almost exclusively to the mouth region and evolve dynamically over time. Detecting such deepfakes requires precise temporal and spatial modeling of lip motion. In this paper, we propose LoCC, a novel detection framework that performs fine-grained detection and localization of lip-syncing deepfakes at both segment and frame levels. Unlike prior approaches that analyze videos holistically, our method evaluates whether each frame aligns with a counterfactual estimate generated from its temporal neighbors. Real videos exhibit strong and stable consistency, whereas lip-sync deepfakes introduce localized inconsistencies. Following a teacher–student learning paradigm, our model effectively captures these frame-level discrepancies and achieves superior performance over state-of-the-art methods on multiple benchmark lip-syncing deepfake datasets, including LAV-DF, AVDF1M, FakeAVCeleb, and KODF, and generalizes well across compression levels and datasets.

records.title: Identifying Encrypted LLM Dialogue Traffic via Contrastive Dual-View Temporal Attention
records.abstract: The rapid adoption of Large Language Model (LLM) services poses challenges for enterprise network management and security. Network administrators require reliable methods to identify LLM dialogue traffic within encrypted flows to prevent sensitive data leakage and to understand bandwidth consumption patterns. However, existing methods struggle with HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 multiplexing, in which LLM dialogue traffic is interleaved with other concurrent streams within the same connection. In this paper, we propose DELTA (Dual-view Encrypted LLM Traffic Analysis), a novel framework that addresses these challenges through three key designs: (1) dual-view temporal encoding that captures complementary patterns from packet lengths and inter-arrival times using parallel Transformer encoders; (2) cross-view contrastive alignment that learns coherent representations across modalities; and (3) Multiple Instance Learning with gated attention that automatically localizes dialogue-relevant segments within noisy sessions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DELTA achieves 99.24% accuracy and 99.17% F1, outperforming state-of-the-art methods.
