records.title: BridgeARD: Bridging the Latent Gap for Dual-Teacher Adversarial Robust Distillation
records.abstract: Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) transfers robustness and clean accuracy from teacher models to compact students, enabling deployment under resource constraints. While existing dual-teacher ARD methods leverage separate clean and robust teachers, they face limitations: (1) inherent representation discrepancies induce conflicting optimization objectives; and (2) reliance on worst-case adversarial examples leaves vulnerability gaps unaddressed. To tackle these, we propose {BridgeARD}, a dual-teacher framework bridging representation and optimization gaps through \textit{joint alignment in both instance and weight spaces}. Specifically, {BridgeARD} introduces: (i) an \textit{intermediate sample bridging} mechanism constructing smooth transitions between clean and adversarial samples via perturbation interpolation; and (ii) a \textit{targeted weight patching} mechanism dynamically exposing latent vulnerabilities to align with the robust teacher. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 demonstrate {BridgeARD} outperforms state-of-the-art dual-teacher approaches. For instance, distilling to MobileNet-V2 on CIFAR-10 improves PGD robustness by +5.03\% while narrowing the accuracy--robustness trade-off.

records.title: UniGuard: A Unified In-Process Watermarking Framework for Text-to-3D Generation
records.abstract: The rapid proliferation of 3D AIGC necessitates robust intellectual property protection. Existing watermarking solutions for text-to-3D generation predominantly rely on post-processing, which leaves raw assets unprotected during the initial generation phase and incurs additional computational overhead. To address these limitations, we propose UniGuard, a unified in-process watermarking framework compatible with diverse score distillation-based 3D representations, including NeRF and 3DGS. Unlike prior methods that require training auxiliary watermark networks, UniGuard seamlessly embeds spectral watermarks into the latent space of diffusion priors without additional pre-training. Furthermore, to resolve the intrinsic conflict between reconstruction and watermark embedding, we propose Frequency-Adaptive Scheduling (FAS). This strategy effectively prevents structural interference while ensuring high-fidelity generation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UniGuard achieves state-of-the-art robustness against both image-level distortions and model-level geometric manipulations without compromising visual quality.

records.title: Enhancing Adversarial Contrastive Learning via Semantic-driven Data Augmentation
records.abstract: Self-supervised adversarial training (self-AT) enhances model robustness but lags behind supervised AT. We hypothesize this gap stems from semantically inconsistent positive pairs generated by random augmentations (e.g., random crops) in standard contrastive learning, which weakens robust representation learning. To address this, we propose Semantic-Driven Adversarial Contrastive Learning (SDACL). At its core is a Semantic-Driven Constrained Cropping (SDCC) strategy, which leverages internal model representations to guide augmentation, ensuring positive pairs are anchored to the semantic core of images. Theoretically, based on Mutual Information, we demonstrate that SDACL maximizes the information lower bound between augmented views and latent semantic content, thereby ensuring robust representation learning. Empirically, our results show that SDACL significantly outperforms state-of-the-art Self-AT methods on CIFAR-10 and STL-10, effectively closing the performance gap with supervised counterparts.

records.title: PhysioKamba: A Lightweight Mamba-KAN Framework for Robust Wearable Biometrics
records.abstract: Deploying robust PPG-based biometric identification on edge devices faces a critical conflict between computational constraints and the need to model non-stationary physiological dynamics. To address this, we propose PhysioKamba, a lightweight framework synergizing State Space Models (SSM) with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN). We introduce a Spectral-Guided Rate Estimator that leverages learnable splines to extract cardiac frequency priors. This drives a novel Rate-Aware Selective Scan mechanism, which dynamically modulates the SSM step size to synchronize with instantaneous heart rates, effectively mitigating distribution shifts caused by temporal warping. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PhysioKamba achieves state-of-the-art performance, significantly outperforming existing Transformer and CNN baselines on the challenging PPG-DaLiA dataset (+5.4% accuracy gain) while reducing parameter count by 83% compared to 1D-ViT. This offers a superior trade-off between robustness and efficiency for wearable deployment.

records.title: GGSIACL: Gradient-Guided Spherical Interpolation in Adversarial Contrastive Learning
records.abstract: Adversarial contrastive learning, by bringing the features of clean samples and adversarial samples closer together, has become an effective paradigm for improving model robustness. However, existing methods only anchor themselves to learning these two discrete endpoints, ignoring the feature continuity along the transformation path from clean samples to adversarial samples. This may cause intermediate states to deviate from the data manifold, thereby impairing the inherent robustness of the model. To address this, we propose Gradient-Guided Spherical Interpolation in Adversarial Contrastive Learning, called GGSIACL. GGSIACL integrates Gradient-Guided Sampling to locate vulnerable intermediate states and Spherical Linear Interpolation to ensure semantic consistency within the hyperspherical feature space. By enforcing discriminative stability along the continuous adversarial path, our method effectively mitigates the accuracy-robustness trade-off. Experiments on the CIFAR-10 and STL10 show that GGSIACL outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in improving standard accuracy while also demonstrating superior performance under AutoAttack attacks.

records.title: ProtoGuard-SL: Prototype Consistency Based Backdoor Defense for Vertical Split Learning
records.abstract: Vertical split learning (SL) enables collaborative model training across parties holding complementary features without sharing raw data, but recent work has shown that it is highly vulnerable to poisoning-based backdoor attacks operating on intermediate embeddings. By compromising malicious clients, adversaries can inject stealthy triggers that manipulate the server-side model while remaining difficult to detect, and existing defenses provide limited robustness against adaptive attacks. In this paper, we propose ProtoGuard-SL, a server-side defense that improves the robustness of split learning by exploiting class-conditional representation consistency in the embedding space. Our approach is motivated by the observation that benign embeddings within the same class exhibit stable semantic alignment, whereas poisoned embeddings inevitably disrupt this structure. ProtoGuard-SL adopts a two-stage framework that constructs robust class prototypes and transforms embeddings into a prototype-consistency representation, followed by a class-conditional, distribution-free conformal filtering strategy to identify and remove anomalous embeddings. Extensive experiments are conducted on three datasets, CIFAR-10, SVHN, and Bank Marketing, under three different attack settings demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance.

records.title: DuSDiffPatch: Dual-Modal Diffusion and Smooth Gradient Stability-Guided Patch Attack
records.abstract: Deep neural networks in safety-critical domains remain highly vulnerable to transferable patch attacks. Existing methods, however, struggle with limited transferability and imperceptibility due to reliance on random patch localization and unguided perturbations. To address these, we propose DuSDiffPatch, a novel attack framework guided by dual modal diffusion and smooth gradient stability. Uniquely, we introduce a text modality into patch generation for the first time, using prompts to impose semantic constraints that align perturbations with natural image manifolds, thereby significantly enhancing imperceptibility. Furthermore, we leverage cross-model gradient stability to identify optimal regions for precise patch localization, overcoming the randomness of prior approaches. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DuSDiffPatch outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving a remarkable 20% increase in Attack Success Rate against Vision Transformers and the highest average transferability across diverse models, all while maintaining the lowest L2 distortion norm.

records.title: A Framework Mining Spatial-Temporal Forgery Clues for Low-Quality Deepfake Video Detection
records.abstract: Deepfake technology can generate hyper-realistic synthetic faces, posing serious societal threats. The challenge is especially acute for low-quality, heavily compressed deepfake videos that proliferate on social media, where compression artifacts often obscure genuine manipulation traces, causing detectors to learn spurious correlations and fail under distribution shifts. To tackle this, we present MSTFC -- a purely 2D-based framework that effectively mines spatial-temporal forgery clues for low-quality deepfake detection. MSTFC addresses two entangled challenges: (1) Artifact entanglement: we disentangle invariant forgery signatures from compression noise by applying diversified per-frame augmentations and introducing a multi-augmentation feature alignment loss. This loss enforces feature consistency across differently augmented views of the same video, compelling the model to suppress stochastic artifacts while retaining stable manipulation clues such as geometric distortions and material inconsistencies. (2) Temporal inconsistency: to capture short-range dynamics disrupted by face forgery, we propose temporal channelization, which swaps the time and channel dimensions, enabling standard 2D convolutions to perform temporal fusion across frames and dynamically highlight frames exhibiting anomalies. Extensive experiments show that MSTFC outperforms state-of-the-art methods, proving its effectiveness for real-world low-quality deepfake detection.

records.title: LAVE: Lightweight BERT-Style Evaluator for Efficient AIGV Quality Assessment
records.abstract: The rapid advancement of Text-to-Video (T2V) generation demands reliable metrics for evaluating AI-Generated Videos (AIGVs). Recent state-of-the-art (SOTA) evaluators increasingly rely on Large Language Models (LLMs), achieving impressive performance. However, these models often suffer from prohibitive computational costs, excessive parameter redundancy, and weaker cross-dataset generalization. We argue that a potential cause is a paradigm misalignment: repurposing autoregressive, next-token predictors as feature extractors for discriminative scalar quality regression, which introduces structural redundancy and is less directly aligned with the needs of global spatiotemporal quality assessment. To address this, we propose LAVE, a Lightweight AI-generated Video Evaluator built on a BERT-style bidirectional encoder. LAVE further adapts the text-centric backbone to video assessment via Source-Aware Embedding and Chronological Feature Interleaving, enabling explicit multi-source token identification and efficient modeling of fine-grained spatiotemporal dependencies. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LAVE substantially reduces computational overhead while delivering strong performance, particularly excelling in zero-shot cross-dataset generalization. Code will be released at https://github.com/QiZelu/LAVE-main.

records.title: CRISP: Pre-LLM Yet Text-Driven Visual Token Pruning for Efficient LVLM Inference
records.abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) typically require processing hundreds to thousands of visual tokens, leading to substantial computational overhead during inference. Existing training-free visual token pruning methods either operate before the LLM using text-agnostic heuristics or prune inside the LLM at the cost of efficiency and noisy cross-modal attention. To address these limitations, we propose CRISP, a pre-LLM yet text-driven visual token pruning framework that preserves both instruction-relevant evidence and essential scene context. CRISP works in a two-stage pipeline: a critical-first stage identifies text-aligned visual tokens, and a semantically-covered stage enhances contextual completeness through semantic diversity. Extensive experiments on LLaVA-1.5 and LLaVA-NeXT demonstrate that CRISP achieves superior performance retention under aggressive pruning ratios, maintaining up to 99.5% accuracy while reducing inference cost and latency by more than 2×. CRISP serves as an effective and practical solution for efficient LVLM inference, especially in resource-constrained scenarios.

records.title: REFORGE: Multi-modal Attacks Reveal Vulnerable Concept Unlearning in Image Generation Models
records.abstract: Recent progress in image generation models (IGMs) enables high-fidelity content creation, but amplifies risks including reproducing copyrighted or generating offensive content. Image Generation Model Unlearning (IGMU) mitigates these risks by removing harmful concepts without full retraining. Despite growing attention, the robustness under adversarial inputs, particularly image-side threats in black-box settings, remains underexplored. To bridge this gap, we present REFORGE, a black-box red-teaming framework that evaluates IGMU robustness via adversarial image prompts. REFORGE initializes stroke-based images and optimizes perturbations with a cross-attention-guided masking strategy that allocates noise to concept-relevant regions, balancing attack efficacy and visual fidelity. Extensive experiments across representative unlearning tasks and defenses demonstrate that REFORGE significantly improves attack success rate while achieving stronger semantic alignment and higher efficiency than involved baselines. These results expose persistent vulnerabilities in current IGMU methods and highlight the need for robustness-aware unlearning against multi-modal adversarial attacks. records.title: Benchmarking Cross-Scale Perception Ability of Large Multimodal Models in Material Science
records.abstract: Unraveling the hierarchical structure-property relationships is the central challenge of materials science, necessitating the interpretation of data across vast physical scales from micro to macro. Despite the rapid integration of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) into scientific workflows, existing scientific benchmarks primarily focus on general chart interpretation or isolated common-sense reasoning, failing to capture reasoning ability across intricate physical dimensions. To address this, we introduce CSMBench, a dataset comprising 1,041 high-quality figures curated from premier journals up to September 2025. CSMBench categorizes data into four scientifically distinct regimes: atomic, micro, meso, and macro scales, strictly aligning with the focus and definitions in materials study. Through open-ended figure description and multiple-choice caption matching tasks, we evaluate state-of-the-art open-source and closed-source models. Our analysis identifies that performance varies significantly across physical scales due to the distinct visual characteristics, highlighting the limitations of current generalist models and identifying critical directions for achieving hierarchical and accurate understanding in materials research.

records.title: Minimal Edits, Maximum Privacy: Bayesian-Guided Generative Agents for Silent Geolocation Shielding
records.abstract: The rapid evolution of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) and geolocation techniques has precipitated widespread geoprivacy concerns amidst the explosion of social media imagery. While countermeasures exist, current protection techniques typically rely on naive obfuscation or adversarial perturbations, and these methods often compromise visual aesthetics and consistency while offering limited robustness against localization. To address this gap, we introduce a fully automated pipeline for generating privacy-preserving images via minimal, risk-aware modifications. Our approach leverages feature extraction methods combined with a Bayesian network to identify vulnerable visual factors, utilizing a VLM-driven Edit-Agent Loop to guide generative editing. This ensures modifications are semantically targeted to neutralize risks while maintaining image integrity. Experiments demonstrate that our framework achieves robust protection with edits that remain virtually imperceptible. Consequently, our work offers a fresh perspective on safeguarding image geoprivacy in the era of Large Language Models.

records.title: Predictor–Corrector Flow Matching for Crystal Structure Generation
records.abstract: Crystalline materials discovery empowered by deep generative models is critical for driving progress in applications such as energy storage, electronics, and catalysis. However, current approaches still face challenges in accurately predicting complex structures and in flexibly steering generated candidates toward desired properties, which hinders their practical applicability. In this work, we propose GAT-Flow, a flow-based generative framework for crystalline materials. We employ a graph attention network to jointly model lattice vectors and atomic coordinates, aiming to better capture local coordination environments and periodic patterns. We further incorporate a predictor–corrector sampling strategy to improve sampling efficiency and numerical stability. In addition, by leveraging decoupled guidance from a fine-tuned language model, we demonstrate property-driven crystalline generation from simple textual prompts, using band gap energy as a case study. Experimental results show that GAT-Flow achieves strong and competitive performance on standard crystalline structure prediction benchmarks, outperforming prior generative baselines considered in our study. These results indicate that GAT-Flow provides a flexible framework for crystal structure prediction and for exploring structure–property alignment in computational materials design.

records.title: A Scalable Pipeline for Enabling Non-Verbal Speech Generation and Understanding
records.abstract: Non-verbal Vocalizations (NVs), such as laughter and sighs, are vital for conveying emotion and intention in human speech, yet most existing speech systems neglect them, which severely compromises communicative richness and emotional intelligence. Existing methods for NVs acquisition are either costly and unscalable (relying on manual annotation/recording) or unnatural (relying on rule-based synthesis). To address these limitations, we propose a highly scalable automatic annotation framework to label non-verbal phenomena from natural speech, which is low-cost, easily extendable, and inherently diverse and natural. This framework leverages a frame-level detection model to accurately identify NVs in natural speech and integrates them with transcripts via temporal-semantic alignment method. Using this framework, we created and released NonVerbalSpeech-38K, a diverse, real-world dataset featuring 38,718 samples across 10 NV categories collected from in-the-wild media. Experimental results demonstrate that our dataset provides superior controllability for NVs generation and achieves comparable performance for NVs understanding.

records.title: UniMBG: A Unified Multi-Modal Brain Graph Model for Brain Network Analysis
records.abstract: The integration of structural and functional modalities has emerged as a promising paradigm for comprehensive brain network analysis. However, the multi-modal labeled data scarcity limits the generalization of supervised models and constrains existing graph self-supervised learning paradigms to isolated disease cohorts, modal imbalance, and paradigm separation. To bridge this gap, we propose UniMBG, a unified multi-modal brain graph foundation model that mitigates data limitations by learning universal representations. By scaling pre-training across diverse cross-disorder cohorts, UniMBG captures generalized and transferable correlation patterns. This framework introduces a unified multi-modal graph pre-training strategy that synergizes generative and contrastive paradigms, employing complementary masking to facilitate mutual reinforcement between structural and functional views. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UniMBG achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art baselines. Notably, the model exhibits robustness in few-shot and out-of-distribution scenarios, validating its potential as a general multi-modal backbone in data-scarce contexts.

records.title: SpiRegFormer: A Dual-stage Feature Refinement Framework for Spiking Transformer Inspired by Hierarchical Visual Regulation
records.abstract: Transformer-based Spiking Neural Networks obtain significant advancement in neuromorphic vision but often suffer from "attention distraction", where computational resources are wasted on irrelevant background information. Drawing on the "suppression-enhancement" mechanism of the biological visual system, where early visual pathways filter out background redundancy via center-surround antagonism while higher areas amplify relevant features through gain modulation, we propose SpiRegFormer. Specifically, our method employs a hierarchical attention strategy: a Spiking Spatio-Temporal Differential Attention module in shallow layers which mimics center-surround antagonism to suppress noise, and a Spiking Dual-Threshold Enhancement Attention module in deep layers which emulates gain modulation to amplify foreground features. This approach effectively refines information flow and resolves attention distraction. Extensive experimental results indicate that SpiRegFormer obtains superior performance across various benchmarks, reaching 76.80% accuracy on ImageNet and improving accuracy by 1.98% on CIFAR-100 and 2.3% on CIFAR10-DVS compared to existing spiking Transformers.

records.title: Shifting Uncertainty to Critical Moments: Towards Reliable Uncertainty Quantification for VLA Model
records.abstract: Vision–Language–Action (VLA) models enable general-purpose robotic policies by mapping visual observations and language instructions to low-level actions, but they often lack reliable introspection. A common practice is to compute a token-level uncertainty signal and take its mean over a rollout. However, mean aggregation can dilute short-lived but safety-critical uncertainty spikes in continuous control. In particular, successful rollouts may contain localized high-entropy segments due to benign noise or non-critical micro-adjustments, while failure rollouts can appear low-entropy for most timesteps and only exhibit brief spikes near the onset of failure. We propose a unified uncertainty quantification approach for predicting rollout success versus failure that (1) uses max-based sliding window pooling to preserve transient risk signals, (2) applies motion-aware stability weighting to emphasize high-frequency action oscillations associated with unstable behaviors, and (3) performs DoF-adaptive calibration via Bayesian Optimization to prioritize kinematically critical axes. Experiments on the LIBERO benchmark show that our method substantially improves failure prediction accuracy and yields more reliable signals for failure detection, which can support downstream human-in-the-loop interventions.

records.title: CycleLoRA: A Cycle-Consistent Low-Rank Approach for Continuous Image Editing
records.abstract: While diffusion models have achieved remarkable success in image generation and manipulation, continuous editing remains challenging due to semantic entanglement issues. Existing LoRA-based methods often alter unintended attributes during editing—for instance, changing a person's identity when modifying their age. We present CycleLoRA, a novel continuous editing method that achieves disentangled control by imposing a cycle consistency constraint on noised images during LoRA optimization. Our key insight is to learn a single bidirectional LoRA adapter that can be applied with positive or negative scaling factors to transform the noised image and reconstruct the original state. Unlike previous approaches that apply cycle constraints to clean images, we operate directly on noised images with a proposed inversion strategy that ensures consistent noise levels. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CycleLoRA achieves superior identity preservation and semantic disentanglement compared to state-of-the-art methods, while supporting both real image editing and multi-attribute manipulation.

records.title: AGPL: Adaptive Granularity Prototypical Learning for Multimodal Depression Detection
records.abstract: Multimodal depression detection requires capturing complex behavioral phenotypes, while standard prototypical networks fail to capture this intricacy by enforcing uniform prototype granularity. This limitation causes a granularity mismatch where complex classes lack sufficient expressiveness and simple classes are over-parameterized. Furthermore, conventional fusion strategies often suffer from modal dominance that obscures critical subtle cues. We propose the Adaptive Granularity Prototypical Learning (AGPL) framework to address these challenges. The Complexity-Aware Prototype Selection (CAPS) module dynamically adjusts the number of sub-prototypes based on class complexity to ensure structural alignment with the data geometry. Additionally, we introduce a Dynamic Cross-Modal Collaboration (DCMC) mechanism that utilizes a progressive transition strategy to regulate optimization and prevent the suppression of weaker modalities. Extensive experiments on D-Vlog and LMVD benchmarks confirm that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods, notably increasing the F1 score by 5.09% and Recall by 10.82% on LMVD.

records.title: Implicit Diffusion Distillation with Domain Disentanglement for Domain Generalization
records.abstract: While Vision-Language Models (VLMs) like CLIP have advanced Domain Generalization (DG), adapting them to scarce source data inevitably leads to biased alignment, where models rely on superficial shortcuts (e.g., textures) rather than robust semantics. To rectify this, we introduce Diffusion-Distilled Generalization (DDG), a framework that harnesses the manifold-aware priors of frozen diffusion models to compensate for source data scarcity. Instead of computationally intensive data augmentation, we propose an efficient, end-to-end generative inverse problem paradigm: the visual backbone is optimized as a conditioning agent, guiding a frozen diffusion teacher to reconstruct source images. This implicit objective compels the student to internalize structure-aware knowledge, effectively overriding source-specific biases. Furthermore, to explicitly decouple content from style, we introduce a Domain-Debiasing Guidance mechanism. By explicitly suppressing domain-specific signals via Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG), we ensure the distilled features remain robust across domain shifts. Extensive experiments on the DomainBed benchmark demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, and qualitative analyses confirm its ability to "see through" domain shifts by learning structural invariance.

records.title: Adaptive Bilateral Motion Vector Refinement for Next Generation Video Coding
records.abstract: Efficiently improving the accuracy of Motion Vectors (MVs) in the merge candidate list is a critical challenge for advanced inter coding technology. To this end, Versatile Video Coding (VVC) employs the Merge mode with Motion Vector Difference (MMVD), which refines MVs by adding predefined MVDs. Nevertheless, to balance coding efficiency and signaling overhead, MMVD restricts MVDs to cardinal directions and assumes symmetry in bi-predicted MVs. These constraints may result in inaccurate refinement in regions with complex motion, leading to imprecise MV. To address this issue, we propose an Adaptive Bilateral Motion Vector Refinement (ABMVR) approach to achieve more accurate MV refinement for complex motion while maintaining low bitrate overhead. Specifically, ABMVR comprises three key components: 10 precise distance candidates, 16 uniformly distributed diagonal directions, and two unidirectional refinement templates. These components are integrated into a Bilateral Matching (BM) based multistage search strategy to accurately characterize complex motion. Furthermore, a Temporal-Context-Aware Syntax Optimization (TCASO) method is designed to reduce signaling overhead by adaptively adjusting ABMVR syntax elements according to motion consistency with co-located blocks in reference frames. Finally, meticulously designed fast algorithms are implemented to skip unnecessary candidate evaluations, thereby effectively reducing both encoding and decoding complexities. The simulation result shows that on top of the VVC Test Model (VTM-23.13), ABMVR achieves 1.40% BD-rate gain for Random Access (RA).

records.title: Modularized Dynamic-Granularity Video LLM for Multi-Event Long Video Understanding
records.abstract: Video Large Language Models (Video LLMs) have made significant advancements in various video understanding tasks. However, long-video scenarios remain challenging due to the inherent tension between limited visual token budgets and the need to capture multiple key events. Existing approaches typically process long videos in two stages, i.e., i) select keyframes and ii) perform detailed perception, which exhibit significant limitations: they lack a modular mechanism for adaptive capacity allocation and self-correction, resulting in unreliable modeling. To tackle these challenges, we propose MoD-VLLM, a novel Modularized Dynamic-Granularity Video LLM framework for multi-event long video understanding, which seamlessly unifies temporal grounding and semantic understanding in an iterative, self-reflective manner. Specifically, we propose a Positive-Negative Video Segments Grounding module and a Modularized Dynamic-Granularity Reflection module, which form a closed loop to progressively localize the question-related video segments. The grounding module instructs a Video LLM to distinguish relevant from irrelevant video segments based on the video question. The reflection module employs a modularized scheduler that dynamically selects fine-grained encoding for relevant positive segments to capture detailed perception and coarse-grained encoding for negative segments to efficiently maintain global context, thereby enabling adaptive granularity allocation. We further propose a dynamic-granularity reinforcement learning strategy, allowing MoD-VLLM to learn optimal grounding policies and dynamic granularity visual representation jointly. Moreover, we propose MEventBench, a challenging Multi-Event Long Video Benchmark to evaluate models for complex long video understanding and reasoning. Extensive experiments on several long video understanding benchmarks and our MEventBench demonstrate that the proposed MoD-VLLM is able to significantly outperform state-of-the-art baselines.

records.title: GT-PCQA: Geometry-Texture Decoupled Point Cloud Quality Assessment with MLLM
records.abstract: With the rapid advancement of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs), MLLM-based Image Quality Assessment (IQA) methods have shown promising generalization. However, directly extending these MLLM-based IQA methods to PCQA remains challenging. On the one hand, existing PCQA datasets are limited in scale, which hinders stable and effective instruction tuning of MLLMs. On the other hand, due to large-scale image-text pretraining, MLLMs tend to rely on texture-dominant reasoning and are insufficiently sensitive to geometric structural degradations that are critical for PCQA. To address these gaps, we propose a novel MLLM-based no-reference PCQA framework, termed GT-PCQA, which is built upon two key strategies. First, to enable stable and effective instruction tuning under scarce PCQA supervision, a 2D–3D joint training strategy is proposed. This strategy formulates PCQA as a relative quality comparison problem to unify large-scale IQA datasets with limited PCQA datasets. It incorporates a parameter-efficient Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) scheme to support instruction tuning. Second, a geometry-texture decoupling strategy is presented, which integrates a dual-prompt mechanism with an alternating optimization scheme to mitigate the inherent texture-dominant bias of pre-trained MLLMs, while enhancing sensitivity to geometric structural degradations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GT-PCQA achieves competitive performance and exhibits strong generalization.

records.title: Self-Corrective Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Visual-spatial Reasoning
records.abstract: Visual spatial intelligence is crucial for tasks requiring the understanding and reasoning of physical spaces using visual information. While existing methods, such as Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), have improved spatial reasoning, they often suffer from limited generalization. Reinforcement Fine-Tuning (RFT) enhances reasoning through policy iteration but struggles with fostering advanced behaviors like self-correction in visual spatial tasks. To address these limitations, we propose Self-Corrective Reinforcement Fine-Tuning (SC-RFT), a novel approach that promotes self-correction during visual spatial reasoning. SC-RFT integrates Self-Correction Guidance into low-reward paths after reward assignment, encouraging error correction and leading to higher rewards, thereby improving path exploration efficiency. Our method surpasses RFT in activating self-correction and enhances data efficiency. Additionally, we introduce VSR-4K, a 4K visual spatial reasoning dataset based on ARKitScenes, offering verifiable reward signals for reinforcement fine-tuning. Extensive experiments on the VSI-Bench demonstrate that SC-RFT outperforms both RFT and SFT, allowing a 3B model to surpass the 72B mainstream MLLMs. Performance on ScanQA and SQA3D benchmarks further confirm SC-RFT's superior generalization.

records.title: Completing the Response Space: Unifying Rejection and Multi-Interval Video Grounding via Cardinality-Rectified GRPO
records.abstract: Existing Temporal Video Grounding (TVG) methods fail to reject irrelevant queries or distinguish disjoint events due to a forced single-interval assumption. We unify these failures under the perspective of Cardinality Generalization, theoretically demonstrating that standard RL objectives suffer from a Gambling Bias in zero-instance scenarios (incentivizing guessing) and a Unimodal Bias in multi-instance scenarios (favoring merging). To rectify this, we propose CaR-GRPO (Cardinality-Rectified Group Relative Policy Optimization). Our framework introduces an implicit calibration mechanism via negative sampling to establish a robust rejection boundary, alongside novel Cardinality and Endpoint Distance objectives to enforce structural precision. Extensive experiments show that CaR-GRPO effectively eliminates the identified biases, achieving state-of-the-art performance in both rejection capability and multi-interval retrieval.

records.title: EchoMark: Acoustic Environment Matching with Watermarked Room Impulse Response
records.abstract: Recent advances in acoustic environment matching (AEM) allow creators to edit room acoustic effects using only a reference reverberant recording, enabling applications such as voice dubbing and immersive auditory virtual reality. However, such easy ``relocation” of audio environments raises security concerns, including realistic voice spoofing. We propose EchoMark, the first watermarked AEM framework that proactively protects and augments room impulse responses (RIRs). EchoMark adopts an EWG-D architecture with physics-inspired inductive biases to exploit watermark capacity that is imperceptible to human listeners. The embedded watermark remains detectable after convolution with arbitrary speech. Experiments show that EchoMark achieves competitive AEM quality among RIR reconstruction models while uniquely providing near-perfect watermark detection performance.

records.title: EmoStory: Emotion-Aware Story Generation
records.abstract: Story generation aims to produce image sequences that depict coherent narratives while maintaining subject consistency across frames. Although existing methods have excelled in producing coherent and expressive stories, they remain largely emotion-neutral, focusing on what subject appears in a story while overlooking how emotions shape narrative interpretation and visual presentation. As stories are intended to engage audiences emotionally, we introduce emotion-aware story generation, a new task that aims to generate subject-consistent visual stories with explicit emotional directions. This task is challenging due to the abstract nature of emotions, which must be grounded in concrete visual elements and consistently expressed across a narrative through visual composition. To address these challenges, we propose EmoStory, a two-stage framework that integrates agent-based story planning and region-aware story generation. The planning stage transforms target emotions into coherent story prompts with emotion agent and writer agent, while the generation stage preserves subject consistency and injects emotion-related elements through region-aware composition. We evaluate EmoStory on a newly constructed dataset covering 25 subjects and 600 emotional stories. Extensive quantitative and qualitative results, along with user studies, show that EmoStory outperforms state-of-the-art story generation methods in emotion accuracy, prompt alignment, and subject consistency. records.title: Mitigating Bystander Blindness in MLLMs for Multimodal Harmful Meme Moderation
records.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) show promise in visual understanding but struggle to reliably {annotate} and {explain} implicit harmful memes due to \textit{Bystander Blindness}, where generic safety alignment enforces a detached neutrality, blinding models to the subtle, identity-situated nuances of hate. To address this, we propose \underline{Vi}be \underline{Lens} for Harm (ViLens), a framework that embodies diverse {Vibe Lenses} to surface the missing socio-cultural bridge suppressed by bystander alignment, and moderates memes based on these bridged rationales. Specifically, \textbf{Vibe Lenses Instantiation} identifies potential related reception stances. \textbf{Multi-View Rationale Elicitation} conditions MLLMs on each stance to surface harm-relevant cues and plausible negative impacts. \textbf{Normative Aggregation} calibrates and synthesizes multi-lens rationales into a robust final verdict. Experiments on English (FHM, MAMI) and Chinese (ToxiCN-MM) dataset show that ViLens achieves excellent performance while effectively exposing affected parties to bridge the gap between moderation and explanation.

records.title: EmoGuide: A Training-Free Dual-Level Emotion Steering Framework for High-Fidelity Image Emotion Editing
records.abstract: While diffusion-based image editing has mastered visible attributes, controlling high-level semantics like emotions remains challenging. Existing methods often fail to balance emotional expressiveness with structural fidelity, leading to either ambiguous edits or content distortion. To address this, we propose EmoGuide, a training-free framework that decouples emotion injection into coarse-grained directional steering and fine-grained semantic sharpening. EmoGuide first employs an Emotion Prior Vector Guidance (EPVG) to establish a global editing direction in the latent space without disrupting layout. Subsequently, a Contrastive Emotion Distribution Guidance (CEDG) sharpens the specific emotional semantics by maximizing the margin between the target and competitor emotions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EmoGuide achieves superior emotion controllability while preserving the original identity and background, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art baselines. records.title: AesBench: Benchmarking Large Multimodal Models on Image Aesthetics Understanding
records.abstract: Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) are undergoing flourishing development, promoting human-machine interaction and collaboration in daily life. However, their capacities for understanding image aesthetics largely remain unexplored. This may impede the applications of advanced LMMs in real-world scenarios, e.g., art design and image generation. To address this dilemma, this paper introduces AesBench, an expert benchmark to systematically evaluate the aesthetic understanding capacities of LMMs. In this benchmark, high-quality annotations are first collected from aesthetic experts, based on which an aesthetics understanding benchmark dataset is built. In addition, we design a set of integrative criteria to evaluate LMMs from four shallow-to-deep perspectives, including perception, empathy, assessment and interpretation. Based on Aesbench, we comprehensively evaluate and analyze 16 general-purpose LMMs. Finally, we present three fine-tuned versions based on open-source counterparts. Experimental results indicate that several advanced LMMs have preliminary aesthetic understanding abilities, and could be further enhanced by aesthetic instruction tuning. Nonetheless, there is still a significant gap between current LMMs and humans. We hope this work can encourage the community to delve into more profound investigations of the yet untapped potential of LMMs in image aesthetics understanding. records.title: Modality-Decentralized Network for Incomplete Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
records.abstract: Incomplete multimodal sentiment analysis poses the challenges of both various modality absence and cross-modal sentiment conflicts. While existing approaches primarily address missing modalities—either by imputing absent modalities or learning a shared feature space from available ones, the issue of cross-modal sentiment conflicts remains largely overlooked. In this paper, we propose Modality-Decentralized Network (MoDNet), shifting the focus from modality-centric processing to direct sentiment modeling. MoDNet mines latent sentimental cues from the available modalities to adapt to diverse incomplete inputs. Specifically, a Hierarchical Mixture of Sentiment Experts module (Hi-MoSE) is employed to hierarchically distill sentiment via: (i) token-level modality-agnostic decomposition and (ii) sequence-level cross-modal consistency aggregation. Then, a Dynamic Modality Routing (DMR) module is used to identify optimal modality combinations for sentiment inference. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of MoDNet across 7 modality combinations, showcasing average gains of +7.53% on CMU-MOSI and +4.45% on CMU-MOSEI, while boosting inference speed by 15.8%.

records.title: Disentangle-then-Refine: LLM-Guided Decoupling and Structure-Aware Refinement for Graph Contrastive Learning
records.abstract: Conventional Graph Contrastive Learning (GCL) on Text-Attributed Graphs (TAGs) relies on blind stochastic augmentations, inadvertently entangling task-relevant signals with noise. We propose SDM-SCR, a robust framework anchored in Approximate Orthogonal Decomposition. First, the Semantic Decoupling Module (SDM) leverages the instruction-following capability of Large Language Models (LLMs) to actively parse raw attributes into asymmetric, task-oriented signal and noise views. This shifts the paradigm from random perturbation to semantic-aware disentanglement. Subsequently, Semantic Consistency Regularization (SCR) exploits the spectral observation that semantic signals are topologically smooth while residual noise is high-frequency. SCR functions as a selective spectral filter, enforcing consistency only on the signal subspace to eliminate LLM hallucinations without over-smoothing. This “Disentanglethen-Refine” mechanism ensures rigorous signal purification. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SDM-SCR achieves SOTA performance in accuracy and efficiency.

records.title: HQ-MPDS: A Multilingual Artifact-Controlled Benchmark for Partial Deepfake Speech Detection
records.abstract: Detecting partial deepfake speech is challenging because manipulations occur only in short regions while the surrounding audio remains authentic. However, existing detection methods are fundamentally limited by the quality of available datasets, many of which rely on outdated synthesis systems and generation procedures that introduce dataset-specific artifacts rather than realistic manipulation cues. To address this gap, we introduce HQ-MPDS, a High-Quality Multilingual Partial Deepfake Speech dataset. HQ-MPDS is constructed using linguistically coherent splice points derived from fine-grained forced alignment, aiming to preserve prosodic and semantic continuity and minimize audible and visual boundary artifacts. The dataset contains 350.8 hours of speech across 8 languages and 550 speakers, with background effects added to better reflect real-world acoustic conditions. MOS evaluations and spectrogram analysis confirm the high perceptual naturalness of the samples. We benchmark state-of-the-art detection models through cross-language and cross-dataset evaluations, and all models experience performance drops exceeding 80% on HQ-MPDS. These results demonstrate that HQ-MPDS exposes significant generalization challenges once low-level artifacts are removed and multilingual and acoustic diversity are introduced, which provides a more realistic and demanding benchmark for partial deepfake detection. The dataset is available at: https://zenodo.org/records/17929533

records.title: IKMo: Image-Keyframed Motion Generation with Trajectory-Pose Conditioned Motion Diffusion Model
records.abstract: While text-to-motion generation is mainstream, integrating explicit spatial constraints has become a standard solution for precise animation. Existing state-of-the-art models are tailored for professional workflows, effectively processing high-quality, pre-aligned 3D inputs via unified conditioning mechanisms. However, this strictly aligned setting restricts accessibility for general users who rely on unaligned, in-the-wild 2D reference images. This accessible scenario introduces a fundamental conflict: heterogeneous geometric constraints, where user-defined global trajectories clash with local image-derived poses. To resolve this coordinate mismatch, we propose TPMDM, a diffusion model featuring a decoupled parallel control strategy that explicitly isolates and aligns these divergent signals. Furthermore, we introduce IKMo, a holistic framework that synergizes TPMDM with a VLM-powered multi-agent system. By bridging the semantic-geometric gap, IKMo translates user-friendly inputs into explicit motion constraints to drive the diffusion backbone. Experiments on HumanML3D and KIT-ML demonstrate that our method establishes a new state-of-the-art in the task of generating motions under heterogeneous trajectory and keyframe pose constraints.

records.title: DualCoreAgent: A Black-Box Safety Controller for Web Agents
records.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents have progressed from basic chatbots to systems capable of operating in complex interactive web environments, invoking tools, accessing authenticated accounts, and automating multimodal workflows. These advancements introduce significant safety risks. Conventional safety approaches, such as prompting, fine-tuning, and post-hoc filtering, are often inadequate in long-horizon scenarios. Agents may either act effectively while violating policies or remain compliant but perform unreliably. This study introduces DualCoreAgent, a plug-and-play safety controller designed to wrap existing web agents without modifying their internal planning logic. DualCoreAgent separates goal-directed planning from rule-aware compliance reasoning and connects them through cross-layer arbitration and memory-augmented inference. This architecture transforms safety into an active control signal that guides the agent’s trajectory. Experimental results on web-agent safety benchmarks demonstrate that DualCoreAgent outperforms existing methods in terms of constrained task success, policy compliance, and reduction of unnecessary refusals.

records.title: ReSIP: Reinforcement Learning with Symbolic Inductive Planning for Interpretable and Generalizable Pixel-Based Control
records.abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has struggled with pixel-based control tasks that have long sequences and logical dependencies. Methods using structured representations have shown promise in generalizing to different objects in manipulation tasks. However, they lack the ability to segment and reuse atomic skills. Neuro-symbolic RL excels in handling long-horizon tasks with sequential and decomposable structure, yet it heavily relies on expert-designed predicates. To address these challenges, we propose ReSIP, a novel framework for pixel-based control that combines Reinforcement Learning with Symbolic Inductive Planning. Our approach first automatically discovers and learns atomic skills through experiences in simple environments without human intervention. Then, we employ a genetic algorithm to enhance these atomic skills with symbolic interpretations. Therefore, we convert the complex controlling problem into a planning problem. Taking advantage of symbolic planning and object-centric skills, our model is inherently interpretable and provides compositional generalizability. The results of the experiments show that our method demonstrates superior performance in long-horizon sequential tasks and complex object manipulation.

records.title: MTMS: A Jailbreak Attack on MLLMs via Dual-Vector Perturbation on Hidden Embeddings
records.abstract: Jailbreak attacks pose a significant security risk to Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). Existing methods mostly perform perturbations on input prompts, failing to exploit internal safety mechanism, and suffer from poor cross-scenario robustness and low response utility. To gain deeper insight into MLLM safety mechanisms, we find that safety alignment induces separable clusters in MLLM internal representations, implicitly forming a cognitive safety boundary between harmful and harmless instructions. Building on this insight, we exploit this boundary to design Multi-Targeted Manipulation Strategy (MTMS), a novel jailbreak attack strategy. MTMS adopts a dual-vector perturbation mechanism, consisting of a Concept-Misleading Vector that enables category-level bypass and an Instruction-Shifting Vector that facilitates fine-grained modulation. By injecting dual-vector perturbation into the model’s safety-aware layers during inference, MTMS induces the model to misjudge harmful instructions as harmless, achieving jailbreak. Furthermore, to evaluate the robustness of attack performance, we propose the Stability Score (SS), which jointly measures both the attack effectiveness and stability across different scenarios. Experiments show that MTMS increases toxicity scores by approximately 22% over the baseline methods and SS by 27%, validating its efficacy.

records.title: FreeEdit-AR: Enabling Flexible Training-Free Editing on Autoregressive Models
records.abstract: Despite dominating training-free editing, diffusion models require heavy priors to suppress inherent stochasticity. Traditional autoregressive (AR) models also fail at controllable editing due to raster-scan serialization. However, the emergence of scale-based AR modeling overcomes these barriers by preserving spatial correlations. Exploiting these structures, we introduce FreeEdit-AR, a training-free framework for flexible, inference-only editing. Our framework seamlessly supports reference-driven, text-guided, and hybrid editing modes within a unified pipeline. Specifically, we propose an attention-driven reference fusion module; unlike diffusion models requiring manual masks for alignment, it utilizes native self-attention scores as adaptive pixel-wise coefficients for interpretable integration without auxiliary modules. Moreover, we introduce a flexible prompting mechanism that redistributes token-level semantic weights via $L_2$-norm conservation, effectively sharpening text-based control. Experimental results demonstrate that FreeEdit-AR excels in structural fidelity and flexibility, offering a robust training-free alternative for AR-based image editing.

records.title: Thinking Like Van Gogh: Structure-Aware Style Transfer via Flow-Guided 3D Gaussian Splatting
records.abstract: In 1888, Vincent van Gogh articulated: "I am seeking exaggeration in the essential." This principle—magnifying structural form while eliminating photographic detail—defined Post-Impressionist art. However, current 3D style transfer methods invert this philosophy, treating geometry as a rigid canvas for texture projection. To authentically replicate Post-Impressionist stylization, we must embrace geometricabstraction as the mechanism of expression. We present a flow-guided geometric advection framework for 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) that computationally realizes this principle. Our method extracts 2D directional flow from paintings and back-propagates these patterns to rectify 3D Gaussians, producing flow-aligned brushstrokes that wrap around scene topology without mesh priors. Our key innovations including: (1) mesh-free flow guidance via projection analysis, (2) luminance-structure decoupling that separates geometric deformation from color optimization, preventing artifacts during structural abstraction, and (3) VLM-as-a-Judge framework that assesses artistic authenticity through aesthetic judgment rather than pixel metrics, addressing the inherent subjectivity of art.

records.title: TriCD: Tri-View Credibility-Guided Disentanglement for Multimodal Multi-Domain Rumor Detection
records.abstract: Multimodal multi-domain rumor detection is crucial for maintaining online information credibility. Existing statistical paradigms often fail to identify logically fallacious rumors and struggle to adaptively weigh heterogeneous semantic and social views across diverse domains, leading to misjudgments when evidence conflicts under uncertainty. To address these challenges, we propose Tri-view Credibility-guided Disentanglement (TriCD). This framework synergizes semantic cues, propagation struc- tures, and a Chain-of-Thought (CoT)-driven cognitive view via a multimodal large language model (MLLM). The cognitive view performs deliberate analytical reasoning (System 2) to capture deep logical cues beyond surface correlations. A domain- aware fusion engine grounded in Dempster–Shafer theory is then employed to dynamically estimate the credibility of each view and aggregate evidence while accounting for epistemic uncertainty. Furthermore, a dual-mechanism disentangler integrating adver- sarial learning with an Information Bottleneck (IB) constraint filters domain-specific stylistic noise to isolate invariant decep- tion primitives. Experiments on Pheme, Weibo, and FineFake demonstrate that TriCD consistently achieves superior overall performance and robust multi-domain generalization.

records.title: Leveraging Textual Prompts for EEG-Based Depression Recognition
records.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a common mental illness marked by persistent low mood and cognitive dysfunction. Electroencephalography (EEG), with rich temporal dynamics and non-invasive acquisition, is promising for objective depression assessment, yet current methods face information redundancy, high computational cost, and limited domain knowledge use. We propose TS-LLM, a dual-branch framework combining time–frequency EEG encoding with large language model (LLM) prompt guidance. The EEG branch captures correlated time–frequency features, while the LLM branch leverages clinically informed symptom descriptions to generate semantically aligned, noise-resilient embeddings. This knowledge–signal alignment enables robust fusion of EEG patterns with expert-level semantics. Experiments on two real-world datasets show up to 4.23\% accuracy improvement over state-of-the-art baselines, underscoring the promise of prompt-guided EEG representation learning for intelligent mental health assessment.

records.title: DCG-Net: Dual Cross-Attention with Concept-Value Graph Reasoning for Interpretable Medical Diagnosis
records.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved strong performance in medical image analysis, but their internal decision processes remain difficult to interpret. Concept Bottleneck Models (CBMs) partially address this limitation by structuring predictions through human-interpretable clinical concepts. However, existing CBMs typically overlook the contextual dependencies among concepts. To address these issues, we propose an end-to-end interpretable framework DCG-Net that integrates multimodal alignment with structured concept reasoning. DCG-Net introduces a Dual Cross-Attention module that replaces cosine similarity matching with bidirectional attention between visual tokens and canonicalized textual concept-value prototypes, enabling spatially localized evidence attribution. To capture the relational structure inherent to clinical concepts, we develop a Parametric Concept Graph initialized with Positive Pointwise Mutual Information priors and refined through sparsity-controlled message passing. This formulation models inter-concept dependencies in a manner consistent with clinical domain knowledge. Experiments on white blood cell morphology and skin lesion diagnosis demonstrate that DCG-Net achieves state-of-the-art classification performance while producing clinically interpretable diagnostic explanations.

records.title: Vivid-Animator:Expressive and Controllable Human Animation with Facial-Body Hybrid Guidance
records.abstract: Realistic human animation remains a crucial but challenging task. Although current methods have made significant progress in controlling body poses, they still suffer from identity drift, motion jitter, and inadequate modeling of facial expressions. In this paper, we propose a novel Vivid-Animator framework that leverages dual temporal cues from facial expressions and body poses to achieve realistic and controllable human animation. Specifically, we first introduce a Dynamic Reference Strategy to generate expression-disentangled dynamic identity sequences, enhancing identity preservation during animation. Central to our approach, the effective combination of extracted facial expressions with diverse 3D control sequences jointly model expressive appearance and motion dynamics in the latent space. Furthermore, we employ a Spatio-Temporal Fusion Module to perform spatial fusion and temporal refinement of facial and pose features, reinforcing full-body motion coherence and expression stability. Extensive qualitative and quantitative experiments demonstrate that Vivid-Animator consistently outperforms previous methods in animation quality, producing expressive human videos while better preserving identity.

records.title: SkinCLIP-VL: Consistency-Aware Vision-Language Learning for Multimodal Skin Cancer Diagnosis
records.abstract: The deployment of vision-language models (VLMs) in dermatology is hindered by the trilemma of high computational costs, extreme data scarcity, and the "black-box" nature of deep learning. To address these challenges, we present SkinCLIP-VL, a resource-efficient framework that adapts foundation models for trustworthy skin cancer diagnosis. Adopting a frozen perception, adaptive reasoning paradigm, we integrate a frozen CLIP encoder with a lightweight, quantized Qwen2.5-VL via low-rank adaptation (LoRA). To strictly align visual regions with clinical semantics under long-tailed distributions, we propose the Consistency-aware Focal Alignment (CFA) Loss. This objective synergizes focal re-weighting, semantic alignment, and calibration. On ISIC and Derm7pt benchmarks, SkinCLIP-VL surpasses 13B-parameter baselines by 4.3–6.2% in accuracy with 43% fewer parameters. Crucially, blinded expert evaluation and out-of-distribution testing confirm that our visually grounded rationales significantly enhance clinical trust compared to traditional saliency maps.

records.title: TriPAH: Imbalance-Aware Tri-Prompt Affinity Hashing for Cross-Modal Medical Retrieval
records.abstract: In the era of big medical data, efficient cross-modal retrieval is pivotal for evidence-based diagnosis and large-scale case management. Cross-modal medical hashing retrieval aims to enable efficient image–text search and support downstream tasks such as case-based reasoning and decision support by learning compact, semantically aligned binary codes. However, current methods suffer from semantic fragmentation due to noisy clinical language, long-tailed labels, and brittle quantization that weakens alignment. We propose TriPAH, a Tri-Prompt Affinity Hashing framework. TriPAH synthesizes ontology-grounded, patient-level prompts conditioned on normalized clinical cues to yield low-noise textual representations for initial alignment. A lightweight prompt–token mixer performs hierarchical, multi-granularity alignment and produces quantization-ready features under an asymmetric multi-task objective coupling multi-positive contrastive alignment, imbalance-aware classification, and progressive quantization regularization. A patient-level consistency module further stabilizes codes across complementary views. Extensive experiments on three public datasets demonstrate that TriPAH significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

records.title: Hierarchical Slide Aggregation for Whole-slide Question Answering with Large Vision-Language Models
records.abstract: Whole-slide image visual question answering (WSI-VQA) requires reasoning over gigapixel pathology slides, where diagnostically relevant evidence is often scattered across spatially distant regions. Existing pathology VQA models, whether based on patch-level LVLMs or WSI-specific architectures, struggle to combine fine-grained cellular cues with global tissue-level context, limiting their ability to perform whole-slide reasoning using general-purpose LVLMs. We introduce HiSA, a hierarchical slide aggregation framework designed to bridge this gap. Unlike prior WSI-VQA approaches that couple bespoke slide encoders with task-specific decoders, HiSA enables multi-scale, LVLM-compatible slide representations through a dual-tier feature distillation module that progressively integrates patch-level signals into semantically structured slide embeddings. This allows LVLMs to conduct question-conditioned reasoning over entire WSIs without sacrificing alignment with patch-level pathology knowledge. We further construct an instruction-following WSI-VQA dataset to fully leverage LVLM generative capabilities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that HiSA yields substantial improvements over state-of-the-art WSI-VQA systems across both natural language generation and factual-consistency metrics, while simultaneously advancing patch-level pathology chatbot performance. These results highlight HiSA as an effective and generalizable framework for scalable whole-slide reasoning with large vision–language models.

records.title: PromptFix: Anatomy-Aware Text Prompting for Semi-Supervised Lumbar MRI Segmentation
records.abstract: Accurate lumbar spine substructures segmentation in MRI is essential for diagnosing spinal disorders, yet remains challenging: existing visual-modal-based solutions struggle to incorporate anatomical priors, struggling to discriminate similar substructures, while the high-cost annotation leads to labeled data scarcity that limits performance. To address this, we propose \textit{PromptFix}, pioneering an anatomical-aware text prompt-driven semi-supervised segmentation for fine-grained lumbar spine segmentation. PromptFix generates text describing the global semantics and anatomical structures through an Anatomy-aware Prompt Generator (AAPG), and uses a Hierarchical Cross-modal Fusion (HCF) module to fuse text semantics with visual features, enhancing the model's ability to distinguish structurally similar regions. At the same time, we designed a Dual-Sensitivity Weighting (DSW) mechanism to improve the class imbalance problem and proposed an Anatomy-Preserving Augmentation (APA) strategy to ensure anatomically consistent augmentation, boosting model robustness with limited labeled data. Extensive experiments on MRSpineSeg and SPIDER datasets demonstrate that in various label ratios, PromptFix outperforms promising competitors on both region overlapping and boundary accuracy, offering a robust solution for clinical spinal analysis.

records.title: Hierarchical Decoupling Learning for Optimization Conflict in Text-to-Image Person Re-Identification
records.abstract: Recent progress in text-to-image person re-identification (TIReID) has been primarily driven by instance-aligned vision-language pre-training models. Despite their success, existing fine-tuning strategies suffer from an overlooked dilemma: the instance-centric nature of these models inherently conflicts with the identity-dominated TIReID task, where a person representation is simultaneously optimized for instance alignment and identity discrimination. In this work, we propose Hierarchical Decoupling Learning (HDL), a framework that explicitly resolves this conflict by decoupling feature learning across a two-level hierarchy. Specifically, HDL disentangles the optimization of instance alignment from identity discrimination by assigning them to distinct hierarchical levels. Consequently, HDL effectively promotes representation discriminability while maintaining robust cross-modal correspondence. Extensive experiments on CUHK-PEDES, ICFG-PEDES, and RSTPReid demonstrate that HDL achieves state-of-the-art performance.

records.title: AP-FCIL: Anchored Prototype-Based Federated Class-Incremental Learning
records.abstract: Federated Class-Incremental Learning (FCIL) aims to train a global model on decentralized data from continuously arriving new classes. However, it faces the catastrophic forgetting challenge, exacerbated by data heterogeneity across clients. Our analysis traces this challenge to spatio-temporal degradation. Spatially, Non-IID client data gives rise to classifier bias and feature shifts; temporally, sequential task learning also triggers these issues. To address these challenges, we propose an Anchored Prototype-Based Federated Class-Incremental Learning method called AP-FCIL. By replacing learnable classifiers with fixed anchored prototypes based on a simplex equiangular tight frame (ETF) geometry, classifier bias is eliminated while consistent decision boundaries are maintained. To address feature shifts, we introduce a class-aware weighted alignment loss that enforces feature-prototype consistency while handling class imbalances. Additionally, we design a boundary-aware sampling strategy that maximizes buffer utility. Extensive experiments demonstrate that AP-FCIL outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in both knowledge retention and new class adaptation.

records.title: DiffReport: Radiology Report Generation via Local-to-Global Cross-modal Diffusion Model
records.abstract: Diffusion models have emerged as the state-of-the-art in generative modeling, yet their potential in radiology report generation remains under-explored. Adapting diffusion models to this domain poses two fundamental challenges: bridging the gap between the continuous diffusion process and the discrete nature of language tokens, and effectively conditioning the model on medical priors to capture accurate clinical findings. To address this, we propose DiffReport, the first diffusion model to leverage local-to-global cross-modal controls for radiology report generation. Our approach tackles the challenges with two key designs. First, we perform the diffusion and reverse processes within a continuous domain while bridging it to discrete text via embedding and rounding techniques. Second, we introduce a local-to-global cross-modal control mechanism that guides the model with image-derived features to generate higher-quality reports. Extensive experiments on IU-Xray and MIMIC-CXR demonstrate that DiffReport outperforms existing state-of-the-art models, achieving an average improvement of 17.4% and 11.9%, respectively.

records.title: Flora: Real-Time and Efficient Detection for Abnormal Chunk Requests in Video Streaming
records.abstract: Video content has become the dominant component of network traffic, with major platforms such as Netflix and YouTube relying on Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP (DASH). In these systems, videos are segmented into fixed-duration chunks at multiple bitrates, and clients request chunks based on network conditions. However, malicious clients may issue excessive requests or repeatedly request high-bitrate chunks, causing unfair bandwidth usage, network congestion, or service disruption, leading to significant revenue loss. Detecting such anomalous behavior in real time is challenging due to the massive scale of concurrent users. To address this challenge, we propose Flora, a novel approach based on an approximate data structure that efficiently detects suspicious senders under tight memory constraints. Flora achieves fast and accurate detection with low estimation error, supported by rigorous analysis. Extensive trace-driven evaluations show that Flora improves detection accuracy by 25.08% and processing speed by 22.01% compared to state-of-the-art methods.

records.title: SDSGN: A Novel Paradigm via Cooperative Path Fusion
records.abstract: Graph representation learning (GRL) aims to encode node attributes and topological structures into low dimensional embeddings. Although existing GRL models widely adopt message passing mechanisms to simultaneously capture node attributes and structural information, they typically employ a coupled modeling approach, attempting to compress global consistency and local flexibility into a single propagation process. This overlooks the representation bottleneck caused by cross-scale information coupling and traps the model in a dilemma of conflicting global and local optimization. To address this, we propose the Symmetric Dual-Stream Graph Network (SDSGN), which performs functional decoupling of global consistency and local flexibility. SDSGN utilizes a static stream with ordered gated convolutions to robustly capture global topology, alongside a reinforcement learning-driven dynamic stream for precise, node-level adaptive aggregation. Through efficient integration via parameter-free symmetric fusion, our model achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on 11 out of 12 benchmark datasets. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/haohuizhou99/SDSGN.

records.title: TATTOO: Training-free AesTheTic-aware Outfit recOmmendation
records.abstract: The global fashion e-commerce market relies significantly on intelligent and aesthetic-aware outfit-completion tools to promote sales. While previous studies have approached the problem of fashion outfit recommendation, most of them require expensive, task-specific training on large-scale labeled data, and no effort is made to guide outfit recommendation with explicit human aesthetics. In the era of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), we show that the conventional training-based pipeline could be streamlined to a training-free paradigm, with better recommendation scores and enhanced aesthetic awareness. We achieve this with TATTOO, a Training-free AesTheTic-aware Outfit recommendation approach. It first generates a target-item description using MLLMs, followed by an aesthetic chain‑of‑thought used to distill the images into a structured aesthetic profile. By fusing the visual summary of the outfit with the textual description and aesthetics vectors using a dynamic entropy‑gated mechanism, candidate items can be represented in a shared embedding space and be ranked in a human-accessible way. Experiments on a real‑world evaluation set Aesthetic-100 show that TATTOO achieves state-of-the-art performance compared with existing training-based methods. Another standard Polyvore dataset is also used to measure the advanced zero-shot retrieval capability of our training-free method.

records.title: DualGeo: A Dual-View Framework for Worldwide Image Geo-localization
records.abstract: Worldwide image geo-localization aims to infer the geographic location of an image captured anywhere on Earth, spanning street, city, regional, national, and continental scales. Existing methods rely on visual features that are sensitive to environmental variations (e.g., lighting, season, and weather) and lack effective post-processing to filter outlier candidates, limiting localization accuracy. To address these limitations, we propose DualGeo, a two-stage framework for worldwide image geo-localization. First, it establishes a geo-representational foundation by fusing image and semantic segmentation features via bidirectional cross-attention. The fused features are then aligned with GPS coordinates through dual-view contrastive learning to build a global retrieval database. Second, it performs geo-cognitive refinement by re-ranking retrieved candidates using geographic clustering. It then feeds them into large multimodal models (LMMs) for final coordinate prediction. Experiments on IM2GPS, IM2GPS3k, and YFCC4k show that DualGeo outperforms state-of-the-art methods, improving street-level (<1km) and city-level (<25km) localization accuracy by 3.6%-16.58% and 1.29%-8.77%, respectively. Our code and datasets are available : https://github.com/CJ310177/DualGeo.

records.title: ViThinker: Active Vision-Language Reasoning via Dynamic Perceptual Querying
records.abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning excels in language models but struggles in vision-language models due to premature visual-to-text conversion that discards continuous information such as geometry and spatial layout. While recent methods enhance CoT through static enumeration or attention-based selection, they remain passive, i.e., processing pre-computed inputs rather than actively seeking task-relevant details. Inspired by human active perception, we introduce ViThinker, a framework that enables vision-language models to autonomously generate decision (query) tokens triggering the synthesis of expert-aligned visual features on demand. ViThinker internalizes vision-expert capabilities during training, performing generative mental simulation during inference without external tool calls. Through a two-stage curriculum: first distilling frozen experts into model parameters, then learning task-driven querying via sparsity penalties, i.e., ViThinker discovers minimal sufficient perception for each reasoning step. Evaluations across vision-centric benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements, validating that active query generation outperforms passive approaches in both perceptual grounding and reasoning accuracy.

records.title: Generalized Confidence-driven State Space Modeling for Source-Free Domain Adaptation
records.abstract: Source-Free Domain Adaptation (SFDA) adapts a pre-trained model to an unlabeled target domain without source data. Conventional methods, primarily Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs), face limitations: CNNs have restricted receptive fields, while ViTs suffer from high computational complexity. The Mamba model, a structured state space model (SSM), offers a promising alternative with a global receptive field and linear complexity. To leverage this, we propose GCMamba, a novel framework that synergistically combines the strengths of CNNs, SSMs, and ViTs. Its Structural Feature Flow (SFF) design integrates efficient local feature extraction (CNNs), global context modeling with linear scalability (SSMs), and powerful representation learning (ViTs). We also introduce a Progressive Soft-Label Refinement strategy to reduce pseudo-label uncertainty and a confidence-driven mechanism to mitigate noisy samples. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks show that GCMamba achieves state-of-the-art performance while maintaining faster inference speeds. Our code and data will be available.

records.title: Hierarchical Semantic Correlation-Aware Masked Autoencoder for Unsupervised Audio–Visual Representation Learning
records.abstract: Learning aligned multimodal embeddings from weakly paired, label-free corpora is challenging: pipelines often provide only pre-extracted features, clips contain multiple events, and spurious co-occurrences. We propose HSC-MAE (Hierarchical Semantic Correlation-Aware Masked Autoencoder), a dual-path teacher–student framework that enforces semantic consistency across three complementary levels of representation — from coarse to fine: (i) global-level canonical-geometry correlation via DCCA, which aligns audio and visual embeddings within a shared modality-invariant subspace; (ii) local-level neighborhood-semantics correlation via teacher-mined soft top-k affinities, which preserves multi-positive relational structure among semantically similar instances; and (iii) sample-level conditional-sufficiency correlation via masked autoencoding, which ensures individual embeddings retain discriminative semantic content under partial observation. Concretely, a student MAE path is trained with masked feature reconstruction and affinity-weighted soft top-k InfoNCE; an EMA teacher operating on unmasked inputs via the CCA path supplies stable canonical geometry and soft positives. Learnable multi-task weights reconcile competing objectives, and an optional distillation loss transfers teacher geometry into the student. Experiments on AVE and VEGAS demonstrate substantial mAP improvements over strong unsupervised baselines, validating that HSC-MAE yields robust and well-structured audio–visual representations.

records.title: MultiSafeRAG: A Benchmark for Evaluating the Safety of Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
records.abstract: MM-RAG has become a practical way to ground multimodal LLMs in external evidence (e.g., document pages and images), but it also broadens the attack surface: toxic visual payloads can be retrieved directly or piggybacked within benign layouts and then propagated into harmful outputs. We introduce MultiSafeRAG, a benchmark for evaluating safety failures across the retriever, generator, and end-to-end MM-RAG pipeline on text-in-image inputs. MultiSafeRAG includes an ATOMIC cross-modal suite to probe modality-level toxicity alignment and VTDR, which injects toxic visual needles into realistic benign pages via layout-preserving, source-side dynamic sampling to test direct and piggyback retrieval. We further provide hierarchical metrics, showing that benign queries can retrieve harmful pages in poisoned corpora and that retrieved toxic evidence often leads to high attack success in generation and end-to-end settings.
