records.title: DYNA-PRUNER: Input-Adaptive Data–Model Co-Pruning for Efficient and Scalable Spatio-Temporal Media Prediction
records.abstract: Spatio-temporal prediction supports radar/satellite nowcasting and city-scale traffic monitoring, but modern models are often too expensive for real-time deployment. This stems from a mismatch between dense computation and strong input-dependent redundancy (e.g., calm seas or clear skies). To enable automated, resource-aware architecture optimization in scalable media analysis, we propose Dyna-Pruner, an end-to-end framework for input-dependent co-pruning of data and model structure. A shared-importance synchronization mechanism generates coupled masks that prune redundant regions and their corresponding computational units (e.g., convolutional filters), yielding per-sample sparse sub-networks at inference time. Experiments on WeatherBench, SEVIR, and TaxiBJ show seamless integration with CNN, RNN, and Transformer backbones, reducing FLOPs by up to 70% and achieving a 2.5× speedup on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin with negligible accuracy loss (<1%).

records.title: Is One-Shot In-Context Learning Helpful for Data Selection in Task-Specific Fine-Tuning of Multimodal LLMs?
records.abstract: Injecting world knowledge into pretrained multimodal large language models (MLLMs) is essential for domain-specific applications. Task-specific fine-tuning achieves this by tailoring MLLMs to high-quality in-domain data but encounters scalability challenges as datasets grow, necessitating a trade-off between performance and computational overhead. Existing data selection methods rely on additional scoring models or heuristic clustering, failing to concentrate on both data importance and diversity. Moreover, both methods overlook the interplay among training samples. To address these limitations, we propose CLIPPER, a training-free data selection pipeline that separates parameter and world knowledge, and leverages in-context learning to probe model responses to different demonstration-query combinations. CLIPPER identifies coresets that mirror the original dataset's perplexity distribution, preserving critical samples while maintaining diversity. Experiments on two MLLMs and three datasets show that CLIPPER matches full fine-tuning performance with significantly lower costs: Qwen2.5-VL-7B attains 47% data efficiency on VRSBench, and Llama-3.2-11B-Vision-Instruct reduces ScienceQA training time by 37%.

records.title: SemantiCL: Unlocking Semantic Knowledge Transfer for Multimodal Continual Learning
records.abstract: Multimodal continual learning (MCL) remains challenging because models often forget previous tasks and gradually lose their pretrained zero-shot ability. Existing approaches mainly adjust visual branch and depend on coarse text prompts, which restricts semantic transfer across tasks. We present SemantiCL, a parameter-efficient framework that enhances semantic knowledge transfer in MCL. SemantiCL first leverages large language models (LLMs) to generate fine-grained conceptual descriptions that expand the semantic space of the text encoder. This richer semantic space offers stronger cross-class semantic association, which enhances implicit knowledge transfer. SemantiCL then builds a conceptual prototype memory (CPM) that stores text-aligned concept embeddings for each task. These prototypes help identify semantically relevant tasks and enable more effective adapter routing, which enhances explicit semantic reuse. Extensive experiments on the MTIL benchmark demonstrate that SemantiCL improves knowledge transfer and retention over state-of-the-art methods. The results highlight the value of fine-grained semantic knowledge in multimodal continual learning.

records.title: SG-VIB: Semantic-Guided Variational Information Bottleneck for Efficient High-Resolution Document Understanding
records.abstract: High-resolution Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) utilizing cropping strategies face severe computational bottlenecks due to visual token explosion. Existing pruning methods often fail to preserve the critical spatial layout required for document understanding. To address this, we propose SG-VIB, a semantic-guided pruning framework grounded in the Variational Information Bottleneck (VIB) principle. We introduce a Residual VIB Gate to integrate semantic priors with task-aware corrections and a Dynamic Structure-Preserving Pruning strategy to maintain relative spatial order while adapting to varying information densities. Experiments demonstrate that SG-VIB significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods on benchmarks such as DocVQA, achieving a superior accuracy-efficiency trade-off with an average token reduction of 40%.

records.title: Pyramid Diffusion with Kolmogorov-Arnold Representation for Low-light Image Enhancement
records.abstract: Diffusion models have achieved remarkable progress in low-light image enhancement. Recent methods employ sequential denoising refinements to progressively reconstruct normal-light images, conditioned on low-light inputs and previous results with increasing resolutions. However, starting from a Gaussian distribution often leads to inaccurate reconstructions, which are further propagated by sequential up-sampling. Moreover, noise bursts in low-light images and artifacts introduced by down-sampling resemble Gaussian noise, limiting denoising effectiveness. To address these issues, we propose DiffKAR, which adopts a squeeze-and-expansion pyramid strategy and incorporates an artifact discriminator. Specifically, low resolutions are preserved in early refinements, followed by alternating down- and up-sampling operations to compress reconstruction deviations and enlarge the global receptive field. In addition, the artifact discriminator distinguishes Gaussian noise from down-sampling artifacts by extracting Kolmogorov–Arnold representations via high-order pixel differences. Extensive experiments on six benchmark datasets demonstrate superior performance and generalization over state-of-the-art methods.

records.title: MetricTransEdit: Real-World Distance-Controlled Object Translation with Diffusion Transformers
records.abstract: Geometric image editing aims to modify the spatial layout of scene content, yet most existing methods remain limited to pixel-space manipulation and thus lack real-world metric awareness. This limitation is particularly evident for object translation, a fundamental geometric editing operation that should be anchored to real-world distance scale rather than being performed solely as a 2D pixel-space displacement. In this paper, we propose MetricTransEdit, a two-stage editing framework built on Diffusion Transformer (DiT) that enables explicit real-world distance-controlled object translation from a single image. To provide reliable metric supervision, we introduce RealTrans-4K, a fine-grained real-world dataset with manually measured translation displacements. Moreover, we propose a physics-inspired regularization based on an area-depth consistency invariant to mitigate implausible scale changes under translation. Extensive experiments and a user study demonstrate that MetricTransEdit achieves superior metric translation accuracy while maintaining high perceptual quality compared with representative geometric and general editing baselines.

records.title: MDPF-Net: Multi-modal Object Detection via Modality Decoupling and Polarized Fusion
records.abstract: Multi-modal object detection aims to leverage the complementary features of RGB and Infrared (IR) images to enhance detection performance. However, existing feature extraction networks often overlook the inherent physical heterogeneity between modalities and struggle to effectively distinguish between feature commonalities and differences during the fusion phase. To address these issues, we propose a Modality Decoupling and Polarized Fusion Multi-modal Detection Network (MDPF-Net). Specifically, we construct a Modality-Specific Decoupling Backbone (MSDB). For the RGB modality, we utilize a Spatial-Spectral Synergistic Modulation Unit (S³M). For the IR modality, we employ a specialized Spectrum-Decoupled Structure Reshaping (SDSR) Module. Furthermore, we propose Polarized Linear Cross-Attention (PLCA). This mechanism utilizes positive and negative polarized pathways to process the consistency and complementarity between modalities during the feature fusion stage. Our method achieves 91.6\% and 96.3\% mAP on the M3FD and LLVIP datasets respectively, surpassing existing state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods.

records.title: A Unified Panoramic Pathology Segmentation Framework via Explicit Prior-Feature Decoupling
records.abstract: Panoramic pathology segmentation faces a critical scale mismatch, as fixed pixel resolutions conflict with biological structures ranging from millimeter-scale tissues to micrometer-scale nuclei. Traditional deep learning methods are often limited to single-scale processing, making them incapable of simultaneously delineating these heterogeneous targets with vast scale differences within a unified framework. Recent methods integrate task and scale clinical priors to achieve unified segmentation; however, their direct integration can introduce semantic ambiguity due to the inherent modality gap. To tackle this, we propose PFDNet, which incorporates a novel `Prior-Feature Decoupling' strategy to realize explicit prior-guided feature learning. By transforming static priors into active modulators and modeling the bidirectional interaction between priors and visual contexts, our framework effectively bridges the modality gap. Specifically, PFDNet incorporates a Hierarchical Guidance Adapter (HGA) for scale-aware dynamic recalibration and a Guidance Embedding Modeling (GEM) module for instance-specific prior refinement. Finally, an Adaptive Mask Decoding (AMD) module synthesizes these elements to achieve high-fidelity segmentation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PFDNet consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both accuracy and interpretability. The codes are available at https://github.com/aquiloo/PFDNet.

records.title: LIMQ-ViT: Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization for Vision Transformer via Layer Importance-Guided Bit-width Allocation
records.abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) offer remarkable performance but face deployment challenges due to extreme activation distributions in post-GELU and post-LayerNorm components. These distributions cause significant errors and high computational overhead during post-training quantization (PTQ). To address this, we propose component-specific strategies: shifted log-uniform quantization (SLG) for GELU and bias-smoothing quantization (BSL) for LayerNorm. Integrating these, we introduce LIMQ-ViT, a mixed-precision PTQ framework. LIMQ-ViT leverages extended layer-wise relevance propagation (LRP-ϵ) to evaluate layer importance and employs integer linear programming (ILP) to dynamically allocate optimal bit-widths. This balances high accuracy with reduced model size. Extensive experiments on ViT, DeiT, and Swin validate LIMQ-ViT’s effectiveness. The results show that LIMQ-ViT significantly outperforms existing quantization methods under 4-bit and 6-bit quantization. In particular, for image classification on ImageNet-1K, LIMQ-ViT achieves up to 3.21% improvement in Top-1 accuracy for ViT-B under 4-bit quantization compared to state-of-the-art approaches.

records.title: Action Transition with Optimal Transport for Egocentric Procedural Error Detection
records.abstract: Procedural error detection in egocentric videos is essential for intelligent assistants that provide assistance during task performance. Despite recent progress, existing methods mainly rely on matching with prototypes or statistically constructed task graphs, which inadequately model dependencies between actions and lack a reliable similarity metric for action verification. To address these limitations, we propose Action Transition with Optimal Transport (ATOT), a probabilistic framework for egocentric procedural error detection. Specifically, ATOT consists of two key components: (1) The Optimal Transport Correlation Graph, which leverages Optimal Transport to organize Wasserstein distance among normal actions into a probabilistic transition model, enabling effective filtering of plausible next actions. (2) The Spatial Action Consistency Verification module, which adopts Wasserstein distance as a principled similarity metric to compare the current action distribution with candidate Gaussian mixture models for fine-grained error assessment. Our proposed ATOT method consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods across all benchmark datasets.

records.title: Efficient Interactive Gland Instance Segmentation via Mamba-Based Dynamic Guidance
records.abstract: Complex gland morphology and their densely packed spatial distribution hinder accurate segmentation and instance discrimination. Interactive segmentation uses user guidance for precise gland delineation, yet existing methods cannot jointly model multiple instances and remain computationally expensive due to repeated full-network inference. Leveraging the linear computational complexity of the Mamba architecture and its decision-guided state weight matrix, we propose DG-Mamba, an efficient dynamically guided model tailored for interactive gland instance segmentation. We encode user click sequences into spatio-temporal guidance tensors that dynamically regulate internal states and focus attention on foreground regions. All gland instances are jointly modeled within a shared latent space, enabling accurate multi-instance segmentation without recomputing global features and significantly reducing computational cost. To better model cross-scale relationships and fine-grained boundaries in dense glandular imagery, we introduce a hierarchically structured encoder with modular division. A round-robin grouping strategy enhances multi-scale semantic fusion, while a mask-guided mechanism progressively refines target localization, improving instance separability and boundary precision. We conduct comprehensive comparisons against state-of-the-art segmentation approaches on the publicly available GlaS and CRAG datasets, achieving clear advantages in both segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.

records.title: PoseCompass: Intelligent Synthetic Pose Selection for Visual Localization
records.abstract: In visual localization, Absolute Pose Regression (APR) enables real-time 6-DoF camera pose inference from single images, yet critically depends on fine-tuning data quality and coverage. While recent methods leverage 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) for novel view synthesis–based data augmentation, random sampling generates redundant views and noisy samples from poorly reconstructed regions. To mitigate the research gap, we propose PoseCompass, an intelligent pose selection pipeline for 3DGS‑based APR. PoseCompass starts from formulating synthetic pose selection and deriving a value‑based pose ranking mechanism to identify informative poses. The ranking integrates three dimensions: (1) Localization Difficulty, favoring challenging regions; (2) Coverage Novelty, exploring under‑sampled areas; and (3) Rendering Observability, filtering artifacts and noise. Then, PoseCompass generates trajectory‑constrained candidates, selects the top‑K ranked poses, and synthesizes views using 3DGS with lightweight diffusion‑based alignment. Finally, the pose regressor is fine‑tuned on mixed real and synthetic data.We evaluate our PoseCompass on 7-Scenes, PoseCompass reduces adaptation time from 15.2 to 5.1 minutes (3 times speedup) while cutting median pose errors by 53.8%, significantly outperforming random baselines.

records.title: EviRCOD: Evidence-Guided Probabilistic Decoding for Referring Camouflaged Object Detection
records.abstract: Referring Camouflaged Object Detection (Ref-COD) focuses on segmenting specific camouflaged targets in a query image using category-aligned references. Despite recent advances, existing methods struggle with reference-target semantic alignment, explicit uncertainty modeling, and robust boundary preservation. To address these issues, we propose EviRCOD, an integrated framework consisting of three core components: (1) a Reference-Guided Deformable Encoder (RGDE) that employs hierarchical reference-driven modulation and multi-scale deformable aggregation to inject semantic priors and align cross-scale representations; (2) an Uncertainty-Aware Evidential Decoder (UAED) that incorporates Dirichlet evidence estimation into hierarchical decoding to model uncertainty and propagate confidence across scales; and (3) a Boundary-Aware Refinement Module (BARM) that selectively enhances ambiguous boundaries by exploiting low-level edge cues and prediction confidence. Experiments on the Ref-COD benchmark demonstrate that EviRCOD achieves state-of-the-art detection performance while providing well-calibrated uncertainty estimates. records.title: ASTA: Adaptive Semantic Anchoring and Topology-Guided Affinity for CLIP-based Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation
records.abstract: Weakly supervised semantic segmentation (WSSS) with image-level labels remains challenging due to incomplete class activation maps (CAMs) and the lack of structural constraints. To address these issues, we propose ASTA, a unified CLIP-based framework that enhances both semantic alignment and structural consistency. ASTA introduces Adaptive Semantic Anchoring (ASA), which dynamically updates category anchors via exponential moving average to align patch features with evolving semantics. In addition, Topology-Guided Affinity (TGA) combines semantic clustering with spatial connectivity to refine inter-patch relations and preserve coherent object structures. Extensive experiments on PASCAL VOC 2012 and MS COCO 2014 demonstrate that ASTA achieves state-of-the-art performance under image-level supervision.

records.title: Cross-View Consistency Learning for Semi-Supervised Camouflaged Object Detection
records.abstract: Semi-Supervised Camouflaged Object Detection (SSCOD) is hindered by noisy pseudo-labels at both pixel and image levels. To address this issue, we propose Cross-View Consistency Learning (CVCL), which constructs two complementary views: model-generated pseudo-labels (M-PL) and Segment Anything Model (SAM) prompt-guided pseudo-labels (P-PL). CVCL exploits cross-view consistency to estimate pseudo-label reliability at both pixel and image levels, with pixel-wise and image-wise reweighting to down-weight inconsistent pixels and unreliable images. To alleviate the quality degradation of P-PL in challenging scenes, a lightweight Pseudo-label Density Adapter (PDAdapter) estimates a scale-normalized foreground-density prior to modulate the contribution of low-quality P-PL during training. Extensive experiments on COD benchmarks show that with only 10% pixel-labeled data, our method surpasses prior semi-/weakly-supervised approaches and remains competitive with fully supervised methods.

records.title: Hyperbolic Uncertainty–Aware Multi-Prototype Alignment Network for Semi-Supervised Few-Shot Medical Image Segmentation
records.abstract: Existing few-shot segmentation methods have made progress in medical imaging, but limited support sets often fail to adequately represent class distributions, weakening segmentation robustness. Although some studies incorporate unlabeled samples, they typically ignore substantial intra-class variability, which can mislead network learning and degrade performance. To address this issue, we propose a Hyperbolic Uncertainty-Aware Multi-Prototype Alignment Network (HUMPAN), which leverages unlabeled samples more effectively by aligning features and suppressing unreliable predictions. HUMPAN first employs a Position-prior Sparse Attention module to align query/unlabeled features with support foregrounds by exploiting intrinsic positional priors of medical images. To stabilize training and enhance prototype reliability, the Hyperbolic Uncertainty-Aware strategy estimates prediction uncertainty on query/unlabeled samples to suppress low-confidence predictions. Finally, a Multi-Prototype Adaptive Fusion module integrates support and unlabeled prototypes to capture diverse class representations and obtain the final segmentation. Extensive experiments on three public datasets demonstrate its superior performance compared to other methods.

records.title: Patches to Pixels: Collaborative Mining and Implicit Decoding for Unsupervised Camouflaged Object Detection
records.abstract: Unsupervised camouflaged object detection (UCOD) remains challenging due to the high visual similarity between targets and backgrounds without human annotations. Existing methods often suffer from inaccurate localization and incomplete structures, caused by insufficient semantic mining and discrete patch-level decoding. In this paper, we propose a novel UCOD framework with patch-to-pixel learning via global-local collaboration, called UCOD-P2P, which comprises a global-local collaborative mining (GCM) and continuous implicit segmentation (CIS). Specifically, the GCM fully mines camouflage-related knowledge in self-supervised representation through the collaboration of global contextual localization and local consistency refinement. Additionally, a multi-view consensus filtering (MCF) scheme is incorporated to remove extremely hard samples from learning, preventing distractions and improving robustness. The CIS models segmentation as an implicit representation to map discrete patch-level features into the pixel-level spatial domain, significantly mitigating the detail-recovery limitations of discrete representations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance.

records.title: SAM-based Self-Refining Framework for Weakly-Supervised Camouflaged Object Detection
records.abstract: Direct application of the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to Weakly-Supervised Camouflaged Object Detection (WSCOD) faces challenges due to domain shifts and sparse annotations. To address these challenges, we propose SR-SAM, a SAM-based progressive self-refining framework. Specifically, the adaptive camouflage prompter (ACP) module injects learnable camouflage semantics into the frozen SAM embeddings to generate dense structural prompts. Subsequently, the dual-path self-refiner (DSR) module leverages these prompts to produce reliable pseudo-labels, which in turn supervise the ACP in an online self-refining loop. This interaction effectively bridges the domain gap and compensates for the lack of dense annotations. Furthermore, we adopt a two-stage training strategy where a lightweight inference network is retrained using these refined pseudo-labels, avoiding the computational overhead of SAM during inference. Experiments on four widely used benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance. The code is available at https://github.com/hxl-2000/SR-SAM.

records.title: Feature Vulnerability-Aware Adversarial Training
records.abstract: Adversarial Training (AT) typically treats all samples uniformly with fixed loss weights and a global perturbation budget, overlooking intrinsic differences in how samples respond to attacks. In this work, we reveal that different samples exhibit significantly distinct \textit{feature vulnerability patterns} under adversarial perturbations. Building on this insight, we propose \textbf{Feature Vulnerability-Aware Adversarial Training} (FVA-AT), which employs a lightweight, independently optimized feature projector to map final-layer features into a low-dimensional embedding space. Sample vulnerability is quantified via (i) the KL divergence between clean and adversarial embeddings and (ii) a feature-space margin. These metrics guide the dynamic adjustment of per-sample loss weights and perturbation budgets during training. Experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and SVHN demonstrate that FVA-AT consistently yields robustness gains—e.g., +4.57\% improvement in robust accuracy over PGD-AT on CIFAR-10 with ResNet-18—while effectively mitigating robust overfitting. Moreover, FVA is plug-and-play and seamlessly integrates with existing AT frameworks (e.g., TRADES, MART) to form stronger hybrid defenses.

records.title: SDMANet: A Spike-Driven Multi-Axis Self-Attention Network for Event-Based Object Detection
records.abstract: Event cameras offer high temporal resolution and low latency through asynchronous, sparse data capture, making them ideal for dynamic vision tasks. However, their unique data format poses challenges for conventional object detection frameworks. Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs), with their event-driven processing paradigm, are naturally compatible with such data but still lag behind Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) in detection accuracy. To bridge this gap, we propose SDMANet, a novel spike-driven Transformer architecture that introduces a Spike-Driven Multi-Axis Self-Attention (SDMA) mechanism for efficient spatial feature extraction. SDMANet further incorporates spike-driven MLP modules and LSTM blocks to capture rich spatio-temporal dependencies while maintaining low energy consumption. Extensive experiments on two benchmark event camera datasets--GEN1 and 1Mpx--demonstrate that SDMANet achieves state-of-the-art performance among all evaluated SNN-based models. The lightweight SDMANet-T variant also delivers competitive accuracy with substantially fewer parameters, making it ideal for resource-constrained applications.

records.title: SIDN: A Subject Information Disentanglement Network for Calibration-Free Cross-Subject Motor Imagery BCI
records.abstract: Motor imagery-based brain-computer interfaces (MI-BCIs) are promising for rehabilitation and human-computer interaction, yet their deployment remains limited by significant inter-subject variability and time-consuming calibration demands. To address these challenges, we propose a Subject Information Disentanglement Network (SIDN) for fully calibration-free cross-subject MI-BCI decoding. Under the subject-independent setting without any calibration data from the target subject, SIDN disentangles EEG representations into subject-invariant and subject-specific components via covariance minimization, while an adversarial learning strategy with a gradient reversal layer enhances model generalization by implicitly reducing individual differences. Evaluations on BCI Competition IV Datasets 2a, 2b, and OpenBMI demonstrate that SIDN achieves state-of-the-art performance, obtaining average accuracies of 81.35±10.36%, 82.87±10.16%, and 76.50±14.06%, respectively. Notably, unlike conventional cross-subject approaches that suppress subject-specific cues, our results show that appropriately leveraging subject-specific information could improve MI-BCI decoding.

records.title: Siamese-ES: A Multi-Task Learning Framework Leveraging Sleep Features for Interictal Epileptiform Discharge Detection
records.abstract: Interictal epileptiform discharge (IED) detection is crucial for epilepsy diagnosis, but faces two challenges: (1) sleep-related physiological waveforms often resemble IEDs, leading to frequent misclassifications; and (2) conventional single-task models struggle to effectively incorporate sleep information to improve discriminative capability. We propose Siamese-ES, a multi-task framework that jointly models epileptiform and sleep features. Specifically, it employs a shared Frequency-Temporal Converter followed by a trainable Hard Parameter Sharing Encoder to extract unified representations from EEG, EMG, and ECG spectrograms, which are then processed by two specialized branches (Twins-Electron and Twins-Sleep). This design enables the model to disentangle true IED events from sleep-induced artifacts, thereby improving detection accuracy. To support this effort, we introduce EpiSet-265K, a large-scale dataset with 265,551 labeled samples, addressing data scarcity. Extensive experiments show state-of-the-art performance: 71.18% precision at 82.11% sensitivity. Code and data will be publicly released to facilitate future research.

records.title: APLC: Auto-Clustering and Pseudo-Labeling with CLIP for Open-Set Source-Free Domain Adaptation
records.abstract: Open-set source-free domain adaptation (OS-SFDA) requires discovering unknown target classes without access to source data, yet existing parametric and non-parametric clustering methods remain sensitive to class number estimation, lack neighborhood consistency, and struggle with ambiguous unknown labels. To address these limitations, we propose Auto-Clustering and Pseudo-Labeling with CLIP (APLC), a unified framework that automatically infers the target class number and assigns semantic labels to unknown classes. Specifically, we first introduce a novel Neighborhood Driven Soft Clustering with Metropolis–Hastings (NDSC-MH) that enables adaptive split/merge clustering to achieve compact and separable target clusters. To auto-label discovered categories, we integrate VLM-based semantic pseudo labels generation with alignment and refinement modules. Finally, a CLIP guided consistency alignment loss provides robust cross domain adaptation under zero-shot supervision. Extensive experiments on OS-SFDA benchmarks show that APLC achieves SOTA performance and precise target-private classes discovery.

records.title: MCAP: Modality Characteristics-Aware Pruning for Multimodal Models
records.abstract: Multimodal deep learning has attracted increasing attention; however, the rapid growth in model sizes hinders its application in resource-constrained devices. Although pruning has been extensively studied to reduce the model size of unimodal models, prior studies have failed to explore the diverse characteristics of different modalities, resulting in undesired pruning performance. To address this gap, we propose MCAP, a modality characteristics-aware pruning for multimodal models. MCAP exploits the multimodal characteristics (MMC) to perform automated pruning in coarse- and fine-grained stages. First, we propose a modality-aware coarse-grained pruning method. It allows for elastic expansion and compression of each feature extractor, deriving a compact structure that adapts well across modalities. Second, we propose an evolutionary algorithm (EA)-based fine-grained pruning method. This formulates the pruning as an EA search guided by the MMC, thereby eliminating redundancies in multimodal models. Extensive experiments across various tasks, datasets, and models validate the effectiveness and versatility of the proposed MCAP framework.

records.title: Spatial Graph Distillation Transfer for Depression Detection with Few-Channel EEG signals
records.abstract: Electroencephalogram (EEG)-based depression de-tection typically requires full-channel devices, which are costly and impractical. Few-channel wearable EEG systems improve practicality but suffer from significant spatial information and temporal loss, reducing detection accuracy. To address this prob-lem, we propose a Spatial Graph Distillation Transfer (SGDT) network for cross-dataset depression detection: a full-to-few channel EEG transfer learning framework that transfers spatial knowledge from a full-channel model to two few-channel models. SGDT introduces the Spatial Graph Adapter (SGA)—consisting of SGA-FuC for full-channel EEG and SGA-FeC for few-channel EEG—to extract Aligned Spatial Embeddings (ASE). Then, we design a two-stage knowledge distillation strategy using the Teacher–Assistant–Student learning. In Stage 1, a full-channel (Teacher) model and a few-channel (Assistant) model are jointly trained, enabling the Assistant model to learn spatial priors aligned with full-channel ASE representations from the Teacher model. In Stage 2, the pre-trained Assistant model guides the target few-channel (Student) model by reducing the ASE distance between the pre-trained Assistant and Student models. Extensive cross-dataset experiments demonstrate that SGDT consistently improves few-channel EEG depression detection performance and significantly reduces the ASE discrepancy between the Assistant and Student models. The proposed SGDT network offers a principled solution for accurate depression detection on low-cost, few-channel EEG devices.

records.title: RAWIC: Bit-Depth Adaptive Lossless Raw Image Compression
records.abstract: Raw images preserve linear sensor measurements and high bit-depth information crucial for advanced vision tasks and photography applications, yet their storage remains challenging due to large file sizes, varying bit depths, and sensor-dependent characteristics. Existing learned lossless compression methods mainly target 8-bit sRGB images, while raw reconstruction approaches are inherently lossy and rely on camera-specific assumptions. To address these challenges, we introduce RAWIC, a bit-depth-adaptive learned lossless compression framework for Bayer-pattern raw images. We first convert single-channel Bayer data into a four-channel RGGB format and partition it into patches. For each patch, we compute its bit depth and use it as auxiliary input to guide compression. A bit-depth-adaptive entropy model is then designed to estimate patch distributions conditioned on their bit depths. This architecture enables a single model to handle raw images from diverse cameras and bit depths. Experiments show that RAWIC consistently surpasses traditional lossless codecs, achieving an average 7.7\% bitrate reduction over JPEG-XL. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/chunbaobao/RAWIC}.

records.title: ShapePruning: Shape-Aware ESD-Based Pruning via the Marchenko--Pastur Law
records.abstract: Pruning is an effective way to reduce the computational and memory cost of large language models, yet existing methods either impose uniform sparsity or rely on heuristic layer-wise ratios. Recent Heavy-Tailed Self-Regularization (HT-SR) approaches use empirical spectral densities (ESD) to estimate layer importance, but implicitly assume that all weight matrices provide equally reliable spectral signals. We show that this assumption fails in modern Transformers: due to the Marchenko--Pastur (MP) shape constraint, highly rectangular matrices exhibit compressed spectra with poorly separated bulk and tail, yielding unstable tail statistics, whereas near-square attention projections retain clear heavy-tailed structure. Motivated by this, we propose ShapePruning, a shape-aware refinement of HT-SR that restricts spectral analysis to square attention submatrices and derives stable layer-wise importance scores. Across the LLaMA, Vicuna, and Mistral families, ShapePruning consistently outperforms uniform schedules and prior HT-SR strategies when combined with Magnitude, Wanda, and SparseGPT.

records.title: FRFDet: Efficient UAV Small Object Detection with Symmetric Sampling and Scalable Fusion
records.abstract: Small object detection in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) imagery remains challenging under adverse conditions, including complex weather, low illumination, and sensor noise. These challenges mainly stem from severe background clutter, fine-grained detail degradation, and suboptimal semantic–spatial feature fusion, which jointly hinder robust small-object representation. To this end, we propose FRFDet, a lightweight yet effective single-stage detector tailored for UAV-based small object detection. FRFDet proposes two plug-and-play modules: Inverse Bidirectional Sampling (IBS) and Scale-Feature Relationship Cross-Fusion (SFRCF). IBS preserves critical spatial details via channel expansion–compression and bidirectional pattern reconstruction, improving feature alignment. SFRCF explicitly models scale-dependent fusion behaviors, revealing that inter-group element-wise multiplication favors compact models, while inter-group additive fusion benefits larger architectures. Extensive experiments on VisDrone, UAVDT, HazyDet, and MS COCO demonstrate that FRFDet achieves state-of-the-art performance among lightweight detectors with low computational cost, compact parameters, and fast inference, making it well suited for resource-constrained UAV platforms.

records.title: Diff-KD: Diffusion-based Knowledge Distillation for Collaborative Perception under Corruptions
records.abstract: Multi-agent collaborative perception enables autonomous systems to overcome individual sensing limits through collective intelligence. However, real-world sensor and communication corruptions severely undermine this advantage. Crucially, existing approaches treat corruptions as static perturbations and passively conform to corrupted inputs, failing to actively recover the underlying clean semantics. To address this limitation, we introduce Diff-KD, a framework that integrates diffusion-based generative refinement into teacher-student knowledge distillation for robust collaborative perception. Diff-KD features two core components: (i) Progressive Knowledge Distillation (PKD), which treats local feature restoration as a conditional diffusion process to recover global semantics from corrupted observations; and (ii) Adaptive Gated Fusion (AGF), which dynamically weights neighbors based on ego reliability during fusion. Evaluated on OPV2V and DAIR-V2X under seven corruption types, Diff-KD achieves state-of-the-art performance in both detection accuracy and calibration robustness.

records.title: SynerDiff: Synergetic Continuous Batching for Fast and Parallel Diffusion Model Inference
records.abstract: The expansion of Artificial Intelligence-generated content service requires diffusion model serving to simultaneously achieve high throughput and low task end-to-end (E2E) latency. However, existing continuous batching methods suffer from severe resource contention during UNet-VAE concurrency, leading to latency spikes. Furthermore, concurrent multi-task scheduling entails a trade-off between UNet throughput and VAE latency across varying scheduling strategies. To address these, we propose SynerDiff, an efficient continuous batching system built on intra-inter level synergy. At the intra-concurrency level, SynerDiff alleviates resource contention by pruning component-specific resource bottlenecks via VAE Chunking and Adaptive Skip-CFG. At the inter-concurrency level, leveraging components' differential sensitivity to scheduling granularities, a threshold-aware scheduler plans concurrent sequences and tunes intra-concurrency decisions to minimize VAE latency while maintaining UNet within high-throughput threshold. Additionally, a feedback controller dynamically adjusts this threshold based on queue loads to boost system capacity ceiling. Experimental results show that, SynerDiff improves throughput by 1.6x and decreases both average E2E and P99 tail latencies by up to 78.7%, compared to benchmarks while guaranteeing high image fidelity.

records.title: LAD: Label-Aware Anchor Distillation for CLIP-based Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation
records.abstract: Weakly supervised semantic segmentation (WSSS) has recently benefited from CLIP priors, yet directly decoding CLIP patch embeddings often suffers from class entanglement, causing ambiguous cues and confusion. We propose LAD (Label-Aware Anchor Distillation), a label-conditioned framework that explicitly couples image-level tags with frozen CLIP features. LAD treats multi-label tags as category queries and performs label-aware anchor search via lightweight channel modulation, reorganizing dispersed patch representations into a compact, well-separated anchor space. An anchor branch generates anchor pseudo masks, and an image-only student is trained with anchor-based supervision and feature distillation that aligns student features with anchor embeddings in this space. During inference, the anchor branch is removed, preserving standard image-only segmentation while inheriting improved class discrimination. Experiments on PASCAL VOC 2012 and MS COCO 2014 show consistent gains on CAM seeds, pseudo masks, and final mIoU, achieving state-of-the-art results among CLIP-based methods.

records.title: Efficient Long Video Understanding by Incentivizing Models to Use Tools
records.abstract: Long-video understanding is fundamentally challenged by the low signal-to-noise ratio. To address this, we introduce the ``Think with Videos" paradigm, extending the successful ``Think with Images" concept to the temporal domain. We present the Spatio-Temporal Magnifier (STM), a model that embodies this paradigm. During reasoning, STM actively explores video content by dynamically invoking intrinsic ``temporal zoom-in" and ``spatial zoom-in" tools, allowing it to efficiently locate and process critical information missed during initial sparse sampling. Training a model to use such tools effectively via reinforcement learning presents a significant challenge, often leading to training collapse where the model abandons tool usage. To overcome this, we propose a novel algorithm, Difficulty-aware Exploration Incentive Policy Optimization (DEIPO). DEIPO adaptively encourages tool exploration based on task difficulty, fostering effective tool use while improving the model's difficulty awareness. We conduct comprehensive evaluations on four long-video understanding benchmarks (LongVideoBench, MLVU, LVBench, and Video-MME). Our results show that STM significantly outperforms baseline models while consuming approximately half the tokens. This work validates the ``Think with Videos" paradigm as a highly effective and efficient approach for long-video understanding and demonstrates that DEIPO is crucial for successfully instilling this capability.

records.title: Efficient VLSI Design of Rough Mode Decision for VVC Intra Prediction
records.abstract: The Versatile Video Coding (VVC) standard enhances compression efficiency via more flexible block partitioning and prediction modes, but substantially raising the complexity and posing a major challenge for Very Large Scale Integration Circuit(VLSI). In this work, we propose a hardware-oriented Rough Mode Decision (RMD) solution featuring: (1) reuse of 4x4 unit costs across parent blocks sharing the same reference position; (2) a consolidated single-step RMD merging look-up-table-based cost estimation with a multi-round mode decision; (3) an overall two-stage pipeline, where the cost estimation stage employs a six-level sub-pipeline with Ping-Pong buffering, and mode decision stage reuses cost comparison module by a cascaded multiplexer tree. Experimental results demonstrate that our implementation in TSMC 40nm technology, outperforms existing VVC solutions, operating at 300 MHz and supporting 4K@38fps Ultra High-Definition (UHD) video encoding, with only a 0.473\% Bjontegaard Delta Bitrate (BDBR) increase and an area utilization of 2699.7K gates.

records.title: Towards Automatic Soccer Commentary Generation with Knowledge-Enhanced Visual Reasoning
records.abstract: Soccer commentary plays a crucial role in enhancing the soccer game viewing experience for audiences. Previous studies in automatic soccer commentary generation typically adopt an end-to-end method to generate anonymous live text commentary. Such generated commentary is insufficient in the context of real-world live televised commentary, as it contains anonymous entities, context-dependent errors and lacks statistical insights of the game events. To bridge the gap, we propose GameSight, a two-stage model to address soccer commentary generation as a knowledge-enhanced visual reasoning task, enabling live-televised-like knowledgeable commentary with accurate reference to entities (players and teams). GameSight starts by performing visual reasoning to align anonymous entities with fine-grained visual and contextual analysis. Subsequently, the entity-aligned commentary is refined with knowledge by incorporating external historical statistics and iteratively updated internal game state information. Consequently, GameSight improves the player alignment accuracy by 18.5% on SN-Caption-test-align dataset compared to Gemini 2.5-pro. Combined with further knowledge enhancement, GameSight outperforms in segment-level accuracy and commentary quality, as well as game-level contextual relevance and structural composition. We believe that our work paves the way for a more informative and engaging human-centric experience with the AI sports application. Demo Page: https://gamesight2025.github.io/gamesight2025

records.title: Tri-Prompted Visual-Text Alignment with Ordinal-Aware Regression for Blind Image Quality Assessment
records.abstract: Blind image quality assessment depends jointly on content, distortion, and perception, yet existing CLIP-based methods often use entangled prompts that limit sensitivity. We propose TP-IQA, which disentangles visual features via three independent, learnable prompt branches: Scene, Distortion and Quality Rank. Crucially, while text priors guide representation learning, we employ a query-conditioned mechanism to autonomously generate instance-adaptive prompts for precise alignment. This design ensures that text features actively participate in inference without requiring ground truth labels for degradation, scene, or rank. Furthermore, to encode rank information and mimic coarse-to-fine human perception, we adopt an ordinalaware prediction strategy that classifies discrete quality ranks before performing regression. Extensive experiments confirm that TP-IQA yields state-of-the-art results and robust generalization, demonstrating the benefits of disentangled semantic modeling and progressive quality prediction. Code is available at https://github.com/Why0322/ICME-TP-IQA.

records.title: A Proposal-Free Query-Guided Network for Grounded Multimodal Named Entity Recognition
records.abstract: Grounded Multimodal Named Entity Recognition (GMNER) identifies named entities—including their spans and types—in natural language text and grounds them to the corresponding regions in associated images. Most existing approaches split this task into two steps: they first detect objects using a pre-trained general-purpose detector and then match named entities to the detected objects. These methods face one major limitation. The pre-trained general-purpose object detectors operate independently of textual entities, thus tend to detect common objects and frequently overlook specific, fine-grained regions demanded by named entities. This object detector-entity misalignment introduces imprecision and can impair overall system performance. In this paper, we propose a proposal-free Query-Guided Network (QGN) to unify multimodal reasoning and decoding by incorporating text guidance and cross-modal interaction. QGN enables accurate grounding and robust performance in open-domain scenarios. Extensive experiments demonstrate that QGN achieves top performance among compared GMNER models on widely used benchmarks. Our source code is available at https://github.com/Jennyliu1114/QGN_code.

records.title: Image-Conditioned Instance Prompt Network for Referring Remote Sensing Image Segmentation
records.abstract: Referring Remote Sensing Image Segmentation (RRSIS) is a situated, task-driven cross-modal task related to the embodied perception paradigm, requiring models to align visual-spatial features with linguistic intentions for precise target perception. Recent research has focused on refining the granularity of textual features and optimizing image-text feature fusion to better guide target feature representations. However, insufficient descriptive granularity and sensitivity to semantic shifts can cause bottlenecks in cross-modal feature fusion. To address these issues, we propose the Image-Conditioned Instance Prompt Network (ICIPNet) with Bilateral Information Fusion, which is designed to alleviate bottlenecks in cross-modal feature fusion. ICIPNet introduces an Image-Conditioned Instance Prompt (ICIP) module to generate self-adaptive visual and semantic representations without external knowledge. The Bilateral Information Fusion (BIF) module enhances feature fusion along the token and channel dimensions. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed ICIPNet outperforms existing RRSIS models.

records.title: EDCDS: Energy-Guided Dynamic Collaboration and Competition in Dual-Student Learning for Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
records.abstract: Semi-supervised medical image segmentation (SSMIS) effectively alleviates the issue of scarce labeled medical data. However, the heterogeneity of student models and fixed optimization strategies may limit the widespread applicability of teacher-student-based SSMIS methods. To address this challenge, we propose the Energy-Guided Dynamic Collaboration and Competition in Dual-Student Learning (EDCDS) framework based on the Mean Teacher (MT) architecture. EDCDS includes a teacher and two trainable students. By introducing an energy mechanism, the prediction capability of the student models is quantified, and the collaboration and competition strategies between students are dynamically adjusted based on the energy differences. The core of EDCDS is to dynamically optimize the learning process of student models, enhancing segmentation accuracy and generalization ability through energy measurement and interaction between student models. We conducted experiments on three publicly available medical image datasets, and the results demonstrate that the EDCDS method outperforms the current state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods by 0.92%, 0.46%, and 0.56% in Dice scores on the Pancreas-CT, LA, and Brats-2019 datasets, respectively. Additionally, on the Pancreas-CT dataset, EDCDS even surpasses fully supervised methods, further proving its effectiveness and superiority.

records.title: Can Talkers Drive Non-Human Characters: A Novel Talking Head Quality Assessment Benchmark
records.abstract: With the rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence, speech-driven Talking Head (TH) methods, which commonly known as ``Talker'', have become important in film production, game design, and digital content creation. Modern entertainment increasingly relies on Non-Human characters to support audience engagement. Thus high-quality talking head generation for these characters is essential for reducing manual animation costs, ensuring expressive consistency, and enabling scalable automated workflows. Yet, existing Talkers and evaluation standards are largely built around human facial structures. This bias leaves studios without reliable tools to evaluate or improve speech-driven Non-Human, creating production bottlenecks. To address this gap, we conduct a detailed investigation into the performance of existing Talkers on Non-Human characters, through which we construct the Non-Human Talking Head Quality Assessment (THQA-NH) database. To ensure that the constructed THQA-NH dataset exhibits sufficient diversity and generality, we consider 6 categories of Non-Human character types, and select 55 different types of speech clips that cover a wide range of phonetic and lip-shape characteristics as the source material. Using 10 representative Talkers, we produce 1,260 Non-Human Talking Head (NHTHs) videos spanning multiple styles, speech attributes, and character categories. Through the subjective experiments, we reveal the limitations of current Talkers for Non-Human characters and also expose the distortions of existing NHTHs. In addition, the benchmark experimental results show that existing quality assessment methods struggle to capture the diverse distortions occurring during NHTHs, which highlights the need for more targeted quality assessment approaches.

records.title: MIAR: Medical Image Super-Resolution With Autoregressive Modeling
records.abstract: Medical Image Super-Resolution (MISR) aims to enhance spatial resolution and anatomical visibility without necessitating hardware modifications. Although deep learning has yielded promising results, existing paradigms face a critical trade-off: diffusion-based methods suffer from prohibitive inference latency, while regression-based models often produce suboptimal perceptual quality. In this work, we propose MIAR, a multi-scale autoregressive framework that reformulates super-resolution as a conditional, progressive next-scale prediction task. To ensure structural fidelity and semantic consistency, we augment the visual autoregressive backbone with a Scale-Adaptive Structural Decoder. Furthermore, we integrate multi-scale beam search during inference to facilitate more stable and high-fidelity generation trajectories. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MIAR establishes new state-of-the-art benchmarks while maintaining high competitiveness across full-reference metrics. Notably, our framework achieves a 7.86% improvement in the perceptual metric MUSIQ relative to the state-of-the-art, while simultaneously delivering a 2.02x speedup over diffusion-based methods.

records.title: Behavior-Guided EEG Multimodal Learning for Enhanced Addiction Diagnosis
records.abstract: Substance Use Disorders (SUDs) are highly heterogeneous and impose a substantial burden on individuals and society. However, current diagnostic pipelines still rely heavily on subjective clinical self-reports and coarse EEG indices, offering limited insight into how neural dynamics relate to multi-dimensional behavioral phenotypes. We introduce a behavior-guided contrastive multimodal learning framework that explicitly aligns resting-state EEG signals with behavioral metrics to learn a shared, interpretable EEG–behavior embedding space. The EEG network is used as a plug-and-play backbone, and a cross-modal InfoNCE objective with regularization shapes behavior-aligned EEG embeddings that can be deployed using EEG alone at inference. On a multi-center dataset of N=744 subjects (healthy controls, methamphetamine use disorder, heroin use disorder), our framework achieves 94.1% accuracy on a three-way cross-disease classification task, outperforming functional connectivity features and strong unimodal deep learning baselines. Furthermore, clustering on the multimodal embeddings reveals robust EEG–behavior subgroups and provides a modality-agnostic scaffold for integrating additional neural readouts via lightweight mapping networks.

records.title: Proxy-Guided Selective Expansion Adaptation Network for Face Forgery Detection
records.abstract: With rapid generative AI development, detecting forged faces in deepfake videos has become increasingly challenging. Despite significant advancements, two key challenges remain: (1) Existing models tend to neglect inter-domain discrepancies, impeding the effective extraction of common forgery features; (2) Fixed decision boundaries learned during training are often rigid and fail to adapt to the distributional shifts encountered in test samples.To address these challenges, we propose a Proxy-guided Selective Expansion Adaptation Network (PSEA-Net) for face forgery detection. During training, we introduce a Multiple Proxy Refinement (MPR) mechanism. MPR encourages learning multiple proxy vectors per class for similarity-based prediction, rather than relying solely on common forgery features. At test time, we implement a Selective Expansion Adaptation (SEA) strategy for test-time training. SEA ensures pseudo-label reliability via entropy filtering while employing spherical linear interpolation to expand features, effectively optimizing the decision boundary. Extensive experiments validate PSEA-Net's superior generalization capability. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/Yiming0331/PSEA-Net.

records.title: FedLRQ: Differentially Private and Communication Efficient Heterogeneous Federated Learning via Client-Specific Learnable Randomized Quantization
records.abstract: Federated learning (FL) has to cope with several challenges in real-world deployments, including the high communication cost, privacy leakage, and system heterogeneity across clients. To address these, we propose FedLRQ, an end-to-end learnable randomized quantization framework for differentially private FL with the client-wise mixed precisions of model training. Specifically, FedLRQ assigns each client a resource-aligned bit-width and then applies a randomized quantization during its local training according to the assigned precision. The induced quantization randomness provides provably a differential privacy guarantee without the need of additional noise injection. To balance the privacy and accuracy during local training, FedLRQ learns the client-specific privacy-governing parameters and locally updates them jointly with the model weights, adapting to the client’s data distribution and assigned bit-width. Empirical results demonstrate that FedLRQ achieves a higher accuracy than existing differentially private quantization baselines under a smaller privacy budget.

records.title: Dual-Domain Adaptive Graph Convolutional Network for Medical Image Segmentation
records.abstract: Medical image segmentation remains challenging due to complex structures and multi-scale dependencies. Conventional CNNs are limited in modeling global context, while Vision Transformers incur high computational cost and weak structural priors. Graph-based methods provide relational modeling but often focus on a single domain. In this paper, we propose a Dual-Domain Adaptive Graph Convolutional Network (DDAGCN) that jointly models spatial and spectral relationships through learned graph representations. Spatial adjacency is constructed using Gaussian kernels with KNN sparsification, while spectral graphs are built based on Fourier energy similarity. An adaptive gating mechanism dynamically fuses the two domains within a hierarchical decoder for progressive feature refinement. Experimental results demonstrate that DDAGCN achieves state-of-the-art performance on the Synapse dataset with a Dice score of 85.12\%, and shows strong generalization on ISIC 2017 and ISIC 2018.

records.title: CorticalNet: A Lightweight Bio-Inspired Framework with Cortical Hierarchy Integration, Neural Oscillations Propagation and Adaptive Boundary Perception for Medical Image Segmentation
records.abstract: Accurate medical image segmentation is a prerequisite for effective diagnosis, yet remains hindered by multi-scale anatomical variations, intrinsic speckle noise, and ambiguous boundaries. To address these challenges, we propose CorticalNet, a lightweight bio-inspired framework that emulates the spatial filtering mechanisms of the human brain. To enhance feature representation, CorticalNet integrates three novel modules: Multi-scale Cortical Fusion Integration (MCFI) to orchestrate context-aware semantic binding via feature coherence modulation; Neural Oscillation Propagation (NOP) to suppress intrinsic noise through spatial phase-amplitude coupling; and Adaptive Boundary Perception (ABP) to refine segmentation boundaries through multi-scale orientation tuning and adaptive gain control. Extensive validation on six diverse benchmarks demonstrates the superiority of our method, achieving a competitive Dice score of 86.36% and HD95 of 14.17. Notably, with only 5.38M parameters and 9.54G FLOPs, CorticalNet offers a robust and ultra-efficient solution for resource-constrained clinical deployments. Our code is available at https://github.com/6GeTang/CorticalNet.

records.title: EETalk: Emotion-Enhanced Talking Face Generation via Diffusion Models
records.abstract: Audio-driven talking face generation is an interesting and challenging task. Although existing methods have made progress in temporal synchronization and image quality, the performance (i.e., geometric precision and emotional accuracy) of the mouth region in emotional scenarios still needs improvement. To address this, we propose EETalk, a two-stage method based on latent diffusion models (LDMs), which achieves emotion enhancement by incorporating audio emotion features. In the Audio2Landmark stage, the content and emotion features extracted from audio are fed sequentially into a Transformer-based generator to produce content-aligned and emotion-enhanced facial landmarks as an intermediate representation between audio and lip motion. In the Landmark2Face stage, these facial landmarks serve as the primary geometric condition, combined with audio content and emotion, to guide the LDMs in generating high-quality talking faces with emotion-consistent mouth region. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EETalk can generate high-fidelity talking faces of arbitrary identities without fine-tuning, and significantly improves mouth region performance in fixed emotional scenarios.

records.title: Disentangled Feature Augmentation for Multimodal Incremental Perception
records.abstract: Embodied agents face severe adaptation challenges when they continuously interact in an open world. The environment not only introduces new objects (class increments), but also undergoes drastic changes in lighting, weather, or style (domain increments). The mixed and unpredictable distribution shift seriously hinders agents from building a robust model of the world. To this end, we propose a multi-modal disentangling and feature enhancement framework that aims to achieve continuous sensing against hybrid incremental streams. We design the dual encoder architecture to disentangle the input sensory data into semantic content and environmental style. By synthesizing cross-domain conflict samples through a feature exchange strategy, we force the agent to strip away context-style interference and focus on extracting context-invariant core semantic features. In addition, the parameter fusion strategy is adopted, and the low-rank decomposition and parameter stacking mechanism are used to solidify historical knowledge without any data replay. Experiments show that the framework shows superior robustness in complex dynamic scenes, which provides effective support for the continuous learning and perception ability of agents in complex dynamic environments.

records.title: EgoPrune: Efficient Token Pruning for Egomotion Video Spatial Reasoning in Embodied Agents
records.abstract: Egomotion videos, captured from a continuously moving first-person view, serve as the primary visual input for embodied AI agents whose core task is spatial reasoning—understanding layout, topology, and relative relations. Improving the efficiency of such egomotion-based reasoning is crucial for real-world deployment. Unlike third-person videos with discontinuous cuts, egomotion videos exhibit strong motion continuity and natural redundancy, enabling simpler and more effective token pruning. We propose EgoPrune, a training-free pruning framework tailored for egomotion video spatial reasoning. EgoPrune consists of three components: a keyframe selector adapted from EmbodiedR for efficient temporal sampling; Perspective-Aware Redundancy Filtering (PARF), which uses homography-based alignment to remove temporal redundancy and generate the compact egomotion video representation; and an MMR-based token selector to remove spatial redundancy from this representation while simultaneously balancing prompt relevance and spatial diversity. Experiments on two egomotion spatial reasoning benchmarks and two LVLMs show that EgoPrune consistently outperforms existing training-free methods while substantially reducing FLOPs, memory usage, and inference latency.

records.title: FlashSign: Pose-Free Guidance for Efficient Sign Language Video Generation
records.abstract: Sign language plays a crucial role in bridging communication gaps between the deaf and hard-of-hearing communities. However, existing sign language video generation models often rely on complex intermediate representations, which limits their flexibility and efficiency. In this work, we propose a novel pose-free framework for real-time sign language video generation. Our method eliminates the need for intermediate pose representations by directly mapping natural language text to sign language videos using a diffusion-based approach. We introduce two key innovations: (1) a pose-free generative model based on the a state-of-the-art diffusion backbone, which learns implicit text-to-gesture alignments without pose estimation, and (2) a Train-able Sliding Tile Attention (T-STA) mechanism that accelerates inference by exploiting spatio-temporal locality patterns. Unlike previous training-free sparsity approaches, T-STA integrates trainable sparsity into both training and inference, ensuring consistency and eliminating the train-test gap. This approach significantly reduces computational overhead while maintaining high generation quality, making real-time deployment feasible. Our method increases video generation speed by 3.07× without compromising video quality. Our contributions open new avenues for real-time, high-quality, pose-free sign language synthesis, with potential applications in inclusive communication tools for diverse communities.

records.title: Embodied Multimodal World Modeling with 4D Scene Graphs for Long-Distance Teleoperation
records.abstract: Long-distance robot operation inevitably suffers from network delay and temporary disconnections, leading to a persistent mismatch between human-issued instructions and the robot’s actual environment during task execution. In such settings, simply pausing execution or relying on static perception is impractical. This paper presents 4D-OVSG, an embodied multimodal world modeling framework that enables robust task execution under delay. The core idea is to compress delayed RGB-D video streams into a compact 4D open-vocabulary scene graph. The framework introduces a GMM–based keyframe extraction module to reduce computational redundancy, together with a Multi-Object Tracking (MOT) pipeline to maintain stable object identities over time. Furthermore, a hierarchical planning strategy based on VLMs/LLMs is employed to validate instructions and detect environment change. Real-robot experiments show that 4D-OVSG achieves reliable task execution with up to 68.9% success rate while maintaining inference times as low as 79.89 s. Compared to ST-OVSG, our approach achieves over 7× faster inference with higher success rates in complex dynamic scenarios. This work provides a robust semantic foundation for long-distance task-level teleoperation.

records.title: Match6D: Matching-Centric Zero-Shot 6D Pose Estimation
records.abstract: Although 6D pose estimation has advanced rapidly, achieving robustness in heavily occluded scenarios remains an open problem. Current pipelines are prone to failure because purely visual descriptors cannot distinguish valid geometric structures under occlusion, nor can they effectively filter out background interference to focus on the target object. To address these issues, we propose Match6D, a two-stage framework for robust 6D pose estimation. The pipeline leverages the prevailing segmentation model Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2) to deliver accurate object segmentation. A novel Geometric-Aware Fused Matching module is proposed to integrate semantic, appearance, and geometric features from the segmentation results. Additionally, we introduce an Enhanced-Contextual Token to enhance the matching between objects and proposals by focusing on background contextual features within the pose estimation module. Experiments on BOP datasets demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on the 6D pose estimation task.

records.title: Triple-Consistent Representation Learning for Robust Multimodal Sentiment Analysis with Uncertain Missing Modalities
records.abstract: Uncertain missing modalities severely degrade the performance of Multimodal Sentiment Analysis (MSA) models that assume full-modality availability. While state-of-the-art methods attempt to reconstruct missing cues from observed modalities, they lack adequate cross-modal mapping from three aspect: distributional authenticity, structural integrity, and semantic alignment. To overcome this limitation, we pioneer the Triple-Consistent Representation Learning (TRL) framework, which simultaneously enforces distribution, structural, and semantic consistency for robust cross-modal mapping. Specifically, TRL integrates Attention-guided Disentangled Distillation to enforce distribution consistency between complete and missing modality representations, Entropy-guided Adaptive Distillation to maintain structural consistency and Cross-modal Contrastive Learning that ensures semantic consistency. Systematic experiments on CMU-MOSI and CMU-MOSEI demonstrate that TRL outperforms other state-of-the-art methods by 0.967% in terms of AUILC under varying missing rates.

records.title: PASE: Phoneme-Aware Speech Encoder to Improve Lip Sync Accuracy for Talking Head Synthesis
records.abstract: Recent talking head synthesis works typically adopt speech features extracted from large-scale pre-trained acoustic models. However, the intrinsic many-to-many relationship between speech and lip motion causes phoneme-viseme alignment ambiguity, leading to inaccurate and unstable lips. To further improve lip sync accuracy, we propose PASE (Phoneme-Aware Speech Encoder), a novel speech representation model that bridges the gap between phonemes and visemes. PASE explicitly introduces phoneme embeddings as alignment anchors and employs a contrastive alignment module to enhance the discriminability between corresponding audio–visual pairs. In addition, a prediction and reconstruction task is designed to improve robustness under noise and partial modality absence. Experimental results show PASE significantly improves lip sync accuracy and achieves state-of-the-art performance across both NeRF- and 3DGS-based rendering frameworks, outperforming conventional methods based on acoustic features by 13.7% and 14.2%, respectively. Importantly, PASE can be seamlessly integrated into diverse talking head pipelines to improve the lip sync accuracy without architectural modifications.

records.title: Integrating Uncertainty-Aware Correction and Symmetric Cross Entropy for Robust Multi-View Learning
records.abstract: Instance-dependent label noise (IDN) presents a critical challenge in robust multi-view learning, often causing models to overfit misleading supervision signals. Although existing methods utilize robust loss functions, they frequently overlook the reliability of the correction process itself, leading to error propagation. To address this, we propose USCE, a unified framework integrating Uncertainty-Aware Correction and Symmetric Cross Entropy. Specifically, we incorporate Symmetric Cross Entropy (SCELoss) as a robust anchor to balance clean pattern learning with noise rejection. Furthermore, we design a novel Uncertainty-Aware Correction (UACR) mechanism that dynamically estimates epistemic uncertainty via predictive divergence. This module effectively down-weights unreliable samples and guides the model to perform precise label rectification. By jointly optimizing these components, USCE prevents noise memorization while maintaining view consistency. Extensive experiments on five benchmark datasets demonstrate that USCE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, particularly in high-noise regimes.

records.title: FedVaDE: Federated Variational Deep Embedding for Privacy-Preserving Generative Clustering
records.abstract: Federated Clustering (FC) enables unsupervised knowledge discovery from decentralized, privacy-sensitive data across heterogeneous clients. However, existing methods typically rely on distance-based heuristics or autoencoder-derived embeddings, which tend to oversimplify non-iid distributions, thereby limiting interpretability, or require transmitting latent features, incurring high communication costs. Moreover, these approaches often decouple representation learning and clustering, misaligning latent spaces with global cluster structures. To address these challenges, we propose FedVaDE, a novel Federated Variational Deep Embedding framework extending generative clustering to federated settings. FedVaDE models the global latent space as a Mixture-of-Gaussians (MoG) via a client-server dual-model optimization strategy. Each client independently trains a local VaDE, while the server aggregates model parameters to generate training samples for global VaDE optimization, without accessing raw data or client-shared synthetic data. A client-server alignment loss is introduced to harmonize local and global latent structures. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that FedVaDE significantly outperforms state-of-the-art FC baselines.

records.title: Federated Adversarial Reentangled Feature Augmentation
records.abstract: In federated learning, data collected by different clients often contain bias features arising from location, environment, or device differences. Directly using such biased data may lead the model to learn spurious correlations and suffer from model drift. While existing studies attempt to remove bias via feature disentanglement, we observe that bias features also contribute valuable diversity that can enhance model performance when properly leveraged. Based on this insight, we propose FedRAug, a federated feature augmentation technique that re-entangles essential and bias features. Each client trains two encoders to extract disentangled essential and bias representations. Then, two generators are trained to model the distributions of these separated features. Finally, augmented clients created by re-entangling different pairs of generators and incorporated into the global training process. These augmented clients synthesize diverse samples, enriching the training dynamics. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets show that FedRAug mitigates the negative impact of biased data and substantially improves overall model performance.

records.title: Towards Training-Free Universal AI-Generated Video Detection via KL Divergence Trajectory
records.abstract: Current advanced video generation technology like Veo3 enables the production of high-fidelity AI-generated videos, precipitating a crisis of trust in digital media. However, training a robust AI-generated video detection model typically requires a large number of videos, which is time-consuming and constrains its generalizability. To bridge this gap, in this paper, we propose a novel training-free and interpretable universal AI-generated video detection model that deeply mines the KL distribution difference in a single shot segment between real and AI-generated videos as the judging cue. Through analyzing existing AI-generated models, we find that they heavily rely on the initial frame to ensure high-quality video content, where the resulting sequences exhibit abnormal distributional convergence. In contrast, real-world videos manifest significantly higher natural volatility during spatio-temporal evolution. Specifically, we extract the latent semantic feature of keyframes, quantify the KL-divergence trajectory of subsequent frames relative to the lead-frame within a single shot segment, and then identify non-natural statistical clustering by RMSE-based volatility scoring. Empirical results across multiple benchmarks demonstrate a 10.99% improvement in Mean Average Precision (mAP) over state-of-the-art methods.

records.title: Hard-Label-Based Data-Free Extraction of Robust Ensemble Models
records.abstract: While model extraction attacks on a single deep neural network model have been well-studied, extracting an ensemble model along with its functionality and robustness to adversarial attacks remains a challenging task, especially under the restrictive data-free hard-label (DFHL) setting. Existing methods are constrained by high-frequency synthetic artifacts that diverge from natural data distributions as well as ensemble gradient conflicts that hinder optimization. To address these limitations, we propose Spectral-Synergistic Robustness Extraction (S2RE). Our framework incorporates Dynamic Spectral Refinement, which is a frequency-domain filtering mechanism that progressively suppresses artifacts. Additionally, we introduce Gradient Synergy Weighting to dynamically calibrate the contribution of sub-models based on attack transferability, thereby maximizing global gradient synergy. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 show that S2RE can achieve high-fidelity cloning of both accuracy and robustness under the DFHL setting.

records.title: Conformal Regression-Based Feature Restoration for Robust Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
records.abstract: Robust Multimodal Sentiment Analysis (RMSA)aims to achieve reliable emotion understanding in complex real-world scenarios. However, real-world noise is not merely superficial; it induces significant semantic drift in the feature space. This distortion disrupts reliable mappings between features and sentiment strengths, resulting in inference bias. To address this fundamental challenge, we propose a novel framework termed Conformal Regression-Based Feature Restoration (CoRe-FR), which leverages conformal prediction to establish a statistically grounded reliability mechanism for semantic recovery from noisy data. CoRe-FR hinges on a semantic self-restoration loop that integrates two pivotal modules: (1) Conformal Decomposition and Anchor Selection, which leverages conformal prediction to select high-confidence semantic anchors from orthogonal latent variants, thereby circumventing the inherent fallibility of deterministic mappings. (2) Anchorguided Feature Restoration, which uses the selected anchors as navigational references to execute global feature alignment and variance suppression, thereby rectifying corrupted distributions toward the true semantic centroid. Extensive experiments on two benchmark datasets demonstrate that our CoRe-FR framework consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in both performance and robustness. The corresponding source code is available at https://github.com/SuperKAI102900/CoRe-FR.

records.title: Beyond Modal Consistency: Counterfactual Intervention Based on Large Language Models for Robust Multimodal Rumor Detection
records.abstract: Short videos have emerged as a dominant medium for news dissemination, and existing multimodal detection methods have achieved significant success in capturing and fusing multimodal semantics of news. However, they often overlook the multimodal consistency bias, leading to two critical misjudgment patterns: (1) misclassifying crudely captured, low-consistency real news as fake; (2) misclassifying meticulously spliced or AI-generated high-consistency fake news as real. To address these limitations, we propose CIMC (Counterfactual Intervention with Multimodal Correction), a framework designed to mitigate multimodal consistency bias in short video fake news detection. CIMC employs a Counterfactual Mixture-of-Experts network with five experts (time, location, context, logic, and fact), dynamically intervened using targeted counterfactual samples and LLM-generated logic/fact confidences. Meanwhile, a Dual-path Consistency-Logic Correction mechanism suppresses false positives on low-consistency real news and penalizes suspicious high-consistency in generative fakes. Extensive experiments on two public benchmarks demonstrate that CIMC significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods.
