records.title: Backdoor Defense via Graph-Structured Reinforcement Learning for Targeted Neuron Pruning
records.abstract: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are increasingly vulnerable to sophisticated backdoor attacks, where adversaries manipulate specific neurons to control model behavior. However, existing defense strategies predominantly rely on heuristic rules and localized neuron analysis, failing to exploit the global topological relationships critical for precise backdoor mitigation. To bridge this gap, we propose a graph-structured reinforcement learning framework (GSRL) for targeted neuron pruning. GSRL models DNNs as directed graphs that encode both inter-layer connectivity and intra-layer neuron weights. The target DNN is transformed into a graph based on neuron connectivity, where a graph-based Reinforcement Learning (RL) agent learns graph embeddings to discover optimized pruning policies. Unlike conventional methods, our approach dynamically adapts pruning decisions by jointly considering neuron saliency, attack persistence, and model fidelity. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first topology-aware pruning mechanism that leverages graph-based analysis for backdoor mitigation. Extensive evaluations demonstrate state-of-the-art backdoor mitigation performance across multiple attack scenarios. Code is available athttps://github.com/HaiyangYu-Lab/GSRL-Prune.

records.title: Season: Spectrum-Aware Orthogonal Gradient Refinement for Transfer-Based Adversarial Attacks
records.abstract: Transfer-based adversarial attacks often transfer poorly across heterogeneous architectures because CNNs favor local textures while Vision Transformers (ViTs) rely on global shapes. We propose Season, a spectrum-aware orthogonal gradient refinement framework for L-infinity transfer attacks against black-box target models on ImageNet, using a white-box surrogate. Season decomposes each update into a low-frequency branch capturing structural cues and a high-frequency branch capturing textures. A low-saliency guidance scheme reallocates high-frequency energy to background regions, preserving foreground structures that ViTs depend on. An orthogonal projection then forces the textural update to lie in the orthogonal complement of the structural direction, mitigating feature interference. As a training-free plug-and-play wrapper, Season enhances eight gradient-stabilization and input-enhancement attacks without modifying their cores. Across eight CNN, ViT, and MLP targets, Season improves transfer success rate by 6.6 percentage points on average and up to 16.0 points over strong baselines under a unified protocol.

records.title: MixFake: Benchmarking and Enhancing Audio Deepfake Detection in Diverse Real-world Mixed Audio
records.abstract: Speech deepfake detection has achieved remarkable success in clean environments but faces significant challenges in complex, real-world scenarios where speech is often mixed with background music or noise. Current state-of-the-art methods rely on semantic features from self-supervised learning (SSL) models, which often fail when processing non-speech or mixed-source audio. In this paper, we first introduce MixFake, a large-scale benchmark dataset designed to simulate diverse acoustic environments with varying SNR levels and mixed authenticity components. To address the "semantic-centric" limitation, we propose a Multi-stream Prompt Tuning framework that injects signal-level priors into SSL backbones. By integrating semantic, frequency, and texture streams through deep prompt injection, our model effectively captures acoustic artifacts. Experimental results demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing baselines, achieving a 0.95% EER in foreground detection and a substantial 7.72% absolute improvement in complex background detection tasks.

records.title: 3D Scene Graph Prediction via Shadow-Mentor Partner Network for Multimedia Scene Perception
records.abstract: 3D scene graph prediction based on multimodal data has recently become a prominent research focus. While existing methods leverage 2D visual and language information to enhance the semantic representation of 3D point clouds, they still face significant challenges in cross-modal cooperation. Our goal is to leverage the collaborative relationships between modalities, using visual and textual modalities to enhance the semantic representation of 3D features. Hence, we propose SMPNet for 3D scene graph prediction, Shadow-Mentor Partner Network, which utilizes visual-language guidance to enhance the semantic modeling of nodes and edges in 3D Scene graphs. Firstly, our SMPNet features a mentor network that employs a CLIP-based semantic feature library to guide the 3D network through gradient-based optimization. Then, a shadow-mentor network acquires semantic knowledge from the mentor network through distillation. We propose a novel hybrid-attention fusion strategy to inject the semantic knowledge of the Shadow-Mentor Partner network into the 3D representation, achieving multi-branch cross-modal and intra-modal feature enhancement. Finally, we devise a category-based predicate feature enhancement module, which further leverages self-learned object category labels to enhance the relationship predictions. Extensive experiments on public datasets, such as 3DSSG, demonstrate significant performance improvements across various metrics.

records.title: Memory-Augmented Dynamic Graph Attention for Event-Driven 3D Human Pose Estimation
records.abstract: 3D human pose estimation in dynamic and high-speed scenarios remains challenging due to motion blur, extreme illumination, and sparse asynchronous events. Event cameras, with microsecond temporal resolution and ultra-high dynamic range, offer a promising solution. Existing methods are limited by fixed skeletal topologies, insufficient exploitation of sparse events, and uniform joint processing. To address these issues, we propose the Memory-Augmented Dynamic Graph Attention (MDGA) framework with a spiking transformer encoder. MDGA includes a topology-free dynamic graph attention mechanism to capture per-frame inter-joint dependencies, a memory-augmented mechanism that propagates historical motion context to improve temporal coherence, and a sparse activation mechanism focusing computation on motion-relevant joints. Refined features are regressed into SMPL parameters, producing anatomically plausible and temporally consistent 3D human meshes. Extensive experiments on the MMHPSD dataset showed that MDGA outperformed state-of-the-art methods, reducing PA-MPJPE from 45.3 mm to 42.9 mm, a 5.3% improvement, particularly under high-speed motion and extreme illumination.

records.title: Breaking Channel Uniformity: Channel-Aware Low-Rank Attention for Human-Aware Image Deraining
records.abstract: Embodied AI systems operating in human-shared spaces require reliable perception during rain, the most frequent adverse weather in urban deployments. Rain severely degrades the fine-grained visual features essential for human detection, pose estimation, and facial recognition, thereby directly threatening safe interaction. While Transformer-based deraining has advanced significantly, we identify a critical bottleneck: standard Multi-Head Attention mechanisms enforce "Channel Uniformity", forcing all feature channels to share identical spatial attention maps. This constraint prevents independent modulation of diverse human-centric features that naturally reside in different channels. We propose Channel-Aware Low-Rank (CARL) Attention, which computes r shared basis attention maps through low-rank decomposition, then synthesizes channel-specific attention via learnable per-channel mixing coefficients. By formulating attention as unique linear combinations of these bases, CARL enables each channel to obtain distinct attention patterns. This facilitates the precise modulation of diverse visual features and achieves high-fidelity human-centric restoration. Experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art deraining performance across multiple benchmarks. We further validate CARL on image dehazing and semantic segmentation of rainy scenes, confirming its effectiveness as a general mechanism for human-aware perception in embodied AI systems.

records.title: LatentFix: Efficient Text-Driven 3D Human Motion Editing in Latent Space
records.abstract: Text-driven human motion editing aims to manipulate source sequences based on textual descriptions to satisfy fine-grained user requirements. However, current approaches struggle to deliver high-fidelity edits that accurately conform to the input text. Existing methods typically operate directly on raw high-dimensional motion data; this introduces excessive kinematic redundancy and poses significant hurdles to accurately mapping source sequences to target motions. To address this, we propose LatentFix, a novel framework that decouples motion representation from semantic manipulation by shifting the editing process to a compact latent manifold. In our framework, we first employ a Transformer-based Variational AutoEncoder (VAE) to compress raw motions into robust latent codes. Subsequently, we introduce a latent diffusion model (MLD) designed to perform precise semantic transformations within this unified feature space. Extensive experiments on the MotionFix benchmark demonstrate that LatentFix achieves state-of-the-art performance in both editing accuracy and motion preservation. Notably, it delivers a 70× speedup over the raw-space baseline while surpassing its full-data performance using only 50% of the training data. Code and model weights will be publicly available at https://github.com/pkwq09/LatentFix.

records.title: ISCS: Parameter-Guided Feature Pruning for Resource-Constrained Embodied Perception
records.abstract: Prior studies in embodied AI consistently show that robust perception is critical for human-robot interaction, yet deploying high-fidelity visual models on resource-constrained agents remains challenging due to limited on-device computation power and transmission latency. Exploiting the redundancy in latent representations could improve system efficiency, yet existing approaches often rely on costly dataset-specific ablation tests or heavy entropy models unsuitable for real-time edge-robot collaboration. We propose a generalizable, dataset-agnostic method to identify and selectively transmit structure-critical channels in pretrained encoders. Instead of brute-force empirical evaluations, our approach leverages intrinsic parameter statistics—weight variances and biases—to estimate channel importance. This analysis reveals a consistent organizational structure, termed the Invariant Salient Channel Space (ISCS), where Salient-Core channels capture dominant structures while Salient-Auxiliary channels encode fine visual details. Building on ISCS, we introduce a deterministic static pruning strategy that enables lightweight split-computing. Experiments across different datasets demonstrate that our method achieves a deterministic, ultra-low latency pipeline by bypassing heavy entropy modeling. Our method reduces end-to-end latency, providing a critical speed-accuracy trade-off for resource-constrained human-aware embodied systems.

records.title: Contrastive Multi-Modal Hypergraph Reasoning for 3D Crowd Mesh Recovery
records.abstract: Multi-person 3D reconstruction is pivotal for real-world interaction analysis, yet remains challenging due to severe occlusions and depth ambiguity. Current approaches typically rely on single-modality inputs, which inherently lack geometric guidance. Furthermore, these methods often reconstruct subjects in isolation, neglecting the collective group context essential for resolving ambiguities in crowded scenes. To address these limitations, we propose Contrastive Multi-modal Hypergraph Reasoning to synergize semantic, geometric, and pose cues for crowd reconstruction. We first initialize robust node representations by combining RGB features, geometric priors, and occlusion-aware incomplete poses. Additionally, we introduce a pelvis depth indicator as a global spatial anchor, aligning visual features with a metric-scale-agnostic depth ordering. Subsequently, we construct a shared-topology hypergraph that moves beyond pairwise constraints to model higher-order crowd dynamics. To improve feature fusion, we design a hypergraph-based contrastive learning scheme that jointly enhances intra-modal discriminability and enforces cross-modal orthogonality. This mechanism enables the network to propagate global context effectively, allowing it to infer missing information even under severe occlusion. Extensive experiments on the Panoptic and GigaCrowd benchmarks confirm that our method achieves new state-of-the-art performance. Code and pre-trained models are available at https://github.com/SunMH-try/CoMHR.

records.title: FreeTailor: Tuning-Free Trajectory Control for Video Generation via Noise Customization
records.abstract: Recent advancements in text-to-video (T2V) generative models have demonstrated impressive capabilities in generating realistic and high-quality videos. However, customized video generation remains a significant challenge, particularly in precise and reasonable trajectory control. Existing methods often rely on complex layer-wise modification to attention during inference, which struggles with balancing control precision and inference time. Additionally, noise guidance in these methods only serves an auxiliary role, with its potential yet to be thoroughly explored. In this study, we propose \textbf{FreeTailor}, a tuning-free method that achieves trajectory-controllable video generation by leveraging the noise-generation dependency. Specifically, we comprehensively delve into the 3D spatio-temporal distribution in initial noise and reveal that the spatio-temporal anomalous regions in the initial noise can more effectively control the motion trajectory of generated content in various trajectories. With this insight, we further design the spatio-temporal anomalous regions based on variance deviation and noise reuse, which have the characteristics of high spatial response and temporal correlation, and then utilize them to achieve initial noise customization for trajectory-controllable video generation. Additionally, we utilize simple attention modifications with minimal time cost to prevent the influence of anomalous regions. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority and versatility of our FreeTailor, achieving efficient and precise trajectory control in both text-to-video and image-to-video generation.

records.title: SGW-ULIC: Saliency-Guided Grid Warping for INR-based Extreme Image Compression
records.abstract: Implicit Neural Representation (INR) methods employ multiscale grids for image modeling and demonstrate strong potential for highly efficient image compression. However, their uniform grid structures distribute representational capacity indiscriminately, causing notable quality degradation in salient and high-frequency regions at extremely low bitrates (below 0.1 bits per pixel (bpp)). We propose SGW-ULIC, a saliency-guided grid-warping framework specifically designed for INR-based extreme image compression. SGW-ULIC introduces an explicit warping module and leverages density-guided warping with ROI-aware perceptual losses to adaptively reallocate grid capacity toward visually important regions. Extensive experiments on kodak and tecnick-40 datasets show that SGW-ULIC consistently delivers significantly better perceptual quality than multiple image codecs.

records.title: QER: Co-Visible Query Embedding is All You Need for Robust Point Cloud Registration
records.abstract: Transformer-based point cloud registration methods has achieved significant progress via global feature interaction. However, in partially overlapping point cloud registration, such interaction introduces a lot of noise from non-overlapping regions, degrading feature discriminability and robustness. To address this, we propose a partial-to-partial registration method based on co-visible feature interaction. By collaboratively performing overlap estimation and global interaction specifically within co-visible regions, our method effectively suppresses noise and reduces computation. Specifically, we introduce an attention mechanism to interact a query embedding with each point cloud to obtain features that capture co-visible information. Based on these features, we simultaneously achieve estimation and interaction tasks using a cross-attention module and a lightweight segmentation module. In addition, we further use the estimated overlap scores to filter out non-overlapping correspondences. Experiments on 3DMatch and KITTI demonstrate state-of-the-art performance with a superior balance of robustness and efficiency. Moreover, our approach can serves as a plug-and-play module for existing frameworks.

records.title: DROC: Diagnosing and Resolving Objective Conflicts in Open-Set Semi-Supervised Learning
records.abstract: High-dimensional sensing systems (e.g., event cameras, NeRF) often have few labeled in-distribution (ID) samples but massive unlabeled streams mixing ID and out-of-distribution (OOD) data, motivating open-set semi-supervised learning (OSSL) that supports accurate ID classification and reliable OOD detection. Experiments reveal that semantically similar OOD samples (near-OOD) in the unlabeled pool induce substantial performance degradation. Gradient analysis on shared representations further reveals that (i) as OOD–ID semantic similarity increases, gradient conflict between supervised closed-set objectives and generic unlabeled objectives (U-objectives) on the mixed pool intensifies, and (ii) within each U-objective, gradients from unlabeled ID and OOD subsets exhibit increasingly severe directional conflict. We address this with a decoupled OSSL framework that factorizes the last-layer representation into ID-discriminative and OODness subspaces and routes U-objectives via soft responsibilities, improving closed-set accuracy and AUROC on CIFAR-10/100 with similar and dissimilar OOD data.

records.title: Generative High Resolution Imaging of mmWave Radar from 24GHz to 77GHz
records.abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar at 24 and 77GHz is widely used in autonomous driving, indoor sensing, and security screening. Compared with hardware-friendly 24GHz systems, 77GHz systems provide much higher spatial resolution and richer high-frequency detail sensitive to surface roughness and subtle material differences. Recovering such 77GHz–style structural and material-sensitive detail from 24GHz measurements would enable high-resolution sensing at low cost, but this 24-to-77 cross-frequency generation is fundamentally difficult because much of the high-frequency, material-related information is intrinsically absent at 24GHz and the two bands suffer from geometric misalignment. To address this, cross-frequency generation is reformulated as a generative modeling problem for downstream sensing, and a Joint Spatial–Frequency Generation (JSFG) framework is introduced accordingly. JSFG explicitly decouples cross-frequency generation into two complementary objectives in the spatial and frequency domains. In the spatial domain, JSFG regularizes 24GHz observations by suppressing clutter and stabilizing object contours, thereby recovering a clean and reliable low-frequency geometric layout from noisy 24GHz measurements. In the frequency domain, JSFG operates in a multi-scale transform space to refine high-frequency components and to complete the missing frequency-dependent scattering details that characterize 77GHz signals. Experiments on the MITO dataset show that JSFG substantially outperforms representative mapping and super-resolution baselines in SSIM, PSNR, and amplitude/phase error. Furthermore, in a downstream object-level anomaly detection task using PatchCore, JSFG-generated 77GHz signals yield higher F1 and AUC than using 24GHz inputs or other synthesized 77GHz variants, demonstrating that JSFG improves not only signal fidelity but also downstream sensing performance.The code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/JSFG-74E7

records.title: Revitalizing Hyperspectral Image Reconstruction via Cross-Domain Aligned Generative Codebook
records.abstract: Abstract—Hyperspectral image reconstruction aims to recover high-quality spectral distribution and high-fidelity spatial details from RGB inputs. However, we find that existing methods often fail in some challenging scenarios due to directly learning the mapping from the RGB to the hyperspectral domain without guidance on spectral distributions. We suggest that learning real-world spectral distributions in the hyperspectral domain can serve as a fundamental prior that significantly reduces the uncertainty and ambiguity of reconstruction mapping by casting the ill-posed inverse problem as a code prediction task. Specifically, we first model the spectral distribution using a VQGAN framework to obtain a discrete spectral codebook, which serves as generative spectral prior guidance for the next reconstruction stage. In the reconstruction stage, we first customize a quantized cross-attention (QCA) module based on Top-K selection to align the RGB latent feature distribution to hyperspectral latent representations, relieving the ambiguity of codebook prediction and ensuring correct codebook retrieval. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method (denoted as HyperCode) outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of spectral fidelity and structural consistency. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/Zik-code/Hypercode.

records.title: PAFNet: A Phase-Aware Frequency Attention Network for SAR Autofocusing
records.abstract: SAR imaging was relied on the relative motion of target and radar. The imaging quality was therefore degraded in the non-ideal motion scenarios. The inaccurate phase compensation made the image defocused. This paper addressed the issue by proposing a dual-domain coordinated network (PAFUnet). To decouple magnitude and phase information for better structural and energy representation, the Phase-Aware Frequency Attention (PAFA) and Spectral Gating (SG) modules were unified into an encoder-decoder framework. So the complementary information across the spatial and frequency domains can be combined. A residual learning strategy was further configured to protect the detail information, and reduce the computational cost simultaneously. Multiple rounds of experiments were performed on simulated and measured datasets. The results demonstrated that the proposed method improved the imaging quality significantly in comparison to the mainstream methods. The SSIM and PSNR on magnitude improved by 27.42% and 9.01% respectively.

records.title: AdaGS-Net: An Adaptive Sparse Network for Multimodal Fusion in Alzheimer’s Disease
records.abstract: With the advancement of multimodal learning,integrating sMRI anatomical structures with PET metabolic function for Alzheimer’s disease (AD) diagnosis has garnered increasing attention. However, existing methods struggle with the inherent conflict between fine-grained edge preservation and deep semantic alignment, while global interactions often introduce background noise, limiting clinical applicability. To address this, we propose AdaGS-Net, aiming to establish a fusion mechanism that synergistically integrates structural and semantic features to precisely localize associated lesions. Extensive experiments on the ADNI dataset demonstrate that AdaGS-Net comprehensively outperforms current state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods in both AD diagnosis and early MCI screening tasks.

records.title: Can LLM Understand Medical Imaging With Long Context?
records.abstract: Medical applications place stricter demands on multi-image context and high-resolution imagery, which require decisions that depend on long temporal horizons and complex examination histories. In this paper, we propose a training-free framework that couples frozen CT/WSI foundation encoders with a long-context for spatiotemporal reasoning without finetuning of LLM. To mitigate noisy, low-yield visual evidence, we first use CAM-based scoring to retain informative CT slices and WSI regions, then compress encoder features with PCA and align them to the LLM embedding space via an optimal-transport calibration. The aligned vectors are injected as pseudo-tokens and interleaved with a handful of concise textual exemplars, enabling few-shot in-context inference for diagnosis, staging, and longitudinal response assessment directly within the decoder. This design (i) preserves fine-grained radiologic and histologic cues while scaling to long visual contexts, (ii) supports modular swap-in of lightweight projection strategies under different resource budgets, and (iii) approaches supervised multimodal baselines on public cancer cohorts while avoiding cross-modal fine-tuning. Overall, our results suggest a practical path toward privacy-conscious multimodal decision support that requires only inference-time preparation and alignment of embeddings.

records.title: CoDAC: Confidence-Driven Collaborative Denoising with Constraint-Aware Learning for Robust Multimodal Fusion
records.abstract: Detecting structural variations (SVs) from noisy long-read sequencing is challenged by high false-positive rates in single-modality methods. While multimodal learning can integrate structural and sequence cues, naïve fusion often suffers from cross-modal noise propagation and a lack of domain knowledge integration. We propose CoDAC, a Confidence-Driven Collaborative Denoising with Constraint-Aware Learning framework for robust multimodal fusion. CoDAC employs dual-stream encoders to capture complementary structural representations and text-like sequence features. Centrally, a Confidence-Driven Collaborative Denoising module dynamically estimates local feature reliability and guides cross-modal correction to suppress noise. Furthermore, Multi-granularity Knowledge-Aware Constraints are introduced to inject domain priors into representation learning, ensuring biologically consistent and discriminative joint embeddings. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that CoDAC achieves state-of-the-art performance, establishing a robust paradigm for learning from noisy, heterogeneous multimodal genomic data. The code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/CoDAC-5A41.

records.title: MeniOmni: A Structured Multimodal Benchmark for Holistic Meniscus Injury Assessment
records.abstract: Clinical diagnosis of meniscus injuries requires radiologists to integrate volumetric MRI evidence with patient context (e.g., sex, age, BMI) and to produce structured diagnostic reports. Existing knee MRI benchmarks are typically unimodal and rely on coarse labels, limiting their ability to evaluate holistic clinical reasoning. We introduce MeniOmni, a structured multimodal benchmark for meniscus injury assessment, consisting of 746 multi-center MRI studies with tri-planar volumetric inputs, Clinical Priors, and expert-annotated clinical text. MeniOmni supports two tasks: (1) fine-grained Stoller severity grading and (2) diagnostic report generation. We further propose risk-aware ordinal evaluation and a semantic consistency metric (Meni-Score) to better reflect clinical relevance. Baseline experiments show that incorporating Clinical Priors improves grading performance and reduces severe errors, highlighting the value of multimodal context for safer assessment. Code and data are available at https://github.com/ShuruiXu/MeniOmni.

records.title: Mitigating Multimodal Hallucinations via Uncertainty-aware Adaptive Decoding
records.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) perform strongly on multimodal tasks but remain prone to hallucinations, posing challenges to their reliability in practical applications. Recent contrastive decoding methods attempt to mitigate hallucinations by constructing perturbation-based distributions. However, they overlook the varying demands of different tasks and generation stages, typically relying on fixed decoding strategies, resulting in limited adaptability across scenarios. Motivated by the strong correlation between hallucinations and uncertainty, we leverage uncertainty to guide decoding decisions and propose Uncertainty-aware Adaptive Decoding (UAD), a training-free and model-agnostic framework. UAD first selects an appropriate basic decoding strategy based on task-level uncertainty, and then uses token-level uncertainty during generation to decide whether contrastive decoding should be applied at each step, enabling fine-grained control and better adaptation across different scenarios. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that UAD consistently outperforms baselines and prior contrastive decoding methods, significantly reducing hallucinations while maintaining high generation quality.

records.title: Fine-Grained Geometry for Relightable Gaussian Splatting via Localized Point Management
records.abstract: Relightable 3D Gaussian Splatting with SDFs has achieved strong results, but its geometric fidelity remains constrained by global gradient-based densification, which ignores local geometric consistency and often yields unstable SDF optimization and loss of fine detail. To address this, we introduce the first framework to integrate localized point management (LPM) into an SDF-based Gaussian Splatting pipeline, specifically designed to reconstruct fine-grained geometry. Our key idea is to replace the simplistic global densification with a targeted, multi-view consistent strategy. We propose a novel SDF-aware LPM that performs localized point addition only in regions of high geometric and photometric uncertainty. This is achieved by synergistically combining fine-grained neighbor-camera sampling with a new set of criteria, including depth-projection consistency and proximity to the SDF surface, ensuring that new geometry is added precisely where it is most needed. This targeted densification strategy results in a far more accurate and stable distribution of Gaussian primitives, leading to smoother SDF convergence and a dramatic improvement in the reconstruction of high-frequency surface details. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method substantially outperforms existing relightable Gaussian Splatting baselines, particularly in capturing the complex, fine-grained geometry of real-world objects. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/AutoHDR/FG3DGS-LPM.git}.

records.title: Geometric Enhancement in 3D Gaussian Splatting for Sparse-view Scene Reconstruction
records.abstract: Although sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) like InstantSplat has made significant progress, it still suffers from geometric inconsistencies including floating artifacts, incomplete surfaces, and unstable primitives, which degrade visual quality and geometric fidelity. Inaccurate camera poses further exacerbate these issues. We present a novel geometric enhancement framework for 3DGS to address these limitations. Our approach comprises three key components: Side-view Inconsistency Filtering (SIF) at initialization, Local Depth Regularization (LDR), and Anisotropy-aware Shape Regularization (ASR) during training. SIF leverages multi-view information to eliminate geometrically inconsistent points, reducing floating artifacts and improving surface coherence. LDR enforces spatial consistency by identifying and penalizing regions with high geometric uncertainty through patch-based depth correlation analysis. ASR constrains Gaussian primitives to geometrically plausible shapes by controlling opacity and scale ratio, preventing degenerate elongated structures. Extensive experiments on two widely used datasets demonstrate our method's superiority over pose-free and pose-known baselines.

records.title: Moving Light Adaptive Colonoscopy Reconstruction via Illumination-Attenuation-Aware 3D Gaussian Splatting
records.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables real-time view synthesis in colonoscopy but assumes static illumination, making it incompatible with the strong photometric variations caused by the moving light source and camera. This mismatch leads existing methods to compensate for illumination attenuation with structure-violating Gaussians, degrading geometric fidelity. Prior work considers only distance-based attenuation and overlooks the physical characteristics of colonscopic lighting. In this paper, we propose ColIAGS, an improved 3DGS framework for colonoscopy. To mimic realistic appearance under varying illumination, we introduce a lighting model with two types of illumination attenuation factors. To satisfy this lighting model's approximation and effectively integrate it into the 3DGS framework, we design Improved Geometry Modeling to strengthen geometry details and Improved Appearance Modeling to implicitly optimize illumination attenuation solutions. Experimental results on standard benchmarks demonstrate that ColIAGS supports both high-quality novel-view synthesis and accurate geometry reconstruction, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in rendering fidelity and Depth MSE. Our code is available at https://github.com/haowang020110/ColIAGS.

records.title: Learning Explicit Geometry Priors for Generalizable Human Gaussian Splatting from Sparse Views
records.abstract: Clothed human reconstruction has made significant progress, but existing methods face key limitations: multi-view approaches require substantial view overlap, while single-view diffusion-based methods often fail to preserve human identity. To tackle these challenges, we present a new feed-forward method for reconstructing humans via 2D Gaussian Splatting from sparse views, requiring as few as 3 input views. Specifically, our approach involves two main steps: (1) We use refined normal cues to guide upsampled SMPL mesh learning with vertex displacement, obtaining coarse geometric priors. (2) We regress dual-branch Gaussians: vertex-aligned Gaussians and pixel-aligned Gaussians. The former maintains the topological structure of the human body and ensures completeness in regions not visible from input viewpoints, while the latter guarantees high-quality texture detail reconstruction. Experimental results demonstrate our method's effectiveness in both geometric and texture reconstruction, with strong robustness across within-dataset and cross-dataset generalization scenarios.

records.title: TETRIS-4DGS: Efficient Post-Training Compression of 4D Gaussian Splatting
records.abstract: 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) has emerged as a powerful dynamic scene representation, supporting real-time high quality rendering but suffers from prohibitive storage overhead. Existing methods typically attempt to solve this by treating compression as a per-scene optimization problem, limiting generalizability and applicability where low-latency compression is required. In this work, we leverage existing image and video codecs and propose a generalized post-training compression framework for 4DGS to address these issues. Specifically, we apply importance-based adaptive quantization to Gaussians according to their importance levels, effectively refining bitrate allocation while remaining fully compatible with existing codecs. To further improve compression efficiency, we utilize the statistical properties of 4DGS and propose motion- and importance-aware packing to reorganize attributes into codec-friendly 2D maps. Our approach can achieve over 40× compression rate in seconds while maintaining high quality, facilitating the practical deployment of 4DGS.

records.title: Multimedia-Aware Fuzzy Logic Loss: Embracing Age Vagueness for Robust Age Estimation
records.abstract: Facial age estimation is an inherently vague task in multimedia visual analysis, yet most existing neural network-based methods enforce precise predictions by over-relying on ground-truth labels, thereby ignoring the biological vagueness of aging. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel Multimedia-Aware Fuzzy Logic loss (FL loss) function that explicitly models age vagueness. Our proposed loss introduces an adaptive age range centered on the ground truth, guiding the model to concentrate its top predictions within this biologically plausible interval. Furthermore, we employ learnable hyper-parameters to balance the influence of losses within the range. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed FL Loss consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, offering a more robust and human-like approach to age estimation.

records.title: Dual-view Graph Learning for Multimodal Recommendation
records.abstract: Graph neural networks have exhibited exceptional modeling capabilities in multimodal recommendation tasks. However, existing approaches often directly leverage behavioral graphs or simply construct similarity graphs within individual modalities. Training on such suboptimal graph structures will accelerate the propagation of noise inherent in both behavioral data and multimodal data. To address this limitation, we propose a Dual-View Graph Learning framework for multimodal recommendation (DVGL). Specifically, to achieve more robust graph structures, we devise two ingenious graph learning modules for behavioral and modality views respectively. Subsequently, we employ a two-stage feature purification strategy within each modality, fully leveraging multimodal information to further refine the embedding representations. Finally, multilevel contrastive learning tasks are employed to enforce consistency between behavioral and modality features. Experimental results on three real-world public datasets demonstrate the superior performance of our proposed method.

records.title: Mutual Information-Based Multimodal Partitioning Combination Clustering for Cluster Number Determination
records.abstract: Multimodal clustering has emerged as a fundamental technique for discovering latent structures within multimodal data. However, two critical challenges remain unsolved: how to effectively leverage cross-modal consistency for clustering, and how to automatically determine the optimal number of clusters without prior knowledge. To address these problems, we propose Multimodal Partitioning Combination Clustering (MPCC). Specifically, we introduce a partitioning combination scheme that considers each modality as a super-dimension, define normalized intra-modal mutual information to measure the structural consistency within each modality, and inter-modal mutual information to quantify cross-modal agreement between clustering assignments. Based on these metrics, we design a decision graph mechanism that uses MI gains to automatically determine the optimal number of clusters without any prior knowledge. Comprehensive experiments on five multimodal benchmark datasets demonstrate that MPCC outperforms nine baseline methods in cluster number estimation. Our approach provides a principled solution for automatically determining the number of clusters in multimodal scenarios.

records.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation for Multi-Model Architectures Lithography Hotspot Detection
records.abstract: As a special type of multimedia data, Lithography Hotspot Detection (LHD) training often requires stronger privacy protection than conventional multimedia data, and federated learning provides a promising potential solution to this challenge. However, existing approaches rely solely on either parameter aggregation or Knowledge Distillation (KD), failing to fully exploit the potential of collaborative learning. To address this, we propose FedKD-hybrid, a novel framework that synergizes the strengths of both paradigms. Specifically, FedKD-hybrid utilizes a public dataset to facilitate consensus, where clients exchange both parameters of agreed-upon layers and logits. This hybrid information is aggregated to refine local models, enhancing knowledge transfer. Extensive experiments on ICCAD-2012 and real-world FAB datasets demonstrate that FedKD-hybrid consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both effectiveness and robustness.

records.title: Neural Architecture Search for Class-Incremental Learning in Medical Image Analysis
records.abstract: Medical multi-label class-incremental learning (CIL) requires models to incorporate newly introduced disease categories while preserving previously learned knowledge under missing annotations and severe label imbalance. Existing methods typically rely on fixed network architectures combined with regularization or rehearsal strategies, which limits their effectiveness as class distributions evolve across incremental stages. This paper presents a neural architecture search (NAS) framework for medical multi-label CIL that focuses on task-critical architectural modules rather than the entire backbone network. The proposed approach searches over lightweight components related to label correlation modeling and knowledge distillation in a stage-wise manner, while keeping the backbone fixed to ensure efficiency and reproducibility. A class-incremental-aware search objective is employed during architecture selection to balance new-class learning and old-class knowledge preservation. Experiments conducted under standard class-incremental protocols on public medical imaging datasets demonstrate that the proposed NAS-driven method consistently improves average accuracy and reduces forgetting compared with representative regularization-based and rehearsal-based baselines.

records.title: Feedback Guided Interactive Multimodal Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis
records.abstract: The Joint Multimodal Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (JMASA) task aims to extract aspects and their sentiment polarities from multimodal inputs in an end-to-end manner. Existing JMASA methods have achieved impressive results on public datasets. However, their strong dependence on automatic aspect extraction and sentiment identification restricts user intervention, as users cannot explicitly influence how the model detects aspects of interest or analyzes the corresponding sentiments. To address this issue, this paper proposes an interactive JAMSA framework, namely interactive feedback guidance model (IFGM), which incorporates simulated user feedback to guide the model in extracting user-desired aspects and identifying their corresponding sentiments. Specifically, the framework allows users to mark missing and incorrect aspects and then leverages a token-level guidance interaction strategy to prompt the model to focus on the aspects marked by the user. Extensive experiments have proven the effectiveness of our interactive method.

records.title: FedUAF: Uncertainty-Aware Fusion with Reliability-Guided Aggregation for Multimodal Federated Sentiment Analysis
records.abstract: Multimodal sentiment analysis in federated learning environments faces significant challenges due to missing modalities, heterogeneous data distributions, and unreliable client updates. Existing federated approaches often struggle to maintain robust performance under these practical conditions. In this paper, we propose FedUAF, a unified multimodal federated learning framework that addresses these challenges through uncertainty-aware fusion and reliability-guided aggregation. FedUAF explicitly models modality-level uncertainty during local training and leverages client reliability to guide global aggregation, enabling effective learning under incomplete and noisy multimodal data. Extensive experiments on CMU-MOSI and CMU-MOSEI demonstrate that FedUAF consistently outperforms state-of-the-art federated baselines across various missing-modality patterns and Non-IID settings. Moreover, FedUAF exhibits superior robustness against noisy clients, highlighting its potential for real-world multimodal federated applications.

records.title: FedDSC: Federated Dynamic Subspace Clustering for Efficient and Generalizable LVLM Fine-tuning
records.abstract: Federated fine-tuning of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) enables privacy-preserving adaptation but is severely hindered by statistical heterogeneity. Naive global aggregation ignores the underlying shifts in client data distributions, causing destructive interference among parameters updated in conflicting directions. Although prior works attempt to mitigate this via parameter decoupling or expert routing, they neglect the fundamental impact of data distribution on optimization trajectory. Therefore, we propose FedDSC, a Federated Dynamic Subspace Clustering framework that aligns optimization directions by grouping clients with similar update subspaces. By integrating Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) with Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), FedDSC efficiently extracts principal subspaces to characterize client-specific optimization directions. Furthermore, we construct a dynamic bottom-up hierarchical clustering tree, where a global proximal constraint regularizes cluster-wise optimization to maintain global generalization. Extensive experiments on general and medical fields demonstrate that FedDSC consistently outperforms state-of-the-art federated fine-tuning methods under diverse heterogeneity settings.

records.title: QoS-Aware Token Scheduling and Private Data Valuation for Multi-Modal Agentic Networks
records.abstract: In agentic systems, human-generated data records anchor the value of AI services. Yet cloud compute pipelines centralize processing on remote servers. Data centralization reduces personal data sovereignty and may potentially degrade the quality of service (QoS). Meanwhile, user contributions are diverse in quantity and quality: decentralized records can be biased, noisy, and heterogeneously distributed. To address the data challenge, we study fair token allocation and private data valuation for decentralized and resource-constrained agentic systems. Our approach embeds multi-modal representations in a shared semantic space and releases differentially private (DP) prototypes to preserve utility while reducing semantic leakage. With the DP guarantee, we design a fair token allocation scheme that rewards effective contributions and remains robust to data heterogeneity and AI resource scarcity. Extensive simulations demonstrate improved contribution-based fairness and QoS compared to standard benchmarks. The improved resistance to image reconstruction attacks indicates enhanced privacy for multi-modal personal data.

records.title: DIAL:A Distributed Inference Framework for Adaptive Partitioning and Layer-skipping VLM on Edge Multimedia Devices
records.abstract: With the application of Visual Language Model (VLM) in video and image understanding, classification, and labeling, implementing offline inference on home multimedia devices is an effective protection for data privacy. Due to limited computing resources, traditional multimedia devices can’t run VLM independently. Fortunately, distributed inference on heterogeneous edge multimedia devices provide a good solution. However, factors such as fluctuating network bandwidth and device load make real-time decision-making for model partitioning of VLM challenging. To address these challenges, this paper introduces DIAL, a distributed inference framework for VLM tailored for edge multimedia devices. Specifically, this framework adaptively partitions VLM based on dynamic environmental factors and offloads the partitions to heterogeneous edge multimedia devices for collaborative inference. The experimental results indicate that, compared to the full edge inference method, DIAL reduces total latency by 44.6% under varying device loads while retaining 95.2% of full benchmark performance.

records.title: Exploring World Transitions via 3D Occupancy World Model
records.abstract: Occupancy world models have emerged as a pivotal paradigm for autonomous systems to perceive and predict the evolution of complex 3D environments. Recent advances leverage GPT-like autoregressive and diffusion-based architectures to forecast future occupancy from historical observations. Despite their success, these approaches struggle to capture heterogeneous motion correlations of surrounding scenes due to the entanglement of ego-motion and scene dynamics, leading to severe scene degradation in long-term predictions. We present OccTrans, a novel 3D occupancy world transitions modeling framework that explicitly decouples ego-motion states from token-level dynamics. Our approach introduces a temporal warping module that applies ego-pose transformations to align tokens from previous frames into the coordinate of the current frame, effectively isolating vehicle motion. A dynamic world model then predicts residual token-level dynamics induced by moving objects and structural variations. This disentangled formulation mitigates cumulative errors, preserves scene consistency, and improves prediction fidelity. Evaluations on the Occ3D-nuScenes benchmark demonstrate that OccTrans achieves substantial improvements over state-of-the-art methods while maintaining efficiency. Moreover, OccTrans exhibits strong capability in generating coherent 3D occupancy sequences.

records.title: CORE: Collaborative Observer-Reasoner Execution via Multi-Agents for Smart Home
records.abstract: The integration of Large Language Model (LLM) has significantly advanced the development of smart home assistants via single-agent paradigms. However, due to the lack of real-time perception of the physical environment, LLMs are prone to serious grounding illusions and often face cognitive overload problems in complex mixed instruction scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose Collaborative Observer-Reasoner Execution (CORE), a novel framework featuring a hierarchical architecture via multi-agents. Specifically, a collaborative input observation layer decouples high-entropy instructions into orthogonal atomic intents and structured graphs to mitigate cognitive load. Subsequently, an adversarial game reasoning layer introduces a "proposer-verifier" loop based on Nash equilibrium to force semantic outputs onto the physically feasible manifold. Extensive experiments on large-scale datasets including SAGE and HomeBench demonstrate that CORE achieves significant improvements in complex instruction grounding accuracy and strict physical consistency compared to existing baselines.

records.title: EMOS: Efficient Multi-Output Aerodynamic Surrogates for Rapid Vehicle Design Iteration
records.abstract: Automotive aerodynamic design requires accurate prediction of both global aerodynamic metrics (e.g., drag coefficient Cd) and local surface fields (e.g., pressure and wall shear stress). Existing surrogates often focus on only one output, limiting their usefulness for rapid design iteration. We present EMOS, an efficient multi-output Transformer that predicts Cd and dense surface fields from 3D vehicle geometry in a single forward pass. EMOS combines a physics-guided mixture-of-experts, scalable local attention for large surfaces, and geometry-aware position encoding for fine-grained shape sensitivity. On three industrial datasets, EMOS reduces drag error by 12% and improves local-field accuracy by 16% over strong single-task baselines, while achieving 1s inference per vehicle on a single GPU---orders of magnitude faster than CFD.

records.title: Fed-D3GS: Physics-Informed and Dictionary-Guided Federated 3D Gaussian Splatting for Low-Dose CT Slice Reconstruction
records.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a promising privacy-preserving paradigm for Low-Dose CT (LDCT) denoising. However, existing FL frameworks primarily address statistical heterogeneity while overlooking the severe physical heterogeneity arising from diverse scanner geometries and dose levels across medical centers. Consequently, standard implicit representations (e.g., CNNs) suffer from catastrophic client drift, failing to generalize to worst-case clients with extreme degradations. To address this, we propose Fed-D3GS, a novel physics-informed federated framework that leverages 3D Gaussian Splatting for robust CT reconstruction. Unlike grid-based approaches that couple geometry with texture, Fed-D3GS explicitly models the 3D anatomical structure, enabling coherent aggregation of geometric features. Specifically, we introduce a Dual-Domain Consistency mechanism that enforces constraints in both projection and image domains to bridge the domain gap caused by sparse views. Extensive experiments on the AAPM-Mayo dataset under a physically-driven non-IID partition demonstrate that Fed-D3GS significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Notably, on the most challenging client (5×10^3 photons, 180 views), our method achieves a +2.65 dB improvement over physics-guided FL methods, effectively removing streak artifacts while preserving high-frequency trabecular details.

records.title: SME-VIS: Structure-aware and Memory-Enhanced Video Instance Segmentation for Echocardiography
records.abstract: Accurate segmentation of anatomical structures in echocardiography is crucial for cardiac function assessment. Video instance segmentation (VIS) enables end-to-end segmen tation and cross-frame tracking without first-frame annotation. However, blurred boundaries, speckle noise, and anatomical deformations from cardiac motion pose challenges for adapting VIS to this domain. We propose SME-VIS, a structure-aware memory-enhanced framework for accurate and robust echocar diography segmentation. We design a dual-branch semantic structure decoupling (DB-SSD) module, where the semantic branch models spatial location and appearance, and the multi scale structure-aware perception (MSP) branch extracts bound ary features to enhance boundary perception. The temporal gated memory unit (TGMU) encodes cardiac cycle patterns via LSTM and computes temporal gating weights to adjust atten tion distribution during memory reading. Experiments on the CAMUS dataset demonstrate that SME-VIS achieves superior segmentation performance.

records.title: CoDehazeNet: An End‑to‑End Collaborative Network for Global-to-Local Remote Sensing Image Dehazing
records.abstract: Remote sensing imagery is crucial for Earth observation tasks, yet spatially non-uniform haze frequently compromises its visual quality and interpretability. To address this, coarse-to-fine or dual-branch strategies have gained attention for their potential to balance global structure restoration and local detail recovery. However, effectively coordinating these stages to avoid artifacts remains a challenge. Inspired by the human visual system’s collaborative processing—specifically the interplay between the Magnocellular and Parvocellular pathways—we propose CoDehazeNet, an end-to-end collaborative global-to-local network. CoDehazeNet mimics this biological mechanism by decoupling restoration into parallel feature extraction and structure-guided integration. In the extraction stage, a low-resolution Global Structure Restorer (GSR) simulates the Magnocellular pathway to capture atmospheric degradation and yield a pixel-wise confidence map, while a full-resolution U-shaped backbone (CoDehaze-U) acts as the Parvocellular counterpart to preserve fine-grained representations. In the integration stage, a Detail Texture Refiner (DTR) employs Conditional Spatial Residual Compensation (CSRC). Guided by the confidence map, CSRC adaptively modulates the fusion of these streams, selectively replenishing missing texture details in haze-impacted regions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CoDehazeNet surpasses state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative accuracy and visual quality. Code is available at: https://github.com/Aaronwangz/CoDehazeNet.

records.title: TUGS: Physics-based Compact Representation of Underwater Scenes by Tensorized Gaussian
records.abstract: Underwater 3D scene reconstruction is crucial for multimedia applications in adverse environments, such as underwater robotic perception and navigation. However, the complexity of interactions between light propagation, water medium, and object surfaces poses significant difficulties for existing methods in accurately simulating their interplay. Additionally, expensive training and rendering costs limit their practical application. Therefore, we propose Tensorized Underwater Gaussian Splatting (TUGS), a compact underwater 3D representation based on physical modeling of complex underwater light fields. TUGS includes a physics-based underwater Adaptive Medium Estimation (AME) module, enabling accurate simulation of both light attenuation and backscatter effects in underwater environments, and introduces Tensorized Densification Strategies (TDS) to efficiently refine the tensorized representation during optimization. TUGS is able to render high-quality underwater images with faster rendering speeds and less memory usage. Extensive experiments on real-world underwater datasets have demonstrated that TUGS can efficiently achieve superior reconstruction quality using a limited number of parameters. The code is available at https://liamlian0727.github.io/TUGS

records.title: RAVSTORM: Region-Aware Video Super-Resolution Transformer for Real-World Motion Blur
records.abstract: Real-world video super-resolution (VSR) remains challenging due to complex degradations and the difficulty of exploiting long-range temporal cues, especially under motion blur—a frequent artifact in low-quality videos. Directly propagating artifact-free features across frames for reconstruction is particularly unreliable in such conditions. To address this, we introduce RAVSTORM, a region-aware VSR Transformer for real-world motion blur. It features a clear-region estimator for accurate blur localization and a double-branch Transformer that separately processes blurred and clean features. A center-oriented spatio-temporal shifted 3D alignment module captures long-term context, while a refinement module further improves blur detection. RAVSTORM achieves state-of-the-art results on real-world motion-blurred VSR datasets, while maintaining acceptable computational efficiency.

records.title: BEV-CMF: Bird's-Eye-View-Based Cross-Modal Radar-Camera Fusion for 3D Object Detection
records.abstract: Reliable perception is critical for safe autonomous driving. While fusing radar point clouds with camera images is a promising path to enhance robustness, existing 3D detection methods still struggle with missing critical obstacles. To address this gap, we propose a Bird's-Eye-View-based cross-modal fusion framework fusing the radar with camera for 3D object detection, named BEV-CMF, which is a three-stage BEV processing pipeline that: 1) enriches the complete BEV features after initial sensor fusion; 2) focuses on false-positive objects and hierarchically aggregates true-positive objects based on the inheritance mechanism; and 3) refines features via query iteration. Our BEV-CMF approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on the nuScenes benchmark, with 47.6% mAP and 56.7% NDS for 3D object detection, significantly improving recall and precision for safer navigation in complex scenarios.

records.title: JSTSSM-RAWVSR: Joint Spatial-Temporal State Space Model-based RAW2RGB Video Super-Resolution
records.abstract: Performing video super-resolution (VSR) in the RAW domain offers advantages in information preservation and dynamic range over RGB-based approaches. However, RAW-to-RGB (RAW2RGB) VSR remains challenging due to the difficulty of fully exploiting RAW representations and jointly modeling spatial–temporal information flows. To address these challenges, we propose JSTSSM-RAWVSR, a lightweight framework based on a visual Mamba architecture. Our method fully leverages RAW information by jointly modeling two complementary modalities, Bayer and RGGB. We introduce transposed-attention-based cross state space modules for effective cross-modality interaction, and a joint spatial–temporal state space module for efficient long-range video sequence modeling. In addition, an RGB channel-aware gradient-weighted loss is designed to suppress color noise. Extensive experiments demonstrate that JSTSSM-RAWVSR achieves state-of-the-art performance with the computational complexity comparable to the lightest models.

records.title: Towards Energy-Efficient Multimedia Applications via Bio-Inspired Sparse Spiking Neural Networks
records.abstract: Multimedia applications such as dynamic vision recognition and video analysis require temporal modeling and energy efficiency, while spiking neural networks (SNNs) with inherent event-driven processing and low power consumption are naturally suitable for these scenarios. However, the limited information capacity of binary spikes forces SNNs to rely on dense spike activity to maintain information precision, resulting in redundant computation and undermining energy efficiency. In this paper, we propose a Sparse Spiking Neural Network (SparseSNN), drawing inspiration from biological mechanisms to achieve a better balance between performance and energy efficiency. Inspired by quantal synaptic failures, we introduce a spatially correlated spike sparsification mechanism that emulates the probabilistic nature and spatial dependencies of synaptic transmission. This mechanism effectively suppresses redundant spikes and reduces computational overhead. We also design an adaptive excitability modulation strategy that dynamically adjusts neuronal firing thresholds. This enhances neural heterogeneity and maintain network performance. Extensive experiments on diverse multimedia benchmarks validate the effectiveness of SparseSNN. The results show that our method achieves substantial improvements in both energy efficiency and accuracy. In particular, SparseSNN reduces energy consumption by up to 53.97% and improves accuracy by 4.16% on the DVS128 Gesture, demonstrating its potential for energy-efficient multimedia applications.

records.title: Cognitive Immunity Multi-Modal Agent: Embodied Robustness via Adversarial Graph Reasoning
records.abstract: The deployment of Vision Language Action models in adversarial physical environments reveals critical vulnerabilities to semantic perturbations that corrupt attention mechanisms. To address this fragility we propose Cognitive Immunity as a bio-inspired framework formulating embodied robustness through a unified bi-level optimization game involving three specialized agents. An Immune Orchestrator dynamically eliminates non-causal nodes using an Adversarial Information Bottleneck while an Endogenous Adversary drives structural evolution. Simultaneously a Homeostatic Actuator employs active geometric consistency for perceptual verification. Extensive experiments on Hiwonder robot demonstrate that our approach maintains a 92.4% success rate under severe physical attacks and achieves an 85.4% success rate for zero shot transfer from simulation to reality. These findings establish that robust generalizability emerges from the structural refinement of cognitive graphs driven by internal adversarial dynamics.

records.title: GEAR: Graph-enhanced Anchoring and Reasoning Orchestration for Multimodal Intent Recognition
records.abstract: Multimodal Intent Recognition (MIR) is crucial for understanding human goals in dialogue systems by integrating linguistic, acoustic, and visual signals. Despite recent advancements, existing methods face two fundamental challenges: (1) Semantic-agnostic fusion, where non-verbal modalities are not explicitly aligned with textual semantics, resulting in modality interference instead of complementarity; and (2) Limited structured reasoning, where models fail to capture the structural dependencies between utterances and intent labels, as well as the fine-grained contextual cues necessary for handling complex scenarios.To address these challenges we propose Graph-enhanced Anchoring and Reasoning Orchestration(GEAR), a unified framework of three complementary modules. First, the hierarchical semantic alignment module anchors cross-modal fusion on text semantics and refines local details for hierarchical consistency. Second, the graph-guided semantic enhancement module models joint text-label dependencies with graph encoding and contrastive learning to strengthen semantic representation and robustness. Finally, fine-grained multimodal reasoning orchestration leverages multimodal large language models to generate intermediate reasoning content, fused through label-aware gating and cross-attention for fine-grained intent reasoning. Extensive experiments on the MIntRec and MELD-DA benchmarks demonstrate that GEAR systematically reduces semantic misalignment and improves structured reasoning, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

records.title: Neuro-Causal Drive: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Long-Horizon and Interpretable Traffic Accident Analysis
records.abstract: Automated analysis of traffic accidents from long-horizon video faces computational bottlenecks and interpretabil-ity challenges. Existing end-to-end models struggle with minute-long contexts and conflate correlation with causation. We propose Neuro-Causal Drive, a neuro-symbolic framework that decouples perception from reasoning through a three-stage pipeline: (1) per-ception via tracking and segmentation, (2) symbolic abstractionusing a novel Traffic Event Domain-Specific Language (DSL) toencode spatio-temporal events, and (3) causal reasoning via LLM-guided Structural Causal Models with counterfactual verification.Experiments show our method reduces token consumption bytwo orders of magnitude while achieving superior accuracy and interpretability compared to state-of-the-art baselines. The framework generates regulation-aligned accident reports suitable for liability attribution.

records.title: Cloud-Edge-Terminal Collaborative Unsupervised Visual Enhancement System for Coal Mine Monitoring
records.abstract: With the deepening advancement of intelligent coal mine construction, high-quality video surveillance is pivotal for ensuring underground production safety. However, the pervasive conditions of low illumination, uneven lighting, and high dust density severely constrain the perception capabilities of machine vision systems. Existing low-light enhancement algorithms struggle to balance restoration quality with computational efficiency: high-precision deep learning models are too computationally expensive for resource-constrained underground terminals, while purely cloud-based processing faces bottlenecks in bandwidth consumption and transmission latency. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Cloud-Edge-Terminal collaborative unsupervised low-light image enhancement method. Adopting a Split Computing strategy, the proposed method designs differentiated model structures tailored to heterogeneous computing nodes, achieving a synergy between enhancement performance and inference efficiency. Specifically, at the Terminal side, a lightweight texture feature enhancement module is deployed to preprocess image details via guided filtering; At the cloud side, leveraging massive computing resources to build a logarithmic adaptive brightness adjustment network, utilizing unsupervised learning to enhance illumination while maintaining color consistency through shared parameters; At the edge side, achieving low-latency saturation adjustment and multi-scale exposure fusion to effectively suppress local overexposure and optimize overall visual perception. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system not only outperforms 11 state-of-the-art algorithms in brightness balance, detail recovery, and color fidelity but also significantly reduces network latency and terminal computational burden, providing a real-time and efficient solution for intelligent monitoring in coal mines.

records.title: A Comprehensive Review of Multimodal Facial State Analysis: Tasks, Methods, and Resources
records.abstract: Facial state analysis plays a crucial role in understanding human expressions, psychological modeling, and human–computer interaction. Traditional unimodal vision-based methods are often limited by environmental sensitivity and weak interpretability. Multimodal facial state analysis addresses these issues by integrating complementary cues from visual, audio, textual, physiological, and other related modalities. This survey emphasizes two key aspects: on one hand, multimodal learning enables contextual semantic understanding for improved facial state reasoning and leverages interpretable language generation to enhance model explainability; on the other hand, multi-task learning allows simultaneous analysis of expressions, action units (AUs), and face-based soft biometrics (e.g., age, gender), effectively capturing fine-grained expressions and improving cross-scene generalization. This survey reviews core tasks, representative methods, and datasets in multimodal facial state analysis, focusing on facial expression recognition, AU detection, and face-based soft biometric estimation, and emphasizing the unique value of language in providing contextual semantics, enhancing reasoning, and generating explanations. The survey aims to provide an up-to-date overview of the literature and to highlight future research directions for multimodal, interpretable, and multi-task adaptive facial state analysis.

records.title: A Multimodal Fusion Network with Cross-Attention and Self-Adaption Gating for 3D Human Pose Estimation
records.abstract: 3D human pose estimation is essential for virtual reality, robotics, rehabilitation, gaming, and emerging domains involving affective–cognitive understanding of human behavior. Visual-based approaches often struggle with accuracy and robustness under occlusion, while the simple concatenation of IMU and vision signals neglects their distinct temporal and structural characteristics. We present a multimodal fusion network that explicitly models three modalities—3D visual joints, IMU acceleration, and IMU rotation. Each modality is encoded by a dedicated RNN stream to capture modality-specific motion patterns. A cross-modal interactive attention module then facilitates effective information exchange, and a gated fusion mechanism adaptively integrates complementary cues into a unified motion representation. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method achieves superior accuracy and robustness, particularly in challenging conditions, highlighting the advantages of hierarchical multimodal fusion for real-time human motion and behavior understanding.

records.title: Decentralized Personalized Federated Learning with Dynamic Graph Collaboration for Healthcare
records.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables privacy-preserving collaborative training but is constrained by centralized server bottlenecks and the limited capacity of a single global model to accommodate client heterogeneity. Decentralized Personalized Federated Learning (DPFL) alleviates these issues by enabling peer-to-peer collaboration for locally tailored model training. However, DPFL performance is often undermined by statistical heterogeneity, particularly severe label distribution skew. To address these limitations, we propose FedDyG, a novel framework that constructs a dynamic collaboration graph to integrate structural alignment with temporal adaptability. Specifically, FedDyG initializes a distribution-aware topology that prioritizes connections based on inherent cross-client data consistency. It then introduces dynamic neighbor reweighting that continuously calibrates interaction strengths through local pseudo-validation, ensuring neighbor contributions accurately reflect their instantaneous model utility. Finally, knowledge distillation transfers peer knowledge to enhance local performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FedDyG substantially outperforms existing DPFL approaches under extreme heterogeneity while effectively mitigating intra-client cross-class fairness issues.

records.title: Exploring the Integration of Specialized Tool Knowledge with MLLMs for Emotion Recognition
records.abstract: Image emotion recognition aims to automatically identify human emotional states explicitly or implicitly conveyed in visual content. While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have advanced this field, their reliance on static internal representations may hinder reasoning adaptability in complex scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Tool-based Emotion Reasoning and Acting Agent (TERAA). By simulating human expert, our framework incorporates three complementary tools: a color-tone tool for visual atmosphere, a humanistic background tool for cultural context, and a visual aesthetics tool for subjective perception. Furthermore, we introduce an adaptive prompt strategy enabling the MLLM to dynamically balance internal knowledge with external tool invocation based on reasoning uncertainty. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly surpasses traditional Chain-of-Thought methods in Zeroshot scenario, while substantially enhancing the interpretability and transparency of the emotion reasoning process. Code is available at https://github.com/ikun404ikun/TERAA.

records.title: PALM-AD: Prototype Aggregation and Learnable Medical Prompts for Anomaly Detection
records.abstract: Rapid advancements in vision-language models like CLIP have enabled robust zero-shot anomaly detection (ZSAD). However, current research largely focuses on industrial inspec- tion, where defects are typically structural and conspicuous. Transferring these paradigms to medicine is challenged by the subtle nature of clinical lesions and the semantic inadequacy of generic prompts. To bridge this gap, we present PALM- AD, a framework that adapts frozen VLMs to medical anomaly detection via lightweight tuning. Specifically, deviating from static templates, we employ learnable text prompts to explicitly capture the nuanced semantics of medical normality and abnormality. Additionally, to better capture sparse lesion cues that are scat- tered across layers, we introduce Multi-layer Informative Patch Aggregation (MIPA). Evaluated under a strict zero-shot leave- one-out protocol, PALM-AD is trained on non-target datasets and generalizes directly to held-out targets. It outperforms strong baselines across ten datasets, achieving dataset-wise averages of 84.32% image AUROC (over the six datasets with image-level labels) and 92.32% pixel AUROC (over the seven datasets with lesion masks).

records.title: Reliable Depth-Aware Camouffaged Object Detection
records.abstract: Camouflaged object detection (COD) is highly challenging due to the intrinsic similarity between objects and their surroundings. Inspired by human binocular vision, depth cues offer complementary geometry beyond RGB appearance. However, existing RGB-D methods often assume reliable depth and overlook modality imbalance, leading to noisy or overconfident predictions. To address these issues, a reliable depth-aware network (RDANet) is proposed. First, a modality distribution consistency modeling is designed, where prior and posterior distributions are aligned in the latent space to quantify uncertainty and suppress unstable predictions. Then, a semantic consistency modality fusion strategy is introduced to adaptively downweights unreliable depth while enhancing consistent regions. Finally, an efficient structural cue enhancement module is constructed, in which uncertainty is incorporated into linear attention to achieve precise boundary modeling. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods, underscoring the importance of depth reliability modeling for robust COD.

records.title: Reliability-Guided Gradient Correction for Visible-Infrared Object Detection
records.abstract: Visible-infrared object detection benefits from complementary modality information, but remains vulnerable to semantic conflicts caused by inconsistent object representations across modalities. Existing works typically address this by feature alignment or modality reweighting. However, these methods often suffer from unreliable features learned by the model, which can mislead the fusion process and impair overall performance. To address this, we propose a reliability-guided gradient correction method (RaGrad) that promotes reliable feature learning, thereby alleviating semantic conflicts. Specifically, to assess the reliability of modality features, we design the reliability estimation via parameter attribution (REPA) module. The REPA module estimates reliability by quantifying parameter effectiveness via counterfactual reasoning and parameter sensitivity via gradient variation. Additionally, we devise the reliability-guided conflict resolution (RGCR) module, which resolves cross-modal conflicts by correcting the gradients of less reliable modalities under the guidance of more reliable ones. The RGCR module promotes the learning of more reliable features and enhances cross-modal consistency. Extensive experiments on three challenging datasets demonstrate the efficacy and generality of RaGrad.

records.title: Cross-Modal Heterogeneous Prototype Alignment and Consistency for Few-Shot 3D Point Cloud Segmentation
records.abstract: Few-shot 3D point cloud segmentation targets novel classes with only a handful of labeled samples, but remains difficult due to sparse geometry, diverse structures, and weak cross-episode generalization. Existing prototype-based approaches often overlook the heterogeneity between geometric cues and semantic priors, and their support--query relations can be unstable under label scarcity. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Cross-modal Heterogeneous Prototype Alignment and Consistency for few-shot 3D point cloud segmentation, CHPAC. First, we propose cross-modal heterogeneous prototype alignment and adaptive fusion, which aligns geometric and semantic prototypes and dynamically weights their contributions to improve discriminability and transferability across tasks. Second, we propose heterogeneous graph relation consistency to preserve structural relations between support and query sets across episodes, stabilizing relational reasoning. Experiments on standard few-shot point cloud segmentation benchmarks show significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods.
