records.title: Density-Guided Adaptive Query Allocation with Boundary Refinement for UAV Object Detection
records.abstract: Tiny-object detection in UAV imagery is challenging due to severe foreground--background imbalance and spatially non-uniform object distributions. Although end-to-end Transformer detectors enable NMS-free set prediction, a fixed query set is suboptimal under strong density variation, yielding redundant background hypotheses and missed detections in object-dense areas. Moreover, close-proximity instances exacerbate boundary ambiguity and increase confusion among neighbouring instances. To address these issues, we propose Boundary–Density Aware DETR (BDA-DETR) for UAV tiny-object detection under highly heterogeneous object densities. BDA-DETR predicts a fine-grained density map to guide image-adaptive query cardinality and density-aware query selection, focusing decoding on informative regions while reducing background redundancy. In addition, an auxiliary boundary-aware refinement strengthens fine-scale boundary cues to improve localisation in crowded regions .Extensive experiments demonstrate that BDA-DETR achieves strong performance, with +3.1 AP on VisDrone2019-DET and +13.8 AP on UAVVaste over a strong DETR-style baseline.

records.title: Camera-Aware Cross-View Alignment for Referring 3D Gaussian Splatting Segmentation
records.abstract: Referring 3D Gaussian Splatting Segmentation (R3DGS) aims to ground free-form language queries in 3D Gaussian fields. However, existing methods rely on single-view pseudo supervision, leading to viewpoint drift and inconsistent predictions across views. We propose CaRF (Camera-aware Referring Field), a camera-aware cross-view alignment framework for view-consistent referring in 3D Gaussian splatting. CaRF introduces Camera-conditioned Alignment Modulation (CAM) to inject camera geometry into Gaussian-text interactions, and Gaussian-level Cross-view Logit Alignment (GCLA) to explicitly align referring responses of the same Gaussians across calibrated views during training. By turning cross-view discrepancy into an optimizable objective, CaRF enables geometry-aware and view-consistent reasoning directly in the Gaussian space. Extensive experiments on three benchmarks demonstrate that CaRF achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving mIoU by 16.8%, 4.3%, and 2.0% on Ref-LERF, LERF-OVS, and 3D-OVS, respectively. Our code is available at https://github.com/eR3R3/CaRF.

records.title: AudioGS: Spectrogram-Based Audio Gaussian Splatting for Sound Field Reconstruction
records.abstract: Spatial audio is fundamental to immersive virtual experiences, yet synthesizing high-fidelity binaural audio from sparse observations remains a significant challenge. Existing methods typically rely on implicit neural representations conditioned on visual priors, which often struggle to capture fine-grained acoustic structures. Inspired by 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), we introduce AudioGS, a novel visual-free framework that explicitly encodes the sound field as a set of Audio Gaussians based on spectrograms. AudioGS associates each time-frequency bin with an Audio Gaussian equipped with dual Spherical Harmonic (SH) coefficients and a decay coefficient. For a target pose, we render binaural audio by evaluating the SH field to capture directionality, incorporating geometry-guided distance attenuation and phase correction, and reconstructing the waveform. Experiments on the Replay-NVAS dataset demonstrate that AudioGS successfully captures complex spatial cues and outperforms state-of-the-art visual-dependent baselines. Specifically, AudioGS reduces the magnitude reconstruction error (MAG) by over 14% and reduces the perceptual quality metric (DPAM) by approximately 25% compared to the best performing visual-guided method.

records.title: VarRecSplat: 3D Scene Question Answering via Variance Recovery in Gaussian Splatting
records.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting has emerged as a promising approach for interactive 3D scene representation due to its exceptional rendering efficiency and geometric reconstruction capability. Recent advances have extended it to semantic understanding through CLIP-based features for text-based segmentation. However, existing methods remain limited to object-level queries and lack conversational question answering capabilities. To address this, we propose VarRecSplat, an end-to-end framework integrating visual question answering into 3D Gaussian Splatting. Our approach addresses three core challenges: aligning geometric representations with vision language model tokens, compactly representing high dimensional VLM features in scene specific Gaussians, and preserving semantic discriminability during alpha-blending. We design a lightweight semantic feature autoencoder for feature compression while maintaining semantic fidelity, introduce a differentiable channel-wise feature enhancement module to compensate for variance collapse, and adopt a two-stage decoupled training strategy. Experiments demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms baselines while providing detailed semantic responses for natural language questions.

records.title: CoGeo-GS: Concept-Driven and Geometry-Aware Multi-Object Removal in 3D Scenes
records.abstract: Multi-object removal in 3D scenes is challenging due to severe occlusions, semantic entanglement, and the difficulty of maintaining geometric and multi-view consistency. Existing 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) methods perform well for single-object editing but scale poorly to multi-object scenarios, often requiring repetitive optimization and yielding unstable geometry in removed regions. We propose CoGeo-GS, a concept-driven framework for controllable multi-object removal in 3D scenes. CoGeo-GS assigns concept-aware semantic tags to Gaussians, enabling flexible object selection and reducing interference between foreground objects and background structures within a single optimization stage. To recover plausible geometry, we introduce a geometry-aware completion pipeline that combines monocular depth priors with diffusion-based refinement and boundary-aligned blending. A geometry-regularized refinement strategy further stabilizes reconstruction and preserves multi-view consistency. Experiments demonstrate that CoGeo-GS outperforms existing methods in visual quality and reconstruction fidelity.

records.title: EvFlow-GS: Event Enhanced Motion Deblurring with Optical Flow for 3D Gaussian Splatting
records.abstract: Achieving sharp 3D reconstruction from motion blurred images alone becomes challenging, motivating recent methods to incorporate event cameras, benefiting from microsecond temporal resolution. However, they suffer from residual artifacts and blurry texture details due to misleading supervision from inaccurate event double integral priors and noisy, blurry events. In this study, we propose EvFlow-GS, a unified framework that leverages event streams and optical flow to optimize an endto-end learnable double integral (LDI), camera poses, and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) jointly on-the-fly. Specifically, we first extract edge information from the events using optical flow and then formulate a novel event-based loss applied separately to different modules. Additionally, we exploit a novel event-residual prior to strengthen the supervision of intensity changes between images rendered from 3DGS. Finally, we integrate the outputs of both 3DGS and LDI into a joint loss, enabling their optimization to mutually facilitate each other. Experiments demonstrate the leading performance of our EvFlow-GS.

records.title: PSGEN: Planning The Sketch for Common and Uncommon Scenes Generation
records.abstract: Despite impressive advances in text-to-image generation, diffusion models still struggle with complex scene composition, particularly in uncommon scenarios that require faithfully arranging objects in rare or novel spatial configurations. This limitation arises because such scenes are less observed in training data, leading diffusion models to internalize strong priors toward frequent real-world layouts. As a result, they exhibit a pronounced performance gap between commonly and uncommonly composed scenes. To rigorously quantify this gap, we introduce CUBench, a paired benchmark in which each common scene is matched with a semantically relevant yet compositionally novel counterpart. This design enables a fair and controlled evaluation of compositional generalization in text-to-image models. However, bridging this gap is challenging: the distributional shift between training data and uncommon prompts renders coarse control signals (e.g. bounding boxes) insufficient to override the models’ entrenched layout biases. To address this, we propose PSGEN, a training-free framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) to translate input prompts into fine-grained sketch-based conditioning. These sketches explicitly encode object shapes, spatial positions, and object relationships, delivering precise structural guidance that effectively steers diffusion models away from their default priors. Experiments on RFBench and our CUBench demonstrate that PSGEN significantly outperforms existing methods, especially on uncommon prompts. The ablation study further underscore the critical role of LLM-driven semantic understanding and detailed sketch control in uncommon scene synthesis. Code and dataset will be released.

records.title: Fine-Grained Human Pose Editing Assessment via Layer-Selective MLLMs
records.abstract: Abstract—Text-guided human pose editing has gained significant traction in AIGC applications. However,it remains plagued by structural anomalies and generative artifacts. Existing evaluation metrics often isolate authenticity detection from quality assessment, failing to provide fine-grained insights into posespecific inconsistencies. To address these limitations, we introduce HPE-Bench, a specialized benchmark comprising 1,700 standardized samples from 17 state-of-the-art editing models, offering both authenticity labels and multi-dimensional quality scores. Furthermore, we propose a unified framework based on layer-selective multimodal large language models (MLLMs). By employing contrastive LoRA tuning and a novel layer sensitivity analysis (LSA) mechanism, we identify the optimal feature layer for pose evaluation. Our framework achieves superior performance in both authenticity detection and multi-dimensional quality regression, effectively bridging the gap between forensic detection and quality assessment. records.title: AHFAControl: Adaptive Hierarchical Feature Aggregation for Controllable Diffusion Models
records.abstract: Controllable diffusion models introduce trainable condition encoders that accept conditioning images as input to enable spatial control in image generation. However, existing methods still face significant challenges in generation quality and control precision. We identify two key limitations: (1) full-capacity condition encoders are uniformly allocated across all denoising steps, ignoring the distinct capacity requirements of different steps; (2) these condition encoders lack multi-level feature communication, causing loss of crucial structural cues. To address these issues, we propose AHFAControl, which automatically allocates condition encoder capacity across timesteps at runtime, with the optimal allocation strategy identified via evolutionary search. A hierarchical feature aggregation mechanism is also designed to fuse multi-level features from condition encoding blocks before injecting them into the diffusion backbone, providing richer conditional guidance for more precise spatial control. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves significant improvements in both generation quality and control precision with reduced computational costs compared to other competitive methods.

records.title: PersonalQ: Select, Quantize, and Serve Personalized Diffusion Models for Efficient Inference
records.abstract: Personalized text-to-image generation lets users fine-tune diffusion models into repositories of concept-specific checkpoints, but serving these repositories efficiently is difficult for two reasons: natural-language requests are often ambiguous and can be misrouted to visually similar checkpoints, and standard post-training quantization can distort the fragile representations that encode personalized concepts. We present PersonalQ, a unified framework that connects checkpoint selection and quantization through a shared signal—the checkpoint’s trigger token. Check-in performs intent-aligned selection by combining intent-aware hybrid retrieval with LLM-based reranking over checkpoint context and asks a brief clarification question only when multiple intents remain plausible; it then rewrites the prompt by inserting the selected checkpoint’s canonical trigger. Complementing this, Trigger-Aware Quantization(TAQ) applies trigger-aware mixed precision in cross-attention, preserving trigger-conditioned key/value rows (and their attention weights) while aggressively quantizing the remaining pathways for memory-efficient inference. Experiments show that PersonalQ improves intent alignment over retrieval and reranking baselines, while TAQ consistently offers a stronger compression–quality trade-off than prior diffusion PTQ methods, enabling scalable serving of personalized checkpoints without sacrificing fidelity.

records.title: FreeGraftor: Training-Free Cross-Image Feature Grafting for Subject-Driven Text-to-Image Generation
records.abstract: Subject-driven image generation aims to synthesize novel scenes that faithfully preserve subject identity from reference images while adhering to textual guidance. However, existing methods struggle with a critical trade-off between fidelity and efficiency. Tuning-based approaches rely on time-consuming and resource-intensive subject-specific optimization, while zero-shot methods fail to maintain adequate subject consistency. In this work, we propose FreeGraftor, a training-free framework that addresses these limitations through cross-image feature grafting. Specifically, FreeGraftor leverages semantic matching and position-constrained attention fusion to transfer visual details from reference subjects to the generated images. Additionally, our framework introduces a novel noise initialization strategy to preserve the geometry priors of reference subjects, facilitating robust feature matching. Extensive qualitative and quantitative experiments demonstrate that our method enables precise subject identity transfer while maintaining text-aligned scene synthesis. Without requiring model fine-tuning or additional training, FreeGraftor significantly outperforms existing zero-shot and training-free approaches in both subject fidelity and text alignment. Furthermore, our framework can seamlessly extend to multi-subject generation, making it practical for real-world deployment. Our code is available at https://github.com/Nihukat/FreeGraftor.

records.title: HMRNet: Hierarchical Motion Relation Learning for 3D CAD Assemblies
records.abstract: Understanding hierarchical motion relations among parts is crucial for precise interaction and functional reasoning in assembly analysis. However, existing datasets and approaches largely overlook this structural hierarchy, focusing instead on isolated motion prediction or part segmentation. To bridge this gap, we introduce a new benchmark task: hierarchical motion relation prediction in assemblies. To support this task, we construct HR-Motion dataset. The task presents two challenges: (1) the need for hierarchical representation learning at multiple granularity levels, and (2) class imbalance due to the structure of assemblies. To address these challenges, we propose HMRNet, a novel framework for learning hierarchical motion relations. HMRNet mainly includes three modules: solid internal structure modeling, multi-solid structure modeling, and solid relation modeling to learn hierarchical motion relations. A weighted cross-entropy loss handles class imbalance, while a weighted contrastive loss enhances relation feature discriminability. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of our approach.

records.title: Gram-KAC: Gram Polynomials based Kolmogorov-Arnold Convolutions for Class-Incremental Learning
records.abstract: Most existing CNN-based Class-Incremental Learning (CIL) methods suffer from forgetting due to the global weight-sharing mechanism. This mechanism results in non-orthogonal inter-task gradient directions, which cause parameter updates to propagate across all task-specific features, thereby eroding prior task knowledge. To address this issue, this paper leverages the localized adaptation property of Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (KANs) and pioneers the integration of KAN concepts into convolutional architectures for CIL. We first analyze how inter-task gradient directions affect forgetting and reveal that locally supported, orthogonal basis functions can promote gradient orthogonality, mitigating feature interference. Building on these insights, we propose a novel Gram polynomial-based Kolmogorov-Arnold Convolution (Gram-KAC), with regularization terms to disentangle task-specific parameters for continual learning. Extensive experiments across standard and exemplar-free CIL benchmarks demonstrate that replacing conventional convolutions with Gram-KAC consistently improves accuracy while reducing parameter count.

records.title: TARAC: Mitigating Hallucination in LVLMs via Temporal Attention Real-time Accumulative Connection
records.abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities, yet they suffer from hallucinations that limit practical deployment. While various mitigation strategies exist, they often incur high computational overhead or require extensive retraining. In this paper, we address the issue of visual attention decay during generation, a key factor contributing to hallucinations. We propose Temporal Attention Real-time Accumulative Connection (TARAC), a novel training-free framework that dynamically accumulates and re-injects historical attention to sustain visual grounding. Inspired by cognitive reinforcement mechanisms, TARAC operates as a lightweight, plug-and-play module. Extensive experiments across diverse models (e.g., LLaVA, Qwen2-VL) and benchmarks demonstrate that TARAC significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods. Remarkably, it achieves these gains with negligible inference overhead (~4% TPOT increase), compared to the substantial costs of existing training-free baselines. Specifically, TARAC reduces hallucinated sentences by 25.2\% on CHAIR and improves Perception score by +10.65 on MME, validating its effectiveness and efficiency.

records.title: Towards Generalizable Facial Action Unit Detection via Semantic-Aware Regional Context
records.abstract: Facial Action Unit (AU) detection is critical for facial expression analysis but remains challenging in in-the-wild scenarios due to limited training data and subtle, localized muscle movements. Existing methods often rely on dataset-specific statistics or local visual features while overlooking global context. In this paper, we propose SARC-Net, a Semantic-Aware Regional Context Network that improve robustness and generalization across subjects and environments. Specifically, we introduce an Image-Conditioned AU Representation Constructor that initializes AU queries by combining semantic embeddings with global image representations for enhancing generalization capability, and a Region-Aware Cross-Attention Module that aggregates features exclusively from anatomically relevant AU-specific ROIs. Extensive experiments on BP4D and DISFA demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance. More importantly, SARC-Net exhibits superior generalization capabilities on the challenging Aff-Wild2 dataset, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art approaches in cross-dataset evaluations.

records.title: Class-aware Prompt Disentanglement Tuning for Vision-Language Models
records.abstract: Prompt tuning methods via CLIP struggle with the Base-Novel Tradeoff (BNT) challenge, where improving performance on base (target) classes often comes at the cost of reduced accuracy on novel (unseen) classes. To mitigate this, mainstream CoOp-based methods adopt a unified prompt to retain both base-specific and class-general knowledge. However, such a unified prompt inevitably entangles the discriminative patterns of base and novel classes, boosting base-class performance while compromising novel-class accuracy. To address this, we propose Class-aware Prompt disentanglement Tuning (CaPT), a decoupled approach that can be integrated into existing CoOp frameworks to separate class-specific knowledge for base and novel classes. Specifically, CaPT designs two complementary prompts: a class-specific prompt that preserves discriminative cues for base classes, and a class-general prompt that captures transferable semantics generalizing to both base and novel classes. For the class-specific prompt, we introduce a Self-Category Alignment Loss (SCAL) to align the specific prompt with its corresponding base class distribution, ensuring it encodes the category-specific knowledge. For the class-general prompt, we design a Category-Agnostic Regularization (CAR) to encourage a uniform probability distribution over base classes, guiding it to learn shared patterns and preserve novel-class discrimination. In this way, CaPT effectively decouples base and novel knowledge, achieving improved base-class classification while maintaining recognition of novel classes. Extensive experiments validate that CaPT achieves better performance on both base and novel classes compared with the prompt tuning methods and decoupling-oriented methods.

records.title: Unleashing Text Potentials for Text-Video Retrieval
records.abstract: Despite recent advances in text-video retrieval, the full potential of textual information remains unleashed. Existing studies have explored various strategies to enrich text semantics, but most remain confined to the text domain and rely heavily on rule- or model-based imagination. Inspired by diffusion models, we propose TextDiff, which treats text as a source domain and guides its diffusion under visual constraints to bridge the modality gap. Specifically, we first apply continuous diffusion to progressively align text embeddings with the visual domain, refining their representations based on proximity to visual features. We then employ a Cross-Attention Gated Fusion (CAGF) module to integrate the generated features, coupled with an Adaptive Fusion Contrastive Learning (AFCL) strategy to enhance cross-modal alignment. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TextDiff outperforms existing methods on four widely used text-video retrieval benchmarks, with minimal additional computational overhead during inference.

records.title: Improving Few-Shot Change Detection Visual Question Answering via Decision-Ambiguity-guided Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
records.abstract: Change detection visual question answering (CDVQA) requires answering text queries by reasoning about semantic changes in bi-temporal remote sensing images. A straightforward approach is to boost CDVQA performance with generic vision-language models via supervised fine-tuning (SFT). Despite recent progress, we observe that a significant portion of failures do not stem from clearly incorrect predictions, but from decision ambiguity, where the model assigns similar confidence to the correct answer and strong distractors. To formalize this challenge, we define Decision-Ambiguous Samples (DAS) as instances with a small probability margin between the ground-truth answer and the most competitive alternative. We argue that explicitly optimizing DAS is crucial for improving the discriminability and robustness of CDVQA models. To this end, we propose DARFT, a Decision-Ambiguity-guided Reinforcement Fine-Tuning framework that first mines DAS using an SFT-trained reference policy and then applies group-relative policy optimization on the mined subset. By leveraging multi-sample decoding and intra-group relative advantages, DARFT suppresses strong distractors and sharpens decision boundaries without additional supervision. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent gains over specialist methods and SFT baselines, particularly under few-shot settings.

records.title: Semantic-Aligned Poisoning: Stealthy Attacks on Multimodal RAG Systems
records.abstract: With the rapid advancement of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), substantial progress has been achieved in Visual Question Answering (VQA) tasks. However, current MLLMs often generate inaccurate answers due to their lack of up-to-date knowledge. To mitigate this issue, recent research has introduced the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) technique, widely used in Large Language Models (LLMs), to MLLMs. Multimodal RAG enhances the visual reasoning abilities of MLLMs and reduces hallucinations by dynamically retrieving information from external knowledge sources. Nonetheless, the integration of external knowledge also exposes multimodal RAG systems to the risk of knowledge poisoning attacks. In this paper, we propose a novel attack paradigm, named Semantic-Aligned Poisoning (SAP), targeting multimodal RAG systems. SAP injects carefully crafted image-text pairs into multimodal knowledge bases to manipulate the MLLM's responses to specific queries, thereby generating the desired outputs for the attacker. Through extensive experiments across multiple knowledge bases and MLLMs, we demonstrate that SAP outperforms existing methods, achieving an attack success rate of up to 94\% with the injection of only a few malicious image-text pairs. Additionally, we evaluate several commonly used defense strategies, revealing their limitations when confronted with SAP attacks, and highlighting the potential threat they pose to multimodal RAG systems.

records.title: CERTrack: Exploiting Complementary Event Representations for RGBE Tracking
records.abstract: RGBE tracking leverages event cameras to enhance visual object tracking. However, most methods compress events into a single RGB-compatible representation, failing to fully exploit the abundant event information. To mitigate this limitation, we propose CERTrack, which leverages complementary event representations: high-resolution event images for spatial anchors, low-resolution voxels for temporal guides. Specifically, we introduce the Progressive Sparse Aggregator (PSA) to efficiently extract motion priors from voxels. Furthermore, we introduce the Voxel-Guided Evolver (VGE), a gated module that evolves event-image prompts layer-by-layer with voxel-derived motion priors, producing motion-aware prompts injected into the RGB backbone. Our CERTrack achieves state-of-the-art performance on VisEvent and COESOT. Ablation and exploration studies demonstrate the strategy's effectiveness and generalizability.

records.title: Grid-VidLM: Spatial Visual Search for Long Video Multimodal Perception
records.abstract: Vision-language perception in intelligent transportation systems (ITS) involves analyzing complex spatio-temporal dynamics over varying durations, such as continuous monitoring in ground or low-altitude scenarios. However, existing approaches often treat video streams as linear 1D sequences. This sequential scanning method struggles to efficiently capture global temporal structures and incurs high computational costs when processing long-form content. In this work, we introduce Grid-VidLM, a framework that reformulates temporal grounding as a spatial visual search problem. Instead of scanning frames sequentially, Grid-VidLM projects the temporal dimension onto a 2D spatial grid, allowing the agent to perceive the entire event timeline at a glance. This approach leverages the spatial reasoning capabilities of Video-Language Models (VidLMs), enabling intuitive localization of target behaviors and anomalies. Additionally, to tackle the diverse granularity of transportation scenarios, we present a Duration-Aware Dual-Path mechanism that adaptively switches between spatial grid search for global context and direct sequential inference for fine-grained action understanding. Extensive experiments show that Grid-VidLM achieves state-of-the-art performance across distinct benchmarks (MVBench, MLVU, NEXT-QA), consistently outperforming complex agent-based baselines. Our work demonstrates that spatial-temporal projection provides a highly effective and unified interface for robust video reasoning in dynamic environments. Code is available at https://github.com/hanzif1/Grid-VidLM.

records.title: HAA-Fin: A Hierarchical Agentic Architecture for Efficient Multimodal Financial Regulation Parsing
records.abstract: The deployment of large language models (LLMs) in financial verticals is frequently bottlenecked by computational constraints and the strict imperative for zero-defect accuracy. This paper challenges the prevailing scaling law paradigm by introducing HAA-Fin, a resource-efficient and high-precision framework for regulatory compliance. We construct a Hierarchical Agentic Architecture (HAA) that decomposes complex multimodal auditing tasks, such as detecting layout-dependent loan rate violations or identifying illegal advertising claims, into atomic sub-tasks orchestrated by specialized agents including TimeAgent and RuleAgent. By synergizing a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) module with layout-aware hybrid search and re-ranking, we enable 8B-parameter models to rival or even surpass the performance of models with over 32B parameters. Validated on a challenging national-level financial benchmark, our method effectively handles multimodal inputs of text and visual layout. It achieves a significant 20.7% accuracy boost via re-ranking and reduces single-document review time to under 1.5 seconds, demonstrating that orchestrating specialized agents is a superior pathway to scalable industrial AI compared to merely increasing model size.

records.title: Camera Artist: A Multi-Agent Framework for Cinematic Language Storytelling Video Generation
records.abstract: We propose Camera Artist, a multi-agent framework that models a real-world filmmaking workflow to generate narrative videos with explicit cinematic language. While recent multi-agent systems have made substantial progress in automating filmmaking workflows from scripts to videos, they often lack explicit mechanisms to structure narrative progression across adjacent shots and deliberate use of cinematic language, resulting in fragmented storytelling and limited filmic quality. To address this, Camera Artist builds upon established agentic pipelines and introduces a dedicated Cinematography Shot Agent, which integrates recursive storyboard generation to strengthen shot-to-shot narrative continuity and cinematic language injection to produce more expressive, film-oriented shot designs. Extensive quantitative and qualitative results demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms existing baselines in narrative consistency, dynamic expressiveness, and perceived film quality.

records.title: Frequency-aware Neural Representation for Videos
records.abstract: Implicit Neural Representations (INRs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for video compression. However, existing INR-based frameworks typically suffer from inherent spectral bias, which favors low-frequency components and leads to over-smoothed reconstructions and suboptimal rate–distortion performance. In this paper, we propose FaNeRV, a Frequency-aware Neural Representation for videos, which explicitly decouples low- and high-frequency components to enable efficient and faithful video reconstruction. FaNeRV introduces a multi-resolution supervision strategy that guides the network to progressively capture global structures and fine-grained textures through staged supervision . To further enhance high-frequency reconstruction, we propose a dynamic high-frequency injection mechanism that adaptively emphasizes challenging regions. In addition, we design a frequency-decomposed network module to improve feature modeling across different spectral bands. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate that FaNeRV significantly outperforms state-of-the-art INR methods and achieves competitive rate-distortion performance against traditional codecs.

records.title: Evaluating Emotional Accuracy in Facial Text-to-Video Generation
records.abstract: While facial text-to-video (T2V) generation has achieved remarkable progress, current systems often fail to produce expressions that faithfully match the intended emotion in the prompt, and standard evaluation metrics are largely insensitive to such errors. To address these limitations, we propose an evaluation framework that specifically targets emotional accuracy in facial T2V generation. In particular, we construct a controlled dataset by combining 16 emotion categories with diverse prompt templates and character attributes, and generate 900 facial videos using six state-of-the-art T2V models. Each video is rated by human observers on how well its facial expression matches the target emotion, yielding reliable mean opinion scores (MOS). Analysis of this benchmark reveals clear performance disparities across models, relatively high accuracy for basic positive and common negative emotions, and systematic failures on subtle self-conscious emotions. We further find that demographic attributes and prompt phrasing have minimal influence on accuracy, whereas common text--video similarity metrics and facial expression classifiers correlate only weakly with human judgments, highlighting the need for emotion-aware evaluation tools and models.

records.title: PROOFREAD: Bridging the Vision-Language Knowledge Gap via Large Language Models
records.abstract: Knowledge-based visual question answering is a very challenging and widely concerned task. Previous methods adopt the implicit knowledge in large language models (LLM) to achieve excellent results, but we argue that existing methods may suffer from biasing understanding of the image and insufficient knowledge to solve the problem. In this paper, we propose PROOFREAD -PROmpting vision language model with knOwledge From laRgE lAnguage moDel, a novel, lightweight, and efficient knowledge-based VQA framework, which makes the vision language model and the large language model cooperate to give full play to their respective strengths and bootstrap each other. In detail, our proposed method uses LLM to obtain knowledge explicitly, uses the vision language model, which can see the image to get the knowledge answer, and introduces the knowledge perceiver to filter out knowledge that is harmful for getting the correct final answer. Experimental results on two datasets prove the effectiveness of our approach. Our method outperforms all state-of-the-art methods on the A-OKVQA dataset in two settings and also achieves relatively good performance on the OKVQA dataset.

records.title: Lycosidae: Overcoming the Blind Spots of Intrusion Detection Based on Logs and Provenance Graphs
records.abstract: As a recorder of system behavior, system logs can serve as key data for intrusion detection and defense against modern cyberattacks. Provenance graphs enhance causality representation by converting logs into directed graphs. However, log-text models underperform on low-frequency logs, while Graph Neural Networks struggle with high-degree entities. Moreover, unimodal methods fail to simultaneously capture fine-grained log semantics and provenance logic. Therefore, we propose an intrusion detection framework based on multimodal embedding alignment, Lycosidae, which constructs a hierarchically decoupled attention mechanism for complementary semantic-structural enhancement, adopts a dual-stream encoder to extract deep heterogeneous representations, and designs a bidirectional dynamic alignment module to establish global-local correlations. Results show that Lycosidae outperforms state-of-the-art methods across all datasets. Ablation studies validate its key components, offering a novel methodology for detecting complex attack chains.

records.title: Parameter-Efficient Subspace Decoupling ViT for Mitigating Multi-Task Negative Transfer in Histological Scoring
records.abstract: Histological scoring is essential for diagnosing Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD), yet its automation remains challenging due to the high annotation cost and negative transfer among the strongly correlated NAFLD Activity Score (NAS) indicators in multi-task learning. To address this issue, we propose a subspace-decoupled multi-task Vision Transformer (ViT) that integrates lightweight task-specific Adapters with orthogonality-based constraints. This design constructs independent feature subspaces for steatosis, ballooning, and inflammation, effectively reducing task interference while retaining shared representations. We further release a curated multi-task mouse NAFLD histology dataset with expert annotations for all NAS components. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method improves multi-task stability and generalization with substantially reduced computational cost compared to training separate single-task models. The code and the curated dataset have been prepared and will be made publicly available upon acceptance to support reproducibility.

records.title: Causal Dual-Interventional MedVQA via Textual Perturbation and Counterfactual Visual Verification
records.abstract: Medical Visual Question Answering (MedVQA) aims to answer medical questions from clinical images. However, current models often rely on spurious language shortcuts rather than visual evidence, compromising clinical reliability. To this end, we propose a causal dual-interventional framework to mitigate language shortcuts in MedVQA. Our method specifically incorporates two components: a textual interventional module and a counterfactual visual verifier. The textual interventional module disrupts linguistic shortcut biases via concept-agnostic perturbations to block backdoor pathways. Meanwhile, it aligns clinical terms with anatomical regions, compelling the model to establish genuine visual dependencies. In addition, the counterfactual visual verifier evaluates visual reliance by masking key regions and measuring prediction confidence drops under occlusion, thereby reducing language-driven artifacts. Extensive experiments conducted on the two public datasets show that our method significantly outperforms the existing baselines.

records.title: PromptPalm: Textual Prompt Template Substitution for Privacy-Preserving Palmprint Recognition
records.abstract: Palmprint recognition offers reliable biometric authentication but is vulnerable to privacy leakage under feature reconstruction attacks. Existing encryption-based defenses incur high computational costs, while transformation methods struggle to balance privacy and accuracy. To address these issues, we propose PromptPalm, a textual prompt template substitution framework for privacy-preserving palmprint recognition. Specifically, identity-specific textual prompt features, generated from learnable prompts, are utilized to replace visual palmprint templates, effectively impeding visual recovery. To enhance discriminability, the prompt features are aligned with learnable class center proxies during training. Evaluations on four public palmprint datasets show that PromptPalm achieves superior recognition performance while providing effective privacy protection.

records.title: Toward Model-centric Heterogeneous Federated Graph Learning: A Knowledge-driven Approach
records.abstract: Most Federated Graph Learning (FGL) approaches assume homogeneous client models, failing to address Model-centric Heterogeneous FGL (MHtFGL) where GNN architectures and scales vary across organizations. This architectural diversity precludes direct parameter aggregation and disrupts the transfer of topology-dependent structural knowledge to support the collaborative training. We propose FedGKC, a framework introducing a lightweight, architecture-agnostic Copilot Model on each client to bridge heterogeneous representation spaces. FedGKC leverages two key mechanisms: Self-Mutual Knowledge Distillation (SMKD) for bidirectional, topology-aware knowledge exchange between local and Copilot Models, and Knowledge-Aware Model Aggregation (KAMA), which dynamically weights client contributions based on prediction confidence and clarity to optimize global convergence. Extensive evaluations on eight benchmarks demonstrate that FedGKC achieves an average accuracy gain of 3.88% over state-of-the-art MHtFGL baselines.

records.title: FedMETF: Magnitude-adaptive Equiangular Tight Frame for Federated Long-Tail Learning
records.abstract: In real-world applications, federated learning often faces a globally long-tailed label distribution together with highly non-IID local data, which makes existing federated long-tailed methods struggle to learn a stable global model and decision boundaries that are friendly to tail classes. To address this problem, we leverage the geometric insights revealed by neural collapse and propose Federated Magnitude-adaptive Equiangular Tight Frame (FedMETF). It employs a geometric regularizer to encourage all classes to share common feature directions while allowing class-wise feature magnitudes to adapt, and aggregates these magnitudes on the server side to implicitly construct a global class prior. Furthermore, we design a logit adjustment scheme that adaptively mixes this global prior with each client’s local distribution according to their discrepancy, yielding decision boundaries that are both globally stable and tail-class friendly. Experimental results on multiple federated long-tailed benchmarks demonstrate that FedMETF significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of overall accuracy, tail-class performance, and cross-client consistency.

records.title: Sketch-and-Screen: Efficient and Robust One-Bit Federated Compressive Learning
records.abstract: Trustworthy federated learning for multimedia is bandwidth-limited and often involves partially trusted participation, where some clients may transmit malicious updates. Under one-bit communication, the server observes only signs, making magnitude-based defenses less effective. We study robust one-bit federated compressive learning with a unified client–server design. On clients, we embed a learnable one-bit update sketcher into local optimization so that the transmitted signs are aligned with the training dynamics, avoiding post hoc quantization mismatch. On the server, we screen clients using sparse inner products computed on a randomly selected element subset, together with two sign references that capture cross-round stability and within-round consensus. An adaptive gate selects trusted clients, and aggregation is performed only over them. We provide high-probability guarantees for the sparse screening statistics and demonstrate robustness under malicious participation and non-identically distributed data.

records.title: DCAG-Net: Decoupled Coarse–Fine Alignment and Group Encoding for Emotion-Aware Representation Learning
records.abstract: Achieving affective-cognitive understanding is a key goal for next-generation multimodal intelligence, requiring systems that can seamlessly integrate internal physiological experiences with exterior semantic inputs. However, extracting robust, subject-invariant representations from diverse inputs remains a problem, mostly due to the intricacies of synchronizing modality-specific temporal dynamics and addressing diverse cognitive patterns. This article presents DCAG-Net, a framework designed to rectify this discrepancy by decoupled coarse-to-fine alignment and group-aware modeling. DCAG-Net first isolates modality-shared affective semantics from intricate temporal details, subsequently synchronizing them via a hierarchical graph distillation technique. To tackle cross-subject variability, a major obstacle for socially aligned and human-centric multimodal intelligence, we present a group-aware encoder that utilizes latent EEG spectral similarities to enhance personalized cognitive modeling. Experiments on DEAP and MAHNOB-HCI demonstrate that our methodology significantly enhances cross-subject generalization. This study introduces a physiologically grounded and adaptive framework for representation learning, which is essential for creating emotionally sensitive multimodal systems.

records.title: ReGIA: Rethinking Gradient Inversion Attacks via Matrix Extraction Convolution
records.abstract: Federated learning (FL), a prominent distributed learning paradigm, enables multiple clients to privately train a global model by sharing gradients instead of raw data. However, recently emerged gradient inversion attacks (GIAs) can reconstruct clients' raw data from shared gradients, thereby undermining the privacy protection in FL. Existing studies on GIAs remain limited, especially in elucidating their fundamental mechanisms and the key factors that affect reconstruction performance. To address this gap, we propose an innovative method called matrix extraction convolution (MEC), which mathematically transforms the convolution operation into a strictly equivalent linear matrix multiplication by decoupling and reorganizing the convolution process. Building upon MEC, we develop two complementary GIAs. The first closes the research gap in analytical reconstruction for convolutional neural networks (CNNs), whereas the second establishes a tighter upper bound on the reconstruction error of optimization-based GIAs. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed attacks successfully achieve pixel-level reconstruction for CNNs.

records.title: pFedGAT: Personalized Federated Learning via Learning Dynamic Graphs
records.abstract: Personalized Federated Learning (PFL) aims to address data heterogeneity by tailoring models to individual clients. However, many existing aggregation strategies rely on predefined heuristics or static client similarities, which fail to capture task-specific and evolving relationships among clients. To overcome this limitation, we propose \texttt{pFedGAT}, a framework that formulates personalized aggregation as a dynamic graph learning problem. By leveraging a Graph Attention Network (GAT), \texttt{pFedGAT} learns asymmetric inter-client collaboration weights in an end-to-end manner, enabling fine-grained and adaptive model aggregation. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and FashionMNIST under diverse non-IID settings demonstrate that \texttt{pFedGAT} consistently outperforms 12 baselines and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

records.title: Dual-Domain Path-Controllable Deep Unfolding Network for Image Compressed Sensing
records.abstract: Embodied AI systems rely heavily on efficient visual perception for physical interaction. Compressed Sensing (CS), characterized by simultaneous sampling and compression, offers an efficient solution for visual data acquisition in their resource-constrained environments. Recently, Deep Unfolding Networks (DUNs) have demonstrated significant potential in CS, with mainstream research predominantly focusing on enhancing performance through increasingly complex architectures. However, this rigid inference paradigm requires every sampled image to undergo the complete reconstruction process, incurring high computational overhead. To overcome this limitation, we propose the Dual-Domain Path-Controllable Network (DDPC-Net) by integrating a path-control mechanism into a dual-domain optimization framework. This model can selectively activate specific modules within each stage based on image content during inference, significantly reducing computational costs while maintaining high-quality reconstruction.

records.title: GSC-Point: Geometry-Semantics Collaborative Learning for Roadside LiDAR Scene Completion
records.abstract: In this paper, we propose a geometry-semantics collaborative learning approach for roadside LiDAR scene completion (GSC-Point). Conventional methods have shown excellent performance in object-level completion and scene-level completion from ego-vehicle perspective. However, global and refined scenes completion remains major challenges for roadside LiDAR because of severe sparsity. Instead, our GSC-Point balances global scene consistency with local object details. Specifically, the GSC-Point generates explicit supervision signals by near-zero returns for long-range objects. Moreover, we design a geometry-semantics collaborative learning framework with the diffusion model to balance global consistency and local refinement in roadside scene completion. Additionally, we propose a region perception weighted reconstruction loss to optimize the diffusion model training process. Evaluations on the real-world V2X-Seq and TUMTraf-V2X dataset demonstrate that the GSC-Point achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming previous methods with an average reduction of Chamfer Distance by 8.1% and 3D Jensen-Shannon divergence by 3.7%.

records.title: One-to-Two Acting: A Novel Framework for Single-arm Agent Action Expansion to Dual Arms
records.abstract: Dual-arm manipulation can improve throughput via parallel execution, but collecting bimanual demonstrations for training is costly and difficult. We present ExS2D (Extending Single-Arm Agent Actions to Dual Arms), a hierarchical action expansion framework that enables dual-arm manipulation from single-arm supervision. ExS2D first generates structured subtasks according to textual instructions while explicitly capturing their temporal precedence. Then, ExS2D grounds each subtask into executable actions via subtask-guided action mapping in observation. Finally, precedence-aware action allocation and synchronized planning are then performed by an Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) driven coordinator so as to select collision-free dual-arm executions. Simulation experiments demonstrate that ExS2D reduces the average execution steps by 54.4%, while maintaining a comparable success rate to a single-arm baseline. Real-robot experiments on four tasks further demonstrate the ExS2D’s reliability in terms of dual-arm execution under few-shot single-arm samples, while using zero bimanual demonstrations.

records.title: VLA-InfoEntropy: A Training-Free Vision-Attention Information Entropy Approach for Vision-Language-Action Models Inference Acceleration and Success
records.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models integrate visual perception, language understanding, and action decision-making for cross-modal semantic alignment, exhibiting broad application potential. However, the joint processing of high-dimensional visual features, complex linguistic inputs, and continuous action sequences incurs significant computational overhead and low inference efficiency, thereby hindering real-time deployment and reliability. To address this issue, we use image entropy to quantify the grayscale distribution characteristics of each visual token and introduce attention entropy to capture the distribution of attention scores over task-related text. Visual entropy identifies texture-rich or structurally informative regions, while attention entropy pinpoints semantically relevant tokens. Combined with timestep information, these metrics enable a dynamic transition strategy that shifts the model's focus from global visual features to attention-guided local informative regions. Thus, the resulting VLA-InfoEntropy method integrates spatial, semantic, and temporal cues to reduce redundancy while preserving critical content. Extensive experiments show that our method reduces inference parameters, accelerates inference speed, and outperforms existing approaches.

records.title: MirrorBench: Evaluating Self-centric Intelligence in MLLMs by Introducing a Mirror
records.abstract: Recent progress in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) has demonstrated remarkable advances in perception and reasoning, suggesting their potential for embodied intelligence. While recent studies have evaluated embodied MLLMs in interactive settings, current benchmarks mainly target capabilities to perceive, understand, and interact with external objects, lacking a systematic evaluation of self-centric intelligence. To address this, we introduce MirrorBench, a simulation-based benchmark inspired by the classical Mirror Self-Recognition (MSR) test in psychology. MirrorBench extends this paradigm to embodied MLLMs through a tiered framework of progressively challenging tasks, assessing agents from basic visual perception to high-level self-representation. Experiments on leading MLLMs show that even at the lowest level, their performance remains substantially inferior to human performance, revealing fundamental limitations in self-referential understanding. Our study bridges psychological paradigms and embodied intelligence, offering a principled framework for evaluating the emergence of general intelligence in large models.

records.title: Is-NeRF: In-scattering Neural Radiance Field for Blurred Images
records.abstract: Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) has gained significant attention for its prominent implicit 3D representation and realistic novel view synthesis capabilities. Available works unexceptionally employ straight-line volume rendering, which struggles to handle sophisticated lightpath scenarios and introduces geometric ambiguities during training, particularly evident when processing motion-blurred images. To address these challenges, this work proposes a novel deblur neural radiance field, Is-NeRF, featuring explicit lightpath modeling in real-world environments. By unifying six common light propagation phenomena through an in-scattering representation, we establish a new scattering-aware volume rendering pipeline adaptable to complex lightpaths. Additionally, we introduce an adaptive learning strategy that enables autonomous determining of scattering directions and sampling intervals to capture finer object details. The proposed network jointly optimizes NeRF parameters, scattering parameters, and camera motions to recover fine-grained scene representations from blurry images. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate that it effectively handles complex real-world scenarios, outperforming state-of-the-art approaches in generating high-fidelity images with accurate geometric details.

records.title: Advanced Context Modeling for Enhanced Aircraft Trajectory Prediction in Terminal Airspace
records.abstract: Predicting the future movement of aircraft, particularly in complex scenarios such as near-terminal airspace, is a critical yet challenging problem in aviation, essential for intelligent air traffic management tasks such as capacity estimation. Unlike land transportation networks, airway maps, such as Standard Instrument Departures (SIDs) and Standard Terminal Arrival Routes (STARs), offer less constrained guidance for typical flight departures and arrivals. This is due to frequent maneuvering practices, such as vectoring and holding, which introduce significant deviations from predefined routes. As a result, effectively leveraging map information remains challenging and is largely underexplored in existing aircraft trajectory prediction methods. To bridge this gap, we introduce RecTrajNet, a novel multitask learning framework that jointly encodes airway maps, preceding flights, agent dynamics, and environmental context into a compact and informative representation. It first extracts individual features for aircraft and waypoints, and subsequently models their interactions through a Graph Attention Network. Two related tasks, trajectory prediction and estimated time of arrival, are jointly optimized to learn informative node representations, which not only improve prediction accuracy but can also be seamlessly integrated into existing trajectory prediction models as a map-related feature. The effectiveness of our proposed method is demonstrated on two real-world aircraft trajectory datasets, where it outperforms existing approaches and achieves state-of-the-art performance on trajectory prediction in both towered and non-towered near-terminal airspace.

records.title: ReciproNet: Semantic-Spatial Reciprocal Feature Enhancement for Radar-Camera 3D Object Detection
records.abstract: Radar-camera fusion is critical for 3D object detection, yet simple feature fusion fails to address the inherent physical limitations (e.g., radar noise and visual occlusion) of each modality. In particular, the extreme sparsity of radar data hampers geometric representation, while visual depth ambiguity leads to feature misalignment in the Bird’s-Eye-View (BEV) space. To address these issues, we propose ReciproNet, which employs a bidirectional guidance mechanism to enhance modality-specific features prior to fusion. First, we introduce a Semantic-Guided Radar Generation (SGRG) module that leverages image semantics to densify radar points and suppress noise. Second, we present a Radar-Guided View Transformation (RGVT) module that exploits radar depth priors to correct geometric distortions in visual features. Experiments on the View-of-Delft dataset demonstrate that ReciproNet achieves strong detection accuracy with negligible parameter overhead, demonstrating the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed reciprocal enhancement strategy.

records.title: Visual Visibility Estimation with Physics-Aware Ordinal Prompt Learning
records.abstract: While deep learning has revolutionized meteorological sensing, a fundamental dissonance persists: the stochastic, continuous evolution of atmospheric aerosols is conflicts with the rigid, discrete regression paradigms dominating modern visibility estimation. Purely data-driven approaches frequently decouple from physical reality, struggling particularly in data-scarce regimes. Visibility Estimation Contrastive Language-Image Pre-Training (VEClip) bridges this physical-semantic gap. By repurposing the CLIP framework, this architecture enforces ordinal constraints through a dual-stream, physics-grounded lens. The visual stream employs Gated Feature Fusion to synergize high-level RGB semantics with explicit dark channel and depth priors, effectively strictly capturing haze density manifolds. Concurrently, the textual stream abandons static class tokens in favor of Physics-Informed Ordinal Prompt Learning, anchoring embeddings via LLM-synthesized scattering descriptions to align the latent space with meteorological laws. Complementing this framework is Mapped Foggy Highway Visibility Images (MFHVI), a benchmark of 13,661 images distinguished by rigorous spatial calibration that eliminates the sensor misalignment artifacts plaguing existing datasets. Empirical benchmarks are decisive: VEClip reduces Mean Absolute Error (MAE) by 55.2\% against specialized baselines, demonstrating robust generalization even within strict few-shot constraints.

records.title: Decoupling Scene-Agnostic and Scene-Specific Knowledge: A Continual Learning Framework for Motion Prediction
records.abstract: Motion predictors for autonomous vehicles must support continuous evolution under unseen scenarios. To this end, we propose a Continual Learning Framework for motion prediction that decouples the learning of Scene-Agnostic Knowledge and Scene-Specific Knowledge. To ensure stability, we integrate Vector Quantization (VQ) modules into a Transformer-based backbone of the predictor, preserving Scene-Agnostic Knowledge through codebooks generated during VQ pre-training. During continual learning, we employ a Dual-Consolidation mechanism to prevent catastrophic forgetting through anchoring intermediate representations to pre-learned codebooks and imposing regularization on critical parameters. To foster plasticity, we devise a Hierarchical Adaptive Prompting mechanism. By leveraging multi-level scene queries generated from intermediate features, this mechanism dynamically generates scene context-aware prompts that guide the prediction process toward effective learning of Scene-Specific Knowledge. Extensive experiments under intra-dataset and cross-dataset settings demonstrate that our method achieves a superior stability-plasticity balance, significantly mitigating catastrophic forgetting while enhancing prediction performance.

records.title: Beyond Quantity: Distribution-Aware Labeling for Visual Grounding
records.abstract: Visual grounding requires large and diverse region–text pairs. However, manual annotation is costly and fixed vocabularies restrict scalability and generalization. Existing pseudo-labeling pipelines often overfit to biased distributions. Through a systematic analysis of data coverage, we find that performance gains come less from raw data volume and more from effective distribution expansion. Motivated by this insight, we propose DAL, a distribution-aware labeling framework for visual grounding. The proposed method consists of three steps: (1) initial labeling through both closed-set and open-set paths; (2) explicitly generate out-of-distribution data to broaden semantic coverage; and (3) filtering to remove noise and rebalance data distribution.Extensive experiments on four visual grounding tasks demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms strong baselines and achieves state-of-the-art results, underscoring the critical role of distribution-aware labeling.

records.title: T-MOR: Learning Motion-Aware Skeleton Representations for Human Action Recognition
records.abstract: Vision-language models such as CLIP have recently achieved strong performance on a wide range of visual understanding tasks. However, most existing models rely primarily on appearance-level supervision from images or videos, and do not explicitly model human motion, which is essential for fine-grained and human-centric action recognition task as actions are defined by temporally structured and physically grounded body movements. To address this problem, we propose Transferable skeleton MOtion Representation (T-MOR), a motion-aware framework that learns transferable action representations from skeleton sequences with the aid of video and language supervision during training. T-MOR adopts a multi-modal contrastive learning scheme that aligns skeleton motion with visual and textual representations, while performing inference using only lightweight skeleton inputs. To support large-scale pre-training, we construct PoseCap-1M, a new dataset that contains over one million synchronized video, skeleton, and text triplets covering diverse human activities. We evaluate T-MOR on a range of human-centric action recognition benchmarks, including action classification and frame-wise temporal detection. Experimental results show that T-MOR consistently improves performance across multiple datasets, such as Toyota Smarthome, Penn Action, UAV-Human, TSU, and Charades. In addition, T-MOR demonstrates strong generalization ability in few-shot and zero-shot settings, highlighting the effectiveness of motion-centric and embodied representations for transferable action understanding.

records.title: Pay More Attention to Irregular Targets: A Complexity-Aware Framework for Incremental Infrared Small Target Detection
records.abstract: Incremental infrared small target detection aims to train a model to segment infrared small targets in sequentially arriving scenarios, with only current-scenario data accessible. As scenarios evolve, detection performance on previous scenarios usually degenerates due to catastrophic forgetting. We observe that, in incremental infrared small target detection, the target complexity varies drastically in different scenarios, and catastrophic forgetting occurs mainly in irregular and complex targets. Although typical incremental learning methods can be directly applied to incremental infrared small target detection, they ignore the target complexity, which constrains their performance. In this paper, we pay more attention to the irregular targets and propose a complexity-aware framework for incremental infrared small target detection. Specifically, we propose a Dual-Scale Attention module, a Complexity-Aware Small Target Buffer, and its corresponding training method. Experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms previous state-of-the-art incremental learning methods.

records.title: Prototype-Based Low Altitude UAV Semantic Segmentation
records.abstract: Semantic segmentation of low-altitude UAV imagery presents unique challenges due to extreme scale variations, complex object boundaries, and limited computational resources on edge devices. Existing transformer-based segmentation methods achieve remarkable performance but incur high computational overhead, while lightweight approaches struggle to capture fine-grained details in high-resolution aerial scenes. To address these limitations, we propose PBSeg, an efficient prototype-based segmentation framework tailored for UAV applications. PBSeg introduces a novel prototype-based cross-attention (PBCA) that exploits feature redundancy to reduce computational complexity while maintaining segmentation quality. The framework incorporates an efficient multi-scale feature extraction module that combines deformable convolutions (DConv) with context-aware modulation (CAM) to capture both local details and global semantics. Experiments on two challenging UAV datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. PBSeg achieves 71.86 mIoU on UAVid and 80.92 mIoU on UDD6, establishing competitive performance while maintaining computational efficiency. Code is available at https://github.com/zhangda1018/PBSeg.

records.title: AdaSAM-MOT: Uncertainty-Aware Mask-Informed Association for High-efficiency UAV Tracking
records.abstract: UAV Multi-Object Tracking is a cornerstone of intelligent multimedia surveillance, yet relies heavily on bounding boxes that inevitably introduce severe background noise. While segmentation-based paradigms offer fine-grained semantics, their prohibitive latency hinders real-time deployment on edge devices. To resolve this, we propose AdaSAM-MOT, a framework pioneering Mask-Informed Feature Purification. Unlike prior association-centric decoders that operate on noisy global features, we introduce a Mask-Guided Similarity Decoder. It utilizes on-demand masks as hard spatial attention to strictly suppress background interference, distilling noise-robust object semantics for precise identification. Crucially, to reconcile the conflict between fine-grained sensing and computational efficiency, we design an Uncertainty-Aware Gating Mechanism(UGAM). Operating on the principle of Semantic Sparsity, this module synthesizes motion instability and association ambiguity to dynamically allocate computational resources, triggering expensive segmentation strictly for high-uncertainty targets. Experiments on VisDrone and UAVDT demonstrate state-of-the-art HOTA and real-time performance, validating our paradigm as a feasible solution for high-precision aerial multimedia systems.

records.title: OmniFood-Bench: Evaluating VLMs for Nutrient Reasoning and Personalized Health Advice
records.abstract: The rapid integration of Large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) into critical infrastructure promises to revolutionize personalized healthcare and dietary management. However, in the domain of food systems, autonomous agents face a unique and persistent challenge: the "Systemic Information Asymmetry" between visual appearance and intrinsic nutritional composition. Existing benchmarks primarily focus on coarse-grained classification tasks, such as food category recognition, which fail to evaluate the intricate reasoning chain required for real-world dietary management—specifically, the ability to traverse from identifying hidden ingredients to estimating physical mass, and finally synthesizing safety-critical medical advice. In this paper, we introduce OmniFood-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark constructed from the MM-Food-100K dataset. Unlike previous works, OmniFood-Bench evaluates VLMs across three progressive capabilities: Basic Perception (Ingredients & Cooking Methods), Quantitative Reasoning (Portion Size & Nutritional Profiling), and Safety-Critical Advisory (Disease-Specific Recommendations). We evaluate six state-of-the-art VLMs, including gpt-5.1, gemini-3-flash, and qwen3-vl-8B. Our extensive experiments reveal a startling "Semantic-Physical Gap": while models achieve near-human accuracy in naming dishes, they exhibit catastrophic failure in mass estimation and frequently hallucinate benign advice for high-risk diabetic profiles. This work establishes a rigorous standard for trustworthiness in autonomous agents deployed for public health.The code and datasets are available in:https://anonymous.4open.science/r/OmniFood-Bench-7D0B

records.title: ILAgents: Edge-Native Cognitive Kernels for Resilient and Deterministic Food Perception
records.abstract: Resilient food systems require intelligent monitoring beyond passive observation. While Agentic AI relies on Large Multimodal Models for reasoning, their high latency, energy inefficiency, and probabilistic hallucinations make them unsuitable for real-time, safety-critical industrial edge applications. To address this, we propose ILAgents, a decentralized framework of Edge-Native Autonomous Agents governed by a consortium blockchain. Unlike passive federated learning nodes, ILAgents use heterogeneous Cognitive Kernels, which are specialized convex optimization-based learners designed for interpretability and efficiency. The agents employ a dynamic Objectivity-Based Consensus (OBCA) mechanism for self-evaluation of perceptual confidence and model aggregation. By harmonizing diverse visual interpretations without the overhead of generative models, ILAgents resolve Visual Isomerism and data silos. This work establishes a deterministic, trust-based collaborative paradigm, showing that agency is defined by autonomy and negotiation, not model size.

records.title: TV-Hint: A Hybrid Intelligence Approach for Enhancing Cognitive-Aging Adults' TV Viewing Experience
records.abstract: Watching television series remains the most prevalent entertainment activity among old adults in China. Though excessive television viewing may lead to physical and psychological risks, watching TV properly can still bring potential benefits, such as maintaining cognitive ability through watching TV series with complex plots, narratives, and relationships among characters. However, many old adults, due to cognitive decline, often find it difficult to enjoy those complex TV series. This paper proposed TV-Hint, an approach combining state-of-the-art video scene segmentation techniques and human effort to enhance cognitive-aging adults' TV viewing experience. We evaluated TV-Hint with 21 old adults in 60s and 70s. The results show that (1) helps them better understand the plots, and (2) makes them more engaged in TV viewing, thus demonstrating TV-Hint's effectiveness. We also discussed the future work.

records.title: Structure-aware Keypoint Localization for Videofluoroscopic Swallowing Study
records.abstract: Videofluoroscopic Swallowing Study (VFSS) is one of the gold standard for diagnosing swallowing disorders, providing dynamic X-ray imaging of the swallowing process. Automated kinematic analysis in VFSS relies fundamentally on precise anatomical keypoint localization. However, existing studies focus on limited keypoints (e.g., cervical vertebrae or the hyoid) and overlook critical regions such as the soft palate, while annotating only active swallowing segments and ignoring abundant non-swallowing data, resulting in poor data efficiency. Moreover, leveraging this unlabeled data via standard semi-supervised learning is suboptimal, as generic methods are prone to spatial bias. In medical X-rays with fixed layouts, models tend to memorize absolute coordinates rather than understanding anatomical structures. To tackle these challenges, we introduce VFSSKep, a novel dataset that extends annotations to the soft palate and incorporates large-scale unlabeled data. We further propose S$^3$KL, a Structure-aware Semi-Supervised Keypoint Localization framework designed to overcome spatial bias. It integrates a Structure-Aware Learning strategy to extract high-resolution structural cues for structure-aware representation learning, and a Structural Representation Consistency Learning strategy with block shuffling to enforce invariant structural recognition. Experiments show our method achieves state-of-the-art semi-supervised performance, even with unlabeled and 25% labeled data surpassing fully supervised learning with 100% labeled data. Code and data will be made publicly available at: https://github.com/kaai520/S3KL.

records.title: A Trustworthy Watermarking Framework for LLM-Generated Food Safety Content
records.abstract: Large language models are transforming many industries with their text generation abilities. However, their outputs can be easily tampered with, creating serious risks in critical areas like food safety reporting. To protect the integrity and traceability of AI-generated content, this paper introduces ToSS (Token Oriented Repartitioning and Strategic Selection), a reliable authentication method using adaptive dual watermarking. The key innovation of ToSS is its dual watermark encoding approach that divides vocabulary tokens into black and white sublists, enabling precise bit-level embedding of traceability information. Additionally, an entropy adaptive mechanism dynamically selects text regions with high prediction uncertainty for watermark insertion, maintaining text fluency and factual accuracy while ensuring reliable traceability. Experiments on multiple datasets, including food domain texts, demonstrate that ToSS achieves leading performance in both watermark capacity and decoding accuracy.

records.title: ReaCH: Diagnostic Reasoning Enhanced Radiology Report Generation via Hierarchical Contrastive Learning
records.abstract: Radiology Report Generation (RRG) automates diagnostic reporting from medical images. However, existing methods typically treat the task as direct image-to-text translation, bypassing explicit reasoning. This reasoning-free paradigm often leads to hallucinations and clinically inconsistent statements, thereby undermining clinical trust. To bridge this gap, we propose ReaCH, which reconstructs the radiologist's cognitive workflow via a Clinical Diagnostic Reasoning Chain to ensure reports derive from verified conclusions. To supervise the model's alignment with clinical evidence throughout this chain, we also design a Hierarchical Contrastive Learning Framework with three complementary strategies: (1) Region Contrastive Learning for fine-grained visual grounding, (2) Context Contrastive Learning for logical consistency, and (3) Feature Augmentation Contrastive Learning for linguistic robustness. Experiments on MIMIC-CXR and IU-Xray demonstrate ReaCH's superiority in generation quality and clinical efficacy.

records.title: Q1B: Toward Efficient 1-Bit CT Image Quality Assessment via MLLM Representation
records.abstract: Conventional Computed Tomography (CT) blind image quality assessment (BIQA) relies on full 8-bit image data, imposing burdens on transmission bandwidth and storage capacity. Inspired by the fact that human perception is more sensitive to structure than pixel values, we conduct experiments and verify that even 1-bit structure images can achieve promising performance using MLLMs, indicating that high bit-depth might be redundant. However, the information loss in 1-bit images limits performance, and the high MLLM computational cost restricts their practicality. To address these, we propose Q1B, the first dedicated BIQA model for 1-bit CT images. Q1B utilizes MLLM encoders to leverage their powerful representation capabilities for extracting rich visual structural features. To compensate for information loss, we develop an information enhancement network utilizing original 8-bit image histogram statistics as prior knowledge. Furthermore, a text-conditioned cross-attention adaptively modulates channel and token-wise importance to focus on critical image features. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that Q1B achieves superior performance, with a PLCC reaching up to 94\%, which is comparable to full 8-bit assessments. Meanwhile, Q1B reduces the parameter count by approximately 88\% compared with MLLMs.

records.title: Diag2RG: Diagnosis-Aligned Regional Reasoning for Reliable CT Report Generation
records.abstract: Automated CT report generation is pivotal for mitigating the increasing workload of radiologists. However, prevailing methods primarily rely on global features, wherein substantial background noise dilutes the feature density of pathological lesions, consequently inducing model hallucinations and erroneous descriptions. To circumvent these limitations, we propose a novel paradigm termed Diag2RG. We eschew the noise-prone global branch to concentrate on key anatomical regions guided by anatomical segmentation priors. We introduce a diagnosis-aligned visual representation learning strategy that leverages diagnostic knowledge to constrain the visual encoder to precisely localize abnormalities. Furthermore, we model topological dependencies among anatomical regions via a hybrid cross-region reasoning module, thereby supplementing global contextual information and ensuring report logical consistency. Empirical evaluations on two chest CT datasets demonstrate that Diag2RG outperforms current state-of-the-art methods; critically, it effectively reduces diagnostic errors induced by noise, thereby enhancing the clinical credibility of the generated reports.
